What is the Ignore Feature?

In addition to Blocking and Muting, Discord also lets users ignore specific users.

When ignoring a user, here’s what happens:

  • When a user is ignored, their direct messages (DM) appear darkened. You’ll also see the Ignore [] icon next to their messages.
DM with an Ignore Icon
  • Their messages will be hidden in DMs, group chats, and servers. If you want to view these ignored messages, simply press the Show button.
Show Button For Ignored Message
  • Before viewing an ignored user’s profile, you’ll see a warning screen. Their profile will display their ignored status.
Warning Screens: Ignored User’s Profile (Left) and Profile Ignore Status (Right)
  • If you attempt to join a voice or video call that includes someone you’ve ignored, you’ll receive a warning before connecting.
Example of Voice or Video Warning

How to Ignore a User

There are a few different places to find this setting for each user. You will see the Ignore option when:

When Viewing a User’s Profile
  • To ignore a specific user, right-click the user’s avatar to open the drop-down menu.
  • Select the Ignore option.
  • After making your selection, press Ignore in the confirmation pop-up window.
How to Ignore a User While Viewing a User’s Profile on Desktop

To ignore a user on mobile, tap their avatar, then tap the ellipsis [] in the upper-right corner > Ignore.

How to Ignore a User While Viewing a User’s Profile on Mobile
In Safety Tools and Safety Alerts

Safety tools and Safety Alerts warn teen users when we detect potentially inappropriate messages. Teens can choose to select the Ignore option when these tools and alerts appear.

Safety Tools Ignore Option: Desktop (Left) vs. Mobile (Right)
After Submitting a Report

To ignore a user, right-click the message you would like to report and press Report Message. After submitting a report, you will be able to select the Ignore option in the More you can do menu.

Message Reporting: Right-Click Menu (Left) and Ignore Option in “More You Can Do” Menu (Right)

On mobile, long press the message you would like to report and tap Report. After the report has been submitted, you will be able to ignore the user.

After Report Submission: Mobile Ignore Option
In a Direct Message

  1. To ignore a specific user in a DM, right-click the user’s avatar to open the drop-down menu.

  2. Select the Ignore option.

  3. After making your selection, press Ignore in the confirmation pop-up window.

How to Ignore a User in DMs on Desktop

On mobile, tap the user in DMs, then select the ellipsis [] > Ignore and confirm your choice.

How to Ignore a User in DMs on Mobile

Managing the Accounts You’ve Ignored

Desktop/Browser

To manage the accounts you’ve ignored on desktop or browser, you can view your list at any time by going to your User Settings [] > Content & Social. There you’ll find the Accounts you’ve blocked & ignored list.

Content & Social on Desktop: Accounts You’ve Blocked & Ignored List
Mobile
  1. On mobile, you can view your list of ignored users by tapping your avatar in the bottom-right corner.
Avatar Icon on Mobile

  1. Then, tap the cogwheel [] in the upper-right corner to navigate to Settings > Content & Social.

  2. There you can scroll down to the Accounts you’ve blocked & ignored list where you can tap Ignored accounts.

Content & Social on Mobile: Accounts You’ve Blocked & Ignored List

How to Un-Ignore a User

You can un-ignore a user at any time. Here are three ways to do this on desktop or browser:

  1. Un-Ignore from Friend List: Right-clicking the ignored user in your Friends List, then select Unignore.
Un-ignoring a User in the Friends List
  1. Un-Ignore from Profile: Select the ellipsis [] and press Unignore or use the Unignore button next to the You ignored them notice.
Unignore Options in a User’s Profile
  1. Un-Ignore in Content & Social: Go to User Settings > Content & Social. Then scroll to the Accounts you’ve blocked & ignored list and select Unignore next to the specific user you would like to un-ignore.
Un-ignoring a User in Content & Social

On mobile, tap the user’s avatar, then select the ellipsis [] > Unignore. Alternatively, go to Settings > Content & Social > Accounts you’ve blocked or ignored, then tap Unignore in the Ignored accounts list.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Will the user know that I ignored them?

A: No, they will not be able to visually detect in their Discord experience that you have ignored their account.

Q: Can ignored users still see my messages?

A: Yes, they can still view your messages and profile. They will not be able to visually detect in their Discord experience that you have ignored their account.

Q: What’s the difference between blocking and ignoring?

A: What Happens When You Ignore Someone:

Feature

Your Experience

The Ignored User’s Experience

Direct Messages

You can still send them direct messages. Their messages to you will be hidden without notifications.

They can still message you (but you won’t get notifications).

Messages in shared spaces

You can still tag or reply to their messages. Their messages to you will be hidden without notifications.

They can still message, tag, and interact with you (but you won’t get notifications).

Profile Visibility

Their profile is hidden unless you choose to unhide it.

They can see your full profile.

Activity Visibility

Limited activity visibility; some group activity may still show.

They can see your online presence and activity.

Friendship Status

Friends are not removed; if you are not friends, their friend requests go to the friend request inbox without alerts.

They remain your friend, or non-friends can still send new friend requests.

What Happens When You Block Someone:

Feature

Your Experience

The Blocked User’s Experience

Direct Messages

You cannot send messages to a blocked user.

They cannot message you

Messages in shared spaces

You can still tag or reply to their messages. Their messages to you will be hidden without notifications.

They can still message, tag, and interact with you (but you won’t get notifications).

Profile Visibility

Their profile is hidden unless you choose to unhide it.

They see a limited version of your profile.

Activity Visibility

Limited activity visibility; some group activity may still show.

Limited activity visibility; some group activity may still show.

Friendship Status

Friendship is removed, and they cannot send new friend requests.

They are unfriended and see an error when trying to re-add you.

Inactive Account Deletion

If you have not been on Discord for a couple of years, you may have received an email or text to let you know your account is going to be deleted. Oh no!

On Discord, accounts that have not been used for 2 years or more may be scheduled to be deleted. As your account nears the 2 years mark you may get an email or text message warning you that your account is scheduled to be deleted.

How Do I Prevent Deletion

If you were notified that your account is going to be deleted because of inactivity - you can prevent the deletion by logging into Discord on the website or app. The email/phone number associated with your account should have been included in the message you received.

Once you log into your account you should receive a message from Discord to let you know that the account deletion has been canceled:

Note: If you have two-factor authentication enabled and you can’t find your codes you can learn more here. If you do not have access to your backup codes, we are unable to remove 2FA and you will have to create a new account. Unfortunately, Discord cannot remove 2FA or issue you new backup codes.
How Do I Request My Account To Be Deleted?

You can always manage your account in user settings including asking for your account to be deleted.

Limited Access FAQ

If Discord detects suspicious account behavior on your account, we may place your account in Limited Access.

If your account is in Limited Access, you will not be able to join new servers or initiate new direct messages. Placing accounts with suspicious behavior in limited access helps us maintain a high quality experience for everyone on the platform.

How do I know I’ve been placed in Limited Access?

You will see a red bar at the top of your Discord client that says: Hey, something looks off with your account so we limited your access, but sometimes we make mistakes.

While you are in Limited Access, you will not be able to dismiss this notice.

In Limited Access, you can:

  • Message your existing friends You can’t:

  • Send outgoing friend requests

  • Direct message any new friends added while you were in Limited Access

  • Join new servers When attempting to join new servers, you will see this notification:

When attempting to message new friends added while you were in limited access, you will see this notification instead of the chat box:

How You’ll Appear to Others when in Limited Access

Other users will not see any indication that your account is in Limited Access.

Getting out of Limited Access

If you think we’ve made a mistake, you can use any of the methods below to submit a ticket to regain access:

  1. Clicking on the ‘Regain Access Here’ button at the top of your Discord client

  2. Clicking on the ‘Regain Access Here’ link in the Limited Access notification that appears when you try to join a new server

  3. Submit a ticket here.

My Discord Account was Hacked or Compromised

Important: Discord Staff will never contact users directly through the Discord app for support-related matters. If someone requests personal information, asks for payment, or urges you to change your login credentials, please do not comply and avoid further interaction.

As per our Terms of Service, you are responsible for the security of your account.

Please note that if you fail to secure your account and it is compromised, Discord may be unable to assist in its recovery.

What this article covers:

  • How to Keep Your Discord Account Safe
  • What to Do if You Suspect Your Discord Account Has been Hacked or Compromised
  • How to Report Abusive Behavior on Discord
  • Frequently Asked Questions Important: If you suspect your account has been compromised, check your email first! You can temporarily change your email on your account through a link in the “Discord Email Address changed” email. If you still need support, submit a report to the Discord team through our support form linked here.

How to Keep Your Discord Account Safe

To keep your Discord account safe, always avoid clicking on links or downloading files from unknown or untrusted sources. Malicious links and downloads can compromise your account and personal data. Additionally, enable Multi-Factor Authentication, use a strong, unique password, and be cautious of unsolicited messages—especially those requesting personal information. Staying vigilant and following these security practices will help keep your account protected.

For more information on how to keep your account safe, visit our Discord Safety Center to read these articles below:

  • Four steps to a super safe account
  • Scams and what to look out for
  • Tips against spam and hacking

What to Do if You Suspect Your Discord Account Has Been Hacked or Compromised

If you’re concerned about the security of your account, a good first step is to reset your password and ensure that Multi-Factor Authentication is enabled.

Review your Authorized Apps and remove any unwanted applications that have access to your account:

  1. On desktop/browser, tap on the cogwheel icon [] in the lower-left corner of the app to access your User Settings.
Cogwheel icon
  1. Tap on Authorized Apps. Here you can deauthorize any apps that are unwanted by pressing on Deauthorize.
Deauthorize button

  1. If you’re on mobile, tap on your avatar in the bottom-right corner and then select the cogwheel icon [] at the top-right.

  2. Tap on Authorized Apps and remove any you don’t recognize by tapping on the x button.

Authorized Apps on mobile

Finally, to ensure your device’s security, we recommend running a Windows defender scan if you’re on Windows to check for any potential viruses.

For your protection, be mindful of the most common types of security threats:

  • Suspicious Links or Files – These may appear as “games” or promises of “free Nitro” but are often designed to steal your login credentials.
  • Social Engineering – This involves individuals attempting to manipulate you into sharing your login, confidential, or personal information, which can then be used for fraudulent activities or to target other users.
    • Examples include scammers impersonating Discord employees offering to “appeal actions on your account” or asking for your credit card details to help you “win a giveaway.” Staying informed and cautious can help keep your account secure! For additional tips on how keep your account secure, please check out these articles:
  • Understanding and Avoiding Common Scams
  • Scams and What to Look out for
  • Protecting Against Scams on Discord

How to Report Abusive Behavior on Discord

When you encounter abusive behavior, please submit a report through the Discord app. Here’s how:

  1. Select the Message you wish to report. On mobile, hold down on the Message, and on desktop/browser, “right-click.”

  2. Select Report Message.

  3. Select the type of abuse you’re seeing.

You can learn more about how to send reports to Discord (including how to report user profiles) through here. Additionally, you can learn about customizing your Discord experience and avoiding unwanted interactions in our Safety Center.

Important: If you believe your account has been compromised or accessed, please submit a ticket to our team through here: dis.gd/hackedaccount. Please provide all required information if there have been any unauthorized transactions resulting from your compromised account. Our team will assist you according to our policies and guidelines.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What do I do if I see billing charges on my account that may have happened after losing control of my account?

A: If you haven’t already, please be sure to submit a request to our team through here and include that there have been unauthorized transactions.

Please note that filing a chargeback or refund request directly with your financial institution for any transactions that occurred on Discord may result in account suspension pending further investigation on our end. For more information regarding our Chargeback Policy, please refer to our Chargeback FAQ. To request a refund, please submit a request to our billing team: dis.gd/billing

My Discord Email was Changed and I Want to Undo It

What this article covers:

  • How to Undo an Email Address Change
  • I Got an Error When Trying to Undo My Email Change
  • How Does the Account Recovery Link Actually Work? Note: Please note that account recovery links will become invalid after a 48 hour time period. Do not share this link to others.

Changing the email on your Discord account is a big deal! That’s why we send you an extra email notification to the original email address after it’s been confirmed.

This message also includes a button to let you revert or undo the email change within 48 hours, as an extra method to keep you in control of your account.

How to Undo an Email Address Change

Note: The URL will always start with discord.com - anything else is fake and not from Discord!

  1. To start, press the button in the email notification we sent you that says Start Account Recovery.

This link is uniquely generated for your account and is only valid for 48 hours - don’t share it with anyone!

  1. After tapping the link, you’ll be taken to an Account Recovery page where you will be able to complete the following:
  • Change your Discord account’s email back to the previous email address
  • Log out the Discord account from all devices
  • Update your password
  • Remove any phone number on the Discord account
  • Remove any Multi-Factor Authentication methods on the Discord account
  • Invalidate existing recovery URLs for email changes to your account made after this one
  1. To complete the process, follow the instructions after pressing Start revert process.

You’ll provide a new password, and then the email address for your Discord account will be reverted to the one we sent the recovery link to - alongside the other changes listed on the page.

Note: If you had a phone number or MFA device enrolled on the account, be sure to add those back after completing the recovery process! For more details, check out the Setting up Multi-Factor Authentication Help Center article.

I Got an Error When Trying to Undo My Email Change

For technical reasons, you’ll only see an error when trying to complete the password reset part of this process, and not before that.

Common reasons you could see an error here are:

  • It’s been more than 48 hours since we sent you the recovery link, and it’s no longer valid.
  • A recovery has already been performed on this account using a link we sent before the one being used.
  • The email address that the link was sent to is currently in use by another Discord account. To complete the account recovery, ensure that no other Discord accounts are using that email address.
  • The password you’re attempting to set is invalid. For example, we don’t accept passwords less than 8 characters, and some regions may have additional password requirements Note: If your account recovery link has expired, the Discord support team is not able to send you a new one.

How Does the Account Recovery Link Work?

To ensure the security of the account (and prevent scammers from regaining access to the account after you perform the recovery), the following restrictions are in place for the recovery process:

  • The link is only valid for 48 hours.
  • If multiple recovery links have been generated for an account, using one will invalidate any that were created after the one that was used.
  • Any phone number and MFA devices associated with the account are removed.
  • You are required to change your password during this process (in case someone knows your current password), and the Discord account will be logged out from all devices. Note: If you’d like to learn more information about compromised or hacked accounts and how to report abusive behavior on Discord, please review our My Discord Account was Hacked or Compromised Help Center article.

Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery Reporting Under the UK Online Safety Act (OSA)

Note: Individuals to whom the UK Online Safety Act does not apply may submit reports of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) through our standard in-app reporting system. Our non-consensual intimate imagery policy applies globally in addition to other legal rights you may have where you live.

The Online Safety Act (OSA) is a UK law that applies to companies like Discord and carries certain obligations regarding illegal content, including non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII), sometimes referred to as “revenge porn” or “image-based sexual abuse.” Under the OSA and relevant codes of practice, covered platforms, like Discord, must provide a clear reporting process, review qualifying removal requests, remove NCII content, and use tools such as hash-matching to help prevent that content from being shared or re-uploaded.

Important: Need immediate help? If you have concerns about your personal safety, or the safety of someone you know, please contact local law enforcement or social services.

What this article covers:

  • Our Responsibilities Under the OSA
  • What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request Under the OSA

Our Responsibilities Under the OSA

If you are affected, you, or a representative acting on your behalf, may:

  • Notify Discord of any non-consensual intimate image published on Discord that depicts you and was shared without your consent; and,

  • Submit a request for Discord to remove the content. For more details about how to submit a removal request, you can refer to our help article. So that we can help you, please make sure your removal request meets these requirements:

  • You are identifiable in the content or via the context in which it is displayed (for example, your face is visible or your name is mentioned);

  • The content shows you nude, partially nude, or engaged in sexual activity; and,

  • The content was shared without your consent. Discord may also action content submitted for removal through this process even if it does not meet the criteria above, such as for violation of our Community Guidelines, or where other UK laws may apply. Discord also reports content that it reasonably believes depicts persons under the age of 18 years old to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, and takes enforcement action against users who post such content.

Under the OSA, Discord, as a regulated service, is required to:

  • Maintain a clear and accessible process that allows an affected individual (or their authorised representative) to report non-consensual intimate imagery;
  • Review each report and assess it against illegal content requirements;
  • Remove the reported content confirmed to be illegal NCII within the 48 hour time period required by law; and,
  • Make reasonable efforts to identify and remove known copies of the same non-consensual intimate visual depiction.

What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request Under the OSA

We will promptly review your report to assess whether the content meets the legal requirements for removal. If your report is complete and the content is confirmed to be non-consensual intimate imagery, we will remove it and take reasonable steps to prevent known copies from being re-shared, including through hash-matching where applicable.

If your submission is incomplete, we may be unable to process your report until sufficient information is provided.

You can also find independent support from organisations such as the Revenge Porn Helpline or StopNCII.org.

Reporting Abusive Behavior to Discord

If you encounter a violation of our Terms of Service or Community Guidelines, we ask that you report this behavior to us.

For more information on reporting abusive behavior, visit our Discord Safety Center to read this article below.

Discord Safety Center: 🔗 Reporting Abusive Behavior to Discord

Safety Resources for Australian Users

Discord is committed to helping keep Australian users safer online. This page brings together important information about Discord’s safety tools, how to report harmful content, and your rights under Australia’s online safety laws — including how to contact Australia’s independent online safety regulator, the eSafety Commissioner.

What this article covers:

  • Introduction to Australia’s eSafety Commissioner
    • Default Safety Settings for Australian Users
    • Additional Protections for Teens
  • Safety Tools You Can Use
  • How to Report a User or Content on Discord

Introduction to Australia’s eSafety Commissioner

The eSafety Commissioner is Australia’s independent regulator for online safety. eSafety works to protect all Australians from the most serious forms of online harm and promotes safer, more positive online experiences.

  • Learn more about eSafety:
    • Visit eSafety’s homepage to understand their role, functions, and the protections available to you at: esafety.gov.au
  • Contact eSafety:
    • If you’ve experienced serious online harm and feel it hasn’t been adequately addressed, you can submit a complaint directly to eSafety. Find out how to contact them at: esafety.gov.au
  • Get support:
    • If you or someone you know needs counseling or support services after exposure to online harm, you can find a list of support services at: esafety.gov.au Australian users who believe Discord has not met its obligations under the Online Safety Act may submit a compliance complaint onlinesafetyau@discord.com.

To learn more about Australia’s Online Safety industry codes and what they require of platforms like Discord, visit esafety.gov.au.

Default Safety Settings for Australian Users

All Australian users have a default teen-appropriate experience with enhanced safety settings.This means updated communications settings, restricted access to age-gated spaces, and content filtering, nearly all of which require age assurance to modify or access, including:

  • Message Requests turned on by default, so messages from people you don’t know go to a separate inbox before reaching you

  • Sensitive content filters enabled by default

  • Age assurance is required to access age-gated content like age-restricted servers and channels. Users can complete age assurance to update these default safety settings or access age-gated content and features.

  • Want to learn more about how age assurance works? Read this article here: How to Complete Age Assurance on Discord

  • Want to learn more about what’s different for Australian users? Read this article here: Age Assurance for Australia

Additional Protections for Teens

Discord has additional default protections in place for teen users, including:

  • Direct messages from unknown users, including adults, are filtered by the Message Request feature and teen users cannot disable Message Requests (users must be confirmed adults via one of Discord’s methods of age assurance).

  • Safety alerts when interacting with unfamiliar accounts

  • Stricter content filters

  • Family Center, which lets parents and guardians stay connected to their teen’s Discord activity For a full overview of Discord’s safety features, visit the Discord Safety Center and check out our Help Center articles below:

  • Discord Safety Alerts

  • Family Center for Parents and Guardians

  • Family Center for Teens

Safety Tools You Can Use

Discord gives you control over who can contact you and what content you see. In addition to your default settings, you can actively manage your experience using these tools:

  • Stop any user from messaging you

  • Manage who can send you direct messages

  • Filter messages from people you don’t know

  • Set your preferences for sensitive content

  • Leave any group DM at any time Want to learn more? Read these articles below for more information:

  • Blocking & Privacy Settings

  • How to Ignore Users

  • Message Requests

  • Safer Messaging on Discord

  • Sensitive Content Filters

  • Group Chat and Calls

How to Report a User or Content on Discord

If you see content or behaviour that violates Discord’s Community Guidelines or Terms of Service, you can report it directly within the app.

Discord’s Trust & Safety team reviews reports and takes action where our policies have been violated.

If you are an Australian user seeking specific assistance with a suspected financial scam, you can report this to Discord by following the instructions in our Deceptive Practices Policy Explainer, and report the issue to your financial institution or local law enforcement.

Want to learn more?

To learn more about to report a user of content, please read this article for more information: How to Report Abusive Behavior to Discord

Scam/Phishing Bots

You all know and love our Safety Officer Jim. He’s here to give you another reminder, and this time it’s about scam/phishing bots.

If you receive a Direct Message from a bot offering you something, or asking you to click on a link, disregard it! We have never created a bot designed to offer you free products, so you can safely determine that this is a scam. Do not add these bots to your server in hopes of receiving something in return as they likely will compromise your server. If anything gets deleted, we have no way of restoring what was lost!

Whenever you’re curious about a bot, your best bet is to reach out to the developer. If you’re unsure of how to proceed, or your account gets compromised, you should reach out to our support team. Options to reach our support team are listed at the bottom of this page.

If a bot is contacting you to be added to your server, or asking you to click on a suspicious link, please report this to our Trust & Safety team so they can investigate it.

What is Decree No. 12,976/2026

Note: Individuals to whom Decree 12,976/2026 does not apply may submit reports of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) through our standard in-app reporting system. Our non-consensual intimate imagery policy applies globally in addition to other legal rights you may have where you live.

Decree No. 12,976/2026 is a Brazilian federal regulation issued under Brazil’s Marco Civil da Internet that sets out guidelines for protecting women online and addressing violence against women in digital environments. It requires covered platforms like Discord to:

  • provide a clear reporting channel;
  • review removal requests, including notifications about crimes or unlawful acts or coordinated harassment committed against women because of their gender;
  • remove non-consensual intimate content within a defined timeframe;
  • take reasonable steps to limit the spread of that content; and
  • block artificial intelligence (AI) tools from generating or altering intimate images of real people without their consent. Important: Need immediate help? If you have concerns about your personal safety, or the safety of someone you know, please contact local law enforcement or social services.

What this article covers:

  • Your Rights and Our Responsibilities Under Decree No. 12,976/2026
  • What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request Under Decree No. 12,976/2026

Your Rights and Our Responsibilities Under Decree No. 12,976/2026

If Decree No. 12,976/2026 applies to you, you or a representative acting on your behalf may:

  • Submit a request for Discord to remove the content that was shared without your consent. That includes images, video, audio, text, or any combination of these that depicts nudity, partial nudity, a sexual act, or a sexualized context, including content wholly or partly generated or manipulated by AI.
  • Learn more on how to report this content to Discord for removal via our dedicated reporting channel. If you’re outside Brazil, or you’re reporting images of someone else that you don’t have legal authority to represent, you can report content under our Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery policy via our standard reporting process using the in-app report menu.

Important: Please note that intimate imagery of a person under the age of 18 constitutes Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM). We report illegal child sexual abuse material and grooming to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC). Discord takes enforcement action against users who post such content.

Discord’s obligations as a covered provider under Decree 12,976/2026 include:

  • Maintain a permanent, free, and easily accessible space for receiving reports of non-consensual intimate content and other forms of gender-based violence, with confirmation of receipt and a way for the reporting party to track their case;
  • Display information about Brazil’s Women’s Assistance Center (Call 180) helpline;
  • Take swift action when Discord receives a valid report, making reasonable efforts to identify and remove known copies of the same visual depiction, and applying measures to help block re-uploads of the same content;
  • Take steps to reduce the reach and visibility of coordinated attacks or harassment against women.

What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request Under Decree No. 12,976/2026

We will confirm receipt of your report and review it to determine whether the reported content falls within the scope of the Decree.

  • We will promptly review your request to confirm that it meets the requirements of the Decree.
  • If your report concerns non-consensual intimate content, and the request is valid and complete, we will remove the reported content and we will make reasonable efforts to identify and remove known copies to prevent it from being re-uploaded.
  • If your report concerns another form of gender-based violence covered by the Decree, we will evaluate it and communicate our decision — including the reasoning — to you and, where relevant, to the user who posted the content. We will not share the information in your report with users who posted the content to Discord. They will only be notified that the content has been removed, not who reported it. If your submission is incomplete, we may be unable to process it until you provide the missing information.

What is the Take It Down Act (TIDA)

Note: Individuals to whom the Take It Down Act does not apply may submit reports of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) through our standard in-app reporting system. Our non-consensual intimate imagery policy applies globally in addition to other legal rights you may have where you live.

The Take It Down Act (TIDA) is a US law that allows certain individuals to request the removal of intimate images shared or created without their consent, sometimes referred to as “revenge porn” or “non-consensual pornography.” It requires covered platforms, like Discord, to provide a clear reporting process, review qualifying removal requests, remove covered content within a defined timeframe, and take reasonable steps to limit the spread of that content.

Important: Need immediate help? If you have concerns about your personal safety, or the safety of someone you know, please contact local law enforcement or social services.

What this article covers:

  • Your Rights and Our Responsibilities Under TIDA
  • What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request Under TIDA

Your Rights and Our Responsibilities Under TIDA

If you are authorized to make a request under TIDA, you, or a representative acting on your behalf, may:

  • Notify Discord of any “non-consensual intimate visual depiction” published on Discord that depicts you and was published without your consent; and,

  • Submit a request for Discord to remove the depiction. For more details about how to submit a removal request, you can refer to our help article. So that we can help you, please make sure that your TIDA removal request meets these requirements:

  • You are identifiable in the content or via the context in which it is displayed (for example, your face is visible or your name is mentioned);

  • The content shows you nude or engaged in sexual activity; and,

  • The content was published without your consent. Discord may also action content submitted for removal through this process even if it does not meet the criteria under the Take It Down Act such as for violation of our Community Guidelines, or where other laws may apply.

Under TIDA, Discord, as a covered platform, is required to:

  • Maintain a clear and accessible process that allows a depicted individual (or their authorized representative) to request the removal of non-consensual intimate visual depictions;
  • Review each removal request and determine whether it satisfies the requirements of the law;
  • Remove the reported content within the 48 hour time period required by law when a valid request is received; and,
  • Make reasonable efforts to identify and remove known copies of the same non-consensual intimate visual depiction.

What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request Under TIDA

We will promptly review your removal request to confirm that it meets the requirements of TIDA. If the request is complete and valid, we will remove the reported content within 48 hours. We will also make reasonable efforts to identify and remove known copies of the content.

If your submission is incomplete, we may be unable to process your request until sufficient information is provided.

What Protections Do You Get in the Teen Age Group?

If you have been determined to be in the teen age group (13-17), your account automatically receives certain protections. This article explains what those protections are, what they affect, and what can be changed.

We work to place users into the right age group automatically via our age estimation model, so if you’re a teen, these settings may already be in place without you having to do anything.

Note: If you’re an adult (18+) and these protections have been applied to your account incorrectly, you can confirm you’re an adult to access age-restricted content, spaces, and settings at User Settings > Account Status. Find more detailed instructions here.

What this article covers:

  • What Stays the Same for Teens
  • What are the Teen Safety Protections
    • Content: What You Can and Can’t See
    • Social: Who Can Reach You
    • Profile & Activity: What Others Can See
  • If We Haven’t Determined Your Age Group Yet
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What Stays the Same for Teens

The core Discord experience, messaging friends, joining voice calls, or servers that are not age-restricted, works the same. Users in the teen age group can still:

  • Message friends and server members you’re already connected with
  • Join and participate in servers that aren’t age-restricted
  • Make voice and video calls
  • Participate in gaming, communities, study servers, and everything Discord is built for

What are the Teen Safety Protections

Users in the teen age group have a slightly different experience across three areas: what content you can see and can’t see, who can reach you, and what others can see about you. Some of these can only be changed by confirming you’re an adult. Others can be adjusted at any time.

Note: Teen safety protections may vary slightly depending on where you live, as some regions have specific requirements under local regulation. For region-specific information, see our directory here.

Content: What You Can and Can’t See

Sensitive content that we flag is filtered automatically. Images and videos flagged by Discord’s content filters are blurred or blocked depending on where they appear:

  • Direct messages from friends: blurred
  • Direct messages from strangers: blocked
  • Server channel messages: blurred
Blurred image warning in a channel, showing “May contain sensitive content” with a blurred attachment

Viewing blurred content, or changing these settings to “Show,” requires confirming you’re an adult.

Sensitive Content Filters settings screen, showing direct messages and server channel media set to Blur or Block

Age-restricted servers and channels are not accessible. Servers and channels marked as age-restricted (18+) are not accessible. Accessing them requires confirming you’re an adult.

“Age-Restricted Server” pop-up blocking access, with Confirm Age and Go Back buttons

Age-restricted commands are off. App commands flagged as age-restricted are disabled. Enabling them requires confirming you’re an adult.

Messaging Permissions settings showing “Allow access to age-restricted commands from apps in DMs”

For iOS only: The setting “Allow access to age-restricted servers on iOS” is off. This is a separate, additional step adults must take on iOS to reach age-restricted servers described above. It does not apply to teen accounts, which remain blocked regardless of this setting, and it does not apply on Android. Turning it on requires confirming you’re an adult.

Content Filters settings showing “Allow access to age-restricted servers on iOS” off
Social: Who Can Reach You

Message requests are on. All direct messages from people you’re not friends with are sent to a separate message requests inbox, so you can review them before they appear in your main DM list. Turning this off requires confirming you’re an adult.

Direct Message Permissions settings showing Message Requests toggled on with a note that teen accounts can’t turn it off

DM spam filters are set to “filter all”. Spam filtering is applied to all incoming DMs. This can be adjusted at any time.

Friend request alerts are on. You will be alerted before accepting a friend request from an unfamiliar user. Unfamiliar users are those you do not have any mutual friends or shared small servers (< 200 members) with. These alerts can help you make more informed decisions about new connections. These alerts cannot be turned off at this time whether you’re in the adult or teen age group.

“Accept friend request?” alert for a message from an unfamiliar user
Profile & Activity: What Others Can See

Activity sharing is limited. Your activity will only be visible to your friends and members of any small servers (< 200 members) you join, not members of all shared servers. This can be adjusted at any time.

“Where I Share Activity” settings, with “Share in servers with 200 or fewer members” selected

Profile visibility is limited. Your full profile details will only be visible to your friends and members of any small servers (< 200 members) you join, not members of all shared servers. This can be adjusted at any time.

Profile Privacy settings, with “Friends & Small Servers Only” selected

Speaking in Stage channels is not available. Speaking in a Stage channel requires you to confirm you’re an adult, as it can broadcast your voice to large audiences.You can still listen to any Stage channel.

“Confirm you’re an adult to speak on stages” prompt shown from a voice channel

If We Haven’t Determined Your Age Group Yet

If your account hasn’t been placed into an age group yet, your age group status is unconfirmed.

Account Status screen showing an unconfirmed age group with a Confirm Age button

You’ll get the same protections as what’s stated above, except for your Profile Privacy and Activity Sharing settings:

  • Unconfirmed users: Profile Privacy and Activity Sharing is open to Friends & All Servers meaning your profile and activity is visible to friends and to members of any server you join, regardless of size. This can be updated at any time.
“Where I Share Activity” settings with “Share in all servers” (Top) & Profile Privacy settings with “Friends & All Servers” selected (Bottom)

If you are unconfirmed, it doesn’t affect core Discord features like messaging friends, joining voice calls, or servers that aren’t age-restricted.

If you’re an adult and want to access age restricted content, spaces, or settings, you can confirm your age group at User Settings > Account Status. See more information here.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: I’m an adult and I’ve been placed in the teen age group. What do I do?

A: Head to User Settings > Account Status, pick whichever method you’re most comfortable with, and you can confirm your age group, usually in a few minutes. Find more detailed instructions here.

Q: My account hasn’t been placed into an age group yet. What does that mean?

A: It means our age estimation model doesn’t have enough signals yet to determine your age group. Additional protections apply in the meantime. Otherwise, the core Discord experience, messaging friends, joining voice calls, or servers that are not age-restricted, works the same.

If you’re an adult and want access to age-restricted content, spaces, or settings, you can confirm you’re an adult at User Settings > Account Status. Find more detailed instructions here.

Q: Why do these protections apply to my account?

A: You’ve been determined to be in the teen age group. If you’re an adult and think we got it wrong, you can confirm your age group. Find more detailed instructions here.

Q: Can I turn these protections off?

A: Some settings can only be changed after confirming you’re an adult. Others, like activity sharing and profile visibility, can be adjusted at any time. See the sections above for details on which protections can be turned off.

Q: Can other people see that I’m in the teen age group?

A: Your age group isn’t shown on your profile or visible to other members in a server.

Q: Do these protections apply in the UK, Australia, and Brazil?

A: Teen safety protections may vary slightly depending on where you live, as some regions have specific requirements under local regulation. For region-specific information, see our directory here.

Q: Will these protections change over time?

A: We continue to adjust our approach as regulations evolve. We’ll communicate any changes that affect your experience.

Q: I’m a parent, can I manage my teen’s settings?

A: Teen safety protections are applied when we believe a user is a teen and most can’t be changed by anyone other than your teen confirming they’re an adult. A few settings, like Sensitive Content Filters and Message Requests, can be managed by you if you’re connected through Family Center, though you’ll need to be in the adult age group yourself to update Message Requests. For the full list of what you can manage and how to connect, read our help center article on Family Center.

Why video features are currently unavailable in Brazil

Last updated: August 17, 2026

If you’re in Brazil, Discord’s Go Live and real-time video chat are currently disabled. This is due to a government order, not a bug on our end.

What this article covers:

  • What’s affected
  • Why this happened
  • When will video features become available

What’s affected

Brazil’s National Data Protection Authority (ANPD) ordered Discord to suspend Go Live and video chat features for users in Brazil starting August 17, 2026. That covers all real-time video communication functionality on Discord, including in direct messages (DMs), group direct messages (GDMs), voice channels, and Stage channels.

Real-time voice communication and messaging is not impacted by this order. You can still talk, chat, and hang out with your friends and communities as usual, you just can’t video chat, share your screen, or watch your friend’s Go Live streams for now.

Why this happened

ANPD issued the Order in connection with an investigation related to Brazil’s Digital Statute for Children and Adolescents (“Digital ECA”). The Order requires the suspension “of the ‘Go Live’ feature and of any other functionally equivalent video-transmission and video-sharing features.” Discord disagrees with ANPD’s decision but is committed to cooperating with Brazilian authorities in the implementation of the Digital ECA.

When will video features become available

Unfortunately, we don’t have a specific date for you when these features will become available again. We are actively engaged with the ANPD and are seeking a resolution that would restore these video features for our users in Brazil. We’ll keep this page updated as we learn more.

If you, your friends, or servers you’re in rely on Go Live or real-time video chat, you can let them know why those features are unavailable and point them to this page.

How Discord Confirms Your Age Group in Texas

Texas’s App Store Accountability Act requires apps like Discord to use age signals shared from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store to confirm your age group. In compliance with this law, Discord will receive your age range associated with your device’s app store.

What this article covers:

  • How the App Store Age Check Works in Texas
  • What Happens If the Age Check Doesn’t Return a Result
  • Parental Controls and Account Access
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How the App Store Age Check Works in Texas

For Texas users, Discord receives the age range associated with your device’s app store automatically when you open the app. This is different from how age assurance on Discord works in most other regions, where you’re only prompted to confirm your age if you try to access age-restricted content, spaces, or settings.

Here’s how the app store age range check works:

  • Discord checks the account settings for your device’s app store account (such as your Apple or Google account) for an existing age range. You can refer to Apple or Google’s help pages for details on how to ensure your age is accurately reflected in your account.

  • If your app store account shows that you are 18 or older: you are placed in the adult age group and can access age-restricted content, spaces, and settings on Discord.

  • If your app store account shows that you are between 13 and 17: you will be placed into the teen age group, and will not be able to access age-restricted content and spaces, or change certain settings (for example, you cannot disable Sensitive Content Filters). Messaging friends, joining voice calls, and accessing non age-restricted channels and servers all continue to work as normal. If your app store age range incorrectly shows that you’re a teen, you can refer to Apple or Google’s help pages for details on how to update the age that is associated with your account. You can also confirm your age through a different method, see How to Confirm Your Age Group on Discord for instructions.

  • If your app store account shows that you are under 13: your account will be disabled because you must be at least 13 years old to use Discord.

What Happens If the Age Check Doesn’t Return a Result

If the check via the app store doesn’t return a result, you can continue using Discord as usual. You just won’t be able to access age-restricted content, spaces, or settings until you confirm you’re an adult, whether it’s through having your app store age range shared in the future, or through one of our other age assurance methods.

Parental Controls and Account Access

Texas law also gives parents and guardians control over whether their teen can use apps like Discord at all, separate from the age assurance process.

If your parent or guardian removes your permission to use Discord through your device’s app store parental controls, your account will be blocked from accessing Discord until your parent or guardian restores permission. There is no appeal process through Discord for this type of block, and access is restored only when your parent or guardian reverses the change in your device’s parental controls. If your account is blocked in this way; your servers, friends list, and message history will stay intact and will be restored if access is reinstated within our standard retention window of 2 years. Beyond that, your account will be subject to deletion like any other inactive Discord account.

Note: If you’re a parent or guardian, here’s how to restore access on Apple devices.

If you previously removed permissions for your teen to use Discord and want to allow it again:

  1. Your teen will need to initiate an exception request. When trying to open an app with an age rating higher than the app age-rating restriction that you set for them, your teen will see a message that says content restrictions are enabled and can ask for an exception.

  2. If they ask for an exception, you’ll receive a message in Apple’s Messages app. You can approve or decline the request right from the message notification or in the Messages app.

  3. On your device: When you tap Review the request, the app’s page opens. You can approve or decline the exception, or view the app’s Age Rating Details.

  4. Discord will detect the restored permission and lift the account block automatically. No Discord support ticket or appeal is needed.

For more on how these age and consent rules work on Apple devices in Texas, see Apple’s Age requirements for managing an Apple Account in Texas page.

Note: If you’re a parent or guardian, here’s how to restore access on Android devices

If you previously removed permissions for your teen to use Discord and want to allow it again:

  1. Open the Family Link app

  2. Select your teen

  3. Tap Screen time > Time limits > App limits

  4. Select the Discord app

  5. Tap App details > Permissions

  6. Switch the permission on

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Do these changes apply to all Discord users in Texas?

A: Yes, the automatic app store age range check applies to all new and existing Discord accounts in Texas when using Discord on their iOS or Android devices.

Q: Why is my age range shared automatically, when users elsewhere are only asked to confirm their age when they try to access something age-restricted?

A: Texas’s App Store Accountability Act requires app stores to share age signals automatically with developers like Discord, rather than checking when someone tries to access age-restricted content. That’s why Texas users will have their age ranges shared automatically when opening Discord on an iOS or Android device.

Q: What information does Discord receive from the app store check?

A: Discord only receives your age range (for example, whether you’re 18 or older), not your name, Apple or Google ID, birthdate, or any other account information.

Q: What if I don’t want to share my age from the app store?

A: Texas’s App Store Accountability Act requires app stores to share age signals with developers like Discord for users in Texas, when opening Discord on an iOS or Android device. More details can be found in the Apple and Google help pages.

Q: What happens if my app store account says I’m under 18 but I’m actually an adult?

A: If your app store age range is incorrect, you can refer to Apple or Google’s help pages for details on how to update the age that is associated with your account. You can also confirm your age through a different method, the same way any user can if they are initially placed in the wrong age group. See How to Confirm Your Age Group on Discord for instructions.

Q: If my age is shared through the app store once, will I need to confirm it again?

A: In most cases, no. However, if the age range from your app store account later changes (for example, if a parent or guardian updates or removes it), you may need to reconfirm your age.

Q: Can a parent or guardian control my access to Discord separately from age assurance?

A: Yes, if a parent or guardian removes permission for you to use Discord through their app store parental controls you will be blocked from accessing Discord until they restore that permission. See Parental Controls and Account Access above.

Q: Can I appeal if I believe my account was incorrectly restricted?

A: If your app store age range that was shared is incorrect, you can refer to Apple or Google’s help pages for details on how to update the age that is associated with your account, or retry confirming your age. If your account was blocked because a parent or guardian removed app permissions (see Parental Controls and Account Access), those are separate permissions that can only be changed by your parent or guardian, not by retrying to confirm your age.

Q: If my Discord account was blocked via app store parental controls by my parent or guardian, can I unblock it once I turn 18?

A: Yes, assuming you turn 18 within our standard 2 year retention period for inactive accounts, you can end parental controls on your app store account. After, when you launch the Discord app your account will automatically unlock.

How Do I Disable My Account?

If you ever want to take a break away from Discord, instead of permanently deleting your account, you can disable the account until you’re ready to come back.

What this article covers:

  • What is the difference between disabling and deleting your account?
  • How do I disable my account?
    • Desktop/Browser
    • iOS
    • Android
  • How do I restore my account?
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile Note: If you have an active Discord subscription, disabling your account will not cancel your subscription. You will continue to be charged, unless you cancel your subscription. If you need assistance with canceling your Discord subscription, please check out one of the following Help Center articles:
  • How to Cancel your Nitro Subscription
  • How to Cancel your Server Boost Subscription
  • How to Cancel your Server Subscription
  • How to Cancel your Premium App Subscription

What is the difference between disabling and deleting your account?

  • Disabling your account means your account is put on hold. You can reactivate it by logging in and following the prompts.
  • When you disable an account you will no longer receive any @notifications through the email address associated to your Discord account. However, you can still get friend requests. Any friend requests that you receive while your account is disabled will be waiting for you when you re-enable your account.
  • However, if you choose to delete your account, the account will be scheduled to be permanently deleted. Once an account is deleted, it is irreversible! Note: Keep in mind that disabled accounts that are inactive for 2 years or more may be deleted, so if you want to keep yours, you’ll need to reactivate your disabled account (but you can disable it again after this if you like). You can learn more about inactive account deletions here.

What is a Disabled Account?

What is a Deleted Account?

  • Account is on-hold for when you return
  • Temporary
  • Will not receive @notifications, but friend requests will be stored for when you come back
  • Account is deleted
  • Permanent
  • Will not receive @notifications and friend requests
  • Once deleted, your account cannot be restored.

How do I disable my account?

Desktop/Browser:

  1. If you’d like to disable your account via desktop, head over to your User Settings by pressing the cog wheel next to your username.

  2. You will be taken to the My Account tab.

  3. Select Disable Account (under Account Removal).

Once you have selected the Disable Account button, please follow the prompts to complete the process.

Note: Before you are able to disable your account, you will have to transfer ownership of all servers that you own.

iOS:

  1. If you’d like to disable your account via iOS, navigate to your User Settings by swiping right on your iOS device and pressing your user avatar in the bottom right corner. Then select Account.

  2. Once you are in the Account tab, press on Disable Account and follow the prompts to complete the process.

Android:

  1. Similarly, if you’d like to disable your account via Android, navigate to your User Settings by swiping right on your Android device and pressing your user avatar in the bottom right corner. Select Account.

  2. Then, select Disable Account to initiate the prompts to follow.

How do I restore my account?

If you want to come back to Discord, you can login using the email address and previous password associated with your account.

Afterwards, a prompt will appear to let you know that you cannot use the account while it’s disabled. All you have to do is select Restore Account and your account will become active again!

Desktop/Browser:
Mobile:

Disabling your account will let you come back to Discord whenever you’d like. Whenever you’d like to come back to Discord, your servers, friends, and more will be there waiting for you.

How Teens Experience Discord in Australia

Although Discord has not been classified as an Age-Restricted Social Media Platform under Australia’s Social Media Minimum Age Act, we introduced enhanced safety features for our Australian users starting December 9th, 2025.

Note: These defaults include automatic content filtering to reduce the likelihood that teens encounter certain types of potentially harmful content, as well as different social settings. Australian users who wish to access content flagged by our filters or customize those settings can do so only after confirming that they are 18 or older through our privacy-forward age assurance experience.

To check out additional Safety Resources for Australian Users go here.

What this article covers:

  • What Stays the Same
  • What Are the Additional Safety Protections
    • Content: What You Can and Can’t See
    • Social: Who Can Reach You
    • Profile & Activity: What Others Can See
  • Frequently Asked Questions A set of safety protections apply automatically for all users until they confirm they’re an adult. This article explains what those protections are, what they affect, and what can be changed.

In Australia, we don’t use the age estimation model to automatically determine a users’ age group, so you’ll be asked to confirm your age group if you want access to age-restricted content, spaces or settings. You can use our age assurance options to confirm your age group directly at User Settings > Account Status. Find more detailed instructions here.

Note: If you’re an adult (18+), you can confirm you’re an adult to access age-restricted content, spaces, and settings at User Settings > Account Status. Find more detailed instructions here.

What Stays the Same

The core Discord experience, messaging friends, joining voice calls or servers that are not age-restricted, works the same. Users with these additional safety protections applied can still:

  • Message friends and server members you’re already connected with
  • Join and participate in servers that aren’t age-restricted
  • Make voice and video calls
  • Participate in gaming, communities, study servers, and everything Discord is built for

What are the Additional Safety Protections

Users in the teen age group have a slightly different experience across three areas: what content you can see and can’t see, who can reach you, and what others can see about you. Some of these can only be changed by confirming you’re an adult. Others can be adjusted at any time.

Note: Teen safety protections may vary slightly depending on where you live, as some regions have specific requirements under local regulation. For region-specific information, see our directory here.

Content: What You Can and Can’t See

Sensitive content that we flag is filtered automatically. Images and videos flagged by Discord’s content filters are blurred or blocked depending on where they appear:

  • Direct messages from friends: blurred
  • Direct messages from strangers: blocked
  • Server channel messages: blurred
Sensitive Content Filters settings screen, showing Direct Messages and server channel media set to Blur or Block

Viewing blurred content, or changing these settings to “Show,” requires confirming you’re an adult.

Age-restricted servers and channels are not accessible. Servers and channels marked as age-restricted (18+) are not accessible. Accessing them requires confirming you’re an adult.

Age-restricted commands are off. App commands flagged as age-restricted are disabled. Enabling them requires confirming you’re an adult.

For iOS only: The setting “Allow access to age-restricted servers on iOS” is off. This is a separate, additional step adults must take on iOS to reach age-restricted servers described above. It does not apply to teen accounts, which remain blocked regardless of this setting, and it does not apply on Android. Turning it on requires confirming you’re an adult.

Content Filters settings, showing “Allow access to age-restricted commands from apps in DMs” and “Allow access to age-restricted servers on iOS” toggles, both off
Social: Who Can Reach You

Message requests are on. All direct messages from people you’re not friends with are sent to a separate message requests inbox, so you can review them before they appear in your main DM list. Turning this off requires confirming you’re an adult.

DM spam filters are set to “filter all”. Spam filtering is applied to all incoming DMs. This can be adjusted at any time.

Friend request alerts are on. You will be alerted before accepting a friend request from an unfamiliar user. Unfamiliar users are those you do not have any mutual friends or shared small servers (< 200 members) with. These alerts can help you make more informed decisions about new connections. These alerts cannot be turned off at this time whether you’re in the adult or teen age group.

Profile & Activity: What Others Can See

Activity sharing is limited. Your activity will only be visible to your friends, not members of shared servers. This can be adjusted at any time.

Profile visibility is limited. Your full profile details will only be visible to your friends, not shared servers. This can be adjusted at any time.

Speaking in Stage channels is not available. Speaking in a Stage channel requires you to confirm you’re an adult, as it can broadcast your voice to large audiences.You can still listen to any Stage channel.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: I’m an adult and I’ve been placed in the teen age group. What do I do?

A: Head to User Settings > Account Status, pick whichever method you’re most comfortable with, and you can confirm your age group, usually in a few minutes. Find more detailed instructions here.

Q: Can I turn these protections off?

A: Some settings can only be changed after confirming you’re an adult. Others, like activity sharing and profile visibility, can be adjusted at any time. See the sections above for details on which protections can be turned off.

Q: Can other people see what age group I’m in?

A: Your age group isn’t shown on your profile or visible to other members in a server.

Q: Do these protections apply everywhere globally?

A: Teen safety protections may vary slightly depending on where you live, as some regions have specific requirements under local regulation. For region-specific information, see our directory here.

Q: Will these protections change over time?

A: We continue to adjust our approach as regulations evolve. We’ll communicate any changes that affect your experience.

Q: I’m a parent, can I manage my teen’s settings?

A: Teen safety protections are applied when we believe a user is a teen and most can’t be changed by anyone other than your teen confirming they’re an adult. A few settings, like Sensitive Content Filters and Message Requests, can be managed by you if you’re connected through Family Center, though you’ll need to be in the adult age group yourself to update Message Requests. For the full list of what you can manage and how to connect, read our help center article on Family Center.

How Teens Experience Discord in Brazil

Starting March 9th, 2026, we’re rolling out age assurance in Brazil to comply with the Digital Statute for Children and Adolescents (Digital ECA), which takes effect on March 17th. This is part of a government regulation that applies to a wide range of digital services operating in Brazil.

These changes bring updated default safety settings, age-gated access to certain content and spaces, and a privacy-forward age assurance experience, using k-ID, for adults who want to access age-restricted content or change certain default settings. Users who don’t want to access age-restricted content won’t need to confirm their age group at all.

Our goal remains the same: apply the right protections for the right age groups while preserving the genuine community experience that makes Discord special. We will continue to update the Discord experience in Brazil to align with the Digital ECA and will tell you about those changes as we make them.

If We Haven’t Determined Your Age Group Yet

If your account hasn’t been placed into an age group yet, your age group status is unconfirmed.

Account Status screen showing an unconfirmed age group with a Confirm Age button

You’ll get the same protections as the teen experience, except for your Profile Privacy and Activity Sharing settings:

  • Teens users: Profile Privacy and Activity Sharing starts at Friends & Small Servers meaning their profile and activity is only visible to friends and members of any server they’re in with 200 or fewer members. This can be updated at any time.
  • Unconfirmed users: Profile Privacy and Activity Sharing is open to Friends & All Servers meaning your profile and activity is visible to friends and to members of any server you join, regardless of size. This can be updated at any time.
“Where I Share Activity” settings, with “Share in servers with 200 or fewer members” selected

Having an unconfirmed age group doesn’t affect core Discord features like messaging friends, joining voice calls, or servers that aren’t age restricted.

If you’re an adult and want to access age restricted content, spaces, or settings, you can confirm your age group at User Settings > Account Status. See more information here.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: I’m an adult and I’ve been placed in the teen age group. What do I do?

Q: My account hasn’t been placed into an age group yet. What does that mean?

A: It means our age estimation model doesn’t have enough signals yet to determine your age group. Additional protections apply in the meantime. Otherwise, the core Discord experience, messaging friends, joining voice calls or servers that are not age-restricted, works the same.

If you’re an adult and want access to age-restricted content, spaces, or settings, you can confirm you’re an adult at User Settings > Account Status. Find more detailed instructions here.

A: You’ve been determined to be in the teen age group. If you’re an adult and think we got it wrong, you can confirm your age group. Find more detailed instructions here.

Q: Can I turn these protections off?

A: Some settings can only be changed after confirming you’re an adult. Others, like activity sharing and profile visibility, can be adjusted at any time. See the sections above for details on which protections can be turned off.

Q: Can other people see that I’m in the teen age group?

A: Your age group isn’t shown on your profile or visible to other members in a server.

How Teens Experience Discord in the UK

The United Kingdom’s Online Safety Act (“OSA”) introduces responsibilities for online platforms to reduce safety risks and provide age-appropriate experiences for users, especially teens. In compliance with these regulations, all UK users will be assigned updated default settings.

These defaults include automatic content filtering to reduce the likelihood that teens encounter certain types of potentially harmful content, as well as different social settings. UK users who wish to access content flagged by our filters or customize those settings can do so only after confirming that they are 18 or older through our privacy-forward age assurance experience.
