Unfamiliar users are those you do not have any mutual friends or shared small servers (< 200 members) with. These alerts can help you make more informed decisions about new connections. These alerts cannot be turned off at this time whether you’re in the adult or teen age group.

Profile & Activity: What Others Can See

Activity sharing is limited. Your activity will only be visible to your friends, not members of shared servers. This can be adjusted at any time.

Profile visibility is limited. Your full profile details will only be visible to your friends, not shared servers. This can be adjusted at any time.

Speaking in Stage channels is not available. Speaking in a Stage channel requires you to confirm you’re an adult, as it can broadcast your voice to large audiences.You can still listen to any Stage channel.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: I’m an adult and I’ve been placed in the teen age group. What do I do?

A: Head to User Settings > Account Status, pick whichever method you’re most comfortable with, and you can confirm your age group, usually in a few minutes. Find more detailed instructions here.

Q: Can I turn these protections off?

A: Some settings can only be changed after confirming you’re an adult. Others, like activity sharing and profile visibility, can be adjusted at any time. See the sections above for details on which protections can be turned off.

Q: Can other people see what age group I’m in?

A: Your age group isn’t shown on your profile or visible to other members in a server.

Q: Do these protections apply everywhere globally?

A: Teen safety protections may vary slightly depending on where you live, as some regions have specific requirements under local regulation. For region-specific information, see our directory here.

Q: Will these protections change over time?

A: We continue to adjust our approach as regulations evolve. We’ll communicate any changes that affect your experience.

Q: I’m a parent, can I manage my teen’s settings?

A: Teen safety protections are applied when we believe a user is a teen and most can’t be changed by anyone other than your teen confirming they’re an adult. A few settings, like Sensitive Content Filters and Message Requests, can be managed by you if you’re connected through Family Center, though you’ll need to be in the adult age group yourself to update Message Requests. For the full list of what you can manage and how to connect, read our help center article on Family Center.

How to Confirm Your Age Group on Discord

Resolved as of Sep 23, 8:32PM PST

  • Some of you may have saw mismatched experiences across devices - for example, appearing as “unconfirmed” on an older app version, or being unable to access age-restricted servers on certain mobile devices. We had identified a bug causing this issue.

  • This issue has now been resolved! Please close and refresh your app to get the fix for the age group status.

  • For more details, check out: discordstatus.com

Helping to keep teens safer on Discord means making sure the right protections apply to the right accounts. When Discord knows your account belongs to a teen (13-17), we apply additional safety protections automatically, things like filtering sensitive content and restricting access to age-restricted spaces. You can read more about what those protections cover here.

For most users, our age estimation model determines your age group automatically and you would not need to confirm your age group. If you do want to confirm your age group, it’s likely for one of these reasons:

  • We don’t have enough information to place your account in an age group yet and you want access to age-restricted content, spaces, or settings now. Additional safety protections apply in the meantime, while core features like messaging friends, joining voice calls or servers that are not age-restricted stay the same.

  • Your account was placed in the wrong age group. Age estimation works by looking at patterns, so a small percent of accounts will land in the wrong group. You can fix this in a few minutes without needing to contact support. What this article covers:

  • Before You Start

  • Step 1: Go to User Settings > Account Status

  • Step 2: Choose a Method to Confirm Your Age Group

    • Apple App Store
    • Google Play Store
    • Credit Card
    • Google Wallet
    • Video Selfie
    • ID Scan
    • AgeKey

  • Step 3: Finish Confirming Your Age Group

  • If Your Age Group Is Still Incorrect

  • Frequently Asked Questions

Before You Start

A few things worth knowing:

  • Discord does not directly handle your documents or images. To preserve your privacy, Discord doesn’t receive or access any images, ID documents, credit card details, or other info you might provide when you go through an age assurance process. We partner with age assurance vendors who handle this process and only pass back an age signal. We just need to know whether you’re an adult. It works both ways: A vendor has no way to associate any of your information back to your Discord account. You can review the vendors we partner with and the privacy standards we have in place here.
  • Facial age estimation happens on your device. Processing happens entirely on your device and your selfie is not shared with Discord or our vendors.
  • Documents are deleted. Any images or ID documents during age assurance are permanently deleted as soon as your age group is confirmed. They are never stored or linked to your account.
  • Your age group is saved to your Account Status. Once we’ve determined your age group, it’ll be saved and you can check it at User Settings > Account Status. Your age group isn’t shown on your profile or visible to other members in a server.
  • We will never ask you to confirm your age group by email or text. Age assurance only happens inside the Discord app. If you receive a message outside of Discord, do not select any links. It is not from Discord. Note: Because of laws in certain locations, you may be asked to share your age range automatically using Apple App Store or Google Play Store when you open Discord, rather than only when you try to access age-restricted content, spaces, or settings. For more information, you can check our directory for region-specific help articles.

Note: If using the mobile app, please make sure to check that you’re on version 343.0 or later to see your age group status in settings.

Step 1: Go to User Settings > Account Status

Open Discord and go to User Settings > Account Status. You’ll see your current age group status and a Confirm Age button or hyperlink. Tap it to begin.

You can also start from a prompt if you tried to access age-restricted content, spaces, or settings and were asked to confirm your age, just tap Confirm Age in that prompt.

Account Status page showing an unconfirmed age group with a Confirm Age button

Note: You may also see Step 2 if you attempt to access age-restricted content, space, or setting.

Step 2: Choose a Method to Confirm Your Age Group

“Confirm your age group” screen listing method options: Credit Card, Video Selfie, and ID Scan

Note: You can review the vendors we partner with and the privacy standards we have in place here.

Our goal is to give you as much choice as possible when confirming your age group. What’s actually available to you depends on factors such as your region or device, so the options below may not be the same for everyone.

Apple App Store

Allow Apple App Store to share your age range with Discord to determine whether you’re in the adult or teen age group. Your exact birthdate isn’t shared.

  1. Select Apple Age Range on the Confirm Your Age Group screen.

  2. Select Share Age Range on the Discord Would Like To Know Your Age Range page.

  3. Tap Continue to complete age assurance.

iOS system prompt: “Discord Would Like to Know Your Age Range,” with Share Age Range option

You can review the vendors we partner with and the privacy standards we have in place here.

Google Play Store

Allow Google Play Store to share your age range with Discord to determine whether you’re in the adult or teen age group. Your exact birthdate isn’t shared.

  1. Select Google Age Range on the Confirm Your Age Group screen.

  2. Follow the prompts to share your age range from your Google Play account.

  3. Tap Continue to complete age assurance.

You can review the vendors we partner with and the privacy standards we have in place here.

Credit Card

k-ID determines you’re in the adult age group by checking ownership of a credit card. Your card details are processed through k-ID who uses Stripe’s secure payment infrastructure. Discord only receives your age group or a note that the result was inconclusive. We never see your card details.

A small temporary charge (under $0.50 USD) may be placed to confirm your card is valid and will be fully refunded within 14 business days. Stripe retains limited financial records, as required by financial regulations, but this information isn’t shared with Discord.

“Enter card details” screen with card number and Submit button

Note: Only credit cards are accepted for this method. Debit cards and prepaid cards aren’t eligible, since they can be issued to minors in most regions.

  1. Select Credit Card on the Confirm Your Age Group screen.

  2. Enter your credit card details.

  3. Tap Submit.

You can review the vendors we partner with and the privacy standards we have in place here.

Google Wallet

Use a passport stored in Google Wallet to confirm your age group. Only your age group result and issuing country are shared. Your passport details stay private and never leave Google Wallet.

Note: Google Wallet currently only supports passports from Brazil, Singapore, Taiwan, UK, and US.

Google Wallet “Share info” screen requesting to share ID pass age and issuing country with Discord

  1. Select Google Wallet on the Confirm Your Age Group screen.

  2. If you already have a passport uploaded to your Google Wallet, tap Continue when prompted to share your age.

Need help setting up your passport in Google Wallet? Visit Google’s support page.

You can review the vendors we partner with and the privacy standards we have in place here.

Video Selfie

A short video clip or selfie image is taken and then facial analysis is used to estimate your age. This all happens entirely on your device.

Discord and k-ID never see or store it, no data is shared, and nothing ever leaves your device.

“Prepare for Face Scan” screen with camera setup instructions and a QR code for continuing on mobile

  1. Select Video Selfie on the Confirm Your Age Group screen.

  2. Allow camera access when prompted.

  3. Follow the on-screen instructions to record your clip.

  4. Tap Done to submit.

You can review the vendors we partner with and the privacy standards we have in place here.

ID Scan

Upload a photo of a government-issued ID, which is scanned by k-ID along with a selfie to confirm it’s yours. Your ID and selfie are deleted immediately after your age is confirmed and will never be linked to your Discord account. Discord only ever receives your age.

“ID Document Verification” screen with instructions before scanning an ID, and a Get Started button

  1. Select ID Scan on the Confirm Your Age Group screen.

  2. Use your mobile device to scan the QR code if prompted.

  3. Take a clear photo of your government-issued ID.

  4. Take a selfie to match your ID.

  5. Tap Done to submit.

You can review the vendors we partner with and the privacy standards we have in place here.

AgeKey

A reusable age passkey you set up once through k-ID with either a video selfie, ID scan, or credit card. Once created, you can use it across services without confirming your age group again each time. If you already have an AgeKey with another company, you can re-use it here without needing to create another one.

“Prove your age once. Never again.” AgeKey creation screen with a Create my AgeKey button

  1. Select AgeKey on the Confirm Your Age Group screen.

  2. If you already have an AgeKey, confirm to share your age group with Discord.

  3. If you don’t have one yet, you can continue the flow to create one.

  4. Tap Done to submit.

You can review the vendors we partner with and the privacy standards we have in place here.

Step 3: Finish Confirming Your Age Group

After completing a method, you’ll receive a DM from Discord’s official profile with your age group result. You can also check your age group status anytime in User Settings > Account Status.

DM from Discord’s official account confirming the account is in the adult age group (18+)

In some cases, Discord may ask you to complete a second method if more confidence is needed. If we can’t determine your age group, you can retry through another method.

The methods you see might be different based on previous attempts, and there may be a limit on how many times you can retry a given method. If you don’t see a method right now, it may become available again later.

If Your Age Group is Still Incorrect

If you’ve finished confirming your age but believe your age group is still wrong, go to User Settings > Account Status and tap Retry to confirm your age with a different method.

We require all users to meet the minimum age requirement for their region. If your account was banned after being incorrectly determined as under the minimum age required in your region to use Discord, you can appeal by following the instructions here.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Will I need to confirm my age group to keep using Discord?

A: No. You don’t need to confirm your age group just to access Discord. The vast majority of users are placed into an age group automatically by Discord’s age estimation model and don’t need to do a thing. You will only need to confirm you’re an adult if you want to access age-restricted content, spaces, or settings and have not been placed into the adult age group yet. This doesn’t affect core Discord features like messaging friends, joining voice calls, or servers that are not age-restricted.

Q: Is my personal data stored during the age assurance process?

A: Discord only ever receives your age signal. Not your name, not your ID, not your selfie. We work with vendors that handle the age checks on their end to preserve your privacy because the goal is only to establish your age group, not your identity. Once the age check is complete, the underlying data is deleted, and Discord gets an age signal to place you into your age group (teen or adult). Your age group isn’t shown on your profile or visible to other members in a server.

Q: When would I be asked to confirm my age group?

A: In most cases, this should only happen if you try to access age-restricted content, spaces, or settings and are not in the adult age group. There may also be times where you need to try another method if we need more confidence.

Q: How many times will I need to do this?

A: Usually once. After your age group is confirmed, it’s saved to your account and you typically won’t be asked again. In some cases, for example where we need more confidence, you may be asked to try another method.

Q: Which age assurance method should I use?

A: You can choose whichever you’re most comfortable with. All age assurance methods and vendors are described here. We evaluate methods and providers for data security, and we don’t use your data for anything beyond confirming your age group.

Q: Does this affect my account if I switch devices?

A: Your age group is saved to your account once it’s confirmed, so it stays the same across devices. If you haven’t yet confirmed your age group, the methods available to you may change depending on your device or the region where you’re accessing Discord. Legal obligations in some regions may impact what methods you can use or if you need to confirm your age group through a different age assurance option.

Q: Can other users see my age group?

A: Your age group isn’t shown on your profile or visible to other members in a server.

Q: I got an email or text asking me to confirm my age. Is that from Discord?

A: No. Discord will never ask you to confirm your age by email or text. Age assurance only happens inside the app. If you received a message like this, do not select any links, it is not from Discord.

Q: My account was banned after I confirmed my age. What should I do?

A: If your account was incorrectly banned for being under the minimum age required to use Discord, you can appeal and correct your age using the instructions here.

Q: Why do I see different method options when I try to confirm my age?

A: Methods vary depending on factors such as your region or device. The methods you see might also be different based on previous attempts. If you don’t see a method right now, it may become available again later.

Q: Are age signals received from age assurance used for advertising?

A: The age signals we receive through age assurance can only be used for safety purposes. Those signals are used to ensure users in the teen age group don’t see ads meant for adults, and are not used to target ads.

Separately, advertisers on Discord can choose to reach people within broad age ranges that are based on signals (such as self-declared age) that are different and separate from the age signals that are collected through our age assurance process.

How to Fix Phone Errors on Discord

What this article covers:

  • Phone is Already Registered
  • Invalid Phone Number
  • Other Phone Errors There are some error messages that you might notice when trying to register with, add, or change the phone number on your account. Let’s go over those cases and what to do if you’re experiencing those specific errors.

Before you begin the process of adding a phone number, please make sure you have access to that number and your mobile device.

Phone is Already Registered

A phone can only be registered with one Discord account at a time. If you are encountering an error that states This phone number is unable to be associated with this account, this is because the phone number is already tied to another account. As you can only have one number per account, you would need to remove the number from the other account Discord in order to use it.

Note: If you’re unable to remove the phone number yourself, please check out the How to Remove a Phone Number Help Center article for steps.

Invalid Phone Number

Make sure that the phone number you are entering is properly formatted and is valid according to your country’s numbering plan.

Also, make sure the phone number is not associated with a landline or VOIP device, and that the number you are trying to use is associated with a mobile device.

Other Errors

If you’re running into any other error messages, or you’re receiving one of the errors above and it’s still not working, please reach out to our Support team for further assistance: dis.gd

How to Recover Your Discord Account When Locked Out of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

Being locked out of your Discord account due to Multi-Factor Authentication can be frustrating, but with the right approach and Discord’s recovery options, you can regain access to your account.

Important: If you do not have access to your backup codes, Discord is unable to remove MFA or issue you new backup codes.

What this article covers:

  • Disabling MFA if You’re not Logged Into Your Discord Account
  • How to Receive a SMS Authentication Code
  • Disabling MFA if You’re Logged Into Your Discord Account Tip: If you signed up for MFA through the Google Authenticator App via your iOS or Android device, please follow their guide here.

If you aren’t logged into your account on any other clients (desktop, mobile, or browser app), the first thing you want to do is see if you have your Discord backup codes saved anywhere. These could be saved as a txt file called “discord_backup_codes.txt” or a screenshot in your photo gallery of the codes.

After locating your backup codes, you can use one of the unused codes to log into your account.

  1. After logging in you’ll see the prompt to enter authenticator code. To enter a backup code instead, press on Verify with something else.

Verify with something else option

  1. Select Use a backup code.

Important: If the option to use a backup code is not available, this means all of your backup codes have been used. To regain access to your account, please try one of the other verification methods listed on this page. Our support team is unable to generate new backup codes on your behalf.

Use a backup code selection

  1. Enter the 8-digit code and then press on Confirm.

Enter your backup code

  1. After logging in, you can then move MFA from your account so you can add it back later. Tap on User Settings by selecting the cogwheel button [] in the bottom-left.

  2. Under the My Account tab press on Remove Authenticator App and then press Okay to confirm.

Remove Authenticator App button

Want to learn more?

To set MFA back up on your account, please check out the Setting up Multi-Factor Authentication Help Center article.

Unfortunately, if you did not save your backup codes the Discord Support team will not be able to remove MFA from your account.

How to Receive a SMS Authentication Code

If you have SMS MFA set up on your Discord account you can receive a SMS code instead of MFA or use a backup code to log into your account. After logging in, you can remove MFA.

  1. After logging in you’ll see the prompt to enter authenticator code. To enter a backup code instead, press on Verify with something else.
Verify with something else option
  1. Select Use a code sent to your phone.
Use a code sent to your phone button
  1. Enter the SMS code that was sent to your phone and then press Confirm.
Where to enter your SMS auth code

  1. After logging in, you can then move MFA from your account so you can add it back later. Tap on User Settings by selecting the cogwheel button [] in the bottom-left.

  2. Under the My Account tab press on Remove Authenticator App and then press Okay to confirm.

Remove Authenticator App button

Want to learn more?

To set MFA back up on your account, please check out the a Setting up Multi-Factor Authentication Help Center article.

Disabling MFA if You’re Logged Into Your Discord Account

If you’re already logged into your Discord account on your device, you can disable MFA and then re-add it.

  1. Tap on User Settings by selecting the cogwheel button [] in the bottom-left.

  2. Under the My Account tab press on View Backup Codes to access your backup codes if you don’t have them already. You will need to enter your password to access them. Otherwise you can copy a backup code from your saved list.

  3. Press on Remove Authenticator App.

Remove Authenticator App button
  1. Select Verify with something else.
Verify with something else option
  1. Enter the 8-digit backup code and then press on Confirm.
Enter your backup code

Want to learn more?

To set MFA back up on your account, please check out the Setting up Multi-Factor Authentication Help Center article.

How to Remove a Phone Number From a Discord Account

On Discord, phone numbers are used to help with login and verification for anti-abuse purposes. However, there may be situations in which you have to remove and change the phone number under your account. This article will help you remove the phone number under your account.

How to Remove a Phone Number

Contact Us: If you’re unable to remove the number from the account yourself, you can reach out to the Discord Support team under the email address associated with the account to have the number removed: dis.gd/contact

How to Remove a Phone Number on an Accidental Account

A rare instance can happen in which you accidentally create a Discord account using your phone number instead of attaching it to your account. If you want to remove your phone number from the accidental account, the best way to do so is to log into that account:

Entering the phone number at login

How to Restore Your Deleted Discord Account

If your Discord account is pending deletion, you can stop it from getting deleted by restoring your account by following this simple Discord account recovery guide.

What this article covers:

  • How to Restore a Discord Account
  • Having Trouble Restoring your Discord Account?
  • How to Verify Your Discord Account

How to Restore a Discord Account

Important: You have 15 days for the deletion process to be completed. If you wish to restore your account before deletion, it must be done before 15 days. You can learn more about this by checking out the How to Delete your Discord Account Help Center article.

  1. Open the Discord app on your desktop, in a web browser, or through the Discord mobile app.

  2. Enter your account’s login information.

Example of the log in window on desktop/browser (left), example of the log in window on mobile (right)
  1. The Discord app will let you know that this account is pending deletion. If you wish to stop the deletion of your Discord account, select Restore Account.
Example of the Restore Account button on desktop/browser (left), Example of the Restore Account button on mobile (right)
  1. The app will then take you to the Discord account you just logged into and restored!

Having Trouble Restoring Your Discord Account?

If you are having issues restoring your Discord account, there are a few things to remember:

  • If you initiated the deletion of your Discord account, the account is in a “pending deletion” state for 15 days. Once that period of time has passed, the Discord account has been deleted from our system and cannot be restored.
  • If you try to log into your account that you initiated for deletion, the 15 day period has passed, and the Discord app does not dictate that your account is pending deletion, your account has already been deleted from our system and cannot be restored.
  • If you are trying to restore the Discord account you initiated for deletion but cannot remember your account’s password login, you will have to reset your account’s password.
  • If you previously contacted the Support Team to delete your account but now wish to cancel the account deletion, please follow up with our Support Team.
  • If you are trying to restore your Discord account but you are having trouble with logging into your account to cancel its deletion and you suspect that your account has been compromised, please reach out to our Support Team.
  • If your account has been deleted because it was banned, disabled, or actioned on by Discord, you cannot restore it. You may submit an appeal on your account to our Trust & Safety team. Want to learn more? If you are interested in deleting your Discord account, you can check out this support article. If you would rather disable your account, you can read this article here.

How to Verify Your Discord Account

In order to use Discord and check out Discord servers, you may be required to verify your email and phone number as part of our safety system to keep users and communities safe.

What this article covers:

  • Why do I need to verify my account?
  • How does Discord use my phone number?
  • How to verify my account
  • Having trouble verifying?

Why do I need to verify my account?

We want users to feel secure using Discord, and we invest in features that help protect you from scams or abuse. Requiring that you verify your email address or phone number helps prove you are not a robot and helps keep spammers out.

While using Discord, you might have encountered a “Verification Required” message, which is one of our safety efforts for our platform. The “Verification Required” message is part of our verification system to help protect both you and the communities on Discord. This means sometimes our systems detect activity that calls for extra information.

This verification not only serves to help confirm to Discord that you are more likely to not be spam but also provides additional barriers of defense against malicious activity on your account.

So you might see this message because you want to join a server that requires its members to have verified accounts. Some other reasons might be that you:

  • joined multiple servers in a short period of time
  • direct messaged multiple users who are not your friends
  • sent messages or posted content to communities faster than a human can manage
  • used third party clients or modifications to Discord We have seen how these kinds of activities are a signal of harmful behavior that can harm Discord users or communities.

How does Discord use my phone number?

Discord uses your phone number for safety and security purposes. Discord also supports opt-in features like Find Your Friends, which allows you to discover friends on Discord using your phone contacts!

How to verify your account

If you’re looking to verify the email address associated with your Discord account but can’t find the original verification email, you can check out this article here.

We may require you to verify your account using a valid phone number.The phone number you use cannot be associated with an existing Discord account. The process will look a little something like this:

  1. Press on the Start Verification button.

  2. Here is where you will need to provide a valid mobile phone number. Remember that it cannot be attached to an existing Discord account.

If you would like to learn how to remove a phone number from an existing Discord account, be sure to check out this article.

=

  1. Wait for the SMS to be sent to your mobile phone and follow the instructions to input the verification code. This should complete the phone verification process!

Having trouble verifying?

When going through the motions, you may run into the following errors below:

Possible Errors
Steps to Take

Invalid phone number: the phone number was not entered correctly or is unusable.

Be sure to use a valid phone number.

VOIP, Burner, or Landline numbers cannot be used.

Then, try re-entering the phone number you wish to verify. If you are still running into any issues, contact our support team here.

Rate Limit/Recently Used: the phone number was recently used and is currently in a timeout period.

Please wait 24-48 hrs before verifying your phone number once more.

Existing account: the phone number may be associated with an accidental Discord account.

If you’re running into this error, you can refer to our How to Remove a Phone Number article for further steps.

Captcha: this is an additional security step that you may run into while verifying

If you’re running into issues while completing the captcha, please reach out to our support team here.

If you have additional questions about the “Verification Required” message or issues verifying your account, you can submit a ticket to our Support team here: dis.gd

QR Code Login FAQ

What this article covers:

  • How to login with your QR Code
  • Safety Tips With QR code login, you can connect to Discord quickly and securely without typing out your full password or sharing your password on an unfamiliar setup! Scanning a QR code with your logged-in account on your Discord mobile app is a super easy way to get logged in on a new computer, no matter where you are.

How to login with your QR Code

You can scan the QR code using any application that supports QR scanning, including the Camera app on many devices. You’ll get a quick shortcut to the Discord app for final scanning and approval.

To log in using a QR code, you’ll first want to download the Discord mobile app and log in with your account credentials. Once you’re logged in on your mobile device, you can log into the Discord desktop or browser client by scanning a QR code within the app. Here are the full steps on how to do this:

  1. Tap on your user profile image in the Discord mobile app located in the bottom right corner.

  2. Next, tap on the cogwheel [] to enter your User Settings.

  3. Scroll down until you see Scan QR Code under Account Settings.

  4. This will then open up your camera app and you just have to scan the QR code shown in either the Discord app or the browser. QR codes are only available for 2 minutes, so if yours expires, you’ll have to refresh to get a new one!

  5. Next on your mobile device you’ll get the option to approve by tapping on Log in or you can tap Cancel to cancel it.

  6. Now you should be logged in on the desktop app or browser!

After approval, your desktop device will be logged in and ready to go! Want to log out of that device? Just head to User Settings > Log Out on the desktop or browser client and you’ll be logged out until your next session.

Safety Tips

If someone you don’t know is asking you to login using a QR code, they may be trying to phish your account. You can learn more about phishing here.

You have full control over what devices are allowed for login with the verification screen shown above. Even if you’ve scanned a QR code that has opened the Discord app by mistake, you can prevent the login attempt right away.

Never approve a QR code login that you didn’t generate yourself! If you’ve been sent a QR code by someone else that opened the login verification screen, hit Cancel right away.

If you approve a login that wasn’t yours by mistake, you can change your Discord password to log out all devices at once, including those you don’t personally approve of.

Most importantly, don’t forget that any QR code login attempt needs to be approved before it goes through. Keep an eye out for that verification screen and never verify or approve a login that you didn’t prompt.

Resending Verification Email

Have you recently signed up for Discord, but now your verification email has expired? No worries, you have the power to resend the verification email right to your inbox.

What does this article cover?

  • How to resend the email
    • Browser/Desktop
    • Mobile
  • Having trouble receiving the email?

How to resend the email

If you would like to resend the verification email to yourself, you will be able to do so through the Discord browser client, desktop app, and mobile app.

Browser/Desktop

  1. Press on the cog wheel next to your Username at the bottom left of your Discord client to open User Settings.

  2. Next, under My Account you should see a banner at the top that says “Resend Verification Email”. Press on this button to resend the email.

  3. Now just follow the steps in the verification email and you should be verified!

Mobile

  1. Tap on your avatar in the bottom right corner to access your User Settings.

  2. With your User Settings now pulled up, tap on the option that says Account.

  3. Next tap on the banner at the top that says “Verify” to resend the verification email.

  4. Now just follow the steps in the verification email that you received!

Having trouble receiving the email?

If you’re not seeing the email in your inbox, please try allowlisting the following email addresses:

  • notifications@discord.com
  • support@discord.com
  • noreply@discord.com Once you have finished allowlisting those emails, try requesting the verification email again through a different device if possible. If requesting through a mobile device, please try using data to see if the email arrives that way.
Note: Our support team is unable to send verification emails manually. However, if you’re running into any issues while trying the steps above, feel free to reach out at dis.gd.

Security Keys, Passkeys, and Passwordless Login on Discord

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA for short) is a great way to add an extra layer of security to your Discord account to help you stay in control of logging in.

What this article covers:

  • How to Register Passkey
    • Mobile
    • Desktop/Browser
  • Passwordless Login with Passkeys
  • How to Use Security Keys Discord supports the newest standards for authentication: Passkeys and Security Keys, an easier to use and more secure way to sign into your account! Passkeys are encrypted digital keys you create using your fingerprint, face, or screen lock, and they can be stored in a password manager. When you log into Discord, your device will prompt you to identify yourself using a Passkey/Security Key (e.g., with Face ID), and then you’re logged in! No password needed.

All you’ll need to do is Register a Passkey. Once you’ve done that, you’re set! The next time you sign in, you’ll be able to use that passkey for one-step login - see below for more details.

How to Register Passkeys

Mobile

  1. Tap your avatar in the bottom-right corner and then tap on the cogwheel [] in the top-right corner.

  2. Tap on Account then select Security Keys.

  3. Tap Add to begin the setup process. You may be asked to confirm your password or complete an MFA challenge, if you already have one enrolled.

  4. Your device will prompt you to save the passkey with a password manager. If you want more options on where to save your passkey or want to use an advanced configuration, tap Other Options.

  5. Once you finish registering your key, you can choose a name for it. When you’re done, tap Finish.

  6. And you’re done! Make sure to download and store your backup codes.

Desktop/Browser

  1. Start by selecting the the cogwheel [] next to your username.

  2. This will open your User Settings and take you to the My Account page. While here, you will be able to view the Multi-Factor Authentication options under the Password and Authentication section.

  3. To set up a Security Key, select Register a Security Key and follow the prompts to reauthenticate.

  4. Tap Let’s go to start the Passkey enrollment process. You’ll be prompted by your operating system, if supported, to enroll a Passkey. On MacOS, it looks like this:

  5. After enrolling MFA, the Discord app will also have a list of backup codes for login: each of these can be used once instead of a code generated by your app, in case you lose access to it. Make sure to download and store these backup codes! If you lose these, Discord can’t help you get back into your account.

And you’re done!

You can now register another Security Key on this device or a different device (you can have up to 16 security keys/passkeys at the same time).

Passwordless Login with Passkeys

Using your passkey to log in is simple! As long as you have a password manager available with a passkey saved in it, you will be prompted to select a passkey. If you’re not getting prompted, you can always tap on Or, sign in with Passkey instead. Your system will prompt you to select the Passkey associated with your account and complete a challenge (e.g., Face ID), then you’re logged in!

How to Use Security Keys

While Security Keys function similarly to passkeys, they generally cannot be used for one-step login on Discord. Fear not! You’ll still be able to use Security Keys as a form of MFA - when you log in, you’ll get an additional challenge after entering your username and password to use you security key:

Press Authenticate with security key to interact with your Security Key, and you’re in!

Passkey Troubleshooting

Having issues with your passkey when trying to log in? Here are some troubleshooting steps to try if your passkey isn’t working for any reason:

First, try using your username and password to log in, then using your Passkey on the following MFA Challenge screen. If that doesn’t work, you’ll need to delete the existing Passkey from both your device and Discord account, then set it up once again. To do this:

  1. Make sure you have your Discord backup codes handy just in case. Open your password manager and remove the passkey from your saved credentials for Discord. Refer to your password manager’s documentation for details on how to do this.

  2. Use a different MFA method or device to complete the challenge. If you don’t have another set up, you can use a backup code from the list you saved to complete the MFA challenge and finish the login.

  3. Go to your Account Settings and repeat the enrollment process to register a new passkey with your password manager. See How to Register Passkeys above for more details, and be sure to remember what you name it!

  4. From the Account Settings screen, delete the old passkey associated with your Discord account.

And now you’re starting fresh! Following these steps ensures your remaining saved backup codes continue to work while enrolling a new Passkey.

Setting up Multi-Factor Authentication

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA for short) is a great way to add an extra layer of security to your Discord account to help you stay in control of logging in.

What this article covers:

  • Types of Multi-Factor Authentication
    • Passkeys and Security Keys
    • Authenticator App
    • SMS/Texts
    • Backup Codes
  • I forgot to download my codes
  • I forgot to add my phone as backup Important: Don’t forget to save your backup codes after enabling MFA. The Discord Support team is not able to remove MFA from an account.

Types of Multi-Factor Authentication

Discord supports three types of MFA: Security Keys (Passkeys), Authenticator App, and SMS. We recommend setting up a Security Key , but you can choose any combination of these options to secure your Discord account, and you’ll always have Backup Codes in case you lose access to your MFA device.

Passkeys and Security Keys

Discord supports the newest standards for authentication: Passkeys and Security Keys, an easier to use and more secure way to sign into your account! Passkeys are encrypted digital keys you create using your fingerprint, face, or screen lock, and they can be stored in your password manager so you can sign in to your account on other devices with the installed password manager. When you log into Discord, your device will prompt you to use the passkey the same way you created it (e.g., with Face ID), then you’re logged in! No password needed.

This method is one of the best ways to protect your account because it is simple to use, on your own devices, backed up in the cloud, and most importantly, phishing resistant. To get started, go to your User Settings, go to Account, tap Security Keys, then Add to enroll a Passkey on your device.

For more information and detailed instructions on how to enroll a Passkey, check out Security Keys, Passkeys, and Passwordless Login on Discord.

Authenticator App

An Authenticator App, or Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP), is an established industry standard for MFA. When you register an Authenticator App with Discord, you scan a QR code or manually enter a secret in a dedicated app (like Google Authenticator) or password manager. That app will then generate a new code every 30 seconds - whenever you want to log in to Discord, you’ll need to provide that generated code.

Keep these generated codes safe! Anyone with your password and a recently-generated code can log into your account. Additionally, not all Authenticator Apps support syncing across devices or on the cloud - if you lose your phone and don’t have access to your Authenticator App backup codes, you might not be able to log into your Discord account!

For more information and detailed instructions on how to enroll an Authenticator App, check out Using an Authenticator App on Discord.

SMS/Texts

To be transparent, SMS MFA is better than no MFA, but not by a lot. Hackers have advanced a lot in recent years - they can intercept text messages and take over phone numbers without anyone realizing by performing a “SIM Swap” directly with carriers.

While we do support SMS MFA, we don’t recommend it - and it can only be enabled once you’ve already set up an Authenticator App.

Backup Codes

Tip: If you’re no longer seeing the option to use a backup code, either you have used all your backup codes or you are attempting to use the code for something other than logging in and managing your account identity (e.g., registering a passkey).

What happens when the worst case scenario happens? You’ve registered your security key, but your laptop’s been stolen; or configured your Authenticator, but lost your phone. How can you regain access to your account? With Discord Backup codes!

Backup codes are special one-time use codes we give you after signing up for MFA. Keep these secret and well-protected. We recommend storing them in a password manager, but you can also print them out and hide them if you’d prefer.

If you are locked out of your account and need to get past MFA, you can use one of these codes in order to recover and reconfigure your account. Each code can only be used once, so once your account is under your control again with new MFA configured, generate some new codes and hide them away safely again.

I forgot to download my codes

It’s all good, you can still do this in your account settings! Your settings screen will now look something like this:

  1. Tap on the cogwheel [] in the bottom-left corner to access User Settings then make sure you’re under My Account.
View Backup Codes button
  1. Select View Backup Codes to see your codes (and which one’s you’ve used) as well as get the option to download them.

I forgot to add my phone as backup!

  1. Head back to your account and press Add to add a phone number.
Enter a Phone Number option
  1. Verify that number in Discord with the SMS code you will receive.
Enter SMS code window
  1. Press on Enable SMS Authentication after your number has been confirmed on your account.
Enable SMS Authentication option
  1. Enter your MFA code to approve enabling SMS MFA.

Now when you login, if the feature is enabled, you will have a link to request an SMS with a code to authenticate yourself as a backup option. SMS MFA can only be enabled once you’ve enabled MFA overall.

Using an Authenticator App on Discord

What this article covers:

  • What is an Authenticator App?
  • How to Register an Authenticator App
    • Mobile
    • Desktop/Browser
  • Logging in With an Authenticator App

What is an Authenticator App?

Using an Authenticator App (also called a Time-based One-Time Password or TOTP) is another great way to secure your account by providing a one-time code alongside your password - this ensures that someone can’t log into your account if they only have your password. You can set up an Authenticator App from your Account Settings on the mobile, desktop, and browser app.

How to Register an Authenticator App

Mobile

  1. Tap your avatar in the bottom-right corner and then tap on the cogwheel [] in the top-right corner.

  2. Press on Account and then select Enable Authenticator App.

  3. To begin this authentication process, you’ll need to download either Google Authenticator or Authy on your mobile device.

  4. Follow the instructions in the Discord app to copy your secret key into your Authenticator App so it can generate your one-time codes. You’ll be asked to enter one of those codes generated by the Authenticator App to ensure it’s working properly.

  5. You can now link your phone number to your Discord account to help act as a backup method for obtaining these authentication codes. This can help you be less worried about losing access to your Authenticator app, but reduces how secure your account is.

  6. After enabling an Authenticator App, the Discord app will also have a list of backup codes for login: each of these can be used once instead of a code generated by your Authenticator App, in case you lose access to it. Make sure to download and store these backup codes in a safe, easily accessible place! If you lose these, Discord can’t help you get back into your account.

If you set up your Authenticator App through Authy you can set up a backup by following these steps. If you set it up through Google Authenticator you can back up your account by following these steps.

Desktop/Browser

  1. Start by selecting the the cogwheel [] next to your username.

  2. This will open your User Settings and take you to the My Account page. While here, you will be able to view the Multi-Factor Authentication options under the Password and Authentication section.

  3. Press the Enable Authenticator App button to get started. To begin the authenticator process, you will have to download Google Authenticator app or the Authy app on your mobile device. After you’ve downloaded an Authenticator App, open it on your mobile device and use the camera function to scan the QR code in the Discord app.

  4. After scanning the QR code that is displayed in the Discord app, your Authenticator App will generate a 6 digit code. Enter that 6 digit code into “Login with your code” and then tap on Activate.

  5. You can now link your phone number to your account to help act as a backup method for obtaining these authentication codes. This can help you be less worried about losing access to your Authenticator App, but reduces how secure your account is.

  6. After enabling an Authenticator App, the Discord app will also have a list of backup codes for login: each of these can be used once instead of a code generated by your app, in case you lose access to it. Make sure to download and store these backup codes in a safe, easily accessible place! If you lose these, Discord can’t help you get back into your account.

If you set up your Authenticator App through Authy, you can set up a backup by following these steps. If you set it up through Google Authenticator, you can back up your account by following these steps.
Logging in With an Authenticator App

After enabling an Authenticator App you’ll see an additional prompt to enter an authentication code when you log in to your Discord:

Enter a code from your app or from your list of backup codes, select Confirm, and you’re in!

Announcements

[Notice] Emails from Discord

If you receive an email from Discord and the email address domain is @m.discord.com - it is safe to trust the message and open this email.

Discord owns and uses this @m.discord.com email domain to send official information about your Discord account, including product and feature announcements.

Note: You can modify your email preferences by going to User Settings > Notifications in the mobile, desktop or browser version of the Discord app.

[Recent Update] Apple App Store Age Rating Change

On March 22, 2021, Discord iOS app’s age rating has been updated from 12+ to 17+.

As a result, iOS devices with content restrictions for apps may no longer be able to access the Discord app on their device.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why did Discord update its age rating from 12+ to 17+?

A: Discord updated its age rating to 17+ at Apple’s request. We work hard to create robust controls and policies to help ensure minors are not exposed to content inappropriate for them.

Q: How can I regain access to Discord on my iOS device?

A: If you want to keep using Discord on your iPhone/iPad/iOS device, you will have to change your iOS content & privacy restrictions.

Note: If you are under the age of 18, you may need parental approval in order to make this change.
  • If you want to manage or change your iOS content restrictions, go to Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions > Content Restrictions > Apps.
  • You can select the right setting that is appropriate for you. The Discord iOS app is allowed if you allow “17+” or “Allow All Apps.” Here’s a link to more information on this process: support.apple.com

If you are a parent and would like more information about best practices on safety on Discord, you can learn more at discord.com

A/V E2EE Enforcement for Non-Stage Voice Calls

What is the Update?

Updated clients which support the DAVE (Audio & Video End-to-End Encryption) Protocol are now required to connect to non-stages voice calls across the Discord Platform.

If you attempt to connect with an out-of-date client, the voice gateway will reject your connection with close code 4017.

[Monitoring] Compatibility Mode Issue

Update as of March 3rd, 12:35PM PST

We’ve discovered that some users cannot update their Discord app on Windows because they have set Discord to “Compatibility Mode” and as a result get stuck on the last version of Discord that supported Windows 8.

It is a persistent issue and any attempt to re-install the app will reinstall the old version.

How Can I Resolve This Issue?

The only solution at the moment is to disable Compatibility Mode for the Discord executable and to fully restart the application so that the app picks up the update.

[Resolved] Chrome OS Device Issues

Update as of March 3rd, 1:30PM PST

We were investigating issues with some up-to-date ChromeOS devices connecting to voice channels. Our team has fixed the issue, and this issue should now be resolved.

If you were experiencing this issue, please restart your app or device in order to receive the update.

For More Information

See our Help Center article for Minimum Client Version Requirements and End to End Encryption for Audio and Video for further details.

For more information and updates, head to our status page at discordstatus.com.

Blog: PlayStation® x Discord: Connect Your Account and Show What You’re Playing

This blog post is available in multiple languages. For non-English, head to our Help Center and select your preferred language at the top-right.

Back in May of 2021, our friends at PlayStation announced a new Partnership with Discord, working together to deliver new ways to integrate your PlayStation experience with Discord for your friends and communities to see. Of course, everything needed to stay super-secret at the time, so we couldn’t share anything quite yet.

But your daydreams of Squares, Triangles, and Circles swirling in the sky are over as the news drops now: Starting today, we’re gradually rolling out the ability to link your PSN account from Discord and display your PlayStation®4 or PlayStation®5 game activity in your user profile!

If you’ve ever connected your Discord account to another service that allows you to display your activity, it works similarly here: once your Discord account is linked, the game you’re currently playing on either PS4™or PS5™ will be shown as your activity, just like that!

You can even opt to display your PlayStation™Network online ID on your profile so your Discord friends can add you and tag along. It’s especially great for knowing if your friend is currently playing a game that supports cross-play on another platform.

Don’t see the option quite yet? PlayStation Network account connection is gradually rolling out to U.S. Discord users with additional countries soon to follow — check back later in User Settings > Connections if it’s not there for you at the moment.

How to Connect your PlayStation Network Account to Discord

Have you ever linked one of the… shuffles through the integration list… eleven other services we now offer Discord integrations for? It’s a very similar process, but if this is your first time ever connecting another account to Discord, let’s go through gettin’ it set up:

To connect your Discord account to your PlayStation Network account, open up Discord and head into User Settings > Connections on either desktop or web. On mobile, go to User Settings > Connections.

On this page, you’ll see a newly-added PlayStation icon. Choose that, and you’re already on your way!

From there, a browser window to authorize from your PlayStation account will pop up. Use it to sign in to your account on the login page and boom: your PlayStation Network account is all connected. Simple, right?

Once connected, two new options will appear for your PlayStation Network account: “Display on Profile” and “Display PlayStation Network as your status.” While displaying your PlayStation online ID is all fine and dandy, showing your game activity is the real deal and will inspire your friends to join along for the ride.

Now, the game you’re currently playing on your PlayStation 4 or PlayStation 5 console will be happily displayed in your user profile for all your friends and community members to see!

Do note that on your PSN Privacy Settings, your “PSN Online Status” and “Now Playing” visibility must be set to “Anyone” in order for your status to be visible on Discord. Take a peek at PlayStation’s article on “How to change privacy settings on PlayStation Network” in case you may have adjusted them before.

For more details on the account connection process, be sure to check out our Help Center article.

Whether you stick to single-player games or enjoy having your friends join in on multiplayer endeavors, your friends from all over the world will be able to see all sorts of PlayStation games you’re playing and start a conversation about wanting to jump in and play with you.

The ability to connect your Discord account with your PlayStation Network account is rolling out starting today and will be available on every platform Discord is on: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and the web app.

We’re excited to continue our partnership with PlayStation and explore how we can collectively create great shared experiences for your friends and communities. Show us which PlayStation games you’re excited to share your activity status for, and tell us how you’re using this integration on Twitter or TikTok!

And if you’ve never used Discord and somehow made it to the end of this blog… what’re you doin’?! You can download Discord on your device of choice here.

Discord Checkpoint 2025

Discord Checkpoint is a personalized year-in-review experience that highlights your friendships, favorite games, and the communities that made 2025 special for you.

What this article covers:

  • What is Discord Checkpoint?
    • What’s included in my Checkpoint?
  • How to view Checkpoint
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
    • One-time Pop-Up
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What is Discord Checkpoint?

Note: Not everyone will get a Checkpoint—it depends on your Discord activity and your data personalization settings. Check out the Frequently Asked Questions below to learn more.

Checkpoint is Discord’s first-ever year-in-review experience. It’s a celebration of all the moments that made your Discord year unique!

What’s included in my Checkpoint?

Your Checkpoint includes personalized stats about your year on Discord, such as the friends you talked to most, the games you played, the communities you called home, and more.

You’ll also receive an exclusive Checkpoint Avatar Decoration that you can display on your profile until January 15, 2026, as a thank you gift for being part of the Discord community!

Checkpoint 2025

How to view Checkpoint

Desktop/Browser

  1. Check that you have the latest version of the app.

  2. Press on the flag icon [] in the top-right corner to access your Checkpoint.

Mobile

Important: Checkpoint has been temporarily disabled for Android. Checkpoint continues to be available on iOS, desktop and browser.

  1. Check that you have the latest version of the app.

  2. Tap on the You tab in the bottom-right corner.

  3. Press on the Checkpoint banner to view your Checkpoint.

Checkpoint banner on mobile
One-time Pop-Up

Eligible users may see a one-time modal pop-up that takes you to your Checkpoint.

Modal pop-up for Checkpoint

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Who gets a Checkpoint?

A: Checkpoint is available to users who were active on Discord during 2025 and have the Use data to personalize my Discord experience setting enabled in their Data & Privacy settings. We respect your privacy and only create Checkpoints for users who have chosen to enable this setting.

Q: Why don’t I have a Checkpoint?

A: If you don’t have a Checkpoint, it may be because you’re new to Discord or were not active enough this year to compile stats for Checkpoint, or because you have chosen to have your data personalization setting disabled.

Even if you don’t get a Checkpoint, you’ll still be able to claim the Checkpoint Avatar Decoration as a thank you gift for being part of the Discord community! To claim the decoration, follow the steps for desktop or mobile in the How to view Checkpoint section of this article.

Q: I’d like to change my data personalization setting.

A: You can learn more about your data personalization setting and how to change it in this support article. Note that changing your setting now won’t give you a Checkpoint for 2025.

Q: If I change my data personalization setting now, will I get a Checkpoint for 2025?

A: Changing your setting now won’t give you a Checkpoint for 2025. However, it would allow Discord to create personalized experiences like this for you if we offer them in the future.

Q: How long will Checkpoint be available?

A: You’ll be able to view your 2025 Checkpoint until January 15, 2026.

Q: Who can see my Checkpoint?

Only you can see your Checkpoint. You can choose to share it with others if you’d like.

Q: Can I share my Checkpoint?

Yes! You can share your Checkpoint stats and celebrate your Discord year with friends. There’s a Share button on your Summary page—just press it and choose where on Discord you’d like to share. You can also take screenshots of other pages and share them on Discord or other platforms.

Checkpoint shared in a text-channel

Q: What about my privacy?

A: We respect your privacy choices. Checkpoint is only available to users who have chosen to allow Discord to use their data to personalize their experience. This setting gives you control over whether Discord creates personalized features like Checkpoint for you.

Checkpoint is created using your activity data like games played and time spent in voice—we don’t use the content of your messages.

You can review and change your data personalization settings at any time. Learn more.

Q: Will Checkpoint happen every year?

A: We launched Checkpoint in 2025 to celebrate Discord’s 10th anniversary: a decade of the games you’ve played, the friendships you’ve made, and the communities you’ve built here. It’s something many of you have asked for, so it felt like the perfect time to give you a personalized look back at your year with us. Plans for Checkpoint beyond 2025 are still unfolding. Stay tuned!
