Discord Social SDK Integration for Roblox Games FAQ

When a Roblox game developer has integrated the Discord Social SDK, linking your account can open up social features like game activity sharing, game invites, and a safer, more connected experience in their official game communities — all while hanging out in Discord.

Note: This integration is currently only available in official Discord servers for specific Roblox games. The developer manages the game and server.

What this article covers:

  • What is the Discord Social SDK Integration for Roblox games?
  • How to Link Your Roblox Account to Discord
  • Verified Roles and Server Participation
    • Crossbans
  • Additional Features Powered by the Integration
    • Share Your Game Activity (Rich Presence)
    • Send and Receive Game Invites
  • Managing your Connection
    • Disconnecting Your Roblox Account (User Settings > Connections)
    • Deauthorizing Individual Games (User Settings > Authorized Apps)
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Discord Social SDK Integration for Roblox games?

Discord provides a Social SDK that Roblox game developers can choose to integrate into their games. When a developer does, it can unlock additional features for their official game server and players on Discord — like game activity sharing, game invites, and server verification. The features that are available for a given game and its server depends on what the developer has chosen to implement.

Getting set up to enable these features takes two steps: first, linking your Roblox account to Discord through Connections (the same place you’d connect Spotify or Xbox), then second, authorizing the specific game when prompted in the server.

This article walks through how to get set up, what features may be available, and how to manage your connection.

How to Link Your Roblox Account to Discord

You only need to link your Discord and Roblox accounts once. After that, when you join a server with the integration enabled, you’ll be asked to authorize that specific game - a quick, separate step.

  • Open Discord and select the cogwheel near your username to open User Settings.
  • Select Connections from the left-hand menu.
  • Find Roblox in the list of available connections and select it.
  • Follow the prompts to log into your Roblox account and authorize the connection.
  • Once complete, your Roblox account will appear under your active Connections. Note: When you join a server with the integration enabled, you’ll see a prompt to authorize that specific game. This is separate from your initial account link and lets you choose which games you enable to provide additional features.

Verified Roles and Server Participation

Official Roblox game servers that use this integration can manage access through a Verified role. Here’s what to expect:

  • When you join, you’ll be prompted to link your Discord and Roblox accounts and authorize the specific game.
  • Once authorized, you’ll automatically receive a Verified role.
  • The Verified role unlocks access to channels, chats, and other features the server admin has configured.
  • Without a Verified role, you can join the server but won’t be able to participate until your account is linked. Note: The Verified role and its permissions are set by the server’s admin or owner. Discord’s support team cannot assign or manage roles on individual servers.
Crossbans

Some official game servers may use crossbans as part of their community safety setup. If you’re banned from the Roblox game linked to a Discord server, the server admin may also ban you from that server through the integration. These are moderation actions taken by the game and server, not by Discord.

Crossbans are currently one-directional - a Roblox game ban can affect your Discord server access, but a Discord server ban does not carry over to the Roblox game.

Additional Features Powered by the Integration

Depending on what the developer has chosen to enable, linking your accounts and authorizing a game can unlock additional features.

Share Your Game Activity (Rich Presence)

Instead of a generic “Playing Roblox” status, your Discord profile can display the specific game you’re playing — like Brookhaven or Grow a Garden — along with activity details the developer has set up, like your in-game location or playtime.

To manage your game activity visibility, go to Settings > Activity Privacy > Share my activity.

Note: Rich Presence details are configured by the individual game developer. Not all Roblox games will show detailed activity.

Send and Receive Game Invites

If a game is authorized, you and your friends can send and receive game invitations directly in Discord.

Game invites appear as a Game Invitation card in your DMs — just hit Join to jump straight into a session.

Note: You don’t need your own Roblox account linked to accept a game invite from a friend. You will need to have authorized the game to send invites yourself. Availability depends on whether the game developer has enabled this feature.

Managing your Connection

Your connection on Discord for this integration has two layers: a platform-level account link and individual game authorizations.

Disconnecting Your Roblox Account (User Settings > Connections)

You can disconnect your Roblox account from Discord at any time through User Settings > Connections.

To disconnect your Roblox account:

  • Open Discord and go to User Settings.
  • Select Connections from the left-hand menu.
  • Find your Roblox connection and select the X next to it.
  • A confirmation modal will appear. Select Unlink to confirm. Removing your Roblox connection at the platform level does not automatically deauthorize individual games you’ve previously authorized. Your authorization for a given game and any features enabled through it (including any server access tied to them) will remain active until it is separately deauthorized.
Deauthorizing Individual Games (User Settings > Authorized Apps)

To fully remove a game’s permissions, deauthorize the game separately:

  • Go to User Settings > Authorized Apps.
  • Find the game and select Deauthorize, then confirm. Once deauthorized, you’ll lose access to the features it enabled. This can include the Verified role and the ability to participate in that server until you re-authorize.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: I’ve linked my Roblox account through other bots before. Do I need to do this again?

A: Yes. This Discord Social SDK integration is a separate connection from any third-party bot. You’ll need to link through User Settings > Connections - but you only need to do it once, and it works across all servers that use the integration.

Q: Will I see this in every Roblox game server on Discord?

A: No. This integration is only available in official Discord servers for specific Roblox games where the developer has enabled it. Most Discord servers will not have this feature.

Q: Why isn’t this Roblox integration available in my server?

A: The Discord Social SDK is currently only available to select Roblox developers. If a game hasn’t integrated it yet, it may not be available for that server to enable.

Q: Do I have to link my account to join the server?

A: You can join without linking, but your access will depend on how the developer has configured the integration. Some servers require account linking to participate. Others may use the integration only for social features with no participation requirement. If a server does require it, you can still read the server without linking — but you won’t be able to post or interact until you complete the process.

Q: How many Roblox accounts can I link to my Discord account?

A: You can only link one Roblox account to your Discord account at a time.

Q: What’s the difference between disconnecting my Roblox account and deauthorizing a game?

A: Connecting to your Roblox account lets you verify that you are a Roblox player and share your basic profile information with Discord. Disconnecting removes your platform-level Roblox connection in User Settings > Connections, but does not remove individual game authorizations. Authorizing an individual game lets you enable the additional features described above relating to that game and its server. To remove a specific game’s access and lose access to those features, go to User Settings > Authorized Apps and deauthorize that game separately.

Q: Why was I banned from a game’s Discord server after being banned from the game?

A: Some servers use crossbans - a Roblox game ban can carry over to the connected Discord server. This is configured by the game developer.

Q: Can I control what game information is visible on my Discord profile?

A: Yes. Manage your overall activity visibility in Settings > Activity Privacy > Activity Sharing.

Q: How will I know what permissions and data sharing I’m allowing by authorizing a game?

A: Before authorizing a game, you’ll see a screen outlining the permissions you’re granting the game and the data that you’re authorizing to be shared. For more information about the game’s data practices, please review its terms of service and privacy policy. Any data that Discord receives will be treated like other data shared on Discord consistent with Discord’s Privacy Policy.

You can review and revoke your game authorizations at any time through your Discord Authorized Apps tab within the User Settings.

Q: I have an issue with Roblox itself — can Discord support help?

A: For issues with a specific game’s server or their integration, please reach out to the server admin directly. For issues related to Discord features, you can reach out to Discord support. Discord is unable to assist with Roblox account or platform issues.

Q: I still need help — how do I contact support?

A: Submit a support ticket to dis.gd/support and include any relevant screenshots or error messages to help us assist you faster.

Discordapp.com is now Discord.com

As of May 4th, 2020, we have moved our domain from discordapp.com to discord.com!

Domain Update FAQ

Q: Why did my password manager/browser forget my password for Discord?

A: Because your browser and password managers have your password stored under discordapp.com, you’ll need change your saved passwords to the new domain discord.com

Q: Why am I getting all these new permission requests? (Mic, Camera, Notifications, etc)

A: Since your permissions are only tied to the domain name discordapp.com, you will now need to allow permissions to our new domain discord.com

Q: Why did all of my customizations to my account get reset (ex: Frequently Used emoji, notification settings, etc)?

A: Our team has done their best to make sure that your customized Discord settings will not be impacted. However, some users may have been automatically logged out of their account during the update process.

Unfortunately, if you were automatically logged out of your account with this domain update, your customizations to your account may have also been removed as well and will need to be added once more.

We’re so sorry for the confusion and frustration with those reset customizations.

Q: Why are my images/icons not appearing or loading?

A: It’s possible that a browser add-on, extension, or ad blocker setting is blocking Discord from loading images.

Double check any settings with your browser add-ons, extensions, or ad blockers, and make sure that discord.com has all the necessary permissions in order to have these images load again.

You may also need to allowlist cdn.discordapp.com as well in your browser add-ons settings.

Enhanced Role Styles

Make certain roles in your server shine with Enhanced Role Styles. Choose between eye-catching gradient or holographic designs that make important roles stand out more in your community.

What this article covers:

  • What are Enhanced Role Styles?
  • How to Use Server Boosts to Unlock Enhanced Role Styles as a Server Owner/Admin
  • Setting Enhanced Role Styles as a Server Owner/Admin
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are Enhanced Role Styles?

Example of Holographic Enhanced Role Style

Enhanced Role Styles help to make certain roles stand out more in your server. You can choose between gradient or holographic. The Enhanced Role Styles perk can be added to a server by applying 3 Server Boosts as an owner or admin of the server. This additional perk is separate from Boost Levels, so your server doesn’t need to reach a specific Boost Level to access it.

How to Use Server Boosts to Unlock Enhanced Role Styles as a Server Owner/Admin

The server owner or admin can use any available applied Server Boosts to unlock Enhanced Role Styles.

  1. With the correct server selected, select Server Boosts in the upper-left corner. Only server admins and owners can view this tab.
Example of Server Boosts tab in a server
  1. In the upper-right, you’ll see how many Server Boosts you have available and the recent activity of Server Boosts. If you have 3 Server Boosts available, you can enable this perk right away.
Example of available Server Boosts
  1. To apply to Enhanced Role Styles, hover over the perk and press Enable Perk. A window will appear where you can configure your newly unlocked perk!
Enable Perk Enhanced Role Styles

Setting Enhanced Role Styles as a Server Owner/Admin

Info: Enhanced Role Styles can only be edited on desktop/browser, it’s not available on mobile.

  1. Select your server’s name in the upper-left corner and then press Server Settings.
Server Settings option
  1. Press Roles. You can edit a current role or create a new one. To edit a current one, hover over the right-hand side and press on the pencil icon [].
Edit button
  1. Under role styles, you can choose between the following:
  • Solid
  • Gradient
  • Holographic
  1. If you choose to set a Gradient, you can pick two colors or pick from available options.
Example of the Gradient Role Color options
  1. Press Save Changes once you’re finished!

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: If I set an Enhanced Role Style for a role, what happens to the role color when my server no longer has the available Server Boosts?

A:If your server loses the Enhanced Role Styles perk due to insufficient boosts, any roles using gradient or holographic styles will automatically revert to solid colors using the primary color from their enhanced style.

Q: Can I use Enhanced Role Styles for all roles in my server?

A: Yes! Once you’ve unlocked Enhanced Role Styles by applying 3 Server Boosts, you can apply gradient or holographic styles to as many roles as you want.

Q: How do Enhanced Role Styles appear on mobile devices?

A: Enhanced Role Styles are fully supported on all Discord platforms, including mobile. Members will see gradient and holographic roles on iOS and Android just as they appear on desktop/browser.

Q: Can I combine Enhanced Role Styles with other role features like role icons?

A: Absolutely! Enhanced Role Styles work alongside all other role features, including role icons, so you can create truly distinctive roles for your community.

Q: If I switch from gradient to holographic (or vice versa), will I need to spend additional boosts?

A: No. Once Enhanced Role Styles are unlocked for your server, you can freely switch between gradient and holographic styles for any role without using additional boosts.

Q: Do members need to have a specific Discord version to see Enhanced Role Styles?

A: Members will need a reasonably current version of Discord to see Enhanced Role Styles. Anyone using an outdated app version may only see the solid color version of the roles.

Q: How do Enhanced Role Styles appear in dark mode vs. light mode?

A: Enhanced Role Styles are designed to look great in both dark and light mode, with automatic adjustments to ensure visibility and aesthetic appeal in either theme.

Q: How can I disable the animation effect for Enhanced Role Styles?

A: Select the cogwheel [] next to your Discord username to access your User Settings, select the Accessibility tab, and then enable Enabled Reduced Motion.

Q: Can I add Enhanced Role Styles to a server I’m a member of?

A: If you’re a server member who wants to enable Enhanced Role Styles for your server, you can Boost your server to ensure there are enough Boosts available for a perk like this. However, only server admins & owners can enable this perk and configure it for their server.

Enable Reduced Motion setting

Q: How can I use the current Server Boosts on my server for Server Tags instead?

A: As a server owner or admin, you can disable the currently applied boosts to a level. To do so, head to the Server Boosts tab and then press on Disable Perk. You’ll then receive a confirmation window press on Disable to confirm. You can use all available Server Boosts to unlock additional perks.

Q: What are “additional perks” and how are they different from Levels?

A: Additional perks are new features you can unlock directly with Boosts, separate from your server’s Boost Level. Currently, there are two available: Enhanced Role Styles (which add gradient and holographic effects to roles) and Server Tags (4-character identifiers members can display on their profiles across Discord). Unlike traditional server levels, these perks can be unlocked individually without reaching specific level thresholds.

Q: How much do the new additional perks cost?

A: Enhanced Role Styles and Server Tags each cost 3 Boosts. If you want both perks, you’ll need 6 Boosts total (3 for each perk).

Q: Are additional perks replacing the current server level system?

A: No, this supplements the existing level system. All current server level perks (emoji slots, file upload limits, etc.) remain exactly the same. This new system simply gives you additional ways to use your Boosts for targeted perks without affecting your server’s level progression.

Q: Do additional perks use separate Boosts from my server level?

A: Yes, Boosts used for additional perks are dedicated specifically to those perks and don’t count toward your server’s level progression. Similarly, Boosts allocated to your server level can’t be used for additional perks. You’ll need separate Boosts for each - so if you want Enhanced Role Styles, you need 3 Boosts just for that perk, plus whatever Boosts you want to maintain your current server level.

Q: What happens to my additional perks if my server loses Boosts?

A: Perks require ongoing Boost allocation to remain active. If your server drops below the required number of Boosts for a perk, that perk will be disabled. Enhanced Role Styles will revert to solid colors, and Server Tags will be removed from members’ profiles. Server owners/admins can choose which perks to maintain if Boost counts drop.

Q: Why can’t I unlock perks even though I have enough Boosts?

A: Make sure you’re accessing the Server Boost tab (visible only to server owners/admins) and that your Boosts are “available” rather than already allocated to your server level. Only server members with admin permissions can unlock additional perks. You need to have enough unallocated Boosts to enable additional perks.

Q: Can I move Boosts between levels and perks after I’ve allocated them?

A: Yes, server owners and admins can reallocate Boosts between server levels and additional perks through the Server Boosts tab. However, if you move Boosts away from a perk, that perk will be disabled until you allocate enough Boosts back to it.

Q: Are additional perks a one-time purchase, or do they require ongoing Boosts?

A: Each additional perk requires an ongoing allocation of its required Boosts to stay active, just like levels. If your server drops below the required number of Boosts, the perk will be disabled until the necessary Boosts are reallocated.

Q: Can I purchase and manage additional perks from both desktop and mobile?

A: additional perks can currently only be purchased and configured on desktop.

A Fresh New Look to Celebrate Our 6th Birthday

Discord has become a place to call home to over 150 million people around the world to talk about everything from sneakers, to the deepest details of their favorite game soundtrack, to virtual car meetups and late-night study sessions.

Just under a year ago, we outlined the work we’ve done to welcome the world to Discord, no matter what your interests may be. To help, we also wanted to make our overall look and feel just as welcoming to the world as the ever-improving in-app experience and help everyone enjoy Discord just a bit more.

So, welcome to Discord. Again.

Let’s Get Right Into It… Why Would We Change Our Logo?

Our current logo has stuck around with us since the beginning of time itself… as in, since we first launched Discord in 2015. A lot of people aren’t aware that the little smiley icon in the Discord logo has a name: Clyde. Most people call him Discord, Mickey Mouse pants, a game controller, and of course, ugly. :(

OG Clyde, hiding in his little bubble he calls home.

Most of the time, you’ll see old Clyde within a rounded rectangle chat bubble. Technically, being inside this bubble is Clyde’s “home.” Whether it’s on our website, within a profile icon on our social pages, or inside the app icon on your computer or mobile device, Clyde was always “in” something, like a hamster stuck in a rolling ball.

Only the most eagle-eyed may notice, but the old logo was horizontally asymmetrical — something our Design Team’s been waiting years to fix. Small details such as “Clyde lives within a bubble” and “not symmetrical” can be deceivingly restrictive when creating new interface elements, art assets, and even merch items.

So, we took a step back and thought to ourselves: How can we give Clyde a refresh without going too crazy? And what makes Clyde, well… Clyde? It took a while for us to land in a good place — people around the world are already familiar with the Discord logo, so we can’t have them wake up one day seeing something weird like a banana as our icon.

Below is a preview of all the ideas and experimentation we went through when determining how Clyde should look. We went from lots of circular shapes to what’s basically a :) and eventually refining the more squared-off shape that you’re seeing today.

We’ve also freed Clyde from being stuck in his bubble, and he’s very excited about it. In fact, you might even see Clyde smile. Or be a bit sad. Or sleepy. A good amount of fan art depicts Clyde with expressions, but now we’re officially letting Clyde feel what he needs to feel.

If you take a peek at the top of Clyde’s head, you may notice the old antennas look a bit more like shoulders now. We realized that sharp little antennas didn’t translate well when printed on different types of materials, or when printed on really small surfaces such as a pin.

In the end, we believe changes to Clyde present him in a more friendly tone, reshaped to be more understandable whether smaller or larger, all while still keeping our pal looking unique and familiar to the most veteran of users.

All these smaller details, improvements, and new options that add up to a fresh new look for years to come.

Making Our Mark: The New Wordmark

Alongside the refreshed Clyde, you’ll also see an updated the Discord wordmark, which is a fancy way of saying “the font used to spell out ‘Discord’” — it’s a custom font based upon “Ginto” that we created to go with the new Clyde logo.

We explored hundreds of different fonts before landing on this very unique font face that we believe captures the playfulness of Discord. We even tweaked some elements of the font and letters so it’s easier to read than how it originally was.

The biggest thing that we debated, changed, changed back, changed back again, agonized over and might have even had serious anxiety about was whether we should keep the wordmark in all caps or in title case. Once something is finalized and the world sees, there’s no going back, and that includes how things are capitalized.

In the end, we decided that Title case — making sure it’s always capitalized like someone’s name — made our new wordmark more legible. Although you won’t often see the wordmark used on its own, it does look beautiful.

Shades of Deep Blurple (And Other Colors)

Good ol’ Blurple: Just like Clyde, Blurple is in every corner of Discord. It’s not exactly blue, not exactly purple… but it’s definitely close to our hearts. All of our older colors were a bit on the pastel-y side, along with our cleverly-named shades of Grey including… “Greyple,” “Dark, but not black” and “Not quite black.”

With a new logo comes a brighter, more saturated Blurple: below is our new Blurple, right alongside the new Clyde and our new wordmark so you can cohesively see the new look:

Internally, we first used this new color “blurple_5_plus_adjustments,” but that didn’t quite roll off the tongue as well as Blurple did. The lighter color of Blurple will forever be known as “OG Blurple.”

We wanted to bring more energy to Discord for our entire color palette by brightening up the colors to be more bold and playful. Along with refining many of the existing colors with a brighter hue, we’re bringing a bit more variety to the color palette by introducing a new color: Red.

You might recognize some of these colors — they’re inspired by application features that you’re likely familiar with on Discord, such as Online, Away, and Do Not Disturb status messages. And while pink isn’t a direct correlation to an in-app color, it’s as equally playful and fun as the rest of ’em.

It’s a bit more lively. A little bit brighter. And hopefully, a bit more like home.

You can see the entire set of new colors over at discord.com/branding.

How This Affects Using Discord

When we say our new palette is inspired by using Discord on the day-to-day, that doesn’t mean these colors are strictly for our website or blog.

When you open up Discord next time, things might feel a bit brighter. We’ve got our logos and colors, along with some new typography and art on the login and registration pages.

Once you’re logged in, the changes will be more subtle. New Clyde will be welcoming you on the top-left, just as he always has, and all the colors will be just a bit bolder.

New typography will appear within certain headings throughout the app, but the majority of the headings and fonts will stay the same as they are today. As the year goes on, you may notice additional updates here and there, such as changes to illustrations in empty states and tooltips — we want to make sure they’re perfect first.

How Did The Community Help Out with These Changes?

Discord has become a place for millions around the world to create art, to karaoke nights and sharing plant care tips, speculate about cryptocurrencies, and on occasion, accidentally fall asleep because you’ve been up too late on voice.

When figuring out our new styles, we connected with over 26,000 members of the community to ask what Discord means to them. We got your feedback and direction on style, colors, and even some of the in-app phrasing.

Your feedback and guidance also helped us make sure our new colors are still readable in both Dark and Light themes. Because of this, you may notice that our in-app colors don’t perfectly match the ones you see in our marketing — we’ll continue to fine-tune them as time goes on.

It’s your influence that helped guide us while making changes both big and small, and we’re so grateful to have such dedicated and creative members of our community.

Imagine a Place Millions Call Home

We’re super excited (and just a tiny bit nervous) to unveil our new look today, on our 6th birthday. Around all our websites and social profiles, you’ll see a new phrase: Imagine a Place.

Imagine a Place is our new mantra that brings to life the fact that Discord means so many different things to so many people around the world. It’s a creation and collaboration with the community that we are proud of, and we hope you are too.

After all, that new place you’re imagining on Discord? It’s what you make of it.

Today’s just the beginning. Head on over to our YouTube channel where we’ll be celebrating our birthday with style. We’d love it if you stopped by to celebrate our new look (and birthday!) with us.

Our new look was crafted with your help, and we’d love your thoughts on how it turned out. You’re always welcome to shoot us a tweet at @discord. If your feedback doesn’t fit within a tweet, our feedback forum is always open.

There’s a lot more plans on the horizon. We’re glad you’re with us on this journey. <3

Game Servers

Discord’s Game Servers feature lets you transform your Server Boosts into dedicated game servers for popular titles, creating seamless multiplayer gaming experiences for your community.

Note: The Game Servers feature is currently an experiment and only available to select servers and users.

What this article covers:

  • What is the Game Servers Feature?
  • How to Create a Game Server
    • How to Use Server Boosts to Enable Game Servers as a Server Owner/Admin
    • How to Purchase a Game Server Directly
  • How to Manage Your Game Server Subscription
  • What to Know Before Joining Game Servers
    • How to Join a Server’s Game Server
    • How to Connect to Game Servers by Game
  • How to Modify a Game Server as a Server Owner/Admin
  • Frequently Asked Questions
    • Creating and Managing your Game Server
    • Billing and Subscriptions
    • Sharing and Gifting
    • Troubleshooting and Support

What is the Game Servers Feature?

Discord’s Game Servers feature lets you create dedicated game servers for popular titles — either by unlocking one for your whole community using Server Boosts, or by subscribing to your own directly in the Shop — creating seamless multiplayer gaming experiences for your community.

Note: While Game Servers can be set up and accessed through a Discord server, anyone with the game server’s IP address can join directly from the game, even if they’re not in the Discord server.

How to Create a Game Server

There are two ways to create a Game Server: unlock one for your whole community using Server Boosts, or subscribe to unlock your own directly in the Shop. Pick whichever fits how you want to play.

How to Use Server Boosts to Enable Game Servers as a Server Owner/Admin

The server owner or admin can use any available applied Server Boosts to unlock Game Servers.

Important: Game servers can’t be disabled within 7 days of creation.

Note: We regularly review and adjust the Boost requirements for perks, including Game Servers. If you remove a Boosting perk, the amount of Boosts required may be different if you want to reactivate it. The amount of Boosts required will always be clear before you activate a perk.

  1. With the correct server selected, navigate to the Server Boosts tab in the upper-left corner. Only server admins and owners can view this tab.
Example of Server Boosts tab in a server
  1. In the upper-right, you’ll see how many Server Boosts are available and recent activity of Server Boosts. If you have enough Server Boosts available, you can enable this perk right away.
Example of Available Server Boosts
  1. To apply Boosts to Game Servers, hover over the perk and press Create Game Server. A window will appear where you can configure your game server!
Create Game Server option

  1. From here, you can select which game you want for your server. You can also see the minimum Server Boost cost for each game.

  2. After selecting your game of choice, you can choose the following customizations for your game server setup:

  • Game server name: Pick a name that will help members identify this game server. If you plan to make multiple game servers for the same game, this will help distinguish them from each other.
  • Location: Pick a location to host your game server. Tip: locations closer to your players will have lower latency during gameplay.
  • Plan: Select the plan that works best for your desired gaming needs. Game Server plans are available in three tiers across all supported games:
    • Starter: Entry-level option, best for small groups or lightweight setups
    • Pro: Mid-tier plan with more resources for mods or larger player counts
    • Ultimate: Highest-tier plan with the most power and flexibility Tip: The Boost cost and server specs (like RAM and player slots, storage, and vCPUs) vary depending on the game and plan you choose.
  1. Select Enable Game Server to confirm your setup and create the game server.
Game server setup settings
  1. You’ll then see a confirmation message letting you know your game server has been set up!
Confirmation that your game server has been created
How to Purchase a Game Server Directly

Any Discord user can subscribe to unlock their own Game Server with a payment method on file, without needing a server’s Boosts.

Since you’ve subscribed to the Game Server, you’re fully in control of the game server management — including whether and with whom you share it. Keep it private for solo play, share it with a few friends, or post the link somewhere bigger; it’s entirely your call.

This is a good option if you want to game with friends outside of an existing Discord server, or if your server hasn’t unlocked Game Servers through Boosting.

Note: Each Discord user can subscribe to up to 5 active Game Server subscriptions at a time.

  1. Open the Shop, then select the Game Servers tab.

  2. Under “Start your own game server,” choose the game you want to host.

  3. In the Game server setup window, enter a name for your server, choose a location, and select a plan.

If you have an active Nitro subscription, you’ll see a discounted Nitro price for eligible plans in addition to the standard price.

  1. Press Continue, then choose your payment method and confirm your subscription purchase on the Checkout screen.

Note: Your Game Server may take up to an hour to become available, and you’ll see a confirmation once it’s ready.

  1. Once you’ve completed checkout and your payment is processed, your Game Server subscription is ready to go! You can manage your subscription anytime from the Game Servers tab in the Shop, or from User Settings > Subscriptions > Game Servers, and your Game Server subscription will renew on a monthly basis until you cancel.

  2. Once your Game Server is set up, you can share it with anyone — in a channel, a DM, or a group DM — using a shareable link. Selecting the link shows the server’s info so others can join, without needing to be in a shared Discord server with you.

How to Manage Your Game Server Subscription

Applies only to Game Servers you pay for directly — Boost-unlocked servers are still managed through How to Modify a Game Server as a Server Owner/Admin above.

  1. Open User Settings and go to the Subscriptions section.

  2. Find the Game Server subscription you want to manage.

Upgrading your plan:

  • If you upgrade to a higher plan, you’re charged a prorated amount immediately, and your Game Server is upgraded right away. Downgrading your plan:

  • If you downgrade, your Game Server stays on its current plan until your next renewal. At renewal, you’re charged the lower price and your Game Server is downgraded at that time. Canceling your subscription:

  • Canceling doesn’t stop your Game Server right away. You’ll keep access until the end of your current billing period, after which your server is spun down and we won’t charge you for any subsequent billing periods after you have cancelled. Important: Game Server payments are final and non-refundable.

If you encounter any technical issues with a Game Server subscription you’ve purchased, contact us at dis.gd/support.

Note: Game Server subscriptions can’t be gifted, and payment methods that don’t support refunds (like some prepaid or gift balances) can’t be used for these subscriptions.

What to Know Before Joining Game Servers

Game servers accessed through Discord are hosted by third-party providers and aren’t moderated by Discord. Without Discord’s standard safety features, you should take extra precautions to protect yourself in these external spaces.

Before You Join: Avoid joining servers hosted by people you don’t know and trust in real life or from well-known groups you trust. Be selective—these servers may have different safety features from those you’re used to on Discord, so your choice of which servers to join becomes your primary safety measure.

Protect Your Privacy: Refrain from sharing personal information like your real name, location, age, school, or contact details on game servers. Be especially cautious of anyone who tries to move conversations to other platforms, offers unexpected gifts or special treatment, or asks you to keep interactions secret. These are red flags for potentially harmful behavior that can escalate quickly in unmoderated spaces.

Use Available Safety Tools: Consider enabling any safety features the server offers like chat filters, allowlist controls, and moderation plugins. When creating your own server, use allowlist controls to limit access to known friends, enable moderation tools, and establish clear behavioral expectations from the start. Remember that these tools may differ from what you’re used to with Discord’s built-in protections.

Trust Your Instincts: If someone makes you uncomfortable, leave immediately. Your safety is more important than game progress, maintaining friendships, or avoiding awkwardness. It’s never your fault if someone acts inappropriately toward you. Report concerning behavior happening in the game server to the server admin if you trust them, or use the game host’s reporting system (like Shockbyte’s support form). If you see behavior that violates our Terms of Service or Community Guidelines happening on Discord, please report it directly to us.

Stay Alert: These servers exist outside Discord’s safety ecosystem, meaning the automatic detection systems and rapid response teams you might expect aren’t available. Maintain strong boundaries, be skeptical of unusual requests, and prioritize your wellbeing over gameplay.

How to Join a Game Server

Once created, game servers will appear in the new Game Servers tab at the top of your server. This tab becomes visible to all members after the first game server is set up. You can also join directly using a shared link, without needing to be in the associated Discord server.

  1. Navigate to the server you want to join the game server for and press on Game Servers.
Game Servers tab
  1. Select Join Game Server for the game server you’re wanting to join.
Join Game Server button
  1. Follow the steps listed in the instructions pop-up to join the Game Server!
Instructional steps on how to join a Game Server
How to Connect to Game Servers by Game

Once you’ve joined a Game Server, follow the steps for your specific game below to connect and start playing.

Palworld

  • Launch Palworld.

  • Choose Join Multiplayer Game.

  • Enter the IP:Port of the server.

  • Select Connect. Rust

  • Press F1 to open the in-game console.

  • Type client.connect <IP:Port> and press Enter. Enshrouded

  • In Steam: go to View → Game Servers → Favorites.

  • Select the + Add a Server button and enter the IP:Query Port.

  • The server will appear in Steam → Favorites and will show up in-game. 7 Days to Die

  • Launch the game and select Join a Game from the main menu.

  • Press Connect to IP.

  • Enter the IP before the colon, and the port after. Terraria

  • Launch Terraria, select the Multiplayer option, then select the Join via IP option.

  • From the character selection screen, either select a character you have previously made or make a new character.

  • Enter your Server’s IP address (this is the part before the colon) and your Server’s Port (this is the part after the colon). (Example: 000.00.00.000:0000)

  • Press Accept (or the Enter Key) to connect to your server. Valheim

  • Launch Valheim and select Start Game in the main menu.

  • Select the character you want to join your server on. If you haven’t made one yet, you’ll need to do this before continuing.

  • After selecting or creating your character, press Start.

  • Change to the Join Game tab, and then press the Add Server button.

  • Paste your server IP into the box that pops up, and press the Connect button.

  • After a brief moment, you will be prompted for your server password. You will need to get this password from your Discord Server Admin. Paste your server password into the box, then press Enter. Counter Strike 2

Tip: Currently, the recommended method for joining your Counter Strike 2 server is using the Steam favorites list.

  • In the Steam client, navigate to View > Game Servers.

  • Select Favorites, then press the + button.

  • Enter your server’s IP & port then press OK.

  • Select your server, then press Connect. Hytale

  • Open Hytale.

  • Select on Servers.

  • Press on Add Server.

  • Paste your server IP address, enter a server name and press Add Server.

  • Double click your server in the list to join. Stardew Valley

Tip: You can learn more about connecting to Stardew Valley by checking out this guide by ShockByte.

  • Open Stardew Valley.
  • Select the CO-OP button.
  • Select Join LAN Game.
  • Enter your Server IP and Port then click OK. Minecraft

For Java:

  • Launch Minecraft, then select Multiplayer.

  • Select Add Server, give the server a name, enter the server’s IP address, and press Done.

  • Back in the server list, find the new entry, then double-click it to connect. For Bedrock:

  • Launch Minecraft, then select Play.

  • Select Servers, then Add Server.

  • Enter a server name and the server’s IP address, then press Add and Play. Satisfactory

  • Launch Satisfactory and select the Server Manager button from the main menu.

  • Press Add Server.

  • Enter your server IP into the Address box, and port into the Port box, then press Confirm.

  • Select the newly added server from the list and press Join Game. Necesse

  • Launch Necesse.

  • Select Multiplayer.

  • Select Direct Join.

  • Enter your server’s IP address and port separately, then press Connect. V Rising

  • Press Play.

  • Press Online Play.

  • Press Show All Servers.

  • Press Direct Connect.

  • Enter your IP and port, then press Connect. Factorio

  • Launch Factorio.

  • Navigate to Multiplayer.

  • Select Connect to address.

  • Enter the server’s IP and press Connect. Vintage Story

  • Launch Vintage Story.

  • Select Multiplayer.

  • Select Add New Server.

  • Enter your server details. The server name in this section is just for your own reference and doesn’t need to match your actual server name.

  • Select your server to connect. RuneScape: Dragonwilds

  • Launch RuneScape: Dragonwilds.

  • Press Play.

  • Go to the Public tab and search for the server by name.

  • Press Enter World.

  • Enter the password if prompted. You can get this from your Discord Server Admin.

How to Modify a Game Server as a Server Owner/Admin

Once you’re an admin in the server, you can open the Game Servers tab to view your server and manage its settings.

Note: To modify or make changes to a Game Server’s settings, you will need Administrator permissions in that server.

  1. Navigate to the server that has the game server you want to modify and press on Game Servers.
Game Servers tab

  1. Select View Game Panel to open the Game Server’s options. The Game Panel is your control center for advanced game server management. This includes adjusting game configurations and customizing various server settings beyond what’s available on Discord.

  2. You’ll be redirected to a web browser where you’ll need to log into Discord and authorize Shockbyte to sign into their app. Each game server has its own independent Game Panel with settings specific to that game server. You can learn more about navigating the Game Panel from Shockbyte’s website.

Important: For any questions about Game Panel features, settings, or technical issues within the panel itself, please use the Contact Us button within the Game Panel to reach Shockbyte’s specialized support team
Game Server panel

Frequently Asked Questions

This FAQ is divided into sections:

  • Creating and Managing your Game Server
  • Billing and Subscriptions
  • Sharing and Gifting
  • Troubleshooting and Support
Creating and Managing your Game Server

Q: How many Game Servers can be created in one Discord server?

A: You can have a maximum of 10 Game Servers per Discord server.

Q: Do I need extra Boosts to unlock Game Servers for my server?

A: Game Servers are a separate feature from your server’s Boost level. Boosts used to level up your server do not count toward unlocking Game Servers. To enable Game Servers, you’ll need to apply Boosts specifically toward creating a game server. Once a game server is created, the Game Servers tab will appear in your server.

Q: How many Boosts does it cost to create a Game Server?

A: The number of Boosts required depends on the game and plan you choose. The least expensive option starts at 3 Boosts, with certain games and higher-tier plans requiring more. All Boosts allocated go directly toward that game server, there’s no extra Boost cost just to unlock the feature.

Q: What happens to my game server if I no longer have the Server Boosts to maintain it?

A: If you do not apply the necessary Server Boosts to maintain the server, the Game Server will be deleted after 3 days.

Q: How can I disable my game server?

A: As a server admin or owner, head to the Server Boosts tab > View Game Servers and then press Disable Perk under the specific game server you want to disable.

Billing and Subscriptions

Q: What’s the difference between using Server Boosts and paying directly for a Game Server?

A: With Server Boosts, a server owner or admin unlocks a Game Server for their whole community using Boosts already applied to the server. Signing up through the Shop lets any Discord user subscribe to create a Game Server with their own payment method and share it with whoever they choose, without needing a server’s Boosts.

Q: Do I need Nitro to pay for a Game Server directly?

A: No. Anyone can pay the standard price for a Game Server. If you have an active Nitro subscription, you’ll see a discounted Nitro price on eligible plans.

Q: Can I get a refund for my Game Server subscription?

A: No, Game Server payments are final and non-refundable.

If you encounter any technical issues with a Game Server subscription you’ve purchased, contact us at dis.gd/support.

Q: What happens when I upgrade my Game Server plan?

A: You’re charged a prorated amount right away, and your Game Server is upgraded immediately.

Q: What happens when I downgrade my Game Server plan?

A: Nothing changes right away. At your next renewal, you’re charged the lower price and your Game Server is downgraded at that time.

Q: How many Game Servers can I subscribe to directly?

A: Each Discord user can have up to 5 active Game Server subscriptions at a time.

Sharing and Gifting

Q: Can I gift a Game Server subscription to someone else?

A: No, Game Server subscriptions can’t be gifted.

Q: Can I share a Game Server I subscribed to with people outside of a Discord server?

A: Yes. You can share your Game Server using a shareable link in a channel, DM, or group DM, and others can view its info and join without needing to share a Discord server with you.

Troubleshooting and Support

Q: What does the current game server’s status mean?

Server Status of a Game Server

A: Depending on the state of the server, you may see a variety of different Server Statuses. Here are all of the available Server Statuses:

  • Online: Server is online and available to join.
  • Offline: Admin manually stopped the server.
  • Sleeping: Server is in hibernation (≥7 days of no activity).
  • Starting: Server is in the process of coming online or restarting. This can take a few minutes.
  • Startup Failed: Configuration is required. An admin of the server must visit the Game Panel to change the configuration.
  • Missing Stock: Server location is out of capacity. An admin of the server must select a new location in the Game Panel to resolve.
  • Unavailable: Other error. An admin of the server can visit the Game Panel for more information.
  • Unknown Error: An admin of the server will need to reach out to Shockbyte support to resolve this issue.
  • Deleted: Server is in the process of being deleted. Once deleted, it will disappear from view. Q: Why can’t I create a Game Server right now?

A: New Game Servers may not always be available to create, for example during high demand or while this feature is still an experiment.

If you see a message saying new Game Servers can’t be created right now, check back later.

Q: I need help with my Game Server that I created, who can I reach out to?

A: If you’re an admin of the server, you can reach out to Shockbyte directly through one of the following ways:

For Game Server issues:

  1. Go to the Game Servers tab in your Discord server

  2. Press 3 dots [] next to your game server

  3. Select Get Support to be directed to the appropriate support channel

Get Support option

For Game Panel issues:

  1. Navigate to Game Servers tab > View Game Panel

  2. Press Get Support from the left sidebar within the panel

Get Support option

Important: Discord Support can help with updating your game server information within the app and other in-app functions, but extensive, technical inquiries must be forwarded to Shockbyte Support.

gg sans: Font Update FAQ

gg sans: Discord’s New, Custom Font

Starting December 1, 2022, Discord will begin updating the font across all of its surfaces to our new, custom font, gg sans. Everything from the Discord mobile and desktop apps to our website and blog will use gg sans as their typeface. This change gives Discord the flexibility to customize our font going forward so that we can continuously provide you with the best experience on Discord.

The meaning behind gg sans

gg sans highlights one of our favorite characters in our new typeface, the lowercase “g”, and is an ode to our gaming origins. ‘gg’ is an abbreviation for ‘good game’ and is frequently used on our platform. It’s also baked into the foundation of our company, using discord.gg in any of our shared links.

FAQ

Q: What do I need to do to get the new font?

A: Discord will start to change the font across its surfaces on December 1, 2022. You should see the new font across Discord in the weeks following this date. For the Discord desktop and mobile apps, you may need to refresh the app or make sure your app is updated to the latest version to see the change. For the website, no action is required on your part.

Q: Can I use the custom font for my own projects?

A: gg sans is not currently an open-source font, so you are not able to use it at this time.

Halloween Event 2026 FAQ

Note: This sound pack is available on desktop and browser only. This event was sadly too eerie for iOS and Android at this time. 👻

Another year - another ghostly Halloween! We’ll be exchanging our normal Discord call tone for something eerier. So grab a fiend or friend and give them a call, or have them call you!

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How long will this sound pack be available?

A: The Halloween ringtone will be available from October 7, 2026 - November 2, 2026.

Q: Where can I enable this sound pack?

A: The Halloween sound pack should be available automatically at 10:00AM PST.

If you’ve disabled the Halloween sound pack, you can re-enable it. Go to User Settings > Notifications. Then, under Sounds, toggle on Enable Halloween Sound Pack.

Halloween Event Sound Pack in Notifications Settings

Q: Will this be available on all devices and clients?

A: The Halloween sound pack will be available on our desktop and browser clients. This event was sadly too eerie for iOS and Android at this time. 👻

Q: Can I disable this ringtone and revert back to the default ringtone?

A: For desktop and browser users, you’ll be able to go to User Settings > Notifications. Then, under Sounds, toggle off Enable Halloween Sound Pack. Your sounds will return to Discord’s default.

How to Toggle Event Sound Pack Off in Notifications Settings

Q: Can I download this sound pack?

A: Sadly, there is no downloadable file for the ringtone and is only available in-client until November 2, 2026.

Mobile Visual Refresh: What’s Changing

Discord’s mobile app has a new visual refresh that brings it closer in line with the desktop experience, including updated themes, new shapes, and a decluttered chat bar.

What this article covers:

  • New Themes: Ash and Onyx
  • Updated Device Theme Syncing
  • Nitro Video Call Tile Colors
  • New Shapes: Circles and Squircles
  • Updated Chat Bar
  • Frequently Asked Questions

New Themes: Ash and Onyx

The Ash theme, the original dark theme longtime users know, is back on mobile with improved contrast to meet modern accessibility standards. All four base themes from desktop (Light, Ash, Dark, and Onyx) are now available on mobile.

Onyx, previously known as Midnight on mobile, uses a true black background to match the desktop version. On OLED screens, this can help save battery. You can fine-tune contrast and saturation in your Accessibility settings.

  1. Select Settings.

  2. Select Appearance.

  3. Go to Theme and select your desired theme.

Selecting a theme in Settings > Appearance > Theme

Updated Device Theme Syncing

You can now choose which Light theme and which Dark theme are used when your device switches between Light and Dark mode, instead of being limited to the built-in Light and Dark themes.

  1. Select Settings.

  2. Select Appearance.

  3. Turn on Same as Device Theme.

  4. Choose the Light theme and Dark theme you’d like to use with each device mode.

Turning on Same as Device Theme

Note: Turning on Same as Device Theme takes priority over Sync Across Devices.

Nitro Video Call Tile Colors

Nitro members’ voice and video call tiles now match their profile color on both desktop and mobile.

To change your call tile color, select the You tab, select Edit Profile, and update your Profile Theme.

Updating your Profile Theme

New Shapes: Circles and Squircles

Shapes across the mobile app now follow a consistent shape rule: people are circles, and things are squircles (rounded-corner shapes).

  • You, your friends, and bots in your direct messages (DMs) appear as circles.
  • DMs and group DMs stay as circles.
  • Servers and apps appear as squircles, including in your server list.
Friends, DMs, and group DMs appear as circles; servers and apps appear as squircles.

Updated Chat Bar

The chat bar has been decluttered to make more room for writing a message. Some actions have moved:

  • Still in the chat bar: Emoji, Gift, Voice Message, and other quick actions.
  • Moved into the + menu: Threads, using an App,
  • New shortcut: long-press the + icon to jump directly to an action without opening the full menu.
Using the + menu and long-press shortcut to create a thread

Tip: If you use Apps or Threads often, try the long-press shortcut to save an extra tap.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I still quickly access Threads, Polls, Apps, or file attachments?

A: Yes! Select the + icon to find them, or long-press the + icon to jump straight to your most-used action.

Q: Will my theme change automatically based on my device settings?

A: Only if you turn on Same as Device Theme in your Appearance settings. If it’s off, your selected theme stays the same, no matter what mode your device is in.

Q: Does the Onyx/Midnight theme still help save battery?

A: Yes! Onyx (previously called Midnight on mobile) uses a true black background on OLED-compatible devices, which can help save battery.

Nitro 2-Week Trial Offer

Try two weeks of Nitro for $0 with our promotion valid through January 29, 2026! Read below to learn more.

What this article covers:

  • Promotion Summary
    • Eligibility Conditions
  • What is Discord Nitro?
  • How do Nitro Trials work?
  • How do I claim my Nitro Trial?
    • On Desktop/Browser
    • On Mobile
  • Frequently Asked Questions Note: Please make sure your Discord app is updated to the latest version! If you don’t see the promotion offer in your app after you update, you are not eligible for this promotion.

Promotion Summary

Offer Details: Eligible users can enjoy a 2-week trial of Discord Nitro on us when you subscribe to Nitro (Monthly or Yearly) on Discord’s desktop, browser, or mobile app.

  • Your trial begins as soon as you sign up for a Nitro plan. You will not be charged until your trial ends.
Eligibility Conditions

Eligibility requirements include:

  • You have not had an active Nitro subscription (Nitro, Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, including trials) within the 30 days prior to the date you attempted to claim this promotion.

  • You have not received a Nitro trial or discount offer in the past 45 days.

  • You have not redeemed a Nitro trial or discount in the past 90 days.

  • You do not have an active Server Boost subscription.

  • You must maintain a valid payment method on your account. Note that eligibility on mobile depends on your device and subscription history:

  • Android users are eligible if they meet the other requirements and have not subscribed to Nitro in the past 30 days.

  • iOS users are eligible if they meet the other requirements, have previously subscribed to Nitro through Apple, and have not subscribed in the past 30 days. Regional availability: This promotion is only available in certain regions. If you do not see the promotion offer in your app, you are not eligible for this promotion.

Deadline for Claiming Promo: This promotion must be claimed before January 29, 2026 at 5pm PT.

What is Discord Nitro?

Discord Nitro is our subscription plan that unlocks a world of perks that’ll make your time on Discord as fun as ever! Personalize and enhance your experience with popular perks like HD streaming, 500MB file uploads, profile and avatar customizations, and more:

  • Custom & Animated Emojis
  • Custom Profiles
  • HD Streaming
  • Discord App Color Themes
  • Unlimited Soundboard Access & Entry Sounds
  • Extended Quest Rewards
  • Special Shop Perks
  • More Nitro & Nitro Basic perks

How do Nitro Trials work?

  • Nitro Trial periods are free. You’ll be asked to add a credit card when you redeem a trial, but you will not be charged until the trial ends.
  • For the Nitro 2-week trial, your card will be charged after the two week period unless you cancel beforehand. You can cancel at any time during the trial and you will not be charged. Learn more about cancelling Nitro here.
  • Your subscription will automatically renew at the end of the trial period as a paid plan based on the option you selected (monthly or annual).

How do I claim my Nitro Trial?

If you’re eligible to claim this Nitro offer, you’ll want to head over to the Nitro Tab.

On Desktop/Browser

Step 1: Go to the Nitro tab

On the desktop or browser app, press the Direct Messages button in the top left corner and then select the Nitro tab. Alternatively, you can navigate to your User Settings > Nitro.

Step 2: Subscribe to Nitro Monthly or Yearly

Once you are on the Nitro page - press Claim Offer on the trial banner.

Nitro 2-Week Trial Offer on Desktop

Step 3: Start Your 2-Week Trial

You’ll be asked to select either a monthly or yearly plan for Nitro.

Then, on the next screen, enter your credit card information and other payment details.

Nitro payment page for 2-week trial on Desktop

Step 4: Start Your 2-Week Trial

Upon successful completion of sign up, your account will be upgraded to Nitro and your 2-week trial will begin! At the end of your 2-week trial, your paid subscription will begin based on the plan you selected.

On Mobile

  1. To get started on mobile, tap on your avatar in the bottom right corner.

  2. Select the Nitro button in the upper right to navigate to the Nitro page. Alternatively, tap the Settings icon and navigate to the Get Nitro page.

Mobile App: Avatar Icon (Upper) and Nitro Button (Lower)
  1. Sign up for Nitro by tapping the Claim Offer.

NOTE: If you don’t have any existing payment methods, you’ll be prompted to enter your payment information.

  1. Review the details, then tap Claim Offer to start your trial.
Nitro 2-Week Trial Offer on Mobile
  1. Once you’ve successfully signed up, your trial will begin.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why don’t I see this offer in my Discord app?

A: If you don’t see any promotion details on your Nitro tab across the desktop, browser, or mobile apps, it is because you do not meet the eligibility criteria.

Q: What happens if I have an active Server Boosting subscription?

A: If you have an active Server Boost subscription, you will not be able to claim and redeem this promotion.

Note: if you don’t see the trial on your mobile device, head over to the Nitro page on desktop to check for availability.

Q: Why do I need to submit my payment info to redeem Nitro?

A: Because Nitro is a subscription, at the end of your 2-week trial, we will start your first billing cycle so you can continue to enjoy Nitro.

However, you can cancel Nitro at any time, including during trial. To cancel Nitro on desktop, head to your User Settings > select Subscriptions > press Cancel within the Nitro banner. To cancel Nitro on mobile, tap on the cogwheel [] in the top right > Billing Settings > Manage Nitro. From here, follow the prompts on the screen until the cancellation is confirmed. You may also cancel your subscription through your mobile device app store.

Note: You will not be charged until the trial ends and the membership renews. We’ll send an email before the paid membership begins, and you’ll have the opportunity to cancel before you are charged by following the steps here.

Q: Why do I see a temporary hold/charge on my account when this is supposed to be a trial?

A: There is no charge for this 2-week Nitro trial. However, there will be a temporary hold placed on the payment method upon activating the promotion. This is to help Discord confirm that the submitted payment method is valid. This charge will appear in your Discord transaction history, and it may appear as a hold on your payment method.

After you redeem the trial offer, we reverse the temporary hold to return the funds, and you’ll see that reflected in your Discord transaction history. Your bank may take longer to remove the hold from your payment method.

Note: Banks will usually remove the temporary hold from your account within a few business days.

If your Discord transaction history does not show the hold released after 5 business days, please let us know at dis.gd, and our support team will be able to investigate this issue further.

Q: If I have Nitro Credit, can I still claim the 2-week Nitro trial offer?

A: Yes, if you have Nitro Credit, you are still eligible to claim the trial offer if you meet all other eligibility criteria. Your Nitro Credit will automatically activate after your 2-week trial, before your paid subscription begins. If you have more questions about Nitro Credit, learn more here.

Server Subscriptions for Creators & Server Owners/Admins

Are you a creator and interested in learning more about Server Subscriptions for your server? You can check out the Server Subscription for Creators article in the Creator Support Help Center!

Server Tags

Represent your server with Server Tags - 4-character identifiers that members can display proudly on their profiles, anywhere.

What this article covers:

  • What are Server Tags?
  • How to Use Server Boosts for Server Tags as a Server Owner/Admin
  • How to Select or Customize Your Server Tag as a Server Owner/Admin
  • How to Set or Remove a Server Tag as a Server Member
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • What are Server Tag Badge Packs?
    • How to Purchase Server Tag Badge Packs
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are Server Tags?

Example of a Server Tag

A Server Tag allows members of a server to represent that server everywhere on Discord! A Server Tag is a custom, 4-character label paired with an icon. While not unique to each server, it lets members proudly display a shared identity on their Custom Profile. A server owner or admin can use 3 Server Boosts to unlock a Server Tag for their community. This additional perk is separate from Boost Levels, so your server doesn’t need to reach a specific Boost Level to access it.

How to Use Server Boosts to Unlock Server Tags as a Server Owner/Admin

The server owner or admin can use any available applied Server Boosts to unlock Server Tags.

  1. With the correct server selected, navigate to the Server Boosts tab in the upper-left corner. Only server admins and owners can view this tab.
Example of Server Boosts tab in a server
  1. In the upper-right, you’ll see how many Server Boosts are available and recent activity of Server Boosts. If you have 3 Server Boosts available, you can enable this perk right away.
Example of Available Server Boosts
  1. To apply boosts to Server Tags, hover over the perk and press Enable Perk. A window will appear where you can configure your newly unlocked perk!
Enable Perk Server Tag

How to Select or Customize Your Server Tag as a Server Owner/Admin

Info: If you update the Server Tag for your server, server members will have to reapply the tag again for the change to take effect.

If a Server Tag is unlocked for your server, you can set or change your Server Tag.

  1. Select your server’s name in the upper-left corner and then press Server Settings.
Server Settings option
  1. Press Server Tag to access all available settings. Here you can edit the following:
  • Server Tag name (can use up to 4 characters that are alphanumeric and certain special characters)
  • Badge
  • Color
Setting or customizing your server’s Server Tag

How to Set or Remove a Server Tag from your Profile as a Server Member

You can set or remove a Server Tag from your profile using desktop, browser, and mobile.

Desktop/Browser

  1. Select the cogwheel [] next to your Discord username to access your User Settings.

  2. Press Profiles or select Edit User Profile to customize your profile.

Profiles tab under User Settings
  1. Scroll down until you see Server Tag. Here, you can see all available tags by pressing Select. Pick your favorite and your settings will be saved automatically.
Server Tag selection box on desktop/browser
  1. To remove a tag, press X next to the currently applied tag.
X button located next to Server Tag on desktop/browser

Mobile

  1. Tap on your avatar in the bottom-right corner of the app.

  2. Press Edit Profile.

Example of where to find the Edit Profile option on mobile
  1. Scroll down until you see Server Tags and select which one you’d like to apply. The settings will be applied automatically.
Currently set Server Tag under User Profile on mobile

How to Join a Server Through Server Tag

By viewing another user’s profile and tapping on their currently displayed Server Tag, you can view a Server’s Profile. By viewing the Server Profile you can learn more about the server and also select Join Server to join. If a server has Server Member Applications, you can fill out an application to the server.

What are Server Tag Badge Packs?

Important: To be able to purchase additional Server Tag Badge Packs, you first need to purchase Server Tags.

Server Tag badge Packs

Server Tag Badge Packs allow you to unlock additional badges for your server. You can choose between the following:

  • Creepy Crawlies Badge Pack (2 Server Boosts)
  • Pet Badge Pack (3 Server Boosts)
  • Plant Badge Pack (3 Server Boosts)
  • Flex Badge Pack (5 Server Boosts) Please keep in mind that while you can unlock both badge packs using Boosts, only one badge can be applied to your Server Tag at a time.

How to Purchase Server Tag Badge Packs

The server owner or admin can use any available Server Boosts to unlock Server Tags.

  1. With the correct server selected, navigate to the Server Boosts tab in the upper-left corner. Only server admins and owners can view this tab.
Example of Server Boosts tab in a server
  1. In the upper-right, you’ll see how many Server Boosts are available and recent activity of Server Boosts. If you have the Server Boosts available, you can enable either pack right away.
Example of Available Server Boosts
  1. To apply Boosts to Server Tag Badge Packs, press on View Packs and then select which pack you want to purchase. You’ll see a confirmation window once the purchase has been successful. Now you can edit your Server Tag with one of your new badges!
Enable Perk Server Tag

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How many characters can I use in a Server Tag?

A: Server Tags are non-unique, 4-character tags that can consist of alphanumerical characters and certain special characters.

Q: Do Server Tags need to be unique across Discord?

A: No, Server Tags don’t have to be unique across the platform. Different servers can use the same tag, though the combination of the tag and icon will help distinguish your community.

Q: What happens to members’ profiles if our server loses the Server Tag perk?

A: If your server loses the Server Tag perk due to insufficient boosts, the tag will no longer be available for members to wear on their profile. Any members who had the tag applied will have it automatically removed from their profiles.

Q: Can I change our Server Tag after it’s been created?

A: Yes, server owners and admins can change the Server Tag at any time. However, when you update a Server Tag, members will need to manually reapply the new tag to their profiles.

Q: Can server members customize the color of the Server Tag on their profile?

A: No, the color of the Server Tag is set by the server owner/admin and remains consistent for all members who use it.

Q: How many Server Tags can a user display on their profile at once?

A: Users can display only one Server Tag on their profile at a time, even if they belong to multiple servers with tags.

Q: Can I restrict which members can use our Server Tag?

A: Currently, there’s no way to restrict which members can use the Server Tag. Any member of your server can choose to display it on their profile.

Q: Do Server Tags appear in messages or just on profiles?

A: Server Tags that are applied to a user’s profile will appear next to their name everywhere on Discord. This includes in chat, member lists, and Direct Messages lists.

Q: Can I include emoji or special characters in a Server Tag?

A: Server Tags can consist of alphanumerical characters and certain special characters. Certain characters, spaces, and emojis are not supported at this time.

Q: Can my server have multiple Server Tags?

A: No, each server can only have one Server Tag at a time. If you want to change your server’s tag, you’ll need to update the existing one rather than creating additional tags. Remember that when you update your Server Tag, members will need to reapply the new tag to their profiles.

Q: Will other users be able to click on my Server Tag to join the server?

A: Yes, selecting a Server Tag will open the Server Profile for that server. If applications are enabled, they can apply to join the server from the server profile.

Q: Can I use current Server Boosts on my server for Server Tags?

A: If you are a server admin or owner and you have 3 Server Boosts already available for your server to use, then you can enable Server Tags right away. If you don’t have enough Server Boosts available, you may need to change your current Server Level or get more Boosts from your community.

Q: What happens if I edit or change my current Server Tag in my server?

A: If you update the Server Tag for your server, server members will have to reapply the tag again for the change to take effect.

Q: Is there a rate limit for how many times I can change my server tag once it is set?

A: Yes, there is a rate limit for changing your server tag. You can change your server tag after a certain period of time.

Q: What are “additional perks” and how are they different from Levels?

A: Additional perks are new features you can unlock directly with Boosts, separate from your server’s Boost Level. Currently, there are two available: Enhanced Role Styles (which add gradient and holographic effects to roles) and Server Tags (4-character identifiers members can display on their profiles across Discord). Unlike traditional server levels, these perks can be unlocked individually without reaching specific level thresholds.

Q: How much do the new Additional Perks cost?

A: Enhanced Role Styles and Server Tags each cost 3 Boosts. If you want both perks, you’ll need 6 Boosts total (3 for each perk).

Q: Are Additional Perks replacing the current server level system?

A: No, this supplements the existing level system. All current server level perks (emoji slots, file upload limits, etc.) remain exactly the same. This new system simply gives you additional ways to use your Boosts for targeted perks without affecting your server’s level progression.

Q: Do Additional Perks use separate Boosts from my server level?

A: Yes, Boosts used for Additional Perks are dedicated specifically to those perks and don’t count toward your server’s level progression. Similarly, Boosts allocated to your server level can’t be used for Additional Perks. You’ll need separate Boosts for each - so if you want Enhanced Role Styles, you need 3 Boosts just for that perk, plus whatever Boosts you want to maintain your current server level.

Q: What happens to my Additional Perks if my server loses Boosts?

A: Perks require ongoing Boost allocation to remain active. If your server drops below the required number of Boosts for a perk, that perk will be disabled. Enhanced Role Styles will revert to solid colors, and Server Tags will be removed from members’ profiles. Server owners/admins can choose which perks to maintain if Boost counts drop.

Q: Why can’t I unlock perks even though I have enough Boosts?

A: Make sure you’re accessing the Server Boost tab (visible only to server owners/admins) and that your Boosts are “available” rather than already allocated to your server level. Only server members with admin permissions can unlock Additional Perks. You need to have enough unallocated Boosts to enable Additional Perks.

Q: Can I move Boosts between levels and perks after I’ve allocated them?

A: Yes, server owners and admins can reallocate Boosts between server levels and Additional Perks through the Server Boosts tab. However, if you move Boosts away from a perk, that perk will be disabled until you allocate enough Boosts back to it.

Q: Are Additional Perks a one-time purchase, or do they require ongoing Boosts?

A: Each additional perk requires an ongoing allocation of its required Boosts to stay active, just like levels. If your server drops below the required number of Boosts, the perk will be disabled until the necessary Boosts are reallocated.

Q: Can I purchase and manage Additional Perks from both desktop and mobile?

A: Additional Perks can currently only be purchased and configured on desktop.

Update on Premium Services in Russia

What this article covers:

  • Recurring Memberships
    • Nitro
    • Boosting
    • Gifting and Gift Redemptions
    • Refunds

Purchases and recurring subscriptions for our paid services in Russia have been suspended. We are also no longer accepting Russian payment methods. We will continue to offer the free Discord experience to all users, including those in Russia.

Recurring Memberships

If you are located in Russia or use a Russian payment method, your membership will remain active for the remainder of your current billing period. After that, your membership will end and you will not be charged again. You will still be able to remove your payment methods and cancel your membership; however, you won’t be able to start any new memberships until further notice.

Nitro

You will keep Nitro or Nitro Classic perks until your next monthly or annual billing period. After that, your membership will end and you will not be able to purchase a new Nitro plan until further notice.

Boosting

Servers you have boosted will keep those boosts until your next billing period. After that, your Boosting membership will end, and your boosts will be removed from those servers. You will not be able to purchase new boosts until further notice.

Gifting and Gift Redemptions

If you are located in Russia or use a Russian payment method, you will be unable to purchase, redeem, or access gifted items, including Nitro membership of all tiers as well as Shop gifts, until further notice.

Any unredeemed gifts will remain in your Gift Inventory, but you will be unable to access them at this time.

Please note: If someone offers to donate, trade, or sell you a gift membership, you will not be able to redeem it. If you think it might be a scam, please report the message to our Trust & Safety team.
Refunds

At this time, we are unable to guarantee that refunds can be successfully processed in Russia or for Russian payment methods. Please note that all recurring membership will not renew and you will not be charged for your next billing cycle.

If you have questions, you can always contact our support team here:(http://dis.gd/billing).
