Safer Ways to Shop on Discord

Looking for safer ways to buy Discord Nitro and other premium features? Learn how to protect your account and payment information by purchasing through official Discord channels only.

From accessing Nitro perks to enjoying premium features, ensuring your purchases are made through authorized platforms is key to protecting your Discord account.

Purchases from unauthorized sellers can potentially lead to revoked purchases or compromised personal and payment information. This article will help you understand the official ways to purchase Discord products and stay safer while enjoying all that Discord has to offer.

What this article covers:

  • Official Ways to Buy or Receive Discord Products
  • What Can You Do If You Suspect You’ve Been Scammed?
    • How to Stay Informed to Stay Safer
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Official Ways to Buy or Receive Discord Products

The more secure way to purchase Nitro or other Discord products is directly through Discord or our official Amazon store (available in select countries).

Here’s how you can purchase or receive Nitro and other products on Discord:

  • Direct Purchase: Buy Nitro and Server Boosts through the Nitro Tab in your Direct Messages List or under User Settings > Billing Settings
  • Gift Inventory: Check and manage your purchased or received Nitro gifts within the app. Gifts sent through Discord can only be redeemed on the platform. Learn how to more securely claim a Nitro gift in our Nitro Gifting FAQ.
  • Profile Purchases: Customize your experience by purchasing Profile Cosmetics and Effects through the Shop Tab in your Direct Messages List or under User Settings > Profile
  • Share Nitro Program: As a subscription perk for Nitro subscribers, you can share three 2-week trial passes with friends who don’t already have Nitro. This official program is a more secure way to spread the fun. For more details, check out our Share Nitro article.
  • Quests and Promotions: We’re proud of Nitro and want you to experience it firsthand! That’s why we regularly offer opportunities to try it before buying. Check out our Quests & Promotions page to see all current offers. If you ever encounter a promotion or offer for Nitro, make sure it comes from one of the trusted sources outlined above. Avoid clicking on suspicious links or interacting with third-party sellers offering discounts or giveaways.

Discord’s premium products can only be purchased directly through the Discord app or our official Amazon store (available in select countries). Buying Discord Nitro or other official products from unauthorized sources puts you at risk of scams.

What Can You Do If You Suspect You’ve Been Scammed?

If you suspect you’ve been scammed or purchased Discord products from an unauthorized seller:

  1. Contact Support: Reach out to our support team at dis.gd for assistance.

  2. Report Fraud: Report the issue at dis.gd to help us take action against scammers.

Please note that Discord cannot mediate financial disputes or issue refunds for purchases made through unauthorized third-party sellers.

How to Stay Informed to Stay Safer

Scammers are constantly looking for ways to exploit users. Always double-check that your purchases and gifts come from the official Discord sources described in this article. For more guidance on avoiding scams, check out these resources:

  • Understanding and Avoiding Common Scams
  • Deceptive Practices Policy Explainer
  • Claiming a Nitro Gift FAQ
  • Shop FAQ
  • Server Boosting FAQ By staying vigilant and following these tips, you can enjoy Discord’s premium features with peace of mind.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do you identify a third-party seller?

A: Third-party sellers are unauthorized individuals or websites that offer Discord products at discounted prices or through unofficial channels. These sellers often advertise through unsolicited messages, social media, or unofficial websites. To identify them, look for offers that require external payments, unusual URLs, or methods that don’t involve the Discord app or official Amazon store. Remember: if it’s not from a Discord source described in this article, it’s not official.

Q: What does a phishing attempt look like?

A: Phishing attempts often appear as fake messages or links designed to trick you into providing sensitive information, like your login credentials or payment details. Common signs include:

  • Messages claiming you’ve won or received free products or rewards, like Nitro, but requiring you to click a suspicious link.
  • Threats to your account status unless you take immediate action.
  • Requests for your password, account login, or personal information. Discord will never ask for your login details or for your payment information through unsolicited messages. Always verify links and contact Discord support directly if you’re unsure.

Q: What are safer messaging practices to avoid unsolicited scams?

A: To protect yourself from unsolicited messages and scams:

  • Avoid engaging with messages from unknown users, especially those offering deals or rewards.
  • Enable Safer Direct Messaging under User Settings > Privacy & Safety to automatically scan DMs from non-friends for harmful content.
  • Report suspicious messages or users by following the steps outlined here.
  • Never click on links from untrusted sources. Even if they appear to come from someone you know, accounts can be compromised. If you ever need to verify if a source is a legitimate Discord source or not, you can reach out to the Discord support team.

Information for Users in Japan

Overview: This page provides important information in accordance with Japan’s Specified Commercial Transactions Act. Discord is committed to transparency and helping users in Japan understand their rights and the terms of any purchases made through our service.

Payment and Delivery: Accepted payment methods vary by region but typically include credit cards, PayPal, or app store purchases (such as Apple in-app purchases or Google Play store purchases).

For one-time purchases, payment is processed immediately. For subscriptions (such as Discord Nitro), payments are recurring and are charged at the beginning of each billing cycle. You can manage or cancel your subscription at any time from your user settings.

Once payment is successfully processed, the service is typically provided immediately. Subscriptions remain active until canceled by the user, and users will retain access to subscription benefits until the end of their then-current billing cycle.

Unauthorized Transactions Suspension FAQ

Abusing or defrauding Discord or our payment system violates our Terms of Service.

When we receive a fraud report from a payment method owner regarding a purchase made on Discord, we take that seriously. These reports indicate that the transaction was reported as unauthorized or unrecognized.

In response, we may suspend your account to protect our platform from potential abuse, fraud, or misuse of our payment systems. This is done in line with our responsibility to maintain a safe and secure environment for all users.

If your account has already been suspended for this violation, you can appeal by submitting a request to Discord’s Trust & Safety Team at dis.gd/request.

What this article covers:

  • How do I appeal an unauthorized transaction suspension?
  • How can I avoid an unauthorized transaction in the future?
  • For More Information

How do I appeal an unauthorized transaction suspension?

If you believe this action was taken in error, you can submit an appeal within 48 hours of receiving the suspension notice.

To appeal a suspension, follow the steps below:

  1. Visit dis.gd

  2. Select Appeals & Age Update Requests as the request type from the “How can we help?” dropdown menu

  3. In the “What would you like to appeal?” section, select An action taken on my account.

  4. Include one of the following with your appeal:

  • A screenshot of your most recent Discord transaction(s) from your billing statement
    • Please ensure the screenshot displays the amount and date of transaction along with the descriptor.
  • OR, A photo of the card (physical or virtual) used on Discord
    • All digits must be obscured except the last 4
    • Include a note in the photo showing your full Discord username and the current date Important: If you’re not the cardholder, the person who owns the payment method must withdraw all open fraud report requests within 48 hours to restore account access.

How can I avoid an unauthorized transaction in the future?

Only use payment methods that you are authorized to use.

Before submitting a fraud report to Discord, we recommend:

  • Reviewing your Discord account(s) to make sure the charges are not on an account you own
  • Or reaching out to any family members who you may have previously authorized to use your payment method/card If you notice any unauthorized charge(s) on your Discord account, please refer to our Reporting Unauthorized Discord Transactions article for more information.

Bug Reporting

Discord Bugs

What this article covers:

  • What is a Bug?
  • How do I Report a Bug?
  • What is Discord Testers?

What is a Bug?

Bugs are unintended behavior of the Discord app that diminish a user’s experience.

Think of the app crashing unexpectedly, or the “Add Friends to DM” button not letting you add your friends into a Group DM when you haven’t reached the limit!

How do I Report a Bug?

When issues pop up that negatively impact Discord users, we want to be able to understand and fix it as soon as possible. Any user can help us by reporting the bugs!

Bug reports should be submitted with a ticket to the Bug Reporting form. Be sure to fill out each field, as each is important.

The most helpful bug reports include:

  • A concise description of the bug, generally one sentence
  • Simple step by step direction on how to make the bug occur
  • Explanation of what you believe the behavior should be
  • What is actually happening
  • What version of Discord this occurs on
  • What device the bug occurs on There are some bug reports that are not currently supported. We ask that you check out this Unsupported Reports article before submitting a bug report, to familiarize yourself with what topics are unsupported.

Additionally, if you’re experiencing a bug related to Accessibility aka (A11Y), these issues can also be submitted via our Bug Reporting form.

What is Discord Testers?

Announcement: Thanks for your interest in the Discord Testers Consideration Quiz. The quiz is currently closed, but we’ll share an update on this page when the next opportunity opens!

Discord Testers (also known as DTesters) is an official, invite only Discord server for adept volunteer bug testers. Our goal is to identify, reproduce, and provide high-quality bug reports.

We want to thank those of you that took the time to fill out the recent Discord Testers Consideration Quiz! For those who were not able to apply, but are interested in joining Discord Testers in the future, here are a few tips to help prepare:

  • Become familiar with Discord and its features.
  • Use the Discord Help Center to learn how features work. What happens next? We received a high volume of quiz submissions, so we’ll take the time to review each one carefully. We’ll contact selected candidates within a month after the quiz closes. Due to the number of submissions, we can’t reply to everyone individually, but we’ll update this post once we’ve sent all invitations.

Thanks for your interest and patience!

Discord Tester FAQ

Q: How can I report bugs if I am not a part of the Discord Testers server?

A: Bug reports should be submitted with a ticket to the Bug Reporting Form. Be sure to fill out each category, as each is important.

Q: Are members of the Discord Testers server required to have previous experience?

A: Members of the Discord Testers server are expected to have submitted quality bug reports prior to joining the server.

Q: Are DTesters required to sign a non-disclosure agreement (NDA)? Why?

A: DTesters may be asked to test features that have not yet been released. Due to the sensitive nature, an NDA is required to be signed. If an invitation is extended to you, you are welcome to review the details of the NDA so you can decide whether to sign or not.

Q: What is the time and submission requirement for a Discord Tester?

A: DTesters are volunteers, and as such, we want to encourage them to find balance between DTesters activities and personal lives. There is currently no minimum activity requirement, but complete inactivity for a long period of time may result in removal.

Q: What is the minimum age requirement for DTesters?

A: Discord users must be 13 years of age. If a Discord Tester is between 13 and 18 years of age, a parent or guardian will need to sign the NDA as well as the tester.

Q: Can I be a Discord Tester even if I don’t live in the United States?

A: Discord is a place for all to find belonging, and we have DTesters from all around the world. Clear written communication in English is necessary at this time.

Q: Can I join DTesters if I don’t want to participate in bug reporting/testing?

A: The new version of DTesters is for adept and active bug reporters/testers.

How do I get a Bug Hunter Badge?

A: Bug Hunter Badges are available to Discord Testers who meet specific requirements.

Q: How can I prepare to be a tester?

A: Check out the Discord Bugs article for guidance on the elements of a quality bug report. Keep in mind that the most helpful bug reports are those that affect the usability and enjoyment of Discord.

Q: Why was the original format of the DTesters server changed?

A: The original Discord Testers was a vast community of bug testers and curious folks alike, making it challenging to facilitate great communication. Additionally, the size and scope of interests meant that the features that could be tested were limited. We’ve updated the program in order to provide more enjoyment and participation opportunities to the most active testers in the community.

Introduction to Testing Clients

We have a couple of early access programs for all desktop clients, where you can get a sneak peek at the new features, and you can still do all of the stuff you normally do on Discord. The catch is that these new features are untested and are probably full of bugs.

The different versions can be categorized as:

Stable - The standard version. This usually doesn’t have a lot of bugs and everyone can use it.

Beta - Also called public test build (PTB) for Desktop, for iOS it is Testflight, and for Android it is Beta. This version usually has more bugs than Stable but should not hinder your normal usage.

Alpha - Commonly called Canary on Desktop and on Android it’s called Alpha. This is the most unstable version of Discord, with lots of updates. Bugs usually happen here so use this client at your own risk.

  • Stable - discord.com and click open Discord.
  • PTB- ptb.discord.com and click open Discord.
  • Canary - canary.discord.com and click open Discord. Note: Internet Explorer and versions of Microsoft Edge prior to version 17 are not supported.

All stable installers can be found at discord.com or the Google Play Store and Apple AppStore.

How do I find my client info?

Whether you’re bug hunting or running into an issue on the app, one of the most important pieces of information you need to determine is that you’re running the most up-to-date version of Discord. Here’s how to check what version you’re running for both desktop and mobile apps. You can also provide this information to our Support team if you have any questions or need assistance with anything.

What this article covers:

Desktop

How to Report a Bug

What this article covers:

  • What is a Bug?
  • How to Complete the Bug Form
    • Description
    • Steps to Reproduce
    • Expected Results
    • Actual Results
    • Discord Client Info
    • Debug Logs
    • Attachments
  • How to Report a Bug

What is a Bug?

Bugs are those annoying glitches in Discord that disrupt your experience. Imagine you’re in the middle of a voice chat, and the app suddenly crashes, or you’re trying to add a reaction to your gaming guild’s announcement, but behold your favorite emoji is cut in half! These bugs can be really frustrating, but Discord is always working to fix them and make sure everything runs smoothly.

How to Complete the Bug Form

Please note that not all types of Bug Reports are supported. To determine if your issue falls within the unsupported category, we kindly ask you to review our Unsupported Reports article before submitting your report.

Here’s a full breakdown of what information to provide when filling out the bug form.

Example of Submission Form for Bug Reporting
Description

When describing a bug, keep it short and clear, which is usually just a sentence or two.

For instance, instead of saying “It’s broken” or “It glitches,” try to be specific about what’s happening. This helps us understand the problem better and fix it faster.

Example:

When attempting to react to a message, my emojis don’t appear.

Example of Bug Description Entry
Steps to Reproduce

Write easy step-by-step instructions on how to make the bug happen. Be descriptive and include any details you feel are important to make the bug occur. Avoid saying things like: “Do Bug!”

Example:

  • Hover over a message you want to react to

  • Click on the “Add Reaction” button

  • Tap an emoji you want to react with

  • Observe

Example of Steps to Reproduce Entry
Expected Results

Tell us what you think should be happening instead of the bug. Describe how you believe the feature is supposed to work. The more details you provide, the easier it will be for us to understand and fix the issue.

Example:

After tapping the emoji to react with it would show up on the bottom of the message.

Example of Expected Result Entry
Actual Results

Let us know what’s actually happening when the bug occurs. Describe the unexpected behavior you’re seeing.

Example:

When attempting to react to a message, the emoji doesn’t appear at the bottom of the message.

Example of Actual Result Entry
Discord Client Info

What version of the Discord app are you experiencing this bug on? You can find this info in your settings.

If you are having trouble with finding this info, check out this Help Center article.

Example:

stable 297274 (a779dec) Host 0.0.305 arm64 macOS 14 (23.1.0)

Discord Client Info in User Settings
Debug Logs

These are records of what’s happening behind the scenes in your Discord app. They help us track down and fix issues by showing us where things might be going wrong. It’s important to remember to reproduce the bug before sending your logs.

Mobile

  1. Reproduce the bug on your mobile device.

  2. Tap the You button in the bottom-right corner.

  3. Tap the cogwheel in the upper-right corner.

  4. Scroll down to the Support category and tap Upload Debug Logs to Discord Support to upload your debug logs.

Mobile: Navigate to Settings > Support to find the Upload Debug Logs to Discord Support option

Desktop

Uploading Debug Logs through Discord

Here’s how to upload your Debug Logs through Discord:

  1. Open your User Settings by pressing the cogwheel in the bottom-left corner of the desktop app.

  2. Select Voice & Video and press the Debugging tab.

  3. Enable Debug Logging by toggling it, then reproduce the bug.

  4. After reproducing the bug, go back into your User Settings.

  5. Press Voice & Video > Debugging tab.

  6. Under Debug Logging, select Upload to upload your debug logs. You’ll receive a confirmation message confirming it’s been uploaded.

When you upload Debug Logs through Discord, they are sent automatically to Support.

Desktop: Navigate to User Settings > Voice & Video > Debugging to find the Upload option

Uploading Debug Logs Using File Explorer

You can locate and upload your Debug logs through File Explorer on your desktop computer:

For Windows Users: To find your Debug Logs manually, open File Explorer and enter this path, replacing “username” with your Windows username: C:*username*

For Mac Users: On macOS, find your Debug Logs by opening Finder > Go > Go to Folder and entering: ~/Library/Application Support/discord/

When using the File Explorer method, remember to attach the Debug Log file to your bug report.

Attachments

Sometimes bugs are tricky and we need to dig deep to figure out what’s causing the problem which is where attachments come in handy.

Here’s some info you can provide to help us get to the bottom of bugs faster and squash those bugs. These types of files are especially helpful for audio, video, screen sharing, and crash-related bugs.

DxDiag

DxDiags are only available on Windows devices.

These are reports about your computer’s system and drivers. They help us troubleshoot issues with audio, video, and crashes more effectively.

Please note: these are only available on Windows devices.

  1. Press the Windows key + R button on your keyboard to open the Run Dialog Box.

  2. Type dxdiag and hit the Enter key on your keyboard. The Diagnostic tool will open, make sure to wait until the green bar has fully loaded.

  3. Select the Save All Information button.

  4. Attach the TXT file generated to your Bug Report.

Run Dialog Box

Screen Recordings

To upload screen recordings, attach the files directly to your Bug Report. Avoid using online storage drive links. Discord’s Support team will not open those links.

How to Report a Bug

Once you are ready to submit a bug, please head to the Discord Support form and select Bug Reporting under “What can we help you with?”. Fill out all of the information as outlined above and then press Submit once you’re ready.

You can always keep track of patch updates and if your bug that you submitted has been fixed, by checking out the Discord Blog.

If you need help troubleshooting an issue or have general questions about Discord, please submit a ticket to our Support Team here.

This is a feature that Discord Developers use for testing new versions of code! By clicking on that nifty “Apply” button, it’ll automatically restart your client and set your client to a special version of our code!

Note if you see a “Incorrect User” error message, you won’t be able to access this build since it’s been bestowed to a different tester!

If you are a tester and want to get back to the everyday code, you can clear the build override by either 1) clicking that red “Clear” button in the build override link…

Or 2) right clicking on that Gear icon by your Discord tag and avatar in the bottom left hand corner- and selecting “Clear Build Override”

Non-Standard Bug Reports

These are issues that are not supported by standard Bug Reporting, but may be reported elsewhere:

Payment related issues (submit to Billing Support)

Security bugs

Translation bugs that do not break functionality. These should be submitted to dis.gd

API bugs. These should be reported on the API Docs GitHub Repository

Feature Requests should be submitted to feedback.discord.com

Unsupported Reports

This is a list of unsupported report topics, please check this list before you submit a bug.

Client modifications (BeautifulDiscord, BetterDiscord, etc.)

Using multiple instances of Discord on the same device at the same time. Example: Using Discord Stable, PTB, and Canary all at once.

Any bug that occurs only on virtual machines. If they can be reproduced on real hardware, it’s valid

Alpha, Nightly, or developer environment browsers. If a developer environment browser update causes Discord to stop working, when it previously worked, this should be reported to the browser developers.

Minor Reports

Visual bugs with a low pixel offset (“Pixel-Bugs”)

Bugs that involve spam-pressing buttons

Bugs that only appear for about a second

Reports that involve a high amount of steps to reproduce (Think if the Konami-Code resulted in a bug)

Behavior that only happens by waiting for several minutes/hours

ChromeOS

Community Onboarding Examples

Customize a set of questions that your server members can answer to be given channels and roles relevant to their answers. Check out these example questions below.

Questions that Assign Channels

For your first question, create something that helps members pick channels in addition to the Default Channels you set up.

  • Note: Your most popular channels should be included in Default Channels. You don’t want members to accidentally miss those!
  • Don’t put too many options or members will get overwhelmed. 6 is a good maximum for questions like this.
    • Make separate questions for off-topic channels
    • You can assign multiple channels/roles in an answer to reduce the number of answers.
  • Make questions Required if they assign important channels and you think members should try at least some of them.
Cap’s Book Community
Mallow’s Science Enthusiasts

Questions for Everything Else

Make questions to help members sign up for notifications, customize their profile, or express themselves.

  • If you have a lot of answers, keep it simple and remove descriptions.
  • Remember: you can assign roles and channels in the same answer. Consolidate where you can!
  • Not all questions need to be answered before a member joins. Uncheck “Ask members before join” for questions that can be answered later. These will appear in a special “Channels & Roles” tab in your server.
Tipp’s Fandom
Cap’s Book Community

What NOT to Do

  • DON’T use too many answers if one very long question could be made into two shorter questions
  • DON’T put rules inside your onboarding questions. Members will be asked to accept rules after they join.
  • DON’T use too much writing in your answer titles and descriptions. The faster members can understand the question, the better their answers will be!

Community Onboarding FAQ

As of March 30, 2023, Community Onboarding is available to all community servers. Also, we’ve begun testing a new feature within Community Onboarding called Server Guide.

More and more people come to Discord every year to experience awesome communities like yours. But sometimes the experience of joining a new community can feel like being cannon-blasted into a strange, foreign land that gets new people asking “Sooo… what am I supposed to do here?” or “Why are there so many channels?!”

The truth is, many new people on Discord trying to join your community don’t understand what “bots” are, what roles do, or which of your many channels to check out. And when they get confused and overwhelmed, they just leave. Surely there has to be an easier way to get people to join your community, know their way around, and actually stay and become a part of your tribe.

That’s where Community Onboarding comes in to help you save the day.

What does this article cover?

  • Here’s how it works
  • How do I set up Community Onboarding?
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Here’s how it works

To help anyone join your communities on Discord with ease and delight, we’re giving community admins the ability to create a personalized onboarding experience. With Community Onboarding, new members get to pick out their own roles and channels and enjoy a personalized channel list in your server by answering a few simple questions.

Once they’re in, they can adjust their answers to your questions to swap roles or channels at any time in a new Channels & Roles tab above their channel list.

Great! How do I set up Community Onboarding?

  1. Add Default Channels

First, head over to Server Settings > Onboarding and start the setup process by adding Default Channels.

Your Default Channels will be the channels that all new members will see in their channel list when joining your Community. These should typically be your most popular and valuable channels you think every new member should have on their channel list.

Best practices:

  • Prioritize channels with healthy activity and friendly for new joiners, like #general, #polls, #giveaways, forums, or LFG channels.
  • Avoid including channels that aren’t useful or relevant for most new members as part of your Default Channels - you’ll be able to assign those later!
  1. Create Customization Questions

Members will answer Customization Questions to pick additional channels and roles. Create a question, give it some answers, and then assign relevant channels and/or roles for each answer choice. When a member picks that answer, they will be granted those roles and those channels will be added to their channel list!

Customization questions let you create questions and answers that let new members pick out their own roles and channels.

Start by asking questions that assign new members additional channels

  • Try using a question like “What would you like to do here?” to assign your main channels
For each question, add answer options that assign channels and/or roles when selected
What new members will see

  • You can also ask a question like “What off-topic channels do you want?” to assign off-topic channels For each question, you can choose to:

  • Ask before a member joins - this shows your questions and answers to new members right before they join your server. Questions that assign channels and important roles should be asked before a member joins.

    • Questions without this toggled on will be included in the Channels & Roles tab above everyone’s channel list, for members to check out later. Use this for questions around non-urgent customizations, like vanity roles.

  • Allow multiple answers - lets new members select multiple answer choices for the same question. Great for those “Choose all that apply” questions.

  • Make Required - members must answer the question to proceed into your server. If a question assigns important channels, consider making it required! Best practices:

  • Use the “Preview” button at the top to test out the look and feel of your questions and answer options, and ensure they assign the correct channels and/or roles as intended.

  • Avoid including too many answer options or members will feel overwhelmed.

  • Don’t make answer options or descriptions too long! Keep them short and sweet where possible so new members can read and answer them easily.

  • Check out our Community Onboarding examples article for specific examples of good, simple questions to ask new members.

  1. Make sure most of your member channels are assignable through Onboarding

Most of your member channels should be included in either Default Channels or Questions, so that members can select them.

If channels are left out of onboarding, newer members may not ever find those channels! If there are lots of channels left out, try creating additional questions or answers that assign them.

Make sure most of your member channels are assignable through Onboarding! We’ll let you know which channels haven’t been assigned.
  1. Review and publish

Once you’ve selected your Default Channels and set up your Customization Questions, you’ll be able to enable and preview your Onboarding setup from the point of view of a new member joining your server, assuming you meet the following criteria:

  • You must have selected at least 7 Default Channels
    • At least 5 of these channels must allow @everyone to View and Send Messages
  1. Remove verification steps that overwhelm or lock new members from joining your server

Remember how confusing it can be for newer folks who get easily confused and overwhelmed by bot-powered verification steps that block access to certain parts of your server?

With Community Onboarding, you have an easy way to grant new members their own roles and channels from the start and show them all the cool things your community has to offer.

At this stage, consider removing bot-powered restrictions that add confusion and turn away new members trying to join your server.

“But Discord, wouldn’t that make my server more vulnerable to raiders also trying to join my server?!”

To that, we have the solution: Raid Protection

Enjoy greater peace of mind from join-raids without the downside of restricting well-intentioned folks from your server. Our Raid Protection system uses machine learning to automatically detect suspicious behavior or activity happening in your server that are indicative of a likely join-raid about to take place.

How it works: If a possible join-raid is detected, our system will take automated actions to protect your server before it happens, such as sending you an alert so you can investigate and take action, and requiring CAPTCHA for new joiners within the next hour to help keep out botted accounts trying to join your server in large numbers. This way, you can feel comfortable using Community Onboarding without worrying about complicated bot restrictions or raiders trying to join your server en masse.

You can enable alerts to receive notifications when suspicious server-join activity or behavior is detected in Server Settings > Safety Setup > Raid Protection. Learn more about how to protect your server from raids here.

Left: Set up to receive alerts when a possible join-raid has been detected in your server.
Right: What an alert looks like

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I access Community Onboarding?

You’ll find Community Onboarding in Server Settings > Onboarding.

Q: What permissions are required to access and set up Community Onboarding?

You must have “Manage Server” and “Manage Roles” or “Administrator” permissions to set up Community Onboarding.

Q: Who is Community Onboarding currently available to?

A: As of March 30, 2023, Community Onboarding is available to all community servers.

Q: What devices is Community Onboarding available on?

Users can experience Community Onboarding on any device.

However, admins can only configure and enable Community Onboarding on desktop.

Q: Are there examples of Community Onboarding questions I can check out?

Yup, check out Community Onboarding Examples.

Q: What happens to channels that I don’t assign to any Customization Questions?

Channels you don’t assign to Customization Questions will still exist in your server but won’t be assignable for new members going through your Community Onboarding experience.

Members will be able to find, access, and add these channels to their channel list by going to Channels & Roles > Browse Channels.

Q: What’s the point of unmarking “Ask before member joins” for a Customization Question?

If you create a Customization Question and choose to unmark “Ask before member joins,” it will appear in Channels & Roles > Customize but will no longer appear to new members who go through your onboarding experience.

You may choose to do this if you want to ask members that are already in your server questions that easily assign them roles and channels.

Q: Will members who leave my server and rejoin have to go through my onboarding process again?

Yes.

Community Server Guidelines

As an owner of a Community server, you and your moderation team are responsible for helping users find a place to hang out and be part of a new community. Here’s what you’ll need to be a Community. Your server must:

  • Have a title and description that accurately describes the server. Help potential members understand why they want to join. Be accurate here — no one likes being misled.
  • Have clearly posted rules and guidelines. Clearly label what is and isn’t allowed in your community. Effective rules define what kind of content and behavior is or isn’t encouraged and tolerated.
  • Have a moderator team. Moderators can help ensure nothing rule-breaking is happening in your community and can find meaningful ways for your members to engage. Build a moderator team that members of your community can trust and turn to for help.
  • Foster a healthy and positive environment. People should feel welcome in your community. Create spaces where people want to spend time with each other, share interests, participate in community events, and build friendships. Do not cultivate general toxic behavior, harassment of others, or other derogatory content.
  • Abide by the Community Guidelines and Terms of Service. This means that issues reported to Discord should be resolved, and your moderator team should know when to escalate issues to Trust & Safety. Servers found to be facilitating violations against Discord’s Community Guidelines and Terms of Service will be subject to further action from our Trust & Safety Team. If your server is found violating these guidelines, your server may lose its status as a Community, and you may lose the ability to be discoverable on Discord.

In order for your server to be considered for becoming discoverable, your server must abide by the Community Server Guidelines. Please note that servers whose primary purpose is to facilitate sexually explicit content are not eligible for Discovery at this time.

Community Server Welcome Screen

If your server has the Welcome Screen enabled, you will no longer be able to edit it. We recommend enabling Community Onboarding instead on your server.

There is now an easier way for you to identify if a community is right for you.

Discord is home to many servers and interesting user-interface designs ranging from the pound sign next to a channel (#hash-tag), a million names on the right side of the screen (Members- 99999), and disabled chat bars (please read the #rules first).

We understand this can be very overwhelming to users, so we have created a better user experience on first contact with these communities.

Whether this is your first couple of servers you are joining, the 50th, or a Server Owner looking to simplify your community, we introduce to you the Community Server Welcome Screen.

In this article we will cover:

  • How to enable the Welcome Screen
  • Customization for Community Server Owners
  • Recommended Channels Guide
  • Why Should I Set This Up?
  • Feedback

How to Enable the Welcome Screen

To enable the Welcome Screen, your server must have enabled the Community Server Settings! If you haven’t done so yet, check out this support article on how to do so!

Customization for Community Server Owners

Community Server Owners and those with Manage Server permission now have access to this option, you can customize it under Server Settings.

From here you can click on “Set Up Welcome Screen” to get started, you will then receive a window to “Add a Recommended Channel”. Select any channel that you prefer users to see within your server and write a little description about it you want others to see.

Once you have saved your customization you will get an overview of what it will look like. From here, you can continue to add 4 more options or hit “Enable” to show it off to new, incoming users.

Lastly, you can select “Preview” to get a visual on how it will look to new users to give you a better idea of their end.

And that is it! Congratulations on setting up your Community Server Welcome Screen!

Recommended Channels Guide

Now that you have an idea of how to set up your Welcome Screen, it can be a bit difficult to decide what channels to spotlight in your summary from your already amazing 100+ other #text-channels.

Here are some recommendations from us on what type of channels to add to your Welcome Screen.

  • A channel where new users can interact (talk, chat, react) with others already within the server. (e.g. #general, #discussion)
  • #Rules channel to make sure active engagement is safe for everyone in the community and within ToS/guidelines.
  • An #announcements channel to get the latest news specific to your community activities.
  • #Finding-Friends or #Looking-for-Group channels for those that want to jump right into the action. We also suggest naming these channels to ones that are easily definitive and understood by those within and outside of the community for extra clarity.

By naming the channel after the action or activity that is to take place within that text/voice channel, this can prevent confusion on what users are allowed to do within each channel. (e.g. #pictures-only, #meet-new-friends, #introduce-yourself)

Why Should I Set This Up?

Sometimes large communities with many channels, users, and large walls of text can be a bit too confusing for newcomers that want a clear direction of where to go.

This can contribute to bad user experience and cause a user who would have contributed greatly to your community to get lost in our UI.

To combat this, the Welcome Screen provides ease of access and less friction for new Discord users and long time users alike. The impact generated from setting up a Welcome Screen will help with increased retention of users old and new, and raise engagement within your community.

This means more people to stick around and engage with the community in a positive way!

We hope this helps you in your future endeavors in growing your user base by offering a bit more customization and simplicity.

Feedback

We’re always open to hear about how you feel about features, so don’t hesitate to reach out to us at dis.gd/feedback and let us know what you think.

Discord Admin FAQ

Welcome! We’re excited to tell you more about the Discord Admins server, a server for community builders and leaders.

What this article covers:

  • What is the Discord Admins Server?
  • Join the Discord Admins Server
  • Frequently Asked Questions
  • How to Contact

WHAT IS THE DISCORD ADMINS SERVER?

This server allows Discord to chat with admins, moderators, content creators, and server owners who manage a server with Community Settings enabled.

Here you can learn more about features, use best practices, and meet other members who want to improve their communities!

JOIN THE DISCORD ADMINS SERVER

What are the requirements to join this space?

Below are the requirements your server will have to meet.

  • Have at least 1,000 members on your server
  • Have at least a 60% monthly member retention rate
  • Your server must be at least 3 months old
  • Enable Community Settings on your server If your server meets the above requirements and you have the Manage Server permission on that server, you will be able to join the Discord Admins server.

You, as an individual, can join as long as you have the “Manage Server” permission natively in Discord. If you would like other admins or moderators from your server to join the community, you will have to temporarily grant them the Manage Server permission in order to see the join button.

To join the Discord Admins server…

  • Access Discord on the desktop/browser app
  • Go to your server’s Server Settings
  • Select Overview in the Community section
  • Press on Join Discord’s Admins Server
Note: The only way to join the Discord Admins Server is on the desktop/browser app. This is unavailable on the mobile app.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What can I find in the Discord Admins server?

A: The Discord Admins server primarily focuses on engaging, managing, protecting, and growing thriving communities on Discord.

Here you can find chatter about best practices, safety, apps, monetization, and more. Members will also receive updates on new features or updates directly from Discord. We also use the community as a way to gather feedback on some features and ask members to provide us with feedback.

Q: Where can I find the rules for the server?

A: Current rules can be found in the #rules channel. Be sure to read them completely!

However, Discord reserves the right to act on misbehavior and violations not explicitly listed in our rules. At all times, use common sense and good judgment for anything you do on the server. Moderation actions by Staff or Moderators will ensure that we continue to promote healthy communities and assume that all Admins will be acting with positive intent.

Q: I’m in the server, but I can’t see any channels! What should I do?

A: You must complete our Community Onboarding to access channels in the server. If you are still struggling with this, you can message our Modmail bot and ask a moderator for assistance.

Q: Manage Server is a pretty high permission to give out, why is it locked behind this?

A: We want to ensure that we are reaching server owners, admins and moderators with this community. As such, this will require us to ensure we are reaching an audience that has this permission or capability in order to create a welcoming and fun community for all.

Discord Server Web Pages

Note: Starting November 16, 2026, every Discoverable Server will have a Server Web Page. If you haven’t set one up yourself, a default page will be created automatically from your existing Server Profile details. Server Web Page settings are available on desktop and browser only. Learn more about server types.

What this article covers:

  • What is a Server Web Page?
  • Which servers can create a Server Web Page?
  • How do I set up a Server Web Page?
  • What content should I add to my Server Web Page?
  • What content can appear on my Server’s Web Page?
  • Can I turn off my Server Web Page?
  • Does my server need a specific Boost Level?

What is a Server Web Page?

A Server Web Page is a public page on the open web that helps people discover and learn about your Discoverable Server. Anyone can see it, including people without a Discord account, and search engines like Google can show it in their results. Beyond the content you add yourself, it may also show content from your server’s public channels, such as Channel Summaries and Channel Messages. New members can join directly from this page.

To manage which content appears on your page, see Server Web Presence.

Which servers can create a Server Web Page?

Server Web Pages are exclusive to Discoverable Servers.

See Clarifying Server Types to learn how a Community Server can become Discoverable.

How do I set up a Server Web Page?

Automatic setup: If you don’t set up your own Server Web Page for your Discoverable Server, Discord publishes a default one for you, built from your server’s existing details from the Server Profile. You don’t need to do anything for your Discoverable Server to have a page.

To customize your Server Web Page:

  1. Open Server Settings on Discord desktop or browser.

  2. Under Community, select Web Presence.

Web Presence is under Community in Server Settings.
  1. Edit your server’s Landing Page.
Complete each requirement in the Landing Page panel, then select Publish Landing Page.
  1. Once your page is live, select View Page to see it. You can update your page content at any time after publishing.

What content should I add to my Server Web Page?

All web page content needs to abide by Discord’s Discovery Guidelines. Discord’s Trust and Safety team may remove web pages that violate these guidelines, and consider whether further action is necessary.

Describe your server in ways that help people find it. When adding content to your web page, use words that describe your community accurately and specifically. This will help new community members easily find your server when they’re searching the web for relevant terms. If your server is for underwater basket weaving enthusiasts, use these words rather than more generic ones. Your next basket weaver may be just one search term away!

What content can appear on my Server’s Web Page?

Channel Summaries. A small slice of what’s being talked about in your server, directly on your Server Web Page. These automated summaries only cover conversations from November 16, 2026, onwards. Admins can change which channels they draw from, curate the summaries that are shown, or turn them off entirely. Usernames will not be shown in summaries.

Channel Messages. From mid-December 2026, answers to questions your members sent in public channels can be found in a web search, in their own words. Server admins decide which channels take part, and server members can opt out of having their own messages appear. Usernames will not be shown alongside these messages.

Summaries on the web and Messages on the web are controlled independently; each has its own settings for which channels are included. See Server Web Presence to manage them.

Can I turn off my Server Web Page?

A Server Web Page is a required part of being a Discoverable Server. If you don’t want a public page, you can turn off Discoverability, which reverts your server to a Community Server. See Clarifying Server Types for how to turn off Discoverability and what changes when you do.

To turn off Discoverability, go to Access and select Invite Only or Apply to Join.

You can still control what appears on your page. Server Settings > Web Presence lets you edit your server’s landing page, and separate controls let you turn off Channel Summaries or Channel Messages for specific channels without leaving Discoverable status.

Turn Channel Summaries and Channel Messages on or off separately in Web Presence.

See Server Web Presence for those settings.

Does my server need a specific Boost Level?

No. Server Web Pages are available to all Discoverable Servers, regardless of Boost Level.

Discord Student Hubs FAQ

Note: This feature is slowly rolling out so not everyone has access yet! Stay tuned for more details in the future!

WHAT ARE DISCORD STUDENT HUBS?

A Discord Student Hub is a place for students to meet classmates from their school.

Each hub is only accessible to users with an email address associated with that school. Students will be able to find other classmates that have joined the hub, add their servers to the hub, and find their classmates’ servers, all in one place.

General FAQ

Where are Student Hubs available?

  • Hubs are currently live for a number of schools in Australia, Canada, Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Mexico, the Philippines, Poland, Spain, the UK, and the USA. It is now possible for students in many countries across the world to sign-up for the waitlist. Is this a Discord partnership with high schools/colleges?

  • Hubs are not officially affiliated with or managed by schools. A Student Hub is a collection of student-run servers. The Hub’s function is to make it easier for classmates to find and join one another’s servers if they choose to do so. Who has access to a hub?

  • Only people with a school-issued email address can access their school’s Student Hub. Even though the servers listed in the school’s Student Hub are run by students, people do not need to be a member of the Student Hub to be invited to join the listed servers. How will my school email address be used?

  • Your school email address will be used to verify which student hub you can access. It will not be visible to other users on Discord, and it will not be shared with your school. I am a student, where do I sign up for Student Hubs on Discord?

  • You can find Student Hubs in the following place:

    • Desktop/Browser: Click on the Explore Public Servers button at the bottom of the left panel in Discord
    • Mobile: At the very bottom of the left panel in the Discord app

  • If your Student Hub is not yet available you can sign up for the waitlist How do I add a server to the hub?

  • Servers can be added using the “Add Servers” button in the left panel of the hub, or by using the “Add Server” button in the hub server list. How do I remove my server from the hub?

  • You can remove your server from the hub by hovering over a server preview in the hub on the top right corner to access a smaller menu that includes the option to “Remove from Hub”. You will be asked to confirm before removing the server from a hub. How do I leave the hub?

  • Click on the Student Hub name for a drop-down menu. From here - you can leave the hub, in addition to changing your nickname or inviting more classmates. If you decide to leave a hub, you will be asked to confirm prior to leaving. What safety measures are in place for the students participating?

  • Only those with a school-assigned email address can access a school’s specific hub. Click here to dive into our Student Hubs policy. All servers and users in the hub must also comply with our Community Guidelines, ToS, and Privacy Policy. We also have all of our existing user controls for servers, such as setting specific roles and access to #channels in a server, blocking, banning, mod bots, and more.

Waitlist FAQ

How do students find the hubs waitlist?

  • If the hubs waitlist is available in their region, students can find it in the following place:

    • Desktop/web: Click on the Explore Public Servers button at the bottom of the left panel in Discord
    • Mobile: At the very bottom of the left panel in the Discord app What does an invite to the waitlist look like?

  • Text may change slightly, but invites to hubs look similar to this: How do I remove myself from the waitlist?

  • By signing up for the waitlist you will not be automatically entered into the hub when the hub is live. When the hub goes live you will receive an email at the email address you provided, letting you know that the hub is live if you would like to join it.

Discord Verified Server Program FAQ

What this article covers:

  • What is the Verified Server Program?
  • How do I get my Server Verified?

What is the Verified Server Program?

The Verified Server Program lets official game servers get recognized on Discord. A Verified Server has gone through Discord’s verification process, which confirms its connection to a game through Steam.

This program is currently exclusively for games — meaning only a game and its directly associated server can participate. It is not available for other types of communities such as companies, movies, music artists, or general interest servers. To be eligible, your game must be a playable, fully-released game on Steam. Early access counts as released, but games that are not yet available to play – including those with only a “Coming Soon” store page, wishlist page, demo, or playtest—are not eligible. You cannot verify a server before the game it belongs to has launched.

Verified is a status a server earns on top of its server type. It doesn’t change whether your server is a Friend, Community, or Discoverable Server. Verified servers automatically qualify as Discoverable Servers. Learn more in Clarifying Server Types.

Important: Previously the Verified Server Program included large companies, films, and musicians. That broader program has been discontinued. The current verified program applies to games only.

How Do I Get My Server Verified?

Server verification is done through game claiming: Discord’s self-serve flow that lets developers prove ownership of their game and verify their server in the process. To claim your game and verify your server, you’ll need:

  • A Discord server for your game
  • The game live on Steam, with your Discord invite link added to the Steam store page
  • The game launched and available to download and play
  • A Team in the Discord Developer Portal, with an Application for your game associated with it
  • The server owner added to that Team, since they’ll receive the verification code by email Once you start the claim, Discord emails a verification code to the server owner, you submit your claim, and our team reviews it. After approval, your server is verified and you gain control over your game’s identity on Discord.

Want to learn more?

If you want to claim your game, you can learn more about that process in Discord’s Claim Your Game documentation.

  • Clarifying Server Types
  • Partnered vs. Verified Servers

Discoverable Content on the Web

Messages from public channels in Discoverable Servers can appear on the web through a server’s web pages, either as individual messages or as summaries of a channel’s conversation. This article explains what that means for you as a member and how you can control your own content.

What this article covers:

  • What Content Can Appear on the Web
  • How will I know if I’m in a channel where this applies?
  • Controlling Whether Your Messages Can Appear
    • How to Turn This Setting On or Off
    • What Happens When You Change This Setting
    • Deleting Individual Messages
  • Can my messages appear on the web by default?
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What Content Can Appear on the Web

A Server Web Page can show two different kinds of content pulled from public channels:

  • Channel Summaries on the web: A small slice of what’s being talked about in your server, directly on your Server Web Page. These automated summaries only cover discussions from November 16, 2026 onward. Admins can change which channels they draw from, curate the summaries that are shown, or turn them off entirely. Usernames will not be shown in summaries.
  • Channel Messages on the web: From mid-December 2026, answers to questions your members sent in public channels can be found in a web search, in their own words. Server admins decide which channels take part, and server members can choose whether their own messages appear. Usernames and avatars will not be shown alongside these messages.

How will I know if I’m in a channel where this applies?

Discoverable content on the web can only appear from public channels in a Discoverable Server. Channels taking part in Channel Summaries or Channel Messages are labeled, with an icon in the channel header, so you know before you send a message.

You’ll also see a pop-up near the channel header letting you know before you post. This pop-up reappears any time a channel newly enables this feature. Your server’s admins choose which channels take part in Channel Summaries and Channel Messages on the web, so you may see this in some channels and not others.

Channel Messages roll out gradually from mid-December 2026, so it may be a few weeks before messages from labeled channels appear on Server Web Pages.

Controlling Whether Your Messages Can Appear

The Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages setting controls whether your messages in eligible channels can be shown on the public web. It applies across all your servers, not per server.

Note: You can change this setting on desktop or in your browser. It applies to your whole account, including on mobile.

How to Turn This Setting On or Off

  1. Open User Settings.

  2. Select Data & Privacy.

  3. Turn Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages on or off.

Data & Privacy Setting for Web Pages
What Happens When You Change This Setting

Whether a message can appear on the web depends on your Channel Messages setting when you send it. Messages you send while the setting is off won’t appear on the web.

Turning the setting off doesn’t change this for messages you sent while it was on. Those messages can still appear on the server’s web pages, even if they haven’t appeared yet. To prevent one of those messages from appearing, or to remove one that’s already on Discord’s web pages, delete it from Discord.

  • While your setting is on: eligible messages you send can appear publicly. Messages may be displayed by search engines (including, but not limited to Google), which may be based outside your country.
  • When you turn it off: Discord stops displaying on web any new messages from you going forward.
  • Messages already shown on web before you turned it off can remain visible. Turning the setting off is not a bulk “remove my history” action.
Deleting Individual Messages

If you delete an individual message, that deletion applies on Discord and is reflected on the Server Web Page, so the message will be removed there too. Deleting a message removes its visibility on the Discord app and Discord web pages. While Discord has its own data retention policy, we do not control how long others may retain cached or indexed copies of content. Search engines have their own deletion processes and retention policies so it may take additional action or time for content to stop appearing in their results.

Can my messages appear on the web by default?

Yes, in most regions. Your Channel Messages setting is on by default, so messages you send in Discoverable channels can appear on the web unless you turn it off. It’s off by default if your account is in the EU/EEA, UK, Canada, Brazil, Australia, or South Korea. If you’re in the teen age group, your messages won’t appear on the web and you can’t turn this setting on.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I stop my messages from appearing on the web as Channel Messages?

A: Yes. Turn off your Channel Messages setting in User Settings > Data & Privacy (Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages). This applies to messages you send from then on. Messages you sent while the setting was on can still appear on the web.

Q: If I delete a message, does it disappear from search results?

A: Deleting a message removes it from Discord and from Discord’s web pages. Search engines keep their own copies of pages, so it may take some time, or an extra removal request, before it stops appearing in their results. Discord doesn’t control how long they keep cached copies. Learn more about how long Discord keeps your information in our data retention policy.

Q: What happens if I don’t change anything?

A: If you do nothing, eligible messages you send starting mid-December 2026 may appear on the web, unless your region or account defaults it off (default off in EU/EEA, UK, Canada, Brazil, Australia, or South Korea).

It may be a few weeks before messages from labeled channels appear on a server’s web pages. Channel Messages on the web must also meet server, channel, and content requirements.

Q: Are messages in threads and forums included?

A: Yes, if the parent channel is public, eligible, and Channel Summaries on web or Channel Messages on web is turned on for the channel. Private threads and private forums are never included, regardless of the parent channel’s settings.

Q: Are messages text only?

A: Currently, Channel Messages on the web will show text only. A small number of existing partner communities have images and videos appearing on their Server Web Pages today as part of an earlier pilot. We’ll update this answer as that capability becomes more broadly available.

Q: Are you selling my messages to AI companies?

A: No. Nothing has changed. We are making Discord content easier to find if admins and users choose to make their content available on the web.

Discoverable Server Web Presence

Web Presence is where you control what content from your Discoverable Server can appear publicly on its Server Web Page and in search engines like Google.

Note: Web Presence settings are available on desktop and browser only at this time. Only the server owner or members with the Administrator permission can change them, and bots can’t change them.

Want to learn more?

Learn more about Server Web Pages. To learn how members control their own messages, see Discoverable Content on Web.

What this article covers:

  • How to Open Web Presence
  • What You Can Control Here
    • What makes a channel eligible?
    • Channel Summaries on the Web
    • Channel Messages on the Web
    • Setting This When Creating a Channel
  • Removing Content from the Web
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How to Open Web Presence

  1. Open Server Settings.

  2. Under Community, select Web Presence.

Web Presence in Server Settings

Tip: The first time you visit your server on desktop after October 27, 2026, you may see a pop-up titled Reach new members on the web. Select Web Presence to go straight to these settings.

Reach new members on the web Pop-up

What You Can Control Here

Controls for both Channel Summaries on the web and Channel Messages on the web roll out gradually starting October 27, 2026.

Server Web Presence manages two independent features. Each has its own toggle and its own list of eligible channels. Both toggles are under Discoverable Content on Web Pages and are on by default.

  • Channel Summaries on the web: These show a small slice of what’s being talked about in your server, directly on your Server Web Page. These automated summaries focus on active conversations from November 16, 2026, onwards. Admins can change which channels they draw from, curate the summaries that are shown, or turn them off entirely. Usernames and avatars will not be shown in summaries.
Channel Summaries Channel Settings
  • Channel Messages on the web: From mid-December 2026, answers to questions your members sent in public channels can be found in a web search, in their own words. Server admins decide which channels take part, and server members can choose whether their own messages appear. Usernames and avatars will not be shown alongside these messages.
Channel Messages Settings
What makes a channel eligible?

From November 16, 2026, summaries from public channels in your Discoverable Server may appear on your Server Web Page. Starting mid-December 2026, messages from public channels can appear too. Private channels, like role-restricted channels, are never included.

Channels taking part in Channel Summaries or Channel Messages are labeled, with an icon in the channel header.

Public channels in Discoverable Servers are included by default. You can change which ones are included at any time. Read below for more information on toggles for Channel Summaries on the web and Channel Messages on the web.

Channel Summaries on the Web

Choose which channels contribute to Channel Summaries on your Server Web Page. You can:

  • Select or deselect individual channels
  • Turn Summaries off entirely for your server Use Search channels to find a specific channel, or select Select All or Deselect All to change every channel at once. Select Save Changes when you’re done.

Summaries are generated automatically and are subject to Discord’s Discovery Guidelines. Discord’s Trust & Safety team can remove summaries that violate these guidelines.

Channel Messages on the Web

Choose which channels are eligible to have members’ messages shown on the server web pages. You can:

  • Select or deselect individual channels, independently of your Channel Summaries selections
  • Turn Channel Messages off entirely for your server
Setting This When Creating a Channel

When you create a public text channel in a Discoverable Server, the channel creation window includes a Discoverable section where you can choose All Content, Summaries Only, Messages Only, or Off. This only changes the channel you’re creating. For private channels, this section shows as Disabled.

Removing Content from the Web

To remove a Channel Summary or Channel Message from your Server Web Page:

  • Delete the message. Deleting a message removes it from the Discord app and Discord web pages.
  • Turn off the feature. Toggling off Channel Summaries or Channel Messages stops new content from being generated or shown going forward, but content already published may remain visible until individually removed.
  • Remove specific channels. Deselect individual channels under Web Presence settings to stop them from contributing new content. Keep in mind that while Discord removes content from its own pages, search engines have their own caching and indexing processes. It may take additional time or action for content to stop appearing in search results.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I know if my server is Discoverable?

A: Open Server Settings > Access > Discoverable. If your server meets all requirements and Server Discovery is turned on, your server is Discoverable, and the settings in this article apply to it. If you can’t open the Discoverable tab, or your server doesn’t meet all Server Discovery requirements, it isn’t Discoverable yet. See What if my server doesn’t meet requirements? above, or learn how a server becomes Discoverable in Clarifying Server Types.

Q: What happens if I don’t do anything?

A: If you don’t do anything, starting November 16, 2026, Channel Summaries may start appearing on your Server Web Page, and Channel Messages will roll out starting mid-December 2026. If you haven’t published your own Server Web Page, a default page goes live for you on November 16, 2026.

In some regions, members’ Channel Messages setting is off by default, so their messages won’t appear unless they turn it on.

If you want to turn off or change these settings, visit Server Settings > Community > Web Presence.

Q: If I turn off Channel Summaries or Channel Messages, does existing content come down immediately?

A: Turning off a feature stops new content from being generated or shown going forward. Content already published may remain visible until it’s individually removed. Deleting a message removes its visibility on the Discord app and Discord web pages. While Discord has its own data retention policy, we do not control how long others may retain cached or indexed copies of content. Search engines have their own deletion processes and retention policies so it may take additional action or time for content to stop appearing in their results.

Q: Can I stop my server from appearing on the web entirely?

A: Turning off both Channel Summaries and Channel Messages stops new content from appearing, though content already published may remain visible (see the FAQ above). Your Server Web Page stays live while your server is Discoverable. To remove your Server Web Page, turn off Discoverability, which changes your server back to a Community Server. See Clarifying Server Types for how to do this.

Q: Do Channel Summaries and Channel Messages use the same channel selections?

A: No. They’re independent. You can select different channels for each, or turn one off without affecting the other.

Q: How are Channel Summaries created?

A: Discord creates Channel Summaries using AI, based on recent discussions in your server’s public channels. Summaries may not always be accurate.

Q: Is Discord selling user messages to AI companies?

A: No. Nothing has changed. We are making Discord content easier to find if admins and users choose to make their content available on the web.

Q: What happens if my server stops being Discoverable?

A: If your server is no longer Discoverable, your Server Web Page is taken down, and Channel Messages and Channel Summaries turn off so your server no longer contributes new content to these features. However, this does not automatically remove content that was already published on the web.

To remove a specific message from Discord web pages, delete the original message in Discord. Search engines may still have cached copies, even after the message is deleted. Discord doesn’t control those copies, so removal from search results may require additional time or action through the search engine.

See Clarifying Server Types for more about what changes when you turn off Discoverability.

Q: Does turning off a feature here affect my members’ individual privacy settings?

A: No. Members have their own separate control over whether their individual messages can appear. Members control this with the Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages setting in User Settings > Data & Privacy.

Region, age, and each member’s own privacy setting can affect whether a specific message is eligible. See Discoverable Content on Web to learn more about individual user controls.

Discovery Guidelines

We want to help connect people to the things and places that they love and we want to make sure we do this in a safe manner. To help ensure that communities and people are safer, we’ve created guidelines to help servers understand what is and isn’t allowed if you choose to make your community open to everyone. Having the ability to reach more people on Discord is a big privilege which means that there is some additional responsibility for each server owner and their moderation team.

  1. Abide by the Community Guidelines and Terms of Service. This means that issues reported to your server should be addressed by your moderators and admins. Your moderator team should know when to escalate issues to Trust & Safety. Servers that violate Discord’s Community Guidelines and Terms of Service will be subject to further action from our Trust & Safety Team.
  • We want Discord to be a safe, positive, and inclusive experience. Our Trust & Safety team will investigate spaces that are reported to us or that we proactively identify as likely in violation of our policies, and Trust & Safety team members may temporarily join these spaces to investigate potential violations.
  • We may remove an affiliated server or account from one or more means of discovery if the server or account recently violated our Community Guidelines and received an enforcement action.
  1. Foster a healthy and positive environment. People should feel welcome in your server and its affiliated spaces. Create environments where people want to spend time with each other, share interests, participate in community events, and build friendships. Examples include:
  • No content or behavior meant to single-out, bully, or harass users and/or other communities. This includes off-platform spaces as well.
  • No discussions about controlled substances or drugs. This may get you reported to law enforcement.
  • No servers dedicated to use of regulated goods, such as alcohol.
  • Do not cultivate general toxic behavior or other derogatory content.

  1. Do not host graphic or sexual content. Graphic violence and sexual content are not allowed in public spaces. Servers opting into any publicly viewable feature should be appropriate for audiences of all ages 13+.

  2. Have a server name and description that accurately describes the server that is free of profanity. Help potential members understand why they want to join the server, conversations, and activities taking place.

  3. Respect people’s intellectual property and other rights. Only incorporate content that you own or have a license to use. Do not invade anyone’s privacy, libel them, or otherwise violate their rights.

  4. Have a moderator team. Moderators can help ensure nothing rule-breaking is happening in your server and its public spaces and can find meaningful ways for your members to engage. Build a moderator team that members of your community can trust and turn to for help.

We may consider off-platform behavior when assessing an account or server for violation of Discovery guidelines.

Enabling Server Discovery

Server Discovery is how a Community Server becomes a Discoverable Server, which anyone can find and join without an invite. Here’s how to turn it on, and where to go if you want to turn it off. Discoverable Servers also have a Server Web Page that anyone can find through web search. Summaries of public channels may appear on it from November 16, 2026, and messages can appear starting mid-December 2026. Both are on by default, and you can change which channels are included in your server’s Web Presence settings.

Not sure if your server is already Discoverable? Check the Discovery page in Server Settings.

What this article covers:

  • How to Enable Server Discovery
  • Looking to turn off Discoverability features?

How to Enable Server Discovery

Note: Members with the Manage Server or Administrator permission can enable and disable Server Discovery.

Your server needs to meet these requirements before you can enable Server Discovery:

  • Enabling safety requirements for a safe environment.
  • Server must have at least 1,000 members to qualify.
  • Servers need to be at least 8 weeks old to be in Discovery.
  • Servers must meet certain activity requirements to be in Discovery.
  • Your server name, description, and channel names follow the Discovery Guidelines.
  • Enable the 2FA Requirement For Moderation setting. Eligibility criteria may be updated over time, and servers are expected to continue meeting them to remain Discoverable.
  1. Open Server Settings by selecting your server’s name in the upper-left corner.
Server Settings Option in the Server Menu
  1. If your server isn’t a Community Server yet, select Enable Community, then select Get Started and follow the prompts to set up the required safety settings. Learn more in Enabling Your Community Server.
Enabling Community in Server Settings
  1. After your server has been set to Community, select Access, then select the Discoverable tab to see if your server meets the requirements for Server Discovery.
Discoverable Tab under Access
  1. If your server meets all Server Discovery requirements, select Save to turn your server into a Discoverable Server.

Looking to turn off Discoverability features?

See the Turning Off Discoverability section of Clarifying Server Types for how to turn off Discoverability and what changes when you do.

Important: If your server is Discoverable, disabling Community also turns off Discoverability automatically.

Want to learn more?
