How to Connect My Account for PlayStation Network from Discord

Note: You can connect your Discord account with your account for PlayStation Network, on every platform Discord is on: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and the Discord web app!

To connect your Discord account to your account for PlayStation Network, start by going to your Discord app on the desktop or mobile app!

In Discord, head into User Settings > Connections on desktop or web, or User Settings > Connection on mobile.

In the Connections tab, press the PlayStation Network icon and a new browser window will appear for you to authorize the connection to your account on PlayStation Network.

Sign in to your account on PlayStation Network with your credentials on the login page and when everything has been authorized, you’ll see a message confirming that your account for PlayStation Network is now all connected to Discord

In Discord, head into User Settings > Connections on desktop or web, or User Settings > Connection on mobile.

Connections tab

In the Connections tab, press the PlayStation Network icon and a new browser window will appear for you to authorize the connection to your account on PlayStation Network.

Sign in to PlayStation

Sign in to your account on PlayStation Network with your credentials on the login page and when everything has been authorized, you’ll see a message confirming that your account for PlayStation Network is now all connected to Discord!

Confirmation of successfully connected PlayStation account to your Discord account
How Do I Remove the Connection from My Account?

To remove the connection from your Discord account, you can go to the Connections tab in your User Settings once more.

Press the (X) symbol by the PlayStation connection option! You’ll then see a new menu pop up where you will need to confirm that you want to proceed by pressing the Disconnect button.

Once you’ve pressed Disconnect, the PlayStation connection will be removed from your Discord account.

X button to remove a connection

How to Display Connection & Game Activity on My Profile

Once connected, you’ll see two new options appear in the Connections tab for your account for PlayStation Network:

  • Display on User Profile
  • Display PlayStation Network as your status
Example of PlayStation connection under Connections tab
Display on User Profile

When you enable Display on User Profile, your PlayStation Network online ID will be displayed on your User Profile along with any other connections that you’ve decided to display.

Discord user profile showing PlayStation connection
Display PlayStation Network as your status

When you select Display PlayStation Network as your status, the game that you’re currently playing on PlayStation 4 or PlayStation 5 console will be displayed in your user profile for all your friends and community members to see.

User profile showing PlayStation game activity
Why isn’t my PlayStation Network status displaying on Discord?

If you are experiencing issues with your Game Activity status, we recommend that you check your PlayStation privacy settings to ensure ‘Anyone’ is enabled. If you would like to display your PSN status on Discord, follow these steps for your respective PlayStation console:

On PS4

  1. Go to your PlayStation account Home screen and navigate to Profile
PlayStation profile
  1. For PS4: Press Profile > Change Privacy Settings page.
Privacy settings on PS4
  1. Open up Privacy Settings and locate Personal Info | Messaging
Personal Info | Messaging on PlayStation
  1. Expand Online Status and Now Playing and make sure Anyone is enabled.
Online Status and Now Playing setting on PlayStation
Setting options for Online Status and Now Playing
  1. Go back to your Discord client and refresh to see if the issue persists.

On PS5

  1. Go to Settings.

  2. In Settings, go to Users and Accounts.

PS4 Settings
  1. Go to Privacy in the left-hand column, then choose View and Customize Your Privacy Settings.
PS5 View and Customize Your Privacy Settings
  1. Under the Who can see your online status and what you’re currently playing option, choose “Anyone”.
PS5 privacy settings
  1. Go back to your Discord client and refresh to see if the issue persists.

How to Voice Chat with Discord on PS5 Consoles

On PS5 console

Joining Discord directly is only available on your PS5 console.

  1. First make sure you’ve already connected your PlayStation account to your Discord account. If you haven’t yet, you can do so by following these steps above.

  2. Navigate to the Game Base in the PS5 Control Center.

  3. Next, select the Discord tab.

Discord tab on PlayStation
  1. Choose a voice channel in a server or group message to join.
Voice channels on PlayStation
  1. After selecting the correct voice channel, tap on Join to join through your PS5.
Join button while on PlayStation
On Discord Mobile app

  1. Ensure that your Discord account is connected to your account for PlayStation Network by following the steps in the How to Connect My PlayStation Network Account from Discord section above.

  2. Open the Discord app on your mobile device, navigate to the intended voice channel, swipe up for audio control, and then choose Join on PlayStation.

Transfer to PlayStation on mobile
  1. Within the app, a pop-up will appear that will allow you to choose the PS5 console associated with your account for PlayStation Network connected to your Discord account. Select the intended console and press Transfer Voice.

On your PS5, open up the console’s control center by pressing the PlayStation button on your controller and you’ll see the voice chat card with your transferred Discord voice chat. Selecting that card will show all your friends with you in the voice channel. You will also be able to manage your personal audio settings, see other peoples’ PSN accounts if they’re connected to their Discord accounts, and Report voice chat participants.

On Discord Desktop/Browser client

Transferring Discord voice chat is only available on the PS5. However, displaying your PlayStation Network status under your Discord account is available to all PS4 and PS5 users!

To transfer Discord voice chat to the PS5, please ensure your PS5 is updated to the latest system software!

  1. Ensure that your Discord account is connected to your account for PlayStation Network by following the steps in the How to Connect My PlayStation Network Account from Discord section above.

  2. Join the desired voice channel on your Discord desktop client. Then, in the focused voice channel view, press on the ellipses

[ ] and then Transfer Voice to PlayStation. You may also right click on the voice channel name.

Transfer to PlayStation on desktop/browser app

  1. Select Transfer to PlayStation.

  2. The Transfer Voice to PlayStation pop-up will appear that will allow you to choose the PS5 console associated with your account for PlayStation Network connected to your Discord account. Select the intended console and press Transfer Voice.

How to Complete Discord Quests on Your PlayStation

To get started, follow the steps above in the How to Connect My PlayStation Account from Discord section to properly connect your Discord and PlayStation accounts.

Verify Your Privacy Settings via PlayStation Website

  1. Via the PlayStation website, log in to your PlayStation Network account.

  2. Once you’re logged in, go to your Account Settings > Privacy Settings > Personal Info | Messaging.

  3. In Personal Info | Messaging, be sure to set your Online Status and Now Playing settings to “Anyone” to make progress on a Discord Quest.

Verify Your Privacy Settings on PS4 Console

  1. On your PS4 console, go to Settings > Account Management > Privacy Settings.

  2. Select Personal Info | Messages.

  3. Set Online Status and Now Playing to “Anyone”.

Note: Make sure your online status is not hidden:

  • On your PlayStation console, open your PSN profile.

  • Your Online Status should be “Online” and not “Appear Offline”.

Verify Your Privacy Settings on PS5 Console

  1. On your PS5 console, go to Settings > Users and Accounts > Privacy.

  2. Select View and Customize Your Privacy Settings.

  3. Set Who can see your online status and what you’re currently playing to “Anyone”.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I get Discord on PlayStation?

A: Discord isn’t a standalone app on PlayStation. Instead, you can connect your Discord and PlayStation accounts to display your gaming activity on Discord and use Discord voice chat on your PlayStation console. You’ll need both the Discord mobile app and PlayStation mobile app to set this up. Follow the connection instructions above to get started.

Q: Is the Discord activity status feature available for child accounts on PlayStation Network?

A: No, this feature is not available for child accounts on PlayStation Network. For more information, please refer to playstation.com.

Q: Is there a minimum age requirement to use Discord?

A: Please refer to this support article to learn more about the minimum age requirement to use Discord per country.

Q: Why won’t my Game Activity Status display correctly on Discord?

A: You will have to check your PlayStation Network settings. Specifically, you need to set your PSN Online Status and Now Playing privacy settings to “Anyone” for your status to also be visible on Discord. Follow these steps below:

For PS4:

  • Go to your PlayStation account Home screen and navigate to Profile.

  • Press Profile > Change Privacy Settings page.

  • Open up Privacy Settings and locate Personal Info | Messaging.

  • Expand Online Status and Now Playing and make sure Anyone is enabled.

  • Go back to your Discord client and refresh to see if the issue persists. For PS5

  • Go to Settings.

  • In Settings, go to Users and Accounts.

  • Go to Privacy in the left-hand column, then choose View and Customize Your Privacy Settings.

  • Under the “Who can see your online status and what you’re currently playing” option, choose Anyone.

  • Go back to your Discord client and refresh to see if the issue persists. Q: Why won’t my PlayStation Network status display when I’m streaming, listening to Spotify, or having a different game open on my computer?

A: This is due to how the client interacts with presence from other devices and activities. In other words, what you do locally on your computer will always take priority for what you see as an Activity status. In addition, rich presence will take priority over basic presence; which means the PlayStation Network integration won’t display while you’re also listening to Spotify or playing games which support rich presence.

Voice Transfer to PS5

Q: I already linked my account for PlayStation Network to my Discord account. Do I have to re-link my PSN and Discord account again?

A: If you’ve previously linked your Discord and PSN accounts, you’ll have to re-link them again in order to enable Discord Voice on PS5. If you participated in the beta for Discord voice chat on the PS5, you do not need to re-link your PSN account.

Q: I’m getting an error message when I try to transfer Discord voice to my PS5.

A: As an initial step, please make sure your console is up-to-date and to reset and reconnect your PSN/Discord accounts. Otherwise, if following the instructions indicated on the error messages doesn’t solve your issue, please reach out to our Discord support team with a screenshot of the error message you’re receiving so that we can provide next steps to help address your issue!

Q: Can I stay in a PlayStation Party while being part of Discord’s voice chat through the voice chat feature?

A: If you are in a Discord voice channel and you transfer the voice chat to your PlayStation, you will not be able to stay in a PlayStation Party when you are part of a Discord voice chat.

Q: I’m having issues with my audio on Discord!

A: If you’re having trouble with your audio on Discord before transferring the voice chat to PS5, please check out our various support articles here. If you need further assistance, please reach out to the Discord support team!

Q: I’m having issues with my audio after I transfer Discord voice chat to the PS5!

A: If you’re having issues with your audio on the PS5, check out this article first: playstation.com

Q: How does Discord’s privacy & safety standard apply when using Discord voice chat on PS5?

A: When chatting on PS5 with Discord Voice, Discord’s policies and safety standards apply.

Q: Are PSN child accounts able to use the Discord voice chat transfer feature?

A: Yes! For parents and family managers, you may control your child’s access and use of communication features, including access to Discord, through the Communication and User-Generated Content parental control setting.

To restrict access to linked social account experiences, parents and family managers must unlink any previously linked social accounts and select Restrict in the Communication and User-Generated Content parental control setting.

For more information on setting parental controls, please refer to this support article here.

How To Link Your Discord And Xbox Accounts

Tip: Each Discord account supports one linked Xbox account at a time. If you’d like to connect a different Xbox account, simply remove your current connection first.

To take full advantage of an Xbox connection for your Discord experience, you will need to connect your Discord and Xbox accounts. Connecting your Xbox account to your Discord account means you can:

  • Display your Xbox GamerTag
  • Display your Xbox game activity
  • Display how long you’ve been playing on your Xbox console
  • Use Discord voice chat on your Xbox console
How To Connect My Xbox Account From Discord

Info: If you connect your Discord and Xbox accounts prior to Discord Voice on Xbox becoming available to you, you’ll have to relink your accounts again to use Discord voice chat on Xbox.

On Desktop/Browser

  1. Press on the cogwheel [] at the bottom-left of your client to go to your User Settings and then navigate to the Connections tab.

  2. Select the Xbox icon and press Continue to begin the account linking.

Navigating to Connections to Connect to Xbox

  1. To establish the connection of your Discord and Xbox accounts, pressing Continue will open a browser page for you to provide your Microsoft account credentials.

  2. After you read over the in-client authorization message, press Authorize and Continue.

Authorize and Continue Button in Connection Window
  1. And that’s it! You can now show your Xbox GamerTag, game activity, and how long you’ve been playing on Xbox in your Discord user profile.
Example of Successful Xbox Connection

On Mobile

  1. Navigate to User Settings on your Discord mobile app by tapping your avatar icon in the bottom-right corner.

  2. Select the cogwheel [] in the upper-right corner to navigate to Settings > Connections.

Navigating to Settings > Connections
  1. Select the Xbox icon. You can also tap Add in the upper-right corner to add a new connection.
Xbox Icon (Left), Add Button to Add New Connection (Right)
  1. The app will let you know that you will need to connect both your Xbox and Discord accounts. Press Getting Started.
Get Started Button in Connection Window

  1. To establish the connection of your Discord and Xbox accounts, press Continue which will open an in-app browser page for you to provide your Microsoft account credentials.

  2. After you read over the in-client authorization message, press Authorize and Continue.

Authorize and Continue Button in Connection Window
  1. Your accounts are now connected! You can now show your Xbox GamerTag, game activity, and how long you’ve been playing on Xbox in your Discord user profile. Don’t forget to download the Xbox app on your mobile device for Discord Voice on your Xbox console!
Example of Successful Xbox Connection
How To Connect My Discord Account From Xbox

On Xbox app

  1. Open the Xbox app on the mobile device and select the Discord spotlight on the app’s homepage.
Discord Spotlight in Xbox App
  1. The app will let you know that you will need to connect both your Xbox and Discord accounts. Press Continue.
Continue Button

  1. Input your Discord credentials and press Login.

  2. Input your Microsoft credentials and press Login.

  3. Your accounts are now connected! You can now show your Xbox GamerTag, game activity, and how long you’ve been playing on Xbox in your Discord user profile.

On Xbox Console

  1. Log into your Xbox device and press the Xbox button on the controller to open the console’s guide.
Example of Xbox Console Guide View
  1. Navigate through Profile & System > Settings > Account > Linked social accounts.
Settings Button in Xbox Console Guide
Linked social accounts Button in Account

  1. Under the Not Linked section, choose the Discord tile and select Link.

  2. Follow the prompts to connect your Discord and Xbox accounts.

On Desktop App

X Icon in Xbox Connection

Disconnect Button in Disconnect Xbox Window

How to Use Discord Voice Chat on Your Xbox Console

On Xbox Console

  1. Make sure to follow the steps above in the How to Connect My Xbox Account from Discord section to properly connect your Discord and Xbox accounts.

  2. Log into your Xbox device with your Xbox account connected to your Discord account and press the Xbox button on the controller to open the console’s guide.

  3. Navigate to Parties & chats then select Discord Voice in the menu list.

  4. Select the Discord server with the desired voice channel.

  5. Choose the voice channel to join a Discord voice channel from your Xbox console.

On Discord Mobile App

  1. Make sure to follow the steps above in the How to Connect My Xbox Account from Discord section to properly connect your Discord and Xbox accounts.

  2. Once you have connected your accounts, you must install the Xbox app from your mobile device’s app store.

If you don’t install the Xbox app, you will not be able to transfer Discord Voice to your Xbox console.

  1. On your Discord app, select a voice channel, swipe up for audio control settings, and select Join on Xbox.

  2. If you’ve downloaded the Xbox app on your mobile device, it will open at this point. If not, you will be prompted to download it from your device’s app store. Once you have the Xbox app downloaded, choose the Xbox console you would like to transfer the Discord audio to then press Transfer Audio.

  3. And that’s it! In your Discord mobile app, you will be able to Mute and Deafen your audio by swiping up in the voice channel, which will be reflected in your Xbox Console.

You should also see in your Xbox under Parties & Chats the connected Discord voice chat, its participants, and other audio management settings. You can also Report voice chat participants to Discord from your Xbox console.

Info: You will not be able to communicate outside of your Xbox console if your Privacy Settings in the Xbox mobile app is set to “In-game friends” or “Blocked”.

  • To join cross-network play > set this to Allow

  • To communicate outside of Xbox with voice & text > set this to Everybody.

On Discord Desktop Client

  1. Make sure to follow the steps above in the How to Connect My Xbox Account from Discord section to properly connect your Discord and Xbox accounts.

  2. Once you have connected your accounts, you must install the Xbox app from your mobile device’s app store.

If you don’t install the Xbox app, you will not be able to transfer Discord Voice to your Xbox console.

  1. On your Discord desktop client, join your desired voice channel. Then press on the bottom left phone + game controller icon in the bottom left of the focused voice channel view. You may also right click on the voice channel name.

  2. Select Transfer Voice to Xbox.

  3. A QR code will appear in your client and you must scan the code on your mobile device. It is crucial that you download the Discord mobile app and the Xbox mobile app on your mobile device.

  4. Follow the prompts on your Discord mobile app to complete the Discord voice transfer to Xbox.

How To Complete Discord Quests On Your Xbox

To get started, follow the steps above in the How to Connect My Xbox Account from Discord section to properly connect your Discord and Xbox accounts.

Verify Your Privacy Settings Via Xbox Website

  1. Via the Xbox website, log in to your Microsoft account.

  2. Once you’re logged in, go to Xbox Settings > Privacy Settings Management > Others Can.

  3. While there, set the Others can see if you’re online option to “Anyone” to make progress on a Discord Quest.

Other can Settings in Xbox Privacy Settings

You can accomplish this on your account via Xbox website or directly on your Xbox console

Verify Your Privacy Settings On Xbox Series X/S Console

  1. On your Xbox Series X/S console, go to Settings > Accounts > Privacy & online safety.

  2. Then, navigate to Xbox privacy > View details & customize > Online status & history.

  3. Once there, set the Others can see if you’re online option to “Everybody”.

Info: Make sure your online status is not hidden:

  • On your Xbox console, go to Xbox home screen and open your Xbox profile.

  • Your Xbox status should be “Appear online” and not “Appear offline”.

Stream Gameplay To Discord From Xbox

Want to learn more?

Check out our blog post on Streaming to Discord from Xbox!

Stream your game option in Xbox Console Guide

Eager to stream your Xbox gameplay to your friends on Discord? Follow the steps below!

If you are having trouble streaming to Discord from Xbox, please refer to Xbox’s “Why can’t I live stream my game?” support article. For general tips on how to livestream your Xbox gameplay, please check out Xbox’s “How to live stream on Xbox” support article.

  1. Your Xbox account and Discord account must be linked first! To link your accounts, please follow the steps in the How To Link Your Discord And Xbox Accounts section. If you have already linked your accounts, you do not need to relink your Discord and Xbox accounts.

  2. Log into your Xbox Series X|S or Xbox One device with your Xbox account connected to your Discord account and press the Xbox button on the controller to open the console’s guide.

  3. Navigate to Parties & chats then select Discord from the menu.

  4. Select the Discord server and then the server’s voice channel you want to stream to.

  5. Once you’ve joined the voice channel, press the Stream your game option in the dedicated Xbox menu for your Discord chat on console.

  6. You can adjust your stream’s resolution and frame rate if you have a Nitro subscription on your Discord account. When you’re ready, press Start stream.

Info: The 60 FPS option is unavailable on Xbox One.

  1. You are now streaming your Xbox gameplay to Discord! If you would like to stop streaming from Xbox, you can find the Stop streaming option and other livestream settings in the dedicated Parties & chats menu for your Discord chat on Xbox.

Contact Support:

If you are experiencing issues with streaming from the Xbox console, please reach out to Xbox support here.

How to View Your Discord Friend’s List on Your Xbox

If you’ve connected your Xbox account to Discord, you can opt-in to have your Discord friends displayed in the Xbox Guide Friends List. Your Discord friends will be displayed under Happening now, if they are playing a game or chatting in a Discord voice channel.

How to Watch a Stream on Your Xbox

You can now watch a stream on Discord through your Xbox console. Here’s how:

  1. Open up your active call’s member list within the Xbox guide.

  2. Select the profile of someone that is currently streaming and then tap on Watch Stream.

  3. Their stream should now display in full-screen for you to watch and enjoy!

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I get Discord on Xbox?

A: Discord isn’t a standalone app on Xbox. Instead, you can connect your Discord and Xbox accounts to display your gaming activity on Discord and use Discord voice chat on your Xbox console. You’ll need both the Discord mobile app and Xbox mobile app to set this up. Follow the connection instructions above to get started.

Q: I’m running into the error “Transfer didn’t work. Your console needs an update before it can connect to Discord.”

A: Before you can join Discord Voice on your Xbox console, you must make sure your Xbox console is updated to the latest version.

Q: I already linked my Xbox account to my Discord account. Why do I have to re-link my Xbox and Discord account again?

A: If you have previously linked your Discord and Xbox accounts, you will need to re-link them to access the latest Discord features on Xbox.

Q: Can I stay in the Xbox Party Chat while being part of Discord’s voice chat or streaming to Discord from Xbox?

A: If you are in a Discord voice channel and you transfer the voice chat to your Xbox console or you start streaming to Discord from your console, you will not be able to stay in an Xbox Party Chat.

Q: Can I stay in the Xbox Party Chat while being part of Discord’s voice chat through the Voice Chat feature?

A: If you are in a Discord voice channel and you transfer the voice chat to your Xbox console, you will not be able to stay in an Xbox Party Chat when you are part of a Discord voice chat.

Q: I’m having issues with my audio on Discord!

A: If you’re having trouble with your audio on Discord before transferring the voice chat to Xbox, please check out our various support articles here. If you need further assistance, please reach out to the Discord Support team!

Q: I’m having issues with my audio after I transfer Discord voice chat to the Xbox console!

A: Please refer to this Xbox support article: support.xbox.com

Q: I’m having issues with my Xbox gameplay stream after I started streaming to Discord from the Xbox console!

A: If you’re having issues with your Xbox gameplay stream to Discord, please refer to this Xbox support article: support.xbox.com

Q: Why can’t I view a Discord stream on my Xbox due to an unsupported stream resolution?

A: Currently, Xbox supports viewing Discord streams at resolutions of 480p, 720p, 1080p, and 1440p. If you encounter an issue with stream resolution, please request the streamer to adjust their stream to one of these supported resolutions.

Q: If I am a Nitro subscriber and I stream using my linked Xbox account from the Xbox console to Discord, will my HD streaming perk apply?

A: Yes! If you have a Nitro subscription on your Discord account and your Xbox and Discord accounts are linked, you will be able to stream to Discord at higher quality, up to 1080p and either 60fps on Xbox Series X|S or 30fps on Xbox One.

You must stream from the applicable Xbox console utilizing the Xbox account linked to your Discord account with the Nitro subscription.

Q: How does Discord’s privacy & safety standard apply when using Discord Voice on Xbox and Stream to Discord from Xbox?

A: Even when chatting on Xbox with Discord Voice and streaming to Discord from Xbox, Discord’s policies and safety standards will still apply.

Q: Am I able to watch Discord streams from my Xbox?

A: Yes, you can watch Discord streams on your Xbox.

Q: What am I able to stream to Discord from my Xbox console?

A: You can stream the audio and video of any game you’re currently playing on your Xbox console! All other non-game apps and Xbox services available on your Xbox console are not streamable to Discord.

Q: What happens when I switch to a different app in Xbox or I close the game I’m streaming to Discord from my Xbox console?

A: If you switch to a different app or close the game you’re streaming, your stream to the Discord voice channel or direct message/group message will be paused. However, you will still be in the Discord voice channel on Xbox and still be heard by your friends in Discord.

Q: Is there a minimum age requirement to use Discord?

A: Please refer to this support article to learn more about the minimum age requirement to use Discord per country.

Q: Do I need to change my privacy settings on Xbox to transfer my Discord voice chat to the console?

A: Yes, you must adjust your privacy settings on Xbox to allow the transfer of Discord voice chat to the console. Check out the “Privacy error setting” section near the bottom of this Xbox support article: support.xbox.com

Q: Do I need to change my privacy settings on Xbox to stream to Discord from the Xbox console?

A: Yes, you must adjust your privacy settings on Xbox in order to stream to Discord from the console. Check out the “Privacy & online safety” section in this Xbox support article: support.xbox.com

Q: I have parental controls enabled on my child’s Xbox account/console. How does that interact with Discord?

A: For more information and support on Xbox’s parental controls, please go to the “Privacy error setting” section near the bottom of this Xbox support article: support.xbox.com

Additionally, Xbox child accounts aren’t allowed to stream, as referred to under the “Child accounts” section in this Xbox support article: support.xbox.com

Q: I have an issue with my Microsoft/Xbox account!

A: For general information and help with Microsoft/Xbox accounts, please refer to support.xbox.com

Discord on Meta Quest FAQ

Discord is available to download directly from the Meta Horizon Store — bringing the full Discord experience to your Meta Quest headset.

What this article covers:

  • Is Discord Available on Meta Quest?
  • How to Download Discord on Meta Quest
  • What Discord Features Are Available on Meta Quest?
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Is Discord Available on Meta Quest?

If you’re a Meta Quest user, you can use Discord while in your VR experience. Through Meta Quest, you can access the full Discord app, like your servers, direct messages (DMs), group DMs, voice/video calls, without needing a separate device or using the VR headset web browser.

You can get Discord on your Meta Quest by downloading the app through the Meta Horizon Store.

A Discord server as seen in the Discord app on a Meta Quest device.

How to Download Discord on Meta Quest

Discord is available to download from the Meta Horizon Store. You can find it directly from your headset or through the Meta website.

  1. Open the Meta Horizon Store on your Meta Quest headset, or visit the Meta Horizon Store page on your web browser.

  2. Select Install (or Get) to install Discord on your headset.

  3. Once installed, open the Discord app and log in to your existing Discord account, or create a new account if you don’t have one yet.

The Discord app on the Meta Horizon Store for installation.

Note: Note: If you’re having issues with the Meta Horizon store or downloading the Discord app to your Meta Quest, please reach out to Meta Support.

What Discord Features Are Available on Meta Quest?

Discord on Meta Quest includes all the features you’re used to from the Discord app, including:

  • Your servers, DMs, and Group DMs
  • Voice calls using your headset’s built-in microphone
  • Video calls if you’ve set up a Meta Avatar
  • Streaming Meta Quest gameplay to your friend on Discord

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Do I need a new Discord account to use Discord on Meta Quest?

A: No. You can log in with your existing Discord account. If you don’t have one yet, you can create a new account directly from the app on your headset.

Q: Is Discord on Meta Quest free to download?

A: Yes. Discord is free to download from the Meta Horizon Store. Some features require a Discord Nitro subscription.

Q: Where can I download Discord for my Meta Quest headset?

A: You can find the Discord app in the Meta Horizon Store on your headset or on your browser.

Q: What Meta Quest devices is Discord available on?

A: Discord is available to use on the following Meta Quest devices: Quest 2, Quest Pro, and Quest 3 series.

Q: Can I use Discord voice and video calls while in VR?

A: Yes. Because Meta Quest headsets have a built-in microphone, you can join Discord voice and video calls directly from your headset without needing a separate device. You can also use your Meta Avatar in video calls if you’ve created one.

Q: I’m having issues with my Discord app on my Meta Quest device.

A: If you’re having issues with the Discord app itself, please reach out to our Support team. If you’re having issues with your Meta Quest device, please reach out to Meta Support.

Q: Does Meta see my activity in Discord because I use the app on Meta Quest?

A: No. Using the Discord app on Meta Quest is like using Discord on any other supported device.

Q: How does Discord use my data when I use the Discord app on Meta Quest?

A: Discord uses your data consistent with our Privacy Policy, like on any other device.

Discord Spotify Connection

What this article covers:

  • How to Connect Spotify to Discord
  • How Spotify Displays on Mini-Profile and Profile
  • Inviting your Friends to Listen

How to Connect Spotify to Discord

  1. Open up the Discord app and next to your username access the cog wheel to open up your User Settings.

  2. Under your User Settings head to Connections.

  3. Connect your Spotify account by pressing on the Spotify tile and then logging into your Spotify account.

Once your Spotify is connected, you can also change how it displays through on your Discord account profile.

To do this, head to User Settings > Connections and then you can toggle Display on Profile and Display Spotify as your status.

If you are transmitting with your mic in voice chat for 30 seconds while Spotify is playing, Spotify will stop playing! For more info check out this article.

How Spotify Displays on Mini-Profile and Profile

Once Spotify has been connected to a Discord account, what someone is listening to can be seen on both the mini and full profile (if enabled).

If someone is actively using Spotify, you can use the Play on Spotify option or Listen Along to join them while viewing their profile.

Inviting Your Friends To Listen

For friends to listen along, they’ll need to have Spotify Premium or they’ll receive an error.

Not only can you invite your friends to listen to your music, but you can also join them and listen to theirs!

While Spotify is playing, click the + in your text box to invite your friend(s) to listen with you. You can send this either through a Direct Message, Group Direct Message, or even through a specific channel.

You’ll get a Message Preview of your invite, and you’ll be able to add a comment before sending it.

After sending the invite, your friends will be able to click Join and listen to your sweet tunes with you.

The invite link is also dynamic and will change when you change songs. The invite will show the session has ended if you stop your music and will update again when you resume playing!

You’ll be able to see what friends are listening with you on the bottom left of your app:

And that’s it! Enjoy sharing and listening to sweet tunes with your friends.

If you have additional questions or any issues, please reach out to our support team: dis.gd.

How Games Integrate Discord-Powered Features

Discord offers tools that game developers can use to power various social and communication features within their games. For you as a player, this means some aspects of your in-game experience will be powered by Discord—which can include in-game voice chat and friends lists, as well as the ability to directly link your Discord account to unlock additional features (such as a combined friends list and seamless messaging across the game and Discord).

You can enjoy what you love about Discord directly in your game! Even without a Discord account, it’s never been easier to keep the party going—whether you’re actively playing or just hanging out.

What this article covers:

  • How do I make the most out of my linked Discord account?
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How do I Make the Most Out of My Linked Discord Account?

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Does that mean I need a registered Discord account to play the game?

A: Players will not be required to connect a registered Discord account to play games that integrate Discord-powered social features.

Q: Can I exchange messages with my friends on Discord while playing this game?

A: Yes, in some games, players are able to exchange messages with friends across Discord while they’re in-game, even if their friends aren’t playing in the same game.

Q: Will this integration impact my game performance?

A: These integrations are designed to avoid impacting game performance.

Q: Am I required to use the in-game features that enable me to send/receive Discord messages and view my Discord friends from within a game?

A: No, the social features that enable you to to send/receive Discord messages and view your Discord friends from within a game are optional. You can choose whether to use them.

Q: Do I need to connect my Discord account to view my Discord friends on my in-game friends list?

A: Yes. If you want to view your Discord friends on your in-game friends list, you will need to connect your Discord account.

Q: Do I need to connect my Discord account to be able to send or receive messages in the game?

A: You can use the game’s messaging features without connecting your Discord account. In-game communication functions, such as direct messages with friends, can work without the need for a connected Discord account.

If you choose to connect your Discord account, you’ll gain the added convenience of sending and receiving some of those same in-game messages on Discord. The connection simply extends where you can access your conversations – your friends can continue chatting with you in-game even if they haven’t connected their own Discord accounts.

Q: Why can’t I see a certain feature in a game with this integration?

A: Developers control which features are implemented in their game and when. Check out the game’s support resources or reach out to the developer to learn more about what’s currently available or ask about additional features you want to see.

Q: What will the game developer be able to do with my Discord messages?

A: Before connecting your Discord account, you’ll see a clear permissions screen outlining the data that you’re authorizing the game to receive from your Discord account. Developers are only permitted to use this data to power the integration, which includes accessing messages that appear in their game for moderation purposes.

For more information about the developer’s data practices, please review the developer’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. You can review and revoke your account connection at any time through your Discord Connections tab within the User Settings.

Q: What will Discord do with my messages from the game that appear in Discord?

A: Messages sent from the game that appear on Discord are treated like any other message on Discord consistent with Discord’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

Q: Which messages from the game will be synced with Discord?

A: Direct messages with a Discord user or in-game friends will be shown in Discord for linked users.

Lobby text messages will not be in Discord, unless that lobby is linked to a Discord channel.

Messages in Linked Channels will be displayed in Discord, regardless of whether an account is linked.

Q: If I’m messaging someone on Discord, how can I tell when they’re messaging me from within a game?

A: When a user is sending a message from within a game, a controller icon will appear next to their name as a visual indicator.

Q: How can I tell when I’m sending messages in a Linked Channel?

A: There are a few visual indicators that you are viewing a Linked Channel while on Discord. You will see a controller icon at the top right corner of the channel symbol. You will also see the title of the game that’s linked.

In the desktop app, it will be next to the channel name in the header; in the mobile app, it will be in the channel profile. In addition, a system message will be sent in the channel notifying members that the channel has been linked to a game.

Note: If you’re running into an issue connecting your Discord account to your game, please reach out to the game developer for further assistance. Discord Support is not able to assist with in-game connection of accounts.

How to Connect your Bluesky account to Discord

What this article covers:

  • What is Bluesky?
  • How to Connect Bluesky to your Discord Account
  • An Unknown Error Occurred. Maybe check your handle?
  • Using a Custom Domain with Bluesky
    • Custom PDS Providers
    • did:web: accounts

What is Bluesky?

Bluesky is a social media platform that allows you to post short messages, photos, videos and more.

How to Connect Bluesky to your Discord Account

  1. Head into your User Settings by pressing the cogwheel [] icon.

  2. Tap on the Connections tab and then the Bluesky butterfly icon.

Connections tab under User Settings
  1. Type in your handle for Bluesky and then follow the on-screen instructions to connect your account.
Example of where you enter your Bluesky Account handle
  1. You’ll know you’ve successfully connected when you receive this confirmation message:
Confirmation window that your Bluesky account has been connected to Discord

An Unknown Error Occurred. Maybe check your handle?

If we can’t find a Bluesky account associated with the handle you enter, you’ll see an error message like this:

Error example when the wrong handle has been entered

This usually means you’ve made a typo when entering the handle, so please make sure to double-check the account name that you have entered.

If your account uses a custom domain or custom PDS, see Using a Custom Domain with Bluesky below for more details. Otherwise, it’s possible that you may be hitting a temporary server error due to excessive load on the Bluesky network and you’ll have to try connecting your Bluesky account again later.

Using a Custom Domain with Bluesky

In order to link a Bluesky account with a custom-domain handle, Discord will need to look up your account’s DID. This happens when you initially connect the Bluesky account on Discord and then on an ongoing basis to keep your account connected to Discord.

Verification happens in the same way described in the AT Protocol documentation and the Bluesky blog.

When verifying a domain using the /.well-known/atproto-did method, Discord will use a user-agent string in the form of Discord/1.0 (Discord API; +https://discordapp.com.

Please ensure that your web server does not block requests with this user-agent, or severely rate-limit requests to this endpoint.

You can simulate the request Discord will make to verify your handle using a curl command in this form: curl -H 'User-Agent: Discord/1.0 (Discord API; +https://discordapp.com)' https://{your-handle-here}/.well-known/atproto-did

Custom PDS Providers

Discord supports linking AT Protocol accounts hosted by third-party PDS providers in the same way as accounts hosted by Bluesky. If hosting your own PDS, please ensure that your web server allows Discord’s user-agent on the authentication and PDS data endpoints, in addition to the /.well-known/atproto-did endpoint.

did:web: accounts

Discord also supports linking AT Protocol accounts that use did:web: identifiers. The requirements for the /.well-known/atproto-did endpoint also apply to the /.well-known/did.json endpoint.

Note: If you run into any issues with linking your Bluesky account to your Discord account, please reach out to our support team through here: dis.gd

Data Privacy

App Tracking Transparency for iOS

App Tracking Transparency is a privacy feature that gives iOS users control over how apps access and share their data. This guide explains what this permission is, why Discord uses it, and how it enhances your privacy while using the app.

What this article covers:

  • What is App Tracking Transparency for iOS?
  • Why Does Discord Need this Permission?
  • Your Privacy Choices
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What is App Tracking Transparency for iOS?

App Tracking Transparency is Apple’s privacy framework that requires apps to obtain user consent before accessing device identifiers used for tracking. This helps users make informed choices about their privacy while using iOS apps.

Why Does Discord Need this Permission?

Discord uses tracking to enhance your experience with Quests and mobile features. When you allow tracking:

  • You’ll receive more personalized Quests that match your interests
  • Discord can better support game developers and businesses that rely on ads for discovery
  • The platform can continue providing a high-quality, free service to users

Your Privacy Choices

When prompted about tracking, you have two options:

  • Allow: Discord can access your device identifier to provide personalized Quests and experiences
  • Ask App Not to Track: Discord will respect your choice and not access your device identifier You can modify this choice at any time through your Privacy & Security settings or App settings in your iOS device’s Discord app settings. Whether you allow tracking or not, you’ll still have full access to Discord’s core features.
App Tracking Transparency Notification

Info: Discord remains committed to protecting your privacy. For more information about how we handle your data, please visit our Privacy Policy.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Does allowing tracking affect my Discord messaging experience?

A: No, your core Discord features including messaging, voice chat, and server participation remain fully functional regardless of your tracking choice.

Q: Can I change my tracking preferences later?

A: Yes, you can modify your tracking preferences at any time through your iOS device settings under Privacy & Security > Tracking.

Q: What exactly is a device identifier?

A: A device identifier is a unique code that helps identify your device. For iOS, this is known as the Identifier for Advertisers (IDFA) and is used to deliver personalized experiences and advertising.

Q: Will Discord sell my data if I allow tracking?

A: No, Discord does not sell your personal data. The tracking permission is used solely to enhance your in-app experience and provide relevant Quests and features.

Q: How does tracking improve my Quests experience?

A: Tracking helps Discord understand your interests and activity patterns, allowing it to suggest Quests that are more likely to appeal to you and match your gaming preferences.

Q: Is my personal information safe if I allow tracking?

A: Yes, Discord maintains strict security measures and follows privacy regulations to protect your personal information, regardless of your tracking preferences.

Data Privacy Controls

Discord’s Data Privacy Controls explains how your information is used and provides options for how to control your data and manage the way Discord uses your information.

These settings can be found under User Settings > Privacy & Safety > How We Use Your Data.

Data Privacy Control Settings in Data & Privacy on the desktop app

Learn more about each specific setting here:

  • Data Used to Improve Discord
  • Data Used to Personalize Discord
  • Data Used for Sponsored Content
  • Profile Privacy Setting on Discord

Requests may be “incomplete” for a variety of reasons, including if we were unable to verify a user’s account, the user provided an invalid or no email address, or the request was pending and completed in the following calendar year.

As described in our Privacy Policy, Discord does not sell your personal information to third parties.

Data Used for Sponsored Content on Discord

Sponsored content is paid for by our partners, such as game developers, who want to offer our users a reward for engaging with their game or related content via Quests while using Discord.

We may tell you about sponsored content that we think will interest you based on your use of Discord and your activities on the services that are associated with your Discord account, as well as data about you that we may receive from advertisers and third-party data providers.

If you’re not interested in receiving personalized sponsored content based on your use of Discord and your activities on the services that are associated with your Discord account, you can control the use of this data.

If you’re not interested in receiving personalized sponsored content based on data about you that we may receive from advertisers and third-party data providers—including how you engage with games and other content or services outside of Discord—you can also opt out of this use of your data.

Desktop/Browser

  1. On the Discord desktop app or browser client, go to User Settings > Data & Privacy > How Discord uses your data.

  2. Configure these options:

  • Use data based on my Discord activity to personalize sponsored content: Uses your Discord activity to surface relevant sponsored content.
  • Use data from third party sources about me to personalize sponsored content: Uses your data from advertisers and other third parties to surface relevant sponsored content.
Data & Privacy controls in Data & Privacy

Mobile

  1. On the Discord mobile app, go to Settings > Data & Privacy > How Discord uses your data.

  2. Adjust the Use data based on my Discord activity to personalize sponsored content and the Use data from third party sources about me to personalize sponsored content options to your preference. Learn more about these options as described above.

Data & Privacy controls in Data & Privacy on mobile

Important Notes:

  • If you disable the use of data based on Discord activity to personalize sponsored content, Discord will also disable the use of data from third party sources. By contrast, if you choose not to allow the use of data from third party sources to personalize sponsored content, this will have no impact on personalization based on your Discord activity.
  • This supports an opt out for residents of certain U.S. states who are entitled to an applicable opt out under those state laws (please refer here).
  • If you opt out of personalization using these controls, you may still see sponsored content, like Quests, but they won’t be personalized. For example, you may see a Quest when you’re in a particular server, where anyone in that server sees the same Quest.

Data Used to Improve Discord

We use certain information to help us understand and improve Discord and to develop features that make Discord safer and better for you to use. This includes information such as how you use our services, the games you play, and how servers are structured.

Turning the Use Data to Improve Discord setting off means we will no longer collect new information about how you use and/or navigate Discord in order to understand and improve our products. We may continue to use the information we collected when the setting was enabled. More detail can be found in our Privacy Policy.

On desktop, head to User Setting > Data & Privacy and on mobile, head to Settings > Data & Privacy to disable the Use Data to Improve Discord toggle.

Use data to improve Discord toggle in Data & Privacy on Desktop

It will also prevent us from automatically improving the quality of voice or video communications on Discord based on your usage.

If you’d like to further assert your right to object to our processing of your data, email privacy@discord.com.

When you turn the setting off, the signals associated with your use of Discord continue to be sent, but we do not use the information for the purposes described above. This is an account-based setting and applies to your use of Discord regardless of the device used to access your account. This allows us to keep your account experience consistent across devices and access points of Discord.

Data Used to Personalize Discord

We use certain information to personalize our services. This includes features like customizing your experience on our discovery surfaces, highlighting activity on Discord that may interest you, and surfacing Discord features and promotions from us and our partners that may be of interest to you. For example, we may use information about who you interact with to rank a Friend who you interact with often higher in the “Active Now” section of your Friends List.

The information used to power personalized features for you include:

  • The games you play
  • Who you interact with
  • The way you use Discord
  • Connections made between your Discord account and another service (e.g., Xbox or Steam)
  • The servers you join On desktop, head to User Setting > Data & Privacy and on mobile, head to Settings > Data & Privacy to disable the Use data to personalize my Discord experience toggle.

Use data to personalize my Discord experience toggle in Data & Privacy on Desktop

Disabling the Use data to personalize my Discord experience toggle means we will no longer use information specific to your account to power features that recommend content or promotions to you.

Your ability to access conversations, voice channels, or other spaces on Discord will not be impacted by this setting.

Digital Services Act - Information on Average Monthly Active Recipients in the European Union

Last updated: August 17, 2026

Discord is committed to working with regulators worldwide to meet our obligations in the countries in which we operate, including the EU Digital Services Act (“DSA”).

The DSA is a new law that regulates many different types of online services. One aspect of the law (Article 24(2) for the law wonks) requires online platforms to publish information about the average monthly active recipients of their services in the European Union.

Under the DSA, some elements of the services Discord provides may qualify as an online platform. We’ve calculated the average number of monthly active recipients of these services in the EU for the six months from January 1, 2026 through June 30, 2026 and that number is well below 45 million.

This information was prepared for the DSA and its specific requirements. It may differ from Discord user metrics reported in other contexts and should not be used for other purposes.

End-to-End Encryption for Audio and Video

What this article covers:

  • How to Verify that a Call is End-to-End Encrypted
  • How to Verify Participants on a Call
  • Persistent Verification Keys
  • Managing Verified Devices
  • Frequently Asked Questions Important: All audio and video conversations in direct messages (DMs), group messages (GDMs), voice channels, and Go Live streams on Discord will require end-to-end encryption starting on March 2nd, 2026. You must ensure that your Discord app is on the latest version to support the end-to-end encryption requirement. Learn more about the minimum requirements here.

End-to-end encryption for audio and video (E2EE A/V) on Discord makes your calls even more private and secure by default. This added layer of security for audio and video calls gives visual confirmation that no one else can listen in on your calls or watch your stream besides the intended participants/viewers.

Below explains how to verify that a call is end-to-end encrypted and how to confirm that the people who you are on a call with are verified too.

Note: Desktop and mobile calls between users with updated clients are end-to-end encrypted without any user action. The features described in this article do not “turn on” end-to-end encryption. We developed these features to show our work and help you confirm that our end-to-end encryption is functioning as intended.

How to Verify That a Call is End-to-End Encrypted

You can verify that your voice call on Discord is end-to-end encrypted by checking the Voice/Video Details of the call.

On the desktop app, open the Voice/Video Details in the bottom left corner of the app to see a new Privacy tab, as well as a green lock icon stating that your call is End-to-end encrypted.

On the mobile app, you can find that green lock icon while in a voice call by pressing on the voice channel name in the top left corner of the focused voice call view.

The Privacy tab contains the Voice Privacy Code for the call. Privacy codes can be compared with other voice call participants to confirm that everyone in the call sees the same code. Comparing codes should occur out-of-band, for example on a different communication platform.

Note: Privacy codes are long so we split them up into groups of five digits to make them easier to read.

Privacy codes update when participants join or leave calls, so these codes must be compared at the same time with all current call participants in order to verify that the call is end-to-end encrypted.

Each Go Live stream associated with a call also has a Stream Privacy Code that can be accessed via the context menu for the stream, which you can find by right-clicking directly on the Go Live stream and selecting it from the dropdown menu.

By verifying the privacy code for the voice call or for any Go Live stream in the call, you can confirm that all participants have the same encrypted view of the call and that no unexpected participants have joined the call.

How to Verify Participants on a Call

Whether you’re on a call with your best friend, or a group of people in a voice channel on your favorite server, you can choose to verify the identity of the people you’re on a call with for an additional layer of privacy assurance.

  1. Navigate to “View Verification Code”.
  • On Desktop, right click on the user in the voice call members list or right click on their tile in the call view and select View Verification Code from the dropdown menu.
  • On Mobile, open the user’s profile either from the call member list or by long pressing on their call tile and then select View Verification Code.
  1. You will then see a series of numbers that should match for both you and the person you’re on a call with.

Note: When you show the Verification Code for another participant, you may see a warning if you have previously verified that participant and the code has changed.

  1. Compare the codes out-of-band (via a different communication platform) with the person you’re speaking with.

  2. If the codes are a match, then you can select Mark as Verified to confirm that you have successfully verified who you are chatting with.

Once you’ve verified each person in the call, a small icon will appear next to their name in the call to confirm this action is complete.

These codes are device-specific and change every time you join a new call with that person by default. With each new call, you will have to repeat the verification process.

You can opt-in to persistent verification keys to make the verification others perform of your given device permanent. More information on how to do this in the next section.

Note: Verification Codes are long so we split them up into groups of five digits to make them easier to read.

Persistent Verification Keys

To avoid repetitive verification each time you are on a call with the same person, you can enable persistent verification keys. If you have this setting enabled, people you’re speaking with will be able to remember your device and mark it as verified.

To enable persistent verification keys:

  1. Navigate to User Settings, then select Privacy & Safety.

  2. Select the Encryption tab, and toggle the Enable persistent verification codes

Considerations for setup:

  • For you to save a persistent verification key for the person you’re speaking with, they’ll need to have the Enable persistent verification codes setting enabled as well.

  • Persistent verification keys are tied to your device, not your user account. This means that if both you and a friend enable this setting, you’ll remain verified to each other every time you join a voice call from those devices.

  • If you log out and back in again on your device, you will lose access to any previously used persistent verification key on that device and others who previously persistently verified your device will see that you are unverified. If you want to use persistent verification keys, you will need to enable the Enable persistent verification codes setting again. Someone you previously persistently verified may appear unverified when:

  • They’re using a different device than the one you persistently verified

  • They had to log in again on the device you persistently verified

  • Their persistent verification key was removed from local device storage

  • They are being impersonated by someone else

Managing Verified Devices

If you have verified other users with persistent verification codes enabled, you can manage these verified devices in your User Settings.

  1. Navigate to User Settings, then select Privacy & Safety.

  2. Select the Encryption tab where you’ll see Verified Devices.

  1. On Desktop, select the Encryption tab.

  2. On Mobile, select End-to-end Encryption under the Privacy & Safety tab.

Each user, along with their verified device(s), will be displayed. You can choose to remove the verification for a specific device, identified by the time it was verified, or remove all verifications for a specific user.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I know if my call is end-to-end encrypted?

A: You can verify that your call is end-to-end encrypted by checking for the green End-to-end encrypted lock icon in the Voice/Video Details on the desktop app or by pressing on the voice channel name details in the top left corner of the focused call view on mobile.

Q: When will E2EE A/V roll out to Discord web and consoles?

A: Web and consoles will get E2EE A/V support in the second half of 2025.

Q: Why is my call not end-to-end encrypted when I’m on an updated Discord app?

A: Your call may not be end-to-end encrypted because you may be on a call with someone who is not on an updated Discord app. On March 2nd 2026, all DMs, GDMs, voice channels, and Go Live streams will require updated clients that support end-to-end encryption.

Q: Can I opt out of E2EE A/V?

A: E2EE A/V is enabled by default and cannot be turned off. E2EE A/V currently won’t apply to calls where an unsupported client (i.e., web and consoles) is being used by at least one user. Unsupported clients will no longer be able to connect to calls from March 2, 2026. Stage channels also will not be end-to-end encrypted.

Q: Will the preview of my Go Live stream now be private for users not yet in the call?

A: Stream previews – when you are able to see a snippet of an ongoing Go Live stream - are NOT end-to-end encrypted. This means that users not in a call with an ongoing stream may be able to see a preview of the stream. You can disable stream previews forever, or on a per-stream basis.

Q: Can I verify the end-to-end encryption status in Go Live streams?

A: Yes, each Go Live stream has a Stream Privacy Code that can be accessed via the context menu for the stream. You can compare this code out of band with other participants to verify that the stream is end-to-end encrypted.

Q: What happens if I change my device/log into my Discord account on a new device?

A: If you change your device and have persistent verification codes enabled, you will need to go through the verification process again as verification is tied to the specific device. Persistent verification keys must be re-enabled on a new device.

EU DSA Dispute Resolution Options

This article explains how users covered by the European Union’s Digital Services Act (“DSA”) can exercise certain rights. Parts of the DSA only apply to certain online spaces (called “online platforms”) and to certain types of actions by those platforms. That’s all to say that not every report or action on Discord will be eligible for action under the DSA.

We work hard to remove violative content and bad actors from our services. This includes responding to user reports about content. The easiest way to report content that violates our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines is through our in-app reporting surfaces. Certain users also have the option to report illegal content under the DSA through this webform.

The DSA also provides specific appeal rights for certain users. If the DSA applies to you and you think we’ve made a mistake in arriving at one of the decisions listed below, you have six months to appeal our decision through our internal appeals process. A link to appeal Discord’s decision can be found on the violation notice.

You may also appeal a decision on your account directly in the Discord app by going to User Settings > My Account > Standing.

Reviewing Account Standing in User Settings on Desktop

Then, select the decision you want to appeal by selecting Let us know in account standing window.

Let us know Option in Suspension Notification on Desktop

Please keep in mind that these DSA appeals mechanisms only apply to decisions about the following, if they are made on the ground that information provided is illegal or violates our Terms of Service:

  • removing or disabling access to or restricting visibility of content;
  • suspending or terminating access to Discord (in whole or in part);
  • suspending or terminating a user’s Discord account; or
  • suspending, terminating, or restricting a user’s ability to monetize their Discord activity. You may also have the option of selecting an out-of-court dispute settlement body certified by an EU Member State’s Digital Services Coordinator to help resolve a dispute relating to any such decision. The European Commission will maintain a website listing the available settlement bodies as they become certified. Discord will work with the out-of-court settlement body where required by law, but is not bound by any decisions made by these out-of-court settlement bodies. Discord also has the right not to engage with an out-of-court dispute settlement body if a dispute has already been resolved concerning the same information and the same grounds.

How long Discord keeps your information

We collect certain information as you use Discord. Our Privacy Policy describes the information we collect, how we use and share it, and how you can control your information. This page describes how long we hold on to different types of information and why.

As mentioned in our Privacy Policy, we require the information that enables us to create your account, provide our services, meet our commitments to our users, and satisfy our legal requirements. The rest is optional.

We retain personal information for as long as it is needed for the purposes for which we collected it. In general, this means that we retain your personal information for as long as you have an active Discord account. Some information you can delete directly from the services. We may also retain information for a certain period of time for specific purposes as described below.

As described in our Privacy Policy, you can limit Discord from collecting some types of information used for specific purposes.

What this article covers:

  • Information You Can Delete Directly from the Services
  • Information Retained Until Your Account Is Deleted
  • Retention Periods for Specific Purposes
  • What Happens When You Delete Your Account
  • Your Rights

Information You Can Delete Directly From The Services

You may edit or erase content that you post within Discord. For example:

  • You can edit or delete any message you have sent or content you have posted if you still have access to the space where you posted it.
  • You can edit or delete a Discord server if you have the permissions needed to do so.
  • You can edit or delete a channel from a Discord server if you have the permissions needed to do so. Once you delete content, it will no longer be available to other users (though it may take some time to clear cached uploads). Deleted content will also be deleted from Discord’s systems, but we may retain content longer if we have a legal obligation to preserve it as described below. Public posts may also be retained for 180 days to two years for use by Discord as described in our Privacy Policy (for example, to help us train models that proactively detect content that violates our policies).

Information Retained Until Your Account Is Deleted

We keep some data for the life of your Discord account. This includes information about how you use Discord, which helps us understand how users interact with our services, what features or products users may want, or how to improve our services. This also includes information like your username, email, and phone number. Some of that information may be kept for longer periods for specific purposes, as described below. You can delete your account at any time, and if your account is inactive for two years, we may delete it for you. For more on our deletion processes, see the “What happens when you delete your account” section below.

Retention Periods for Specific Purposes

Business and legal requirements may mean that we need to retain certain information for set periods of time, some of which may extend beyond the deletion of your account. For each type of information, we set these data retention periods based on the reason for its collection:

  • Age assurance. If you submit personal information to one of our trusted providers as part of a process to confirm your age, Discord does not access or receive this data directly. Our providers process this information and send us your age signal only, which is retained until you delete your account or update that information. How long your information is retained by one of our providers varies depending on the process you use:
    • On-device facial age estimation. Your video selfie is processed locally on your device. This involves facial analysis, which may be considered biometric or sensitive in some places. This data is not used to identify you, it does not leave your device, and is deleted once the process is completed.
    • ID scan. Your selfie and ID are analyzed (including facial structure and ID details), which may be considered biometric or sensitive data in some places. This data is not used to identify you and is deleted once the process is completed.
    • Credit card check. Credit card details (such as card number and billing information) are redacted and truncated once the process is complete. A financial record (including truncated card detail, transaction amount, and timestamp) is typically retained by our provider for up to 10 years, consistent with tax and financial obligations for payment processors.
    • Age appeals or correction requests. If you contact Discord Support to change or verify your age, you may use an age-confirmation method noted above, in which case your data is retained as described for the applicable process. If you submit an ID and selfie as part of a manual review, it will be deleted after the verification is complete.
  • Backups. Our database backups are stored for 30-45 days upon which they are deleted.
  • Compliance with our legal obligations. We may need to retain certain information for longer periods to comply with legal requirements. For example, when you purchase something through Discord, we need to retain information related to that transaction for specific periods for tax and accounting purposes.
  • To meet our safety and security commitments. We retain certain information (including email addresses and phone numbers) for 180 days after deletion for trust and safety purposes. If a user has been reported or flagged for violations of our Terms of Service or Community Guidelines, we may retain this information for up to two years. This information helps us keep Discord secure, prevent fraud, or prevent bad actors from creating new accounts or otherwise engaging in behavior that violates our policies.
  • To exercise or defend legal claims. When you contact Discord directly (such as for customer support inquiries and requests to access your information), we retain related information for five years from the closure of your request in case of a dispute or to exercise or defend our legal rights.
  • Continuity of our service: If you delete your account, we continue to retain and display the content you shared with other users, but that content is no longer tied to your account. We do this in order to ensure that other users continue to have access to the content shared with them. If you want to delete specific content, please do so before you delete your account. You can delete specific content as described in the “Information you can delete directly from the services” section above, or if you need help deleting content, you can write in to privacy@discord.com.

What Happens When You Delete Your Account

When you delete your account, we will typically first put your account on hold for 15 to 30 days so that it can be recovered in case it was deleted unintentionally. Once that period expires, we begin the process of deleting identifying information and anonymizing or aggregating other information. Most of this happens quickly (unless the information is subject to a longer retention period as described above), but it can take up to 45 days to delete identifying information from backups. We retain aggregated and anonymized information, which is information that no longer enables us to identify you and is no longer tied to you as an individual.

Your Rights

As provided in our Privacy Policy, all our users have control over their information and can directly edit or delete information from their account and limit what data we process. If you are located in the European Union, the GDPR grants you the following specific rights that you can exercise through the Discord app directly or by contacting us:

  • Right of access to your personal data
  • Right to rectify your personal data if they are incorrect
  • Right to erase your personal data
  • Right to limit the processing of your personal data
  • Right to the portability of your personal data
  • Right to object to the processing of your personal data If you have any questions about data retention or our deletion practices, or if you wish to exercise control over your information, please reach out to privacy@discord.com.

How to Report Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery Under Local Laws

Discord prohibits non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and works to identify, remove, and prevent its spread across the platform. This article covers how to submit a report to remove NCII under specific laws that might be available to you in your region.

Note: You can also submit reports of NCII through our standard in-app reporting system. Our NCII policy applies globally in addition to any legal rights you may have where you live.

What this article covers:

  • What Can Be Reported
  • How to Submit a Report
    • Accessing the Report Form
    • Required Information
    • How to Find Content Links for Your Report
    • Message Attachments
    • Third Party Links / Embedded Media in Messages
    • Emojis
    • Stickers
    • User Profiles (Avatars, Banners)
    • Server-related Images (Avatars, Banners)
  • What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request
  • Frequently Asked Questions Important: Need immediate help? If you have concerns about your personal safety, or the safety of someone you know, please contact local law enforcement or social services.

What Can Be Reported

Discord’s NCII policy applies globally. In addition, you may have legal rights concerning NCII reporting depending on where you live.

Depending on the specific law available to people in those regions, Discord’s obligations and what happens after you submit a report will vary.

For people based in the US: What is the Take It Down Act (TIDA)

For people based in Brazil: What is Decree No. 12,976/2026

For people based in the UK: Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery Reporting Under the UK Online Safety Act (OSA)

Where a legal removal process applies to you, you can report content that:

  • Shows you (or someone you’re authorized to represent) nude or engaged in sexually explicit conduct
  • Was shared without your consent, or was captured when you had a reasonable expectation of privacy
  • Is either authentic, AI-generated, or digitally manipulated depicting you This includes images or videos you may have originally consented to create but did not consent to have shared. There’s no time limit—you can report content regardless of when it was created or posted.

Important: Please note that you can still submit your report but that intimate imagery of a person under the age of 18 constitutes Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM). We report illegal child sexual abuse material and grooming to the relevant authorities. Discord takes enforcement action against users who post such content.

How to Submit a Report

Reports must be submitted through our public report webform found at discord.com/report.

We’ll review your report and take appropriate action within the timeframe required under the specific law where you live. You will be notified via email on the status of your report.

Reports may be submitted by the depicted individual or an authorized representative (e.g. a parent, guardian, attorney) of the depicted individual. Multiple reports are allowed - please create one report for each piece of media.

Accessing the Report Form

  1. On desktop or mobile devices, navigate to discord.com/report on your preferred browser.

  2. Follow the steps in the form to file a report.

Required Information

We recognize that reporting NCII can be difficult. Your report will remain confidential, and we will not disclose your information to the person who uploaded the imagery of you.

To file a report, you will be asked for information such as:

  • Legal name of the person that is depicted in the reported content
  • Email address where you wish to receive updates on your report
  • Country of residence
  • Link to the content you are reporting (see the instructions in the next section on how to get the content link)
  • Your relationship to the content
  • Content type (what is depicted and the age of the depicted individual)
  • A good faith statement that the content was distributed without consent
  • Electronic signature, where required
