What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request

We will promptly review your removal request to confirm that it meets the requirements of the law that applies to you. If the request is complete and valid, we will remove the reported content. We will also make reasonable efforts to identify and remove known copies of the content.

If your submission is incomplete, we may be unable to process your request until sufficient information is provided.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: When should I report NCII using the webform at discord.com/report and when should I report NCII using the standard in-app reporting process?

A: The right process depends on your situation: If a legal removal process is available where you live (refer to “What Can Be Reported” section above), and the images are of you or someone for whom you have legal authority to represent, the webform may be your best option—we also take steps to remove other copies of the same content, not just the one you report.

If a legal removal process isn’t available where you live, or you’re reporting images of someone else that you don’t have legal authority to represent, you can report content under our Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery policy via our standard reporting process using the in-app report menu.

We review your reports and take action where our policies apply. Whichever approach you use, your report will be reviewed.

Q: How quickly will the content be taken down after I report it?

A: We work to review your report and remove the content, if it meets the legal criteria for removal, within the timeframe required by the law that applies to you. For more information about the specific law that applies in your region, refer to the “What Can Be Reported” section above.

Q: If an image is found to meet the criteria for removal and is removed, can Discord prevent the same image from being uploaded again?

A: Yes, once an image is found to meet the criteria for removal, it will be tagged in our systems and we will prevent it from being uploaded again to the best of our ability.

Q: Does Discord disclose my information to the person who shared the content that I report?

A: No. We will not share the information you provide to us via the report form with users who posted the content to Discord. They will only be notified that the content has been removed, but not who reported it.

Q: How will I know what happened to my report?

A: After submitting your report, you’ll hear from us twice. First, a confirmation email so you know your report reached us. Then, we work to remove the content within the timeframe required by the specific law that applies in your region. We’ll send a follow-up email with an update on whether the content was removed.

Q: Can I submit an appeal if action was not taken on my report?

A: You have the option to submit another report if you believe we did not take appropriate action on your initial report.

Q: How can I appeal if action is taken on my account?

A: If you posted content that was found to meet the criteria for removal under applicable law or our Community Guidelines, you may be entitled to an appeal under your local laws. See our blog post with instructions on how to appeal here.

Q: What resources are available for me if my sensitive photos have been shared or published online?

A: If your sensitive photos have been shared or published online, there is help available, including the following resources:

StopNCII is a free tool designed to support adult victims and survivors of NCII abuse.

Take It Down is a free tool designed to support removal of online nude, partially nude, or sexually explicit imagery taken before the depicted person was 18.

More resources are also available in our Wellbeing Hub.

Q: Is there a limit to how many reports I can submit?

A: We have rate limits in place to prevent mass reports of the same content, and submitting too many reports in a short timeframe can result in your reports being rejected. If you encounter an error message after submitting several reports in a row, please wait 24 hours before submitting additional reports.

Discord lets you choose topics you don’t want to see in Sponsored Content. These topics are defined in Discord’s Ad Policy. When you select a topic, Discord will stop showing you Sponsored Content associated with that topic.

This is a separate control from your Sponsored Content personalization settings. For information about how Discord uses data to personalize Sponsored Content, see Data Used for Sponsored Content on Discord.

Desktop/Browser

  2. Select any topic you don’t want to see. When a topic is selected, you won’t see any Sponsored Content associated with that topic.

Manage Sponsored Content in User Settings on Desktop

Mobile

  2. Hide any topic you don’t want to see. When a topic is hidden, you won’t see any Sponsored Content associated with that topic.

Manage Sponsored Content in User Settings on Mobile

Important Notes:

  • Discord will control certain content you see regardless of these selections to ensure a relevant and trustworthy ad experience.
  • Availability of topics may vary by region.

Minimum Client Version Requirements for Voice Chat

Important: Starting March 2nd, 2026, all audio and video conversations in direct messages (DMs), group messages (GDMs), voice channels, and Go Live streams on Discord will require end-to-end encryption support. To participate in these conversations, you must be running a client version that supports end-to-end encryption.

This article covers the minimum client and browser versions required to join voice chat on Discord.

What Happens If You’re on an Unsupported Version

If you attempt to join a voice call with a client version that does not support end-to-end encryption:

  • Before March 2, 2026: You can still join calls with no issues
  • After March 2, 2026: You will be unable to join voice calls, video calls, or Go Live streams until you update to a supported version.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I know if my current version supports end-to-end encryption?

A: If your call is end-to-end encrypted, you’ll see a green lock icon labeled “End-to-end encrypted” in the Voice/Video Details panel. If you don’t see this icon, you or another participant may be on an unsupported version. See our article on End-to-End Encryption for Audio and Video for more details.

Q: What about console clients (PlayStation, Xbox)?

A: Consoles generally require you to be on the latest system version which will include support for end-to-end encryption.

Q: I use a third-party client or bot that connects to voice. Will it still work?

A: Third-party applications and bots that connect to Discord voice must implement DAVE support to continue functioning after March 2, 2026. Developers should consult Discord’s updated voice documentation and the open-source DAVE implementation examples.

Q: Where can I learn more about end-to-end encryption on Discord?

A: See our article on End-to-End Encryption for Audio and Video for details on how encryption works, how to verify calls, and how to manage your verification keys.

Protecting Your Data

Over the past few months, we’ve investigated reports of bad actors who join public Discord servers to scrape user information to create unauthorized databases of server members.

To be super clear, issues like these are 100% on our radar. This kind of activity is completely against our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. Bad actors like these use a couple methods for scraping user data from our site: harvesting server information from server widgets (which is a server-configurable option in the server settings) and creating automated user accounts, called “self-bots”, to join as many servers as possible through proxy manipulation.

Self-bots are and have always been a violation of our API Terms of Use, and we have implemented a number of methods to detect this kind of abuse. Additionally, we have made several recent changes to limit the ability of bad actors to abuse our API in this way:

  • We’ve anonymized and limited data returned on server widgets
  • We’ve added stricter rate limits to widget data and to profile data
  • We’ve added stricter permission requirements and other limitations to downloading member list as an ordinary user These changes have helped limit mass gathering of new information by known bad actors, and our engineers will continue to improve our ability to prevent these bad actors from creating new accounts in the future. On top of that work, we have a dedicated team working on a new service, scheduled for launch in the near future, to help us even better detect this kind of abuse on our platform.

We care deeply about maintaining and protecting the privacy of all of our users, and we’re always here to answer your questions. If you have any concerns regarding your privacy on Discord, please don’t hesitate to contact us at privacy@discord.com.

Requesting a Copy of your Data

Learn how to request your personal Discord data with these easy steps. Whether you’re using Discord on desktop, browser, or mobile, we’ll show you the step-by-step process to request and receive your account information. This article covers everything you need to know about data requests, processing times, and important considerations to keep in mind.

What this article covers:

  • Requesting Your Data
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Requesting Your Data

To request a copy of your personal data from your account’s entire history, go to your User Settings.

Once you submit your request, Discord will begin collecting your data. Here are a few key details you should know:

  • The data request process can take up to 30 days to complete.
  • You must wait for your current request to finish before submitting a new one.
  • Discord will send a download link to the email address linked to your account when you made the request.
  • Changing your email address later will not redirect the download link.
  • Your request will be canceled if you disable or delete your account before receiving the download link. NOTE: Your Discord account must be verified with an email address before requesting your data. Having trouble accessing your account? Contact privacy@discord.com for help with your data request.
Desktop/Browser

  1. Select the cogwheel [] in the lower-left corner.

  2. Select the Data & Privacy tab.

  3. Under Request your data, select the Request Data button.

  4. In the Submit Data Request window, select which data you’d like to receive. The data will be sent to your Discord account’s email address.

Requesting your data in User Settings on Desktop
Mobile

  1. Select your avatar in the lower-right corner.

  2. Tap the cogwheel [] in the upper-right corner, then tap Data & Privacy.

  3. Under Request your data, tap the Request all of my data button and confirm. Discord will send the data to your account’s email address.

Requesting your data in User Settings on Mobile

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How long does it take to receive my Discord data?

A: The data request process can take up to 30 days to complete.

Q: Can I submit multiple data requests at once?

A: No, you must wait for your current request to be completed before submitting a new one.

Q: What happens if I change my email address after submitting a request?

A: The download link will be sent to the email address that was linked to your account at the time of the request. Changing your email address later will not redirect the download link.

Q: What if I delete my account before receiving my data?

A: Your data request will be canceled if you disable or delete your account before receiving the download link.

Q: Do I need a verified email address to request my data?

A: Yes, your Discord account must be verified with an email address before you can request your data.

Q: Who should I contact if I’m having trouble accessing my account?

A: If you’re having trouble accessing your account, you can contact privacy@discord.com for assistance with your data request.

Q: Can I choose which data to receive?

A: Yes, when submitting a data request on desktop/browser, you can select which specific data you’d like to receive. On mobile, you can only request all of your data.

Visibility of Bot Data Access

Privacy and safety are high priorities for Discord, including with the use of bots. That’s why we want to make it easier for you to understand what information about bots and other apps in the servers you’re in may have access to through Discord.

Certain data access is unique to each bot, based on factors like its selected settings and verification status. To see this data access that a bot currently has in a server, open its profile in the server from the Discord desktop or browser app and click on the “Data Access” tab.

In addition to the data described above and information they get from their direct communications or other interactions with users (e.g., a user’s command for the bot to take a specific action), all bots and other apps have access to a baseline set of data in the servers that they’re in, including:

  • Basic user profile information of server members (e.g., usernames, avatars, banners, discriminators, and nicknames);
  • Roles that members have in the server;
  • Metadata about messages (e.g., day and time sent);
  • The voice channel members join, as well as metadata about voice channels (e.g., muted, deafened, streaming, or have video on);
  • Message reactions by members; and
  • Language information selected by members in their User Settings. As described in our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, bots may be developed by third parties and you should review any terms and policies provided by the developer of a bot to understand how it may use this data and to choose if you want to use it and participate in a server that incorporates it. Since a bot’s data access may change from time to time, we encourage you to regularly review this page and the bot’s profile for updates.

Have more questions? Submit a request!

What is a Data Package?

A Data Package is a ZIP folder of files that you can request through your User Settings that contains all of your Discord data for your account. This includes messages, current servers you’re in, activity, and more. The files within the ZIP folder are JSON files that can be opened easily in Notepad on Windows or through Textedit on MacOS. You can also drag and drop them into a browser like Chrome or Firefox.

How to Request a Data Package

Contact Us: If you’ve permanently lost access to your account and need your data package for personal records, contact privacy@discord.com.

Want to learn more? For more information about requesting your data package, check out our Help Center Article: How to Request and Download Your Discord Data.

You can request your Data Package through the Discord desktop, browser, and mobile app.

Desktop/Browser
  1. Press the cogwheel [] in the bottom-left of the Discord app to navigate to User Settings.
Cogwheel icon

  1. Select the Data & Privacy tab and scroll to Request your data.

  2. Press the Request Data button. The Submit Data Request window will appear for you to select which data you would like to request.

  3. Once you made your selections, press Request My Data in the bottom-right of the window.

  4. You’ll receive a confirmation stating you should receive your data package within 30 days. Press Okay to confirm.

We’ll send a data package to the email address associated with your Discord account. The download link will remain active for 30 days.

Request Data on desktop/browser app

Important: If you disable or delete your account before you receive your download link, it will cancel your request.

Mobile
  1. Tap your avatar icon in the bottom-right corner of the app to navigate to your profile.
Avatar icon

  1. Navigate to Settings by tapping the cogwheel [] in the upper-right corner.

  2. Press Data & Privacy and then select Request all of my data.

  3. The Submit Data Request page will appear for you to select which data you would like to request in your package.

  4. Once you made your selections, press Request My Data to submit your request.

  5. You’ll receive a confirmation stating you should receive your data package within 30

days. Tap Okay to exit out of this confirmation.

We’ll then send a data package to the email address associated with your Discord account. The download link will remain active for 30 days.

How to request your Data Package on mobile

What information is inside a Data Package?

Account

The account folder contains information pertaining to your account. The first item you’ll see is the avatar that you are currently using, as well as a folder containing any recently-used avatars. If applicable, there will also be a folder containing information about any applications you own. Finally, you’ll see a JSON file containing the following information about your account:

  • Basic information, such as your user ID, username name, phone number, and email

  • Your account settings

  • Any flags on your account (such as whether you have an active Nitro subscription)

  • Your IP Address

  • Any accounts you have connected to Discord (“Connections”). (Twitch, Twitter, Steam, etc.)

  • A list of any active sessions you have; PC, Mobile, Browser (IP Address included)

  • Your user relationships (Friends and Block lists), as well as Friend suggestions, and Friends lists from external platforms

  • Your payment information, including payment sources, payment history, and your Orbs balance and Orbs transaction history

  • Your developer information (For any webhooks, bots, etc.)

  • Activity statistics

  • Notes you have written about other users

  • Library applications You’ll also see some different age signals we use across the platform:

  • date_of_birth - This is the date of birth you provide to us when you sign up for the platform. If you’re under 18, it will be anonymized to the first of the month (MM-01-YYYY). If you’re over 18, this will be fully anonymized, and you’ll see (01-01-0001)

  • age_assurance - When you use one of the methods to confirm your age, we retain the vendor and method used, as well as the timestamp of your verification attempt.

    • estimated_age_group is how we store the outcome of the age assurance method you chose, which can be more precise in the case of teens (e.g., 13, 14, 15) or broader for adults (e.g., 22-25).
    • inferred_age_group is the age group assigned to you by the ML model that estimates your age as part of our overall age assurance system (e.g., Teen, Adult).

  • predicted_age - This is a different type of age prediction model that we use to understand how users interact with Discord and to power certain features in the app. This age signal does not determine your age group (e.g., Adult, Teen). Tip: If you have recently deleted an avatar image, it may still show up in your package.

Activity

The activity folder contains four folders, each with a JSON file that has information about the actions you have taken on Discord.

  • Analytics: This is a record of your actions within Discord. The information is used to improve your Discord experience, like improving search relevance.
    • You can disable the use of tracking analytics here: User Settings > Data & Privacy > Use data to improve Discord
  • Modeling: This is data we use to better tailor certain parts of Discord to you, like the Games tab.
    • You can disable the use of this here: User Settings > Data & Privacy > Use data to personalize my Discord experience
  • Reporting: This folder contains a JSON file with data we use in order to operate our business. (Information such as messages sent, or your Nitro subscription, as an example.)
  • Trust & Safety (TNS): This folder contains data we use for safety purposes. This data is retained for up to 2 years.
Activities

The activities folder contains two folders, each with a JSON file that has information about 1st-party activities you have participated in on Discord.

  • Activities_1 - This folder will contain some of your Activities user data and preferences, as well as activity-specific data about Chess in the Park, Checkers in the Park, and Poker Night 2.0
  • Activities_2 - This folder will contain more Activities user data and preferences, as well as activity-specific data about Sketch Heads, Watch Together, Letter League, Land-io, and Know What I Meme
Messages

The messages folder contains all the messages that you have sent on Discord. Please note that your message folder does not include Customer Support or Trust & Safety correspondence as these communications take place outside of the Discord application.

The messages you have sent are broken down separately into folders based on Direct Messages, Group Messages, and channels that you have chatted in. The number for each folder is the Channel ID for where the messages were sent. There is a JSON file which also contains a full mapping of Channel ID to Channel name for all of the folders included.

When you select a folder, you’ll notice it contains a couple items. The first is a JSON file which will include information about where the messages in that folder were sent. If the folder contains messages from a server, this information will include the associated Guild ID, Channel ID, and Channel Name. If the folder contains messages from a DM or group chat, this information will include the associated Channel ID and User IDs.

The second is a JSON file which contains the transcript of your messages. For each message, it will contain the following information:

  • ID: The message ID
  • Timestamp: The date and exact time your message was sent
  • Contents: Your message.
  • Attachments : A CDN link to any images, or files you included in your message Tip: If you manually delete a message - it is no longer stored in Discord and therefore will not be included in your Data Package.
Servers

Important: If you leave a server before requesting your Data Package, that server may not be included. Your Data Package only includes servers you are a member of at the time of the request as well as any recently-departed servers.

The servers folder contains information for all of the servers that you are a member of. This includes servers that you own. The information provided for each is a little different. There is a JSON file which also contains a full list of the folders included.

The folder for a server you own will contain the following:

  • A folder containing emoji that you have uploaded.

  • A JSON file containing actions from your Audit Log.

  • A JSON file containing a list of your channels along with their permissions.

  • A JSON file containing the ID information for the emoji you have uploaded.

  • A JSON file containing the settings for your server (guild).

  • A JSON file containing information for any webhook you have implemented. The folder for a server that you are a member of will contain the following:

  • A JSON file containing actions from the last 90 days that pertain to your account from the Audit Log.

  • A JSON file containing the server ID and name.

Ads

The Ads folder contains information about advertisements (e.g.: Quests) that you have interacted with on the platform and traits we use to serve ads to you. The Ads folder contains the following:

  • A JSON file containing the status of Quests you’ve engaged with on Discord
  • A JSON file containing information we’ve associated with you to tailor ads to you Note that some information related to ads, such as when you saw a Quest, will be captured in the Activity folder.
Support Tickets

This folder contains a JSON file with information about tickets you’ve made through our Help Center in Zendesk that are tied to your Discord email address. Each ticket contains the following information:

  • The body of all public comments on the ticket, including the comment’s author and creation timestamp
  • The time the ticket was created
  • The status of the ticket
  • The subject of the ticket
  • The ticket ID Contact Us: Our Support Team cannot assist you with going through your Data Package, however, if you have any questions or notice something is missing please reach out through here: dis.gd/contact

Discord X Support Account (@discord_support) FAQ

Our X Posts

Our X posts help keep Discord users informed! If you follow our feed, you’ll get updates on:

  • Clarifying information for general Discord feature information
  • Known issues and bugs
  • Ongoing outages
  • Tips for improving your Discord experience If you want to stay on top of the latest Discord news, we highly encourage you to give us a follow!
Issues @discord_support can assist with

To receive help, you can either DM us or tag us in a post. In your message, please provide a brief description of the problem you’re running into and attach a screenshot of any error messages you’re receiving!

Although this list is not exhaustive, here are a few examples of issues that @discord_support can assist with:

  • Basic troubleshooting
  • Connection issues/outages
  • Email verification issues
  • General feedback
  • Launch updates
  • Questions related to features or promotions Make sure to also regularly check our feed for any updates regarding outages, launches, known issues, and updates.
Issues @discord_support cannot assist with

NOTE: Contacting us on X does not replace submitting a ticket through our support portal, nor does the Discord social team directly handle any previously submitted support tickets.

While we are able to assist with a number of issues, some inquiries still lie outside of the @discord_support account scope of support.

Examples of issues @discord_Support cannot assist with:

  • 2FA removal or lost account access
  • Developer support
  • Disabled and banned accounts
  • Hacked accounts
  • Phone verification issues

How to Submit a Support Ticket to Discord

Need help from our support team? This guide will walk you through submitting a support ticket through Discord’s Help Center.

What this article covers:

  • Support Account vs Discord Account
  • Submitting Your First Ticket
    • Create Your Discord Support Account
    • Submit your Discord Support Ticket
  • Submitting Additional Tickets
    • If You’ve Submitted Tickets Before But Never Set Up Your Support Account
  • Sending an Email for Support
    • First-Time Email Submission
    • Already Have a Help Center Account?
  • Tips for Submitting a Support Ticket
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Support Account vs. Discord Account

Your Discord Support account for the Help Center is separate from your Discord app account.

This means:

  • You’ll create different login credentials for the Discord Help Center
  • Your Discord Help Center password is separate from your Discord app password
  • You’ll need to sign in specifically to the Discord Help Center to submit or view tickets

Submitting Your First Ticket

If you’ve never submitted a ticket to our Help Center before, follow these steps:

Create your Discord Support Account

  1. Go to support.discord.com in your browser.

  2. Select Sign in, located in the top-right corner of the page.

  3. On the sign-in page, press on the Sign Up hyperlink next to “New to Discord Support” and you’ll see a new page to:

  • Enter your full name
  • Enter your email address Then once you’ve reviewed your sign-up information, select the Sign up button.

In the sign in box for Discord Support, press on Sign up if you don’t have a Support account yet.In the Sign Up box for Discord Support, input your name and email in their respective text fields.

Tip: At this stage, you won’t create a password yet. Discord Support will send you a welcome email to set up your account.

  1. After pressing Sign up, you’ll see a message that says Check your email with instructions to look for a link to set a new password. Look for an email from Support (support@discord.com) with the subject line Activate account for Discord Support.

You’ll receive a notice to check your email for a link to set a password for your Support account.

Tip: Check your spam folder if you don’t see the email in your inbox within a few minutes.

  1. Open the email and press the Activate account link. This will:
  • Verify your email address
  • Allow you to set your Help Center password (remember, this is separate from your Discord app password)
  • Complete your account setup Press on Activate account in the confirmation email you receive for the creation of your support account.
Submit your Discord Support Ticket

Once your Discord Support account is activated and you’re signed in, you can now submit your ticket:

  1. Choose Your Category

First, you’ll see “What can we help you with?” with several category options, such as: Help & Support, Bug Reporting, Refunds, Cancellations & Payments, Feedback, and more.

Select the category that best matches your issue.

When submitting a support ticket, choose from the dropdown menu under “What can we help you with?” to get started.

  1. Complete the Form

Depending on the category you select, you’ll see different form fields. Common fields include:

  • Type of question: Select the specific type of support you need (this dropdown changes based on your chosen category)
  • Additional category fields: Some categories may ask for more details like “What type of issue are you experiencing?” or “Platform” (Android, iOS, Desktop, etc.)
  • Subject: Provide a brief, clear description of your issue
  • Description: Explain your issue in detail. Include relevant information like:
    • What happened and when
    • Steps you’ve already tried
    • Any error messages you received
  • Attachments (optional): Add any relevant screenshots or files by pressing “Add file” or dragging files into the designated area There are numerous fields to fill out when submitting a support request.
  1. Submit Your Ticket

Review all your information and press the “Submit” button to send your ticket to our Support team.

  1. Check Your Email

You’ll receive a confirmation email with your ticket number. Save this for your records and use it to track your ticket status.

Submitting Additional Tickets

If you’ve previously submitted a ticket, the process is even simpler:

  1. Head to support.discord.com and press on Sign in in the top-right corner

  2. Enter the email and password you created for your Support account

  3. Once signed in, press Submit a request and fill out the ticket form with details about your new issue

  4. Once you’re finished filling out the details, press on Submit to submit your ticket.

  5. When you’re signed in, you can view all your previous tickets and their status by pressing on your profile or navigating to My activities or Requests.

Tip: If you’ve forgotten your password or have never set a password for your support account, use the “Forgot password?” link and follow the prompts to reset your password

If You’ve Submitted Tickets Before But Never Set Up Your Support Account

If you previously submitted tickets via email but never activated your Help Center account or set a password, and attempt to sign up using that email address, you’ll receive a message stating:

“Discord Support sign-up attempt”

In this case:

  • Press “reset your password” from the email you receive
  • Complete the password setup process to gain full access to your Discord Help Center account
  • Once set up, you can view all your previous tickets and submit new ones through the portal

Sending an Email for Support

First-Time Email Submission

If this is your first time contacting Discord Support via email and you don’t have a Help Center account yet:

  1. Send your email to the appropriate Discord Support email address (for example: sample-support-email@discord.com)

  2. Check for the activation email: You’ll receive an email from Support support@discord.com with the subject line “Discord welcome email”

  3. Activate your account: Press the link in the bottom of the email to verify your email address and set your Discord Help Center password

  4. Your ticket is created: Once activated, your email will be converted into a support ticket that you can track in your Discord Help Center account

Important: The email verification step is required for first-time senders to prevent spam and ensure secure communication with our support team.

Already Have a Help Center Account?

If you already have a Discord Help Center account with the email address you’re sending from, your email will automatically create a ticket associated with your account.

You’ll receive a confirmation email with your ticket number.

Tips for Submitting a Support Ticket

To help our support team to resolve your issue:

  • Be specific: Provide as much detail as possible about your issue and include screenshots when applicable
  • Reply to the same ticket: If you have follow-up information about an existing issue, reply to the original ticket email rather than creating a new ticket
  • Check your email OR your Requests & My Activities tab for updates: Our support team will respond via email, so monitor the inbox associated with your Support account. You can also check your Requests or My Activities tab to review any updates to your ticket.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: I forgot my password and I can’t access my Help Center support account!

A: If you’ve forgotten your Help Center password, use the “Forgot password?” link on the sign-in page. The reset link will be sent to the email address associated with your Support account.

Q: Why am I not receiving confirmation emails for my support account/support tickets?

A: Check your spam or junk folder. Add support@discord.com to your contacts to ensure future emails arrive in your inbox.

Q: I need to update support ticket information! How do I do that?

Reply to the confirmation email you received when you submitted your ticket, or sign in to your Support account and add a comment to your existing ticket through the Requests or My Activities tab.

Q: Help! I can’t find my support ticket.

If you’re having trouble locating a ticket you submitted:

  • Check your email: Search your inbox for emails from support@discord.com with your ticket number
  • Search by ticket number: If you have your ticket number, use it to search your email or reference it when contacting our Support team
  • Check spam/junk folder: Ticket confirmation and update emails may have been filtered
  • Sign in to view your tickets: Log in to your support account at support.discord.com and navigate to “My activities” or “Requests” to see all your submitted tickets
  • Verify the email address: Make sure you’re signed in with the same email address you used to submit the ticket Important: Some in-app flows or internal processes may generate tickets automatically, and those tickets will not be available in your email or on the support portal.

Still Need Help?

If you’re experiencing issues submitting a ticket or accessing your Discord Support account, try:

  • Clearing your browser cache and cookies
  • Using a different browser
  • Disabling browser extensions temporarily Also, check out our Help Center for support articles that might answer your question!

Important: Your Discord Help Center login is separate from your Discord app login. Keep your Discord Help Center credentials secure and accessible for future support needs.

Where can I submit Feature Requests, Feedback, and Suggestions?

We love hearing from our community! Whether you have a suggestion for a new feature, thoughts on a recent update, or general feedback about your Discord experience, our Feedback Form is one of the ways to share it with us.

Need help with your account or a specific issue?

· The Feedback Form is not monitored for support requests, and you will not receive a reply.

· If you need help with your account or want to request a refund, please visit dis.gd/contact and select the correct drop down option in the What can we help you with? section to reach our Support team.

What this article covers:

  • Feedback vs. Other Request Types — Which Option Should I Use?
  • How to Submit Feedback Through the Feedback Form
    • What Happens After You Submit Feedback?
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Feedback vs. Other Request Types — Which Option Should I Use?

Discord support requests (including feedback) are submitted through our Support Portal at dis.gd/contact.

When you arrive, you’ll see a dropdown menu that asks: “What can we help you with?”

To submit feedback, select “Feedback” from the dropdown. This will load the Feedback Form, which is specifically designed to collect product suggestions, feature requests, and general thoughts about your Discord experience.

The Support Portal offers several request types to make sure your submission reaches the right team. Here’s a breakdown:

Purpose

Where to go

Feedback Form

Share ideas, suggestions, and general thoughts about Discord

dis.gd/feedback → select Feedback

Help & Support

Get help with account-related issues such as account verification, technical support, account deletion requests

dis.gd/contact → select Help & Support

Refunds, Cancellations & Payments

Resolve billing and payment issues such as refunds, payment questions, billing disputes

dis.gd/billing → select Refunds, Cancellations & Payments

Bug Reporting

Report technical issues with the app such as bugs affecting specific features, clients, or platforms

dis.gd/contact → select Bug Reporting

Looking for safety resources? Visit the Discord Safety Center for information on staying safe on Discord.

How to Submit Feedback Through the Feedback Form

If you need support signing into your Discord Support Account, check out this article here.

  • Sign into your Discord Support Account.
  • Navigate to the Discord Feedback Form at dis.gd/feedback.
  • Select the category that best describes your feedback (e.g., Text Chat, Voice and Video, etc.).
  • Fill in the feedback fields with as much detail as you’d like to share.
  • Check the acknowledgment box confirming you understand this form is for feedback only and does not receive support replies.
  • Select Submit. Once your form has been submitted, you’ll receive a confirmation email letting you know your feedback was received.
What Happens After You Submit Feedback?

Once you submit your feedback, it’s forwarded to the appropriate internal team at Discord — such as Product, Engineering, or Design — for review.

Here are a few things to keep in mind:

  • You will not receive a personal reply. Our Support team does not respond to submissions in the Feedback Form.
  • We can’t guarantee implementation. While all feedback is read and valued, we’re unable to provide an ETA on when — or whether — a suggestion will be acted on.
  • Your feedback matters. Even without a reply, your submission helps shape Discord’s product decisions and roadmap.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I submit a bug report through the Feedback Form?

A: If you’ve found a bug, the best way to get it resolved is to submit a support ticket at dis.gd/contact so our team can investigate. You’re welcome to share broader product feedback about the experience, but bug reports requiring investigation should go through Support.

Q: Will Discord reply to my feedback in the Feedback Form?

A: No. The Feedback Form is a one-way channel used to collect community input. While we cannot reply to individual submissions, we do review feedback internally and share it with the appropriate teams.

Q: What if I submitted a feedback request in the Support Form?

A: Our Support team will redirect you to the Feedback Form so we can properly track this feedback.

Q: I submitted a legal inquiry or formal request through this Feedback Form — what should I do?

A: The Feedback Form is not the appropriate channel for legal inquiries, notices, or demands, or regulatory complaints. Submissions to this form are not reviewed by Discord’s legal team. Please refer to discord.com/terms or contact Discord through the appropriate legal channels.

Q: I submitted feedback but want to follow up or add more context. What should I do?

A: You’re welcome to submit a new feedback entry to the Feedback Form at any time. Since we don’t reply to individual submissions, there’s no way to expand to an existing submission — but every entry is reviewed.

Still Need Help?

  • If you have an account issue, billing question, or need hands-on support, our Support team is here for you - visit dis.gd/contact to submit a new ticket to our Support team.
  • If you need support signing into your Support account, visit this support article to learn more.
  • If you’d like to learn more about staying safe on Discord, visit the Discord Safety Center for more information.

Accessibility Settings Tab

We want Discord to be accessible for everyone. That’s why we’ve rolled out a dedicated Accessibility section in User Settings - making it easier to find and adjust features that help you customize Discord to your needs.

What this article covers:

  • Where to Find Discord Accessibility Settings
    • Desktop Instructions
    • Mobile Instructions
  • Saturation Slider
  • Sticker Animation Control
  • Text-to-Speech Settings
  • High-Contrast Settings
    • High-Contrast Mode on Desktop
    • Sync Contrast Settings on Windows Devices
    • Contrast Slider on Mobile
  • Role Colors
  • Profile and Client Theme Sync
  • Other Accessibility Features

Where to Find Discord Accessibility Settings

From controlling motion and color to adjusting text-to-speech and contrast, you’ll now be able to find everything in one place under User Settings > App Settings > Accessibility.

This includes options such as:

  • Saturation Slider

  • Sticker Animation Control

  • Text-to-Speech Settings

  • High Contrast Settings

  • Role Colors

  • Profile and Client Theme Sync You can also find options to control the following:

  • Reduced Motion

  • Automatically playing GIFs when Discord is focused

  • Playing animated Emojis

Note: Pre-existing options under the Appearance tab have been reorganized and those Advanced settings have been moved to their own tab as well.
Desktop Instructions

To access Accessibility Settings, press the User settings button > App Settings > Accessibility

Mobile Instructions

To access Accessibility Settings on mobile, head to your User Settings by pressing your avatar on the bottom right > App Settings > Accessibility

Saturation Slider

We added a Saturation slider to the Accessibility settings tab that allows users to adjust the richness of the colors in the client for our users with color sensitivities.

The Saturation Slider on the desktop Discord app can be found in User Settings under Accessibility.

On the Discord mobile app, the Saturation Slider can be found by going to the Accessibility page in Settings through the user avatar icon.

Sticker Animation Control

You can set Sticker animations to Always animate, Animate on interaction, or never animate.

Text-to-Speech Settings

Alongside the Text-to-Speech Rate Slider, we also have improved Accessible Drag & Drop available.

Text-To-Speech has been available to all users on Discord for some time now, but over the years we’ve listened to your need to adjust the speed at which message content is read back to you. That feedback led us to build the Text-To-Speech Slider.

From User Settings > Accessibility, use the Text-to-Speech rate slider setting to adjust the speed at which you would like text read back to you.

After adjusting the speed, you can preview the Text-to-Speech rate by clicking on the ‘Preview’ button.

For more information about Text to Speech, check out this article.

High-Contrast Settings

High-Contrast Mode on Desktop

High Contrast Mode provides improved contrast for UI elements across the entire Discord client. It works on all themes and can be enabled at the top of the Accessibility Settings tab. High Contrast Mode can also be used with Window’s High Contrast mode feature to increase the contrast even more.

Sync Contrast Settings on Windows Devices

Please note that this additional setting will only appear for Windows users. It will not show up for MacOS, iOS, and Android users.

If you’re on a Windows device, you can Sync contrast settings on your Discord client if you have Windows High Contrast Mode enabled on your device. Check out this article to find steps on how to enable High Contrast mode on Windows.

With Sync contrast settings enabled on your Windows device, Discord will adopt its theme colors. You can choose to opt-out by turning off Sync contrast settings.

With both High Contrast Mode and the client sync enabled, your original Theme settings for your client will be disabled (i.e. Dark & Light themes). If you prefer to keep Discord’s theme colors on your client even with High Contrast Mode enabled on your device, you will have to disable Sync contrast settings from your Accessibility settings tab. This will reactivate your original Theme settings.

This setting will only take effect if you have enabled High Contrast Mode on your Windows device first. Otherwise, if you have High Contrast Mode disabled on your device, you won’t see any changes to Discord when you interact with Sync contrast settings.

From your Accessibility settings tab, you can Sync contrast settings with your Windows contrast theme. You can only enable/disable if you have Windows High Contrast Mode enabled from your device’s settings.

Have any feedback about contrast settings? Let us know here.

You can learn more about changing your Discord client’s appearance at this article.

Contrast Slider on Mobile

On the Discord mobile app, we added a Contrast slider to allow users to increase or decrease their app’s contrast.

Role Colors

Available on Desktop and iOS. Support on Android coming soon!

On Discord, server admins and moderators can set up permissions for their server members through a role system. A server’s various roles can be identified by color, which defaults to applying a color to your username, or server nickname, based on your highest sitting role of that server. However, users have told us that some role colors make a username or server nickname illegible against their selected Discord theme. To solve for this, users can now determine how role colors are displayed in their personal view of their Discord client.

Go to User Settings > Accessibility, then navigate to the Role Colors section. You can choose from:

  • Show role colors in names
  • Show role colors next to names
  • Don’t show role colors

Profile and Client Theme Sync

Profile themes allow Nitro subscribers to customize the color of the background and border of their profile cards in Discord. If you would prefer for the background colors of all profile cards to be uniform in color in your personal view of the Discord client, you can apply your client theme to profile cards with the Sync profile themes setting. This is ideal for people who have chosen a client theme so that text is easier to read and this setting applies that client theme preference to profile cards.

  1. Go into your User Settings by clicking the Cog/Gear Icon (⚙︎) at the bottom-left corner of the app.

  2. Select Accessibility from the left hand panel, then scroll down the page to find the Profile Colors section.

  3. Toggle on the Sync profile themes. This is also where you can disable the sync of profile themes and the Discord client theme to utilize the color gradation options for profile themes.

Other Accessibility Features

Looking for other accessibility features not listed in the Accessibility Settings page? Check out:

  • Accessible Drag and Drop FAQ
  • Image Alt Text

Accessible Drag and Drop FAQ

We’re constantly working to improve Discord for everyone that uses it—no matter how they use it.

What this article covers:

  • How to Drag and Drop
    • Open-Source Drag and Drop
  • Troubleshooting JAWS screen-reader on Windows
  • Have Questions or Feedback?

How to Drag and Drop

Alongside Drag and Drop, we also have a new Text-to-Speech Rate Slider available.

For years, you could drag and drop everything from server collections, channels, and roles using your mouse. However, this wasn’t optimal for those that would like another way to perform these same actions. That being said, Discord now has Accessible Drag & Drop available, which allows you to perform actions to sort and organize a variety of things within the platform - all from your keyboard.

The drag and drop function is currently available on our desktop and browser clients.

As mentioned above, instead of solely relying on your mouse to rearrange and organize a variety of things on Discord, you can use the following actions to drag and drop certain items using your keyboard. To do so:

  • Press on the server or the channel that you would like to drag and drop, which you can find in the left-hand panel server list or the channel list of a server.
  • Press Ctrl + D/Cmd + D to select that item and lift it from its original position.
  • Use the Up and Down arrows again to move the item into the desired position which will be indicated by a green dot or line.
  • Press on the Spacebar or Enter key to drop the item into its position.
  • You can also press on the Esc key to cancel the drag and drop action for that item.
Open-Source Drag and Drop

We’ve open-sourced Drag and Drop! If you’re a developer, you can utilize and customize our Drag and Drop features in your projects! Check out Drag and Drop on GitHub here: github.com

Troubleshooting JAWS screen-reader on Windows

Not hearing any drag-and-drop updates while using JAWS on Windows? JAWS may block in-app announcements.

If you are using JAWS 2022 (version 2022.2206.9 or later) or 2023, then:

  • Open JAWS

  • Go to Utilities > Settings Center

  • Select “Discord” in the list of Application combo box. This will ensure that any settings changes only apply to the Discord app

  • Search for “Announce Live Region Updates”

  • Ensure the “Announce Live Region Updates” checkbox is checked. You may need to uncheck the checkbox, apply the changes, and then re-check the checkbox

  • Restart Discord If you are on an earlier version of JAWS without the “Announce Live Region Updates” setting and you are not hearing the announcements, then you may need to do one of the following:

  • Upgrade JAWS

  • Switch to NVDA

  • Use JAWS with the browser version of Discord (in Chrome, Edge, or Firefox) where announcements are not blocked

Have Questions or Feedback?

We hope this update improves your Discord experience and if you would like to give our Accessibility team live feedback, please fill out this form: dis.gd.

If you have any additional questions, please reach out to our support team here: dis.gd or Tweet at us @discord_support!

Age-Restricted Commands

What this article covers:

  • What are Age-Restricted Commands?
  • Who can use Age-Restricted Commands?
  • Where can they be used?
  • How do I access Age-Restricted Commands?
  • Help! I’m over 18 years old, but can’t use Age-Restricted commands!

What are Age-Restricted Commands?

Age-restricted commands are commands from apps that may contain age-restricted content, and may only be used by people 18 or older. To ensure that Discord is safe for everyone, our policies require that developers label adult content as age-restricted and not distribute it to people under the age of 18.

Who can use Age-Restricted Commands?

Users who are 18 and older can access them in servers and DMs.

Where can they be used?

They can be used within age-restricted channels in servers, and in DMs after a user has opted-in to use them.

How do I access Age-Restricted Commands?

In servers, you can use these commands only within age-restricted channels. Not all apps have age-restricted commands, but if an app in your server has them, they’ll only be accessible within those designated channels.

In DMs, age-restricted commands are turned off by default. If an app contains age-restricted commands, you can access them by enabling the toggle within User Settings > Privacy> Server Privacy Defaults.

Help! I’m over 18 years old, but can’t use Age-Restricted commands!

If you are over the age of 18 and have been locked out of an age-restricted channel, or are unable to use age-restricted commands in DMs, you can appeal by following the instructions in this Help Center article.

Custom App Icon

Custom app icons let Discord users personalize their mobile app icon and desktop in-app icon by changing the default Discord app icon to unique designs that match their style.

What this article covers:

  • What is a custom app icon?
  • How to set a custom app icon
    • Desktop
    • Mobile
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What is a custom app icon?

Note: Custom app icons are only available to Nitro and Nitro Basic members.

Custom app icons allow Nitro and Nitro Basic members to customize their Discord app icon on their Android and iOS mobile devices. Customize your home screen with a variety of new icons and find the one that matches your style. With Nitro, the app icon can be changed as often as you’d like!

How to set a custom app icon

Desktop

Note: For desktop, your custom app icon will appear within the Discord app.

  1. To get started, navigate to your User Settings by selecting the cogwheel button [] in the bottom-left of the app.

  2. Then, press Appearance to view the App Icon section. While here, you’ll be able to view the various in-app icons you can choose from!

  3. Select the in-app icon you’d like to apply. You can also choose Preview App Icon to make your selection and preview the customized in-app icon in the upper left corner of your Discord app.

  4. While in the Preview App Icon menu, press Back To Settings once you have chosen the desired in-app icon and you’re all set!

Mobile

  1. Start by tapping on your avatar in the bottom right corner to access User Settings.

  2. Scroll down until you see the App Settings category and then tap on App Icon.

  3. Now you can select any available app icon! To select your chosen icon, tap on the icon that matches your style.

  4. Once a new icon is chosen, you’ll receive a pop-up confirming the change (if you’re on iOS).

  5. Navigate back to your device’s home screen to see that the Discord app icon has changed!

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What happens if I set a custom app icon, but my Nitro credit, Nitro, or Nitro Basic expires?

A: Once your Nitro credit, Nitro, or Nitro Basic expires, you will no longer be able to keep the selected custom app icon. To add a custom app icon again, you will need to be subscribed to Nitro, Nitro Basic, or have Nitro credit.

Q: Can I upload my own custom app icon to Discord?

A: No. You can only select from one of the available Discord app icons.

Q: Will the custom app icon carry over to other mobile devices I’m logged in on?

A: No. On each mobile device, you will need to set up the custom app icon.

Q: Why isn’t my Discord app icon on my desktop’s home page changing?

A: The custom app icon feature on desktop only changes the in-app Discord app icon.

Q: Why can’t I see limited edition icons on desktop?

A: At this time, limited edition icons are only available on mobile devices.

Discord’s Beta Programs FAQ

This article covers information about Discord’s Beta Program.

What this article covers:

  • What is Discord’s Beta Program?
  • How Beta Eligibility Works
  • How to Check if You Have a Beta feature
  • Active Beta Features
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What is Discord’s Beta Program?

Discord’s Beta program is how we test new features to help us improve Discord. A small, random group of users gets access to a beta feature so we can gather feedback and see how it performs in the real world. The feature may move toward a wider release. If it doesn’t, it may change significantly or be discontinued.

How Beta Eligibility Works

  • Beta features are given to a small, randomly selected group of users for testing. It’s not something you can request or sign up for.
  • Support can’t manually add users to a beta or override targeting criteria.
  • Having access to one beta doesn’t mean you’ll have access to others.
  • Beta access can be removed at any time, including if the experiment ends or the feature doesn’t move forward.

How to Check if You Have a Beta feature

If you’re one of the users who has access to a beta, you’ll see a label indicating that the feature is in beta. For example, you may see a popover in Discord, along with a beta tag next to the feature.

Active Beta Features

  • Favorites: users can favorite certain channels on Discord and keep the conversations that matter most at their fingertips.
  • Bookmarks: users can bookmark the messages they care about most and return to them later.
  • Personal widget: Nitro users can create a personal widget that’s available on their profile. What’s added there is up to you!
  • Scheduled messages: set a time in the future to send your messages in DMs and channels.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why don’t I have access to this Beta?

A: Users in a Beta experiment are chosen at random. If you don’t have access to the Beta, you’re not currently in the experiment group.

Q: How do I get access to a certain Beta feature? Can support add me?

A: There’s no way to be manually added to a Beta experiment group. If the Beta goes well and the feature is well received, it may be rolled out more broadly — at which point everyone will have access.

Q: Where can I read more about beta terms?

A: Check out our Paid Services Terms for more information about betas.

Discover Tab
