Game Invites

What this article covers:

  • What are Game Invites?
  • How to invite another user to a game
  • How to join a game
    • Ask to Join
  • Troubleshooting Errors
    • Game Not detected
    • Unable to Send Invite

What are Game Invites?

If the game supports it, you’ll be able to spectate or even ask your friend if you can join their party. You can do all this through Discord itself via a user’s profile (mini or main profile) or through a Game Invite within a text channel. Let’s go over how all of this works.

How to invite another user to a game

Whether you’re putting together a party from a server of friends, or creating a group from a larger server, we’ve worked hard to make inviting others to join you as easy as possible:

After you launch your game, keep your eye on the + button in your chat bar (bottom left side of the app). Once you see the Play button, tap on it and drop the game invite directly into chat. Friends can tap on the invite and join your game.

How to join a game

You’ll need to have run the game at least once for Discord to detect it.

There are a few ways to join a game, let’s go over each one.

Option 1

Your friend can send you a game invite in a text channel or through a direct message/group direct message.

To accept the invite, just tap on Join.

Option 2

If your friend has their Activity Status enabled, access their mini profile or profile (by tapping on their username in your friend’s list or server member’s list) and you’ll see a Join option if you’re able to join them.

Ask to Join

If your friend is currently battling their way through a game, instead of being able to join directly, you can instead tap on Ask to Join.

You will receive an invite when your friend accepts it, or an invite will be automatically sent.

If someone requests to join your game, you’ll get a message in-game (displayed through the Discord overlay) and all you have to do is follow the on screen prompt to approve.

Spectating a friend in Game

To watch your friends in game, simply head over to their mini profile, and tap on the Spectate button. The game will launch and you’ll start spectating if the game supports Spectate mode. You can only spectate someone if you’re friends with them and the game supports this.

Troubleshooting Errors

Sometimes invites need some help to work perfectly! Here are some common errors that may come up.

Game Not Detected

Trying to join a friend and you’re getting a “Game not detected” error? In order for Discord to recognize that a game includes these features, you’ll need to have launched it once since they were incorporated into the game. Please try opening the game and trying to accept the invite again.

Unable to Send Invite

If you’re trying to send someone a game invite through Discord, but you’re not seeing the option, here’s how to resolve this.

Option 1

Make sure that you have it enabled so Discord can share your Game Status. Here’s how to check this.

  1. Tap on cogwheel [] next to your Discord username to access your User Settings.

  2. Then head to Activity Settings and tap on the Activity Privacy tab.

  3. Make sure that Display current activity as a status message is enabled.

  4. Also, make sure to check under the Registered Games tab to see if it’s disabled or enabled for that specific game.

Option 2

Make sure that the game you’re trying supports Discord game invites and that you’re in the right state (able to invite someone into your party) in the game so people can join your party.

Note to Developers: The Rich Presence API is now live. If you’re interested in incorporating these features into your game, head over to our developer’s page.

How can I change Discord’s Language?

Changing the language in Discord is super easy! This guide will show you how.

The Process is simple!

Open up your user settings.

Check out the “Language” tab, and select your language from the options available.

Simple as that! Now you can enjoy Discord in its many geographical flavors.

How do I add different Keybinds?

Note:

This feature is only available on the desktop version of our app!

You won’t be able to set keybinds on the mobile or browser client!

If you’ve used Push-To-Talk, you’re most likely familiar with Keybinds, and how they work in order to make Push-To-Talk (PTT) function appropriately.

Discord’s got a couple of other super handy Keybind possibilities that you can use to become a hotkey extraordinaire.

Here’s how to check them out:

  1. Open your User Settings tab

  2. Click the Keybinds tab

And now we’re in business. We’ve got a few points to touch on as far as setting everything up goes.

Getting started

While you can add as many separate Keybinds as you want, you have start add them individually. Start by pressing the “Add a Keybind” button:

Note: When you’re editing keybinds, keybinds are disabled. Leave this page to turn them on.

Pro Tip: You can use multiple keys to bind a key. For instance (SHIFT+ENTER). Just hit the keys in sequence.

You’ll find a drop-down menu with a couple of different selections:

Unassigned: This doesn’t have any function! Make sure you choose a different option in the list.

Push to Talk: Hold this Keybind to temporarily enable your mic while in Push to Talk mode.

Push To Mute: Hold this Keybind to disable your mic activity while in Voice Activity mode.

Toggle Mute: Press this Keybind to toggle your mic’s transmission on or off.

Toggle Deafen: Toggle your output’s playback on or off. Also disables your mic.

Toggle VAD: Toggle to switch between Voice activity and Push to Talk modes.

Toggle Streamer Mode: Turns on and off streamer mode.

Toggle Overlay: Toggle the overlay on or off to display in game.

Toggle Overlay Lock: Toggle the lock of the overlay in game.

Once you’ve chose which selection of separate Keybinds you want to use, go ahead and click the blank box next to it:

Then enter your desired key press:

Note: I wouldn’t recommend using this Keypress combination. It’d probably be pretty difficult to use.

And you’re all set! Wash, rinse, and repeat for all keybinds you want to utilize.

How to Change Discord Color Themes and Customize Appearance Settings

Looking to customize Discord’s appearance? Whether you need better readability or prefer the aesthetic of Dark mode, we’ve got several options to help you personalize your Discord experience. Learn how to change themes and customize your app’s appearance.

What this article covers:

  • How to Change your Discord Theme
    • Desktop
    • Mobile
  • How to Change the UI Density
  • How to Change the Message Display
  • How to Use a Color for my Theme
  • How to Customize Your Theme
    • Creating a Custom Theme
    • Sharing Your Custom Theme

How to Change your Discord Theme

Important: We’re currently running an experiment with Server Themes, an additional perk available to select servers that allows server admins to set a custom color theme for their server with 3 Server Boosts. To configure it, go to Server Settings > Server Theme.

Once enabled, members can choose whether to view the server’s theme while they’re in that server or keep using the theme set on their own device. If you have a theme set under User Settings > Display > Theme, you can switch between the server’s theme and your account theme at any time.

Desktop

First, head into your User Settings by selecting the cogwheel [], then select Appearance.

Access Theme Settings on Desktop: Open User Settings > Appearance

Discord offers several default theme options: Light, Ash, Dark, Onyx, and Sync with computer.

  • The Light theme features a white background with dark grey text and includes an optional Dark Sidebar.
  • The Ash theme uses a mid-gray background with white text.
  • The Dark theme displays a dark gray background with white text.
  • The Onyx theme presents a gray and black background with white text.
  • Sync with computer (known as Automatic on mobile) matches your Discord theme to your device’s appearance setting.
Example of Discord Theme Selection Interface on Desktop
Mobile

Tap your avatar in the bottom-right corner of the mobile Discord app, then tap the cogwheel [] in the upper-right corner. Then, scroll down and tap on Appearance.

Access Theme Settings on Mobile: Open User Settings > Appearance

At the top, you’ll find these theme options: Light, Dark, Midnight, and Automatic (which syncs with your device settings).

  • The Light theme uses a white background with dark grey text. You can also enable the Dark Sidebar option.
  • The Dark theme uses a dark grey/charcoal background with white text.
  • The Midnight theme presents a gray and black background with white text.
  • Automatic matches your Discord theme to your mobile device’s appearance settings. When you enable “Sync across clients” on desktop, your theme syncs across all devices (desktop, mobile, and browser). However, themes may display slightly differently on mobile.

For instance, if you select Ash on desktop, it will appear as Dark on mobile.

Example of Discord Theme Selection Interface on Mobile

How to Change the UI Density

In the Appearance menu, scroll to UI Density. Choose between Compact, Default, or Spacious to adjust the spacing around content (and navigation spacing in the desktop app). UI density doesn’t affect message density.

UI Density options on Desktop

How to Change the Message Display

In the Appearance menu, scroll to Message Spacing > Chat Message Display. You can choose between either Default or Compact to adjust the spacing specifically between message elements.

Chat Message Display options on Desktop

Choosing Compact will remove user icons for a denser chat view.

Example of Light Theme with Compact Message Display

Fine-tune your app’s appearance using the sliders to adjust the following:

  • Zoom Level: Adjusting zoom changes the size of all Discord elements, including text. The Discord desktop app offers a slider control, while browsers use their built-in zoom function. Use Ctrl/Cmd + plus (+) to zoom in or minus (-) to zoom out.
Example of Decreasing Zoom Level
  • Chat Font Scaling: This setting adjusts only chat text size while keeping other elements unchanged. Note that the zoom level will amplify whatever font size you choose here.
Example of Increasing Chat Font Scaling
  • Message Group Spacing: Increase the space between chat messages to make conversations easier to read.
Example of Decreasing Message Group Spacing

Note: These steps may appear slightly different on mobile.

How to Use a Color for my Theme

Nitro subscribers can access additional themes for Discord across all platforms!

Find all available themes in User Settings under the Appearance tab on both desktop and mobile.

Nitro subscribers can customize Discord’s look with colorful themes

Even without Nitro, you can preview themes on the desktop app. Select the Preview Theme button to open a preview sidebar where you can test different themes.

Preview Theme: See How Different Themes Look Before Applying

Need more help? Check our accessibility article for additional appearance settings.

How to Customize Your Theme

Creating a Custom Theme

Make Discord match your unique vibe with custom themes! Nitro subscribers can choose custom themes with endless color combinations to customize their app’s appearance.

When the “Sync across clients” toggle is enabled, custom themes applied on desktop may affect your mobile experience.

Make Discord match your unique vibe with custom themes! Nitro subscribers can choose custom themes with endless color combinations to customize their app’s appearance.

  1. To get started, navigate to your User Settings by selecting the cogwheel icon [] located to the right of your avatar in the bottom-left corner.

  2. Press Appearance where you will find the Theme category.

  3. Under Color Themes, select the Custom Theme icon [].

Navigating to User Settings > Appearance > Theme on Desktop
  1. In the Customize your theme sidebar to the right of your app, you can select the following:
  • Select between Dark or Light mode color palettes
Selecting Between Dark and Light Mode
  • Select your custom colors using the color field and hue slider
Choosing Colors from the Color Field and Hue Slider

Tip: You can use either the color picker icon [] or enter a Hex code to select a color for your theme.

Choosing Colors by Entering a Hex Code or Using the Color Picker
  • Add additional colors to your gradient by pressing Add Color Info: You can select up to 5 colors when creating a gradient.
Using the Add Color Option
  • Use the Gradient Direction slider to control how your colors flow Info: The Gradient Direction slider will only show as an option once you’ve added two or more color options.
Using the Gradient Direction Slider
  • Use the Color Intensity slider to adjust how vibrant your colors appear
Using the Color Intensity Slider
  1. When you’re satisfied with your changes, select Apply in the bottom-right corner of the sidebar to save them.
Apply Button in Sidebar

Tip: Press the Surprise Me icon [] in the bottom-left corner of the sidebar to generate random color combinations for your theme!

Using the Surprise Me Icon

Tip: You can also restore your theme back to your previous custom theme by selecting the Reset button.

Using Reset Button
Sharing Your Custom Theme

Important: Nitro subscribers can share, preview, and apply custom themes on the desktop app and browser client, while mobile is limited to previewing and applying.

Once you’ve created the perfect custom theme that reflects your unique style, you can easily share it with friends on Discord!

  1. Press the Share icon [] in the bottom-left corner of the Customize your Theme sidebar.

  2. In the Share custom theme menu, select the users or channels you want to share with. You can also include a personal message using the message box.

  3. When you’re ready, press the Send button.

Sharing a Custom Theme to a Channel

Tip: To apply a shared custom theme, press the Preview button in the shared Custom Theme box. If you like how it looks, select the Apply button in the sidebar to confirm.

Applying a Shared Custom Theme to Your Discord

How to Use Search on Discord

Looking for a specific message or file in Discord? Discord’s powerful search feature helps you quickly find conversations, media, and links across your servers—no matter how far back when they were sent.

Whether you’re tracking down an important announcement, locating a shared image, or finding that perfect meme from months ago, Discord’s search filters let you narrow results by user, date, channel, and content type. This guide will show you how to use Discord’s search bar effectively, apply advanced filters, and find exactly what you need in seconds.

What this article covers:

  • What is the Search feature?
  • How to Use Search
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • How to Use Search Filters
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • How to Sort Your Search Results

What is the Search feature?

The search function incorporates a few different tools and filters to help you find what you need in the smallest, friends only server, an expansive community-wide server, or in direct messages (DM). Since Discord won’t delete your messages until you decide to, you can refer to anything sent in your server as far back as when it was created.

Note: Server owners and admins/mods with Manage Messages permissions can delete messages within their server.

How to Use Search

Note: Search will index within your current server or DM.

Desktop/Browser

Important: Cross-DM search is available on mobile. On desktop, it’s currently in experiment and available to a limited number of users.

On desktop or browser, select the search bar in the upper-right corner of the app to get started. You can also hotkey your way to search success within the currently-viewed channel by pressing CTRL + F (Win) or CMD + F (Mac).

Example of Using Search on Desktop
Mobile

On mobile, tap the search icon [] in the upper-right corner to open the search bar and start typing.

Example of Using Search on Mobile

How to Use Search Filters

Desktop/Browser

When you open search on desktop or browser, you’ll see filter options to help narrow your results:

  • From a specific user searches for messages sent by a particular person
  • Sent in a specific channel searches within a single channel
  • Mentions a specific user finds messages that @mention someone
  • Includes a specific type of data searches for messages containing links, embeds, polls, files, or other content types
  • More filters combines multiple search criteria for precise results
Example of Using a Search Filter on Desktop

Tip: On desktop or browser, type from:, in:, mentions:, or has: in the search bar as shortcuts to quickly filter results.

Example of Typing from: Shortcut in Search

Tip: Use More filters to combine multiple search options or add criteria like date ranges and author type (user, bot, or webhook).

Example of Using More Filters Option

Note: The More Filters option is only available on desktop and browser, not on mobile.

Mobile

When you open search on mobile, you’ll see the following filter options:

  • From a specific person searches for messages sent by a particular person
  • Mention someone finds messages that @mention someone
  • Has specific data searches for messages containing links, embeds, polls, files, or other content types
  • In a specific channel searches within a single channel
  • Sent on a date searches for messages from a specific date
  • Before a date searches for messages before a specific date
  • After a date searches for messages after a specific date
  • By author type searches by user, bot, or webhook
Search Icon (Left) and Search Filters (Right) on Mobile

How to Sort Your Search Results

Note: Sorting your search results is only available on desktop and browser, not on mobile.

After you search, results will appear in the side menu. Select the sorting icon [] to sort by:

  • Newest shows the most recent messages first
  • Oldest shows the earliest messages first
  • Most Relevant shows the closest matches to your search terms first
Selecting a Sorting Type in the Search Side Menu

Select any message in the results to jump directly to it in the channel.

Selecting a Search Result to Jump to a Message

Note: Search indexes all messages from the very first message in each server channel. Larger servers may take longer to index initially, but once indexed, searches will be fast.

How to Use the LFG Channels to Find Game Sessions on Discord

LFG Channels are a channel type that give players in select servers a dedicated space to post and browse live game invites, so it’s easier to find others to play with.

What this article covers:

  • What is the LFG Channel?
  • Eligibility
  • How to Make an LFG Post
  • How to Join an LFG Post
  • Linking Your Account
  • Frequently Asked Questions Important: LFG Channels are currently an experiment and not widely available. It’s only enabled in a small number of servers at this time.

What is an LFG Channel?

LFG Channels are a forum-style channel where players in eligible servers can post and browse live game invites for select supported games. Instead of sending invites directly to friends where they can get buried in chat, you can post your session to the channel so other players in the server can find and join it.

Each LFG Channel post includes its own thread, so players can chat and connect to voice together before joining.

Eligibility

LFG Channels are currently being tested with a limited group of servers and players.

  • It’s currently available in the official ARC Raiders server. Support for other games is coming soon.
  • It’s available to members of those servers who have the corresponding game installed. Note: Want other players to be able to join you? Set your privacy or activity-sharing settings to public on the platform you play on (e.g. Steam, Epic, Xbox, and etc.).

How to Make an LFG Post

Note: For other players to join you directly, Discord needs to be able to see and share your game activity. That means keeping your game running, and turning on activity sharing in two places:

  1. User Settings > Activity Privacy > What Activity I Share, turn on Share my activity.

  2. Right-click the ARC Raiders server icon, select Privacy Settings, and turn on Share my activity for that server.

You can post your own game session to the LFG Channel so other players can find and join you.

  1. Select Create Post in the top-right corner of the LFG channel.
Example of arc-raiders-lfg Channel (Top) & Create Post Button (Bottom)
  1. Add a description, select relevant tags, and add or remove voice chat. To include an invite embed so others can join you directly from Discord, select Link Account and have your game open. The embed only appears while you’re playing.

Tip: Want other players to join your game directly? Link your account so your post shows a live session card that lets other players see your squad’s open spots and request to join your lobby. If you decide to stay unlinked, you can still create posts and join other players’ games without it.

Invite Creation Window
  1. Select Create to publish your post. It’ll appear in the channel for other players to browse.
Example of Post with Account Linked

How to Join an LFG Invite

You can join another player’s posted invite directly from the LFG Channel.

  1. Browse the LFG Channel to find a session you’d like to join.

  2. Open the post and select Join.

Depending on the game, this either sends a request that the post creator accepts in-game, or joins you directly if the session is open to anyone.

Tip: Chat in the thread before joining to confirm details like play style, mic preference, and what the poster is looking for.

Linking Your Discord Account

Linking your account connects your Discord account to your in-game account for a supported game.

Linking your account is optional, but it’s the easiest way to show your squad’s open spots and get others to join your game seamlessly. Once linked, your post shows a live invite embed so other players can join you directly from Discord. Without it, you can still create posts and join other players’ games.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why don’t I see the LFG Channel in my server?

A: This feature is part of a limited experiment and is only visible in select servers for supported games. If you don’t see it, your server may not currently be part of the experiment.

Q: Can I request access to the LFG Channel experiment?

A: This experiment is currently limited to a small group of servers, and access can’t be requested or manually granted at this time.

Q: Do I need to link my account to use the LFG Channel?

A: No, linking is optional. If you link your account, your post will show a live session card so other players can join you directly.

If you stay unlinked, you can still create posts and join other players’ games, you just won’t have that live session card.

Q: Why am I unable to accept a game invite?

A: This can happen if you’re trying to join from a different platform than where the game is installed.

Make sure you’re using the same platform where the game is installed (e.g. Steam, Epic, Xbox, and etc.) to create or join an LFG post.

Q: Why don’t I see a live invite embed on my post?

A: A live invite embed only shows when all of the following are true: your account is linked, your game is running, and your privacy or activity-sharing settings are set to public on the platform you play on (e.g. Steam, Epic, Xbox, and etc.), and you’ve turned on activity sharing both in your Discord User Settings and for the official ARC Raiders server.

Make sure your account is linked and your game is already running before you create your post. The embed won’t appear if you complete these steps afterward.

Keyboard Navigation FAQ

Note:

- Keyboard Navigation is only available on the desktop and browser app. These navigation settings will not work in the mobile apps.

Whether you rely on your keyboard to use your desktop, or you just don’t feel like reaching for your mouse, Discord now has full keyboard navigation across the entire desktop app so that you can do what you need to in the way that works for you.

What does this article cover?

  • Getting Started with Keyboard Navigation
  • Navigating Messages
    • Message Shortcut Keys List
  • Section Jumping
  • Other Resources on Shortcuts

Getting Around

Navigating Discord with a keyboard is based around two things:

  • moving focus with the Tab key and the arrow keys, and
  • interacting with elements with Enter and Spacebar.
To start navigating in Keyboard Mode, simply press Tab.

Once you’re in Keyboard Mode, you’ll see a blue Focus Ring appear around the element that currently has focus. This ring will move around as you navigate.

For the most part, the Tab key will move you through everything in the app. Buttons, Links, and other interactive content is generally going to be part of the Tab order of the app, so if you can click it, you can probably Tab to it.

For everything else, arrow keys should get you around as you’d expect - list-like content such as the Guilds list, Channels, Messages, context menus, and more.

Because these things can have hundreds of entries at a time, they often aren’t included in the Tab order of the page, so if you see something that looks like a List, try the arrow keys.

Navigating Messages

Messages in Discord can be pretty complex. Sometimes there are just a few words, but other times there are user and channel mentions, links, images, videos, embeds, reactions, and a full list of actions you can take on each message.

To navigate through these messages, start by hitting the Tab key!
Then you can jump from one to the next with the arrow keys, and then move into the content of a message with Tab.

Message Shortcut Keys List

With so many actions to take on messages, there are also a number of dedicated shortcut keys to make things quicker. When you focus on a specific message in Keyboard Mode and you have your blue ring highlighting the message you’d like to interact with, you can use the following shortcuts below!

Key

Action

q

Quote Message

Add a Reaction

r

Reply to Message

e

Edit

Backspace

Delete message

p

Pin message

Ctrl + C (Windows)

Cmd + C (Mac)

Copy message content

Alt+ Enter

Mark unread

Escape

Move back to the Textbox/Chatbar

Moving Faster - Section Jumping

There’s a lot of stuff in Discord. If you’ve got a lot of messages, holding the Tab key to try to get around will quickly get cumbersome.

To make this easier and to help you get around faster, you can use Section Jumping to immediately move between the large sections of the app.

While in Keyboard Mode, pressing F6 will immediately move your focus to the start of the next section in the app (and pressing Shift+F6 will move you backwards through the sections instead).

For example, if you’re focused on a Channel in the Channel List, pressing F6 will take you directly to the Messages section, and pressing it again will take you to the Channel Members, or, if you have an active Search open, to the Search results.

In the server view, the sections you can jump between are:

  • the Server list
  • the Channel list
  • Messages
  • the Member’s List As a reminder on what shortcuts you can use for Section Jumping, check out this table below:

Key

Action

F6

Section jump - Move focus to the start of the next section in the app

Shift+F6

Move focus backwards through the sections

Even Quicker with Shortcuts

Discord also supports keyboard shortcuts. Jumping between guilds or unread channels, using the Inbox, and opening the Quick Switcher. All of these have worked for years!

And you can now more easily find a reference for everything that’s available in the User Settings→Keybinds section.

If you’re interested in learning more about all the possible hotkeys - check out this link for Mac users and this link for Windows users!

New Mobile App Updates & Layout

Hello there! If you’ve been using Discord for a while now, you probably noticed the mobile app was designed to reflect the desktop app. With this new iteration of Discord on mobile, we hope to make the mobile experience feel like it was optimized for your mobile device rather than a scaled-down desktop app. The new mobile design aims to simplify and improve the Discord experience for everyone by creating a more organized, streamlined, and better-looking mobile app that helps you get to your chats quickly and easily.

We’re actively gathering feedback as we release this change to ensure that we continue to provide the best experience on Discord. For those of you who have already experienced previous iterations of our mobile app, thank you for all the thoughtful feedback you’ve shared with us so far! We’ve been paying great attention to it and it’s helping us continue to make improvements. If you’re new to this version of the app, be sure to explore the new mobile experience and all that it has to offer. If something doesn’t work for you, please let us know so we can continue to improve!

This Help Center article will explain the core updates to the mobile app and how you can provide feedback and thoughts on what does or doesn’t work for you.

What this article covers:

  • Home Tab for your Messages and Servers
  • Messages Icon
    • Active Now
    • Favorite DMs and Group Chats
    • DM and Group Chat Details Page
    • DM and Group Chat Creation
    • Add Friends
  • Notifications Tab
  • You Tab
    • Friends List
    • Settings & Settings Search
  • Voice & Video Calls
  • Swipe to Reply
  • Accessing Channel, DM, or Group Chat Details
  • New Customization Options
    • Themes
    • Message Previews
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Home Tab for your Messages and Servers

The Home tab, located in the bottom-left corner of the app, is where you can find all your servers and access your Direct Messages (DMs) and group chats.

Once you open the Home tab, you’ll see the Messages icon and all of your servers on the left of the screen. Tapping on the Messages icon will show all the DMs and group chats you’re part of. Tapping on a server will open it within the Servers tab and allow you to scroll through and open that server’s channels.

In each of your servers, you’ll be able to Favorite channels, use the search bar at the top of the server channel list to find messages and content in a server, and see the channel details of each server channel, which includes a list of the server members in that channel, the Media/Files/Links sent in that channel, the threads created, and more.

Messages Icon

Your DMs and group chats can now be accessed by tapping on the Messages icon [] at the top left corner of the server list.

You can also search across all of your DMs and group chats to find the chat you’re looking for selecting the search icon [].

Active Now

While in Messages, you can easily see what your friends are up to within the Active Now section. Active Now can show things such as:

  • When your friends are currently in a Voice Channel in a mutual server
  • A game your friend is playing
  • If your friend is participating in any activity that supports Rich Presence, like listening to Spotify or watching something on Crunchyroll
  • Your friend’s Status, including their Custom Status Learn more about your own Activity Status settings here.
Favorite DMs And Group Chats

You can favorite direct messages (DMs) and group chats so that they stay pinned to the top of your Messages tab for quicker access.

  1. To favorite a DM or group chat, tap on the Home tab > Messages icon.

  2. While in Messages, navigate to the DM or group chat you would like to favorite.

  3. Then, long-press it to open the options menu where you can tap Favorite.

You will then see the DM or group chat at the top of your messages with a star icon [] next to it.

You can repeat the same process and select Unfavorite to remove a G/DM from your favorites.

DM And Group Chat Details Page

From this page, you can search for messages sent in the DM or group chat, see its members and their statuses, and filter for the media, GIFs, files, and links shared there.

You could also use this page to find a specific photo that you sent, but don’t remember when you sent it. By selecting the Media filter, you can browse all of the images and videos sent in that DM or group chat quickly without having to scroll through the whole chat history.

DM And Group Chat Creation

From the Home tab > Messages, you can press the blurple Message button [] in the bottom right of the screen to start a new DM or group chat.

From here, you can type the names of your friends that you want to add or tap on their profiles to add them to the chat.

Once everyone is there, you can then tap on the text box at the bottom of the screen to begin sending a message. If you have an existing group chat with the users selected for the chat, you will automatically see that group chat instead of starting a new one.

If you do want to create a new group, just select New Group at the top of the screen before selecting any friends.

Add Friends

You can add new friends by heading over to the Home tab > Messages icon and tapping the Add Friends button.

Notifications Tab

We simplified your notifications experience to emphasize the things you can uniquely find in the Notifications tab, like friend requests.

All notifications in the Notifications tab are actionable: Join an event, message someone who just accepted your friend request, etc.

You no longer need to click a notification for it to be considered read in the Notifications tab, just seeing it is enough. The next time you return to the Notifications tab, all read notifications will be de-emphasized and new notifications will be emphasized so you always know what’s new and don’t have to actively clear your notifications.

Red badges will persist on the Notifications tab when you have pending friend requests, and you must resolve your pending friend requests to clear them.

You Tab

The You tab is your dedicated space to view and customize how you appear to others on Discord. You can find the You tab in the bottom right corner of the app. From this tab, you can easily edit your profile, set your status, view your friends, or manage your settings.

Friends List

We moved the Friends list to be in the You tab. To see your existing friends, view pending friend requests, and add new friends, tap Your Friends in the You tab. Only you can see your Friends list.

Settings & Settings Search

App Settings are still in this tab and you can now access them by tapping the gear icon at the top right of the You tab. If you want to get to settings quickly, you can also double-tap the You tab icon at the bottom of the screen.

You can now search within Settings. It’s a small but mighty improvement. Now, you don’t have to waste time scrolling through every single setting to find what you’re looking for. Simply type in the search bar and watch the magic happen.

Voice & Video Calls

We’ve updated the interface for voice and video calls. Before joining a voice call, you can easily preview the Text in Voice for that call without joining the call by tapping the quote icon to the right of the Join Voice button. Tap the microphone icon to the left of the Join Voice button to control whether you will enter the call muted or unmuted. You must tap the Join Voice button to enter a voice call.

Instead of opening the details and settings for a voice call, swiping up from the bottom of the screen now opens the Text in Voice chat for that voice call.

To find the details and settings for a voice call, tap the name of the voice call at the top of the screen. See below for the function of each button at the top of a voice call:

1. Minimize voice call within Discord
2. Open call details and settings
3. Change audio to speakerphone
4. Invite friends to call

To screenshare or start an activity, tap on the screen to reveal the bottom menu. Then you can tap on the rocket icon to pull up all available activities.

When in a voice call, you can double-tap on another user’s tile to make their video fullscreen.

When you’re in a fullscreen activity or stream, double-tap to minimize it and get back to the rest of the call participants.

Swipe to Reply

We added swipe-to-reply on messages for faster witty retorts. Simply swipe from right to left across a message in a DM or channel to reply to that message.

Accessing Channel, DM, or Group Chat Details

Previously, swiping from right to left across a channel, DM, or group chat would take you to see the details of that chat such as pinned messages or a list of who is in the channel, DM, or group chat. To access channel, DM, or group chat details, tap on the name of the channel, DM, or group chat at the top of the screen.

New Customization Options

We’ve added more ways to make the Discord mobile app feel like your space through customization options. We added a new Midnight theme and the ability to toggle message previews in your Messages tab.

Themes

We added the new Midnight theme, which is pure black to go easy on your eyes and save battery on OLED compatible devices.

  1. You can choose your theme by navigating to your Settings.

  2. Select Appearance.

  3. Then go to THEME and select your desired theme.

You can also toggle on Sync across clients to have your themes stay consistent across your desktop and mobile apps.

Midnight theme is currently not available on Desktop.
Message Previews

Make every unread DM a total surprise when you turn off message previews for added privacy and a more simplified chat look. To update your message preview preferences:

  1. Navigating to your Settings.

  2. Select Appearance.

  3. Go to Message Previews and update your preferences.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I get the new mobile app updates and layout?

A: We are currently rolling out the latest updates to our mobile app, including the new layout, to all of our users, but it may take some time for you to be enrolled. Please continue to make sure that your app is up to date with the latest version from the app store. When you become eligible for the new mobile app experience, you will be notified within the app.

Q: Why are you changing the mobile app layout?

A: We’re always looking for ways to improve our users’ experience on Discord and a big part of this is making investments in improving and evolving the features available on mobile.

Q: Are there iOS/OS or Discord app version requirements (ie. iOS 11.0+, Android 5.0+, Discord version 206+)?

A: You must have the latest version of the Discord app to experience these updates. We also recommend that you have the latest version of your mobile device’s OS.

Q: Were there any changes to the layout of the Settings page?

A: Yes, the location has changed and we have added a search bar to Settings. You can find your Settings page in the You tab on the bottom right of the app via the gear icon in the top right of the You tab. If you want to get to settings quickly, you can also double-tap the You tab icon at the bottom of the screen to jump to Settings.

Q: Can I go back to the original mobile app layout?

A: We understand the change might take some getting used to, and we’re here to help make that transition as smooth as possible for you. But with this update, the original mobile layout is no longer available.

Q: Will this be available for both Android and iOS users?

A: Yes.

Q: How do I find the details and members of a channel, DM, or group chat now that I cannot swipe to see it?

A: You can access channel, DM, or group chat details by tapping the name of a channel, DM, or group chat at the top of the chat.

Reduced Motion Setting

Discord uses motion effects to create the perception of depth. However, we understand that these effects can cause problems for users who are affected by excess motion and movement within apps. So, we’re adding Reduced Motion to help!

What does this article cover?

  • What does Reduced Motion do?
    • What Animations and Movement that are limited when Reduced Motion is enabled?
  • Where can I find this setting?
  • Windows
    • Having Trouble Disabling Reduced Motion?
  • MacOS
  • iOS
  • Android

What does Reduced Motion do?

This setting is an accessibility feature that limits the amount and intensity of animations within Discord.

Animations and Movement that are limited when Reduced Motion is enabled:
  • New/Old messages Bar & Jump to Messages - slide animation removed and instead send you directly to the message
  • Disables the shaking animation that happens when trying to close out setting pages that have unsaved changes.
  • Server banner animation is minimized when scrolling down a channel list.
  • Setting pages no longer fade in/out and instead instantly open/close.
  • Disable the message highlight that occurs when your mouse is hovering over a message in chat.
  • Disables the background animations found on the Login/Authentication page.
  • Disables GIF avatars from playing in the chat unless you click into the user profile.
  • Animations for tooltips, menu dropdowns, and context/pop-out menus will now fade in.
  • Discord’s loading animation when launching (spinning Clyde) will now be static.
  • Animated Emojis will now be static in the Emoji Picker, within chat, statuses, and reactions:

Where can I find this setting?

You can find the setting by going to User Settings ⟶ Appearance ⟶ Accessibility.

Currently, you can choose between:

  • Sync with computer
  • Enable Reduced Motion
Sync with computer(default):

If you’d like Discord to automatically match the same settings that you have your computer’s current settings, press on that “Sync with computer” button!

Enable Reduced Motion:

If you’d like to only enable Reduced Motion in Discord, but keep your current computer settings the same, you can instead toggle “Enabled Reduced Motion” on.

When this setting is enabled, Discord will reduce animations and movements within the app regardless of your system configurations.

If you would like to disable Reduced Motion in Discord, simply toggle “Enabled Reduced Motion” off.

Having Trouble Disabling Reduced Motion?

If you’re having trouble getting Reduced Motion to be disabled on Discord, it’s most likely due to pre-configured settings that have been enabled on your system.

For Mac OS, there’s one option, but for Windows, there are multiple settings that could enable Reduced Motion in Discord. We have steps below for where to look to double check on these settings.

To check your current system settings:

Windows
  • Display Settings
    • On Windows 10, go to Settings ⟶ Ease of Access ⟶ Display ⟶ Simplify and personalize Windows. Toggle “Show animation in Windows” off.
  • Advanced System Settings
    • If you’re still unable to disable Reduced Motion, you will need to open Advanced System Settings and make sure that the Animate controls and elements inside windows option checked!
    • This setting will cause Reduced Motion to enable, but you can adjust the individual animations that you prefer to keep disabled on your system within this menu.
Note: If you have motion and animation effects disabled on your system for reasons other than accessibility, then following the step above should allow you to disable Reduced motion for Discord, but enable for your system.
Mac
  • On a Mac, you go to System Preferences ⟶ Accessibility ⟶ Display and uncheck the box for “Reduce motion”.
iOS
  • On iOS, The settings can be found in User Settings (Bottom right by pressing your Avatar) ⟶ App Settings ⟶ Appearance ⟶ Reduced Motion Sync with Device Settings will make it so that the Discord app stays in sync with the Reduce Motion setting in iOS’ accessibility settings: support.apple.com

When reduced motion is enabled it will overwrite two other settings:

  • User Settings ⟶ Text & Images ⟶ Automatically play GIFs when possible will be set to off and disabled
  • User Settings ⟶ Text & Images ⟶ Play animated emoji will be set to off and disabled
Android

  • On Android, The settings can be found in User Settings (Bottom right by pressing your Avatar) ⟶ App Settings ⟶ Appearance ⟶ Reduced Motion When reduced motion is enabled it will overwrite two other settings:

  • User Settings ⟶ Text & Images ⟶ Automatically play GIFs when possible will be set to off and disabled

  • User Settings ⟶ Text & Images ⟶ Play animated emoji will be set to off and disabled

  • User Settings ⟶ Text & Images ⟶ Stickers Animate on interaction

Have Questions or Feedback?

We hope this update improves your Discord experience and if you would like to give our Accessibility team live feedback, please fill out this form: [dis.gd](https://dis.gd/a11y).

If you have any additional questions, please reach out to our support team here: [dis.gd](https://dis.gd/contact) or Tweet at us @discord!

Tabs to Android!

Note: Beginning on August 1st, 2022, Discord users can expect to see improvements to the Discord Android application, including:

- Feature consistency across platforms through a centralized and streamlined app development process across Android, iOS and desktop

- Faster app update release cycles when a new feature is introduced or a pesky bug is fixed thanks to a more consolidated process

Over the next few weeks, the Android app will begin to transition to the React Native framework to enhance the user experience. To use the new version of the Discord app:

- Go to the Google Play Store to manually update your Discord app.

- Otherwise, if auto-update is enabled on your Android device, the app should automatically update.

You can read more about this change in our blog post.

The old Discord Android application will officially sunset on September 1st, 2022, so make sure you’ve updated your Android app from the Google Play Store before then!

Starting today, we will begin rolling out the latest Discord app (version 20) to our Android users with a new, simplified experience that makes the app easier to navigate.

In this article we will cover:

  • Getting Started
  • Tabs
  • Feedback

Get to your conversations faster

Before we talk about the tabs, let’s talk about getting to the tabs. You’ll first notice that we got rid of the drawer and moved to sliding panels. This opened the door for us to implement a couple of better gestures:

  • You can swipe from any area on the screen to navigate between panels. Much easier on the thumbs than reaching for the edge of the screen to open a drawer.
  • You can now “peek” at a new activity without having to leave your current chat. Less time navigating and more time chatting.
Improved access to features

Next, you’ll notice the new bottom tabs. We wanted to find a way to expose important features in a more mobile-native way.

  • Home tab: Discord is where friends and communities come together, so we made the main Home tab front-and-center. Your servers and DMs live here.
  • Friends tab: We know real estate is a precious commodity on mobile devices, and tabs allowed us to remove the Friends page from being buried in the DM list. Previously, it could take up to 5 gestures to accept a friend request (open drawer → tap the home button → tap friends → tap the old “Pending” tab → tap accept). Now with tabs and some improvements to the friends page, it will only take 3. And it can have its own notification badges so you won’t miss a new request.
  • Quick Switcher and Recent Mentions: To our users who are a part of many communities, we built the Quick Switcher and Recent Mentions features to make it easier to navigate around and find messages relevant to you. When we rolled out experiments with giving these features their own space, we noticed that the use of the Quick Switcher nearly doubled! We’ll be making improvements to these experiences as well – stay tuned!
  • User Settings: Your own user settings can be accessed on the right-most tab that displays your avatar and status. Power-user of custom statuses? No problem – you can still change them directly from the tabs view by long-pressing the User Settings tab. While we’re excited about the power of tabs, we also wanted to keep the app uncluttered, especially while you’re in a conversation. So we decided that you should only see the tabs when you need them. The tabs will slide them away when you’re viewing a channel or DM.

The Future

Finally, tabs give us the flexibility to keep investing in making Discord more useful to our users. As an example, millions of users on the desktop have used server discovery to find communities relevant to their interests. In a post-tabs world, we now have a few options to bring a better way to discover new servers to mobile without cluttering the app.

As always, we’re constantly looking for ways to improve. Let us know if you have any feedback!

What is You Bar?

You Bar is a persistent navigation element at the bottom of your Discord mobile app. It displays your avatar, username, and status, keeping your identity visible as you move through servers and conversations.

Note: You Bar is currently available on mobile only. The desktop experience is separate and not affected by this change.

When implementing the You Bar, we ensured that all previously available features remain accessible. Tapping the You Bar opens your profile, where you’ll find the same options as before: profile editing, Quests, Shop, Settings, and more.

Setting a Status

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is You Bar available on desktop?

A: No. You Bar is a mobile-only feature.

Q: Can I turn off You Bar or go back to the old bottom bar?

Q: Does this change affect how I use Nitro or server features?

Q: I’m still confused about where things moved. Where can I get more help?

Find Your Friends FAQ

What is Find Your Friends?

Connecting with your friends on Discord just got a whole lot easier! Introducing Find Your Friends - allowing you to discover friends on Discord using your phone contacts!

What does this article cover?

  • How does Find Your Friends work
  • How do I set up Find Your Friends
    • How do I change my name?
    • How do I disable Find Your Friends
  • Privacy

How does Find Your Friends work:

Let’s say Wumpus and Cap are friends and Wumpus has Cap’s contact in his phone.

Wumpus and Cap both are on Discord and want to find friends, so BOTH of them will need to opt-in to be discoverable via Find Your Friends.

If Wumpus enables Find Your Friends, Wumpus will then see Cap in a friend discovery list, and have the option to send him a friend request. It will look something like this:

However…

If Wumpus has Cap’s contact, but Cap decides not to opt-in to be discoverable via Find Your Friends, Wumpus will not discover him.

How do I set up Find Your Friends?
  1. Navigate to your Friends tab by tapping the second button to the left in the Navbar:
Filled friends list (Left), Empty friends list (right)
  1. Once you are on the friends list, tap Find your friends or Getting Started. The screen will look different depending on if you already have friends on Discord or not😔.

Filled friends list (Left), Empty friends list (right)

  1. Next, you will reach the Permissions screen. Tap the toggle button to enable contacts to add you on Discord. (Tap Learn More for more details)

  2. Next you will have to verify your Phone Number. If your phone number is already verified on your Discord account, you may skip this step.

To Verify your Phone Number, enter your phone number and paste the 6 digit confirmation code (XXX-XXX)

  1. Once you tap Sync Contacts with a verified phone number, a modal will show up asking for access to your contacts list.

  2. Once you press Ok, we will begin syncing your contacts.

  3. Once the sync is complete, we will show you the list of your contacts on Discord with Find Your Friends enabled. If none of your contacts are on Discord or have Find Your Friends Disabled, you will have the option to send them an invite.

  4. In case your contacts do not recognize you by your Discord Tag, you may change the name your contact will see when you send them an invite on this screen.

How do I change my name?

  1. To change the name that shows up in Find Your Friends, navigate to your User Settings tab by tapping the first button to the right in the Navbar (It’s the button with your profile picture).

  2. Once you are at your User Settings page, tap the Name setting.

  3. Update your name and press Next.

How do I disable Find Your Friends?

  1. To disable Find Your Friends, navigate to your User Settings tab by tapping the first button to the right in the Navbar (It’s the button with your profile picture).

  2. Once you are at your User Settings page, navigate to your Privacy & Safety setting.

  3. Tap Allow contacts to add me to enable/disable the feature.

Note: Once disabled, your contacts will no longer discover you through the Find Your Friends feature.

Privacy

How does Discord know my contact is using Discord?

After enabling Find Your Friends, Discord periodically syncs phone numbers from your phone to Discord’s servers.

These phone numbers are cryptographically hashed. When your contact also enables Find Your Friends, and if you both have agreed to be discoverable, we compare the cryptographically hashed data and detect a match. Raw phone numbers are never stored. The names visible in app are manually entered by each user so their friends can recognize them. This process allows us to prevent spam, only matches you to people you know and never to people you block. Disabling Find Your Friends or deleting your Discord account will remove all of your contact data from Discord’s servers.

We won’t use Find Your Friends data for any other purpose other than helping you find and invite people to Discord.

What happens after I disable Find Your Friends?

Disabling Find Your Friends or deleting your Discord account will remove all of your contact data from Discord’s servers.

We won’t delete any existing friend recommendations in either direction, but no new recommendations will be created.

Friends List 101

What this article covers:

What is the Friends List?

The friends list is your list of all of the friends that you have added on Discord. Here is everything you can see under the Friends tab:

  • All: All of your added friends.
  • Online: Your friends who are currently online or idle.
  • Pending: Friend requests you’ve received and sent. You can also view spam requests by tapping the View spam requests sub-section.
  • Blocked: Users you’ve chosen to block.

How to Add a User to Your Friends List

Desktop/Browser

Option 1

  1. Tap on the Direct Messages icon in the upper-left corner of the app. Then select the Friends tab.

  2. Press Add Friend to add a friend. Input their username in the text field and press Send Friend Request to send the request. If the username is not entered correctly, you will receive an error. Otherwise, you can check under Pending to see the pending request.

Option 2

  1. While in a server, group message, or direct message (DM), tap on the profile of the user you’d like to add as a friend.

  2. Tap the Add Friend icon [ ] to send a friend request.

Mobile

Option 1

  1. Tap the Messages icon [] in the top-left corner of the mobile app.

  2. Then tap Add Friends.

  3. Add a friend using any of the listed methods, or select Add by Username to input their username.

  4. Once you’ve entered the username, press Send Friend Request.

Option 2

  1. Tap your avatar in the bottom-right corner and navigate to your friends list by tapping on Your Friends.

  2. In the top-right corner tap Add Friends.

  3. Add a friend using any of the listed methods, or select Add by Username to input their username.

Option 3

  1. While in a server, group message, or DM, you can tap on a user and then tap on the ellipsis in the top-right corner [].

  2. Tap Add Friend to send a friend request.

How to Accept or Decline a Friend Request

Desktop/Browser

  1. If you have any pending friend requests, you can tap the Direct Messages icon in the top-left corner and access the Friends tab.

  2. Then tap Pending to view all of your pending friend requests. To accept a request, tap the checkmark; to decline, tap x to decline.

Mobile

  1. Tap the Notifications tab at the bottom of the app.

  2. Here you will see all pending friend requests. You can tap on Accept to approve it or Ignore to decline it.

Need help managing unwanted friend requests? Learn how to ignore users by checking out our How to Ignore Users on Discord article.

When you’re meeting new people through the games you play, you can now choose between two options when adding someone as your friend on Discord: you can either add them as a Game Friend for a specific game, or you can add them as a Discord Friend!

How do I add friends on Discord?

Looking for ways to connect with friends on Discord? How to Add a Friend

Note: The maximum number of friends you can have on an account is 1,000 (accepted friends only). You can have up to 1,500 pending incoming friend requests and 1,000 pending outgoing friend requests. If the incoming request limit is exceeded, the oldest pending requests will automatically be removed until you’re back to 1,000.

Adding a friend on Discord is as easy as 1-2-3! Let’s go over the various ways to send friend requests and some common errors you might encounter.

If you’re receiving lots of unwanted friend requests, you may want to ignore certain users. Need help managing unwanted friend requests? Learn how to ignore users by checking out our How to Ignore Users on Discord article.

Important: You will be alerted before accepting a friend request from an unfamiliar user. Unfamiliar users are those you do not have any mutual friends or shared small servers (< 200 members) with. These alerts can help you make more informed decisions about new connections. These alerts cannot be turned off at this time regardless if you’re an adult or teen.

Example of Unfamiliar Friend Request Alert
Username

Desktop/Browser

  1. Press on the Discord logo in the top-left corner.

  2. Next, make sure you have the Friends tab selected and then press the button that says Add Friend.

Note: The username needs to be exact, or the request will not go through.

  1. After typing or pasting in the username, press on Send Friend Request to send the friend request.

  5. After you’ve typed or pasted in the username, tap Send Friend Request.

Profile

  2. Select their profile and then press View Profile.

  3. Next, press Send Friend Request to send them a request.

Send Friend Request Button in User’s Profile on Desktop

Mobile

  1. Navigate to a group chat or a server of the user you’d like to add.

2a. Next, if you’re in a group chat, you can tap the user’s profile to add them in the profile view.

2b. If you’re in a server, tap one of the text channels in the server. Now under the Member’s list for the server, tap the profile of the user you’d like to add.

Common Errors When Adding a Friend

Friend Request Failed

If you go to add a friend and you receive the warning “Friend Request Failed” this is because the user is not accepting friend requests. They will need to add you as a friend instead. This means they have their Friend Requests setting disabled.

Friend request failed Notification
Double Check that the Username is Correct

If you receive an error message that states “Hm, didn’t work. Double check that the username is correct.”, it means the username was not typed or pasted correctly.

The username needs to be exact, or the friend request will not go through, so double check each number, letter, underscore, or period you’ve typed and then try submitting the request again.

If you’re still running into an issue adding the friend after confirming that you’ve typed their username correctly, you’ll need to reach out to them to see if they can send you a friend request instead.

Error Message for Incorrect Username

Note: The Discord Support team is not able to manually add a friend for a user.

Instant Invite 102 - Group Invites

When you’re not ready to start a server, but you still want to share goofy gifs with some friends… That’s where group invites have you covered.

Group Invites

Your gif sharing group is ready to go, but it needs more members! Any group member who is currently on a computer will be able to create an invite link by clicking the Add Friends icon at the top of the screen.

Once you have created your invite link - you’re ready to share it with the world. It will appear very similar to a server invite.

Note: If your group fills up (10 members) the invite link will no longer work.

Even though you can only make group invites on a computer, you can use them to join a chat on any version of Discord!

Group Invite Management

Group DM owners, you have some special powers! As the owner of the DM you’ll be able to help manage any invites that have been created. Right-click the icon for your group DM and select Instant Invite.

Instant invite links for group DMs will automatically expire after 48 hours, however, the owner will be able to click the X next to an invite to deactivate it.

Note: If an invitee is blocked by the inviter, they will not be able to use the Group DM invite link.

Beginner’s Guide to Discord

Welcome to the comprehensive beginner’s guide to Discord!

What this article covers:

  • What is Discord?
  • Account Setup and Troubleshooting

  • What are Text and Voice Channels?

What is Discord?

Discord is a communication platform that allows users to interact through text, voice, and video. Users can join or create their own communities, which can be organized around various topics, interests, or gaming groups.

Check out our Video Tutorials to learn even more about Discord.

Account Setup and Troubleshooting

You can register a Discord account through the desktop app, your mobile device, or through a browser.

You can learn more about registering a Discord account, or about any possible registration errors, by checking out these articles:

  • Discord Sign-Up and Registration Guide: Need help signing up and registering for a Discord account? Check out this full guide to help you through the process.
  • How to Verify Your Discord Account: Having trouble verifying your account? Check out this guide for more detailed information on account verification.
  • Discord Login & Email Troubleshooting Guide: Having trouble logging in or registering a Discord account? Please check out this guide for additional help.

What is a Discord Server?

Discord servers provide you with the ability to create private, invite-only spaces for your friends or community—places where you can connect, collaborate, and enjoy meaningful conversations together. These dedicated spaces are what we call servers.

You can join existing servers or create your own for virtually any type of community or interest group. Whether you’re organizing a book club 📚, coordinating with classmates in a study group 🖊️, managing a dance class 💃, or simply staying connected with close friends, Discord servers offer the perfect platform to bring people together around shared interests and activities.

Example of a Discord server

You can learn more about Discord Servers by checking out these articles:

  • Discord Server Setup Guide: Learn more about how to set up your own Discord server.
  • Setting Up Permissions FAQ: Learn more about how to set up Server Permissions to manage and moderate your server members.
  • How do I set up a Role-Exclusive channel?: Need to set up role-exclusive channels for your server? Learn how in this article!
  • Notifications Settings 101: Learn everything you need to know and more about your notification settings.
  • Server Boosting FAQ: Learn more about Server Boosting and Additional Perks you can have for your server.
  • Custom Emojis: Learn how to upload custom emojis to your server or other servers you’re a part of.
  • Polls FAQ: If enabled on the server, you can share and vote in polls.

What are Text and Voice Channels?

Your server is made up of text channels and voice channels. This allows you to communicate with the other members of the server.

Text Channels

Text channels provide dedicated spaces for written conversations, helping to keep discussions organized and ensuring everyone has room to participate. You can create individual channels for each topic your group enjoys discussing—whether that’s planning fishing trips, sharing cooking tips, or any other shared interests.

Example of what a Text Channel is in a Discord server
Voice Channels

Voice channels allow you to connect with others through voice and video chat. Simply click on a voice channel to join—no calling or ringing necessary. Other members of your server can see when you’re in a voice channel and easily drop in to chat, say hello on video, or share their screen with the group.

Example of what a Voice Channel is in a Discord server

You can learn more about text and voice channels below.

  • Text Channels & Text Chat In Voice Channels: Learn more about setting up, editing, and managing text channels.
  • Voice Channels FAQs: Learn more about setting up, editing, and managing voice channels.

How to Share your Screen

You can share your screen or gameplay while connected to a voice channel, a direct message (DM), or group DM.

Example of what it looks like when someone is streaming on Discord

You can learn more about screen sharing by checking out the Go Live and Screen Share Help Center article.

Additional Discord Features

Account Connections

You can connect a variety of outside apps like PlayStation, Spotify, and Xbox to your Discord account. This allows for your User Profile not only to display various information, but also what song you’re currently listening to on Spotify. To learn more about how to connect an account to your Discord account check out this Help Center article.

Desktop Installation Guide

When using Discord, we recommend using our desktop clients for the best experience. Here’s how to install the Discord app on Windows, MacOS, and Linux.

What this article covers:

  • Windows
  • MacOS
  • Linux

Windows

To download the Desktop app for Windows, first head over to the Download Page in your preferred browser.

  1. Tap on the Download for Windows button to download the app.

  2. Follow your browser’s prompts to save and open the DiscordSetup.exe to start the installation process.

  3. Once installed, you can then open the Discord app and register an account or log into an existing account.

MacOS

To download the Desktop app for MacOS, first head over to the Download Page in your preferred browser.

  1. Tap on the Download for Mac button to download the app.

  2. Open the Discord.dmg file.

  3. Drag the Discord logo and drop it over the Applications folder in the pop-up window.

Linux

To download the Desktop app for Linux, first head over to the Download Page in your preferred browser.

  1. Tap on the Download for Linux button to download the app.

  2. For manual installation on a Debian based distribution you can use the following commands:

    cd ~ /Downloads

    sudo dpkg -i package.deb or sudo apt install ./package.deb

  3. If you’re installing with a package manager, please follow the installation prompts.

  4. Now that the app is installed, you can register a Discord account or log into an existing one.

Slash Commands

Discord’s slash commands are a powerful way to interact with apps directly in your chat. These commands start with a forward slash (/) and provide an interactive menu of available options.

Slash commands provide these key benefits:

  • Easy-to-use interface with auto-complete suggestions
  • Built-in command discovery
  • Standardized command format across all Discord apps
  • Enhanced security and permissions management
Using Slash Commands

NOTE: Slash commands only work when an app has been added to a server or your Discord account. Learn how to add apps here.

  • Type “/” in the message box to see available commands
  • Browse through the command list or start typing to filter
  • Select a command and fill in any required parameters
  • Press Enter to execute the command For a comprehensive guide on using slash commands, including troubleshooting tips and best practices, check out the official Slash Commands FAQ.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: On what platforms can I use keyboard shortcuts?

A: Keyboard shortcuts can only be used on the browser and desktop version of Discord.

Q: On what platforms can I use custom keybinds?

A: Custom keybinds can only be used on the desktop version of Discord.

Q: What’s the quickest way to access Discord’s keyboard shortcuts?

A: Press Ctrl + / (Windows) or ⌘ + / (Mac) to open the Keyboard Shortcuts menu for a complete overview of available shortcuts.

Q: How do I search for specific messages in Discord?

A: You can search within the current channel using Ctrl + F (Windows) or ⌘ + F (Mac). To search across all channels, use Ctrl + Shift + F (Windows) or ⌘ + Shift + F (Mac).

Q: Can I customize Discord’s keyboard shortcuts?

A: Yes, you can create custom keybinds through User Settings > Keybinds. This allows you to personalize shortcuts according to your preferences.

Q: How do I quickly switch between servers and channels?

A: Use Ctrl + K (Windows) or ⌘ + K (Mac) to open the quick switcher. For server navigation, use Ctrl + Alt + Right/Left (Windows) or ⌘ + ⌥ + Up/Down (Mac).

Q: What are slash commands and how do I use them?

A: Slash commands are interactive tools accessed by typing “/” in the chat. They provide easy access to app and bot commands. Simply type “/” to see available commands and follow the auto-complete suggestions.

Q: What slash commands can I use in a Discord voice chat?

A: You can use slash commands in Discord voice chats when an app has been added to your server or Discord account. Learn how to add apps here.

Q: How can I format my text in Discord messages?

A: Use keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl/⌘ + B (bold), Ctrl/⌘ + I (italic), and Ctrl/⌘ + U (underline). You can also use markdown syntax for additional formatting options.

Q: Are there accessibility features in Discord?

A: Yes, Discord offers comprehensive accessibility navigation using tab, arrow keys, and specific shortcuts for features like screen readers.

These can be found in the Accessibility Navigation section of the guide. You can find more general information on our Accessibility features here.

Q: How do I manage my audio settings quickly?

A: Use Ctrl + Shift + M (Windows) or ⌘ + Shift + M (Mac) to mute/unmute your microphone, and Ctrl + Shift + D (Windows) or ⌘ + Shift + D (Mac) to deafen/undeafen audio.

If you see the error message Email is already registered, it means this email address is already linked to a Discord account.

Remember, you can only use an email address with one Discord account at a time.

Tip: If you’re already logged into another Discord account, you’ll need to log out to be able to register a new account.

Getting Started

Hello weary traveler and welcome to Discord! If you are here, you must be wondering how you can get started on Discord.

What this article covers:

  • Get the app
  • Create your account
  • Claim your account
  • Verify Your Phone Number

Get the App

You can download Discord for free on desktop here, or through the Google Play store or Apple App Store on mobile and tablets.

Example of where to download the Discord desktop app on the Discord website
Example of where to download the Discord mobile app on the Discord website

Check out the Desktop Installation guide

For the mobile apps, check out the Getting Started on Mobile guide

If you don’t want to download the app, you can use our web client to access Discord directly from your browser.

Example of where to access the Discord app through your web browser on the Discord website

Tip: For an in depth list of compatible Browsers and Operating Systems, check the OS/system requirements guide here.

Create Your Account

Tip: When registering your Discord account, please use an email address you can access and maintain access to. If you want to change the email address of your Discord account, you’ll need access to your original email. The Discord Support team is not able to change the email address of your account.

You can create your account on the Discord registration page, or in the app.

Example of the Register button on the Discord browser/desktop app

Claim Your Account

If your new account is not verified, your username will be given a random 5 digits to the end of your username after 7 days from account creation.

You’ll be able to enjoy all of the chat functions Discord has to offer, but it’s important to claim your account by verifying your email address. This will ensure that you keep your username and Discriminator (those four digits next to your user name), as well as remembering all the servers you’ve joined!

To claim your account, simply check the email that you used to create your account. If you do not see an email, simply press the Resend button in the green banner at the top of the app:

Press Verify Email in the delivered email, and you’re good to go!

Tip: Some servers are locked behind a security Verification wall that requires a verified account before you can access chat functions. Read more about server verification levels here.

Verify Your Phone Number

Additionally, you can also verify your phone number to your Discord account!

To start the phone verification process, head into your My Account tab in your User Settings. Then press the Add button right beside the Phone Number section!

Example of where to add your phone number to your Discord account on the Discord desktop/browser app

Once pressed, you’ll be able to directly enter your phone and then press “Send” once you’ve entered your number! (Note: Make sure to select the correct country code!)

You’ll then receive a text message to your mobile device which will have a 6 digit code! When you receive the code, type those 6 digits into the menu!

Example of adding your phone number to your Discord account on the Discord desktop/browser app
Example of where to add your verification code for your phone number on the Discord desktop/browser app

Last but not least, to confirm your changes, you’ll need to enter the password to your account, and then press the Confirm button.

And then your phone number will be officially verified to your Discord account!
