Getting Started on Mobile

If you are new to Discord and would like to create an account via your mobile device, this guide will help walk you through the steps.

What this article covers:

  • Creating an Account
  • Setting up an Account
    • Changing Your Avatar
    • Changing Your Account Details
  • Adding Friends
    • Sending Friend Requests
    • Adding a Friend in a Server
    • Accepting Friend Requests
  • Joining Servers
  • Creating DMs and Group Chats
  • How to Start a Voice Call
  • How to Answer a Voice Call
  • How to Use Speaker Phone while in a Voice Call
  • Expressing Yourself
    • Sending Photos and Files
    • Sending Gifs
    • Adding Emojis
    • Adding Reactions

Creating an Account

  1. If you’d like to create a Discord account and start using the app, you can download Discord via your mobile device:
  • For Android devices, head into the Play Store
  • For iOS, head into the App Store

  1. Once the app is fully installed, tap on the app icon to launch the app.

  2. If this is your first time using Discord, press Register to create your account. You’ll need to enter:

  • a display name
  • a username
  • your email address or phone number
  • a password
  1. Once you’ve finished entering this account information, you can then select Next to start using Discord.
Remember to head into your email to verify your email address. By verifying your email address, you’ll be able to recover your account if you ever forget your password.
If your new account is not verified, your username will be given a random 5 digits to the end of your username after 7 days from account creation.

Setting up an Account

  1. To set up your account, tap on your profile icon in the bottom right hand corner.

  2. Then, tap the cogwheel [] in the upper right corner.

  3. This will take you to your Settings where you can select various options to personalize your account.

Changing Your Avatar

  1. If you’d like to change your avatar, tap your profile icon to navigate to your Profile.

  2. Then, tap on Edit Profile and select your profile icon to change your profile picture.

  3. After you’ve selected your desired photo, you can adjust the image by zooming in or out of the photo. Then, select the Choose option in the bottom right to reflect the changes.

  4. The image preview will now be reflected in your profile. If it’s to your liking, pressing Save in the upper right corner will save your changes.

Along with customizing your avatar, Nitro members can also add an animated avatar. If you’d like to learn more about animated avatars, you can check out this article.
Changing Your Account Details

As you continue exploring Discord, you may wish to change your username or even your email address associated with your account.

  1. If you would like to change your account details, head over to your Settings and tap Account.

  2. Once redirected to Account, you will see that you can select various options. To edit a specific account detail, tap the specific option.

  3. Before the changes are solidified, you will be asked to verify your password to confirm the changes. Then, you should be all set!

  4. Additionally, if you ever need to change your password, you’ll be able to press Password in the Account settings.

You can only change your username and avatar two times in an hour! So if you’ve reached the limit for the hour, you’ll need to wait before changing your name again!

Adding Friends

Now that you’ve officially created an account, you can directly add friends or receive friend requests from people that you already know on Discord!

Sending Friend Requests

  1. To send a friend request, be sure to tap the Messages tab in the bottom row.

  2. Once you have been redirected to Messages, tap the Add Friends button in the upper right corner.

  3. To add your friend by their username, tap @ Add by Username and input your friend’s username.

  4. Once you’ve typed in your friend’s Discord username and press Send Friend Request, a request will be directly sent!

If you’re not able to send a request, it’s possible that your friend needs to change their Privacy and Safety Settings for who can add them as a Friend. Check out the Friend Request section in our article on Privacy Settings for more details.

If you’d like to view your previously added friends, you can tap on your profile icon in the bottom right corner and select Your Friends.

Make sure that you’re typing your friend’s username exactly as spelled and double check capitalization since usernames are case sensitive. Additionally, make sure to remove any extra spaces.
Adding a Friend in a Server

  1. If you’re already in a server, and you’d like to add someone you’ve become friends with, you can tap on the channel’s name located at the very top to navigate to the Members list and tap on the person’s username to view their profile. You can also tap the user’s avatar in a message to view their profile.

  2. While there, you’ll be able to select the Add Friend option to send a Friend Request.

Accepting Friend Requests

If you’ve received a Friend Request, you’ll see a red notification on your Notifications tab.

  1. Press the bell icon located in the bottom row to be redirected to the Notifications tab.

  2. Then, you can check your pending friend requests by tapping on the Friend Requests icon in the upper right corner.

  3. Once you’ve been redirected to the Friend Request tab, you can view and choose to accept or decline pending requests.

To check if you are adding the correct friend, tap on the requester’s icon to view the requester’s User Profile.

Joining Servers

You can either press directly on an invite link from your friend to automatically join the server, or you can manually enter an invite link through the Join Server menu.

Joining a Server Directly

Manually Entering a Server Invite Link

  1. To manually enter an invite link that you’ve received, start by tapping the green plus sign button in the left side bar.

  2. You’ll then see the option to create or join a server. Select the Join a Server button and then manually input the invite link or the last string of the link that you’ve received.

  3. Once you fill out the appropriate invite link, you can tap the Join Server button.

  4. Afterwards, you will need to accept the invitation to confirm that you’re joining the correct server.

Creating DMs and Group Chats

If you’d like to have a smaller group chat outside of the server you can create a group chat.

  1. To start, tap Messages in the bottom row and select the New Message icon.

  2. Then, you’ll be able to select New Group and select your friends you’d like to add into the group chat.

You can select up to 10 friends to join within a group direct message.
  1. Once you’ve selected the friends you’d like to add, tap Create in the upper right corner. This will redirect you to the new group message you have just created.

How to Start a Voice Call

  1. In order to call a friend and start a voice call with them, you first want to tap the Chat Bubble [] in the top left corner of the Discord mobile app.

  2. Tap on your friend’s avatar icon at the top of the Direct Message list or in the DM you share with them.

  3. Tap on Phone Call icon [] at the top-right of the DM to start a Voice Call.

  4. To end the call, tap on the End Call icon [] in the bottom-right corner when in the Voice Call screen.

How to Answer a Voice Call

  1. If a friend is calling you and you want to answer, you can tap on the check mark or on the Phone Call icon [].

  2. To end the call, tap on the End Call icon [] in the bottom-right corner when in the Voice Call screen.

How to use Speaker Phone while in a Voice Call

There are 2 ways to enable speaker phone while in a voice call:

Option 1

  1. Tap on the speaker icon [] in the top-right corner while in a call to enable speaker mode.

Option 2

  1. While in a call, swipe up from the bottom screen to display all available call audio options. Tap on Change Audio Output.

  2. Tap on Speaker to enable speaker phone.

Expressing Yourself

Now that you’re connected with your friends in servers and DMs, you can now start chatting away through text, emojis, photos and more!

Sending Photos and Files

Want to stay in chat and directly send a photo without opening your camera app?

  1. You can send a photo on the fly to your friends by tapping the Add File () icon in the bottom left corner.

  2. This will let you view your photos within your photo gallery or select the Camera button.

  3. If you would like to directly take a photo, select the Camera button to open the Camera app within Discord. Then, you will be able to take a photo.

  4. Once you have taken or chosen the photo, you will be able to send a message along with the photo to your friends.

Sending Gifs

You’ll also be able to send gifs directly into chat by using the GIF Picker!

  1. To send a gif, tap the emoji icon located to the right of the message bar. This icon resembles a smiley face.

  2. Once you have tapped the emoji icon, the Emoji, GIFs, and Stickers selection menu will appear.

  3. Select the GIFs tab to view and choose various gifs to send to your friends. If you’d like to search for a specific gif, you can type within the Search Tenor bar to populate more choices.

Adding Emojis

You can directly send emojis through chat by pressing on that Emoji icon in the message bar!

You’ll be able to see your most frequently used emojis, or directly search for the exact emoji you’re looking for in the emoji search bar!

Adding Reactions

Not only are you able to send emojis within messages, but you can also choose an emoji to react to posted messages.

  1. To add a reaction on the mobile app, long press the message you’d like to react to. This will allow a new menu to appear.

  2. From this menu, you can choose one of your frequently used emojis as a reaction, or you can directly search for a specific emoji to use as a reaction by pressing on the Reactions icon.

  3. If another person has already reacted to the message, you can tap on their reaction to add to the reaction counter or you press on the emoji icon to select another emoji you’d like to add.

Nitro members can also add Super Reactions to add a little more hype, emotion, and intensity to your reaction! You can learn more about Super Reactions here.

And you’ve made it!

Group Chat and Calls

Whether you’re coordinating with a few friends or just want to chat without setting up a server, Group DMs and calls make it easy to connect directly — no server required. This article walks you through everything from creating a Group DM to managing members and jumping on a call.

What this article covers:

  • How to Create a Group DM
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
    • From Existing DMs
  • What are the Group DM Features
    • Start a Voice Call
    • Start a Video Call
    • Mute Notifications
    • Pinned Messages
    • Add Members
    • Member List
  • How to Manage the Group DM
    • Renaming the Group DM
    • Changing or Removing the Group Icon
    • Removing a Group DM Member
  • How to Leave a Group DM
  • Want to Learn More

How to Create a Group DM

Group DMs start from your Friends List, so you’ll need to add your friends on Discord before getting started — if you haven’t done that yet, check out How do I add friends on Discord? to get set up.

Tip: Group DMs support up to 10 members total (including yourself). If you need to chat with a larger group, consider creating a server instead.

Once that’s done, there are a couple of different ways to create a Group DM:

Desktop/Browser
  • Open your Friends List by selecting the Discord icon [] in the top left of the app.
  • Select the New Group DM icon [] in the top right corner of the Friends List.
  • In the Select Friends window, scroll through your list or search by username to find who you’d like to add.
  • Select everyone you want to include, then press Create Group DM.
Mobile
  • Tap the speech bubble icon [] to open your DMs.
  • Select the New Group DM icon [].
  • Search for or select friends you’d like to add.
  • Tap Create Group DM to confirm.
From Existing DMs

Alternatively, you can start a new Group DM from an existing 1:1 DM. This creates a new group chat without affecting your existing 1:1 DM.

  • Desktop/browser: Open the DM and select the Add Friends to DM icon [] in the top right corner, then select additional friends and confirm.
  • Mobile: Open the DM, tap the username at the top, then press the New Group DM option [], then select additional friends and confirm.

What are the Group DM Features

Once you’re in a Group DM, you’ll have access to a set of actions for calls, notifications, pinned messages, and more.

On desktop and browser, these appear as a row of icons in the top right corner of the chat window.

On mobile, some of these options are accessed by tapping the conversation name at the top of the chat to open the group settings panel.

Start a Voice Call in the Group DM

Voice calls let you talk with everyone in the group at once. Any member can start a call at any time, and calls stay open as long as at least one person remains — members can join or leave the call freely.

  • Desktop/browser: Select the phone icon [] in the top right corner to start a call.
  • Mobile: Tap the phone icon [] at the top of the Group DM to start a voice call.
Start a Video Call in the Group DM

Video calls work just like voice calls, with the added option to share your camera feed. You can toggle your camera on or off at any point once you’re in the call.

  • Desktop/browser: Select the video camera icon [] in the top right corner.
  • Mobile: Tap the video icon [] at the top of the Group DM. Note: Video calls in Group DMs are available on desktop and mobile. Browser support may vary depending on your browser’s camera permissions. Make sure Discord has camera access enabled in your browser settings if you run into issues.

For more help, see the Discord Voice and Video Troubleshooting Guide.

Mute Notifications in the Group DM

If a Group DM gets busy, muting notifications lets you stay in the conversation without being constantly interrupted. When muted, you won’t receive desktop or push notifications and will need to check the chat manually.

  • Desktop/browser: Find the Group DM conversation name in the Direct Messages list, right-click on the conversation in order for the Group DM menu to appear, then select Mute Notifications and choose your Mute Notification option.
  • Mobile: Tap the conversation name at the top, then press the bell icon and you’ll be lead to a menu to Mute Notifications. Tip: You can also manage incoming and outgoing call sounds under User Settings > Notifications on desktop/browser (see Notifications Settings 101), or Settings > Notifications on mobile (see Mobile Notifications Settings 101).
Pinned Messages in the Group DM

Pinned messages are a great way to keep important information — like plans, links, or reminders — easy to find for everyone in the group. From the pinned messages panel, you can jump directly to a message in the chat or unpin it.

  • Desktop/browser: Select the pin icon [] in the top-right corner to view pinned messages. To pin a message, hover over it, select the ellipses icon [] (more options) menu, and select Pin Message.
  • Mobile: Tap the conversation name at the top, then select Pins to view them. To pin a message, long-press it and select Pin Message from the menu.
Add Members to the Group DM

Anyone in the group can invite more friends to join, up to the maximum limit. Any current member can add new people, up to the 10-person cap.

  • Desktop/browser: Select the Add Member icon [] in the top right corner.
  • Mobile: Tap the conversation name at the top, then select Add Members [].
Members List in the Group DM

The member list gives you a quick view of everyone in the Group DM and lets you interact with them directly. From the member list, you can view a member’s profile or send them a direct message.

  • Desktop/browser: Select the member list icon [] in the top right corner to show or hide the panel.
  • Mobile: Tap the conversation name at the top to see the full list of members.

How to Manage the Group DM

Beyond chatting and calling, there are a few ways to customize and manage your Group DM. Some options are available to all members, while others are limited to the person who created the group.

Renaming the Group DM

Giving your Group DM a name makes it easier to find, especially if you have a lot of active conversations. The updated name is visible to all members.

Desktop/browser:

  • Select the Group DM name at the top of the chat window

  • Then edit the name, and press Save to confirm. Mobile:

  • Tap the conversation name at the top, then tap the settings cog icon []

  • Then in the Group DM Settings menu that pops up - press on Customize Group.

  • Then edit the Group DM name, and press Save to confirm.

Changing or Removing the Group DM Icon

You can add a personal touch to your Group DM by setting a custom icon.

Desktop/browser:

  • Press on the Group DM name at the top of the chat window.

  • Select the pencil icon to upload a new image, or Remove Icon to revert to the default icon.

  • Press Save to confirm. Mobile:

  • Tap the conversation name at the top, and then tap the settings cog icon []

  • Then in the Group DM Settings menu that pops up - press on Customize Group.

  • Then press the Group DM avatar icon to upload a new image, or Remove Icon to revert to the default icon.

  • Press Save to confirm.

Removing a Group DM Member

If you created the Group DM, you have the ability to remove members when needed. Only the person who created the Group DM can remove members.

  • Desktop/browser: Right-click the member’s name in the member list and select Remove From Group.
  • Mobile: Long-press the user’s avatar icon within the chat, then tap the 3 Dot Menu icon [] , and select Remove From Group.

How to Leave a Group DM

If you no longer want to be part of a Group DM, you can leave at any time. Any member — not just the group creator — has the option to leave.

On desktop or browser:

  • Right-click the Group DM in your DM list (left sidebar).

  • Select Leave Group.

  • Confirm when prompted. On mobile:

  • Tap the conversation name at the top, and then tap the settings cog icon []

  • Then in the Group DM Settings menu that pops up - tap Leave Group.

  • Confirm when prompted. Tip: Once you leave a Group DM, you’ll stop receiving messages from that chat and it will be removed from your DM list. You can only rejoin if an existing member adds you back.

Want to Learn More

That covers everything you need to know about Group DMs and calls across desktop, browser, and mobile!

  • If you’re new to Discord and want a broader overview, the Beginner’s Guide to Discord is a great place to start.
  • If you run into any audio or video issues, the Voice and Video Troubleshooting Guide can help.
  • For anything else, visit our Help Center for additional support.

What is a Server?

Think of any server you join as a giant tree house - each channel within a server represents another room within your tree house that you can chat with your friends!

Servers act as individual hubs split into two parts: text channels and voice channels.

Server List

The column on the very left-hand side of your Discord app is your server list. Any time you add a server, you’ll see it pop up as a small circular icon in this list, and they’ll show up vertically:

Pro Tip: You can rearrange your server list by dragging server icons up and down. You can even group servers together by dragging them on top of another!

Join a Server

To join or create a server, press the “+” icon at the very bottom of the server list. If you have a server invite link, press the Join a Server button, paste the link, and press Join Server:

Edit Your Server Settings Before Joining

If you press directly on the invite link (for example: discord.gg), you can modify the following privacy and security settings before officially joining the server!

  • Update your server nickname
  • Allow direct messages from server members
  • Show your activity status Once you press the Accept button, you’ll then join the server with your preferred settings!
Server Cap

Users can join/create up to 100 Discord servers.

You can raise this cap to 200 Servers when you subscribe to Discord Nitro.

What happens if I’m in more than 100 servers but lose Nitro?

We won’t remove you from any servers you’ve joined; however, you will no longer be able to join servers until you bring the total count under 100.

How to Log In to your Discord Account

Signing in to your Discord account is quick and easy, whether you’re using the desktop app, mobile app, or web browser. With the Discord sign-in process, you can securely access your account and connect with your communities in just a few steps. This guide will walk you through the different ways to log in, including using your email and password or QR code sign in. Follow along to ensure a smooth Discord sign in experience!

If you haven’t verified your account yet, make sure to do so, otherwise you risk losing access to your account. Check out this link for more information!

What this article covers:

  • How to Log In to Discord on Desktop/Browser
    • Use your QR Code to Log In to Discord
  • Log In to Discord on the Mobile App If you are experiencing issues with logging into Discord or seeing error messages for your login attempts, check out this support article explaining the common login errors.

How to Log In to Discord on Desktop/Browser

  1. If you’re using Discord web login, you can start the login process by heading to discord.com Otherwise, you can open the Discord app on your desktop device.

  2. At the Discord login page, enter either 1) your email address or 2) phone number that has been officially verified to your Discord account in the first text box.

  3. In the second box, type the password associated with your Discord account!

Use your QR Code to Log In to Discord

If you would like to conveniently and securely log in to the Discord on the desktop app or through a web browser, you can also use the QR Code Login feature via the Discord mobile app to do so.

  1. In order to use QR Code Login, start by logging into your Discord account on your mobile device.

  2. Open the User Settings menu by pressing your profile avatar in the bottom left corner, then tap on the cog wheel icon in the upper right corner.

  3. On the Overview page, select the Scan QR Code option to enable your camera mode on your mobile device for the QR scan.

Tip: The app will ask for camera permissions on your mobile device in order to scan the QR Code!

  1. After the QR scanner is triggered, simply line up the box outline in your mobile device’s camera with the QR code on the desktop screen. You’ll be asked to verify your Discord login into the desktop/browser on your mobile Discord app.

Want to learn more?

For more information on this QR login process, make sure to check out this support article here.

Important: Never approve a QR code login that you didn’t generate yourself! If you’ve been sent a QR code by someone else that opened the login verification screen, hit cancel right away.

Log In to Discord on the Mobile App

  1. Open the Discord app that’s downloaded on your mobile device. If you need to download Discord on your mobile device, you can check out this article for how to download Discord.

  2. Enter either 1) your email address or 2) phone number that has been officially verified to your Discord account in the first text field box of the Discord login page.

  3. In the second text field box, enter the password associated with your Discord account!

You will need to verify your phone number to your Discord account before using phone number login! Check out this support article to learn how to verify your phone number to your Discord account.

How to Fix Lag on your Discord

Lag on your Discord app can occur for a variety of reasons and vary on a user-by-user basis. If you are experiencing delayed functionality or stuttering on your Discord app, there are a few troubleshooting steps you can take that might help fix lag:

  • Ensure that your Discord desktop/mobile app is updated to the latest version
    • You can also try reinstalling the Discord app on desktop or mobile
  • Ensure that your device is updated to the latest OS version/drivers
  • Ensure your web browser is updated or try a different web browser for Discord
    • You can also try reducing the number of open tabs and browser windows
  • Test your Internet connection speed and reset your Internet modem and/or router
  • Disable Automatically play GIFs when Discord is focused by going to User Settings > Accessibility > disable Automatically play GIFs when Discord is focused
  • Disable Play animated emoji by going to User Settings > Accessibility > disable Play animated emoji
  • On the Discord desktop app: Disable Hardware Acceleration by going to User Settings > Advanced > disable Hardware Acceleration
  • When streaming: Reduce the stream quality by pressing on the three dots menu icon in the bottom corner of the video stream > pressing Stream Quality > selecting lower Frame Rate and Resolution options
Are you experiencing a bug on Discord?

If you tried the troubleshooting steps above and are still experiencing lag on your Discord app, you may have run into a bug. Before you reach out to us about the potential bug, please check out our Unsupported Bug Reports article for bugs we cannot provide support on. If the bug you’re experiencing is not mentioned in that article, you can learn more about reporting bugs to Discord on the How to Report a Bug article.

Are you experiencing an outage on Discord?

Alternatively, your Discord might be impacted by an outage affecting our Discord services. You can check for outages on the Discord Status page.

How to Connect Your YouTube Channel to Discord

If you’re a YouTube partner, you can integrate your YouTube channel into your Discord server so you can hang out with all of your members.

Or if you’re supporting your favorite YouTube creator through a membership, you can join their Discord server and chat.

What this article covers:

  • How to Connect YouTube to Discord
  • How to Integrate YouTube into your Discord Server for YouTube Partners

  • YouTube Integration for Viewers
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How to Connect YouTube to Discord

  1. On desktop/browser, tap on the cogwheel icon [] in the lower-left corner of the app to access your User Settings.
Example of how to access User Settings through the cogwheel icon
  1. Under your User Settings, head to the Connections tab.
Where to locate the Connections tab under User Settings in the Discord desktop/browser app
  1. Press on the right-arrow [] to display all available connections. Locate the YouTube tile, and then tap on it. This will open a new browser window where you can log into your YouTube account.
Example of the YouTube tile under Connections in the User Settings of the Discord desktop/browser app
  1. After logging into your YouTube account you should get a message stating you’ve successfully connected your account.
Example of what a successful connection between your YouTube account and Discord account looks like

How to Integrate YouTube into your Discord Server for YouTube Partners

Info: This is only available for YouTube Partners. If your YouTube channel does not currently have memberships turned on, you will not be able to integrate your YouTube channel into your Discord server.

You can create a membership-only Discord server for your YouTube channel or dedicate a few channels to only those YouTube members.

To get started, you first need to connect your YouTube channel to your Discord account following the How to Connect YouTube to Discord steps above.

After your YouTube channel is connected to your Discord account, now you can integrate your YouTube channel into your server.

  1. Navigate to your server and press on the server name in the upper left corner to open the Server Settings drop down menu.
  • You can also right-click on the server name to access the same menu.

  1. Press on Server Settings and then head to Integrations.

  2. Next, tap on YouTube to connect your channel.

Example of where the YouTube integration is located in the Integration tab under Server Settings in the Discord desktop/browser app
  1. You should see your channel listed here, tap on Enable to enable the integration.
Example of the location of the Enable button in the Integrations tab under Server Settings in the Discord desktop/browser app

5.You’ll be able to tell if the integration is successful, because you’ll see all available Discord YouTube integration options.

Example of what an integrated YouTube channel with memberships looks like in a Discord server on the desktop/browser app
Modifying Your YouTube Integration

After you’ve integrated your YouTube channel, you can edit your Integration settings.

Syncing

Although your YouTube members should be synced automatically, you can always run a manual Sync.

Grace Period

You can also change the Grace Period and what happens to a user once they no longer have an active membership. You can also make it so a user is kicked from the server or they just simply lose the membership role. To do this, press on the Remove Role option and select Kick instead.

Once you have integrated, you’ll also find that the new permissions role has been auto-created specifically for YouTube members. These roles will be named YouTube Member (for anyone that joins) and then you’ll have additional roles for each tier that you have created. For example, if you have a tier named “Plus” the auto-created role will be called YouTube Member: Plus.

However, you can rename these roles directly in Discord, adjust their permissions under Server Settings > Roles, and even change the colors of the role. Since this role is automatically managed by the YouTube integration, you can’t manually assign or delete members from it.

Tip: If you have Rule Screening set up for your server for new users, they can by-pass this requirement and join a server if they become a member through your YouTube channel.

YouTube Integration for Viewers

If you’ve joined or been gifted a membership to a YouTube channel and you want to access their Discord server, the first thing you need to do is make sure your YouTube account is connected to your Discord account by following the steps outlined under How to Connect your YouTube Channel to Discord.

After you’ve connected your YouTube channel to your Discord account, you’ll see all available YouTube channels that you’re currently subscribed to. There will be the Join option next to any server you haven’t joined yet. If you don’t see the Join option yet, don’t worry, you should see it soon! The system syncs in near real-time, and in the case of any errors, an additional sync is run by the system once a week.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why don’t I see the option to integrate my YouTube channel to my Discord server?

A: You need to be a YouTube partner with Channel Memberships enabled in order to integrate it into your Discord server.

Q: What if I was either gifted a Membership or I joined and I don’t see the server under connections to join or have the membership role in the server?

A: First, try removing your YouTube channel under User Settings > Connections and then reconnecting your YouTube channel. If you still do not see it, please ask the YouTuber or one of their moderators to run a manual sync by heading into Integrations in their Server Settings.

Q: What device can I connect my YouTube channel to Discord on?

A: Desktop app, mobile, and browser.

Contact Us: If you have additional questions or have trouble integrating your YouTube channel, please reach out to our support team: dis.gd.

Linked Channels are a unique type of server text channel that connects your Discord server directly with Discord-integrated games. When you link one of your server’s text channels, messages you send will appear in the game and messages you send in-game will appear in Discord.

Server Integrations Page

There’s lots of ways to customize your Discord server to make it your own. You can add bots to help with moderation, organization, or fun and games for your friends and community. You can use webhooks and Channel Following to get news and updates from other Discord servers and the internet at large posted directly into your server. For those of us that stream or make videos on YouTube and Twitch, our integrations with those platforms help you personalize your Discord server for your fans and subscribers.

All of these things contribute to making your Discord server uniquely yours. They make it feel like home for your friends and community. And now, they all live in one place to see and manage!

Meet the Server Integrations Page!

What is it?

The Integrations page is a place to manage all the bots, webhooks, and other apps that you add to your server to make it your own. For streamers and content creators, it’s also the place to manage your Twitch and YouTube integrations. Let’s dive into the specifics of each section.

The maximum number of integrations a server can have is 50.

Webhooks

Webhooks are a simple way to post messages from other apps and websites into Discord using internet magic. You can learn about all the specifics in our Intro to Webhooks help article.

The webhook page lets you see all the webhooks that have been added to your server, who added them and when, and what channel they post to. You can create new webhooks, as well as edit existing ones by changing their name, avatar, or channel. You can copy their URL for use in your code, or delete them if you’re done using them.

Channel Following

You can now see all the channels your server is following in one place. Channel Following allows you to follow announcements channels in other Discord servers into your own. Whenever a message is sent in those channels, it’ll be posted directly into your server.

On this page, you can see all the channels you’re following, edit their names and avatars, change where they post, or remove them if you no longer wish to get updates from that server.

Twitch and YouTube

If you’re a streamer, your integration management has also received a facelift! All of the functionality that previously existed is still there, as well as new info that wasn’t shown to you before like who added a given YouTube or Twitch account to the server.

For specifics on how these integrations work, check out the help articles for:

  • Twitch Integration FAQ
  • YouTube Channel Membership Integration FAQ

Bots and Apps

And now for something totally new! For the first time, the bots and apps that you’ve added to your server have their own home in Discord. You can see a list of everything that’s been added to your server, when it was added, and who added them.

You can also click into an individual bot or app and see the permissions it requested when it joined the server. Any webhooks that belong to the bot or app will also show up on this page, and can be managed just like other webhooks.

We want to continue to make bots and apps an awesome experience on Discord, because we know how important they are to all of you! We’re excited that they finally have a home in Discord, and you should continue to be excited for more things to come on this page!

Spotify Auto Pause

Oh no! Spotify keeps pausing while you’re listening, but why?!

If you are transmitting with your mic in voice chat for 30 seconds while Spotify is playing, Spotify will stop playing, and you’ll get this error bar at the top of your app:

This autopause error may also appear when using the following features with Spotify:

  • Voice Chat

  • Screenshare

  • Go Live

Because Spotify is intended for personal and private use, the auto pause function allows us to stay in compliance with Spotify’s Terms & Conditions outlined at spotify.com.

To avoid this try using Push-To-Talk or adjusting your voice activity sensitivity so that your mic is not activating while you listen. For more info on how to do that, check out this article!

Spotify FAQ

There are a few things to be aware of when using Discord’s Spotify Connection:

  • Enabling cross fading causes an abrupt stop during song change for listeners.
  • For mobile phones using listening along: the device cannot go to sleep + end a song, or the app will lose connection with Spotify, and the listen along session will end.
  • If clicking play/listen along doesn’t work, try selecting a device in your Spotify client or play a song on your Spotify client so Discord knows what Spotify device you’re listening on!
  • If you are playing a game that Discord detects, the game will take precedence and Spotify won’t show as your status!
  • If you are having odd delay issues, it’s probably due to system time being not in sync with the real time! This can be either on the listener’s end or the user that is being listened to!

TikTok LIVE Subscription’s Customized Perk: Discord Role FAQ

Note: Setting up a new Discord role connection for TikTok LIVE Subscriptions is no longer available. Existing account connections will continue remain active.

Calling all TikTok LIVE creators!

The Discord role is now available as one of TikTok LIVE Subscription’s customized perks. You can now add even more value to your LIVE Subscription by offering access to your Discord server or exclusive channel(s).

To get started, access the Discord role customized perk in the Creator Tools section of your profile in the TikTok app. Additional info can be found in the FAQ below.

What this article covers:

  • Frequently Asked Questions for TikTok LIVE Creators

Frequently Asked Questions for TikTok LIVE Creators

If you run into any issues while using the TikTok LIVE perk, please reach out to TikTok Support for further assistance.
Q: How do I set up my Discord role customized perk?

A. On the TikTok app, access your profile, then go to Creator Tools > Subscription > Customized Perks and toggle on the Discord role. Next, you’ll be prompted to enter your Discord login details to connect your Discord account.

If you don’t already have a Discord account click here to get started or click here to learn more about Discord for creators.

Once your Discord account is connected, select the Discord server you want subscribers to have access to, or create a new server, and then click Authorize. This connects your TikTok account to your Discord server.

Q: How do I create an exclusive Discord server, channel, or channels for my TikTok LIVE subscribers to access?

A. In order to create a private Discord server or channel(s) exclusively for your LIVE subscriber community, you must first create a new Discord role. This role grants subscribers access to any channel(s) designated to that role.

Follow the instructions here to create a new Discord role and channel. Once completed, follow the final step below.

Now that your Discord server has a TikTok LIVE role, select that role by navigating from your profile on the TikTok app to Creator Tools > Subscription > Customized Perks and clicking Discord settings under the Discord role customized perk.

Please note: After the TikTok setup is complete, you must navigate to the Discord server settings and ensure that the TikTok role is higher on the list than the roles you created for your subscribers. If it’s not listed higher, manually drag the role up to ensure the role permission is granted.
Q: What happens if someone unsubscribes from my LIVE Subscription?

A. You can choose what happens when someone unsubscribes by navigating to Creator Tools > Subscription > Customized Perks and then clicking Discord settings under the Discord role customized perk.

Next, under Expired Subscription behavior, you can choose to Remove the Discord Subscription role after 7 days or 24hrs; Kick from server after 7 days or 24hrs; or choose to take no action which allows the user to retain access to the Discord role and channel or server.

Twitch Integration FAQ

For Twitch Partner and Affiliate streamers, you can integrate your Twitch channel into your Discord server so you can chat and chill with all of your subscribers. Or if you’re a Twitch viewer, you can join and chat with your favorite streamers on their Discord servers.

What this article covers:

  • How to Connect your Twitch Channel to Discord
  • How to Integrate Twitch for Streamers
  • Twitch integration for Viewers
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How to Connect your Twitch Channel to Discord

  1. Open up the Discord app and next to your username access the cog wheel.

  2. Under your User Settings head to Connections.

  3. Connect your Twitch account to your Discord account by pressing on the Twitch icon tile and logging into your Twitch account.

How to Integrate Twitch for Streamers

You can either create a sub-only Discord server for your Twitch channel, or you can create a sub-only channel (or two) in your server. To get started, you first need to connect Twitch into your server following the How to Connect your Twitch Channel to Discord steps above.

After your Twitch is connected to your Discord, now you can integrate Twitch into your server.

  1. Navigate to your server and press on the server name to pull up a drop down menu. You can also right-click on the server name.

  2. Press on Server Settings and then head to Integrations.

  3. Follow the instructions on this page to integrate your Twitch into your Discord server!

NOTE: This is only available for Twitch Partners or Affiliates, if your Twitch channel does not currently have a subscription option you will not be able to integrate your Twitch into your Discord server.

After you’ve integrated your Twitch channel, you can edit your integration settings. Your subscribers list is synced automatically by the system, however, you can always run a manual Sync.

You can also change how long of a grace period a user has until they lose the subscriber role in your server or you can even kick a user if the subscriber role is lost. To do this, press on the Remove Role option and select Kick instead.

You’ll also find a new permissions role has been auto-created specifically for Twitch subs after integration. These roles will be named Twitch Subscriber, Twitch Subscriber: Tier 1, Twitch Subscriber: Tier 2, and Twitch Subscriber: Tier 3.

You can rename these roles, as well as adjust their permissions under Server Settings > Roles, and even change the colors of the role. Since this role is automatically managed by the Twitch integration, you can’t manually assign or delete members from it.

NOTE: If you have Rule Screening set up for your server for new users, they can by-pass this requirement and join a server if they are subscribed through Twitch.

Twitch integration for Viewers

If you’ve subscribed or been gifted a subscription to a Twitch streamer and you want to access their Discord server, the first thing you need to do is make sure your Twitch account is connected to your Discord account by following the steps outlined under How to Connect your Twitch Channel to Discord.

After you’ve connected your Twitch to your Discord account, you’ll see all available Twitch channels that you’re currently subscribed to. There will be the Join option next to any server you haven’t joined yet.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why don’t I see the option to integrate my Twitch channel into my Discord server?

A: You need to be either a Twitch Partner or Twitch Affiliate to integrate into a Discord server.

Q: What if I was either gifted a subscription or I joined the server, and I don’t see the server under connections to join or have the subscriber role in the server?

A: First, try removing your Twitch account under User Settings > Connections and then reconnecting your Twitch account. If you still do not see it, please ask the Twitch streamer or one of their moderators to run a manual sync by heading into Integrations in their Server Settings.

Q: What device can I connect my Twitch account to Discord on?

A: Desktop app, mobile, and browser.

If you have additional questions or have trouble integrating your Twitch channel, please reach out to our support team: dis.gd.

Invites

iOS How do I create an Invite link on my iOS device?

Push and hold the channel that you would like to create an invite for. After a couple of seconds a mini menu from the bottom will appear.

Tap “Invite” and don’t forget to set your advanced settings, if you’re fancy like that.

Custom Invite Link

If your server is at the highest server for Server Boosting, you can set a customizable server invite URL known as a Custom Invite Link. This URL can be used in place of an Instant Invite Link.

What this article covers:

  • What is a Custom Invite Link?
  • How to Set a Custom Invite Link
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Custom Invite Link?

A Custom Invite Link is a personalized invite link that replaces Discord’s default randomly-generated codes with a memorable, branded address like discord.gg/phibisparadise.

This feature allows server owners to create professional, easy-to-share invitations that reflect their brand or community name, making it simpler for users to find and join their server.

Available to servers that reached the Level 3 Server Boost, Custom Invite Link is a permanent invite link that’s yours to keep as long as your server maintains its Boost status.

Custom Invite Link being sent as a server invite

How to Set a Custom Invite Link

Tip: Before setting a Custom Invite Link, make sure you have a text channel with the View Channel permission enabled for the @everyone role. Otherwise the custom invite link will not work. Setting a Custom Invite Link makes your server public and anyone able to join with the link.

  1. Navigate to the server you want to set the Custom Invite Link to, select the server name at the top, and then press Server Settings.
Server Settings option
  1. Select Boost Perks and scroll down until you see Custom Invite Link.
Custom Invite Link section
  1. Enter the text that you want for your URL. Please keep in mind, you can use up to 25 characters, including letters, numbers, or dashes. Select Save Changes to save the URL.
Save Changes button after entering your Custom Invite URL
  1. Now you can use your custom invite link to invite anyone to your server!
Custom Invite Link being sent as a server invite

Important: Please keep in mind that a Custom Invite Link can be removed if we discover abuse or if there’s an intellectual property conflict.

For more information, please check out our Community Guidelines and Terms of Service.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What characters can be used in my Custom Invite Link?

A: Letters (lowercase only), numbers, and dashes can be used.

Q: Why do I keep receiving an error message when trying to set a Custom Invite Link?

A: If you receive an error message when trying to set your Custom Invite Link, please try setting it to something else as the URL may be taken or invalid.

Error when setting a Custom Invite Link

Q: Why is my Custom Invite Link showing as invalid?

A: If you later change a text channel to no longer be visible to @everyone, the Custom Invite Link will no longer work. You have to keep at least one text channel to be viewable to @evryone for the Custom Invite Link to work.

Invalid Invite error

Q: When I attempt to create a Custom Invite Link, I get an error saying the URL is already taken. Is there a way to verify URL availability beforehand?

A: Discord Support is not able to confirm if a Custom Invite Link is available or not. If you’re receiving an error message when trying to set a Custom Invite Link, you will need to try something else.

Q: How do I remove my server’s Custom Invite Link?

A: Head to Server Settings > Boosts Perks and scroll down to your Custom Invite Link. Press on Remove Custom Invite Link to remove the link.

Remove Custom Invite Link button

Q: My server ran out of Boosts, what will happen to my Custom Invite Link?

A: Unfortunately, if you no longer have the Server Boosts to maintain the Custom Invite Link then you will lose your Custom Invite Link after 30 days.

How do I invite friends to my server?

Whether your friends are seasoned Discordians, or have never touched the app, inviting them to your server is a piece of cake!

Click the Instant Invite Icon

Open your server and click the Instant Invite icon next to the channel name.

A box will appear with an invite link and direct invite buttons for the friends or group DMs that you’ve communicated with most recently!

Simply press a nifty button or copy, paste, and send that new invite link to any and all of your unsuspecting subjects (er, friends) and begin operation world domination!

Note:
- Each channel in your server has it’s own Instant Invite link, and which ever channel you pull the link from is where the user will land on your server each time they try to access it.
- For example, if you send Glados an invite link from your #rules channel, then every time she accesses your server the #rules chat channel will be the first channel she sees.

Right-Click Profile and Invite

However, if you’re frustrated and tired from figuring out which Portal to take, you can always send your friends an invite by right-clicking on their icon from anywhere in Discord then selecting Invite to Server.

As long as you have the Create Instant Invite permission for your role on a server, you’ll be able to see the server in the drop-down menu that appears.

Once you select the server, a DM will be sent to your friend with the invite!

Copy and Paste the Invite link

Lastly, if your friend has never used Discord before then you can send them the invite link anywhere you can paste text. Upon clicking (or, copy/pasting) it, they’ll be prompted with a quick rundown on Discord including an opportunity to set up an account.

Invalid Invite Links

Let me innnnnnn! You finally got an invite to a server, but you’re getting hit with an error message and can’t join. What does it mean? Why can’t you join? Let’s go over the possible error messages that you might see, what they mean, and what you can do if you’re seeing them.

Invalid Error Messages

Unknown/Expired Invite: Your invite link may have expired. In this case, please ask for a new invite link.

Invalid: You may not have a legitimate invite code. Please check the code again or ask for a new invite link. Remember too, codes are case sensitive.

100 Server Limit: A user cannot be a member of more than 100 servers. If you are in too many servers, you’ll need to leave one before you can join.

If you have Discord Nitro you can join up to 200 servers! If you join over 100 servers while your Nitro is active, and then your Nitro expires, you’ll have to leave enough servers until you’re below 100 to join more.

Banned: You may have been banned from joining this server. Server bans are based on IP addresses, so you would need to contact the server admins and ask them to revoke all bans in their Server Settings.

If you are still unable to join a server, please reach out to our Support team for further assistance: dis.gd

Invites 101

Instant Invites allow you to invite anyone to your server, at any time! You can set a temporary invite link that only lasts 30 minutes, or one that doesn’t expire at all, if you are in a Community Server. Want to set a Custom Invite Link? Please check out this article.

What this article covers:

  • How to Create an Instant Invite
  • How to Edit Invite Settings
  • How to Remove Instant Invite Links as an Admin

How to Create an Instant Invite

If you hover over the right-hand side of a channel you should see an option that says Create Invite if you have the permissions.

After tapping on Create Invite you can send invites to anyone you’ve recently chatted with through Direct Messages or copy the invite link.

The invite panel will appear displaying a 7 days access link by default if you haven’t already adjusted the invite settings for that channel yet. Otherwise, the invite that displays will be dictated by your previous settings for that specific channel.

By clicking on Edit Invite Link, you’ll have the ability to change the duration of the link as well as how many times it can be accessed.

How to Edit Invite Settings

Once you’re in the Create Invite panel you can edit the invite settings by tapping on Edit invite link.

Here you can change how long the invite link will be valid for and how many times this invite link can be used for.

After editing the settings you can simply copy the invite link and directly send it to your friends or by tapping on the Invite button next to their name.

Enabling Grant temporary membership means that members who join through the invite link are automatically kicked when they disconnect unless a role is assigned.

If you want the invite link to have infinite uses, you can set Max number of uses to No limit. It’s important to remember that the only way anyone can access your server is through an invite link so be careful with who you give it to!

Once you’ve adjusted the settings to your needs, tap on Generate a New Link and your new invite link will appear.

How to Remove Instant Invite Links as an Admin

Once an invite has been deleted, it can not be remade with that same invite code. Support is also not able to create this invite link again.

If you have permissions in the server you can remove invite links at any time. Just head to Server Settings > Invites.

You can Pause Invites at any time or remove any generated invite by tapping on the x next to each invite.

Pause Invites FAQ

Chances are you’ve set up invite links to help people easily find and join your Community. But what if you wanted to pause the usage of your invite links, embeds, and vanity URLs without revoking them?

Now you can with Pause Invites!

What does this article cover?

  • How to pause invites
  • When should I pause invites to my server?
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How to pause invites

  1. Those with Manage Server permissions can head over to Server Settings > Invites

  2. Press the Pause Invites button.

Now that your invite links are paused, users will no longer be able to join your Community until you re-enable invites. Rest assured your existing invite links, embeds, and vanity URLs will still be visible.

  1. While your invites are paused, users who press on an invite link will be notified that invites are paused for your Community and will be unable to join:

  2. To re-enable invites so that users can join your Community again, navigate back to Server Settings > Invites and press Enable Invites. Users who now press on your invite link will be able to successfully join your Community.

Why should I pause invites to my server?

  • Your Community is being raided, which is when a large number of users or accounts join your Community with the express intention of causing disruption and issues. New accounts (good and bad users alike) may be joining via any of your existing invite links. You can pause invites to prevent new accounts from joining and focus on de-escalating.
  • Pause invitations indefinitely so you don’t have to revoke your existing invite links and/or vanity URL just to set up new ones later.
  • Let users trying to join your Community know your Community is in a paused state instead of confusing them with invalid or expired invite links.
  • Manage the growth of your Community - sometimes you just want to go into maintenance mode to freshen up your Community for new members without revoking your existing invite links.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Who can pause invites in my Community?

A: Only those with Manage Server permissions can pause invites.

Q: Which devices can I pause invites on?

A: You can currently pause invites on desktop devices. We are working on mobile support.

Q: Will users who tried to join my Community while invitations were paused be notified when I re-enable my invite links?

A: No, users are not notified when your invite links are re-enabled.

Q: How will pausing invites affect people trying to join through Server Discovery?

A: Pausing invites also prevents people from joining through Server Discovery.

Q: Will my links change or look different to users when I pause them?

A: No, pausing invites does not change your links or vanity URL.

Q: Can I set up AutoMod to automatically pause invites?

A: At this time, AutoMod cannot be configured to pause invites.

[Known Issue] Audio Quality Drops When Joining A Call

Listening to something on your Bluetooth headset and noticing a drop in quality when joining a Discord call? The headphones are probably switching to the Bluetooth “headset” profile. This is required for low latency and microphone functionality on most Bluetooth headphones, but it provides a lower quality audio experience.

This is a known limitation of the Bluetooth standard that affects all apps with voice call support. The new Bluetooth 5.3 Low Energy (LE Audio) standard–supported by select phones and headsets–introduces new functionality to help resolve it. Both the headset and the phone need to support LE Audio. Consult your phone and headset specifications to see if LE Audio is supported.

Support for LE Audio is coming soon to Discord, so stay tuned.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I know if my headset and phone support the Bluetooth 5.3 Low Energy?

A: Consult your headset and phone specifications to see if Bluetooth 5.3 Low Energy is supported. Both will need Bluetooth 5.3 Low Energy support to preserve audio quality while on calls.

[Known Issue] Desktop Client Crashing When Starting a Game on AMD Graphics Cards

On May 10, 2026, we identified an issue causing the Discord desktop client to crash, close, or refresh on its own when users start a game. The cause is a regression in AMD’s 26.5.1 graphics driver release. We are working with AMD, who is actively investigating.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Who is affected by this issue?

A: Windows users running AMD graphics driver version 26.5.1 (also identified as 32.0.31007.1017) are affected.

Q: When will this issue be fixed?

A: We do not have an ETA at this time. This article will be updated with any relevant information we receive from our partners at AMD.

Q: What can I do in the meantime?

A: A clean driver reinstall may resolve the issue. For instructions, refer to AMD’s official driver installation guidance. AMD publishes driver updates through AMD Software: Adrenaline Edition, and a fixed release may be available there in the future.

[Known Issue] Expanding Server List with Screen Readers

As of May 28th, 2020, it has come to our attention that Screen Readers on Discord are no longer able to expand the Server List with the “Enter” key.

Unfortunately, this has caused issues for accessing servers further up or down on the list (with the function currently only interacting with the link for the server).

Due to an update made by NVDA (introduced in NVDA 2020.1) which affected our tree view for the Server List, this particular behavior of the special function tied to the “Enter” key was removed.

This means the “Enter” key no longer functions as a switch into “Focus Mode” when looking at a tree view.

The key has now defaulted to the common key bind for interacting with the tree list: “insert+spacebar”.

If you are curious about NVDA or their changes, you can learn more about the open source screen reader technology here: nvaccess.org

We hope this helps but if you’re still running into issues accessing the Server List while using a screen reader, please reach out to our support team at dis.gd/contact.

[Known Issue] Game Overlay

We have paid attention to user feedback regarding the reliability of Discord’s Game Overlay, which has been known to occasionally cause problems during gameplay. Moreover, it is only supported in a limited number of games due to compatibility challenges inherent to the current implementation.

As a result, on April 15, 2024, Discord started to roll-out a revamped Game Overlay designed to significantly enhance stability, reliability, and performance. The new Game Overlay will not interfere with your game, and is expected to be compatible with nearly all games. This is currently out to 100% of users on the Canary and PTB versions of the Discord app. There is no ETA at this time as to when this will be fully rolled out to all users on the Stable version of Discord.

After this date, you will experience the following changes in Game Overlay behavior:

  • Game Overlay is now enabled by default for all games.
  • Game Overlay will work in windowed fullscreen mode and windowed borderless fullscreen mode, but will not work in true fullscreen mode.
    • True fullscreen mode on desktop means that other computer applications cannot be displayed over the application that’s in true fullscreen mode.
  • Game Overlay will be hidden when the game window is not in focus.
  • Screensharing the game window will not capture the Game Overlay, but screensharing the full screen will still capture the Game Overlay.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What do I do if I always run my game in true fullscreen mode?

A: Most games support borderless fullscreen mode, so you can switch to this mode to continue getting Discord’s Game Overlay in game.

If you need to run the game in true fullscreen mode for any reason, there’s also a global Enable legacy overlay option in User Settings > Game Overlay. Please note that this option may be removed in the future.

Q: Can I keep using the legacy Game Overlay?

A: You can continue using it as long as the option exists in the app, but our goal is to eventually move everyone over to the revamped Game Overlay so they can enjoy a more stable and performant experience.

Q: What if the game I play only works with the legacy Game Overlay?

A: Please first check that you are running borderless fullscreen mode, or sometimes called “windowed” fullscreen mode. The revamped Game Overlay should work in this mode.

If you still experience issues with it, please reach out to our Support team for further assistance.

[Known Issue] Screenshare with Audio Not Capturing Chrome

As of August 12th, 2019, our engineering team isolated an issue that’s causing audio capture from Google Chrome during screenshare to fail for some users.

This was due to some changes in Chrome’s audio infrastructure, and our team is working quickly to accommodate Google’s updates to make sure screenshare works as expected! Our team has released a handful of initial patches to address this issue and will continue to work on the screenshare code over the next few patch releases, so please make sure to update to the latest version of Discord as a first step if you’re still having trouble!

As a next step, if you’re still having issues capturing audio from Google Chrome as of our latest update, make sure to try the following workaround!:

  1. End your screenshare session and refresh the app with Ctrl + R

  2. Close Google Chrome then reopen it. Once Chrome is reopened, begin playing audio in the browser before launching a screenshare session.

  3. Enable screenshare and try once more!

If you’re still having trouble after giving this a shot, our support team is collecting data so we can get this fixed for everyone as soon as possible, so please don’t hesitate to reach out to the team directly here!

Note: If you want to learn more about screenshare and audio capture, check out our article here!

[Known Issue] Small Videos Won’t Play in the Desktop App

Some videos with very small dimensions won’t play directly in the Discord desktop app, even though the file itself is valid and plays normally elsewhere. Here’s why this happens, and how to watch the video in the meantime.

What this article covers:

  • Why This Happens
  • What You Can Do
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Why This Happens

The Discord desktop app uses hardware-only video decoding to play videos efficiently. Due to varying hardware decoder compatibility requirements, playing back videos less than 64 pixels on any edge is not supported.

When a video falls below that threshold, playback can’t start on desktop, even though the file itself isn’t damaged or corrupted.

What You Can Do

If a video won’t play in the desktop app, you can still watch it using your device’s default media player:

  • Download the video file from Discord.
  • Open the downloaded file with your device’s default media player (ie. QuickTime Player, Windows Media Player, or VLC).
  • The video should play outside of Discord.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why won’t my video play directly in Discord?

A: Due to varying hardware decoder compatibility requirements, videos less than 64 pixels on any edge aren’t supported for playback. This isn’t an issue with your file - it’s a limitation of the hardware decoder.

Q: Is my video file corrupted?

A: No. The file is valid and plays normally in other media players. This limitation only affects direct playback within the Discord desktop app.

[Known Issue] Support for 32-bit Windows Operating Systems

As of June 15, 2024, Discord will no longer be supported on 32-bit Windows operating systems.

To continue receiving updates and support for your Discord client, you must upgrade to a 64-bit OS version of Windows after this date.

If you are unsure if you are running a 32-bit OS version of Windows, you can check by following these steps:

  1. Open your Start Menu, and search for “about”. 2. Select About your PC to open your System Settings window.

  2. While in System Settings, refer to System Type which will list either a 32-bit operating system or the 64-bit operating system.

To upgrade your Windows from 32-bit OS to 64-bit OS, you can check out the Microsoft FAQ here.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Will the Discord client I currently have installed continue to work after June 15, 2024?

A: Basic functionality may continue to work, however functionality and stability is not guaranteed as the client will no longer receive updates.

Q: If I cannot upgrade my computer right now, can I use the browser version of Discord?

A: Yes, as long as your browser meets the minimum requirements found here, you can continue to use it.

Known Issues New Chat Text Box

With the release of our new and improved Chat Text Box comes the coding critters of the dark—bugs! 🐛

Here is a long and detailed article to satisfy and answer your curiosities of what is currently happening with this really cool box.

Bugs to Squash To-Do List:

Here is the list of known bugs that we will be working on removing in the coming updates:

  • Pasting in a lot of emojis/mentions all at once can be slow
  • Emoticons do not auto-convert to emojis
  • Clicking on a mention does nothing
  • User discriminators are shown in the mention tooltip in streamer mode
  • Manually typing out an emoji, emoticon, or mention will not convert it to the “rich format”
  • Starting a message with /, @, or s/, and then using auto-complete will insert a mention as <@userid> instead of @username#id
  • Discord ignores backslashes when parsing ``` when calculating whether the cursor is currently in a code block or not
  • The tooltip for the character counter, the text for the upload modal, and the text for the setting to disable the new chat box are not translated
  • Leading whitespace is often ignored for markdown syntax highlighting. For example “|| text||” will not put a background color on the first 5 spaces there
  • Clicking away from the editor and back into it on Firefox will move the cursor to the beginning of the text box
Not Bugs:

In the meantime, here is a list of behaviors that may seem like a bug, but are not bugs. They are unlikely to be fixed and are working as intended:

  • and >>> behave the same way

  • Links are not clickable
  • Links won’t show URL encoding or other modifications that appear after sending the message
  • Typing slash commands like “/spoiler” or “/me” does not show a preview of the styled text
  • The backticks show inside of the background color for inline code blocks
  • The character counter may slightly miscalculate the length of the message. For example, if you type “/spoiler foo”, it would count that as 12 characters, but when sent is only 5
  • Hitting backspace after a mention deletes the entire mention
  • Creating an empty code block by putting a space between the two sets of ``` symbols

Bugs That Will Live:

Lastly, here is a list of identified bugs that are considered relatively harmless and will remain in coexistence with the app:

  • The rich chat box is turned off on the Android browser and in certain old browsers (such as Edge <= 18)
  • Multi-line bold/italics/underline/etc does not get styled
  • In compact mode, RTL messages have a line break between the author’s name and the message content
  • You cannot use triple-click to select an entire line of text when that line contains an emoji or mention
  • Inserting an emoji and then wrapping that emoji in an inline code block or multi-line code block will not down-convert it to plain text
  • Typing two regional indicator emojis will not combine them into the corresponding flag emoji
  • If you hold shift-enter to make the text box scroll, the editor will not be scrolled entirely to the bottom (but the last line of text is still visible)
  • Syntax highlighting in code blocks is turned off on the last line if the closing backticks do not end on their own line
  • If you mention yourself it won’t highlight the message with a yellow background

I Found More Bugs!

If a bug needs to be escalated to the Wizards for bad behavior, it would be extremely helpful to include the following, since often these bugs only reproduce on very specific setups:

  • Browser and browser version

  • Operating system

  • Discord release channel

  • Discord build number

  • Keyboard layout (meaning US/French/Chinese/etc)

  • The language they are trying to type in

  • What you are trying to type If you are unable to type something in a non-English language due to a bug, please follow the instructions below:

  • Go to: danburzo.github.io

  • Clear out the “Simple DOM contenteditable” section

  • Click “Clear Log”

  • Start a “Screen recording”

  • Type in exactly what they would type in to Discord that causes Discord to break

  • Stop recording and send it to us, along with an explanation of what is different between the behavior on that website vs Discord This tool records everything you are typing, so it both demonstrates how to reproduce the problem and what is supposed to happen, and your explanation at the end should confirm how Discord is broken.

How Do I Turn this off?

There is an option to turn off the new chat box! It will only show if users have access to the new chat box though, which currently means only Canary & PTB users on the latest release will see it.

We are using this as a temporary option though, so that users who are stuck can turn it off, but our hope is to fix any major blockers so we can remove this option in the future.

Please send all reports of new issues with the new Text Chat Box to dis.gd/contact and we’ll do our best to help out.

Happy bug hunting!

We were investigating reports that users were being asked to perform age verification again and that some verifications were not completing successfully.

If the full restart does not work, please contact our team following the steps in this article: How to Submit a Support Ticket to Discord

[SOLVED] Audio Issues when Screensharing on Android

From approximately April 7, 2026 to June 22, 2026, a bug existed in Android System WebView which could break the audio capture pipeline. This bug was triggered by in-app advertisements and would cause streams to suddenly go silent, and could only be temporarily resolved by rebooting the Android device.

Our partners at Google worked to roll out a fix for this in Android System WebView version 149, which became widely available on June 22, 2026. In the meantime, we advised users to uninstall updates to Android System WebView. Now that a fix is generally available, we recommend that any affected users update Android System WebView via the Play Store.
