About Discord Link Previews and the Discordbot

When you share a link in Discord, you’ll often see a small preview card show up with a title, image, or description. This is built using a bot called Discordbot. This article explains how that works, and how website owners can recognize and confirm its traffic.

What this article covers:

  • How Discord Generates Link Previews
  • The Discordbot
    • Identifying Discordbot
    • Verifying Discord Traffic

How Discord Generates Link Previews

When someone shares a link in a Discord message, it automatically visits that link to grab information about the page, like its title, description, and image. This information is used to build the preview card you see in chat.

This only happens when a link is actually shared in a message. There’s no continuous scanning or crawling of websites on its own.

If the link points to an image or video, a copy may also be saved for a while so it loads faster next time. When someone views that image or video, it’s delivered through Discord’s own servers rather than pulled directly from the original website. This keeps the viewer’s information, like their IP address, private from the site hosting the file.

The Discordbot

Discordbot is the tool that visits links and builds these previews. If you own a website, you might want to know when it’s visiting your site, maybe to show slightly different information, or to make sure your firewall doesn’t accidentally block it.

There are two ways to recognize its requests:

  • Look at the User-Agent (a short bit of text that identifies what’s making the request)
  • Check the IP address the request is coming from
Identifying Discordbot

Every request it makes includes a User-Agent that looks like this:

Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Discordbot/2.0; +[discordapp.com](https://discordapp.com))

You can check for the word “Discordbot” anywhere in that text. Other parts of it might change over time, so don’t rely on matching the whole string exactly.

Important: Just checking the User-Agent isn’t enough to be sure a request really came from Discord, since anyone can fake one. If you’re using this to decide whether to let a request through your firewall, also check the IP address (see below).

Verifying Discord Traffic

To be sure a request truly came from Discord, check that its IP address is on the official list of public IP ranges. This is published in two formats (json and txt) so you can check it programmatically. It’s a good idea to recheck this list every so often, since the ranges can change.

Custom Stickers FAQ

Excited to upload your own custom stickers for your server? Here’s how to upload and manage custom stickers for your server!

What this article covers:

  • Server Boosts and Stickers
  • How to Give or Remove Expression Permissions
  • Uploading Custom Stickers
  • How should I name my stickers?
    • Why do I need to select a relatable Unicode Emoji?
    • Optional: Entering a Description (Alt-text)
    • Tips for Writing Descriptions
  • Editing and Deleting Uploaded Custom Stickers
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Server Boosts and Stickers

As a default, all servers have 5 custom stickers slots for free. Your server can upload more custom stickers once the server has reached Boosting Levels 1, 2, or 3! Depending on what Boost level your server has reached will determine how many custom stickers you can upload.

  • Default: 5 custom sticker slots
  • Level 1: +10 custom sticker slots
  • Level 2: +15 custom sticker slots (30 total)
  • Level 3: +30 custom sticker slots (60 total)

How to Give or Remove Expression Permissions

As a server owner, you can manage which members are able to add, remove, or edit Stickers within the server by enabling or disabling expression permissions.

If you would like to allow a role to add custom stickers, you can enable the Create Expressions permission.

If you want certain server admin and members to have the ability to edit and remove custom stickers, they will need to have the Manage Expressions permission enabled.

  1. To manage expression permissions, head into your Server Settings by selecting the pull-down menu next to the server name.

  2. Once in Server Settings, press the Roles tab and choose the role you would like to manage.

  3. While in the Edit Role page, navigate to Permissions.

  4. You will now be able to toggle the Create Expressions and Manage Expressions permissions under General Server Permissions.

Note: Managing custom stickers are only available on desktop. If you’re on iOS or Android, you’ll need to use the desktop or web apps to upload, edit, and delete custom stickers

Uploading Custom Stickers

If you’re the server owner or have Create Expressions permission enabled, you can head over to the server and add the available amount of custom stickers for that server.

  1. To get started, head into the Server Settings and select the Stickers tab.

  2. Once redirected to the Sticker page, press the Upload Sticker button.

  3. Then, select a file from your desktop. You’ll be required to enter a sticker name and choose a related emoji. We recommend giving your sticker a brief description so that folks who use screen readers can understand the content of the image when it’s used in a conversation.

  4. Once those steps are completed, you should be all set!

For custom sticker requirements and tips, check out this article: Tips for Sticker Creators

How should I name my stickers?

While we don’t enforce a specific naming convention for custom stickers, here are some things to consider when thinking about a name:

  • The sticker name should be easy to remember so members of your server can search for it when they want to use it.
  • If your sticker has text in its image, naming the sticker after the text
  • Naming the sticker after the emotion it displays, or the character and the emotion. Example names for this sticker: Mad, Anger, Rage_Dog
Why do I need to select a related Unicode Emoji?

Adding a related unicode emoji to a custom sticker allows the sticker to show up in our sticker suggestion fields, which means users who can use your custom stickers will be able to find them easier when looking for stickers to send. This includes:

  • Sticker suggestions that appear on desktop and mobile.
  • When typing the related Unicode emoji into chat using :name:
  • Searching for a sticker in your sticker drawer.
Optional: Entering a description (Alt-text)

We strongly recommend adding a short, concise description (alt-text) for each custom sticker. This will allow people who use screen readers to know what your sticker looks like without needing to see the actual sticker.

Good descriptions are short and descriptive of what a sticker looks like, plus describing the emotion the sticker is conveying.

Good Example Description: A pink flower character smiles peacefully as it steps across the screen.

Poor Example Description: Animated flower steps out of a blue circle with green sky and clouds.

Tips for writing descriptions
  • Make sure to use proper spelling, capitalization, spacing, and grammar.
  • Describe the image as you see it, and choose to write about the most important features of the image. Ideas on what to describe:
    • Placement of objects within the image
    • Subject (animal, human, etc)
    • Emotions, like smiling or
    • Colors
    • Clothing detail
    • Text (if there’s some in the image)
  • What not to write:
    • Obvious details (like “human has two eyes and a nose”)
    • Focusing on details not central to what’s happening in the image
    • Using creative writing techniques
    • Do not use emojis

Editing and Deleting Uploaded Custom Stickers

  • Editing: Click on the pencil icon that appears when you hover your mouse over a sticker.
  • Deleting: Click on the red ‘X’ icon that appears when you hover your mouse over a sticker to delete the sticker.
Note: You cannot edit the sticker file once it has been uploaded. If you want to replace the sticker file, you’ll need to delete this sticker and upload a new file!

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Who can use custom stickers that have been uploaded in my server?

A: Anyone who has joined your server can use custom stickers within your server. Users who have a Nitro subscription will be able to use the custom stickers anywhere on Discord (other servers, direct messages, etc).

Q: How can I prevent people from sending stickers in my server?

A: There’s no permission to completely disable sending stickers in a server. If you want to prevent your server members from sending custom stickers from other servers, you’ll need to disable the “Use External Emoji and Stickers” permission for the @everyone role in your server.

Q: What kind of content can I use for my stickers?

A: As is true for all content that you use on Discord, you are responsible for ensuring that any content you use for custom stickers complies with our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.

Q: Once a sticker is deleted, can it be brought back?

A: No it cannot. There’s no way to undo this action, so once a custom sticker is deleted it’s gone for good!

Q: Can I upload multiple stickers at a time?

A: You won’t be able to upload multiple stickers at once right now. If you’d like to see this in the future though, head to our feedback site and vote up the idea: dis.gd

Q: What happens to the previously uploaded custom stickers if the server loses a Boost level?

A: Don’t worry, your custom stickers are safe! If your server loses a Boost level, then you won’t be able to use the custom stickers in that level until the Boost level is reached again. You’ll also be able to see exactly which custom stickers can’t be used after losing a Boost level under Server Settings > Stickers.

Q: Can we delete stickers that are locked behind a recently lost Boost level?

A: Yes, you can still delete stickers in the locked level if you need to by following the same deletion steps listed above!

File Type Questions

Q: What’s the difference between APNG and a PNG file?

A: PNG files are a static, image file format that compresses images in a specific way to prevent quality loss. An APNG file is the animated version of this file format!

Q: Why can’t we use other file types for custom stickers?

A: We wanted to make sure your sticker creations looked just as beautiful in the app as when you’re creating them, so we chose file types that will help support that!

Custom Typing Indicator FAQ

Customize the “is typing…” message that appears when you’re the only one typing, with your own emoji and status word.

What this article covers:

  • Custom Typing Indicator: What Is It?
  • How to Customize Your Typing Indicator
  • Nitro vs. Non-Nitro Access
  • Frequently Asked Questions Important: This feature is rolling out to Nitro subscribers on mobile. Most eligible subscribers will have access soon, with the rest gaining access in the following weeks.

Custom Typing Indicator: What Is It?

“Is typing…” is the default message you see when someone’s composing a message. With Custom Typing Indicator, you can replace that default message with your own 3 emojis and status word whenever you’re the only person typing.

Note: If more than one person is typing at the same time, everyone’s indicator returns to the default “is typing…” message.

Currently available on mobile only, this appears anywhere you can chat on Discord, including direct messages, text channels, forum channels, and voice channel chats.

There are three parts you can customize:

  • Emoji: Select 3 unique emoji that you already have access to.
  • Animation: Choose an animation style: Pulse, Ring, or Wave, or select None to turn animation off.
  • Status: Pick a status word from a preset list to replace “typing,” like “is yapping…” or “is daydreaming…”
Example of a Customized Typing Indicator

How to Customize Your Typing Indicator

Note: This feature is currently mobile only.

  1. Tap the You Bar and select Settings.

  2. Scroll to App Settings and tap Typing Indicator.

Navigating from Settings to Typing Indicator

  1. Select an emoji slot to open the emoji picker. Selecting your first emoji fills all 3 emoji slots at once, so you always start with a complete set. You can then select each slot again to swap in different emoji.

  2. Select Animation to open the motion sheet and choose a style (screen name and options not yet locked).

  3. Select Text to open the status word list and choose from our options of preset status words to replace “typing”.

  4. Once you’ve made a change, select Apply to save your customized typing indicator.

Customizing Your Typing Indicator in Settings

Note: Some long usernames or status words display as much as they can on a single line, then get cut off with an ellipsis depending on your screen size. For example: “mallowmallowmallowmallow is bab…”

Tip: Can’t decide on a combo? Select Surprise Me and let Discord mix up your emoji, animation, and status word for you. It’s a great way to discover a combo you wouldn’t have picked yourself! Not feeling the result? Tap Reset to clear your selections and start over.

Customizing Your Typing Indicator Using Surprise Me and Reset

Note: If a server has the Use External Emoji permission turned off, other members in that server will see the default “…” in place of your custom emoji, but they’ll still see your custom status word (for example, “is yapping…”).

Tip: Tapping on someone else’s Custom Typing Indicator opens the same bottom sheet you’d use to set up your own. It can be used as a quick shortcut to jump straight into customizing yours by tapping Check it Out.

This only works if you’re able to edit your typing indicator; some users can only view others’ custom indicators at this time.

In-app Sheet for Custom Typing Indicator

Nitro vs. Non-Nitro Access

  • Nitro members: Can fully customize and save their typing indicator, including emoji, animation, and status word. This feature is not available for Nitro Basic.
  • Non-Nitro members: Can preview the customization options but need a Nitro subscription to save and use them.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What does Custom Typing Indicator do?

A: It lets you replace the default “is typing…” message with up to 3 custom emoji, a motion style, and an alternative verb, whenever you’re the only person typing in a conversation.

Q: Can I turn off the custom typing indicator?

A: There isn’t a way to disable the custom typing indicator. If you’d like to reduce the intensity of its animation, you can turn on Reduced Motion in User Settings > Accessibility, which minimizes motion effects across Discord.

Q: What happens if more than one person is typing at the same time?

A: Everyone’s typing indicator returns to the default “is typing…” message until only one person is typing again.

Q: Do I need Nitro to use this feature?

A: You need a Nitro subscription to save and use a custom typing indicator. This feature is not available for Nitro Basic. Non-Nitro members can preview the customization options, but can’t save or apply them.

Q: Where can I set up my custom typing indicator?

A: Tap the You Bar, select Settings, then scroll to App Settings and tap Typing Indicator.

Q: Will everyone see my custom typing indicator the same way?

A: Not always. If a server has the Use External Emoji permission turned off, other members in that server will see the default “…” in place of your custom emoji, but they’ll still see your custom status word.

Q: Where does my custom typing indicator show up?

A: It shows up for others anytime you are typing on Discord, including direct messages, text channels, forum channels, and voice channel chats. It only appears if you are the only person typing.

Q: Is this feature available to everyone?

A: It’s rolling out now to Nitro subscribers on mobile. If you don’t see it yet, you should gain access within the next few weeks.

Q: Can I choose any word for my status?

A: You’ll choose from a preset list of status words rather than writing your own. The current options are: is yapping…, is venting…, is oversharing…, is barking…, is babbling…, is daydreaming…, and is meowing….

Q: Is there a quick way to try different combinations?

A: Yes. Select Surprise Me to get a random combination of emoji, animation, and status word.

Q: Can I set a different typing indicator for each server?

A: No. Your custom typing indicator applies everywhere you chat on Discord and can’t be set on a per-server basis.

Q: What happens if I tap on someone else’s custom typing indicator?

A: If you’re able to edit your own typing indicator, tapping on someone else’s opens the same bottom sheet used to customize yours, so you can quickly set one up for yourself. If you can’t edit your typing indicator, tapping won’t open this shortcut.

File Attachments FAQ

What this article covers:

  • What is a File Attachment?
  • How to Attach Files
  • File Upload Settings
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • What is NSFW Content Scanning?
  • How to Use Alt Text
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What is a File Attachment?

Important: We’re currently experimenting with various file upload size limits. Select users may have the ability to upload larger file sizes.

In addition to text messages, users can upload file attachments in Discord to send to others. If you have Nitro, you can upload even bigger files. For non-Nitro subscribers, the maximum file upload is 20MB.

There is a wide variety of file types that can be uploaded to Discord. Here are the most common examples:

  • JPEG
  • PDF
  • MP3
  • MOV
  • MP4 (Video encoded with H264, HEVC/H265, or AV1)

How to Attach Files

Tip: If you upload multiple video files, images, or GIFs in one message, they will be sent together and displayed as a mosaic format.

  1. Tap on the plus sign [] located in the text field of the text channel, text chat of a voice channel, or group message that you want to send a file attachment in and then tap on Upload a File.
Example of sending a file attachment with text

  1. Select the file(s) that you want to attach from your device. You can also write a message to send along with it.

  2. Your file(s) and any text that you included will be sent together in one message.

Attachment sent along with text

If you attach non-image files, such as a PDF, DOC, etc. the files will display as embeds in your message and will not provide a preview of the attached file.

Example of sending a non-image file

Tip: If you want to include Spoiler Tags before sending a file to someone, you can learn how to do that in this Help Center article.

File Upload Settings

There are some settings you can enable to prevent or even minimize the attachments you’ll see in Discord.

Desktop/Browser

  1. Tap on the cogwheel [] in the bottom-left corner of the app.

  2. Navigate to the Chat tab.

Chat tab in User Settings on desktop/browser
  1. The setting is enabled if there’s a checkmark or a setting is disabled if there’s an x.

Here is how each setting works:

  • When posted as links to chat: When an image is posted as a link, the image will be displayed instead of the text link.
  • When uploaded directly to Discord: Any image that is larger than 20MB will be shared as a download instead.
  • With image descriptions: Used for screen readers to describe any shared image.
  • Show embeds and preview website links pasted into the chat: Embeds and website links will display a preview, unless disabled.
Chat setting options on desktop/browser
Mobile

  1. Tap on your profile image in the bottom-right corner.

  2. Press on the cogwheel [] in the top-right corner.

  3. Navigate to the Chat tab.

Chat tab in Settings on mobile

  1. On this page, you can enable or disable any setting. If enabled, you’ll see a checkmark. If disabled, you’ll see an x.

  2. Many desktop/browser settings are also available on mobile, but here are the mobile-only settings:

  • Save to Device: If you directly send an image or video through your mobile device, the file will be automatically saved to your phone.
  • Video Uploads: In this section, you can manage the quality of videos you upload through Discord. By selecting the “Data Saver” option, your videos will upload more quickly and consume less data.
  • Data Saving Mode: If enabled, images and videos will be sent in lower quality through your cellular network to use less data.
Chat settings for mobile

What is NSFW Content Scanning?

“NSFW” or Not Safe For Work (or not suitable for work) is a term to describe inappropriate content that you would not want to look at while in the workplace and is now more widely used to describe content that could be seen as inappropriate for the public.

To help keep users safe, we have both User Settings and Server Settings to scan images for NSFW content. If these settings are enabled and the system detects the image could be NSFW, it will block the upload.

Want to learn more? You can learn more about these settings in our Safer Messaging on Discord Help Center article.

Clyde warning for a blocked message

How to Use Alt Text

ALT text - short for alternative text - is a feature that allows users to write an image description to uploads so that anyone using a screen reader can obtain a description of the image without needing to see the actual image itself.

  1. Once you attach the image(s) you want to upload, tap on the Modify attachment option or the pencil icon [] that appears after hovering your cursor over each file.
Modify Attachment option
  1. You can change the name of the file and add in the ALT text to describe the image. Press on Save when you’re finished.
Example of applying Alt Text

  1. You can now send your image(s) with the alt text you’ve written.

  2. If you have the With image descriptions setting enabled and if an image has ALT text, you should see the word ALT on the image. Select ALT and you will then see the ALT text for the image.

Example of what ALT text looks like when applied to an attachment

If an image has ALT text, you’ll be able to see it when you have With image descriptions enabled in your Text & Images settings. If you need a visual aid, pressing ALT this will show the text.

Contact Us: If you run into any issues with uploading images and files, or using ALT text, please reach out to Discord Support through this link here: dis.gd/contact

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why did Discord’s file upload limit change?

A :We regularly revisit our file limits to reflect how people actually use Discord and to support ongoing improvements to file sharing across platforms. As of August 2026, the free upload limit is 20MB (up from 10MB), and we’ve aligned how that limit is checked on desktop and mobile so it’s consistent and predictable.

One thing worth knowing: because we now check file size before compression rather than after, the real-world effect varies by platform. Desktop and iOS users should generally find uploads easier than before. On Android, where source files tend to be larger, you may hit the size limit more often than you did previously, even though the stated number is higher.

If you need more room regularly, Nitro Basic offers 50MB and Nitro offers up to 1GB.

Q: Does Discord check my file size pre- or post-compression?

A: Every day, millions of files are uploaded to Discord, and we’re always working to make that process faster and more predictable. Previously on mobile, we’d try to compress your file first and only tell you afterward if it was still too large, so the limit you saw didn’t always match what actually applied. We’ve now moved mobile to the same pre-compression check that desktop has always used, so the number you see is the number that counts.

File Preview

You can now preview text files without having to download them!

How it Works

  1. Upload a plain text file to Discord chat. Copy and pasted messages larger than 2000 characters can also be sent as plain text files.
Note: Discord Nitro subscribers will have their character cap raised to 4000.
  1. You can change filenames before submission and add a comment. The comment will appear as a regular message in chat (above the preview box).
Note: There is a 50kb preview limit on file uploads

  1. Now anyone can preview the content without having to download the file.

  2. Press Expand to show more lines in the chat view (up to 100)

  3. Press the resize icon to the right of Expand to show up to 50kb of the file in a popup

How can I disable Text-To-Speech?

You can disable Text-To-Speech by going into User Settings > Accessibility > Disable “Allow playback and usage of /tts command.”

This will now make it so that any instance of /tts will not be played if you or someone else uses it.

For more in-depth information on Discord’s Text-To-Speech abilities, check out Text-To-Speech 101

How do I disable auto-embed?

You can disable Discord’s auto-embed feature at any time through your User Settings.

  1. Click the User Settings cog icon in the bottom left corner

  2. Select the “Text & Images” Tab. Then, un-check the boxes titled:

  1. “When posted as links to chat.” and

  2. “When upload directly to Discord.”

Pro Tip: If you want to cancel an embed for one specific link, you can wrap the link in ‘< >’ tags.

Before:

After:

How do I edit my messages?

It can be embarrassing when you mistype something but it’s ok, we’ve all been there. Lucky for you, there’s a way to edit your message so you can clarify what you meant to say!

Step 1: Hover over the message & select the pen icon to Edit.

Step 2: Correct the typos…

Step 3: And press enter (or click ‘save’) once you’re sure it’s correct.

Note: In case you change your mind, you can always back out at this step and press ‘escape’ if you don’t want to edit the message (or you chose the wrong message to edit).

How do I switch to compact text mode?

Sometimes space is at a premium, we understand just how valuable screen real estate can be. If you need to make the most of your monitor you may want to try out Compact Text Mode.

Here’s how to find it:

User Settings -> Appearance -> Message Display -> Compact Mode

Just check the box for Compact mode and you are all set!

The biggest difference you’ll see is that user avatars no longer show up. What was once:

Now gets shrunk down to:

No more avatars and many more messages! Don’t forget that role colors will still be prevalent as well.

How do I upload images and GIFs?

Have a new image that you’re excited to share with your friends? We will show you how to do that and more!

What this article covers:

  • How to Upload an Image
    • Drag & Drop
    • Upload From File
  • Add Alt Text To Your Image Upload
    • Desktop
    • Mobile
    • When writing image alt text, there a few things to keep in mind Important: We’re currently experimenting with various file upload size limits. Select users may have the ability to upload larger file sizes.

How to Upload an Image

You can also copy and paste a GIF or image URL into chat, and the link preview will display said image.
Drag & Drop

The first way to upload an image into Discord is simple - Just drag an image or GIF from another source and drop it into the Discord window. This can be done on the browser or desktop app!

If you’re having trouble dragging your picture or have to dig a little deeper to find it, then we can try another method, leading us to…

Upload From File

To manually upload a file, you can select the little arrow box right next to the text box.

Then maneuver through your folders until you find the image you’re looking for. Double-click or select & hit open, whichever way suits you best.

Whether you’re uploading via Drag & Drop or file upload, you’ll have the opportunity to add a comment to the file before uploading it. Which will go over a little bit more under Add Alt Text To Your Image Upload.

Any picture files and embedded media files have to be less than 10MB. With Nitro, you’ll get a higher upload limit. Otherwise, you’re free to bombard your friends with your favorite pics to your heart’s content!

Add Alt Text To Your Image Upload

After you choose the image you want to upload, you can add alt text to the image. Alt text is a short text description that you provide for your image, which is helpful for your friends or community who may be visually impaired and rely on a screen reader. Even for users that don’t need a screen reader, image descriptions are good to have for those with sensory/learning disabilities or in place of an image that doesn’t properly load in the browser.

Desktop

After you choose the image you want to upload, press on the pencil icon to Modify Attachment at the corner of the upload preview.

In the in-app pop-up, type in the Description (Alt Text) a brief description of your image. Press Save then upload your image!

Mobile

After you choose the image you want to upload, press on the image preview.

Select Image Description then type in a short description in the Description (Alt Text) text box. Press Save then upload your image!

When writing image alt text, there a few things to keep in mind:
  • Aim to be succinct and specific! Avoid repeating details.
  • Don’t start the alt text with “image of…” or “picture of…” since screen readers will usually announce that an image is a “graphic” then state the provided alt text.
  • Make sure to call out specific details. For example, state any text that’s in the image and the names of prominent figures, landmarks, etc. if they are in the image.
  • Context is key! When describing the image, describe what the image is supposed to communicate to viewers, not just what is literally in the image.

How to Add Custom Emojis on Discord

Custom emojis let you personalize your Discord server by uploading unique images that express your community’s personality. You can add up to 50 custom emojis to any server and Nitro subscribers can use them anywhere on Discord.

What this article covers:

  • Adding Custom Emoji
    • Through Server Settings
    • Through Emoji Picker
  • Animated Custom Emojis
  • Twitch Sub Emotes
  • Frequently Asked Questions Important: Emoji suggestions while typing are currently an experiment on mobile and are not available to all users. If you have this feature and want to turn it off, go to Settings > Chat > Emoji and toggle off Show emoji suggestions as you type.

Adding a Custom Emoji

Note: If you’re not the server owner or don’t have the Create Expressions permission enabled, you won’t be able to add emojis to that server.

Every server by default can add up to 50 custom emojis that any active server members can use within the server. If any user is a Nitro subscriber, they’ll be able to use the custom emojis from any server anywhere in Discord where emojis can be used!

Through Server Settings

  1. To upload custom emojis, choose the server where you would like to add custom emojis.

  2. Head into your Server Settings by selecting the drop-down menu located next to the server name.

  3. Once redirected, choose the Emoji tab to and press Upload Emoji to upload a custom emoji.

Navigating to Emoji Tab to Upload an Emoji

Keep in mind:

  • Emoji names must be at least 2 characters long and can only contain alphanumeric characters and underscores
  • Emojis must be under 256KB in size Tip: Any user who is an active member of a server is able to use all uploaded custom emoji within that server, and any users who have a Nitro subscription will be able to use the server’s custom emojis anywhere on Discord where emojis can be used.
Through Emoji Picker

Important: The Emoji Picker on Discord’s desktop app and browser now includes Emoji Studio, a feature that’s gradually rolling out to all users. Emoji Studio is not available on mobile.

  1. In the Emoji Picker, select Add Emoji to open Emoji Studio.
Add Emoji Button in Emoji Picker

  1. Choose a file to upload. Supported formats include JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WEBP.

  2. Customize your emoji by resizing, rotating, or zooming. You can also give it a name and select which server to upload it to.

Example of Customizing an Emoji in Emoji Studio
  1. When you’re finished, select Upload Emoji.
Upload Emoji Button

Animated Custom Emojis

In addition to the 50 static custom emojis, if you have Nitro or Nitro Basic, you’ll have an extra 50 slots available for animated ones too! Sometimes, just typing out 😓 😤 isn’t enough to fully express your final exam grind (which btw, you’re going to ace). With animated custom emojis, Nelly feels the heat too.

Example of Animated Emoji in Chat

Note: The same naming and sizing requirements listed above apply to the animated custom emojis.

Twitch Sub Emotes

Subbed to some of your favorite streamers on Twitch? If the streamer has enabled their Twitch emotes for subs, you can use their custom emojis globally!

Important: Although animated Twitch emotes will sync into your server, they will be static-only. If you would like to add animated Twitch emotes to your server, you will have to upload them manually.

For this to work, you’ll need to:

  • Sync your Twitch account with Discord
  • Make sure you’re currently subscribed to their channel
  • Join the streamer’s sub-enabled server Note: Please make sure your custom emojis follow Discord Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. If you have additional questions about Custom Emojis, be sure to let our Support Team know via dis.gd.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How many custom emojis can I upload to my Discord server?

A: Every server can add up to 50 static custom emojis by default. Servers with Nitro or Nitro Basic subscriptions can add an additional 50 animated custom emojis, for a total of 100 custom emojis.

Q: What are the file requirements for uploading custom emojis?

A: Custom emojis must be under 256KB in size and use supported formats like JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WEBP. Emoji names must be at least 2 characters long and can only contain alphanumeric characters and underscores.

Q: Can I use my server’s custom emojis on other servers?

A: Custom emojis are only usable on the server where they were uploaded unless you have Discord Nitro or Nitro Basic. With a Nitro subscription, you can use custom emojis from any server anywhere on Discord.

Q: How do I add animated custom emojis to my server?

A: Upload animated emojis (GIF format) the same way you would upload static emojis through Server Settings > Emoji tab. However, you’ll need Nitro or Nitro Basic to unlock the additional 50 animated emoji slots for your server.

Q: Can I use Twitch subscriber emotes on Discord?

A: Yes! Sync your Twitch account with Discord, make sure you’re subscribed to the streamer’s channel, and join their sub-enabled Discord server. You’ll then be able to use their Twitch emotes globally on Discord.

Q: Why are my Twitch emotes appearing as static instead of animated?

A: Animated Twitch emotes sync to Discord as static images only. If you want to use animated versions, you’ll need to upload them manually as custom emojis to your server.

Q: Who can upload custom emojis to a server?

A: The server owner and anyone with the Manage Emojis or Create Expressions permission can upload custom emojis to a server.

Q: What’s the difference between custom emojis and animated custom emojis?

A: Custom emojis are static images, while animated custom emojis are GIF files that play animations. Both count toward your server’s emoji limit, but animated emojis require a separate 50-slot allocation that’s only available with Nitro or Nitro Basic.

Q: Can I use custom emojis from other servers without Discord Nitro?

Q: What permissions do I need to add custom emojis to a server?

Q: Why can’t I see custom emojis from a specific server in my Emoji Picker?

Mention Suggestions FAQ

Mention suggestions on Discord allow you to easily tag and mention users who you’re conversing with in text channels, DM, and group messages. Learn more about how it works below.

What this article covers:

  • What are Mention Suggestions?
    • What do Mention Suggestions search for?
  • Frequently Asked Questions Important: Mention Suggestions are an experiment released to a limited number of users.

What are Mention Suggestions?

Mention suggestion example

When you’re typing in a text channel and you want to tag a friend in your message, you can start typing the username of your friend and automatically trigger the Mention Suggestion pop-up. With Mention Suggestions, you don’t have to enter “@” before typing your friend’s username and you can simply press the TAB key to insert the complete username mention in your message.

What do Mention Suggestions search for?

Mention Suggestions search through the text channel/DM/group message you are currently typing in for users who can view the DM or have View permissions enabled.

The feature looks for the following types of names:

  • Username
  • Display name
  • Server nickname
  • Custom friend nickname Tip: If a user doesn’t show up as a Mention Suggestions, it may be because the information is still loading from your Discord app! Mention Suggestions are dependent on what has been loaded locally on your device. To learn more, check out the Frequently Asked Questions.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Are Mention Suggestions available on the desktop, mobile, and browser apps?

A: Mention suggestions are only available on the desktop app at this time.

Q: How do Mention Suggestions work?

A: This is an app-side feature – meaning that any matching happens directly on your device, not on our Discord servers. We don’t look at your message content to make the match, your Discord app does this locally.

Q: Can I turn Mention Suggestions off?

A: Yes, you can disable Mention Suggestions by navigating to your User Settings, under Chat, then disable the “Show suggestions for user mentions as you type” option.

The “Show suggestions for user mentions as you type” settings option under Chat within User Settings

Alternatively, you can right-click on the text field, go to Suggestions in the context menu, then uncheck the Mentions box to disable Mention Suggestions.

Mention suggestion checkbox option within the right-click context menu

Q: Can I use Mention Suggestions for server roles and apps?

A: No, Mention Suggestions are exclusively for Discord usernames. If you would like to mention a role or app, please make sure to type “@” before the role or app you want to tag in your message.

Message Bookmarks and Reminders

NOTE: This feature is currently experimental and available to a limited number of Nitro members.

What this article covers:

  • What are Bookmarks?
  • Bookmark a Message
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • Creating a Reminder

What are Bookmarks?

Discord’s bookmarks feature is here to transform how you manage your conversations via chat, direct messages (DM), and group chats. Available exclusively for Nitro users, this tool allows you to:

  • Easily save important messages for later reference
  • Organize your Discord content more efficiently
  • Manage your saved items in real-time, with the ability to save or unsave messages as needed NOTE: Bookmarks have a storage limit of 200 messages.

Never miss crucial information again! With bookmarks, you can keep track of important conversations and come back to them whenever you need.

Bookmark a Message

NOTE: As this feature is experimental, the steps may vary slightly.

Bookmarking messages allows you to bookmark important information for easy access later. Whether you’re using Discord on desktop, browser, or mobile, here’s how you can bookmark messages:

Desktop/Browser

  1. On desktop or browser, navigate to the message you would like to save.

  2. Right-click the message and select the Bookmark Message option in the dropdown menu, then press Bookmark.

  3. Once bookmarked, you will see a notification badge letting you know that the message has been saved for later.

  4. To view your bookmarked messages, press the Inbox icon [] in the upper-right corner of the app and select the Bookmarks tab to find your messages.

On desktop/browser: To convert a bookmarked message into a reminder or unsave it, press the Inbox icon [] > Bookmarks tab. Then select the desired option in the upper right-corner of the bookmarked message.

Mobile

  1. On mobile, navigate to the message you would like to save.

  2. Long-press the message and tap Bookmark Message in the menu.

  3. Once bookmarked, you will see a notification badge letting you know that the message has been saved for later.

  4. To view your bookmarked messages, tap Notifications [] located in the bottom hub and select the Bookmarks icon [] in the upper-right corner of the app. This will take you to the Bookmarks tab.

On mobile: To convert a bookmarked message into a reminder or unsave it, navigate to Notifications [] > Bookmarks[]. Then tap the ellipsis [] in the upper-right corner of the message and select the desired option.

Creating a Reminder

Reminders allow you to set notifications for important messages at a specific time.Here’s how to create reminders on both desktop, browser, and mobile:

Desktop/Browser

  1. On desktop or browser, select the Inbox icon [] in the upper-right corner of the app.

  2. Hover over the message you would like to set as a reminder and press the Create Reminder icon [] in the upper-right corner of the message.

  3. In the Remind Me menu, you can choose how long you’d like to wait before being reminded.

Choosing the Custom option in the Remind Me menu allows you to set a specific date and time for your reminder.

  1. To view your reminders, press the Inbox icon [] in the upper-right corner of the app and select the Bookmarks tab. Here, you’ll find your added reminders. Each reminder will display your chosen Due in timeframe above the message.

On desktop/browser: To edit, complete, or remove the reminder, right-click the message you have set as a reminder within Inbox > Bookmarks. From there, choose your desired action.

Mobile

  1. On mobile, navigate to the message you would like to set as a reminder.

  2. Long-press the message and tap Create Reminder in the menu.

  3. Choose when you would like to be reminded in the Remind Me… menu.

  4. Once set, you will see a notification badge letting you know that the message has been set as a reminder.

  5. To view your reminders, tap Notifications [] located in the bottom hub and select the Bookmarks icon [] in the upper-right corner of the app.

On mobile: To edit or remove the reminder, tap the ellipsis [] in the upper-right corner of the reminder, then select the desired option. Tap the checkmark icon [] to mark it as complete.

Message Forwarding

What this article covers:

  • What is message forwarding?
  • How to Forward a Message
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What is message forwarding?

Have you ever wanted to send your friends that cool thing you saw on another server or send them a funny meme from another channel?

Forwarding will let you to select any message or piece of media and send it to another place in Discord.

A forwarded message will show up clearly labeled as “forwarded”.

How to Forward a Message

Desktop/Browser

  1. To get started, hover over a message and press the Forward button [] within the hover bar in the upper right corner of the message.

  2. The Forward To pop-up menu will appear, and you can select where you would like to forward the message and add an optional note to provide context.

Note: You can forward the message to a maximum of 5 places.

  1. Once you’re all set, press Send in the lower right corner of the pop-up menu to forward your message.

Your forwarded messages will be labeled as “Forwarded” without any indication of the message’s original author. The original message’s source destination will only show as a link to those who already have access to that server or if the server is public.

Mobile

  1. To get started forwarding a message on mobile, long-press the message and select the Forward option [] in the context menu.

  2. The Forward To menu will appear, allowing you to select where you would like to forward your message. Once you’re ready, tap Send.

  3. Your message will be forwarded to the selected places and be labeled as Forwarded.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why can’t I forward certain messages?

A: Messages from monetized channels cannot be forwarded as well as messages from age-restricted channels to unrestricted channels.

Q: Can I publish a forwarded message in an announcement channel?

A: No, publishing a forwarded message in announcement channels is not allowed at this time.

Q: Will others see who originally wrote the message I forward?

A: No, the original author of the message will not be shown: only the content is included.

Q: Can everyone see where a forwarded message came from?

A: No, the link back to the original message is only visible to those who have access to the original server and channel, or if it’s from a public server.

Q: If the original message is edited later, will my forwarded message update too?

A: No, the forwarded message is a copy of the original message at the time you forwarded it and will not update.

Q: Can I disable forwarding for my own messages or for messages in/out of my server?

A: No, you cannot control this at this time.

Message Requests

Message Requests are turned on for everyone. If you’re in the teen age group or are unconfirmed, all direct messages from people you’re not friends with go to a separate message requests inbox, so you can review them before they appear in your main DM list, and you can’t turn this setting off until you confirm you’re an adult.

Once you’re in the adult age group, you can turn off Message Requests. If a user in the adult age group has Message Requests turned on, they will still have messages from non-friends routed to the message requests inbox, unless they share a mutual friend or a small server with the sender.

DM spam filters are set to ““filter all”“. Spam filtering is applied to all incoming DMs. This is a default setting that can be adjusted at any time.

  • What do Message Requests look like?

What do Message Requests look like?

Message Requests On Desktop

From this tab, you’ll be able to view user profiles to check shared servers, and accept or ignore Message Requests. While it isn’t possible to retrieve ignored requests, people will be able to resend Message Requests to your account depending on your Server Settings and your User Settings > Content & Social > Message requests settings.

Message Requests Setting in Server Settings

Message Requests limit what content you can see before you accept the message request in order to respond. You can preview a message in Message Requests, but images or other files will not be visible or accessible and any links will be shown as plain text that can’t be selected.

Message Requests Settings in User Settings

Note: The Message Requests tab will only display if there is at least one pending request. All Message Requests will display a notification badge on the client.

What is the Spam Folder?

To view your Spam folder, select the Spam tab inside the Message Requests view.

Spam Tab in Message Requests

From this tab, you’ll be able to view user profiles to check shared servers, and accept or report spam folder message requests. You may also preview and ignore messages by selecting the message itself.

Preview for a Message Requests

Message Requests on Mobile

On your mobile device, you can tap into your DMs and find a tab labeled Message Requests if you have at least one request pending. This will pull up a view listing the requests you’ve received.

You’ll be able to both view user profiles and choose between accepting or declining requests on your mobile app, as shown below:

Direct Messages Tab > Message Requests Tab on Mobile
Preview Enabled (Left) & Preview Disabled (Right)

Message Requests for the Teen Age Group

As part of our additional teen safety protections, Message Requests are turned on for teens automatically. This helps screen out unwanted DMs by routing messages from people teens don’t share a server or friend connection with into a separate inbox, so they can decide whether to accept them.

Users need to be in the adult age group to turn Message Requests off. You can check your age group status under User Settings > Account Status.

If your age group is incorrect or you are unconfirmed, you can confirm your age group. Find more detailed instructions here.

Note: Teen safety protections may vary slightly depending on where you live, as some regions have specific requirements under local regulation. For region-specific information, see our directory here.

How To Turn Message Requests Off

Note: You need to be in the adult age group to turn this feature off. You can check your age group status under User Settings > Account Status. If your age group is incorrect or you are unconfirmed, you can confirm your age group following the detailed instructions here.

To turn this feature off for a particular server, navigate to the Server dropdown menu > Select Privacy Settings > Toggle off “Message Requests”:

Message Requests Disabled

Note: Turning this feature off in a server will disable Message Requests from that server.

This means that, unless restricted by Server Settings or your User Settings > Messaging Permissions > Direct Message (DM) Permissions settings, messages sent from other members of that server will automatically populate in your DM list.

You can also toggle your global message request setting in User Settings > Messaging Permissions l, as shown in the screenshot below.

Managing Direct Messages: Controlling Who Can Contact You

When a teen receives direct messages (DMs) from a sender for the first time, Discord will detect if a safety alert should be sent to the teen for this DM. If detected, Discord will notify the teen with a safety alert encouraging them to double check if they want to reply, and will provide links to block the user or view more safety tips to safeguard themselves. Learn more about this experience here.

Note: The spam folder cannot be disabled at this time.

Pin Messages FAQ

Use Pin Messages to save important messages and keep them easy to find, no matter how far back they were sent. Pinned messages stay accessible in any text channel or DM, so your community’s most important information is always within easy reach.

  • Frequently Asked Questions Note: Only users with the Manage Messages permission (or server owners) can pin or unpin messages in a server channel. Any member can view pinned messages.

Managing Pin Permissions (Server Owners & Admins)

By default, users with the Manage Messages permission can pin messages. If you want to restrict or grant this ability to specific roles, you can manage this through your server’s role settings.

Want to learn more?

To learn more about Manage Messages and other text channel permissions, visit Channel Permissions Settings 101.

Desktop/Browser
  1. Select your server name in the upper-left corner, then press Server Settings.
Selecting Server Settings from the server name dropdown
  1. Press Roles, then select the Edit icon [] next to the role you want to edit.
Edit icon next to a role in Roles settings

  1. Select Permissions and scroll down to Text Channel Permissions.

  2. Toggle Pin Messages on or off to control whether this role can pin messages. Press Save Changes when done.

Pin Messages permission toggle under Text Channel Permissions (Desktop)
Mobile
  1. Tap your server name in the upper-left corner, then press Settings [] and select Roles.
Selecting a role to edit in Roles (Mobile)

  1. In Roles, tap the role you would like to edit.

  2. Then, tap Permissions and scroll down to the Pin Messages permission.

  3. Toggle Pin Messages on or off to control whether this role can pin messages. Press Save when done.

Pin Messages permission toggle under Text Channel Permissions (Mobile)

How to Pin a Message

You can pin any message in a text channel or DM as long as you have the Pin Messages permission (or are the server owner).

Desktop/Browser

  1. Hover over the message you want to pin. Select the More icon [] that appears at the far right of the message.

  2. Select Pin Message from the dropdown menu.

  3. A confirmation dialog will appear. Press Oh yeah. Pin it to confirm.

Selecting Pin Message from the message dropdown (Desktop)

Note: The pinned message will be saved to the channel’s Pins window. A system message will appear letting members know something was pinned.

System message in channel after a message is pinned
Mobile

  1. Long-press the message you want to pin.

  2. Tap Pin Message.

  3. Confirm by tapping Yes.

Tapping Pin Message from the long-press menu (Mobile)

How to View All Pinned Messages

You can view all pinned messages in a channel or DM at any time using the pin icon.

Desktop/Browser

  1. Open the channel or DM where you want to view pins.

  2. Select the Pins icon [] in the top-right corner of the channel to open the pinned messages panel.

Pins icon in the channel header (Desktop)

All pinned messages for that channel will appear in the panel, listed from most recently pinned to oldest.

Mobile

  1. Open the channel or DM.

  2. Tap the channel name at the top of the screen to open channel details.

  3. Select Pins to view all pinned messages.

Pins option in channel details (Mobile)

How to Jump to a Pinned Message

Desktop/Browser

Each pinned message includes a Jump button that takes you directly to where the message originally appeared in the conversation.

  1. Open the Pinned Messages window (see above).

  2. Find the pinned message you want to locate, then press Jump.

Jump button next to a pinned message in the Pins window

Discord will scroll you back to the original location of that message in the channel, regardless of how far back it was sent.

Mobile

  1. Open the Pins menu (see above).

  2. Tap the pinned message you want to locate.

  3. Tap Jump to Message.

Discord will scroll you to the original location of that message in the channel, regardless of how far back it was sent.

Jump to Message option after tapping a pinned message (Mobile)

How to Remove a Pinned Message

If you have the Manage Messages permission, you can remove any pinned message from a channel.

Desktop/Browser

  1. Open the Pinned Messages window.

  2. Find the pinned message you want to remove and select the X icon next to it.

  3. Confirm the removal when prompted.

X icon next to a pinned message in the Pins window (Desktop)

Tip: You can also right-click any message and choose Unpin Message to remove it directly from the channel.

Right-click a message to choose Unpin Message

Tip: To skip the confirmation prompt when removing a pin, hold Shift and select the X icon next to the pinned message in the Pins window.

Holding Shift to reveal the Unpin icon in the Pins window
Mobile

  1. Open the Pins window.

  2. Long-press the pinned message you want to remove.

  3. Select Unpin Message from the options that appear, then tap Yes to confirm.

Selecting Unpin Message from the long-press menu (Mobile)

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Who can pin messages?

A: Any user with the Pin Messages permission can pin and unpin messages in a channel. Server owners can always pin messages. Admins can also configure which roles have this permission through Server Settings > Roles.

Q: How many messages can I pin in a channel?

A: Each channel and DM supports up to 250 pinned messages. Once you reach the limit, you’ll need to remove an existing pin before adding a new one.

Q: Can I pin messages in DMs and group messages?

A: Yes! Any participant in a DM or group messages can pin messages. There are no permission requirements like there are in servers.

Q: Does pinning a message notify the person who sent it?

A: No. When a message is pinned, a system message appears in the channel, but the original sender does not receive a notification.

Q: Can I pin images, videos, or links?

A: Yes, you can pin any type of message, including those that contain images, videos, file attachments, or links.

Q: Will members see when a message is pinned?

A: Yes. When a message is pinned, a system message appears in the channel to let all members know. This system message itself cannot be pinned.

Q: Can pinned messages be seen by all members of a channel?

A: Yes. All members who have access to the channel can view its pinned messages, regardless of when the message was originally sent.

Q: Why can’t I see the Pin Message option?

A: The Pin Message option only appears if your role has the Manage Messages permission, or if you are the server owner. If you don’t see it, contact your server admin to have this permission added to your role.

Reactions and Super Reactions FAQ

NOTE: Reaction notifications are currently an experimental feature limited to a select number of desktop and mobile users.

You will receive a notification for any reaction to messages you’ve posted. To customize or disable your reaction notifications, go to Settings > Notifications. There, you can choose your preferred option for Reaction Notifications.

Mobile Experience: Reaction Notifications and Customization Options

Find more information about notification settings here.

Sometimes an emoji is worth a thousand words. Instead of typing out your response to the age-old coffee vs. tea debate, you can react to the post with an emoji and let people know what’s up.

What this article covers:

  • What are Reactions?
    • How to add Reactions
  • What are Super Reactions?
    • How to add Super Reactions
    • How many reactions does my Nitro/Nitro Basic/Nitro Classic subscription allow?
    • How do I disable Super Reactions animations?
    • Removing Super Reactions as Server Admins and Moderators
  • Can I see who reacted with what emojis to a message?
  • Can I remove Reaction/Super Reactions?
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are Reactions?

Reactions on Discord allow you express your reaction to a message with an emoji.

If you want to learn more about emojis on Discord, check out this article.

How to add Reactions

Tip: On the mobile app, you can double-tap a message to react with one of your most used emojis. You can also change this emoji by long pressing on a message and selecting Edit.

Just press the little Add Reaction plus smiley-face icon next to the edit message menu icon to pull up your emoji menu to deal your best reaction:

Wanna add more than one reaction to a message? The same Add Reaction plus smiley-face icon will show up next to the last emoji reaction, where you can add all the different types of fire you can think of:

There are a few more tips and tricks you can use to become an emoji-reacting-expert. Check them out:

  • After bringing up the Add Reaction page, hold shift and left-click on multiple emojis to react with all those selected emojis!
  • Right-click the message you want to react to or hover over the message and press on the ellipses to open up the menu, and Quick React with one of your more commonly used emojis at the top, or select a specific emoji in the Add Reaction tab:

What are Super Reactions?

Unlimited Super Reactions are available on both desktop and mobile. Super Reactions are a Nitro locked feature.

Want to take your reactions to the next level? Would you like to react to a message with an emoji and apply it with emphasis? You can with Super Reactions!

A Super Reaction adds an animation when you react to a message with your chosen emoji. Super Reactions are great for when you want to add a little more hype, emotion, and intensity to your reaction!

How to add Super Reactions

To use a Super Reaction, find one of the entry points noted above to access the emoji picker. From there, click on the Super Reaction icon on the top right corner of the emoji picker. Once you see a blurple glow border, all emojis selected will be shared as Super Reactions.

How many reactions does my Nitro/Nitro Basic/Nitro Classic subscription allow?

All Nitro, Nitro Basic, and Nitro Classic users have an unlimited amount of Super Reactions.

Everyone can see Super Reactions! To use Super Reactions, you must be a Nitro, Nitro Basic, or Nitro Classic subscriber.

How do I disable Super Reaction animations?

If you would like to turn off the Super Reaction animations, you’ll need to disable the Play Animated Emoji setting. Here’s where to find that setting:

  1. Go to your account’s User Settings.

  2. Go to the Accessibility page.

  3. Navigate down the page to the Play animated emoji option and use the toggle to enable and disable the Super Reactions animations.

Removing Super Reactions as Server Admins and Moderators

If you are an admin or moderator for a server and you would like to remove Super Reactions from a message, you can do so on the desktop or browser app.

In order to remove Reactions and Super Reactions as a server admin or moderator, you must have the Manage Messages permission.

At this time, you cannot remove Super Reactions as an admin/mod on the mobile app.

  1. Go to the message with the Super Reaction you would like to remove.

  2. You can right-click on the message or press the ellipses icon from the message toolbar to find the View Reactions option.

  3. In the View Reactions window, navigate to the Super Reaction you would like to remove and hover or focus on a server members’ name under the Super Reaction. This will reveal an X besides their name, which you can press to remove the Super Reaction.

Can I see who reacted with what emojis to a message?

You can right-click on a message or press on the ellipses icon of a message to open the menu and see the View Reactions tab. This nifty little menu will let you view who reacted and super reacted with what emoji:

Can I remove my Reaction/Super Reactions?

If you want to take a Reaction back, just select the box with the emoji of the reaction you sent, and it’ll disappear.

You can also open the View Reactions tab from the menu when you right-click on a message or the ellipses icon and select the X next to your username under the emoji of the Reaction.

In that same View Reactions window, you can remove your Super Reaction by selecting the X next to your username under the emoji with the Super Reaction.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I use Super Reactions without a Nitro subscription?

A: No, Super Reactions are a Nitro-exclusive feature. You need a Nitro, Nitro Basic, or Nitro Classic subscription to use Super Reactions.

Q: How many Super Reactions can I use with my Nitro subscription?

A: All Nitro, Nitro Basic, and Nitro Classic subscribers have unlimited Super Reactions.

Q: Can non-Nitro users see Super Reactions?

A: Yes, everyone can see Super Reactions, but only Nitro subscribers can use them.

Q: How do I turn off Super Reaction animations?

A: You can disable Super Reaction animations by turning off the Play Animated Emoji setting in User Settings > Accessibility.

Q: Can I remove someone else’s Super Reaction from a message in my server?

A: Server admins and moderators with the Manage Messages permission can remove Super Reactions from messages on desktop or browser apps, but not on mobile.

Q: How do I view who reacted to a message?

A: Right-click on a message or click the ellipsis icon, then select View Reactions to see who reacted and with which emojis.

Q: Can I remove my own Reaction or Super Reaction?

A: Yes, you can remove your own Reaction by selecting the emoji you used to react, or by using the View Reactions menu and pressing the X next to your username.

Q: What are reaction notifications?

A: Reaction notifications are alerts you receive when someone reacts to your messages with emojis.

Q: How can I control reaction notifications?

A: You can manage reaction notifications in Settings > Notifications > Reaction Notifications. You have three options:

  • All Messages: Receive notifications for all reactions
  • Only Direct Messages: Only receive notifications for reactions in direct messages
  • Never: Don’t receive any reaction notifications Q: Do reaction notifications respect my channel settings?

A: Yes, reaction notifications follow your channel notification settings. If you have muted a channel or server, you won’t receive reaction notifications for messages in those spaces.

Q: Why don’t I receive a reaction notification for every message?

A: There’s a general rate limit for push notifications.

Q: Where will I see reaction notifications?

A: If enabled, reaction notifications can appear as:

  • Mobile push notifications
  • Mobile in-app notifications
  • Desktop notifications Q: What if I’m still receiving too many reaction notifications?

A: If you’re still overwhelmed by reaction notifications, you can:

  • Adjust your Reaction Notifications setting to Only Direct Messages or “Never.
  • Mute specific channels or servers where you don’t want to receive notifications
  • Contact our support team for further assistance

Replies FAQ

What is the Reply feature?

The reply feature lets you respond to a piece of conversation in the channel without having to recapture the context. This is especially useful in conversations that can get very noisy or move very quickly when multiple people are engaging at the same time.

How do I use the Reply feature?

Desktop

To reply to a message directly, simply click on the Reply button when you hover over a message.

You can also access the reply feature by clicking the three dots on the side of the message or by right-clicking the specific message.

Mobile

To reply to a message directly on mobile devices, long press a message and tap on the reply button.

Reply Ping Toggle

Replies will ping the recipient by default. You can toggle this off by clicking

ON
OFF

That’s all for the reply feature, we hope you enjoy it!
