Sending GIFs on Discord

Is it pronounced JIF or GIF? Nevermind that! Did you know, you can search for and post GIFs directly on the Discord app? Let us assist you with sending GIFs to your friends in a snap! No more hunting around folders or websites!

First things first - you can only send gifs, not jif.

What does this Article Cover?

  • How to Send a GIF
    • On Desktop
    • On Mobile (Android/iOS)
  • Favoriting GIFs
    • How to View and Use your Favorite GIFs

How to Send a GIF on Desktop

It’s super simple! You’ll see the GIF icon hanging out with the emoji picker in your text channels.

By clicking on the GIF icon, you’ll find a variety of categories. All that and much more accessible for your GIF needs.

You can also use the search bar at the top to really capture your emotions.

How to Send a GIF on Mobile

If you’re on Android or iOS, you’ll also be able to upload GIFs directly into chat as well using the GIF Picker!

Once you tap the chat/text box, you’ll then see the emoji icon (that looks like a smiley face) pop up! Tap on that emoji icon and you’ll see the Emoji and GIF tab appear!

When you tap on the GIF tab, you’ll now be able to either search directly for the GIF of your choice, or choose one from one of the categories available!

Favoriting GIFs

You also have the ability to favorite GIFs & add them to a Favorites GIFs folder for easy access. You’ll be able to favorite a GIF anywhere on Discord. See a GIF your friend posted & want to add it to the collection? Cool, hit that gold star & it’s yours!

When favoriting a GIF you’ll notice a gold star appear in the corner of a GIF when you hover your mouse over that GIF.

The gold star will not be filled in signaling you have not favorited this GIF. Clicking the same gold star will unfavorite the GIF.

Note: Currently, you can only favorite GIFs on the desktop and browser client at this point in time! We’re still working on building this feature for the mobile app! Hang in there for now!

Just remember:

  • filled in star = favorite
  • unfilled star = unfavorited.
How to View and Use your Favorite GIFs

To view your favorite GIFs, click on the GIF icon in the message bar, and you’ll see your Favorites folder in the very first GIF category!

Once you click on the Favorites category, you’ll be able to admire your full favorite GIF collection!

You’ll be able to quickly access all the GIFs you love and send them in chat in a snap! (You can also directly unfavorite GIFs from inside the Favorites folder too!)

Spellcheck in Discord

Discord’s spellchecker is available on machines currently running macOS and Windows 10+.

Doo youe ned a litle halp wiht wat yur typeing in Diskord? Well, we have you covered. If enabled, you can use your system’s spell checker to check for possible typos!

What this article covers:

  • How to add words to Spellcheck
  • How to disable Spellcheck
  • How to set your language
    • Windows
    • macOS

How to add a words to Spellcheck

Did you accidentally add a word to Spellcheck? Since the spellchecker is based on the dictionary in your computer’s system, you’ll need to go into your computer’s settings to remove the word.

If a word is getting flagged by the Spellcheck, you can add the word to your dictionary.

  1. To do this, after the squiggle appears under the word indicating the spelling needs to be checked, right-click and tap on Add to Dictionary.

  2. Now the word is in your dictionary!

How to disable Spellcheck

While using the desktop app, if at any point you want to turn off the Spellcheck, all you have to do is right-click on a chat window and uncheck the Spellcheck box.

To enable it again, simply follow the same steps above and make sure the box next to Spellcheck has a check mark.

How to set your language

Spellcheck is based on the language of your system and Discord. If your system is a different language than your Discord app, it may flag words that are spelled correctly. Here are some steps on how to set your language on your device.

Windows

  1. Open up Language settings on your system.

  2. You’ll see an option to not only set your Windows display language, but any additional preferred languages.

  3. After adding additional preferred languages you’ll be prompted to install a language pack for each one. Once completed, you can change your Windows display language.

macOS

  1. Go to your Keyboard settings then Text Input.

  2. Here you can set your language preference and add any additional languages by tapping on the plus (+).

  3. After you finish adding any additional languages, you can tap on Done.

Spoiler Tags!

Don’t you just hate it when you have that one friend that tells you that Wumpus McWumperton dies in the next season of Discord High?

We now have a solution for you! Introducing Spoiler Tags!

How does it work?

With spoiler tags, you can mark individual parts of messages or the entire message as a spoiler. The easiest way to mark your message as a Spoiler is by highlighting the text, click on the eye icon. This will mark that portion of the message as a spoiler.

Please note that text marked as Spoiler within code blocks will not be hidden.

Once you mark it as a spoiler, you will see two bars in the front and back of the selected message. The spoiler text should look something like this:

You can also manually tag spoilers by using the Markdown syntax ||Insert spoilers here|| or typing /spoiler before your message.
I need to see it!

Once you made up your mind, and decide to peek into Pandora’s box, go ahead and click on the spoiler box.

I made a mistake, please hide it from my eyes

You can re-hide all spoilers revealed by leaving the channel, but keep in mind, you can never unsee what you have seen.

Image/Video/Link Spoilers

You can mark attachments as spoilers by adding the attachment to your message and then clicking the Mark as Spoiler “eye” icon (eye-con, if you will) before you send your message.

You can mark a link as spoilers by simply adding the two bars in front and back of the link URL.

Please note that Discord server invites embeds cannot be hidden via spoiler tags.

Bold of you to assume I fear spoilers

For the brave souls who wish to journey into the spoiler territory: If you wish to turn off the spoiler tag feature, you may do so by going to User Settings > Text & Images:

On click: Never mind, I want to go back. Please hide all spoilers.

On servers I moderate: I am the Law, therefore I cannot have spoiler tags slowing me down.

(Moderate means you have a role with Manage Messages enabled)

Always: As I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I take a look at my life and realize there’s nothing left to spoil.

Currently, you can only disable the spoiler tag feature on the Desktop/Browser app
Spoiler Tags on Mobile

You can mark text as spoilers on mobile using the same Markdown syntax as on desktop. Wrap your text in bars ||just like this|| and it’ll show up as spoilers when you post it!

This works for embedded links, too. If you want to make a link into a spoiler, just wrap your link in bars!

On iOS specifically, you can mark text as spoilers by selecting the text in the text box and tapping it to open the context menu. Once you have the text selected, you can tap Mark as Spoiler to wrap the selected text in bars.

Sticker Suggestions FAQ

Discord will show you sticker suggestions when you’re typing messages to help remind you of all the great stickers that you have ready to use in your conversations!

Depending on your situation, you’ll see either Nitro and/or custom stickers appear in your sticker suggestion box when you begin typing a message.

Using Sticker Suggestions

After typing your message, you can select a sticker to add to a message a couple ways:

  • Using your keyboard:
    • Press the up arrow key on your keyboard to navigate to the suggestion window.
    • Then, using the left and right arrow keys to select a sticker.
    • Pressing ‘ENTER’ will either send the sticker in chat or attach it to your message.
  • Use your mouse:
    • Move your mouse cursor to hover over the sticker you’d like to select.
    • Clicking the left mouse button will either send the sticker in chat or attach it to your message.
Protip: You can close the suggestion window by hitting the Escape key on desktop! This will prevent the suggestion box from showing until you clear the message field.

Disabling Sticker Suggestions

If you don’t want to see the user suggestions at all, you can disable them on each OS through the following steps!

Desktop

  • Open User Settings by clicking the cogwheel icon in the bottom left corner of the app.

  • Select Text & Images on the left sidebar.

  • Scroll down to Sticker Suggestions and disable the setting. Mobile

  • Open the left menu by swiping left across the screen.

  • Tap your user icon on the right-hand side of the bottom menu.

  • Select the Text & Images section.

  • Scroll down to Sticker Suggestions and disable the setting.

Text Channels & Text Chat In Voice Channels

In Discord, there are three ways to communicate with your friends: voice, video, and text. For this article, you’ll learn more about where to engage with others through text. If you want to learn more about communicating through voice, please check out the Voice Channels FAQs article.

What this article covers:

  • Text Channels
    • Owner/Moderator permissions to edit and create Text Channels
      • Desktop/Browser
      • Mobile
  • Text Chat in Voice Channels
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
    • Message Previews and Notifications
    • Channel permissions for Text Chat in Voice Channels

Text Channels

Text channels, distinguished by the # symbol (also known as the pound sign, hashtag, or octothorpe) in the channel list of a server, are where text communications can take place.

When you want to utilize text channels, here are a few things to keep in mind:

  • Selecting a channel in the left-hand panel will highlight it and bring the channel’s content to the main view of the Discord app.
  • Pressing on the cogwheel next to the text channel’s name is how you can edit a channel, if you have the permissions to do so. You may also see the Invite People icon which looks like a symbol of a person with a plus sign next to the channel name. This will allow you to send an invite to the channel.
  • Enter your message in the text box at the bottom of the client and press the Enter key to send the message to the text channel.
  • You can also send GIFs, stickers, emojis, and gifts through the text box.
  • You can interact with already-sent messages in the text channel by adding a reaction, creating a thread, replying directly to a message, and more, depending on the permissions allowed to you or the role(s) you have in the server.
Owner/Moderator permissions to edit and create Text Channels

If you’re the owner of a server, or a moderator with the permissions to edit a text channels, here is how to do that.

  1. Navigate to the channel that you want to edit the permissions for and then tap on the cogwheel [] next to it to edit the permissions.

  2. Next, tap on Permissions and select the role you’d like to edit the permissions for.

  3. To enable a setting, tap on the checkmark and to disable a setting, tap on the x.

  4. Once you’re finished, tap on Save Changes to save.

In order for a member of your server to chat in a specific channel they at least need the following permissions enabled: View Channel, Send Messages, and Read Message History.

There are other settings you may want to make sure are enabled or disabled, to learn more about Text Channel Settings, please check out the article Channel Permissions Settings 101.

You can also learn more about permissions in general through here.

Text Chat in Voice Channels

Using the embedded text chat in voice channels, users can send message content, comment on something being said without interrupting the speaker, and share links, memes, and more, all in the dedicated text chat within the voice channel. This feature allows users to chat without having to switch to a different text channel while in a voice channel, missing the stream you’re actively watching, or potentially distracting you from the live conversation happening in the voice channel.

Desktop/Browser

There are 2 ways to access the text chat in a voice channel, let’s go over both for desktop and browser.

Option 1

  1. Select on the Open Chat bubble to the right of the voice channel name.

  2. This will automatically pull up the text chat for this voice channel on the right side.

Option 2

  1. Press the voice channel to fully open it.

  2. Next, tap on the Open Chat bubble in the top right corner and this will open the text chat.

Mobile

  1. While in a voice channel, tap on the screen so the bottom menu appears.

  2. Once the bottom menu is active, tap on the Open Chat bubble to access the text chat.

  3. Now you can type anything into the text chat for the voice channel!

Message Previews And Notifications

If you are in a voice channel, but the text chat within that voice channel is closed, you can see message previews in the upper right-hand corner of the voice channel. Message previews will show new messages as they are sent and will disappear after some time or if other messages appear (three messages at the most and truncated after a certain number of characters).

Message previews keep you in the loop of the active message conversation happening in the voice channel without needing to open the chat itself. However, if you want to turn these previews off for whatever reason simply press the three dots icon above and uncheck Show New Message Previews.

As for other indicators of new messages while in the voice channel - unread mentions will have a red number indicator, while unread messages will simply be indicated with a gray number indicator. Mentions within a text chat will also appear in your inbox, which can be accessed in the upper right corner of the client.

Left: mention notification, Right: unread notification
Channel permissions for Text Chat in Voice Channels
If a user or role does not have the correct permissions for a text chat or if the text chat permissions for a voice channel are disabled, then impacted users will be unable to write or read previous messages in the text chat.

Like many of the features on Discord, there are permissions that can be customized and managed by the server owner or a moderator to dictate how various roles or a particular voice channel can utilize the new embedded chat in voice channel feature.

Here’s where to find the permissions for text chat in voice channels below.

Desktop/Browser

  1. After navigating to the server you want to update the permissions for, tap on the cogwheel [] next to the voice channel you want to edit the permissions for.

  2. Next, tap on Permissions.

  3. Now you can go through each setting and determine what you want to enable or disable. In order for a member of the server to be able to chat in the text chat in a voice channel they at least need the Send Messages and Read Message History enabled.

  4. Once you’re finished managing the settings, tap on Save Changes.

Mobile

  1. After navigating to the server you want to update the permissions for, tap and hold on the voice channel you want to edit and then scroll down to Edit Channel.

  2. Next tap on Channel Permissions and then select a role or you can add a new role or member and edit those permissions instead.

  3. Now you can go through each setting and determine what you want to enable or disable. In order for a member of the server to be able to chat in the text chat in a voice channel they at least need the Send Messages and Read Message History enabled.

  4. You do not need to save your settings, as these will save automatically. You can either swipe out of this menu or tap the back button to leave the permission settings.

There is so much you can do through text communication on Discord! You can learn more about how to use text in the Text Chat section of Help Center. Here are some of the articles you’ll find there:

  • Markdown Text 101 (Chat Formatting: Bold, Italic, Underline)
  • Text-to-Speech 101
  • Adding Emojis and Reactions

Text-to-Speech 101

Microphones are great however sometimes you just want to be a robot, right?

The Text-to-Speech (TTS) function will help you achieve your wildest robot dreams by reading what you type directly to your channel.

Sending Text-to-Speech

This is the easy part. To have a sentence read in Text-to-Speech, just type /tts before your sentence. So, to read this sentence:

“Discord’s pretty awesome”

Just type:

/tts Discord’s pretty awesome

Important Note: TTS follows the default system settings of how Discord is being used. Internet browsers such as Chrome or Firefox have a different Text-to-Speech reading bot than Windows or Mac do. Depending on what platform you’re using, you’ll be hearing different TTS voices!

Make it stop!

We get it, the troll in your channel just had the TTS bot read “WWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWW”… Well, we have two selective methods to trim who and what channels have the privilege of utilizing TTS.

Method One: Notification Settings & Server-Wide Mute

The first TTS toggle setting can be found here:

User Settings -> Notifications -> Text-to-Speech

You’ll see three selections here:

  • For all channels: This setting allows any channel, across any server, to have messages be read in Text-to-Speech, regardless if they use the /tts command or not. You’ll be hearing a fair amount of TTS across all of your channels if you have this enabled. Use with caution!
  • For current selected channel: This setting means the current text channel you have selected will have messages read in Text-to-Speech.
  • Never: No matter how hard your friends try, you won’t ever hear the dulcet tones of the Text-to-Speech bot anywhere within Discord. (Unless you engage it yourself, of course.) This Screen is particularly useful if you want to hear what your friends are typing.
Method Two: Read your own sentences!

The second TTS toggle setting can be found here:

User Settings button > App Settings > Accessibility

Use the Text to speech rate setting to adjust the speed at which the text is being read back to you.

What this does is enable or disable the /tts command. If you have this option de-selected, and type in a /tts sentence the Text-to-Speech bot will not read it aloud. A sad tale indeed.

Important Note: The TTS option in the Accessibility tab is completely separate from the TTS options in the Notifications tab. If a user has TTS notifications enabled like in method one, they will hear your sentences written in TTS, regardless of what TTS settings you’ve selected. Similarly, if they disable TTS notifications, they won’t hear your sentences read in TTS at all.

That wraps that up! We wish you the best in your robot adventures and hope that these tips will help you Discord!

Tips for Sticker Creators FAQ

Note: If you’re just getting started with sticker creations, read this article first before you begin creating stickers!

What does this article cover?

  • Custom Sticker Requirements
  • Things to Keep in Mind
    • Transparency
    • Sizing your custom stickers
  • Q&A

Custom Sticker Requirements

Custom stickers are available through Boosting your server. Once boosted, server admins and owners can upload custom stickers under Server Settings > Stickers.

For the best looking stickers, you’ll need to follow these requirements:

  • Animated File types: APNG
  • Static File type: PNG
  • Max File size: 512KB
  • Dimensions: 320px x 320px (exact)
  • Matching Unicode Emoji for Sticker Suggestions
  • [Optional] Description text so people who use screen readers can understand what a sticker looks like.

Things to Keep in Mind

In addition to the requirements listed above, we recommend considering the following items when creating your custom sticker creations.

Transparency

Due to their uniqueness, stickers are often created with transparent backgrounds. This can be achieved through a few different methods depending on what you’re using to create stickers:

Transparent background (left), Solid background (right)

  • Make sure your background layer is transparent when saving the image.
  • Cutting the background out with a photo editing tool
Sizing your custom stickers

When creating stickers, make sure that your sticker takes up as much canvas space as possible for the best results.

Stickers in the desktop chat will render at 160x160 dp, which is why we recommend uploading stickers as 320x320 px exactly. This scaling helps keep your stickers looking crisp on most displays.

Note: Keep in mind that depending on what device you’re using, and depending on where stickers are displayed (in the sticker drawer, in chat, etc), the sticker may display at different sizes.
Note:
- Your APNG stickers will not render if you only upload the files through the chat bar > upload file section!
- You’ll need to preview the stickers instead in the Server Settings > Stickers > Upload window.

Q&A

Q: Is there a frame rate limit for my stickers?

A: We only allow up to 60 FPS!

Q: What’s the difference between APNG and a PNG file?

A: PNG files are a static, image file format that compresses images in a specific way to prevent quality loss. An APNG file is the animated version of this file format!

Q: Why can’t we use other file types as custom stickers?

A: We wanted to make sure your sticker creations looked just as beautiful in the app as when you’re creating them, so we chose file types that will help support that!

Q: What size will my stickers display in chat?

A: Stickers in the desktop chat will render at 160x160 dp, which is why we recommend uploading stickers as 320x320 px exactly!

Q: What kind of content can I use for my stickers?

A: As is true for all content that you use on Discord, you are responsible for ensuring that any content you use for custom stickers complies with our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.

Q: How can I report someone who’s stolen my original sticker content?

A: Please note that you must be the original owner of the content to file a report.

To report stolen sticker content, you can file a DMCA through our website at: dis.gd. Select “File a DMCA Takedown Request” from the dropdown menu and follow the instructions there.

Voice Messages

Need to send a quick message to all of your friends but can’t type because you’re on the go? Or do you want to make sure your joke lands by adding comedic timing? Well, you’re in luck - You can now send Voice Messages on Discord!

What this article covers:

  • What are Voice Messages?
  • How do I use Voice Messages?
    • Sending Voice Messages
    • Canceling Voice Messages
    • Listening to Voice Messages
  • How to Disable Voice Messages in your server
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are Voice Messages?

Voice Messages give you the ability to send an audio recording directly to your friends. For now, you can only send Voice Messages through a direct message, group direct message, or in a server with Voice Messages enabled. These can be listened to on any device where you can access Discord, but can only be sent through the mobile app.

How do I use Voice Messages?

Sending Voice Messages

There are 2 ways to record and send a Voice Message. After navigating to the DM or server where you want to send a Voice Message, you’ll want to try one of the following:

  1. Press and hold on the Mic button located on the right of the chat input box until you are done recording your message. Once completed, release the button to send the message.

  2. While pressing and holding down the Mic button swipe up to lock the recording mode in place. Once you’re done recording, tap on send.

Canceling Voice Messages

There are two ways to cancel sending a Voice Message that you recorded.

  1. While pressing and holding the Mic button down while recording, drag your finger to the Trash icon on the left side and then release.

  2. After swiping up to lock recording mode in place, in order to cancel the recording, just tap the Trash icon on the left side.

Listening to Voice Messages

You can listen to Voice Messages on either desktop or mobile devices. To listen, simply click the “Play” button on any Voice Message for it to play. The audio will play through your default device.

If you’re on mobile and you do not have an external audio device connected, the audio will play through your mobile speakers.

How to Disable Voice Messages in your server

If Voice Messages are available in your server, you can disable or enable them per role. To do so, go to Server Settings > Roles and navigate to the Send Voice Messages toggle to enable or disable.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is the maximum length of a Voice Message?

A: Voice Messages can be up to 20 minutes long.

Q: Can I upload my own audio files and get them to look like Voice Messages and play inline in chat?

A: No.

Q: Can I send voice messages on Discord Web or the Discord Desktop app?

A: No, you can only send voice messages from the mobile app, but you can listen to them on any Discord platform.

Q: Can I change the audio output the Voice Message plays on?

A: On Desktop, Voice Messages will use the default audio output for Discord. On mobile, they will play through your connected device, if you do not have one connected they will play through your mobile speakers.

Q: How can I report a Voice Message?

A: To report on Desktop right click the voice message and select Report Message. To report on mobile, tap and hold on the message until you see a pop-up that says Report Message.

Why isn’t my DM going through?

If your direct message was unable to be sent, you’ll receive an error message from Clyde that states the following:

Your message could not be delivered. This is usually because you don’t share a server with the recipient or the recipient is only accepting direct messages from friends.

Clyde’s message will look something like this:

Possible Reasons for This Error

There can be a few reasons why you are unable to send a direct message to someone. Here are possible reasons for the error that you may be encountering:

  • You don’t share a server with the DM recipient.
  • You’ve disabled direct messages on your shared server.
  • You have not completed the required membership screening steps in your shared server.
  • The DM recipient is only accepting direct messages from friends.
  • You were blocked by the DM recipient.
  • This error may also appear if the content you’re trying to share has been identified as violating Discord’s Community Guidelines and cannot be uploaded If it seems you are running into a technical error when trying to send a DM, please reach out to our Discord Support team. Otherwise, the Discord Support team will not be able to provide further assistance.

For further information, please review our Blocking & Privacy article to learn more about these features.

Why was my message not delivered?

Communities are public spaces with many active people which can make the community an attractive target for bad actors. Thus, Community servers come equipped with a variety of safety and content moderation tools to help protect members from undesirable messages containing threats like phishing links or malware.

When attempting to post a message that contains content that violates the Community’s guidelines or content filters we enable for all Communities, you may receive an error notifying you that your message failed to deliver.

Possible Reasons for This Error

Below are possible reasons why you received a “Your message could not be delivered” error in a Community Server:

  • Your message contains content prohibited by the community Admins and moderators of a community may be using AutoMod to set up content filters that can automatically detect and block messages containing unwanted content that the community has elected to filter out.

Receiving this error means you tried to post a message that was flagged by any of these AutoMod filters:

  • Keyword filters - your message contains specific words, phrases, or symbols that the community does not allow.

  • Mention spam filter - your message contains an excessive number of unique mentions that exceeds the Community’s limit.

  • Spam content filter - your message contains content that has been reported as or is similar to reported spam. To reduce the likelihood of getting your messages flagged by AutoMod, make sure you’re correctly following the community’s #rules and #guidelines. If you still believe your message was incorrectly or unfairly blocked by AutoMod, look to ask and confirm with your local community moderator.

  • Your message contains a suspicious link Every Community on Discord is equipped with a suspicious link filter designed to detect and block harmful or dangerous messages, such as those containing links to malware or phishing sites.

How does Discord detect suspicious links?

We work to identify links that might mislead or redirect users such as by reviewing a regularly updated list of unsafe and phishing websites. Some of the things we block with this filter are sites that might try to steal personal information like passwords or credit card numbers, your Discord login information, or even financial information.

Claiming a Nitro Gift FAQ

Important Notes:

- Before claiming a gift, make sure you are logged into the correct Discord account on the desktop/browser version of the app!

- If you accidentally claimed the gift on the wrong account, Discord is unable to provide you with another code or transfer the gift!

What this article covers:

  • Claiming a Gift sent within Discord
  • Claiming a Gift sent outside of Discord
  • Already Claimed Gifts
  • What if I already have an Active Nitro Subscription?
    • How do I activate my Account Credit?

Claiming a Gift sent within Discord

If you’re already logged into your account on the browser or desktop version of the Discord app, you can easily claim a gift!

  1. If you’re in a DM or server in Discord and you’ve received a gift link, you can directly press on the Open gift button that’s tied to the gift!

  2. You’ll see a confirmation pop-up asking you to accept the gift! Press the Accept gift button in this confirmation window to apply the gift to your Discord account!

  3. After accepting the gift to your account, you’ll then see a confirmation that the subscription has been directly applied to your Discord account!

Claiming a Gift sent outside of Discord

If you receive a code within your email or through another platform, you can follow these steps below to claim your gift to your Discord account!

Step 1 - Clicking the Gift Link

  • Start by directly clicking the gift link or copying and pasting the gift link into your browser window. Step 2 - Logging into Discord

  • If you’re not logged into Discord already in your browser, you will then be automatically redirected to either: Register for a New Account

If you don’t have an account, you can directly register a new Discord account

Login to your Account

If you already have a Discord account, you can login to your account using your email and password or using QR code login

Step 3 - Confirming the Correct Account

  • Once you have logged into your Discord account, you’ll see a new message asking you to confirm if you would like to accept the gift. Be sure to double-check that you’re logged into the correct Discord account. When you’re ready to claim this gift, press the I accept button. Step 4 - Gift Now Activated

  • After accepting the gift to your account, you’ll now be automatically redirected to your Subscriptions tab in your User Settings to see your newly activated gift subscription on your account.

Already Claimed Gifts

If you’re not sure when a gift has been claimed or not, you can double check by clicking and opening the link in your browser! If a gift has been successfully claimed, you’ll see a “This gift has already been claimed” error in the browser.

If you’re already using the browser or desktop version of Discord, and you’re viewing a gift link shared within Discord, you’ll see there is a grayed out “Claimed” button in the gift after it has been claimed!

What if I already have an Active Nitro Subscription?

Whenever you accept a gift while you have a running subscription, or accept a gift that differs from your current subscription, that gifted subscription will be added to your Discord account as Account Credit.

To view your Account Credit:

  • Start by logging into your Discord account on the desktop or browser version of the app
  • Head into your User Settings (by clicking on the cog icon in the bottom left corner)
  • Then select the Subscriptions tab in the left side bar
Note:
Account Credit can only be used for desktop/browser subscriptions. It cannot be used on Google Play or iOS App Store subscriptions.
How do I activate my Account Credit?

When your current Nitro subscription has expired or is removed, the Account Credit for the gift will apply when you activate that matching subscription on the desktop/browser Discord app!

For example, if you currently have 9.99 Nitro Monthly Credit, you will need to activate a 9.99 Nitro Monthly subscription to use this account credit!

Note:
- The account credit will only be consumed for redeeming exact matching subscription plans in both type and time! (Nitro > Nitro, Nitro Basic > Nitro Basic, Monthly > Monthly, Yearly > Yearly)
- If the subscriptions do not match, the account credit will not be applied!

To activate the matching subscription:

- Start by heading to the Subscription tab, you'll need to press the Subscribe button for the matching subscription type for Discord Nitro or Nitro Basic.
- Then a new window will pop up where you will need to select the matching plan for the subscription.
- If your Discord account does not have your payment information, you'll be asked to fill out your payment details. (Note: You will not be charged unless the subscription renews)
- Once you've finished submitting that information, you'll then see a "Subscription Credit applied" message as you are reviewing the purchase details for activating the subscription
- After you confirm your activation, your gifted subscription will then be activated!

Have any other questions?

If you have any questions around claiming gifts or account credit, just contact our support team at dis.gd/billing and we’ll be able to look into your question further from there!

Discord x Cloudflare Privacy Perk FAQ

Some Nitro users now get access to Cloudflare’s premium version of WARP, WARP+ Unlimited, as part of their subscription. WARP+ enhances your privacy by encrypting a user’s traffic that makes it harder to track or sell your data. While WARP can take advantage of the many Cloudflare data centers around the world to give you a more private and robust connection, WARP+ Unlimited subscribers get access to a larger network. It applies to all internet traffic outside of Discord, covering browsing and any other online applications.

Important: This experiment has concluded and is no longer available as of 3/04/2026

What this article covers:

  • What is the Nitro Privacy Perk?
  • How to Access the Privacy Perk
  • How to Use the Privacy Perk
    • Turning WARP+ On and Off
  • Frequently Asked Question Info: This is an experimental feature available to select Nitro users. It is not available for Nitro Basic or Classic subscribers, users with Nitro obtained through Nitro credits (including trials), or when accessing Discord via mobile or web browser. Additionally, this feature may be unavailable in certain countries where the service is not supported.

What is the Nitro Privacy Perk?

Note: The Nitro Privacy Perk is currently in beta and only available on the Discord desktop app for Windows or Mac. Eligible users need an active, paid Nitro subscription to access this perk.

The Nitro Privacy Perk gives eligible Nitro subscribers access to Cloudflare’s WARP+, a service that enhances your privacy while you browse the web and use other online applications outside of Discord by encrypting your internet traffic.

Please note WARP+ provides an added layer of privacy when you’re browsing external websites and using other apps on your computer. WARP+ only covers traffic outside of Discord, it does not affect any activity or data shared with Discord directly.

To access the Nitro Privacy Perk, you need:

  • Part of the experiment, which is available to select users only
  • An active, paid Nitro subscription
  • Discord desktop app installed on Windows or Mac Note: When your Nitro subscription ends, you’ll automatically be placed into WARP, Cloudflare’s free version of its service.

How to Access the Privacy Perk

The Nitro Privacy Perk is available through your Discord desktop app.

Note: WARP+ only works while the Discord desktop app is running on Windows or Mac. This feature is not available on mobile devices or web browsers.

  1. Open the Discord desktop app.

  2. Press User Settings icon [] in the bottom-left corner of the app located next to your username.

  3. In the left sidebar, select WARP+.

WARP+ tab in User Settings

  1. Select Download to install.

  2. Follow the instructions in WARP+ including accepting Cloudflare’s Terms and Service conditions. This will show up as an external pop-up on your desktop.

Note: You will also need to grant admin permissions. If you are on Windows, look for the Microsoft Admin icon [] on the icons bar. Click on this icon to accept admin permissions.

  1. After installing, you can then toggle WARP+ on.
WARP+ enabled

Note: If you already have a WARP+ account, you’ll see an option that says Use WARP+ now toggle to enable it.

How to Use the Privacy Perk

Once you’ve downloaded WARP+, you can turn it on or off whenever you want. When WARP+ is active, you’ll see an indicator in your system tray (Windows) or menu bar (Mac).

Turning WARP+ On and Off

Tip: The toggle in the Discord app and WARP+ are synced, so any changes you make in one will automatically apply to the other.

  1. Make sure Discord is open on your desktop.

  2. Look for the WARP+ icon in your system tray (Windows) or menu bar (Mac).

Cloudflare WARP icon on Windows system tray
  1. Press the WARP+ icon and toggle it on or off.
WARP+ on Windows (top) and Apple (bottom)

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Does the Privacy Perk protect my activity on Discord?

A: WARP+ protects your privacy when browsing external websites and using other applications on your computer. Your activity within Discord follows our standard privacy practices, which you can learn about in our Privacy Policy.

Q: Will this slow down my internet connection?

A: WARP+ is designed for speed, but because it encrypts your traffic, you may notice slight changes in connection performance. Most users won’t notice a difference during regular browsing.

Q: WARP+ is affecting my gaming performance. What should I do?

A: Because WARP+ encrypts all your internet traffic, it may occasionally increase latency in some online games. If you notice performance issues while gaming, try turning off WARP+ temporarily while you play, then turn it back on when you’re done. Your privacy protection will resume automatically.

Q: Can I use WARP+ on mobile devices?

A: The Nitro Privacy Perk is currently only available on Windows and Mac desktop apps. We’re always exploring ways to bring more value to Nitro subscribers across all platforms.

Q: Does this hide my Discord activity from Discord?

A: No, WARP+ enhances your privacy while browsing outside of Discord. Discord can still see your activity within the Discord platform according to your privacy settings and and our Privacy Policy. WARP+ does not provide IP masking for Discord platform activity.

Q: What’s the difference between WARP and WARP+?

A: WARP is Cloudflare’s free privacy service, while WARP+ (included with Nitro) offers enhanced performance and routing. When you have an active Nitro subscription, you automatically get access to WARP+ features. If your subscription ends, you’ll have access to the standard WARP features.

Q: Can I use this perk if I already have other privacy tools installed?

A: You can have WARP+ installed alongside other privacy tools, but running multiple services simultaneously may cause connection conflicts. We recommend choosing one privacy solution at a time for the best experience.

Q: Will this perk impact safety on Discord?

A: No, we remain deeply committed to creating positive experiences for our users and this tool is part of that commitment. Everything you could ever want to know about safety on Discord can be found here.

Q: Will WARP+ allow me to use an IP address from another country?

A: No. WARP+ will assign you a Cloudflare IP address corresponding to the region in which you are connecting from.

Evolving Nitro Badges

Learn about Discord Nitro’s evolving profile badges, which show how long you’ve been a Nitro subscriber and automatically update to celebrate your membership milestones.

What this article covers:

  • What are Evolving Nitro Badges?
  • How Evolving Badges Work
  • Checking Your Nitro Badge Progress
    • Desktop
    • Mobile
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are Evolving Nitro Badges?

All Nitro subscribers get a special profile badge when they sign up for Nitro. When you’re subscribed to Nitro, your profile badge will evolve to showcase different designs with each milestone that you reach.

Note: The evolving version of the Nitro badge is not available for Nitro Basic or Classic.

How Evolving Badges Work

Your Nitro badge will automatically evolve once you’ve reached each subscription milestone. The badge that displays on your profile will be the most recent milestone that you’ve reached.

Nitro Milestone Badge Evolution

Note: If your Nitro subscription ends at any time and you resubscribe later, your badge progression will start fresh from the beginning. This means you’ll need to maintain an active subscription to maintain your badge progress.

Checking Your Nitro Badge Progress

Desktop

To check your current badge level and when you’ll reach the next milestone, just hover your cursor over the badge on your profile. You can also check your progress under Direct Messages > Nitro Tab.

On Desktop: Evolving Profile Badge Card in Nitro Tab
Mobile

  1. To check your current badge level on mobile, tap your avatar in the bottom right corner.

  2. Then tap the cogwheel icon [] to enter your Settings > Manage Nitro.

On Mobile: Avatar Icon and Settings Icon (Left), Manage Nitro Settings (Right)
  1. In your Nitro Home, you’ll find the Evolving Profile Badge card where you can select See All Badges to view your current badge progress.
On Mobile: Evolving Profile Badge Card (Left), Nitro Badge Milestones (Right)

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What happens to my badge if I cancel or end my Nitro subscription?

A: You’ll keep your badge for the rest of your current billing cycle. After your subscription ends, your badge progression will reset. When you resubscribe, you’ll start fresh from the beginning of the badge progression.

Important: The Discord Support team does not have the ability to update, change, or restore the evolving Nitro badge or any previous badge progress under any circumstances.

Q: Can I keep my evolved badge if I switch between Nitro and Nitro Basic?

A: The evolving version of the Nitro profile badge is only available with Nitro.

Q: How do I view my current badge progress?

A: Simply hover your cursor over the Nitro badge on your profile to see your current level and when you’ll reach the next milestone or visit Direct Messages > Nitro Tab > press on the Evolving Profile Badge card to view where you are in the progression of available badges.

Q: Can I choose which badge design to display?

A: No, the badge that is displayed on your profile will be the last milestone you reached and cannot be manually selected.

Q: Can I hide or remove my Nitro badge?

A: No, the Nitro badge cannot be hidden or removed from your profile once earned.

Favorites FAQ

Keep the conversations that matter most right at your fingertips. With Favorites, Nitro users can add your most-used channels and DMs into a single, dedicated space. Whether it’s a text channel or direct message you check constantly, Favorites puts everything important in one easy-to-reach place.

What this article covers:

  • What are Favorites?
  • How to Favorite a Channel or DM
    • How to Remove a Channel or DM from Favorites
    • How to Create a Category for your Favorites
  • How to View your Favorites
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are Favorites?

Important: Favorites is currently available as a Nitro experiment on desktop and browser. Access may vary by user, and mobile support is limited to view-only.

Favorites is a feature that places all your top channels and DMs in a place that’s easy to find. Any channel or direct message you mark as a favorite will appear in a dedicated Favorites section at the top of your server list, keeping your most important conversations separate from the rest.

You can favorite channels from any server you’re in, as well as DMs and group DMs — making Favorites a handy home base for everything you actually use on a regular basis. Plus, you can group these chats into custom categories to keep everything neat and tidy.

How to Favorite a Channel or DM

Important: Favorites are view-only on mobile. All management actions (editing, adding, moving, and renaming) require desktop or browser.

You can favorite text channels, direct messages (DMs), group direct messages (GDMs), forum channels, and voice channels. While you can’t favorite specific threads, you can favorite the text channel a thread is in.

Tip: Even if you disable Favorites in Settings or unsubscribe and re-subscribe to Nitro, your Favorites will still be saved.

  1. Navigate to the channel or DM/GDM that you want to favorite.

  2. Right-click on what you would like to favorite and then select Add to Favorite. If you have a Category set up, you can add the item to your preferred category instead.

Adding a text channel to Favorites
How to Remove a Channel or DM from Favorites

  1. Navigate to your Favorites by selecting the Favorites icon [] in the top-left corner above your server list.

  2. Right-click on a channel or DM/GDM and select Remove from Favorites.

Removing a text channel from your Favorites
How to Create a Category for your Favorites

To organize your Favorites even more, you can create a variety of Categories. Uncategorized channels will appear at the top of your favorited items.

  1. While under the Favorites tab right-click and select Create Category.

  2. Name your Category and then press Create Category.

  3. Now when you add a channel or DM/GDM to your Favorites, you can add them into a category instead or drag your current favorites items to the category.

Create a Category for Favorites

How to View your Favorites

Tip: If you didn’t enable Favorites when you received the pop-up about the experiment, you will not see the Favorites icon []. You will have to head to User Settings > Chat and enable or disable the Show Favorites Server toggle.

To view everything in your Favorites select the Favorite icon [] in the top-left corner above your server list on desktop, browser, or mobile.

Favorites icon

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What all can I add to my Favorites?

A: Text channels, voice channels, DMs, GDMs, and forum channels. Only threads can not be favorited.

Q: Does favoriting a channel notify anyone?

A: No, it’s personal and private.

Q: Is there a limit to how many items I can favorite?

A: You can add up to 200 items to your Favorites. This includes any Categories you create.

Q: Can I reorder my Favorites?

A: Yes, you can move a favorited channel or DM, or organize them in a category.

Q: Are Favorites available on mobile?

A: Yes, Favorites is available on desktop, browser, and mobile. However, you can only edit Favorites from desktop/browser.

Q: Can I preview Favorites if I don’t have Nitro?

A: Yes! You can preview the Favorites feature in settings even without a Nitro subscription. And if you are a past subscriber and re-subscribe, your Favorites are saved. For Nitro users, Favorites are saved even if you toggle the feature off — so when you turn it back on, everything will reappear exactly as you last set it up.

Q: Can I turn off Favorites from displaying?

A: Yes, if you are a Nitro user you can go to User Settings > Chat and enable or disable the Show Favorites Server toggle. Your Favorite will be saved even if you toggle it off or unsubscribe and re-subscribe to Nitro.

Show Favorites Server toggle

Monthly Orbs Drop for Nitro Members FAQ

Nitro subscribers can now receive 250 Discord Orbs on a monthly basis just for maintaining their Nitro subscription! These Orbs are automatically added to your account, giving you even more ways to get Nitro Credit or Shop items to better customize your Discord experience.

What this article covers:

  • What are Monthly Orbs drops?
  • How to Earn a Monthly Orb drops
    • Eligibility Requirements
  • How Often You’ll Receive Orbs
  • Viewing Your Monthly Orbs Drop
  • Frequently Asked Questions Important: Monthly Orbs drops are gradually rolling out to all eligible users.

What are Monthly Orbs Drops?

Want to learn more?

You can learn more about Discord Orbs here.

Monthly Orbs Drop is a benefit for Nitro subscribers that provide additional Discord Orbs on a monthly basis. As a Nitro member, you’ll automatically receive 250 monthly Orbs that you can use in the Shop to get Nitro Credit, Avatar Decorations, Profile Effects, and other eligible Shop items.

These Orbs are added directly to your total Orbs balance. They’re in addition to any Orbs you earn through Discord Quests, giving you more opportunities to personalize your Discord experience.

How to Earn Monthly Orbs with Nitro

Eligibility Requirements

Tip: For eligible users who subscribe to Nitro, it may take up to 1 week until your first Monthly Orbs drop.

To receive a Monthly Orbs Drop, you need:

  • An active paid Nitro subscription through the desktop app or browser

  • Your subscription must be in good standing (for example, subscription is not in a grace period due to payment issues)

  • Be part of the Monthly Orbs Drop experiment group Monthly Orbs Rewards are included for:

  • Monthly Nitro subscriptions

  • Annual Nitro subscriptions

  • Subscriptions with selected promotional discount (including BOGO offers) Monthly Orbs Rewards are NOT included for:

  • Gifted Nitro subscriptions

  • Nitro through Nitro Credits

  • Nitro Basic or Classic plans

  • Accounts with suspended or terminated subscriptions

  • Nitro trials from partnership promotions

How Often You’ll Receive Orbs

Note: Your Orbs are automatically deposited into your Orbs balance on a monthly basis—you don’t need to claim them manually.

For eligible users in the Monthly Orbs Drop experiment, you will see a notice in your Discord app each month when your Monthly Orbs have been added to your Orbs balance.

You’ve got Orbs! notification

Viewing Your Monthly Orbs Drop

Note: Currently, you can only view your total Monthly Orbs earned and your upcoming Monthly Orbs Drop on the desktop and web versions of Discord. This information isn’t available in the mobile app just yet.

However, your total Orbs balance will remain consistent across all platforms.

  1. Navigate to your Direct Messages list by selecting the Discord app icon in the upper-left corner.

  2. Press the Nitro Home tab to the right of your server list.

  3. Scroll down the page until you see “Earn monthly Nitro Rewards”.

Nitro Rewards earned

Here you’ll see a Monthly Orbs Drop banner that shows:

  • Number of Days left until your next Monthly Orbs Drop
  • The total amount of Orbs you’ve earned through Monthly Orbs Drops Note: Days where you are consuming Nitro Credits are not included in your monthly countdown. You may notice your countdown increase when Nitro Credits are added. Learn more about Nitro Credits here.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Do Orbs expire?

A: No, your Orbs will not expire! Once they’re granted to your account, you can hold onto them for as long as you like.

Q: Does the platform I subscribed to Nitro from matter?

A: Yes, the monthly Orbs drop feature is only available to Nitro members who subscribed through the desktop app, browser, or mobile web.

Q: What happens to my Orbs if I cancel my subscription?

A: You keep any Orbs you’ve already earned from previous months. After you cancel, you’ll stop receiving future Monthly Orbs drops.

Q: My payment failed—will I still get my Orbs?

A: If your payment failed, you will not receive your next Monthly Orbs drop. Learn more about Payments and Billings here.

Q: Are Monthly Orbs different from Discord Orbs?

A: No, Monthly Orbs and Discord Orbs are referring to the same virtual rewards that you can earn on Discord. You can use them in the Shop to get Nitro Credit or items from the main collections.

Q: Can I see which Orbs came from Monthly Orbs Drops vs. Quests?

A: Yes. To view your total Orbs balance, including Orbs from Monthly Orbs Drops and Quests, select the Clyde logo in the top left of your Discord app, go to the Shop tab, then select the Orbs logo in the top right. To see how many Orbs you received from monthly Monthly Orbs Drops specifically, check the Nitro Rewards section in your Viewing Your Nitro Orbs Drop.

Monthly Orbs balance

Nitro - Free Trial Offer FAQ

DISCORD AND ITS OFFICIAL STAFF WILL NEVER DIRECTLY MESSAGE YOU ANY OFFERS IN YOUR DMS. PLEASE BE CAUTIOUS OF DMS FROM STRANGERS AND BOTS OFFERING FREE NITRO.

The following FAQs are only applicable during the initial, trial period. After your trial period has ended and your subscription has begun, you can refer to our general Nitro and Boosting FAQs!

Canceling Nitro Subscription

Can I cancel during my free trial period?

Yes, you may cancel at any time before the end of your trial. When this occurs, you’ll finish out your trial period, and we will not charge you on the renewal date.

How do I cancel my trial?

If you’d like to cancel, open User Settings > select Subscriptions then Cancel next to your subscription.

I purchased Boosts during my free trial. What happens to them if I cancel my trial period?

Your additional purchased Boost subscriptions will still be active! Keep in mind that if you cancel your Nitro subscription, you’ll no longer receive a 30% discount on Boost purchases, and your current Boosts will renew for their full amount on their renewal date.

Check User Settings > Billing to see when your Boost subscriptions renew.

I bought additional Boosts during my trial period, but I don’t want them to renew. How do I cancel?

You can also cancel your Boost subscriptions under User Settings > Subscriptions.

Changing Nitro Subscriptions

Can I change my Nitro plan from Yearly to Monthly or vice-versa?

No, you may not make any Nitro plan changes during the free 30 days. You can upgrade or downgrade your Nitro subscription once the first 30 days are complete.

Nitro Credits FAQ

Nitro credits are an Orbs-exclusive item in the Shop that give you Nitro for a limited amount of time.

What this article covers:

  • What are Nitro Credits?
  • How do I earn Nitro Credits?
  • Where can I view my Nitro Credits?
  • How do I use Nitro Credits?
  • Managing Your Subscription with Active Nitro Credits
    • Nitro Subscription
    • Server Boost Subscription
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are Nitro Credits?

Nitro credits give you Nitro for a limited amount of time.

  • They are earned by purchasing in the Shop, or occasionally completing specific Quests.
  • The duration of each credit varies depending on the purchase credits and/or Quest.
  • Nitro credits do not expire and can stack if multiple Nitro credits are earned.
  • Nitro credits do not become a recurring subscription.
  • Once all your Nitro credits have been used and their duration is over, your Nitro subscription will revert to its normal state.
  • Some Nitro Perks are not available with Nitro credits. Perks that are not included:
    • Two Boosts
    • Boost discount
    • Profile badge
    • Share Nitro (Referral Program) Nitro credits do not give you 2 free Server Boosts or the 30% discount on additional Boost purchases. However, you can still enjoy all the other Nitro perks. To learn more about all Nitro perks, check out this article.

How do I obtain Nitro Credits?

Nitro credits can only be obtained on the Discord desktop app and browser app, but if you have active Nitro credits, you can enjoy your Nitro benefits on any device, including mobile.

You can claim Nitro credits in the Shop using Discord Orbs. Orbs are virtual rewards that you can earn by completing Quests.

Once you have earned Orbs, you can get Nitro credits in the Shop > Orbs Shop page.

Want to learn more?

Find out how to earn Discord Orbs here.

Claiming Nitro credit in Orbs Shop

Nitro credits are also occasionally offered as Quest rewards. For more details on accepting and completing Quests, check out our Discord Quests FAQ.

Where can I view my Nitro Credits?

To view your Nitro credits, go to your User Settings by selecting the cogwheel [] icon in the bottom-left corner of the app.

Cogwheel icon on desktop

Then, press Subscriptions. In the Nitro Credit section, you can see how many credits you’ve earned, check their expiration date, and verify if your credits are active.

Example of Nitro credits displayed in Subscriptions tab

How do I use Nitro Credits?

Once they are earned, Nitro credits activate automatically at different times depending on whether you have a pre-existing subscription or not.

  • If you have no Nitro subscription:
    • Credits activate instantly upon earning them.
  • If you have an active Nitro subscription:
    • Credits activate automatically at the end of your current billing cycle.

Managing Your Subscription with Active Nitro Credits

Nitro Subscription

If you have active Nitro credits and a Nitro subscription here’s what happens in different scenarios:

  • Starting a new Nitro subscription or upgrading: Your credits will pause and start again at the end of your billing cycle.
  • Downgrading or removing additional Boosts from Nitro: Any changes will take effect after your current credits expire.
  • Cancelling Nitro: Changes happen right away, but don’t worry - your active credits will still work.
Server Boost Subscription

If you have a Boost-only subscription, you can freely manage your Boosts, including cancelling your subscription, without any impact to your Nitro credits.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What happens to my Nitro subscription if I obtain Nitro credits?

A: Your Nitro subscription will continue until the end of your current billing cycle. Then, your Nitro credits will activate automatically. Once your Nitro credits have been fully used, your paid Nitro subscription will automatically renew again.

Q: I’m a current Nitro subscriber. What happens to my billing date if I obtain Nitro credits?

A: Your billing date will be adjusted based on how long your Nitro credits last.

Q: I have active Server Boosts with my current Nitro subscription. What happens to these Boosts if I activate my Nitro credits?

A: Your existing Server Boosts will remain active and unchanged. While Nitro credits are active, you’ll be able to transfer your Boosts between servers as long as it follows the normal cooldown periods. See our Server Boosting FAQ for more information.

Q: Can I purchase new Server Boosts when Nitro credits are active?

A: No, you won’t be able to purchase new Server Boosts when Nitro credits are active.

Q: Can I cancel any Server Boost subscriptions I have while Nitro credits are active?

A: No, you won’t be able to cancel any pre-existing Boost subscriptions until your Nitro credits have been completely used.

Q: What if I obtain Nitro credits while my subscription is past due?

A: If you obtain Nitro credits while your subscription is past due, they will be applied in one of two ways:

  • If no successful payment is made during the 30-day grace period, the credits will be applied after the grace period ends.
  • If a payment is successful, the credits will be applied at your next billing cycle. Q: Can I use my Nitro credits at any time?

A: No, Nitro credits automatically activate at different times depending on your subscription status:

  • If you’re a current subscriber: Nitro credits automatically apply at the end of your current billing cycle.
  • If you don’t have an active Nitro subscription: Your Nitro credits will be activated immediately upon getting them. Q: How do Nitro credits interact with subscription credits (gifts)?

A: The interaction between Nitro credits and subscription credits depends on your specific situation. Here are some common scenarios:

  1. Active gift credit, no stored credits: Nitro credits activate after the current gift period ends.

  2. Multiple stored gift credits with an active subscription: Nitro credits activate after the current billing period. Then, the next gift credit will be used to continue the subscription.

  3. Stored gift credits, no active subscription: Nitro credits activate immediately. Doesn’t affect existing gift credits.

How to Purchase a Nitro Gift in Discord

Discord Nitro gifts can be purchased within direct messages (DMs), group chats, server channels, and the Nitro page.

Gifts purchased within a DM on desktop or browser will allow you to customize your gift by selecting a card design, adding a personal note, a soundboard effect, and emoji confetti. You will not be able to customize your gift with these personal touches within group chats and server channels.

  1. To get started, open up the Discord app and head over to where you would like to send your gift.

  2. While there, select the gift icon to the right of the textbox.

  3. Once the Gift Nitro window appears, select the gift you would like to send and press Next when you’re ready to proceed.

Customizing your gift is currently only available within direct messages (DMs)
If your Discord account does not have a previously saved payment method, you will need to add your payment method details before proceeding.
  1. Afterwards, you will be able to review your gift and select Buy Gift to complete your purchase.

Note: Some Nitro gifts are available at localized prices. Depending on a user’s region, they may be able to pay for a gift in their local currency, but the price will still be equivalent to the USD price. You can learn more about localized pricing here.

If you have shared a gift within a group chat or server channel, anyone can claim it. If you would like to share the private gift link to a specific friend, send the link through a DM to the recipient.
Once a Nitro gift has been claimed by another user, the gift cannot be switched to another user account. Our support team is unable to issue a refund for a claimed Nitro gift. Our standard refund policy applies, but only for an unclaimed Nitro gift.
Note: Discord Nitro Basic will not be available for purchase through DMs, group chats, or server channels. To purchase a Discord Nitro Basic gift on desktop or browser, head over to the Nitro page by navigating to your direct messages and pressing the app icon in the upper left corner. You can also navigate to the Nitro page by heading into your User Settings > Nitro. On mobile, tap on your avatar to head into User Settings > Nitro Gifting.

Important: Bulk Gifting is currently an experiment on desktop and isn’t widely available yet. If you have access, select the gift icon to the right of the text bar in server channels, group chats, or the gifting option in the Nitro Home or the Billing page, then choose multiple friends to send Nitro gifts to at once. During this experiment, you may see one of the two experiences below.

Preset gift quantities with a custom amount option (Left) & a gift quantity stepper with the bulk gifting (Right)

Our standard refund policy applies. Learn more in our Refund Policy.

How to Send a Gifted Subscription

With a Gifted Subscription, you can send a friend a Nitro gift that renews automatically every month until you cancel. You pay for the first gift at checkout, and recurring charges begin only after your friend accepts it.

Important: Gifted Subscriptions are currently an experiment on desktop and are not widely available at this time.

  1. Open a DM with the friend you’d like to send a gift to.

  2. Select the gift icon to the right of the text bar.

  3. In the Gift Nitro window, choose the Nitro gift you’d like to send under Select gift.

  4. Then select Recurs monthly to make your gift recurring.

Example of the Recurring Gift Option in the Gift Nitro window

  1. Press Select to continue to checkout.

  2. Review your checkout details. The checkout screen shows that your gift renews monthly until you cancel.

  3. Follow the prompts to complete your purchase.

Your gift is sent to your friend in your DM, and you’ll receive an email confirming your purchase. Your friend has 5 days to accept it.

Note: Gifted Subscriptions can only be sent for Nitro through DMs on desktop. Each friend can have only one active Gifted Subscription at a time, from any sender, but you can send Gifted Subscriptions to multiple different friends.

If a gifting promotion is running, a Gifted Subscription is only eligible for one promotion redemption, even though the gift renews each month.

Accepting a Gifted Subscription

When a friend sends you a Gifted Subscription, it appears in your DM with them. Accept it within 5 days to start your Nitro perks. After that, you’ll automatically receive a new Nitro gift from your friend each month, with nothing else to do on your end.

If you already pay for Nitro yourself, each gift is added to your account as gift credit. When your subscription renews, your gift credit is used before your payment method is charged, starting with your oldest credit.

If your account can’t use the credit right away, such as when you subscribe to Nitro through the App Store or Google Play, your gift credits are saved to your account and stack month over month.

Important: If gift credit isn’t available when your own subscription renews, for example if the Gifted Subscription ends or arrives late, your saved payment method will be charged as usual.

If a Gifted Subscription Isn’t Accepted

If your friend declines a Gifted Subscription or doesn’t accept it within 5 days, the recurring gift won’t start and you won’t be charged again. The gift you already paid for is not automatically refunded. Instead, it goes back to User Settings > Gift Inventory as a one-time gift, where you can send it to your friend or anyone else. Sending it again from your Gift Inventory won’t start a new Gifted Subscription.

If you’d like to try again, you can send a new Gifted Subscription from your DM with that friend.

Canceling a Gifted Subscription

You can cancel a Gifted Subscription at any time. To cancel, go to the Subscriptions tab in your User Settings and select Cancel next to the gift under Gifted Subscriptions. If you received a Gifted Subscription, you can cancel it the same way you cancel any Nitro subscription. Canceling stops future gifts and charges, and your friend keeps Nitro until the end of the current gift period. Gifts that have already been redeemed are not refunded. A Gifted Subscription can also end automatically, for example if a renewal payment fails. To send a Gifted Subscription to a different friend, cancel your current one and start a new one from a DM with that friend.

Want to learn more?

For step-by-step instructions, see How to Cancel your Nitro Subscription.

Now you can apply the digital code through Discord to activate your subscription or send it to a lucky somebody as a gift!

Note: If you have any questions regarding your Nitro digital gift card purchase through Amazon, please be sure to reach out to Amazon support for further assistance.

Managing Your Nitro Gift

If you missed the shareable link for any reason, you can always access it at any time as long as the gift hasn’t been claimed already.

Head to User Settings > Gift Inventory you’ll see your unclaimed Nitro gift here. You’ll be able to revoke a Nitro gift link & generate a new one.

Please note, only unclaimed gifts will be listed here, any claimed gifts will no longer display in your inventory. If you are looking for your Account Credit, go to the Subscriptions tab in your User Settings.

If you sent a Gifted Subscription that wasn’t accepted within 5 days, the gift you purchased will appear in your Gift Inventory as a one-time gift. You can send it to anyone. Active Gifted Subscriptions also show their renewal dates here and in the Subscriptions tab of your User Settings. To cancel an active Gifted Subscription, see How to Cancel your Nitro Subscription.

Super important to note that once you share this link with another user, that user will be able to claim this gift of Nitro. When sharing a gift to someone else, we recommend sending it in a DM to ensure no one else can claim it!

Purchasing a Gift On Mobile

You can now customize your Nitro and Nitro Basic gift on iOS and Android devices in DMs, group chats, and channels!

  1. To get started, head over to a DM, group chat, or channel.

  2. Select the gifting [] icon located to the left of the text bar.

  3. Then, choose a plan you would like to send. You can also customize your gift by selecting a gift card style.

  4. If you are sending the gift through DMs, you can add a custom message and send the gift directly to the gift recipient once the purchase is complete.

Otherwise, a sharable link will be generated for you to share with others. You can also go to User Settings > Nitro Gifting and generate a new link if needed.

The refund policy also applies to both iOS and Android, once a gift of Nitro has been claimed by another user you (or this user) won’t be able to unclaim the gift. Our support team is unable to issue a refund for any claimed gifts. Our standard refund policy applies, if you are on iOS please reach out directly to Apple to request a refund. If you are on Android, please reach out to our billing team within 5 days of the initial purchase date to request a refund.

What are Nitro Rewards?

Important: Nitro Rewards are available to all eligible members. Perk availability varies by region. Nitro Basic and Nitro Classic members are not eligible.

Nitro Rewards is a benefits program included with your Nitro subscription at no additional cost. It gives members access to perks from partners that matter to people who play games.

Nitro Rewards will evolve and change over time. You can check your Nitro Home to see what’s currently available to you. As long as your Nitro subscription is active, you’ll have access to whatever perks are currently available in your rewards collection.

For a full list of the other perks you get with Nitro, check out What are Nitro & Nitro Basic? Article.

You can access Nitro Rewards through your Nitro Home tab in the Discord desktop app.

Nitro Home tab
Nitro Rewards Program Terms

Nitro Rewards is included with eligible paid Nitro subscriptions at no additional cost, giving you access to perks from partners we think you’ll actually use. The program is designed to grow and evolve — we’ll be updating the partners and offers over time, and what’s available may change.

Note: If you are an eligible Xbox Game Pass subscriber, you get access to 3 Discord Nitro perks at no extra cost. For more info, check out this Help Center article: Taste of Nitro for Xbox Game Pass Subscribers.

Individual perks have their own eligibility conditions, redemption requirements, and availability limitations, which you’ll find described in connection with each perk. Not all perks are available in all regions or to all subscription types. Nitro Basic and Nitro Classic members are not eligible for Nitro Rewards.

Perks provided through Nitro Rewards are supplementary to your core Nitro benefits and are offered in partnership with third parties. Discord isn’t responsible for third-party products or services accessed through the program, and the third parties may impose their own terms, restrictions, and limitations.

Access to Nitro Rewards perks requires an active Nitro subscription. Some perks, once claimed, may remain valid after your subscription ends per the terms applicable to that perk.

Xbox Game Pass

Take your gaming further with Xbox Game Pass, included with your Nitro subscription. Whether you’re looking for something new to play or want to stream your existing Xbox library, this benefit puts more gaming within reach — no extra subscription needed.

Your Nitro subscription includes:

  • 50+ games like Stardew Valley, DayZ, and Fallout 4
  • 10 hours of cloud gaming each month
  • Play and earn up to $25 a year in the Store with Rewards This benefit is available to active Nitro subscribers in eligible regions that do not have an existing Xbox Game Pass subscription.

Eligibility Requirements

You are eligible if:

  • You have an active Discord Nitro subscription (through a paid subscription, Nitro gift, and some Nitro trials, with exceptions noted below)

  • You are not an existing Xbox Game Pass subscriber

  • You are located in an eligible region (see below) You are not eligible if:

  • Using Nitro Credits without a Nitro subscription.

  • You are a Nitro Classic or Nitro Basic member

  • Your Nitro subscription came from a third-party inbound promotion (for example, a 1-month Nitro trial from an external partner) or a large-scale campaign trial (for example, an annual Nitro trial offered to all users) Eligible regions for Xbox Game Pass (Starter Edition): Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Hungary, India, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovakia, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom, United States

How it Works

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Are Nitro Rewards available in my country?

A: Availability varies by perk. If a perk has regional requirements, you’ll find them in that perk’s Eligibility Requirements section above. Some perks list their eligible regions directly, while others are available wherever the partner offers or ships its products. For those perks, check the partner’s website to confirm availability in your region. If you don’t see a specific Nitro Reward in your Nitro Home, that perk may not be available in your region.

Q: Do Nitro Rewards cost extra?

A: No. Nitro Rewards are included with your Nitro subscription at no additional cost. Your subscription price stays the same.

Q: What happens to my Nitro Rewards if I cancel Nitro?

A: You’ll lose access to all Nitro Rewards perks when your subscription ends. Any active partner benefits like Xbox Game Pass will also end.

Q: Do I need an existing Xbox or Microsoft account to use this benefit?

A: Yes, you’ll need a Microsoft account to redeem and access Xbox Game Pass (Starter Edition). If you don’t have one, you can create one for free at microsoft.com.

Q: What happens to my Xbox Game Pass (Starter Edition) access if I cancel my Nitro subscription?

A: Your access to Xbox Game Pass (Starter Edition) is tied to your active Nitro subscription. If you cancel, you will automatically lose access to this benefit at the end of your current billing period.

Q: Does this benefit stack with an existing Xbox Game Pass subscription?

A: Xbox Game Pass Starter Edition is intended for Nitro members who do not already have an active Xbox Game Pass subscription. If you already subscribe to Xbox Game Pass, this benefit is not be applicable.

Q: What counts toward my 10 hours of cloud gaming per month?

A: Cloud gaming hours are counted from the time you begin streaming a session. Hours reset at the beginning of each calendar month.

Q. Can I play my own games with the 10 hours of cloud gaming?

A: Yes, if a game is cloud playable and you own it digitally with Xbox, you can stream it using your 10 hours of cloud gaming each month.

Q. Can I play from the library of 50+ games on my devices without using my 10 hours of cloud gaming?

A: Yes, you can download and play games on PC, Xbox console, and supported handhelds without impacting your 10 hour cloud gaming limit.

Q: Why does my benefit show as “unavailable”?

A: If you’re seeing “Unavailable,” there may be a temporary issue generating access. No action is needed on your end — check back later to claim your benefit.

Q: I think I found a bug. How do I report it?

A: If you’re experiencing technical issues or suspect you’ve encountered a bug, please reach out to Discord Support for help. We can investigate and assist you further.

Q: What happens to my discount code if I cancel my Nitro subscription?

A: Any codes you’ve already claimed will remain valid until their expiration date, but you won’t receive new codes unless you resubscribe to Nitro.

Q: Can I use my Best Buy code if I already have a My Best Buy Plus or My Best Buy Total membership?

A: This offer is only available to Nitro members who are not currently a My Best Buy Plus member.

Q: When do the discount codes expire?

A: It depends on the type of code. Monthly codes are valid through the end of the current month. One-time codes (such as for Logitech’s new products and the Pro Series sim line) do not expire and can be redeemed at any time.

Your YouTube Premium code is a one-time code and must be redeemed by December 31, 2027.

Your Best Buy code is a one-time code and must be redeemed by November 19, 2026.

Your Call of Duty blueprint code must be redeemed by August 6, 2027.

Q: Are there any restrictions on the products I can purchase with the discount?

A: Yes, see above for individual product restrictions for each partner discount.

Q: Is there a limit to how many times I can use my discount code?

A: Each discount code can be used once, and you can only use one code per transaction on each website. However, you’ll receive a new code each month your Nitro subscription is active.

Q: When exactly do new codes become available?

A: New discount codes become available at the beginning of each calendar month for active Nitro members.

Q: Can I use my code on any device?

A: Yes! Once you receive your code through the Discord desktop app, you can copy it and redeem it at the appropriate webstore on any device of your choice.

Q: Why does my discount code show as “unavailable”?

A: If you’re seeing “Unavailable”, that means there are issues generating discount codes. No action is needed on your end. Check back later to claim your code!
