Nitro Squad Experiment FAQ

Nitro Squad is a Discord Nitro plan that allows a user to purchase a plan to share Nitro with 5 of their friends.

What this article covers:

  • What is Nitro Squad?
    • Nitro Squad Perks
  • Who is eligible for the Nitro Squad Beta?
    • Additional Eligibility Guidelines
  • How do I create a Nitro Squad plan?
  • How do I join a Nitro Squad plan?
  • Managing Your Nitro Squad and Subscriptions
    • As a Plan Owner
    • As a Plan Member
  • Frequently Asked Questions Important: Nitro Squad is currently in Beta and only available to desktop users in Australia and France.

What is Nitro Squad?

Nitro Squad is a monthly subscription that provides Nitro memberships for up to 6 accounts under one plan. Each Nitro Squad includes 1 plan owner and up to 5 plan members.

Nitro Squad Perks
  • Plan Owners: All Nitro perks
  • Plan Members: All Nitro perks EXCEPT Server Boosting perks Important: Plan members cannot purchase Server Boosts while on a Nitro Squad plan.

Who is eligible for the Nitro Squad Beta?

To purchase or be added to a Nitro Squad plan, plan owners and members must meet the following conditions:

  • All plan members, including the owner, must be located in the same country.
  • Cannot have an annual Nitro subscription
  • Cannot have a pre-existing subscription from a mobile app store
  • Cannot have an active Gift subscription or active Nitro Credits
  • Can only be in one Nitro Squad every 12 months, starting from the day you create or join a Nitro Squad.
Additional Eligibility Guidelines

If you have a separate Server Boost subscription

  • You can create a Nitro Squad.
  • You can’t join a Nitro Squad while your Server Boost subscription is active.
  • To join, you’ll need to cancel your Server Boost subscription first. If you have Nitro Credits

Active Nitro Credits

  • You can’t join a Nitro Squad until your active Nitro Credits are fully used. Inactive Nitro Credits

  • You can join a Nitro Squad.

  • Your Nitro Credits will be saved and will be used after you leave the Nitro Squad. Both Nitro plan owners and members cannot purchase Nitro Credits in the Shop while on a group plan.

How do I create a Nitro Squad plan?

  1. Press on the Discord icon in the upper left corner of the Discord app, then navigate to the Nitro tab.

  2. Press Subscribe at the top, or locate the Nitro Squad card farther down the page

If you’re an existing Nitro subscriber, you can upgrade to a Nitro Squad plan by locating Switch Plans in Subscription Settings under User Settings.

  1. Follow sign up steps.

Tip: If you’re the plan owner and you’re upgrading from an existing Nitro subscription, you’ll receive proration for your remaining subscription time.

Note: If you’re on a free Nitro trial, you’ll need to wait until it ends before upgrading to a Nitro Squad plan as a plan owner.

How do I join a Nitro Squad plan?

  1. You will receive an invite to join a Nitro Squad in your direct message (DM) with the Nitro Squad plan owner.

  2. Press the See Invite button to begin the process of joining a Nitro Squad and to determine whether your account is eligible to join a Nitro Squad.

Important: When you accept an invitation to join a Nitro Squad plan, you immediately forfeit any remaining time on your individual Nitro subscription. You will not receive a proration or refund.

Managing Your Nitro Squad and Subscriptions

As a Plan Owner

Plan owners of a Nitro Squad can manage their subscription and perform the actions below in the Subscriptions Settings page under User Settings.

Inviting Members:

  • You can invite up to 5 members

  • Members don’t need to be on your friends list

  • Invitations do not automatically expire. You’ll need to cancel the invite if you want to send it to someone else by selecting Cancel Invite when hovering over someone’s name.

  • You cannot send more invitations than available slots Removing Members:

  • You can remove members at any time by hovering over someone’s name in Subscription Settings

  • When removed, members lose access immediately to all perks except their Nitro Badge, which will remain available for a 7-day grace period. Removed members can re-subscribe to Nitro during the 7-day grace period to maintain their current Nitro Badge level. Other:

  • You can cancel your Nitro Squad subscription at any time

  • If you want to downgrade to another Nitro plan, you must first cancel your Nitro Squad subscription. If you cancel your Nitro Squad subscription, you must resubscribe to Nitro or a Nitro Squad to maintain your current Nitro Badge level.

  • You will receive proration credit when upgrading your existing Nitro, Basic, or Classic individual plan to Nitro Squad if applicable

As a Plan Member

As a Nitro Squad plan member, you don’t need to manage the group plan. This section covers what to know when joining or leaving a Nitro Squad, along with a few limitations for members.

Joining a Nitro Squad:

  • You do not need to be Discord Friends with the Nitro Squad plan owner to be invited to their Nitro Squad

  • You will immediately forfeit all remaining subscription time if you have an existing Nitro, Basic, or Classic individual plan or free trial when you join a Nitro Squad as a member. You do not receive proration credit or refunds.

  • If you have an existing Nitro plan with utilized Server Boosts and you join a Nitro Squad, you will not be able to keep your Server Boosts from your original plan

  • After joining a plan, you will not be able to purchase a separate Server Boost subscription. Leaving a Nitro Squad:

  • You can remove yourself from a plan at any time

  • You lose access to Nitro immediately upon leaving

  • Your 12 month window must finish before joining another group plan, including the one you just left Important: During this Beta, we do not support downgrading from Nitro Squad to an individual Nitro plan. To switch, the plan members must leave the plan and the plan owner must cancel their Nitro Squad plan, then subscribe to an individual plan.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How does badge progression work?

A: Each member gets their own badge streak, starting when they create or join the plan:

  • Nitro Badge: 7-day grace period when entering and exiting the plan to maintain streaks
  • Server Boost Badge: 3-day grace period
  • Plan owners who upgrade and members who join an existing plan keep their streak if they already have a Nitro subscription. Q: Who can purchase additional Server Boosts?

A: Plan members cannot purchase additional Boosts. Plan owners can purchase additional Boosts at the discounted rate.

Q: What happens if I’m removed from a plan unexpectedly?

A: We’ll send you an email to let you know. Your access to Nitro perks ends immediately, except for your Nitro Badge which follows a 7-day grace period. You must also wait for the end of your 12 month cooldowns before joining any other Nitro Squad plan.

Q: When does the 12 month eligibility period begin?

A: The 12 month period begins when you create or join a Nitro Squad.

Q: Can I rejoin the same Nitro Squad plan if I leave?

A: No. Once you leave, you cannot rejoin it. You must also wait for the end of your 12 month cooldown before joining any other Nitro Squad plan.

Q: What happens to my existing Nitro subscription if I join a Nitro Squad plan?

A: You will immediately forfeit any remaining time on your individual subscription with no proration or refund. Make sure you’re ready to switch before accepting an invitation.

Q: What happens if the plan owner’s account is banned?

A: It depends on the type of ban:

  • Limited Access or Temporary bans: No impact on the plan or members
  • Permanent ban: No change until the next renewal date, then the plan auto-cancels. All members will receive email notification when the subscription is cancelled Q: What happens if my account as a member is banned?

A: It also depends on the type of ban:

  • Limited Access or Temporary ban: No impact on your membership
  • Permanent ban: You are automatically removed from the group immediately and the plan owner will receive an email notification Q: What happens if a plan owner or plan member blocks each other?

A: If either the plan owner or the plan member blocks the other, the member will be removed from the plan. This applies whether the owner blocks the member or the member blocks the owner.

Q: Can I have a Nitro Squad membership and a Server Boost subscription at the same time?

A: Only if you are the plan owner. Plan members cannot have additional Server Boost subscriptions while on a Nitro Squad plan.

Q: What if I’m locked out of my account and can’t leave/end a plan?

A: Please reach out to our Support team through our support form here.

Q: I’m a current subscriber with an existing offer. Can I still join Nitro Squad?

A: Yes, you can have an existing subscription from one of our Nitro promotions and still be eligible for Nitro Squad.

Q: Will my billing date change if I upgrade to Nitro Squad?

A: Yes, your billing date will be adjusted based on when you create or join the Nitro Squad plan.

Q: I can’t find the plan invite - where is it?

A: Your Nitro Squad invite can be found in your direct message from the person who manages the plan. If you can’t find it, it might be because you’ve never DM’d the person before. Check Message Requests tab under Direct Messages

Redeeming Codes

Got your hands on a fancy code? Find your way to the Gift Inventory section located in User Settings to obtain your gift via redeem codes. Here is where you’ll be prompted to enter in a 19 character long code.

Share Nitro

As someone who enjoys Nitro, do you ever wish you could share the fun and joy of your favorite perks with friends?

As part of their membership, Nitro members can share up to three friend passes (2-week trials of Nitro) with their friends! Sharing Nitro with friends can be a fun way to discover how they might style their profile and which custom emojis become their favorite to use in daily conversations.

Some members may also earn a reward when a friend they’ve shared a trial with subscribes.

What this article covers:

  • Share Nitro Eligibility
    • Nitro Members Sharing a Trial
    • Friends Receiving a Trial

  • Earning a Reward When Your Friend Subscribes
    • Reward Types
    • When You Get Your Reward
    • If You Cancel Nitro
  • Receiving a Nitro Trial from Someone
    • How to Redeem your 2-week Trial
  • Share Nitro On Mobile
    • Sending Trials
    • Receiving a Trial
  • Frequently Asked Questions
    • Eligibility & Access
    • Sending Trials

Share Nitro Eligibility

Nitro Members Sharing a Trial

Only eligible Nitro members (either monthly or yearly), will be able to see the Share Nitro trial option.

You will not be eligible to send a Nitro trial if:

  • You are a Nitro Classic or Nitro Basic member.
  • You are on another trial or discounted offer plan.
Friends Receiving a Trial

Users who appear in the Select Friends modal are eligible to receive a Nitro trial from you.

If a specific person does not appear in the Select Friends modal, it means the person you’re trying to share a trial with is ineligible to receive a trial. Being ineligible for a trial could occur for several reasons, including having a Nitro membership in the last 30 days, accepting another trial offer, and more.

If you can’t find the specific person you’re looking for, you’ll need to share the trial with another person, or try again later.

How to Share a Nitro Trial with your Friends

As a Nitro member, follow these steps:

  1. On the desktop or browser app, press the Direct Messages button in the top left corner and then select the Nitro tab. Alternatively, you can navigate to your User Settings > Nitro.
Direct Messages Button and Nitro Tab on Desktop
  1. After navigating to the Nitro homepage, you’ll see the Share Nitro banner. Pressing the Select Friends button on this banner will open the Select Friends window.
Select Friends Button in Share Nitro Banner
  1. While here, you can choose the friends to whom you wish to send a Nitro Trial. When you’re ready, select Share Trial to confirm.
Select Friends Window Selection

Once completed, a confirmation should appear. You will also be able to view the shared trial in the direct message (DM) that was sent to your friend.

Shared Trial Confirmation

Note: As an eligible Nitro member, you get 3 Nitro trials to start, with more coming in the future. A trial will expire if not redeemed by the recipient in 10 days, but you’ll get the trial back.

Earning a Reward When Your Friend Subscribes

Note:

  • This is a limited time experiment for a sample of Nitro subscribers. Not all Discord users will have access to this experiment.

  • The reward type you see and the exact amount cannot be manually chosen.

Some Nitro members may see a reward option when they share Nitro trials with friends. If you’re part of this experiment, you’ll see it called out directly on the Share Nitro banner, including what your reward is and how to earn it.

Reward Types

If you are eligible, you will see different promotions in your Nitro banner. Promotions change from time to time, but may include:

  • Orbs: you can earn up to 15,000 Orbs from your 3 available Share Nitro trials. Each friend who becomes a paid Nitro subscriber after starting a trial you shared earns you 5,000 Orbs.
  • A 30% discount on your Nitro subscription: you can earn 30% off your Nitro subscription for up to 3 consecutive months. Each friend who becomes a paid subscriber after starting a trial you shared earns you 1 discounted month.
When You Get Your Reward

Your reward will be delivered 5 business days after your friend’s subscription starts.

You can check your Share Nitro banner in Nitro Home to track your progress on the rewards you’ve earned.

If You Cancel Nitro
  • If you’re earning Orbs, they’re yours to keep and don’t expire, even if you later cancel your Nitro subscription.
  • If you’re earning a subscription discount, and you cancel before the discounted month arrives, you’ll lose that pending discount.

Receiving a Nitro Trial from Someone

If someone generously shares a Nitro trial with you, you’ll see the trial in the form of an embedded message in your DMs with the sharer. You’ll have up to 10 days to redeem the trial before it expires.

How to Redeem your 2-week Trial
  1. Make sure the offer is authentic
  • Confirm the sharer is a Nitro member - only Nitro members can share trials with you.
  • Confirm the trial offer from the sharer looks like this in your DMs with them:
Example of Nitro 2-week Trial in DM

Important: This is NOT a link, file, image attachment, program, nor a QR code! Redeeming the trial is completed entirely within the Discord app.

  1. Select Start Trial.

  2. Select a plan to start once your 2-week trial is over.

Cancel anytime during your trial to avoid being charged after your trial period in User Settings > Subscriptions. Frequently Asked Questions

This FAQ is divided into sections:

  • Eligibility & Access
  • Sending Trials
  • Receiving Trials
  • Rewards
Eligibility & Access

Q: As a Nitro member, who can I share Nitro trials with?

A: As a Nitro member, you can share Nitro trials with any eligible friend. If a friend appears in the Select Friends list in the Share Nitro experience, they are eligible to receive and redeem a Nitro trial from you.

Q: I just subscribed to Nitro but don’t seem to be able to share Nitro trials with others - why?

A: Share Nitro is only available to a limited number of users.

For those who have access, you must be a paying Nitro member for at least 5 days to see the Share Nitro banner and share trials with others. If you’re a new Nitro member, you’ll be able to share Nitro trials with others after 5 days.

Additionally, you may not see it due to the eligibility criteria for Nitro members.

Sending Trials

Q: What happens after I share all 3 of my trials?

A: We hope to provide more sharing opportunities in the future. Keep an eye on the Share Nitro banner in Direct Messages > Nitro for when you get a refresh!

Q: As a Nitro member, do my trials expire?

A: No, your trials will not expire so long as you have an active Nitro membership. Once a trial is redeemed by a friend, you won’t be able to share another until you get more - or you have some left over that were not previously redeemed.

Q: As a trial recipient, will I be charged for redeeming a gifted trial?

A: You will not be charged for redeeming a shared trial. However, once your trial period ends, you will be charged for the plan that you signed up for during the Start Trial process.

If you don’t cancel during your 2-week trial, you will automatically be charged the price associated with your selected plan after your trial ends. Cancel anytime during your trial to avoid being charged after your trial period in User Settings > Subscriptions > Cancel.

Q: What devices is this available on?

A: Share Nitro is only available on the desktop app and browser.

The reward described in Earning a Reward When Your Friend Subscribes is desktop-only as well.

Receiving Trials

Q: Is there a way to revoke or decline a shared trial?

A: There isn’t a way to revoke or decline a shared trial, so if you’re sharing a trial with a friend, double check to make sure it’s the right person!

Q: What happens if someone doesn’t redeem the Nitro trial I shared with them?

A: Recipients have up to 10 days to redeem their trial. If the recipient doesn’t redeem your Nitro trial by that time, the trial will be sent back to you automatically.

Q: How will I know if the trial I’m receiving is legit and not a scam?

A: If someone is sharing a Nitro trial with you, it must appear as such in your direct messages with them:

Important: This is NOT a link, file, image attachment, program, nor a QR code!

Beware of bad actors asking you to redeem a Nitro trial by pressing a suspicious scam link, downloading a program, or scanning QR codes. Don’t click or press on anything suspicious that takes you out of the Discord app. Learn more about common scams and what to look out for.

Q: How can I tell if my friend passes are redeemed?

A: You can refer to the circles in the Share Nitro banner on your Nitro Home tab. When a friend pass is redeemed, the outer circle will fill in with color. If one of your friends becomes a paying member, their circle will glow brighter like the image below.

Line 1: A friend pass has been shared, but not redeemed.
Line 2: A friend pass has been successfully redeemed.
Line 3: Two friend passes have been redeemed, and one friend has signed up for Nitro.
Rewards

Q: I don’t see a reward option on my Share Nitro banner. Why not?

A: The reward is part of a limited-time test and isn’t available to all Nitro members yet. If you don’t see it, it hasn’t reached your account yet, and there’s nothing wrong on your end.

Q: Do I need to do anything to claim my reward?

A: No. Once your friend becomes a paid subscriber, your reward is applied automatically.

Q: Does my friend get a reward too?

A: Their free 2-week trial is their reward for accepting your Share Nitro invite. There’s no separate reward for them beyond the trial itself.

Taste of Nitro for Xbox Game Pass Subscribers

Available Nitro Perks

Active Game Pass subscribers who have linked their Discord account to their Game Pass account will receive these three Nitro perks every month:

  • Quest Orbs Multiplier: Earn Orbs faster when you complete Discord Quests. Starting May 8, 2026, your Quest rewards get a 1.2x boost automatically.
  • Monthly Orbs Drop: Get 250 Orbs every month. No action needed, the extra Orbs will automatically show up in your total Orbs balance of eligible accounts.
  • Shop Discount: Enjoy the same discount on Discord Shop purchases that Nitro Standard subscribers get.
Xbox Connection in the Discord app

Important: Your Discord account must be claimed to receive Xbox Game Pass Nitro perks. To claim your account, you need to add a valid email address. To do this, head to User Settings and select Claim Your Account.

To start receiving your Game Pass perks on Discord, you’ll need to link your Xbox account to your Discord account.

Desktop/Browser

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is this benefit for Game Pass subscribers available in my country/region?

A: Nitro is available globally, with the exception of the following regions: Syria, Ukraine, Russia, Iran, China, and North Korea. If you’re located in one of these regions, you won’t be able to use the Nitro benefit with Game Pass. For info on Xbox Game Pass markets, see: xbox.com/regions

Q: Which Game Pass plans are eligible?

A: All Xbox Game Pass plans are eligible. Whether you’re on Game Pass Essential, Premium, or Ultimate, you’ll receive the same set of Discord Nitro perks.

Q: Do I need a Nitro subscription to get these perks?

A: No. These perks are included with your Game Pass subscription and don’t require a Nitro membership. If you’re curious about what else Nitro offers beyond these perks, you can check out the full list of Nitro benefits in our What are Nitro & Nitro Basic? Help Center article.

Q: I already have Nitro. Can I still claim these perks?

A: If you already have an active Nitro subscription, you’re already receiving these perks (and more) through Nitro! This benefit is designed for users who don’t currently have an active Nitro subscription.

Q: How do I get my monthly Orbs drop?

A: Your 250 Orbs are deposited automatically each month to eligible accounts if your Xbox and Discord accounts remain linked and your Game Pass subscription is active. Once you subscribe to Nitro, you will receive your next monthly Orbs drop 7 days after your subscription begins.

Q: When will my first monthly Orbs drop occur?

A: If you have Xbox Game Pass and connected your account to Discord before May 27, 2026, your first Orbs drop will arrive sometime within 30 days of May 27. If you connect your Xbox Game Pass account to Discord after May 27, 2026, your first Orbs drop will arrive within a week of connecting.

Q: How can I see when I get my next monthly Orbs Drop?

A: Head to Settings > Connections, go to your Xbox connected account section, and select “Learn more” in the banner. A modal will pop up that shows how many more days until your next monthly Orbs Drop.

Learn more option under Xbox Game Pass

Q: Will my Quest multiplier stack with other bonuses?

A: The 1.2x Orb Quest multiplier applies to your Quest rewards for Quests after May 8, 2026 automatically. If you subscribe to Nitro at a later time, you will receive this perk through your Nitro tier benefits instead. If you have Nitro and Xbox Game Pass, the multiplier will not stack.

Q: What happens if my Game Pass subscription ends?

A: If your Game Pass subscription lapses or you unlink your accounts, your perks will deactivate. Any Orbs you’ve already earned will remain in your account.

Q: I linked my accounts but don’t see my perks. What should I do?

A: Make sure your Game Pass subscription is active and that your accounts are fully linked in Discord’s User Settings > Connections. If everything looks correct and your perks still haven’t appeared, try unlinking and re-linking your Xbox account. If the issue persists, reach out to our Support team through dis.gd/contact

Frequently Asked Questions

This FAQ is divided into sections:

All Nitro Subscription Types

The FAQs in this section refer to Nitro, Nitro Basic, and Nitro Classic unless stated otherwise.

Q: How do I cancel or switch my Nitro plan?

A: On desktop or browser, navigate to your User Settings and select the Subscribe tab, then choose Switch Plans or Cancel in the upper-right corner of the subscription banner. Learn more about canceling your subscription in our How to Cancel Nitro Subscription article.

Q: Why is my price for Nitro different from my friends?

A: Discord regularly reviews and updates prices based on factors like your location, local market conditions, currency exchange rates, and regional operating costs. We also test different pricing approaches to better understand what works best for our community.

If your subscription price changes, we’ll always notify you in advance so you know what to expect and can manage your subscription before any new prices take effect.

Q: Can I gift Nitro or Nitro Basic to a friend?

A: Yes! Check out this support article on how to gift Discord Nitro to a friend.

Q: Do you offer Nitro and Nitro Basic in my local currency?

A: We are always considering opportunities to expand the availability of accepted currencies for Nitro and Nitro Basic. Check this article for information on localized pricing.

Q: Can I use a Discord gift card to purchase Nitro or Nitro Basic?

A: Yes! You can use your Discord gift card balance to purchase Nitro and Nitro Basic. Learn more about gift cards, or redeem a gift card here.

Nitro

Q: My Nitro subscription comes with 2 Server Boosts. What are those?

A: Server Boosts are a way to show support for your favorite communities. Each Boost that you give to a server helps collectively unlock perks for everyone in the server to enjoy. You can learn more about Server Boosting here!

Q: I’m having issues with my payment method when I try to buy a Nitro or Nitro Basic subscription.

A: If you’re having trouble with your payment method or if you have any questions about how Discord billing works, you can check out this article here.

Q: Why do I need Nitro to upload more than 10MB of files?

A: Every day, millions of files are uploaded to Discord and stored securely for your future access. Storage management is expensive, so we regularly review how people use Discord and their storage needs. In fact, our data shows that most users stick to files smaller than 10MB.

In order to maintain our service without compromising on quality of storage, we decided to reduce the free file size upload limit. Unlike other platforms, we store your files for as long as you need them, so it’s crucial that we manage our storage sustainably. If you need more upload capacity, Nitro Basic offers a 50MB limit, and Nitro gives you up to 1GB, so you have options that fit your needs.

Nitro Classic

Q: I have a Nitro Classic subscription, but I no longer see Nitro Classic in the UI. Can I still subscribe to Nitro Classic?

A: If you have an active Nitro Classic subscription, you can keep your current plan. Please note that if you cancel your subscription, you will not be able to re-subscribe to Classic.

Q: I have Nitro Classic credits in my account but I don’t know what Nitro Classic gives me.

A: Nitro Classic unlocks the following perks on your account:

  • Profile customization: animated avatar, Nitro badge.
  • 30% off Boost purchases
  • Use custom and animated emojis anywhere
  • Unlimited Super Reactions
  • Bigger file uploads (50MB)
  • Screen share up to 1080p/60fps Q: I have Nitro Classic credits, how can I use them?

A: Please keep in mind that you cannot follow these steps if you already have an active Nitro or Nitro Basic subscription. You will need to wait until your current subscription ends in order to use your Nitro Classic credits. You can cancel your current subscription under User Settings > Subscriptions. When your subscription ends, follow these steps:

  • On the desktop or web client (this is not available on mobile), go to User Settings > Subscriptions.
  • On the bottom of the page, you should see a banner for Nitro Classic. Select the“Subscribe” button.
  • After completing the process to begin your Nitro Classic subscription, your subscription should automatically begin using your existing credit. Check out this support article for general information on subscription credits!

Q: I don’t have a Nitro subscription and I want to purchase Classic.

A: At this moment, you can only subscribe to Nitro and Nitro Basic. Nitro Classic is not available for purchase.

Notifications

iOS Provisional Push Notifications

What is a Provisional Push Notification?

Provisional Push Notifications are a type of notification where apps can silently push notifications to users (without sound or banner). They show up in the notification center.

Example provisional push notification
Note:
- Only users that have opted into Discord notifications or have not opted out can see a provisional notification from us.
- Some opt-in users can choose to turn their direct push notifications into silent provisional ones via iOS’ notification center settings.
What do we mean by not opted out?

During the iOS onboarding process, you may have selected “Maybe Later” and so are in a middle state of neither opt-in nor opt-out when it comes to notifications from Discord.

Learn more about iOS notifications here.

Mobile Notifications Settings 101

Discord’s Android and iOS apps each have their own notification settings, separate from the desktop app. This article covers how to manage both global and server-specific notifications on each platform.

What this article covers:

  • In-App Notifications Settings
  • Android
    • App Notification Settings
  • iOS
    • App Notification Settings
  • Server-Specific Notification Settings
    • Mute Server
    • Server Notification Settings
    • Notification Overrides Note: Regardless of the settings below, you won’t receive notifications while the Discord app is open and in focus on your device.

In-App Notifications Settings

Discord’s in-app Notification Settings screen controls whether Discord sends you a notification at all. Once Discord decides to notify you, your device’s OS-level settings (covered separately below for Android and iOS) control how that notification actually appears on your phone, whether as a banner, sound, badge, and so on.

You can reach this screen two different ways:

Notifications Page

  1. Tap the Notifications icon to the right of your profile.

  2. Tap the ellipsis in the top-right corner of Notifications and select Notification Settings.

Accessing Notification Settings from the Notifications page
Settings Menu

  1. Tap your profile icon in the bottom-left corner of the app.

  2. Select the Settings icon on your profile card.

  3. Under App Settings, select Notifications.

Accessing Notification Settings from the Settings menu

Here you can:

  • Toggle In-app notification to get notifications within Discord.

  • Select System notification to manage notifications outside of Discord.

  • Choose how Reaction Notifications work: All Messages, Only Direct Messages, or Never.

  • Select Community Activity Alerts or Highlight Notifications to manage other notification types.

  • Toggle Integrate calls with Phone app.

  • Toggle Voice Activity Notifications to get notified when your friends start streaming.

  • Toggle Friends Online Status Notifications to get notified when friends come online.

  • Toggle Friend Gaming Activity to get notified about games your friends are playing.

  • Toggle Profile Updates to get notified when friends update their profile. Tip (Android): When someone sends you several messages in a row, Discord always groups them into one tidy notification so your phone doesn’t get cluttered. The Notify on every new message in conversations toggle helps decide how many of those messages actually get your attention:

  • On: every new message in that conversation gives you a buzz, ping, or lights up your screen.

  • Off: only the first message does that. The rest still show up in the notification, just quietly.

Notify on every new message in conversations on Android

Tip (iOS): Turn on Integrate calls with Phone app and incoming Discord calls will look and act like a regular phone call. They’ll show up on your iPhone’s native call screen and in your Phone app’s recent calls list, instead of only appearing inside Discord.

Integrate calls with Phone app on iOS

Android

App Notifications Settings

This menu controls which activity sends you a notification, like new messages or a friend going live. Similar to iOS, Android manages these settings through your device’s settings rather than from within Discord.

  1. Open your device’s Settings app and tap Notifications.

  2. Tap App notifications.

  3. Tap Discord from your list of apps.

This opens the Discord notification settings screen, where you can manage global notification behavior for the app.

  • All Discord notifications: This acts as your master notification control. Disabling it means Discord won’t send any push or banner notifications when you receive activity.
  • Notification organizer: When enabled, Android automatically bundles and silences lower-priority Discord notifications.
Discord Notification Settings on Android

Notification Categories

Tap a category to expand it and view or adjust the individual notification types inside. Each category also has an All [category] notifications toggle that turns every notification type within it on or off at once.

  • Real-time: Notifications for live activity.
    • Voice connected: Notifies you when you connect to a voice channel.
  • Server: Notifications from your servers.
    • Forum notifications: Notifies you about new posts in forum channels.
    • Messages: Notifies you about new messages in your servers.
  • Social: Notifications for your friends and direct interactions.
    • Direct messages: Notifies you about new DMs.
    • Friend requests: Notifies you about new friend requests.
    • Reaction Notifications: Notifies you when someone reacts to your messages.
    • Friend Activity: Notifies you about your friends’ activity, like the games they’re playing. Tap Show unused categories to reveal additional notification types that aren’t currently active.
Notification Categories on Android

App Settings

  • Allow full-screen notifications: Allows Discord notifications to take up the full screen when your device is locked.
  • Allow notification dot: Adds a dot to the Discord app icon when you have unread notifications.
App Settings on Android

iOS

App Notification Settings

Unlike Android, the iOS app doesn’t have a global notifications menu within Discord. App-wide notification settings are managed through your device’s settings: open Settings > Notifications > Discord.

All Notifications

Similar to Android, this acts as your master notification control. Disabling it means Discord won’t send any push or banner notifications when you receive a message.

All Notifications toggle on iOS

Device Notification Settings

  • Alerts: Choose whether notifications appear on the lock screen, in Notification Center, and as banners. Check or uncheck each option to enable or disable it individually.
  • Banner Style: Choose between Temporary (default) or Persistent. Temporary banners appear briefly and then disappear, while Persistent banners stay on screen until you dismiss or tap them.
  • Sounds: Controls whether Discord notifications play an audible sound when received.
  • Badges: Enabling this option adds a red notification indicator over the Discord app icon when you receive notifications or specific mentions (@mentions or DMs).
  • Announce Notifications: Siri reads Discord notifications aloud.
  • Show Previews: Choose Always, When Unlocked (default), or Never to control how notifications appear on your lock screen.
  • Notifications Grouping: Choose Automatic, By App, or Off to control how your Discord notifications are grouped.
Device Notification Settings on iOS

Server-Specific Notification Settings

Note: This works the same way on both platforms.

In addition to your global settings, Discord lets you customize notification settings for each individual server.

  1. To access server-specific notification settings, tap the server’s name.

  2. Select Notifications to view the available server-specific settings.

Server-specific Notification Settings
Mute Server

Tapping Mute brings up several muting options:

For 15 minutes: Mutes the server for 15 minutes.

For 1 hour: Mutes the server for 1 hour.

For 3 hours: Mutes the server for 3 hours.

For 8 hours: Mutes the server for 8 hours.

For 24 hours: Mutes the server for 24 hours.

Until I turn it back on: Mutes the server until you manually disable server mute.

Mute duration options
Server Notification Settings

All Messages: Any message posted in this server triggers a notification, based on your app notification settings.

Only @mentions: Only specific @mentions will trigger a notification. This includes direct @username, @role, @everyone, and @here.

Nothing: No messages in this server will trigger a device notification.

Suppress @everyone and @here: Enabling this option prevents both types of mentions from triggering a notification.

Suppress All Role @mentions: When enabled, this prevents role mentions (like @admins or @moderators) from triggering a notification.

Suppress Highlights: Suppresses notifications for noteworthy content like messages, friend activity, events, and more.

Mute New Events: When enabled, this mutes notifications for new events in the server.

Mobile Push Notifications: When enabled, push notifications for this server come through to your mobile device.

Server Notification Settings Options
Notification Overrides

In Notification Overrides, add a specific channel or category to set notification settings that override your server-wide settings. Select the channel or category you want to manage notifications for.

Setting Notification Override for a Channel

Go Live Streaming Push Notifications FAQ

Discord allows users to send push notifications to their friends when they start streaming, or ‘Go Live’, in a mutual server. This feature helps users stay connected with their friends and avoid missing out on any streaming action.

What does this article cover?

  • Streaming Notifications for Streamers
  • Streaming Notifications for Notification Recipients

For Streamers

NOTE: We are currently experimenting with adding this feature to servers that have up to 50 members

This feature is only available on servers with less than 50 members and for streamers that have verified their phone number or email. Before you start streaming in an eligible server, you will see the pop-up below.

If you would like to send a notification to your friends in this server to let them know that you are live streaming, ensure that the box labeled ‘Notify my friends in this server’ is checked before you click ‘Go Live’. Your preferences will be remembered for next time. After sending a Go Live notification, you must wait at least 15 minutes before you can send another notification, but you can still stream without sending a notification.

Other users will receive a notification that you are streaming if:

  • The user is friends with you on Discord
  • The user is a member of the server that you are streaming in and has access to the channel where the streaming is taking place
  • The user has not received a Go Live notification in the last 6 hours
  • The user has not muted the server that you are streaming in
  • The user has not disabled push notifications in their settings

For Notification Recipients

If your friend in a mutual server starts streaming and chooses to notify their friends, you will receive a push notification like below:

You can manage your preferences for this push by:

  1. Turning on/off all ‘Go Live’ notifications

iOS

  1. Navigate to your Notifications settings by clicking on your profile in the bottom right of the app and scrolling to the ‘Notifications’ tab

  2. Navigate to the section headlined ‘OTHER NOTIFICATIONS’ and toggle ‘Get notifications when your friends Go Live’ to manage your preferences

Android

  1. On your device, navigate to System Settings ->Apps & Notifications -> Discord -> Notifications -> Settings. You should see something similar to the image below. To turn off Go Live notifications, toggle off the ‘Friends’ category
  1. Muting all push notifications from a specific server

Desktop/Web

  1. Right click on the server that you want to mute and click ‘Notification Settings’

  2. Toggle off ‘Mobile Push Notifications’ to stop receiving notifications when your friends begin streaming in the server

Mobile

  1. Navigate to the server you want to stop receiving notifications from and click ‘…’ in the top right corner

  2. Select ‘Notifications’

  3. Toggle ‘Mobile Push Notifications’ to manage your preferences

  1. Unfriending the user that is streaming

You can also unfriend a user to stop receiving notifications when they Go Live in any of your mutual servers. To unfriend a user, navigate to Home -> Friends -> find the user you want to unfriend -> click ‘More’ -> click ‘Remove Friend’

  1. Turning off all push notifications

We do not recommend this solution unless you would like to stop receiving ALL push notifications from Discord. However, if you would like to stop receiving push notifications from Discord altogether, see Mobile Notifications Settings 101 for more information on how to manage your notifications settings.

Highlights Notifications

Highlights bring you the best content from the servers you care about. If you are opted in to receive Highlights for a server, Discord will occasionally notify you of the best messages, events, announcements, and more from that server.

What this article covers:

  • What are Highlights notifications?
    • Conversations with your friends
    • Popular Messages
  • Suppress Highlights
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are Highlights notifications?

Highlights lets you know about key moments happening in the servers you care about. This will include things like popular posts, events, friend activity, new forums, and more. We built this for those of you who want a notification option between receiving all messages and receiving nothing.

Today, you might see two types of highlight notifications:

Conversations with your friends
This feature is currently an experiment and only available to a limited number of servers.

Occasionally, you might receive a notification about a conversation your friends are having – something especially useful on busier servers where you don’t want to (or can’t) receive a notification for every message (i.e. your notifications are set to @mentions only). We factor in the people you usually talk to and the servers/channels you care about when deciding when to send the notification.

Popular Messages

Occasionally, you might receive a notification about a popular message in a server. We figure out what’s popular using factors such as how many reactions/replies a message received, and we also consider servers/channels where you are most active.

Suppress Highlights

The Suppress Highlights setting is an additional toggle you can turn on or off in each server. It is located in your server notification settings. This setting operates independently of your server notification settings (all messages, @mentions only, or nothing). For example, you can have your server notifications settings set to Nothing and still receive Highlights notifications if the toggle is on.

Muting a server will turn off the Highlights toggle, and you will not receive any notifications from that server.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How are Highlights Notifications being generated?

A: Highlights Notifications are generated based on information such as (but not limited to) how often you visit or communicate in a server or with friends, the number of reactions to a message, or the number of attendees at an event in the server. Conversation Highlights include a topic in the notification that is automatically generated using summarization models. All aspects of the Highlights feature including summarization are governed by and comply with Discord’s Privacy Policy.

Q: How can I turn on or off Highlights for all of my servers?

A: You can turn Highlights on or off by navigating to the server notifications setting menu and enabling Suppress Highlights. Currently, these settings can only be changed one server at a time.

Q: Are Highlights personalized to me?

A: Yes, the information that Discord uses to determine if something is considered a Highlight might depend on your activity on Discord, along with details about the server or channel. Discord relies on information such as how often you visit a server, the number of reactions to a post, or the number of attendees at an event in a server.

At any point in time, you may choose to turn on or off this personalized experience on Discord via the personalization toggle in your Privacy & Safety settings.

How can I manage my email notifications settings?

Discord’s email notifications will keep you updated on everything happening in the wonderful world of Discord while you’re asleep or on-the-go.

What does this article cover?

  • What email notifications can I receive from Discord?
  • How can I manage my email notification settings?
    • How to Manage Email Notification Settings on Browser
    • How To Manage Email Notification Settings on Desktop

What email notifications can I receive from Discord?

Enabling email notifications is a great way to keep track of all the shenanigans while you’re away from Discord. For instance, Discord will send transactional emails to notify users when subscription updates and purchases have been made to their account.

Aside from these transactional emails, Discord Emails can come in 5 different forms:

  1. Communication Emails show the calls and messages that you have missed

  2. Social Emails show pending friend requests, friend suggestions, and upcoming server events

  3. Announcements & Updates Emails share policy updates, product updates, new features, and bug fixes

  4. Tip Emails provide advice on how to navigate and get the most out of Discord

  5. Recommendation Emails suggest servers and public stage events that you might be interested in joining

How can I manage my email notification settings?

Note: Discord email notifications cannot be managed via mobile app.
How to Manage Email Notification Settings on Browser

  1. Follow this link to get to the Discord browser (https://discord.com/channels/@me).

  2. Navigate to User Settings by selecting on the cog button []located on the bottom left corner.

  3. Afterwards, press on the Notifications tab and scroll down to the Email Notifications section. From here, you can see more information about each type of notification and select the ones you want to receive.

  4. If you would like to unsubscribe from all notifications, you can uncheck each notification type or simply press Unsubscribe from all marketing emails at the bottom of the Email Notifications section:

How To Manage Email Notification Settings on Desktop

  1. Head into your User Settings by pressing the Cog button at the bottom left of the app []:

  2. Choose the Notifications tab in the left-hand menu panel and then scroll down until you see Email Notifications. From here, you can see more information about each type of notification and choose the ones you’d like to receive.

  3. Alternatively, if you would like to unsubscribe from all notifications, you can toggle off each notification type or simply press Unsubscribe from all marketing emails at the bottom of the Email Notifications section:

Customizing which email notifications you’d like to receive is a great way to declutter your space while still being part of the loop!

Can I unsubscribe from Discord email notifications within the emails?

You can unsubscribe from any or all of these emails at any time by pressing Unsubscribe in the email itself. Learn more on how to stop email notifications here.

Note: If you choose to unsubscribe in the email itself, this is a permanent action and you will no longer receive email notifications.

However, if you’d like to continue receiving email notifications, you can customize your preferences through the web browser or desktop app.

How can I stop email notifications from Discord?

Discord’s email notifications help to keep you updated on DMs or server messages you miss while you’re asleep or on the go.

If you want to discontinue getting these email notifications, there are two separate links you can click within the email to unsubscribe. Here at the top:

… Or at the bottom of the email:

Just clicking either of these links will work here.

How do I mute and disable notifications for specific channels?

Do you ever run into the problem of trying to stay focused when using Discord?

We’ve implemented notifications muting! Muting a channel or a server prevents unread indicators and notifications from appearing unless you are mentioned (which includes the @everyone and @here tags).

Discord used mute!

There are two categories of muting notifications, channel mutes and server-wide mutes. They’re super effective.

1. Channel Mute:

If you don’t need to blackout your entire server chat, but rather, just silence a couple that are blowing up your notifications, there are a few different ways to mute them.

Single Channel Mute

If you only have one channel that you’d like to mute, toggle that channel and click the bell icon in the upper right-hand corner. When muted, the icon will update.

Note: Clicking the bell doesn’t mean all your other channels are muted, just this one. You’ll either need to click the bell in each channel to mute them, or use the multi-channel mute screen. Check that out below.

Multiple Channel Mute

In order to mute multiple channels within a single server at once, click on the arrow next to the Server Name to pull up the Server menu.

Then click Notification Settings from the drop-down menu that appears.

Under Notification Overrides you’ll be able to control the specific channels you don’t want to hear from!

2. Server Mute:

Incase you want to go the easy route, open up the same Notification Settings panel from the above step (click on your Server Name, then select Notification Settings in the drop down menu) and enable the first option, Mute [Server Name].

You can also mute an entire server by right-clicking on the server icon in your server list, and selecting Mute Server from the drop-down menu.

Remember muting a server is not immune to notifications pertaining to you personally, such as @username, @role, @everyone, or @here.

You won’t receive the unread dots next to channel names or servers, but if you are mentioned specifically you will get the red indicators showing you how many times you were mentioned in which servers.

How do I stop @everyone mentions from select servers?

Even if you mute a channel or an entire server, @everyone mentions will still bring up notifications. If a server is being particularly spammy with these all-powerful attention-catchers, you can suppress them to regain a little bit of sanity and peace of mind. Step-by-step:

  1. Click the server name to bring down the server pull-down menu:

  2. Click “Notification Settings”, and check out the super spiffy channel notification settings list. When you’re done with that, click the “Suppress @everyone and @here” option:

That simple. Remember, the “Suppress @everyone and @here” option functions on a per-server basis, so you can be selective about who you want to hear from depending on which server you’re on.

Inbox FAQ

Ever wish you had an easier way to quickly check up on conversations across all your channels? Us too. That’s why we’ve added Inbox - a message center where you can view all of your unread messages and mentions!

You’ve Got Mail 📧

Note: This feature is currently only available on Desktop and Browser clients!

What does this article cover?

  • ACCESSING MENTIONS
    • Filtering Mentions
    • Removing Mentions
  • ACCESSING UNREADS
    • Marking Unread Messages as Read
    • Marking All Messages As Read
    • Muting Inbox Notifications
  • INTERACTING WITH MESSAGES
  • SHORTCUTS

ACCESSING MENTIONS

The previous @mentions tab has been added into Inbox! Clicking the Inbox icon and opening Mentions will show you all messages where you’ve been mentioned via one of the following:

@username

@role

@everyone

Filtering Mentions

You can click on the filter button in the upper right corner of the Mentions tab to filter mention messages a few different ways:

  • Include @everyone mentions
  • Include @role mentions
  • Include all servers However, while you’re viewing a DM though, the “Include all servers” option won’t be displayed, and you’ll only see the @everyone mentions and @role mentions options! So you’ll need to make sure to be viewing a server to see all these Filter options!
Removing Mentions

And if you need to close out individual messages in the Mentions menu, click on the “X” icon located next to each message.

Note: Mention messages will automatically clear after 7 days.

ACCESSING UNREADS

The Unreads tab shows any messages from unmuted channels that you have not marked as read. Any messages from direct messages or group direct messages will have a red badge indicator showing you how many messages there are!

Any @here mentions will show under the Unreads tab, not the Mentions tab.

Marking Unread Messages as Read

As you comb through your messages, you can mark messages as read by clicking on the single check mark icon within the individual message!

Marking All Messages As Read

If you want to start over fresh and clear all unreads at once, click on the Mark Inbox As Read button in the top right corner. All unread messages will be marked as read and make way for new notifications!

Muting Inbox Notifications

Lastly, as you’re combing through your Inbox, if there are channels you don’t want notifications from, click on the bell icon and set your mute preference on a channel level or server level!

Note: If you’ve selected to mute a channel or server via Inbox, you’ll need to go to the server to unmute when you want those notifications to appear again.

INTERACTING WITH MESSAGES

In order to reply to specific messages, click on the Jump button that appears on when hovering your mouse over a specific message!

Clicking this button will teleport you directly to the channel that the message you want to reply to is found in.

In the Unreads tab, you can also add new reactions, add reactions to messages that already have existing reactions added to them, and even play media within the inbox itself!

SHORTCUTS

If you’re looking to further level up your inbox skills, you can also use these extra nifty shortcuts!

  • CMD/Ctrl + I = Open Inbox
  • CMD/Ctrl + Shift + E = Mark the top most message as read

Finding Your Server Notification Settings

Game activity notifications are currently an experiment on the desktop app. To turn off these notifications, go to User Settings > Notifications and adjust your Game Activity Notifications settings. To stop sharing your game activities entirely, update your Activity Privacy settings instead. Learn more details on managing your activity settings here.

Example of Game Activity Notification

  1. Go to the server where you want to adjust notifications and press the server name in the upper-left corner to open the dropdown menu. You can also right-click the server name to open this menu.

  2. Select Notification Settings from the dropdown menu.

Accessing Server Notification Settings on Desktop

To find your server Notification Settings on mobile, tap a server’s name, then tap the Notifications icon [] > Server Notification Settings.

Accessing Server Notification Settings on Mobile
How to Mute an Entire Discord Server

In your server Notifications Settings, you can mute an entire Discord server by simply toggle the Mute Server to silence all channels in that server at once. You can also choose how long to mute the server notifications by selecting an option from the Mute duration dropdown menu.

To learn more about managing unwanted notifications, including how to ignore users, check out our Help Center article on How to Ignore Users on Discord.

Muting an Entire Server in Notifications Settings on Desktop

Muting a server will affect:

  • All notifications across the server
  • All channels within the server
  • All server activity and updates However, you will still receive @everyone mentions.

Please note that mobile push notifications will also be disabled when the server is muted.

Muting an Entire Server in Notifications Settings on Mobile
Server Notification Settings Options

Aside from muting an entire server, you can instead choose different levels of notifications. Simply select an option in the Server Notifications Settings list.

On mobile, navigate to Notifications and tap the option you’d like in Server Notification Settings.

Selecting an Option from the Server Notification Settings List

Here, you can also choose suppression options and more:

  • Suppress @everyone and @here: Prevents notifications from @everyone and @here mentions across the entire server.
  • Suppress All Role @mentions: Prevents notifications from all role mentions across the entire server.
  • Suppress Highlights: Controls email notifications for the best content from servers you follow. This toggle works independently of other notification settings - you can receive Highlights even with notifications off, unless you mute the server completely. Learn more.
  • Mute New Events: Prevents notifications for new events across the entire server.
  • Mobile Push Notifications: When you’re signed in on your Android or iOS device, you’ll get push notifications for anything you’d normally be notified about on desktop. Pretty convenient!
Notification Settings Menu Showing Suppression Toggles for @mentions, Highlights, Events, and Mobile Notifications

Finding Your Channel Notification Settings

Discord’s channel notification settings provide granular control over alerts at the individual channel level. You can override notifications for specific channels through Notification Overrides, even when other server notification settings are enabled.

  1. Simply navigate to your server Notification Settings > Notification Overrides.

  2. Select the dropdown menu to see a list of channels and categories. You can customize notification settings for each channel, even if you have other server-wide settings enabled.

  3. Select the channel you want to customize and choose your notification preferences:

  • All: Receive notifications for every message
  • Mentions: Get notified only when you’re mentioned
  • Nothing: Disable all notifications
  • Mute: Silence everything including @mentions This gives you precise control over each channel’s notifications, regardless of your server-wide settings.
Customizing Channel and Category Notifications Using Overrides

You can also set your channel notification settings by right-clicking a channel > Notification Settings.

To find your channel notification settings on mobile, longpress the channel and tap Notifications Settings.
