Parents, Teachers, and Guardians

Family Center for Parents and Guardians

Discord is a place where friends, family, and communities come together to make connections and hangout. Every day, people on Discord build communities and discuss all sorts of topics, play both casual and competitive games, and sometimes even learn something new!

Want to learn more?

For a more in depth look into how Discord works, please check out our article on a Beginner’s Guide to Discord.

Family Center is a tool we’ve built to help parents and guardians stay informed and involved in your teen’s Discord experience while respecting their privacy and autonomy. With Family Center, you can view an Activity Feed, get weekly email summaries, and manage select safety and privacy settings to support your teen’s safety goals. These tools may help encourage regular conversations between teens and their families so they can work together to build positive online behaviors.

Note: You can access Family Center by selecting this link or by heading into Account > Family Center within the Discord App.

Want to learn more?

For additional resources on how to better shape your Discord experience, please check out our Parent Hub.

What this article covers:

  • How to Set Up Family Center
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • How to Use Family Center
    • Your Teen’s Recent Activity
    • Teen Account Settings
    • Setting Your Teen’s Monthly Spending Cap
    • Scheduling Your Teen’s Screen Downtime
    • Your Teen’s Submitted Reports
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How to Set Up Family Center

Desktop/Browser

To connect to your teen in Family Center, your teen needs to either provide you with the generated QR code or share the invite link that is located in their Family Center tab under the Connect with Your Guardian option. You can either scan the QR code or select the invite link and start the connection request. You do not need the mobile app to complete this, it can be done either on web or through the app. After your teen accepts the connection, you’ll both have full access to Family Center.

Family Center Tab Appears in Left Navigation When Enabled (Top) & Example of QR Code (Bottom)

Once connected, you can head into Family Center by selecting My Family to see any connected teens there.

Want to learn more?

If you’d like to learn more about Family Center for teens, you can check out this article.

Mobile
  1. If you have the Discord app installed on your mobile device, you can select your username at the bottom then head into your User Settings by pressing Settings on the bottom-right.
Avatar in the Bottom Navigation Bar (Left) & Settings Option in the Bottom-Right Corner (Right)
  1. After navigating to your User Settings, select the Family Center tab. Once you’re in Family Center, press My Family to scan your teen’s QR code located in their Family Center tab under the Connect with Teen option.
Example of Sending a Connection Request to a Teen

How to Use Family Center

Your Teen’s Recent Activity

Once you’ve connected to your teen’s account, you’ll be able to see the following information for the last 7 days by heading to User Settings > Family Center and tapping on the Activity tab:

  • New Friends: Your teen’s recently added friends, including the display names and avatars of those friends
  • Users Messaged & Called: Users your teen has messaged or called in Direct or Group messages, including their display names and avatars.
  • Total Call Minutes in Voice & Video: Your teen’s total call minutes, including voice and video calls in Direct Messages, Group Messages, and Voice Channels (these support voice and video communication) in servers
  • Top Users and Servers: Teens’ top five users and servers in the last week, in order of message and call frequency
  • New Servers: Servers your teen joined or created, including server names, server icons, and server member counts
  • Active Servers: Servers where your teen joined a Voice Channel (these support voice and video communication) or sent a message
  • Total Purchases: Your teen’s purchases (total amount spent), including Shop purchases and Nitro subscriptions. Nitro subscriptions are shown in the week when they are billed to your teen’s account.
  • Gifts Received: You can view any items that have been gifted to your teen, including both claimed and unclaimed gifts. You’ll see what was gifted, who gifted it, and when. Note: Gifts sent via a link to teens will only show up here after the teen has claimed it Note: You will also be able to see this information in the Family Center page in User Settings.

In addition to seeing information about your teen’s recent activity through Family Center, you’ll also receive weekly updates containing a high level summary of their activity via the email address you provided at sign-up.

Important: The Family Center dashboard and weekly update emails will only contain information about your teen’s activity that happens after they accept the connection request.

Your Teen’s Activity Summary

Tip: You will not see what messages your teen has sent, only the users they have messaged.

Teen Account Settings

You will also be able to see and adjust some of your teen’s settings, including:

  • Sensitive content filters: Choose whether content flagged by our sensitive media filters is blurred or blocked for your teen. You can only choose between blur and block due to our additional safety protections for teens.
  • Friend Requests: Adjust who can send your teen a friend request (Everyone, friends of friends, Server members)
  • Server Direct Messages: Adjust if server members can send your teen Direct Messages
  • Message Requests: Message requests are on for teen users.,With this setting enabled, messages from users who aren’t friends with your teen are filtered into a separate “Message Requests” folder. This helps keep unwanted messages out of your teen’s main direct message inbox. Important: You must be in the adult age group (18+) before you’re able to update your teen’s message request setting. You can go to your User Settings > Account Status to check your age group status or learn more about how to confirm your age group here.
Content, Social Permissions, and Friend Requests Settings in Family Center
  • Data & Privacy Settings: You can adjust a suite of data & privacy settings like allowing users to use their data to improve Discord or personalize their Discord experience.
    • Use data to make improve Discord work
    • Use data to improve Discord
    • Use data to personalize my Discord experience
    • Use my teen’s Discord activity to personalize Sponsored Content
    • Use third-party data to personalize Sponsored Content
    • Use data to make Discord work
Data & Privacy Settings in Family Center

Tip: If you have a linked Family Center account, your teen will not be able to adjust the above settings on their own. We encourage you to talk to your teen about how to customize these safety settings in a way that supports your family’s safety goals.

Setting Your Teen’s Monthly Spending Cap

As a Guardian, you can set a monthly spending cap to limit how much your teen can spend, (this does not include subscriptions such as Nitro, Server Boosts, Server Subscriptions, Premium App Subscriptions). However, in your teen’s recent activity, you can see their total purchases for the last 7 days, including Nitro subscriptions. Nitro subscriptions are shown in the week when they are billed to your teen’s account.

Total Purchases

Once the cap is reached, your teen won’t be able to make additional purchases until the following month. You can also set a monthly spending cap of $0.00.

  1. Under the Family Center tab, look for Monthly Spending cap to start setting up a spending cap.

  2. Select Edit. You can then enter in the box what you’d like the spending limit to be. Once set, select Save to save the limit.

Save Button
Scheduling Your Teen’s Screen Downtime

Screen time limits lets you schedule downtime for your teen during which your teen cannot access Discord. They will be notified when you schedule downtime and also be notified 15 minutes before downtime begins. Your teen won’t receive any Discord notifications during downtime.

For example, if you schedule downtime from 11PM to 9AM, your teen won’t be able to access Discord during those hours. Your teen will see a message letting them know access is currently restricted when they try to open Discord during downtime.

  1. Under the Family Center tab, look for Screen Time Limits under Parental Controls to set up restricted hours.

  2. Select Edit to edit a previous schedule or Schedule Downtime to add a new one.

  3. Here, you can enable or disable the schedule, set the downtime hour(s) or day(s) or delete the schedule.

  4. Select Save Schedule to save.

Save Schedule Button
Your Teen’s Submitted Reports

When your teen reports another user or content to Discord, they can choose to let you know they filed a report. If they choose to share this with you, you’ll get an email notification. This option is only available for linked accounts.

Reports can be about many different things—from spam messages to more serious concerns. When your teen chooses to notify you about a report, it shows they want you to be aware and involved. This is a good opportunity to have a supportive conversation with them. Consider asking how they’re doing, or letting them know you’re proud of them for speaking up, and reminding them that you’re always there if they need help or want to talk about anything they experience online.

The specific details of the report won’t be shared in the email, so checking in directly with your teen will help you understand what happened and how you can best support them.

Important: Although your teen can disconnect at any time, your teen’s account will be automatically disconnected from all connected guardian accounts in Family Center once their age group updates to adult.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why can I only see the last 7 days of activity?

A: Our goal is to surface information that is timely, not overwhelming, and helpful in starting conversations about online safety. Family Center highlights information in a 7 day period in order to provide contextually relevant information for parents and guardians.

Q: Discord thinks my teen is 25 but they are actually 13. How can I update their age?

A: If their age group is incorrect, they can confirm their age group in their User Settings > Account Status > Age Group or go here for additional instructions.

Q: How can I flag inappropriate activity to Discord?

A: As a parent, we encourage you to spend some time reviewing and discussing your teen’s settings so that you can customize their Discord experience and avoid unwanted experiences. You can learn more about Discord’s safety settings here.

Additionally, if your teen encounters a violation of our Community Guidelines please have them submit an in-app report of the behavior by following the instructions here.

In sensitive situations, if you would like to report the behavior on your teen’s behalf, you can do so by following the instructions here.

Q: My teen won’t allow me to connect with them through Family Center, how can I make them?

A: Both parents/guardians and teens must voluntarily opt into connecting to Family Center. If your teen has additional questions about information shared via Family Center they can learn more here. We encourage you to talk with your teen to customize a Discord experience that is right for the whole family.

Q: Why can’t I link to my teen’s account?

A: If your teen is in the adult age group, you will not be able to link to their account. Your teen will have to confirm they’re in the teen age group on Discord before you are able to link to the account. Have them try to confirm their age group by following the instructions here.

Q: How can I join a server my teen is in?

A: Every server on Discord is different and each has their own custom join settings and rules around invites to fit the needs of the community.

To learn more about a server your teen is a part of, we encourage you to discuss and review the server together.

Q: Why can’t I see all of my teens’ friends?

A: Family Center is designed to provide parents/guardians with their teens’ recent activity. At this time we only provide information about their activity on Discord within the last seven days. This includes the number of users they’ve messaged or called, the number of new friends they’ve added, and how many servers they’re actively participating in. Family Center won’t contain a complete archive of activity and will only highlight activity occurring after your teen has accepted your connection request.

Q: Can I make changes to my teen’s friend list or joined servers?

A: Family Center does not allow any connected parent/guardian to make modifications or changes to their teen’s friend list or joined servers on their teen’s behalf. For security and privacy reasons, only account owners can make modifications on their account.

As a parent/guardian, we encourage you to leverage Family Center as a way to spend some time reviewing and discussing your teen’s settings so that you can help customize their Discord experience. We’ve outlined some discussion starters and tips for helping keep your teen safe on Discord here: discord.com

Q: How many teens can I connect to in Family Center?

A: Parents and guardians are able to connect to a maximum of 8 accounts.

Q: I don’t want my teen talking to this user, can I do anything?

A: If you feel uncomfortable with someone your teen is engaging with, we encourage you to talk to your teen about your concerns. We want to make you aware of the tools available to your teen on Discord, such as our sensitive content filters and spam filters. You can also block specific users who you or your teen do not wish to communicate with anymore. Instructions on how to do so can be found here.

Discord takes our teen users’ security and safety very seriously. If you believe there is a violation of our Community Guidelines, we ask that you report this behavior to us. You can find more information on how to submit a request here.

Q: If I accidentally remove my teen’s connection, do they need to re-allow me to connect?

A: Yes. For security and privacy reasons, once a parent has disconnected from a teen, they must go through the connection process again in order to re-establish their connection with that teen.

Q: Can I see if another user is connected to my teen in Family Center?

A: Connected parents and guardians can’t see every account their teen has connected to in Family Center, but you are sent an email confirmation when there is a newly linked account to your connected teen’s account.

Q: Are there recommended safety settings that I should set for my teen?

A: We know that every teen is different, so while we stand by our safety features and default settings for teens, we encourage guardians and teens to actively review these settings together to make sure they are serving the positive Discord experience they want to have.

Q: Will my teen be able to adjust their own safety settings without me? Will my teen be notified when I adjust their safety settings?

A: Teens will not be able to adjust their safety settings unless it’s through your account in Family Center. Teens will not be notified when you adjust their settings, so we recommend chatting through the options with them.

Q: Does Family Center show me my teen’s age group status?

A: No. Family Center doesn’t show you your teen’s age group. If you’re unable to update their message request setting, it’s because you need to confirm you’re an adult, not because of anything about their age group. You can check your own age group status in User Settings > Account Status, and confirm your age group if needed. Learn more about how to confirm your age group here.

Family Center for Teens

Family Center is an optional tool created to help keep up to three parents or guardians informed about how you use Discord while still maintaining your privacy. As you make connections and join servers, the information provided within the Activity Summary will help you and your connected family members stay on the same page. However, to respect your privacy, the summary will not share the messages you send with connected family members.

Note: You can access Family Center by selecting this link or by heading into your User Settings > Account > Family Center within the Discord App.

What this article covers:

  • How to Connect to a Parent or Guardian
  • How is Family Center Used?
    • Your Recent Activity
    • Your Account Settings
    • Your Spending Cap
    • Your Scheduled Screen Downtime
    • Your Submitted Reports
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How to Connect to a Parent or Guardian

To connect with a trusted adult family member, head to User Settings located in the bottom-left of the desktop/browser app and then select Account > Family Center.

While here, select My Family and then press either Show Code or Copy Link.

Note: Your parent or guardian does not need to download the Discord mobile app and can connect to you in Family Center via web. If you would like to see how Family Center works for parents or guardians, you can check out this article here.

Connect with Guardian Button

While here, you’ll be able to choose between showing a QR code that your parent or guardian can scan from their smartphone or copying an invite link to share with your parent or guardian. After they either scan the QR code or click the invite link, you will receive a connection request from your parent or guardian. If you accept that connection request, you and your parent or guardian will be connected in Family Center and you will see your connected parent or guardian in the Connected Parents section under My Family.

Example of QR Code

After completing setup, your parent or guardian will only be able to see activity that has occurred after being connected to you in Family Center. They will not have access to any activity that occurred before the connection was activated.

How is Family Center Used?

Your Recent Activity

Once you are connected to your parent or guardian in Family Center, they will have access to information around your use of Discord by heading to Family Center > Activity. Your connected parent or guardian will be able to see the following information from the last 7 days:

  • New Friends: Your recently added friends, including the display names and avatars of those friends
  • Users Messaged & Called: Users you have messaged or called in Direct or Group messages, including their display names and avatars. call.
  • Total Call Minutes in Voice & Video: Your total call minutes, including voice and video calls in Direct Messages, Group Messages, and Voice Channels (these support voice and video communication) in servers
  • Top Users and Servers: Your top five users and servers in the last week, in order of message and call frequency
  • New Servers: Servers you joined or created, including server names, server icons, and server member counts
  • Active Servers: Servers where you joined a Voice Channel (these support voice and video communication) or sent a message
  • Total Purchases: Your purchases (total amount spent), including Shop purchases and Nitro subscriptions. Nitro subscriptions are shown in the week when they are billed to your account.
  • Gifts Received: Gifts you have received, including both claimed and unclaimed gifts. Information on what was gifted, who gifted it, and when. Note: Gifts sent via a link to you will only show up here after you have claimed it. Note: You will also be able to see this information in the Family Center page in User Settings.

Family Center > Activity can be accessed at any time. Additionally, connected parents or guardians will receive a weekly update via email containing a high level summary of this view. You will be sent a copy of this email as well.

Example of a Teen’s Weekly Activity Summary

Note: Family Center does not show connected parents or guardians what you are sending in a message (server, direct message, or group direct message).

Your Account Settings

If you’re connected to Family Center, certain settings around things like sensitive content, DMs, and privacy are managed by your guardian. These settings are especially important because they shape what you might see on Discord or how people can reach you. That’s why we encourage you to talk about them with your parent or guardian and make sure they match the experience you want:

  • Sensitive content filters: Parents or guardians can adjust whether content flagged by our sensitive media filters is blurred or blocked. Your guardian can’t choose to ‘show’ content that’s blurred, as part of our additional safety protections for teens, but can switch between ‘blur’ or ‘block’.”
Sensitive Content Filters
  • Friend Requests: Parents or guardians can adjust who can send you a friend request (everyone, friends of friends, server members)
Friend Requests Settings

  • Server Direct Messages: Parents or guardians can adjust if server members can send you Direct Messages

  • Message Requests: Parents or guardians can adjust if you have message requests turned on. Message requests are on for teen users. When it’s on, messages from users who aren’t friends with your teen are filtered into a separate “Message Requests” folder. This helps keep unwanted messages out of your teen’s main direct message inbox. Important: Parents or guardians must be in the adult age group (18+) before you’re able to update your message request setting. Parents or guardians can go to Settings > Account Status to check their age group status or learn more about how to confirm their age group here.

  • Data & Privacy Settings: Parents or guardians can adjust a suite of data & privacy settings like allowing users to use their data to improve Discord or personalize their Discord experience.

    • Use data to make Discord work
    • Use data to improve Discord
    • Use data to personalize my Discord experience
    • Use my Discord activity to personalize Sponsored Content
    • Use third-party data to personalize Sponsored Content
    • Use data to make Discord work
Data & Privacy Settings

Note: If you have a linked Family Center account with a guardian, you will not be able to adjust the above settings on your own. We encourage you to talk to your guardian about how to customize these safety settings in a way that supports your experience on Discord.

Check with Guardian Notification
Your Spending Cap

Your guardian has the option to set a monthly spending cap on your account, which doesn’t apply to subscriptions (Nitro, Server Boosts, Server Subscriptions, Premium App Subscriptions).

Under the Family Center tab, look for Spending Cap to see your monthly limit.

Teen’s Spending Cap

If a purchase would put you over that cap, you’ll see an error message and won’t be able to complete the transaction.

Error Message If Over/or at Spending Limit
Your Scheduled Screen Downtime

Your guardian is able to schedule downtime which are specific hours during which you cannot access Discord. Inside of those hours, you’ll see a message letting you know that access is currently restricted.

Restricted Hours Message When Logging in Outside of These Hour(s)/Day(s)

For example, your guardian might schedule downtime from 11PM to 9AM and inside of those hours, you won’t be able to access Discord.

To check your downtime scheduled hours, head to the Family Center tab and look for Screen Time Limits under Parental Controls.

Teen’s Screen Time Limits

If you try to log into the Discord app during your downtime hours, you’ll see a message that tells you when you can log in again.

Your Submitted Reports

When you report another user or content to Discord, you will be given the option to notify your guardian that you filed a report. If you choose to notify your guardian, they will be sent an email. This option will only appear for linked accounts.

Example of Submitted Report

Note: The type of report you made and the content you reported will not be shared, just that you made a report. In the email, we encourage your guardian to reach out to you for more details.

Important: Although you can disconnect at any time, you will be automatically disconnected from all connected parent or guardian accounts in Family Center once your age group updates to adult.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why am I seeing Family Center in parent/guardian view although I am a teen?

A: The view you are seeing is based on the age group you are part of. If this is incorrect, you can confirm your age group by following the directions here.

Q: Do I have to add a parent or guardian? What if I wanted to add someone else?

A: You can connect to any trusted adult family member in Family Center. Whether that person is an older brother, sister, aunt, grandparent, or other guardian, you two can connect your Discord accounts and use Family Center.

Q: How many parents/guardians can list me as their teen?

A: Teens may connect to up to 3 parents/guardians.

Q: Can I revoke connections at any time?

A: Yes, both you and any connected family members can choose to disconnect from each other in Family Center at any time. This can be done by heading to “My Family” and tapping X on the account you wish to remove.

Q: Can my parents/ guardians remove me from servers/DMs/GDMs? (General question around scope of function)

A: No, Family Center does not allow a connected parent/guardian to remove their teen from the servers, DMs, and GDMs that their Discord account is in.

Q: What kind of information will my parent/guardian be able to see?

A: We value your privacy which is why Family Center will not share the contents of your messages with your connected parent/guardian.

If at any time you are curious about what your connected family members are able to see, you can always see the same information they do by going into Family Center.

Q: Can I control what kind of information my parent/guardian sees?

A: For transparency, both connected parents/guardians and their teens will see the same information in Family Center. Connected parents/guardians will only see information about what is listed above.

Q: Can other people see who my parent/guardian is?

A: Only you and your parent/guardian can see which accounts are connected to you via Family Center. When you connect to a new parent/guardian in Family Center, existing connected family members will receive a notification highlighting that someone new has connected to you in Family Center.

Q: My parent/guardian made me enable this - do I have to keep it enabled?

A: You can choose to disconnect from any account in Family Center at any time. If you disconnect from an account in Family Center, they will automatically be notified via email.

Q: Can I change or remove my parent/guardian at any time?

A: You can always choose to disconnect from any account in Family Center. If you disconnect from an account in Family Center, they will automatically be notified via email.

Q: Will enabling this impact my Discord Developer account/access? Will my parents/guardians see my active apps?

A: No, your Discord Developer account will not be impacted in any way. At this time Family Center does not provide information on your active apps.

Q: Can I check my own age group status?

A: Yes. You can check your age group status anytime in User Settings > Account Status. If you think it’s wrong, you can confirm your age group there too. Learn more about how to confirm your age group here.

How to Contact Discord Safety for Parents and Guardians

This article will explain how to submit a report to Discord’s Safety team if you are a parent or guardian.

We recommend that you explore our Family Center, and check out our Safety Center, including our Parent Hub for more information.

In case of an emergency, you may wish to contact your local law enforcement.

If you have access to your teens Discord account, you can submit the report right in the app. Check out this article to learn more about how to submit an in app report.

For reports of violations of our Community Guidelines or Terms of Service, using this form, you’ll select the type of abuse that you’re reporting.

You will need to provide a Message Link of the violating content.

To get the Message Link on iOS, hold down on the Message, then select “Copy Message Link.”

On Android, hold down on the Message, then select “Copy Message Link.”

On desktop, “right-click” on the Message, and select “Copy Message Link.”

Make sure the Message Link is formatted like this:

  • From a DM:
    • discordapp.com
  • From a server:
    • discordapp.com Do not mislead Discord’s support teams. Do not make false or malicious reports to our Trust & Safety or other customer support teams, send multiple reports about the same issue, or ask a group of users to report the same content or issue. Repeated violations of this guideline may result in loss of access to our reporting functions.

What Happens After I Submit a Report?

When we become aware of content that violates our Community Guidelines or Terms of Service, our Safety team reviews and takes the necessary enforcement actions, including: disabling accounts, removing servers, and when appropriate, engaging with the proper authorities.

You can read more about the reports we receive and the actions we take on violations of our Community Guidelines or Terms of Service in our quarterly Transparency Report.

What is Family Center?

What is Family Center?

Family Center is a new tool built to help parents and guardians stay informed about how their teen uses Discord while still respecting their privacy. Parents and guardians will be able to see their connected teen’s recent Discord activity through an in-app activity dashboard and weekly email summaries. Through transparency, our goal is to foster productive dialogue about safer internet habits, and to create mutually beneficial ways for parents, guardians, and teens to connect about their experiences on Discord.

You can access Family Center by selecting this link or by heading into your User Settings within the Discord App.

What this article covers:

  • What is Family Center?
  • How to set up Family Center
    • Desktop/Browser
    • Mobile
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How to set up Family Center

If you run into any issues while setting up Family Center, please reach out to our Support team for further assistance here.
Desktop/Browser

To set up Family Center, you will need to create a Discord account. If you already have an active Discord account, you can set up Family Center by selecting the [ ] cogwheel button to head into your User Settings.

Parents and guardians can then go to the Family Center tab and toggle the Enable Family Center Tab option under General Settings to access this tool. In order to complete setup and connect on Family Center, we require both parent/guardian and teen accounts to complete this process on the Discord mobile app.

Mobile

To connect to Family Center on your mobile device, parents and guardians can head into their User Settings by pressing their profile icon.

After navigating to User Settings, select the Family Center tab. Once in Family Center, press the “Connect with Teen” button within the My Family tab to scan the teen’s QR code that is located in their Family Center tab under the Connect with Parent option. After the teen has accepted their parent or guardian’s request, both can start using Family Center together.

If you would like to learn how to specifically set up a parent/guardian account, you can check out this article here. If you would like to set up a teen account, you can refer to this article here.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why is Discord making this Family Center?

A: Family Center was built to foster productive dialogue about safer internet habits, and to create mutually beneficial ways for parents/guardians and teens to connect about experiences online.

Q: Why would I want to use Family Center?

A: Family Center allows teenagers to easily share information on how they use Discord with a parent, guardian, or other trusted caregiver in a way that respects their privacy.

Q: I do not want this, can I opt out of Family Center?

A: Family Center is a completely opt-in feature and not mandatory for teens. Although anyone can access Family Center in User Settings, you need to go through a multi-step connection process in order to activate the feature and connect your account with a family member. Even after connecting your account, if you decide you no longer want to use Family Center, you can always disconnect your account from a family member at any time.

Q: By using this - what can my parent/guardian see and not see?

A: We value user privacy and ability to control and customize their account. Connected accounts will not have access to the contents of your messages. Parents and guardians will only see information about:

  • Recently added friends, including their display names and avatars
  • Servers joined or participated in, including server names, server icons, and member counts
  • Users messaged or called in direct messages or group chats, including display names, avatars, and the time of the last message or call Q: How does this affect my privacy as a user connected with a parent or guardian?

A: When it comes to privacy, we want to make sure you have information and tools available to make decisions that best support you. With Family Center, you have control over whether or not you use this feature, how long you want to use it for, and who you connect your account to. Each step of the way we’ll let you know what information is being shared and who it is being shared with.

We value your privacy which is why connected accounts will not have access to the contents of your messages. Parents and guardians will only see information about:

  • Recently added friends, including their display names and avatars
  • Servers joined or participated in, including server names, server icons, and member counts
  • Users messaged or called in direct or group chats, including display names, avatars, and the time of the last message or call Q: How will this impact my apps on Discord?

A: Family Center will not have any impact on your apps on Discord.

Authorize Payments for Discord Client FAQ

What this article covers:

  • What is the Meaning of “Action Required” for My Purchase?
  • How Do I Authorize My Payments?
  • What if I Didn’t Make These Purchase Attempts?

What is the Meaning of “Action Required” for My Purchase?

When making a Discord purchase, we may ask you to authorize your payment. This helps us confirm that the purchases are made by you, and to prevent any fraudulent activity.

How Do I Authorize My Payments?

You’ll see an in-app message appear when attempting to complete the purchase that will look like this:

You should then receive an email from Discord with the subject “Authorize Payments for Discord Client” to the email address associated with the Discord account you’re using to make this purchase.

When you open the email, you’ll see a message like this:

If you recognize the purchase on your account, go ahead and tap on the Verify Purchase button. You’ll be redirected to a new Discord landing page letting you know that your payment has been authorized.

Once your payment has been authorized, you can go back to the app and attempt to make the purchase again.

What if I Didn’t Make These Purchase Attempts?

If you didn’t attempt to make these purchases, do not click the Verify Purchase button in the email. This might be a sign that your Discord account has been compromised or hacked.

Note: If you suspect your Discord account has been compromised and need additional support, submit a report to the Discord team through our support form linked here.

We suggest changing your password and enabling two-factor authentication on your email account and Discord account as soon as possible.

To reset your password and set up 2FA on your Discord account, you can check out these articles here:

  • I forgot my Password! Where can I set a new one?
  • Setting Up Two-Factor Authentication If you have unauthorized charges on your Discord account, please submit a request through the email address associated with your Discord account through our support form.

Discord Gift Cards

Discord gift cards are available at select retailers, online and in stores. They’re an easy way to treat yourself or a friend. Just redeem one to add balance to your Discord account, then spend it on things like Nitro, the Shop, and more.

What are Discord gift cards?

Discord gift cards are a prepaid card you can use to make purchases on Discord. Once redeemed, the balance is added directly to your account and can be spent across items in Discord.

Gift cards are a great option if you:

  • Don’t have a credit card or prefer not to link one to your account
  • Want a flexible way to pay for Nitro, Shop items, or other Discord purchases
  • Want to set a budget and add a specific amount to your account before spending
  • Are a parent or friend who wants to give the gift of Discord to someone in your life

Where can I buy a Discord gift card?

You can buy Discord gift cards at select retailers depending on your country or region. If you’re in the US, check our website here. If you’re in the rest of the world, head to our Help Center.

What can I buy with a Discord gift card?

Once redeemed, you can spend your gift card balance on things like:

  • Nitro and Nitro Basic - Discord’s premium subscription plans.
  • Nitro Gifts - Buying Nitro for your friends.
  • The Discord Shop - Avatar Decorations, Profile Effects, Nameplates, and more.
  • Server Boosts - Support your favorite servers and help unlock perks for the whole community.
  • Game Shops - Purchase in-game items for select titles directly through Discord.
Discord Gift Card Balance

How to Redeem Your Gift Card

You can redeem your gift card in two ways: through the discord.com/redeem web page, or directly in the desktop app via Billing.

Important: Before redeeming, make sure you’re logged into the correct account and that your account’s Country/Region setting matches the country where your gift card was purchased. Gift card balances cannot be transferred between accounts once redeemed.

Desktop App

  1. Open the Discord desktop app and select the cogwheel [] next to your username to open User Settings.

  2. Head to User Settings > Billing > Payment Methods, and select the Redeem button by the Gift Card Balance option.

  3. Enter your gift card code exactly as shown and follow the on-screen prompts.

  4. Press Redeem. Your balance will be added to your account immediately.

Redeeming a Discord Gift Card through Billing on Desktop
Discord.com/redeem

  1. Head to discord.com/redeem. You can do this on any mobile, desktop, or tablet device.

  2. Log in to your Discord account, or create one if you’re new.

  3. Enter your gift card code exactly as provided and follow the on-screen prompts.

  4. Press Redeem. Your updated balance will appear on screen.

  5. Select Get Nitro or Get Nitro Basic to start spending your balance, or head to the desktop app to explore more options in the Shop.

Discord.com/redeem Landing Page

Mobile Availability

Redeeming a gift card and spending your balance aren’t available in the mobile app at this time.

You can still redeem a gift card and purchase items using a browser on your mobile phone:

  • Redeem your gift card at discord.com/redeem.
  • After redeeming, open Discord in your browser at discord.com/login to spend on things like Nitro, the Shop, and more.
  • Your purchases will be available across devices on your account.
  • You can view your balance in the web app as well.
Redeeming a Discord Gift Card through Mobile Web Browser

Frequently Asked Questions

Important: Gift cards are frequently targeted by scammers. Do not purchase a Gift Card unless you’re buying it as a gift or for your own use—never buy one to make a payment at someone else’s direction. For more about gift card fraud, visit stopgiftcardscams.com.

This FAQ is divided into sections:

Buying Gift Cards

Q: Are digital and physical gift cards available?

A: Yes! Discord gift cards are available in-store and online at select retailers. You can find select retailers by region in our Help Center.

Q: What countries are Discord gift cards available in?

A: Discord gift cards are available in the United States, United Kingdom along with select retailers in Canada, France, Italy, and Spain. We’re always exploring new places we could bring gift cards in the future, stay tuned!

Q: Where can I buy Discord gift cards?

A: You can buy Discord gift cards at select retailers depending on your country or region. If you’re in the US, check our website here. If you’re in the rest of the world, head to our Help Center.

Q: What gift card amounts are available?

A: Discord gift cards are available in the following options:

  • USD: $25, $50, and variable amounts from $15–$150
  • EUR: €25, €50, and variable amounts from €15–€150
  • GBP: £20, £40, and variable amounts from £10–£100
  • CAD: $35, $75, and variable amounts from $20–$175 Availability will vary by retailer and region.

Q: Can I buy a gift card for someone in another country?

A: Gift cards can only be redeemed in the country they were purchased in, so keep that in mind when buying for someone abroad. One exception: gift cards priced in euros can be redeemed in any country that uses euros as their official currency. Make sure to check which countries Discord gift cards are available in before purchasing.

Redeeming

Q: Do I need an account to redeem my gift card?

A: Yep! You must be logged into a Discord account to redeem a gift card. Don’t have one yet? It’s free to sign up at Discord.com.

Q: Can I redeem a gift card from another country?

A: Gift cards can only be redeemed in the country they were purchased in. To redeem, your account’s Country/Region setting must match the gift card’s currency. Gift cards priced in euros can be redeemed in any country that recognizes the euro as an official currency.

Q: Why isn’t my gift card code working?

A: Let’s help with that! Here are some pro tips and considerations:

  • Typo? Make sure you’re entering the code exactly as shown on the back of the card.
  • Wrong Country? Gift cards can only be redeemed in the country they were purchased in. If your Country/Region doesn’t match the card’s currency, redemption will be blocked. You can see what region your account is set to under Country/Region in User Settings > Billing > Payment Methods.
  • Balance or redemption limit reached. Your account may have reached its wallet balance or redemption limit.
  • Platform pro tip. Just a heads up, you can only view and spend your balance on the desktop app or web browser. Items purchased show up wherever you use Discord. If none of the above apply and your code still isn’t working, please contact Discord support with your card details and a photo of the back of the card.

Q: I’m still having issues with my Discord gift card. What do I do?

A: If you’re still experiencing issues with your gift card, you can submit a request through the Discord support form.

Visit dis.gd/billing and select Refunds, Cancellations & Payments. From there, choose Gift Cards under the Type of Billing Issue and complete the rest of the form based on your specific concern.

Q: What if the code on my physical gift card is scratched off, damaged, or lost?

A: You’ll need to work with the retailer for any issues with your gift card prior to redemption. See the Gift Card Terms for more information.

Your Balance & Spending

Q: Where can I see my gift card balance once I’ve redeemed?

A: You can check your balance anytime under User Settings > Billing > Payment Methods within the desktop app or web browser.

Q: Does my gift card or balance expire?

A: Discord gift cards and balances in the United States do not expire. Expiration terms vary by country in other regions. See our Gift Card Terms and Wallet Terms for more information.

Q: Can I redeem multiple gift cards?

A: Yes! You can redeem multiple gift cards to your Discord account, each one will add to your existing gift card balance up to the maximum balance limit in your country.

Q: Is there a limit for how much money I can have in my account?

A: Yes, there is a limit! If you have multi-factor authentication on your account, you can have a higher balance.

Don’t have MFA set up? You should! Check out how to set up MFA here.

Q: Are there any cases where I cannot use my gift card balance?

A: Yes. Your gift card balance may be temporarily unavailable if your wallet has been frozen, or if you have reached your gift card balance limit. If you believe this is an error, please contact Discord support.

Q: Is there anything I can’t buy with a Discord gift card?

A: You can spend your Discord gift card balance on most purchasable things in Discord - like Nitro, the Shop, Server Boosts, Gifts on Discord, and more. The option to use your balance won’t show up during check-out if you can’t use a gift card balance to purchase that item.

Q: What if my gift card doesn’t cover the total cost of my purchase?

A: Your gift card balance must cover the cost of your purchase to use. Otherwise, you’ll need to use another payment method on file for purchase at this time. We don’t currently support splitting a payment between your gift card balance and another payment method, but we’re working on it!

Q: What happens if my subscription renews and my gift card balance is too low?

A: If your Gift Card balance is insufficient at renewal, you’ll have 3 days to update your payment method before it expires. Discord won’t automatically charge another payment method, so make sure your balance is topped up before your renewal date. You can update your payment method anytime in User Settings > Billing Settings > Subscriptions.

Account & Policies

Q: Can I transfer my gift card balance to another account?

A: No. Gift card balances are tied to the account they were redeemed on and cannot be transferred.

Q: What happens to my gift card balance if I delete my account?

A: If you delete your Discord account, any remaining gift card balance may be forfeited and cannot be recovered. More information can be found in the Wallet Terms.

Q: What happens if my Discord account is suspended or terminated?

A: Use of Discord is subject to our Terms of Service, Community Guidelines, and other policies. Violating these terms may result in action on your account, including suspension or termination. If your account is suspended, you will not have access to your gift card balance for the duration of the suspension. See our Gift Card Terms and Wallet Terms for more information.

Q: What should I do if I think my gift card was stolen or used fraudulently?

A: Discord can assist with suspicious activity on your account, such as an unknown charge using your gift card balance. You’ll need to work with the retailer for any issues with your gift card prior to redemption.

If you suspect a fraudulent purchase was made using your Discord gift card balance, you can reach out to our support team here. Please fill out the ticket with the following categories:

  • What can we help you with?: Refunds, Cancellations & Payments
  • Type of Billing Issue?: I have a question/issue regarding an unauthorized transaction Q: Can I get a refund for a purchase made with a Discord gift card?

A: If a purchase made with your gift card balance qualifies for a refund under Discord’s standard refund policy, the refund will be returned to your account balance, not to another payment method.

Other

Q: What happened to the old Nitro gift cards sold on Amazon?

A: As of October 30, 2026, Discord Nitro gift cards are no longer available for purchase on Amazon.

Keep in mind the new gift cards work a little differently from the old Amazon Nitro gift cards. Instead of applying directly to a Nitro subscription, they load a balance to your Discord account that you can use toward Nitro, the Discord Shop, Server Boosts, and more.

Q: Who is CIMI / Weary Travelers Inc.?

CIMI is the company we work with to bring gift cards to you. Weary Travelers, Inc. is the issuer of our gift cards. Someone at Discord (shhh, it was Byron) thought that Weary Travelers was a fun name - so rest here weary traveler. You have seen too many FAQs. Sit by the fire before you continue. When you’re ready, you can find more information in the Gift Card Terms and Wallet Terms.

Google Play Store Integration FAQ

What this article covers:

  • How do I Purchase A Subscription on Android?
  • How do I Change my Subscription?
  • How do I Cancel my Subscription?
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How do I Purchase A Subscription on Android?

  1. Start by heading into your User Settings by tapping on your avatar in the bottom right corner.

  2. You’ll then need to scroll down until you see the Nitro Settings section! From here, tap on Subscribe Today to start the process.

  3. You’ll then see the option to purchase Nitro or Nitro Basic.

  4. You’ll then be asked to confirm if you want Yearly or Monthly, then you can tap on purchase to proceed.

  5. You’ll then see a Google Play menu pop up explaining your subscription purchase pricing and asking what payment method you want to use.

  6. Once you’ve confirmed your subscription with the Subscribe button (and scanning your fingerprint or inputting your password [if applicable] to verify your purchase), you’ll then see a confirmation that your Nitro has been activated.

How do I Change my Subscription?

If you ever change your mind on the type of subscription you have, you can always switch your subscription as well.

  1. To start, head into your User Settings, scroll down until you see the Nitro Settings section once more, and then select the Manage Subscriptions tab.

  2. In this tab, tap the Switch Plans button (right beside the Manage Boosts button), and you’ll be given the option to choose from all the other subscription types.

  3. Once you have made a decision on what kind of subscription you’d like, you will see the Google Play menu pop up explaining your subscription change, and reviewing the new subscription pricing.

  4. When you’re ready to make the purchase, tap Subscribe, and you’ll see a confirmation that your subscription was activated.

  5. When you head back into your Manage Subscription tab, you’ll then see a notification that your plan change is pending. And soon, your tab will update to show your new subscription.

How do I Cancel my Subscription?

  1. Head into your User Settings and scroll down once more to your Nitro settings section to head into your Manage Subscriptions tab. Then tap on the Cancel button.

  2. You’ll then be redirected to the Google Play Store app, where you’ll need to confirm your decision by tapping on Cancel Subscription.

  3. Once the cancellation is confirmed, and you go back to your Discord mobile app, you’ll see the canceled subscription in your Manage Subscription tab.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What does creating a subscription through Google Play get me?

A: Creating a subscription through Google Play will allow you to use Google Pay as a payment option for your subscription or would like to manage your subscription in the Google Play store along other subscriptions.

Q: I don’t see the type of plan that I want to purchase, does that mean I can’t purchase that?

A: At launch, we’ve had to limit the number of plans available for purchase on Android. If you don’t see the plan type that you want to purchase you can still go on the desktop or browser app and purchase that plan through that platform. You will still be able to use the benefits on your Android device if you purchase through desktop.

Q: I already bought a subscription that I use on Android. Does this change anything about that?

A: If you’re happy with your current subscription, you don’t need to change anything! However, moving forward any changes you want to make to that subscription will need to be done through the desktop/browser app.

Q: I currently have a subscription on desktop, but want to move it to manage it through the Google Play store. How do I do that?

A: You can cancel your subscription on desktop and then re-subscribe through the Android app. However, make sure that you wait until the end of your current billing period to sign back up on Android.

Please note if you cancel your subscription on Android you will either have to sign up for Google Play or sign back up on desktop, but manage your subscription through desktop only. If you cancel your desktop subscription and re-sign up on desktop later you will also lose your streak. The only way to maintain your streak is to continue with your desktop subscription or sign up to Google Play within 7 days of the original desktop subscription ending.

Q: Will I lose my streak if I switch my subscription over to Google Play?

A: If you re-subscribe within 7 days after your desktop subscription ends to a subscription within Google Play your Nitro streak will transfer over and not be lost.

Q: Why can’t I do certain gifting actions through Google Play?

A: Currently, you can purchase and send gifts through Google Play. If you have a desktop subscription you will be able to redeem, apply, and send gifts through your Android app.

Note:
- Currently, gifts purchased through Google Play cannot contribute towards subscriptions managed by the Google Play Store.
- Redeemed gifts can still contribute towards subscriptions purchased on our desktop or browser apps.

If you’re on the Android app, and you already have a Google Play subscription and you redeem a gift purchased through the Google Play store, your redeemed Nitro gift will not contribute towards that subscription and it will become Account Credit that can be used for a subscription on our desktop or browser app!

If you’re on the Android app, and you have no active subscription when you redeem a gift purchased through the Google Play store, you will begin a subscription that can be managed on the desktop or browser app!

Q: Why can’t I create a subscription through Google Play when I already created one on my Android device?

A: You can only have one active platform subscription at a time. If you previously created a subscription on your Android device you currently have a desktop subscription that will need to be managed through your desktop or browser app.

Q: If I currently have a subscription through iOS can I manage that subscription on my Android phone?

A: If you currently have a subscription through iOS you will not be able to purchase, cancel, or otherwise manage your subscription on an Android device.

Q: What happens when I upgrade or downgrade a subscription in Google Play?

A: Similar to a desktop subscription your upgrade will be immediate and the price will be pro-rated. Downgrades will occur at the next billing cycle.

Q: I tried to upgrade my subscription and add onto my current subscription, but it got swapped to another subscription instead! Why did my subscription get swapped instead of upgraded?

A: Please note that subscription plans on Google Play cannot be added to each other and you will only be able to switch between plans.

If you wish to upgrade your subscription, you will need to switch to the plan that includes all of the subscriptions you wish to purchase.

For example:

If you currently have a Nitro Basic subscription, and you would like to update your subscription to include 2 Server Boost subscriptions as well, you will then need to manually select the “Nitro Basic + 2 Server Boost” subscription plan.

If you currently have a Nitro Basic subscription, and you select to purchase the “2 Server Boost” subscription plan, your Nitro Basic subscription will be removed, and you will only have an active subscription for 2 Server Boosts.

How do I use Google Pay and Apple Pay?

Discord now supports Google Pay and Apple Pay for select billing flows on both desktop and browser.

What this article covers:

  • How do I use Google Pay and Apple Pay?
    • Desktop
    • Browser
  • System Requirements
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How do I use Google Pay and Apple Pay?

When you’re prompted to add a payment method, you’ll see Google Pay or Apple Pay buttons if your browser and operating system support them.

Desktop

When purchasing Nitro for yourself through the Discord desktop app, you’ll see Google Pay and Apple Pay as payment options.

Payment method window on desktop

When selecting either of these options, a browser window will open to verify if your system supports the selected payment method.

Example of selecting Google Pay (Left) or Apple Pay (Right) on desktop
Browser

If your desktop or mobile browser supports Google or Apple Pay, you can complete your checkout using that payment method!

If these options aren’t available, you’ll be redirected to our standard credit card form to complete your purchase.

Example of payment method window without Google Pay support on desktop browser

System Requirements

To use Google Pay:

  • Chrome version 61 or newer To use Apple Pay:

  • Safari browser on macOS Sierra or later (desktop)

  • Safari on iOS 10.1 or later (mobile)

  • Active Apple Pay setup with a valid payment card (learn how to set up Apple Pay)

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I use Google Pay on any browser?

A: No, Google Pay is only supported on Chrome browser version 61 or later.

Q: What devices support Apple Pay?

A: Apple Pay works on:

  • Desktop: Safari browser on macOS Sierra or later
  • Mobile: Safari browser on iOS 10.1 or later Q: What happens if my browser doesn’t support Google Pay or Apple Pay?

A: You’ll be redirected to the standard credit card payment form to complete your purchase.

Q: Where can I use Google Pay and Apple Pay on Discord?

A: Currently, these payment methods are supported for select billing flows, including purchasing Nitro for yourself on the Discord desktop app.

Q: Do I need to set up anything before using Apple Pay?

A: Yes, you need to have Apple Pay already set up with a valid payment card on your device before using it on Discord.

Q: How does the payment process work?

A: When you select Google Pay or Apple Pay as your payment method, a browser window will open to verify your system’s compatibility and process the payment securely.

Venmo Integration FAQ

Note: You cannot add a new payment method directly on the Discord mobile app.

What does this article cover?

  • How do I Add Venmo as a Payment Method?
    • On Desktop/Web Browser
    • On Mobile Web Browser

How Do I Add Venmo as a Payment Method?

The Venmo app is required in order to add your Venmo account as a payment method. If you do not currently have it installed on your mobile phone, then you’ll be prompted to download the app before continuing.

On Desktop/Web Browser

After you download the app, you will need to head into your User Settings > Billing Tab > Add Payment Method and select Venmo to add it as a payment method to your Discord account.

When you select Venmo, a QR code will pop-up on your screen and you will be prompted to scan the code using your mobile device.

After you’ve scanned the QR code, you will be redirected in the mobile app where you will be asked to authorize the payment method. The QR code should disappear and you will see that your Venmo account has been authorized.

Upon completion, the name of your Venmo account will appear as the name for your payment method.

Once you’ve authorized your Venmo account, select Next. Here, you will enter your billing address information. This is still required in order to complete the process.

After entering your billing address information, you’re now finished with adding Venmo as a payment method in Discord!

On Mobile Web Browser
As a reminder, you cannot add a new payment method directly on the Discord mobile app. These are steps for a mobile web browser.

Similar to the process on the desktop app, you will need to head into your User Settings > Billing Tab > Add Payment Method and select Venmo.

When you select Venmo, you will be asked to follow steps to complete your account connection. Go ahead and tap on Connect to Venmo.

You will then be redirected to the Venmo app where your Venmo account will be authorized as a payment method.

When you return to the Discord app, you should see that your account has been authorized. The name of your Venmo account will be the name of your payment method.

Once you’ve authorized your Venmo account, select Next. Here you will enter your billing address information. This is still required in order to complete the process.

After entering your billing address information, you’re now finished with adding Venmo as a payment method in Discord!

Why do I see a Temporary Hold Charged to my Account?

What is this Temporary Hold?

We may place a temporary hold on your payment method when you make a purchase or activate a trial/promotion subscription. This is to help Discord confirm the payment method works as expected and to prevent the use of fraudulent payment methods.

This charge will appear in your Discord transaction history, and it may appear as a hold on your payment method. We immediately reverse the temporary hold, which will be indicated as Canceled in your Discord transaction history.

Your bank may take longer to remove the hold from your payment method.

Note: Banks will usually remove the temporary hold from your account within a few business days.

What if I still see a Charge on my account or payment method?

Your bank should release the hold in a matter of days after we reverse the charge.

If your Discord transaction history does not show the hold released after 5 business days, please let us know at dis.gd, and our support team will be able to investigate this issue further.

I see a “Sorry, This Payment Source Cannot Be Used for Redemption” error when trying to redeem my promo link.

If you’re seeing a “Sorry, This Payment Source Cannot Be Used for Redemption” error, that means that the payment method you’ve selected to cover the temporary hold cannot be used for that purpose.

Please keep in mind that prepaid payment methods, such as Gcash, cannot be used to cover temporary holds due to the nature of how prepaid payment methods function.

Ads Policy

Overview

All advertising content is subject to Discord’s community guidelines, however there are additional restrictions for advertising content.

Discord’s Ads Policy, outlined below, provides guidance to advertisers on the platform to publish trustworthy, safe, useful, and high-quality ads to users. Ads are prohibited, restricted, or allowed based on Discord’s content policies below.

  • Prohibited: Content you cannot advertise.
  • Restricted: Content you can advertise, with limitations.
  • Allowed: Content you can advertise. In this policy, you will also find our ads practices and our editorial guidelines for designing and implementing your ad copy and landing page.

This policy is mandatory and applies to all native and third party ads on Discord including ads in Activities. The policy applies to the ad, the landing page, the username, reward, and any other surface directly associated with the ad.

Advertisers on Discord are responsible for their ads ensuring they follow all applicable laws and regulations. In addition to Discord’s Ads Policy, advertisers must comply with our Terms of Service, Community Guidelines, and all other policies governing the use of our services.

Ads Content Policy

Below are examples of ads content that is prohibited or restricted on Discord.

Adult Sexual Content

Discord prohibits the promotion of explicit and implicit adult sexual content.

Adult sexual content includes depiction of, or references to:

  • Compensated sexual acts (e.g. escort services, cuddling sites, intimate massage, sex work),
  • Full or partial nudity,
  • Mail-order brides or international marriage brokers,
  • Models in sexualized poses,
  • Non-consensual sexual themes,
  • Penis enlargement or breast enhancement,
  • Pornography, cartoon porn, or hentai,
  • Products in the shape of intimate body parts (e.g. genitals, butts, female breasts),
  • Reproductive, contraceptive, or fertility products,
  • Sex toys and personal lubricants,
  • Strip and host/hostess clubs,
  • Suggestive live chat or phone calls,
  • Other explicit or implicit suggestive content.
Alcohol Content

Discord prohibits alcohol advertising including branding, online and offline sale, and consumption of alcoholic beverages.

Alcohol advertising includes:

  • Sale of any type of alcoholic beverage (e.g., beer, wine, or liquor),
  • Events sponsored by alcohol brands,
  • Competitions where alcohol is a prize,
  • Non-alcoholic products offered by alcohol brands,
  • Simulated alcohol games,
  • Depicting people under the influence,
  • Hangover treatments.
Body Alteration

Discord prohibits advertising of body-altering products and services.

Body Alteration includes:

  • Invasive cosmetic procedures (e.g. tongue splitting, ear shaping, waist training),
  • Body piercing,
  • Permanent tattoos,
  • Permanent makeup,
  • UV Skin tanning or skin bleaching products and services.
Charitable Causes

Discord restricts the solicitation of funds for or promotion of charitable causes. Soliciting funds or donations is only allowed for tax-exempt organizations. The ad or ad’s destination must clearly state that donations are tax-exempt, or disclose a charity number or a tax exemption number.

The following are allowed:

  • In the United States, organizations that have 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) status,

  • Entities with an equivalent non-profit registration in their home country. The following are prohibited:

  • Soliciting funds on behalf of a politician, political party, or any other violation of the political content policy,

  • Soliciting funds without tax-exempt status.

Children’s Content

Discord prohibits advertisements intended solely for children. Children’s content is defined as any content intended for an audience below 13 which is Discord’s minimum age requirement.

Examples of Children’s content include:

  • Activities that appeal to children, such as play-acting, simple songs or games, or early education,
  • Actors, characters, celebrities, or toys that appeal to children, including animated characters or cartoon figures.
  • Songs, poems, stories, or other subject matter that reflect an intent to target children. This policy does not apply to general audience content that could appeal to everyone, but isn’t intended specifically for children, and/or content that is intended for those 13 years or older.
Dating

Discord prohibits ads for online dating apps or services, matchmaking services, or romance coaching.

Dangerous Activities

Discord prohibits ads that depict or encourage real world dangerous activities.

Dangerous activities create an extreme risk of physical harm to the participant including but not limited to:

  • Physical challenge or stunt trends,
  • Misuse of fireworks.
Drugs and Drugs Paraphernalia

Discord prohibits advertisement of illegal or recreational drugs and paraphernalia.

Drugs and drugs paraphernalia advertising includes but is not limited to:

  • Illegal drugs,
  • Recreational and herbal drugs,
  • CBD products,
  • Accessories associated with drug use and storage (e.g. grinders, syringes, pipes),
  • Drug dispensaries,
  • Depictions of intoxication or drug use.
Financial Products and Services

Discord prohibits the promotion of financial products and services.

Prohibited financial products and services include but is not limited to:

  • Banking services and institutions,
  • Buy now, pay later (BNPL) providers and payment installment services,
  • Currency exchange, trading, and services,
  • Cryptocurrency and related products
  • Contract for Difference (CFDs),
  • Debt relief and consolidation,
  • Digital wallets,
  • Insurance,
  • Loans products and services,
  • Mobile and electronic payments,
  • Mortgage services,
  • Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and related products,
  • Securities,
  • Tax preparation or filing.
Hateful Content

Discord prohibits ads that promote hateful content.

Hateful content includes degrading, mocking, threatening, attacking or advocating against individuals or protected groups based on, but not limited to:

  • Race,
  • Ethnicity,
  • National origin,
  • Color,
  • Sex,
  • Sexual orientation,
  • Gender identity,
  • Religious affiliation,
  • Age,
  • Physical or mental disability,
  • Medical or genetic condition,
  • Veteran status,
  • Refugee status,
  • Immigrant Status,
  • Familial status.
Healthcare Content

Discord prohibits advertisement of healthcare products and services.

Prohibited healthcare products and services include:

  • Clinical trials,
  • Surrogacy services,
  • Telemedicine providers,
  • Online pharmacy,
  • Prescription medicines,
  • Mental health services,
  • Rehabilitation centers,
  • Over the Counter (OTC) medicines,
  • Health and dietary supplements,
  • Medical devices,
  • Surgical and non surgical cosmetic procedures (e.g. lip fillers, botox, skin lightening creams, plastic surgery).
High Fat, Salt, Sugar Food and Beverage (HFSS)

Discord restricts advertising of high fat, salt, sugar (HFSS) food and beverage products globally. Ads for HFSS products are prohibited in the UK.

Illegal Products and Services

Discord prohibits advertising of illegal products and services, including anything that facilitates or promotes illegal behavior.

Illegal products and services include but is not limited to:

  • Fake IDs, passports, or other official documents,
  • Illegal streaming or downloading of copyrighted material,
  • Instructions for or equipment to illegally access websites, cell phones or software.
Inappropriate Content

Discord prohibits advertising that contains inappropriate content.

Categories Discord considers to be inappropriate content include:

  • Distasteful content
    • Content meant to shock or scare,
    • Imagery of guts, gore, sexual fluids, human or animal waste.
  • Offensive and divisive content
  • Sensitive events
    • Content that refers to a sensitive event or topic (e.g. deaths, natural disasters, violent attacks, civil disorder) and contains personal attacks, the selling of goods or services, solicitation of followers, or other attempts to capitalize on these events.
  • Misinformation
    • Content that is false including disinformation, conspiracy theories, and climate change denial.
  • Misleading synthetic or manipulated content
  • Profanity and vulgarity
    • Including obscene uses of symbols, emojis, or gestures.
  • Personal attacks
    • Including the use of non-public personal information in ads.
  • Violence
    • Graphic imagery and realistic displays of crime, violence, physical trauma, execution,
    • Excessive gore, physical or psychological abuse, self-harm, animal abuse or torture.
  • Malware & Software Downloads
    • The advertising of malware products, including software or devices such as VPN promoting access to geo blocked or illegal services.
    • Malware products include but is not limited to:
      • Spyware,
      • Stalkerware,
      • Illegal hacking devices,
      • Phishing links,
      • Software that is deceptive or compromises user safety.
Intellectual Property

Discord prohibits ads that infringe the copyright, intellectual property, trademark, privacy, or other legal rights of any person or entity.

The following are prohibited:

  • References to Discord and uses of Discord-owned trademark, including suggestions of affiliation with or endorsement by Discord,
  • Ads for products or services primarily used to infringe the intellectual property rights of others,
  • Ads for products or services primarily dedicated to selling counterfeit products,
  • Use of the name, likeness, voice, or other identifying features of an individual without consent,
  • Any use of copyrighted material without written permission.
Political Content

Discord prohibits advertising that contains political content.

Political content includes but is not limited to references to a:

  • Candidate,
  • Political party,
  • Political Action Committees (PACs) or Super PACs,
  • Elected or appointed government official,
  • Election or referendum,
  • Ballot measure, proposition, legislation, regulation, or judicial outcome.
  • Advocacy for or against any of the above.
Real Money Gaming and Adjacent Products and Services

Discord prohibits ads for Real Money Gaming and adjacent products and services including brick and mortar casinos, sports betting, sports books, games or apps played for money, horse race betting, lotteries, pay-to-play games of chance with prizes of real-world value, simulated casinos, associated games and others.

Ad or landing page content which promotes odds, tips, picks, forecasts, handicapping or which drive users to real money gaming sites are prohibited.

Discord permits Daily Fantasy Sports ads in some jurisdictions in some circumstances. Contact your Discord Account Executive for more information.

Tobacco and Tobacco Accessories

Discord prohibits the advertising of tobacco products or accessories.

Prohibited tobacco products include but are not limited to:

  • Tobacco of any kind,
  • Hookah,
  • Cigars and cigarettes,
  • Cigar bars and hookah lounges,
  • Imitation smoking,
  • Pipes, rolling papers, or filters,
  • E-cigarettes, e-liquid, or vapes.
Unacceptable Business Practices

Discord prohibits unacceptable business models, products, and services.

Categories Discord considers to be unacceptable business practices include but is not limited to:

  • Animal or insect sale,
  • Bail bonds,
  • Counterfeit goods or services,
  • Homework or essay writing services for students,
  • Extortion and blackmail,
  • Multi-level marketing models or get-rich-quick schemes,
  • Payday loans,
  • Services attempting to change an individual’s sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression,
  • Selling social media followers,
  • False, unsubstantiated, unrealistic, or exaggerated claims,
  • Deceptive or misleading ads which withhold reasonable information on pricing, terms or expenses from the landing page.
Weapons and Weapons Accessories

Discord prohibits the advertising of real-world weapons and weapons accessories.

Prohibited real-world weapons and weapons accessories include but are not limited to:

  • Knives, throwing stars, daggers, spears, or swords,
  • Guns, firearms, airsoft guns, air guns, blow guns, paintball guns, antique guns, replica guns, imitation guns, or gun parts,
  • Stun guns, taser guns, mace, pepper spray, or other weapons of self defense,
  • Bombs, fireworks, flamethrowers, gunpowder, or explosives,
  • Weapon making instructions,
  • Weapon training programs or classes,
  • Ammunition. This policy does not apply to ads of virtual reality weapons and weapons accessories for use in video games.
Weight loss Products and Services

Discord prohibits the advertising of diet and weight loss products and services.

Prohibited diet and weight loss products and services include but are not limited to:

  • Weight loss language or imagery,
  • Diet or weight loss testimonials,
  • Weight loss or appetite suppressant pills or supplements,
  • Before and after weight loss imagery,
  • Procedures such as liposuction, fat burning, or cool sculpting,
  • Encouragement or glamorization of unhealthy or unsafe eating behaviors or eating disorders. This policy does not apply to ads that promote health, wellness, and fitness products and services that do not focus on weight loss.

Campaign Considerations

Targeting

In order to protect user experience on the platform, advertisers are prohibited from targeting ads to certain audiences or using sensitive categories for such ad targeting.

Advertisers are prohibited from:

  • Using copy that asserts or implies knowledge of a user’s personally identifiable information. Personally identifiable information (PII) includes any information that could be used to identify an individual, such as a name, home address, social security number, banking information, driver’s license number, and any other sensitive data.
  • Targeting users based on any of the following categories:
    • Alleged or actual commission of a crime
    • Health
    • Negative financial status or condition
    • Marital or relationship status
    • Race, color, or ethnic origin
    • Religious or philosophical affiliation and/or beliefs
    • Sexual orientation
    • Gender identities other than cisgender
    • Political affiliation and/or beliefs
    • Trade union membership
    • Genetic and/or biometric data In addition to these targeting restrictions, ads for housing or employment are not allowed to target users based on age, sex, gender, or precise location (post code or more precise location).
Editorial Guidelines

To keep ads trustworthy and useful for Discord users, ads and their landing page must meet our editorial criteria for accuracy and quality.

Accuracy:

  • Ads must represent the brand or product being advertised.

  • Ads must not be misleading or make exaggerated, sensationalized or inaccurate claims. Quality:

  • Text must use correct grammar and spelling

  • Text must avoid excessive punctuation, spaces, or symbols.

  • Images, video, and audio must not be unclear, indecipherable, fuzzy, blurry, extremely grainy, or otherwise of low quality.

  • Imagery with artificial functionality is not permitted (e.g. play or download buttons, notification icons, or elements that mimic Discord features).

  • Images and video must be oriented correctly (not sideways or upside down). Landing Page:

  • The destination URL must link to a functional landing page.

  • The landing page’s primary purpose must not be for advertising and must be relevant to what is being promoted in the ad.

  • The landing page must not contain intrusive pop-up ads, automatic downloads, redirect users to another site, or require users to sign in before they can view the page.

  • The contents of the landing page must comply with all of Discord’s ads content policies. Hearing Accessibility:

  • All video advertisements must include accurate closed captions.

  • Captions must be synchronized with the audio, include all spoken dialogue, and relevant sound effects.

Sanctions

Advertisements that violate US or other applicable sanctions are prohibited on Discord.

Additionally, advertisements may not be targeted to individuals located in regions that are subject to general embargoes or comprehensive trade restrictions.
