Discord Partnership Code of Conduct

Partnered servers are at the forefront of the community. We want our Partnered servers to welcome all users, whether complete newcomers to Discord or expert users and longtime members. We look to our partners to provide a positive place for people to come together around their communities.

As a Partner, always remember to conduct yourself responsibly and treat others with respect, patience, and kindness. Whether you’re on-stream, chatting, or showing off the profile badge you’ve earned, your actions reflect on Discord itself.

We require owners, admins, and moderators in Partnered servers to uphold the rules in this Partner Code of Conduct and those detailed in our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.

Failure to uphold these standards will lead to a warning, both through email and in the application itself, and a chance to correct the violation. If action is not taken on the reported content within 48 hours, we will take additional action, including removing the partnership status. Any further violations of the Partner Code of Conduct may also remove the partnership.

The following Code of Conduct outlines our requirements for Partnered servers.

I. BEHAVIOR AND ENGAGEMENT WITH USERS

As a Partner, always consider how others may perceive your statements. Even if you intend something as a joke, there may be others who do not see it as such.

This does not mean we will revoke the partnership if a user says something offensive in your server. We understand the challenges of moderating big servers — especially ones with users from all over the world. However, we expect you to build a moderation team that will take action on issues within a reasonable timeframe. Having no moderation or claiming the server is too big to moderate is unacceptable.

Partnered servers should be an example of the best communities that Discord offers, so we have a higher standard for the conversation and moderation of those servers. The following are prohibited in a partnered Discord:

  • Discriminatory jokes and hate speech (attacks on an individual or group based on their race, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, sexual orientation, religious affiliation, or disabilities)
  • Moderators or admins make verbal abuse, insults, and threats towards others or display offensive, derogatory, or explicit content.
  • Advocating for or encouraging any of the above behavior.
  • Selling a Partnered server or account is prohibited. As a Discord Partner and a representative of Discord, you should be on good behavior on the Discord platform, across other social media platforms, and in real life. If we are made aware of situations where you are representing Discord poorly by, for example, violating other platforms’ Terms of Service or acting in a manner that is unbecoming of a Discord Partner, we may rescind the Partner status. Without warning, we reserve the right to de-partner any community based on their behavior, both on and off Discord.

II. ADULT CONTENT GUIDELINES

Explicit pornographic content does not have a place in Partnered servers. This includes videos, gifs, or still images depicting explicit sexual actions, whether real or illustrated and detailed verbal descriptions of explicit sexual acts. The Discord Partners Program is designed to highlight awesome communities and content creators and generally be welcoming to those of all ages.

However, conversations around adult topics are allowed — we understand that there are Partnered servers that deal with sensitive and difficult topics, and we welcome those conversations and communities. In those servers, those channels should be clearly marked and opt-in.

III. REPRESENTATIONS AND MISREPRESENTATIONS

Servers are Partnered based on their content and community at the point of application and for what that community will likely grow into. That means we expect your Discord will continue to be about the subject you applied for.

  • If you (the partner) are a content creator, your server should be centered around your content. Switching to a community-based server will void your partnership.
  • If you are a community server, your server’s focus should be the content under which you applied for partnership. Switching or repurposing the server from its original purpose will void your partnership. In short, we don’t appreciate a bait-and-switch. It’s totally understandable if you are a content creator and change from one game to another, but it’s less reasonable if you’re a community around RPGs and one day you delete all channels and change to be about your interest in football or vice versa.

Finally, you (the partner) must maintain ownership of your partnered Discord server to stay in the program. If you delete or transfer ownership for any reason without communication to Discord, your partnership, and all Discord perks will be revoked.

IV. MAINTAINING QUALITY CONTENT

Content creators or communities are expected to create original content. Complete copying or plagiarizing another party’s content will result in immediate removal from the partner program. We want our Partnered servers to reflect active Discord communities and users well.

Please note: We have the right to update this Code of Conduct at any time, and as Discord evolves, so may our expectations for our Partners. If this Code of Conduct changes, we’ll communicate those changes to you (the partner) accordingly.

As a Discord Partner, always remember to conduct yourself responsibly and treat others the way you’d like to be treated. We want to ensure that you are a shining example of the best parts of the platform and a prime example that other users should strive to be. Be the awesome you want to see in the world.

Discord Self-Service Advertising Terms

Effective Date: July 1, 2026

These Discord Self-Service Advertising Terms (these “Self-Service Advertising Terms”) govern your access to and use of the Discord Self-Service Ads Services (the “Ads Services”) to create, manage, and run advertising on Discord. They are entered into by Discord Inc. (“Discord,” “we,” or “us”) and the entity that accepts them (“Advertiser,” “you,” or “your”).

You may access the Ads Services through the Ads Manager, Discord’s self-service advertising interface. References in these Self-Service Advertising Terms to the Ads Manager describe a means of accessing the Ads Services and do not limit these terms to interface-based access.

These Self-Service Advertising Terms are subject to, and incorporate by reference, the Advertising Business Services Terms (the “Business Terms”), together with the Ads Policy and, to the extent you use them, the Attribution & Measurement Terms, the Custom Audience Terms, and the Events API Terms. Capitalized terms not defined here have the meaning given in the Business Terms.

Any product-specific terms made available in or linked to these Self-Service Advertising Terms apply when you use that product and such product terms control over any general terms for that product to the extent of any conflict. These Self-Service Advertising Terms control over the Business Terms solely as to their subject matter. The Discord Advertising IAB Addendum governs managed advertising and does not apply to self-service advertising.

Section 1: Definitions

In these Self-Service Advertising Terms:

“Ad” means advertising or other commercial content you create, submit, or run through the Ads Services.

“Ads Account” means the advertising account established and maintained under a Team and used to configure, run, and pay for Ads Campaigns.

“Ads Manager” means Discord’s self-service advertising interface, as made available from time to time, through which you may access the Ads Services.

“Ads Services” means the self-service advertising services Discord makes available, including the Ads Manager, Ads-related APIs, and the other tools and interfaces through which you access them, whether through the interface, an API, or an authorized partner.

“Campaign” means an advertising campaign configured through the Ads Services.

“Order” means your submission through the Ads Services to run a Campaign, including its budget and, where applicable, bid.

“Reward” means the Discord Orbs or other in-platform reward Discord makes available to users in connection with advertising on Discord.

“Team” means your Discord team (the same team construct used across Discord’s developer surfaces, including the Developer Portal) which you access using your Discord account and which serves as the account through which you accept these Self-Service Advertising Terms, provide and maintain your business information (such as your legal business name and tax identification), manage members and their roles, and establish and hold one or more Ads Accounts in the Ads Manager. Team roles, including the Owner and Admin roles, have the meaning given in the Developer Portal.

Section 2: Account Registration and Access

  1. Eligibility and Registration. To use the Ads Manager, you must establish and maintain a Team and at least one Ads Account under that Team, and you must provide accurate and current business, registration, and billing information, including your legal business name and tax identification. You must be able to form a binding contract and meet any eligibility requirements Discord sets. Discord may approve, decline, or condition a Team or Ads Account in its discretion. A Team and its Ads Accounts may be established and operated by an Advertiser for itself, or by an agency or other authorized party on behalf of one or more Advertisers, as described below.

You accept these Self-Service Advertising Terms at the Team level, and your acceptance applies to the Team and every Ads Account under it. Only an individual who holds an Owner or Admin role on the Team — a role with authority to manage the Team and its settings — is authorized to accept these Self-Service Advertising Terms on the Team’s behalf. By accepting, you represent that you hold an Owner or Admin role on the Team and that you have authority to bind the entity on whose behalf you accept; “you,” “your,” and “Advertiser” refer to that entity as well as to the individual accepting. Your acceptance binds that entity whether or not the Ads Manager restricts which role may accept.

If you accept these Self-Service Advertising Terms without authority to bind the entity on whose behalf you purport to accept, you are personally bound by, and liable under, these Self-Service Advertising Terms as the Advertiser for all Campaigns, Orders, charges, and other activity under the Team and its Ads Accounts, to the same extent as if you were the Advertiser.

  1. Responsibility for the Team and Ads Account(s). You are responsible for your Team and all activity under it and under each of your Ads Accounts, including the acts and omissions of every individual, agency, or other party you authorize to access or operate your Team or any Ads Account, and all Campaigns, Orders, and charges. Keep your credentials secure and promptly tell Discord of any unauthorized use. You are also responsible for monitoring your Team and each Ads Account and all Campaigns, Orders, and modifications (whether made by you, by a party you authorize, or by Discord on your behalf) including all Campaign settings, targeting, budgets, bids, and creative, any settings or parameters configured on your behalf before you accept these Self-Service Advertising Terms, and any changes made during a Campaign, and for promptly reviewing your billing statements and charges for accuracy.

  2. Authorized Users. You manage members and their access at the Team level through Team roles, and only an Owner or Admin may add, remove, or change the access of members. You may authorize individuals to access your Team and one or more Ads Accounts, and you are responsible for managing and revoking their access and for their compliance with the Terms.

  3. Advertisers Granting Access. If you authorize an agency or other party to access or operate your Team or any Ads Account, for all or specific Campaigns, you remain responsible for all activity under your Team and Ads Accounts, you control the scope and revocation of that access, you authorize that party to submit Orders, instructions, and approvals within that scope, and you will ensure it complies with the Terms. Granting access does not reduce your obligations. As the Advertiser, you are responsible for establishing your Team and Ads Account(s) and for accepting these Self-Service Advertising Terms, and you remain responsible and liable for all acts and omissions of any agency or other party you authorize, and for all Campaigns, Orders, charges, and other activity under your Team and Ads Accounts, to the same extent as if you had taken those actions yourself. Where an agency or other party will act on your behalf, Discord may require that you establish the Team and Ads Account(s) and accept these Self-Service Advertising Terms, that the agency or other party separately accept these Self-Service Advertising Terms, and that you then authorize it to access and act within your Team and its Ads Accounts; if the Ads Manager does not support a particular authorization method, Discord may require alternative evidence of your authorization. At Discord’s request, you will promptly provide written confirmation that you have authorized a party to act on your behalf and of the scope of that authorization.

  4. Agencies Acting for Advertisers. If you establish or operate a Team or Ads Account, or run Campaigns, on behalf of one or more other parties (for example, as their agency), you represent for each that you are authorized to act for and bind that party to the Terms and that your acts and omissions are within the scope of your authority. Each such party is an “Advertiser” under the Self-Service Advertising Terms. You are responsible for each Advertiser’s compliance with the Self-Service Advertising Terms. If you do not have authority to bind an Advertiser, or that Advertiser does not separately accept these Self-Service Advertising Terms, you are directly and personally bound by, and liable under, the Self-Service Advertising Terms as the Advertiser for all Campaigns, Orders, charges, and other activity associated with that Advertiser. At Discord’s request, you will promptly provide written confirmation of your relationship with, and authority to act for and bind, each Advertiser, and Discord may require other reasonable evidence of your authority.

  5. Multiple Advertisers. If you manage Campaigns for more than one Advertiser, you will accurately associate each Campaign and Order with the correct Advertiser, and the representations in this Section apply to each.

  6. Reliance. Discord may treat any Order, instruction, or approval submitted through your Team or any Ads Account as authorized by you and by any Advertiser on whose behalf you act.

  7. Discord-Operated Service. Where Ads Manager features are limited or unavailable, or at your request, Discord may access and operate your Team and Ads Account on your behalf, including to provide and configure your business, registration, and billing information, establish and manage your Ads Account, manage users and roles, and create, configure, submit Orders for, manage, optimize, or cancel Campaigns. Discord does so as a service and not as your agent; Discord’s operation of your Team or Ads Account does not make Discord a party to, or liable as the Advertiser under, these Self-Service Advertising Terms, and does not reduce your obligations. You remain responsible and liable for your Team, your Ads Account, and all Campaigns, Orders, charges, settings, and other activity, whether configured or submitted by you or by Discord on your behalf (including before you accept these Self-Service Advertising Terms), to the same extent as if you had taken those actions yourself. Discord’s operation does not substitute for acceptance of these Self-Service Advertising Terms by an Owner or Admin of your Team under Section 2(a). You may direct Discord to stop operating your Team or Ads Account at any time, and Discord may decline or discontinue this service in its discretion.

Section 3: Using the Ads Services

  1. License. Subject to the Self-Service Advertising Terms, Discord grants you a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable license to access and use the Ads Services to create and manage your own Campaigns. Discord reserves all rights not expressly granted.

  2. Configuration. You configure Campaigns in the Ads Manager, including the product, available targeting, budget, and bid, and you are responsible for your configuration and for all Ads, content, and destinations.

  3. Orders and Acceptance. When you submit an Order, you tell Discord the advertising you want to run, your spend, and, where applicable, your bid. Discord may accept or decline an Order and runs accepted Campaigns as inventory and availability allow.

  4. Auction and Pricing. Charges are based on the applicable billing metric for the product, including, where applicable, your bid in an auction. Auction, bidding, and pricing mechanics are described in the Ads Manager or applicable documentation; product-specific pricing is in the product terms. Bids, rates, and Charges may vary and change over time based on the auction and other factors, and any modification to a Campaign may affect the applicable rate and your Charges.

  5. Campaign Modifications. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, you may modify a Campaign, including pausing or cancelling it, at any time through the Ads Manager. A modification or cancellation may take a period of time to take effect, and you will be liable for all Charges incurred until the modification or cancellation is effective.

  6. Discord-Operated Campaigns. Some Ads Manager features may be limited or unavailable, and Discord may set up, manage, or optimize Campaigns on your behalf as a service; where it does, the Campaign remains subject to the Terms and your obligations are not reduced. Discord may also access and operate your Ads Account on your behalf as provided in Section 2(h).

  7. Ad Review and Approval. All Ads and Campaigns are subject to Discord’s review and the Ads Policy, and Discord may reject, remove, or decline to run any Ad or Campaign in its discretion.

  8. Your Responsibility for Ads, Targeting, and Compliance. You are solely responsible for your Ads and ad materials, the products and services you advertise, your landing pages and other destinations, and your targeting, bidding, trafficking, and other Campaign decisions, including those you make or change in real time through the Ads Manager and without Discord’s review of each Campaign. You are responsible for ensuring that your Ads and Campaigns, and the foregoing, comply with the Self-Service Advertising Terms, the Ads Policy, and all applicable laws, and that all claims and information in your Ads are accurate and not misleading. Discord’s review of, or decision to run, an Ad or Campaign does not relieve you of these responsibilities or constitute approval of your compliance.

  9. Automated and AI Features. Discord may make available automated or AI-assisted features that generate, suggest, or optimize creative, bids, budgets, targeting, or other Campaign settings. Any output of these features is generated by automated means and is not tested, verified, or guaranteed by Discord to be accurate, complete, or compliant. You are responsible for reviewing and approving any AI-generated or AI-suggested content, targeting, or modification before it is used in, or applied to, your Campaigns, and your use of these features does not reduce your responsibilities or obligations under the Terms, including those in the preceding subsection.

  10. Content License. You grant Discord a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable license to host, use, display, reproduce, and adapt (including resizing) the Ads, content, and marks you provide, as needed to deliver your Campaigns and provide and improve the advertising services. You retain your content and marks; Discord retains the Ads Manager, Rewards, and its data and measurements.

  11. Beta and Experimental Features. The Ads Manager, and some products, features, or campaign types, may be offered on a beta, pilot, or experimental basis, and Discord may test, change, or discontinue them. Beta and experimental features are provided “as is” and “as available,” may not function as described, and Discord has no liability for them beyond what the Self-Service Advertising Terms, or applicable product terms, provide.

  12. Feedback. If you give Discord feedback, suggestions, or ideas about the Ads Manager or the advertising services, Discord may use them for any purpose without restriction or obligation to you, and you grant Discord a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use and incorporate them.

  13. Rewards. Where Discord makes a Reward available to users in connection with your advertising, the Reward is Discord Orbs unless Discord specifies otherwise. Discord Orbs are redeemable only within Discord, have no cash value, and are governed by the Discord Orbs Terms in Discord’s Paid Services Terms. Discord administers and delivers Rewards to users; you have no liability to users for Rewards, and your payment for advertising is not a payment to any user. Discord may modify, substitute, or discontinue Rewards, which will not affect amounts owed for advertising already delivered.

Section 4: Prohibited Uses

In addition to the restrictions in the Business Terms, you will not: use the Ads Services other than as permitted; interfere with or disrupt them; access them by unauthorized means or circumvent their controls; use any robot, spider, scraper, or other automated means, or any data extraction, data mining, or harvesting technique, to access the Ads Services or extract data from them except as Discord expressly permits; misrepresent your identity or authority; use them to build a competing product; or use data obtained through them except as the Terms permit, including the restriction on using such data to train any AI or machine-learning model.

Section 5: Fees and Payment

  1. Charges. You will pay all charges for your Campaigns, based on the applicable billing metric and Discord’s measurements (Section 6).

  2. Budgets and Spend Controls. You may set budgets and spend controls in the Ads Manager. Actual spend may vary from, and may exceed, a stated budget within a reasonable tolerance due to the timing of measurement and delivery, and Discord will not knowingly charge you more than your budget.

  3. Invoicing. Unless otherwise agreed, Discord will invoice you, and you will pay undisputed amounts within thirty (30) days of the invoice date.

  4. Credit and Invoiced Billing. Discord will bill your Campaigns on an invoiced basis as provided in subsection (c). Discord may obtain credit authorizations, set and adjust credit limits, and condition or require continued eligibility for invoiced billing in its discretion. Where you apply for or use invoiced billing, Discord may obtain business credit reports about you and use them to assess your eligibility and to set or adjust your credit limit. Discord may make additional payment methods available in the future, and if it does, the terms governing those methods will apply when they are made available to you.

  5. Taxes. Amounts exclude any applicable taxes. You are responsible for any taxes, levies, or duties that apply to your Campaigns, including withholding taxes, (other than taxes on Discord’s net income,) and you will pay amounts due to Discord without reducing them for any such taxes. You will indemnify Discord for any claim arising from your failure to pay or remit taxes you owe.

  6. Late Payment. If you do not pay undisputed amounts when due, Discord may charge interest on the overdue amount at 1.5% per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law if lower, from the due date until paid. You will reimburse Discord’s reasonable costs of collection, including reasonable attorneys’ fees, and Discord may use a third party to collect overdue amounts.

  7. Billing Disputes. If you believe an invoice or charge is incorrect, you must notify Discord within thirty (30) days after the invoice or charge date, with reasonable supporting detail; charges not disputed within that period are final. Except as required by law or as the Terms expressly provide (for example, a credit under a product term), amounts invoiced and paid are non-refundable.

  8. Promotional Credits. Discord may offer promotional or advertising credits, which you may apply to eligible charges subject to any terms Discord specifies. Unless stated otherwise, credits are time-limited, have no cash value, are non-transferable, cannot be combined with other offers, and may be modified or revoked by Discord, and Discord’s decisions on the allocation and use of credits are final.

Section 6: Measurement and Reporting

Discord’s measurements are the authoritative basis for delivery and charges. Discord may provide reporting for your internal use, which is Discord’s Confidential Information and which you may disclose only as permitted in Section 10. While You may receive reports from approved measurement partners, such reports do not control billing, and Discord’s measurements control in the event of a discrepancy. Processing of personal data for measurement is governed by the Attribution and Measurement Terms. Where you, or an agency or other party acting on your behalf, transmit event, conversion, or similar data to Discord through the Discord Events API or a comparable integration in connection with Campaigns, the Events API Terms (or other terms Discord makes available for that integration) govern that data, together with these Self-Service Advertising Terms and the Attribution & Measurement Terms.

Section 7: No Guarantee; Placement Discretion

Self-service advertising is provided “as is” and “as available.” Discord does not guarantee any level of delivery, reach, results, or other outcomes, and estimates (including any estimated or projected CPM, CPC, or CPA rates, conversion volumes, audience sizes, and campaign performance) are not binding. Discord has sole discretion over whether, when, where, and to which users Ads are shown, including placement, targeting, frequency, and delivery, and may suspend or cease delivery at any time. Except as a product term expressly provides, Discord is not required to provide any makegood or credit for failing to deliver an estimated level of delivery.

Section 8: Invalid Activity

  1. Discord may monitor for, identify, and exclude invalid, fraudulent, automated, or otherwise non-genuine activity affecting Campaigns (“Invalid Activity”), by automated or manual means. Invalid Activity includes activity generated by bots, automated scripts, emulators, or click farms; activity resulting from hijacked devices or falsified device, location, or identity signals; and activity that is fraudulent or generated through deception. Discord does not warrant that it will identify or exclude all Invalid Activity.

  2. Invalid Activity is not billable, and Discord’s determination is final for charges, subject to any reconciliation in the Terms or a product term. Product terms may add product-specific Invalid Activity provisions, which control for that product. Discord’s sole obligation with respect to Invalid Activity that affects charges is to adjust or credit amounts as set out in the Self-Service Advertising Terms or the applicable product terms, and Discord has no further liability for Invalid Activity, including activity it does not detect or filter.

  3. You will reasonably cooperate with Discord in connection with the detection and investigation of Invalid Activity.

  4. Where Discord makes a Reward available to users in connection with advertising, the fact that a Reward is offered, or that a user may be motivated by it, does not by itself make activity Invalid Activity; Invalid Activity instead means activity that is automated, fraudulent, falsified, or otherwise not a genuine user’s good-faith engagement. Discord may withhold or revoke Rewards, and exclude or adjust affected Charges, for Invalid Activity. You acknowledge that where Discord makes a Reward available to users in connection with advertising, any related inventory is incentivized and that Discord’s measurements and reporting may identify and account for it as such.

Section 9: Suspension and Termination

Discord may suspend, limit, or terminate your access to the Ads Services, any Campaign, or these terms as set forth in the Business Terms or for any violation of the Terms. You may stop using the Ads Services at any time. You remain responsible for amounts incurred before termination, and provisions that should survive will survive.

Section 10: Confidentiality

Without limiting the Business Terms, you will not disclose Discord’s non-public pricing, bid or auction information, or non-public performance or reporting data relating to your use of the Ads Services, except as the Business Terms permit. Notwithstanding the foregoing, you may disclose performance and reporting data relating to your own Campaigns to your service providers and measurement partners acting on your behalf, provided that Discord has approved any measurement partner that will receive such data (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld), solely to measure, verify, or analyze the performance of your Campaigns and subject to confidentiality obligations at least as protective as these Self-Service Advertising Terms, and you remain responsible for each recipient’s compliance. You will not publish that data publicly or disclose it to any other advertiser, agency, or advertising network, and you will require each recipient to use it solely to provide measurement, verification, or analysis to you and not to further disclose it. You, your service providers, and your measurement partners will retain that data only as long as needed for those purposes and will delete it when it is no longer needed. This Section does not permit disclosure of Discord’s Attribution Results, which are governed by the Attribution & Measurement Terms.

Section 11: Representations and Warranties

In addition to the Business Terms, you represent and warrant that: (a) you have the right and authority to enter into the Self-Service Advertising Terms and to advertise the products, services, and destinations in your Campaigns; (b) you own or have all rights, licenses, and consents necessary to provide the Ads, content, and marks you submit and to grant the license in Section 3; (c) your Ads, content, and destinations comply with the Self-Service Advertising Terms and applicable law and do not infringe or misappropriate any third-party rights; (d) the information you provide is accurate; and (e) you will not engage in, encourage, or facilitate Invalid Activity, and your destinations and applications are not designed or operated to generate it; and (f) any measurement or Events API integration you use is implemented and operated in accordance with such products respective terms, Discord’s technical specifications and documentation, and the event data you transmit is accurate, complete, and not generated by automated, fraudulent, or deceptive means.

Section 12: Other Terms

  1. Indemnification; Liability. The indemnification and limitation of liability provisions of the Business Terms apply to these Self-Service Advertising Terms and your use of the Ads Services, as well as any self-service advertising products. Without limiting those provisions, you will indemnify Discord for claims arising out of your Ads, content, marks, and destinations, your targeting, bidding, and trafficking decisions, your landing pages and destination URLs, the data you transmit to Discord (including through the Events API), the products and services you advertise, and your use of the Ads Services, except to the extent such claim is caused by Discord.

  2. Disputes; Governing Law. The dispute resolution, governing law, and related provisions of the Business Terms apply to these Self-Service Advertising Terms and your use of the Ads Services, including the arbitration agreement and class-action waiver and the governing-law and venue provisions set out there. To the extent the Business Terms allow you to opt out of arbitration within a stated period measured from a signed insertion order or its effective date, for self-service advertising that period instead runs from the date you first accept these Self-Service Advertising Terms.

  3. Modifications. Discord may modify these Self-Service Advertising Terms as set forth in the Business Terms, and your continued use of the Ads Manager or Ad Services after the effective date is considered acceptance.

  4. Entire Agreement. These Self-Service Advertising Terms, including any Supplemental Ads Terms under Section 13, supplement the Business Terms and the other Terms and are the entire agreement on self-service advertising, superseding any prior agreement on that subject.

  5. Notices and Electronic Communications. Discord may give you notices about the Ads Manager and these terms through the Ads Manager, by email to your account address, or by other reasonable means, and you consent to receive communications, including invoices, electronically. You will keep your account contact and billing information accurate and current.

Section 13: Supplemental Ads Products and Services

You may choose to use products, services, features, and tools that Discord makes available to supplement the Ads Services (collectively, “Supplemental Ads Products and Services”). Discord may modify, suspend, terminate access to, or discontinue any Supplemental Ads Product and Service at any time in its discretion. If you use any Supplemental Ads Product and Service, your use is subject to the additional terms and policies Discord makes available for it, and your continued use indicates your acceptance of those terms and policies (collectively, “Supplemental Ads Terms”). A Supplemental Ads Term controls over these Self-Service Advertising Terms for the applicable Supplemental Ads Product and Service to the extent of any conflict.

Discord’s Supplemental Ads Products and Services and the applicable Supplemental Ads Terms include:

Discord-Operated Services (Discord setting up, managing, optimizing, or operating your Team, Ads Account, or Campaigns on your behalf): governed by Section 2(h) and Section 3 of these Self-Service Advertising Terms.

Data tools that import data to, or export data from, the Ads Services (including Custom Audiences, measurement and reporting tools, pixels, postback URLs, and software development kits): governed by the Attribution & Measurement Terms, or the Custom Audience Terms, as applicable.

Ads-related APIs (including the Events API and any other advertising API Discord makes available): governed by the Events API Terms (or other terms Discord makes available for that API) and the applicable API documentation.

You agree to be bound by these Self-Service Advertising Terms and any applicable Supplemental Ads Terms when you access or use the applicable Supplemental Ads Product and Service.

Discord Supplier Code of Conduct

Discord is committed to cultivating belonging and striving for excellence by treating all workers with respect, ensuring safe working conditions, being environmentally responsible, and leading with integrity and good faith ethical practices. We expect our suppliers and their subsidiaries, affiliates, and subcontractors (“Suppliers”) to operate their businesses with social, ethical, and environmental responsibility and integrity. This Supplier Code of Conduct describes the legal, environmental, and social obligations for our Suppliers.

1. Compliance

When providing goods and services to Discord, Suppliers are required to fully comply with all applicable laws and regulations. They must also meet the expectations outlined in this Supplier Code of Conduct, along with any contractual requirements and additional terms.

Suppliers are expected to maintain a system designed to enable its operations to conform to the standards in this Supplier Code of Conduct and also record, identify, mitigate, and remediate any gaps and operational risks. Upon request from Discord, Suppliers will accurately disclose information regarding their labor, health and safety, environmental practices, business activities, structure, financial situation, and performance, in accordance with prevailing industry practices. Suppliers will also allow and enable Discord (and any third party representing Discord) to assess a Supplier’s compliance with this Supplier Code of Conduct by inspecting and reviewing the Supplier’s facilities, practices, policies, and relevant records without notice and interviewing personnel without disruption or monitoring. Suppliers will communicate clear and accurate information about their practices, policies, and expectations to their workers, next-tier supplier(s), and customers, and will train their employees on their requirements under this Supplier Code of Conduct. Suppliers will promptly implement reasonable corrective action to remedy any material non-conformance identified by Discord. Though we might seek to work with Suppliers to improve conditions, we also may terminate our relationship with any Supplier that fails to meet any of these responsibilities.

2. Labor and Human Rights

At Discord, we firmly believe in treating all workers with respect and dignity. We hold our Suppliers to the same standard and expect them to prioritize the well-being of their workers. This includes ensuring that all workers, regardless of their employment type, are treated with human decency. Our Suppliers must adhere to the following standards in their operations:

No Forced Labor. Suppliers will not use forced, bonded (including debt bondage), indentured, or involuntary prison labor, and will not engage in slavery or trafficking of any person. No matter the situation, all work must be voluntary, and workers should be able terminate their employment at any time. Suppliers will not require workers to pay any recruitment or employment fees or expenses. Suppliers will ensure that workers always have access to their identity, immigration, or work permit documents. This means Suppliers may not hold, destroy, conceal, or confiscate identity or immigration documents, such as government-issued identification, passports, or work permits. Suppliers can only hold documentation if required by law. Even so, workers should never be denied access to their documents. Suppliers should make sure that each worker receives a written agreement describing the terms of employment, and if there is international relocation involved, the agreement must be given and signed prior to the relocation.

No Child Labor. Suppliers will not use child labor. “Child” means any person under age 15, under the age for completing compulsory education, or under the minimum age for employment in the country, whichever is greatest. Workers under the age of 18 will not perform work that is likely to jeopardize their health or safety, including night shifts, overtime, or physically or psychologically demanding work. In the absence of local law, suppliers must pay student workers, interns, and apprentices at least the same wage rates as other entry-level workers performing equal or similar tasks.

Wages. Suppliers will pay legally-mandated wages and benefits and comply with the law regarding wage deductions. Suppliers must also provide workers with the basis on which workers are paid via pay stub or similar documentation. Deductions from wages as a disciplinary measure is not permitted.

Working Hours. Except in emergency situations, Suppliers will set a maximum of 60 hours per week (including overtime) for any workers paid on an hourly basis. Workers should be allowed at least one day off every seven days. All overtime hours must be voluntary.

Abuse, Discrimination, and Harassment. Suppliers will not discriminate in screening, hiring, or employment practices based on race, color, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, ethnicity, national origin, caste, disability, genetic information, medical condition, pregnancy, religion, political affiliation, union membership, covered veteran status, or any other category protected by applicable law. Workers’ religious practices should be reasonably accommodated.

Fostering Diversity. Because diversity, equity, and inclusion is crucial to us, our Suppliers must also demonstrate a commitment to fostering diversity and inclusion in all aspects of the workplace.

Freedom of Association. Suppliers will respect workers rights to associate freely, bargain collectively, and seek representation in accordance with local laws. Suppliers are expected to permit workers to openly communicate and share grievances with management without fear of reprisal, intimidation, discrimination, or harassment.

3. Health & Safety

Suppliers must ensure that all operations happen in healthy and safe working conditions for its workers. Suppliers will further ensure that the following requirements are met:

Occupational Safety and Health. Suppliers will comply with all applicable safety and health laws and regulations. Suppliers will identify, evaluate, and control worker exposure to safety and health hazards, such as chemical, biological, physical, and ergonomic stressors, and other elements of physically demanding work, through proper design, engineering controls, maintenance, safe work procedures, and ongoing health and safety guidance. Suppliers must also identify, evaluate, and control worker exposure to the hazards of physically demanding tasks, including manual material handling and heavy or repetitive lifting, prolonged standing, and highly repetitive or forceful assembly tasks. When these methods cannot adequately control risks, suppliers must provide workers with personal protective gear and education about the risks involved in the language of the worker or in a language the worker can understand. Suppliers will implement procedures to prevent, manage, track, and report occupational injury and illness.

Machine Safeguarding. Production and other machinery shall be evaluated for safety hazards. Physical guards, interlocks, and barriers are to be provided and properly maintained where machinery presents an injury hazard to workers.

Emergency Preparedness. Suppliers will identify and plan for potential emergencies, and Suppliers will implement emergency plans and provide guidance to workers on emergency response procedures, including emergency reporting, worker notification and evacuation, drills, fire detection and suppression equipment, exit facilities, and recovery plans in accordance with local law.

Sanitation, Food, and Housing. Suppliers will provide workers with ready access to clean toilet facilities, potable water, and sanitary food preparation, storage, and eating facilities. If Suppliers provide workers with housing, those facilities will be clean and safe, including but not limited to adequate personal space, entry and exit privileges, emergency egresses, heat and ventilation, adequate lighting, and hot water for bathing and showering.

4. Environmental

We expect that our Suppliers will strive to create regenerative processes to minimize adverse effects on the community, environment, and natural resources while safeguarding the health and safety of the public. This includes the following:

Environmental Permits and Reporting. Suppliers will obtain and keep current all required environmental permits, approvals, and registrations and follow their operational and reporting requirements.

Resource Efficiency and Clean Energy. Suppliers will work to reduce consumption of resources, including raw materials, energy, and water. Suppliers will seek to minimize energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, improve energy efficiency, and use cleaner sources of energy.

Hazardous and Restricted Substances. Suppliers will manage chemicals and other materials that pose a hazard to the environment to ensure their safe handling, use, storage, and disposal. Suppliers will identify, monitor, control, treat, and reduce hazardous air emissions, wastewater, and waste generated from its operations.

Waste Mitigation. Suppliers will work to reduce or eliminate waste of all types. Where waste cannot be eliminated, Suppliers will manage all waste streams in compliance with applicable laws and regulations and in an environmentally responsible and secure way; this includes, but is not limited to, preventing illegal discharges and spills from entering storm drains and treating as required prior to discharge or disposal of all wastewater and solid waste from operations, industrial processes, and sanitation facilities.

Air Emissions. Suppliers will characterize, monitor, control, and treat air generated by its operations prior to discharge.

Materials Restrictions. Suppliers are to adhere to all applicable laws, regulations, and customer requirements regarding the prohibition or restriction of specific substances in products and manufacturing, including labeling for recycling and disposal.

Water Management. Supplier shall implement a water management program that documents, characterizes, and monitors water sources, use and discharge; seeks opportunities to conserve water; and controls channels of contamination. All wastewater is to be characterized, monitored, controlled, and treated as required prior to discharge or disposal.

5. Ethics

Discord places a strong emphasis on upholding ethical standards to promote honesty and integrity in business operations. Our Suppliers are expected to comply with all requirements listed below:

Conflicts. Suppliers will avoid actual or apparent conflicts of interest in their work with Discord. Suppliers will immediately disclose any known family or other close personal relationships with Discord’s employees who have an influence over their engagements with Discord.

Gifts. If Suppliers extend any business courtesies to our employees, they will do so infrequently, and the courtesies must be of no more than moderate value. Suppliers will also accurately reflect their business dealings in their books and records. Suppliers will have a zero-tolerance policy that prohibits all forms of bribery (covering promising, offering, giving, or accepting any bribes), corruption, extortion, fraud, and embezzlement, and will implement monitoring and enforcement procedures to ensure conformance with anti-corruption laws. Suppliers will not make illegal payments directly or indirectly.

Intellectual Property. Suppliers will respect intellectual property rights and the confidential information of others. Suppliers will conduct technology and know-how transfers in a manner protecting intellectual property rights and confidential information.

Privacy and Information Security. Suppliers will protect the privacy of personal information of everyone with whom they do business, including suppliers, customers, consumers, and workers.

Responsible Materials Sourcing. Suppliers will maintain a policy reasonably assuring that any tantalum, tin, tungsten, and gold in products they manufacture does not directly or indirectly benefit armed groups that commit human rights abuses, including in or near the Democratic Republic of Congo. Suppliers will exercise, and will make available to us upon request, due diligence on the source and chain of custody of these minerals.

Fair Business, Advertising & Competition. Suppliers must obey applicable laws and industry and regulatory standards of fair business, advertising, and competition.

6. Accessibility.

Discord is committed to incorporating accessibility into the design of its products (learn more here: discord.com). Suppliers will embed relevant web accessibility standards, innovation, and best practices to deliver inclusive products and services for our users and stakeholders.

Discord’s Brand Partnership Guidelines

Discord was designed to bring people together. It is our hope that users on our platform are able to meaningfully connect with others around common interests. Partnerships with individuals, organizations, or brands can greatly assist our effort to create belonging based on the partners our users care about.

We expect those partners and our revenue sources to meet the standards of our values, specifically integrity, impact, and compassion, and policies, such as our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. We created this policy to articulate what kinds of partnerships we prohibit, consideration we will have when partnering, and ways to mitigate issues that may arise.

Partners are companies/entities that our community, talent, BD, branded communities teams directly engage with to support them in the creation or maintenance of a server on our platform.

Thus, Discord prohibits partners who:

  • Inconsistent with our Policies:
    • Target those under 13 years of age.
    • Infringe on someone else’s copyright, trademark, or intellectual property.
    • Engage or attempt to engage in any transaction involving controlled or regulated substances
    • Promote gambling, especially to minors.
    • Conduct harmful off-platform behaviors related to credible violent extremism, violent threats, and child abuse.
    • Promote hate speech or hateful conduct.
    • Share violence and gore with the intent to harass or shock non-consensually.
  • Inconsistent with our Values:
    • Promote pharmaceutical products or specific healthcare services, such as diet products.
    • Spread misinformation around COVID-19, vaccines, climate change denial, or election information.
    • Share or focus on sexually explicit content.
    • Conduct illegal or unethical business practices.
    • Promote the sale, exchange, or building of weapons and weapon accessories. Additional considerations for partnership, such as a partners’ commitments to diversity, equity, & inclusion, human rights, and sustainability, are included. Policy also suggested mitigations of potentially prohibiting content for account managers to get their partners to compliance.

Our Values

Values are quite simply the behaviors that we value in ourselves and the partners we would with. These are the fundamental truths that we hold which guide our decision making and behavior in all our work, especially with the brands, organizations, individuals, and causes we associate ourselves to.

The values we hold ourselves to are integrity, collaboration, excellence, impact, speed, transparency, and compassion. Of our values, we will focus on ensuring partners have integrity, have a positive impact, and are compassionate.

  • Integrity: The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles; moral uprightness.
    • We have always believed that being honest, honoring commitments, and doing what’s morally right in the long run is the best way to live life, even when it’s painful in the short term.
  • Impact: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another
    • We want our time on this Earth to mean something. We want to contribute to improving the human condition, and be a force for good by doing something that leaves the world a little bit better than we found it. This means a relentless focus on what is true, what matters, and building value over time through compounding leverage.
  • Compassion: Empathy and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others.
    • We are all human and with that comes all the challenges and tribulations of life. Work takes up a lot of time for most of us, but is it not the entirety of our experiences. In order to show up and give our mission its all, people need to be able to be themselves - both on good days and bad. Let’s not force people to be half of themselves. Instead, let’s be mindful and supportive of each other, knowing that we all are striving to do the best for ourselves, our families, our company, and our communities.

Our Policies

In addition to Partnership Guidelines, Partners must follow Discord’s Terms of Service, Community Guidelines, and all the policies on our Help Center governing our service. Please take a moment to review them.

Overall, Discord and our partners, their accounts, and their servers should be in compliance with our policies, aligned with our values, and a Force for Good for our users in the communities they live.

Partnership Policy

Prohibit Content or Purposes

Below are prohibited content and partner purposes. If a partner violates any of the below, they cannot partner with Discord. There are some types of prohibitions that can be mitigated, so please check the Mitigations section for more information.

  • Age: Discord prohibits inappropriate content targeting minors and users under 13.
    • Inappropriate content based on targeted user age.
      • For example: Alcohol content, sexually explicit content, etc for minors.
    • Under 13 year olds
      • No partners or their products that feature children under 13 or primarily target children under 13 for their product. A child-related brand, like a children’s TV network, can be a partner if the content in the server is NOT designed to reach or market to under 13.
  • Community Guidelines: Discord prohibits content or activity within the partner’s server or account that violate our Community Guidelines.
    • Past Violations: We should not partner with accounts or servers that have violated our Community Guidelines.
      • If a partner’s account or server violated any of our highest harm Commuinity Guideslines (Violent Extremism, Violent Threats, or Child Sexual Abuse) in the past, they cannot partner with us.
      • If a partner’s account or server violated any of our other Community Guidelines in the last 3 months, they cannot partner with us until 3 months has passed or they express regret and rehabilitation.
  • Copyright & Trademark: Discord prohibits the infringement on others’ copyright, trademark, intellectual property rights, or that promotes the sale of counterfeit goods.
  • Controlled & Illegal Substances: Discord prohibits the sale, buying, trading, or organizing the distribution of controlled, regulated, or illegal substances through our service. We define a controlled substance as any drug or chemical compound that is controlled or otherwise regulated by the US federal government. A non-exhaustive list of such goods includes: alcohol, tobacco (including vaping products), marijuana, pharmaceuticals without a prescription, narcotics, and other drugs.
    • Discussion of legal, controlled substances is allowed in age-restricted spaces.
  • Gambling Content: Discord prohibits the promotion of gambling content. We define gambling content as placing bets or wagers on games of chance for prizes with real-world value. Discussions of gambling and gambling themes do not by themselves constitute a violation of this policy. Special consideration should be given in instances of suspected gambling that appear to target vulnerable populations (e.g., minors, at-risk gamblers) or that feature forms of addictive gameplay.
  • Harmful Off-Platform Behaviors: If we become aware of specific off-platform high harm activities with credible evidence committed by a Discord user, we will take the reported off-platform harmful activities into account when assessing a partnership.
    • This policy applies to our highest harm Community guidelines: Violent Extremism, Violent Threats, and Child Sexual Abuse.
  • Hateful Content: Discord prohibits the user or promotion of hate speech or hateful conduct. We define hate speech as any form of expression that denigrates, vilifies, or dehumanizes; promotes intense, irrational feelings of enmity (“hatred”); or incites harm against people on the basis of protected characteristics. This includes the use of hate symbols as well as claims casting doubt on mass atrocities.
  • Specific Healthcare Products: Discord prohibits the promotion of all pharmaceutical products and services, and some healthcare products and services. Restrictions are based on the specific product or service being promoted, as well as the country that the campaign is targeting.
    • Diet products: A partner cannot be focused on or promote a product focused on dieting, losing weight, or miracle cures for obesity. This content is sensitive and can promote disordered eating and self-harm.
  • Misinformation: Discord prohibits the sharing of some types of false or misleading information (otherwise known as misinformation). Content that is false, misleading, and can lead to significant risk of physical or societal harm may not be shared on Discord. We specifically prohibit:
    • Health misinformation, particularly vaccine misinformation or COVID misinformation.
    • Climate change deniers and misleading information.
    • Election misinformation, including incorrect information around voting registration requirements, due dates for registration, and date or logistics related to voting day.
  • Sexually Explicit Content: Discord prohibits the partnership with partners who primarily produce or are trying to promote a specific server featuring sexually explicit content. Sexually explicit content is defined as simulated, drawn, or real media (images, audio, video) or text of pornography, sexual acts (including with sex toys), full nudity, implied nudity, and soliciting or offering sexual services. This content is shared with the explicit and exclusive purpose of sexual arousal.
  • Illegal or Unethical Business Practices: Discord prohibits partnering with individuals, organizations, or brands with a history of illegal or unethical business practices.
    • Illegal Business Practices is any criminal history or current criminal investigations around business or labor practices.
    • Unethical Behaviors include actions that strongly endanger the human rights of their employees, contractors, or communities they work. Such as a partner with known supply chains featuring slave labor.
  • Violence & Gore: Do not share real media depicting gore, excessive violence, or animal harm, especially with the intention to harass or shock others.
    • Fictional, drawn, or video game violence is OK as long as it is not meant to harass and is gated properly for specific ages.
  • Weapons and Weapon Accessories: Discord prohibits the promotion of weapons and weapon accessories. This includes 3D printed weapons, such as 3D printed guns and instruction manuals to print your own.

Considerations

We will also consider the following dimensions when assessing an individual, organization, or brand to partner. Many of these considerations align closely to our values and would boost the benefit of such a partnership. However, they are not requirements or blockers to partnerships. We will review the following:

  • Diversity & Inclusion Commitments: The partner has made external commitments or shown their diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts internally for their teams and externally in their impact on the world. This includes:
    • External diversity statements and messaging
    • Commitment to or current progress on ensuring diversity in leadership
    • Commitment to or current progress on ensuring diversity in the great employee base.
  • Human Rights & Ethics Commitments: The partner has made external commitments or shown their human rights standards and ethical business practices internally for their teams and externally in their impact on the world.
    • Business & Human Rights Practices
      • Non-profit or BCorporations
      • Companies with high ratings with Better Business Bureau: bbb.org
  • Ethical Labor Practices
    • Feedback from employees and contractors, such as Glassdoor reviews.
    • Recent press coverage of labor practices
    • Formal complaints to government regulators.
  • Political Partners and Content.
    • Partnerships with government, politicians, public officials, and other institutions are OK, as long as the partners do not violate other parts of this policy. Political content remains a highly sensitive content type due to regional tensions, crises, upheavals, and other human rights concerns, so we should review with caution.
  • Sustainability Commitments: The partner has made external commitments to be sustainable and lessen their impact on climate change.
    • Climate Change Commitments
    • Supply Chain Sustainability

Mitigations

When working with a partner who may have content, products, or audiences that may touch upon any of the prohibited content, account managers can build in mitigations to prevent prohibits content or actions , such as:

  • Enact age-gates for servers and channels.
  • Ensure the server is age appropriate to the youngest user they plan to target.
  • Enact notices for the types of content or audiences expected in the server or event. Notices include:
    • Adding language to the server title, description, rules, or verification channels reiterating the expected age of users in the space.
    • Adding a questionnaire to prompt age verification.
  • Enlist the Discord Moderator Program to assist with moderation of the space in compliance with our Moderator Academy standards.

Enforcement

When an account manager reviews a partner or contract, they must review this policy to see if the partner is in compliance. If a partner represents or produces content that is prohibited without necessary mitigations, we will not partner with that individual, organization, or brand.

If an account manager feels there are potential ways to get into compliance with the policy, they can escalate information about the partner and potential mitigations to policy@discord.com

Escalations

If you have a question about whether a partner is in compliance with this policy, mitigations, or any other question, please email policy@discord.com. We will review your question based on the policy and may consult with IDP, Legal, and other policy partners.

Discord’s Copyright & IP Policy

We respect the intellectual property of others, and expect everyone who uses Discord to do the same.

Copyright Policy

Copyright complaints: If you believe your copyrighted material is being infringed upon, the most efficient way to request the removal of the allegedly infringing content is to file a DMCA takedown request using the form here.

Do not mislead Discord’s support teams. Do not make false or malicious reports to our Legal Response or other customer support teams, send multiple reports about the same issue, or ask a group of users to report the same content or issue. Repeated violations of this guideline may result in account warnings or other penalties.

Alternatively, you can email our Copyright Agent at copyright@discord.com (subject line “DMCA Takedown Request”) or send us a letter at Discord, Attention: DMCA Takedown Request, 444 De Haro Street #200, San Francisco, CA 94107. Your notice must include:

  • A description of the work you think has been infringed;
  • A description of where the material you think is infringing is located on our services (detailed enough so that we can find it, including identifiers like message links or other IDs);
  • A statement that you have a good faith belief that the disputed use is not authorized by the copyright or intellectual property owner, its agent, or the law, and that the information in your notice is accurate;
  • A statement, made under penalty of perjury, that you are the copyright or intellectual property owner, or authorized to act on the copyright or intellectual property owner’s behalf;
  • Your name and contact information so you can be reached including mailing address, telephone number, and/or email address;
  • Your physical or electronic signature. Counter-notices: If you believe that your removed or disabled content did not infringe on copyright, or was removed as the result of a mistake or misidentification, you may file a DMCA counter-notice using the form here.

There are legal and financial consequences for fraudulent or bad faith submissions. Please confirm that you are the rights holder, or have the authority to act on the rights holder’s behalf, and that you understand the repercussions of submitting a false claim.

Counter-notices. If you believe that your removed or disabled content did not infringe any intellectual property rights, you may send our Copyright Agent a counter-notice with the following information:

  • Identification of the content that’s been removed or disabled and the content’s location before it was removed or disabled;
  • A statement that you have a good faith belief that the content was removed or disabled as a result of a mistake or a misidentification of the content;
  • Your name and contact information so you can be reached including mailing address, telephone number, and/or email address;
  • A statement that you consent to the jurisdiction of Federal District Court for the judicial district in which your address is located, or if your address is outside of the United States, to the Northern District of California, and that you will accept service of process from the person who notified Discord of the alleged infringement;
  • Your physical or electronic signature. Discord is unable to process counter-notifications with missing or defective elements. If your counter-notification contains missing or defective elements we will notify you of the missing or defective elements and ask that you submit a new, corrected, counter-notification.

Complaint resolution. If our Copyright Agent receives a valid counter-notice to a complaint, we’ll forward it to the complaining party. If there’s still a dispute, it’s up to the parties to then resolve the issue in court. Unless the copyright owner notifies us that they have filed an action seeking a court order against the content provider, member, or user, the removed content may be replaced, or access to it restored, in 10 to 14 business days or more after receipt of the counter-notice, at our sole discretion. Infringement consequences. We may delete or disable content alleged to be infringing. It’s our policy to terminate account holders who we determine to be repeat copyright infringers.

Trademark Policy

Trademark complaints. If you believe someone is infringing your trademark rights, let us know via the procedure below. To submit a complaint of trademark infringement go here and select “Trademark Complaint” from the drop-down menu. Please provide all the information requested in the form. If you submit an incomplete report, we will need to follow up about the missing information, which will likely delay the processing of your request.

Once we have reviewed your request, we will inform the user or server owner of your complaint. We may provide the account holder with your name and other information included in the copy of the report.

Trademark appeals. The user will have 7 days to respond (or longer if required by law) and make a good faith representation that they have a legally defensible claim to use the mark.

Complaint resolution. If we do not receive a response from the subject of the complaint, the content will remain down. If we receive a valid counter-notice, we will inform the complainant. It will be the responsibility of the complainant to seek alternative methods to enforce their trademark rights.

Infringement consequences. If we determine that you violated our trademark policy, we may terminate your account. It is our policy to terminate account holders who we determine to be repeat infringers, and it is within our discretion to ban an account upon receiving a single valid complaint.

Events API Terms

Effective Date: September 18, 2026

This Events API License (the “EAPI Terms”) governs the Partner’s (“you”, “your”, “Partner”, whether acting directly or through third parties on Partner’s behalf, for whom Partner is fully responsible) use of the Events API. The EAPI Terms supplement the Discord Developer Terms of Service (the “Developer Terms”), the Advertising Business Services Terms (the “Business Terms”), the Attribution and Measurement Terms (the “Attribution Terms”); and any applicable terms or conditions in an Insertion Order(s) (each, an “IO”) between the parties (collectively with the Developer Terms, the Business Terms, the Attribution Terms, and any other applicable Discord terms and policies, the “Terms”). Capitalized terms used but not defined in these EAPI Terms have the meanings given in the applicable Terms. In the event of a conflict between these EAPI Terms and any of the Terms, the EAPI Terms will control solely with respect to the subject matter of such conflict. The EAPI Terms apply to Partner Data from the point at which Partner first transmits such data to Discord via EAPI. For the avoidance of doubt, the Developer Terms govern Partner’s access to and use of EAPI as an API, and these EAPI Terms, Business Terms and Attribution Terms govern the advertising and data-related aspects of Partner’s use of EAPI. To the extent Partner transmits data to Discord via EAPI that would otherwise be governed by the Business Terms, any other terms, or any IO, these Terms shall control with respect to such data.

Section 1: Definitions

For purposes of these EAPI Terms, the following definitions apply in addition to those in the Terms:

“Attribution Results” has the meaning set forth in the Attribution Terms.

“EAPI” or “Events API” means Discord’s server-to-server application programming interface that enables Partner to transmit Partner Data directly to Discord for the purposes described in these EAPI Terms.

“Event Data” has the meaning set forth in the Attribution Terms.

“Matching Attributes” means Personal Data (which can include, but is not limited to, hashed emails, hashed phone numbers, hashed mobile identifiers) provided by Partner to Discord via EAPI that enables Discord to match individuals with Discord user accounts for the purpose of targeting advertising or other communications to those matched users on the Discord platform.

“Partner Data” means any data transmitted by Partner to Discord via EAPI, including, but not limited to, Event Data and Matching Attributes.

Section 2: Scope & Purpose

a. Scope

Discord is making EAPI available to you to transmit Partner Data to Discord via a server-to-server integration. EAPI may include, but is not limited to, the following capabilities: (i)transmission of Event Data for attribution, conversion tracking, analytics, and campaign optimization; (ii) transmission of Matching Attributes for audience matching and targeting; and (iii) transmission of other data types.You acknowledge that the EAPI features may be changed or removed at Discord’s sole discretion. Partner also acknowledges that EAPI is provided “AS IS” without warranties of any kind. Discord makes no representations regarding EAPI’s availability, accuracy, or fitness for any particular purpose. Partner assumes all risk associated with its use of EAPI.

b. Purpose

Discord may use Partner Data, alone or in combination with Discord’s own data and other information, for: (i) providing advertising services; (ii) developing and providing campaign attribution, conversion tracking, analytics, insights, and metrics (including generating Attribution Results as described in the Attribution Terms); (iii) creating and managing custom audiences for targeting; (iv) targeting and optimizing campaigns; (v) optimizing Discord’s systems and services; and (vi) developing and improving Discord’s products and services (collectively, the “Purpose”).

c. License

Subject to your compliance with the Terms, Discord grants you a limited, non-exclusive, non-sublicensable, non-transferable, non-assignable, revocable license to access and use EAPI solely as necessary to transmit Partner Data to Discord, to the extent permitted under the Terms. Discord reserves all rights, title, and interest not expressly granted herein.

d. Activation and Cross-Campaign Application

The EAPI Terms apply when you first transmit Partner Data to Discord via EAPI. Once activated, these EAPI Terms govern all Partner Data transmitted to Discord by or through EAPI, and to the extent of any conflict, controls over the Business Terms and any applicable IO with respect to such data. For clarity: (1) EAPI serves as a persistent delivery mechanism for all Partner Data transmitted to Discord by or through EAPI; (2) Partner Data transmitted via EAPI shall be treated according to the Purpose of these EAPI Terms, including for all Ad campaigns whether or not identified in applicable IO(s) between the parties, or whether such IO(s) are in effect as of the Effective Date or entered thereafter; and, (3) if Partner transmits data to Discord using both EAPI and other delivery methods (e.g., through an Attribution Partner), these EAPI Terms govern only the data transmitted via EAPI. Data delivered through other methods continues to be governed by the Attribution Terms, Custom Audience Terms, or other terms, as applicable.

Section 3: Data Provisions

  1. To the extent Partner transmits Partner Data to Discord via EAPI, each party shall act as an independent Controller with respect to such Partner Data under these EAPI Terms. Discord may use and combine Partner Data with Discord’s own data and other information for use consistent with the Purpose. Without limiting the foregoing, all Partner Data transmitted via EAPI is subject to the data protection obligations set forth in Section 4 of the Attribution Terms (Roles, Data Protection Obligations).

  2. To the extent Partner Data is subject to US State Privacy Laws (as included in Applicable Data Protection Laws): (i) you disclose Partner Data to Discord for the limited and specified purposes described in Section 2(b), and Discord will use Partner Data only for those purposes; (ii) Discord receives such data as a third party and independent business, and you are responsible for providing any required notices and honoring consumer opt-outs prior to transmission; and (iii) Discord will provide the level of privacy protection for Partner Data as required of businesses under such laws, will notify you if it determines it can no longer meet its obligations under such laws, and upon such notice you may take reasonable and appropriate steps to stop and remediate any unauthorized use of Partner Data, including by exercising your deletion right under Section 5.

Section 4: Partner Obligations

a. Integration and Compliance

Partner will integrate with EAPI in accordance with applicable documentation made available by Discord and will comply with all applicable rate limits, technical specifications, and security requirements provided to Partner in writing.
