Enhanced Role Styles for your server’s Server Boosting Role is currently available as an experiment only for select servers.

The Server Booster role in your server is set to a pink gradient Enhanced Role Style by default, even if your server doesn’t have this Additional Perk unlocked. This special role helps incentivize members to Boost your server by enhancing how they appear in the server. You can change the color or style at any time. To change the style of this role:

  1. Select the server where you want to make changes. Press the server name in the top-left and select Server Settings.
Server Settings option

  1. Navigate to the Roles tab and then press the Edit icon [] next to the Server Booster role.

  2. By default, the Server Booster role will use a gradient based on the solid color it had before this update. Users with permission can customize it by selecting a different Role Style or adjusting the color. Enhanced Role Styles are available for the Booster role, even if your server hasn’t unlocked this perk for other roles.

All Role Styles that are available for the Server Booster role
  1. After selecting your desired color(s) for the role, press Save Changes.
Server Owner/Admin View Of Server Boosts

If someone uses a Server Boost on your server, and you have the option enabled, you’ll see a message in your designated text channel that states someone has Boosted the server.

Server Boosting feed showing who boosted the server

If you’re the server owner or have Manage Server permissions, you’ll be able to select which channel the Server Boosting message will appear in, or toggle this option on/off within the Overview section in your Server Settings. Here’s how:

  1. Navigate to the server you own or have Manage Server Permissions in, and then tap on the server name in the top-left corner of the app.

  2. Tap on Server Settings and then under Overview, scroll down until you see System Messages Channel.

  3. Here you can change where the system message is sent to and can also enable or disable Send a message when someone Boosts this server.

Send a message when someone Boosts this server option
Managing Your Server’s Boosts and Perks

As a server owner or admin with Manage Server permissions, you’ll have access to the new Server Boosts tab at the top of your channel list. This powerful management interface lets you:

  • View your total available Boosts and how they’re currently allocated
  • See your server’s current level and active perks
  • Enable new perks if you have available Boosts
  • Reallocate Boosts between levels and additional perks as needed
  • Configure settings for Enhanced Role Styles and Server Tags once enabled
Grace Periods for Server Boost Loss

If your server is running low on Server Boosts and loses a level, the server will be able to keep the perks for a grace period of 72 hours. After 72 hours, the perks (such as the server banner and extra emojis) will not be fully removed from the server, but will become temporarily invalid until the level is regained.

However, the Custom Invite Link will be lost and become available to other servers after 30 days.

Unlike level perks which have a grace period, additional perks like Server Tags and Enhanced Role Styles are disabled immediately when their required Boosts are removed or reallocated. If your server is losing Boosts, you can use the Server Boosts tab to prioritize which perks to keep active with your remaining Boosts.

Want to see different perks added to this in the future? We’d love to hear all your feedback and suggestions over at dis.gd

Frequently Asked Questions

This FAQ is divided into sections:

  • Additional Perks
  • Other
Additional Perks

Q: What are ‘additional perks’ and how are they different from Levels?

A: Additional perks are new features you can unlock directly with Boosts, separate from your server’s Boost Level. Currently, there are two available: Enhanced Role Styles (which add gradient and holographic effects to roles) and Server Tags (4-character identifiers members can display on their profiles across Discord). Unlike traditional server levels, these perks can be unlocked individually without reaching specific level thresholds.

Q: How much do the new additional perks cost?

A: Enhanced Role Styles and Server Tags each cost 3 Boosts. If you want both perks, you’ll need 6 Boosts total (3 for each perk).

Q: Are additional perks replacing the current server level system?

A: No, this supplements the existing level system. All current server level perks (emoji slots, file upload limits, etc.) remain exactly the same. This new system simply gives you additional ways to use your Boosts for targeted perks without affecting your server’s level progression.

Q: Do additional perks use separate Boosts from my server level?

A: Yes, Boosts used for additional perks are dedicated specifically to those perks and don’t count toward your server’s level progression. Similarly, Boosts allocated to your server level can’t be used for additional perks. You’ll need separate Boosts for each - so if you want Enhanced Role Styles, you need 3 Boosts just for that perk, plus whatever Boosts you want to maintain your current server level.

Q: What happens to my additional perks if my server loses Boosts?

A: Perks require ongoing Boost allocation to remain active. If your server drops below the required number of Boosts for a perk, that perk will be disabled. Enhanced Role Styles will revert to solid colors, and Server Tags will be removed from members’ profiles. Server owners/admins can choose which perks to maintain if Boost counts drop.

Q: Why can’t I unlock perks even though I have enough Boosts?

A: Make sure you’re accessing the Server Boost tab (visible only to server owners/admins) and that your Boosts are “available” rather than already allocated to your server level. Only server members with admin permissions can unlock additional perks. You need to have enough unallocated Boosts to enable additional perks.

Q: I just added 3 Boosts to my server for an additional perk, but I can’t enable it. Why aren’t my Boosts available?

A: When you add new Boosts to your server, they’re automatically applied toward server levels whenever you have enough for the next level. This means your Boosts might have triggered an automatic level upgrade, making them unavailable for additional perks. To free up those Boosts for additional perks, you’ll need to disable the level.

Q: Can I move Boosts between levels and perks after I’ve allocated them?

A: Yes, server owners and admins can reallocate Boosts between server levels and additional perks through the Server Boosts tab. However, if you move Boosts away from a perk, that perk will be disabled until you allocate enough Boosts back to it.

Q: Are additional perks a one-time purchase, or do they require ongoing Boosts?

A: Each additional perk requires an ongoing allocation of its required Boosts to stay active, just like levels. If your server drops below the required number of Boosts, the perk will be disabled until the necessary Boosts are reallocated.

Q: Can I purchase and manage additional perks from both desktop and mobile?

A: Additional perks can currently only be purchased and configured on desktop.

Other

Q: Can I use a Discord gift card to purchase Server Boosts?

A: Yes! You can use your Discord gift card balance to purchase Server Boosts. Learn more about gift cards, or redeem a gift card here.

Server Invite Background

If your server reaches Boosting Level 1, your server gets access to the Server Invite Background perk! Learn more below about how to set up a background image for your server’s invite link.

What this article covers

  • What is a Server Invite Background?
  • What are the Server Invite Background guidelines?
  • How do I upload an image for a Server Invite Background?
  • Frequently Asked Questions
    • Can I access the Server Invite Background perk for my server at Boosting Level 2/3?
    • How do I remove my server’s current image for the Server Invite Background?
    • Can I edit or adjust the image for a Server Invite Background after I upload it?
    • What is the required image size for a Server Invite Background?

You can learn more about Server Boosting perks here.

What is a Server Invite Background?

A perk for servers that reach Boosting Level 1, a Server Invite Background is the image that appears behind the invite pop-up in the app and web browsers. It’s a fun way to personalize your server’s invites and showcase your server’s theme, purpose, and community!

What are the Server Invite Background guidelines?

In order to upload an image for a Server Invite Background, you should keep in mind the following:

  • The main requirement is that the image size is 1920x1080 and we accept JPG and PNG files.
  • Choose an image that represents your server’s theme, brand, purpose, and community!
  • The server invite itself is an upright rectangular in-window pop-up in the middle of the window, so make sure key parts of your image aren’t covered up by the pop-up
    • You can upload an image and then copy and paste the server’s invite link in an incognito/private window to see how the Server Invite Background looks!
  • We recommend not using an image with a logo or text in it for your Server Invite Background.
  • Server Invite Backgrounds cannot animate/be a GIF.

How do I upload an image for a Server Invite Background?

On desktop/browser:

  1. Press on the downward arrow next to the Server Name and choose Server Settings

  2. Select the Overview tab

  3. Scroll down to Server Invite Background

  4. Press on the Upload Background button

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I access the Server Invite Background perk for my server at Boosting Level 2/3?

A: Yes! If your server goes beyond Boosting Level 1 and reaches Boosting Level 2/3, your server will still have access to this perk.

Q: How do I remove my server’s current image for the Server Invite Background?

A: Go to the Server Settings > Overview then scroll to the bottom of the page and press Remove under the preview of the Server Invite Background image.

Q: Can I edit or adjust the image for a Server Invite Background after I upload it?

A: Unfortunately, you are unable to edit or adjust the image after you upload it as a Server Invite Background.

Q: What is the required image size for a Server Invite Background?

A: The image size must be 1920x1080.

Announcement Channel FAQ

With Announcement channels, you can now effectively broadcast important updates to your entire Community server. Whether you’re sharing critical information or engaging your audience, these channels help you reach everyone who needs to stay informed.

What this article covers:

  • What are Announcement Channels?
  • How to Create an Announcement Channel
  • How to Convert an Existing Channel into an Announcement Channel
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are Announcement Channels?

Announcement channels are special text channels that include a Follow button, allowing server members to receive updates in their own servers.

Want to learn more about following channels? Check out our Channel Following FAQ!

When you publish a message in an Announcement channel, it appears as a regular message in all following servers - perfect for sharing updates where your community already spends their time.

Announcement channels cannot receive messages from other Announcement channels.

How to Create an Announcement Channel

Announcement Channels are only available to servers with Community enabled.

  1. In the channel list, hover over the channel category where you want your Announcement channel to live and hit the plus icon [] to create a channel.
Select the plus sign icon to create a Channel in a Discord server

  1. Select Announcement as the channel type, and enter a channel name.

  2. Press the Create Channel button to confirm.

Choose Your Channel Type & Name for an Announcement Channel in a Discord server

How to Convert an Existing Channel into an Announcement Channel

  1. Hover over the channel name and press the Edit Channel icon [] to open your channel settings.

  2. Scroll down and toggle on the Announcement Channel option.

  3. Press Save Changes to confirm your settings.

Open your Channel Settings to enable or disable an Announcement Channel in a Discord server

Grant permissions only to trusted members. Send Messages permission lets members publish their own messages, while Manage Messages allows them to publish any message in the channel. You can configure these settings in the Permissions tab. Learn more about channel permissions here.

After posting a message in the announcement channel, you’ll see the Publish option appear. Press Publish to share the message with all servers following your announcement channel.

Publish option after posting a message in an announcement channel

Get creative with your Announcement channels! Use them for everything from #daily-tips to #patch-notes, #giveaways to #going-live, and much more. Need more help? Check out our Channel Following FAQ for detailed guidance.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Will @everyone and @here mentions work in following servers?

A: No, these mentions and other similar ones will not be pushed through to following servers.

Q: How do messages appear in following servers?

A: Messages appear exactly as they look in your server when you press Publish, including all embeds, images, videos, emojis, and spoiler tags.

Q: What happens when I edit or delete a published message?

A: Editing a message will update it in following servers. If you delete a message, it will be removed but leave a [Original Message Deleted] note for users.

Example of [Original Message Deleted] note

Q: Is there a limit to how many announcements I can publish?

A: Yes, there is a rate limit of 10 publishes per hour. You’ll see an error message if you exceed this limit.

Audio Bitrate FAQ

Whether it’s speaking, singing, or laughing with others, audio bitrate will affect how you hear it all.

What does audio bitrate do on Discord?

The audio bitrate setting that can be modified to improve the sound quality while in a voice chat with your friends. The higher the bitrate, the better you and your friends will sound.

How to adjust the audio bitrate?

  1. If you’d like to adjust the audio bitrate, hover over the specific voice channel.

As you hover over the voice channel, the Edit Channel cogwheel button will appear.

  1. Selecting the Edit Channel cogwheel button [] , will redirect you to the voice channel’s Overview page.

  2. Once there, navigate to the audio bitrate bar under Bitrate. This bar can be dragged to increase or decrease the audio bitrate.

Note: Increasing the bitrate will require more bandwidth and can affect those with poor connection.

Increasing the Bitrate Cap

If you’d like to increase the audio bitrate for the entire server, you can do so by boosting the server. Learn more about server boosting here.

More Boosts, More Bits!

✨Level 1✨ - 2 Server Boosts = 128 Kbps Audio Quality

✨Level 2✨ - 7 Server Boosts = 256 Kbps Audio Quality

✨Level 3✨ - 14 Server Boosts = 384 Kbps Audio Quality

Once the server has been boosted to the desired level, the maximum audio bitrate cap will be reflected above the right-hand of the bar.

By boosting the server, you and your friends can enjoy higher sound quality across all voice channels in the server!

Channel Following FAQ

Are you a fan of pizza? Do you like getting pizza delivered to your house? Have you ever wished you could get pizza delivered right to your server? Well, if your favorite pizza topping is announcements from other Discord servers, now you can!

With Channel Following, you can now have automated post pizzas topped with announcements from your favorite servers delivered directly to your server in a channel of your choice, using some of the same technology that powers Webhooks!

Tip:Channel Following is now available to all servers with Community Servers enabled

Spotting an Announcement Channel

In select servers with Announcement Channels, which are special channels labeled with a Megaphone icon, you’ll be able to use the new Follow option to have any messages from that channel posted directly into your server as they’re posted!

Let’s say your group of friends wants to know when the new Spellbreak update comes out. First, find the announcement channel in the server you want to follow–in this case, the Spellbreak official server has an announcement channel that looks just like this!

Make sure that you have the Manage Webhooks permission in your server, as you’ll need it to order some post pizzas! Then, click the Follow button!

Tip: The Follow button is only available in Announcement Channels, labeled with the Megaphone icon! Developers can learn how to make an Announcement Channel here!

Adding it to your server

When you click the Follow button in an eligible channel, you’ll be greeted with a whole host of options for where you want that Announcement channel’s posts to appear in your own server!

From here, you can select which server and channel you want your new announcements bot to post in! Keep in mind that only servers and channels you have Manage Webhook permissions in will be shown.

Once you’re finished configuring these options, press Follow and you’re ready to start getting post pizzas delivered to your server by your very own delivery bot!

Sit back & enjoy

As the server you followed continues to post announcements, you’ll receive posts from that server in the channel you picked. The posts will look a bit like this:

The posts will come from a bot named after the server in question. All the links and images in the post will be delivered as you’d expect, but our delivery bots will remove any and all role mentions in the post, including @everyone and @here.

Info: Keep in mind, server admins have the ability to choose which announcement posts will be published and sent to your server through Channel Following. If you’re missing an announcement post, it’s likely the admins have chosen to not publish that post.

How to remove

If you’ve got Manage Webhooks permissions, you can follow and unfollow servers at any time! If you want to stop receiving posts from a server that you followed, it’s easy! Any servers you follow are added to your server as a Webhook. To unfollow a server, look for the server’s listing in Server Settings > Integrations > Channels Followed!

Delete the bot that corresponds with that server’s name to unfollow it! The bot will be removed from your server and you’ll stop receiving posts from the server right away.

Tip: You can use the Webhooks settings to modify your new follow bot too–you can change the channel it posts in, the bot’s name, and the avatar of the bot, all using the Edit button!

All set!

Now you know all there is to know about Channel Following! Channel Following is still in the experiment phase, so it’ll only be available on select servers as our amazing pizza chefs continue to build out the feature! Keep an eye on our changelogs for more information on Channel Following in the future!

If you run a Community Server, please check out the Announcement Channels FAQ.

While we continue to experiment with and improve Channel Following, if you have any suggestions for us, share them on our feedback page!

Clarifying Server Types

Every Discord server is a Friend, Community, or Discoverable Server, depending on how it’s used and how people can find and join it. This article explains each server type and how badges like Partnered and Verified fit in.

What this article covers:

  • What are the types of Discord servers?
    • Becoming a Community Server
    • Turning Off Community
    • Becoming a Discoverable Server
    • Turning Off Discoverability
  • Server Badges
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are the types of Discord servers?

Friend, Community, and Discoverable server types describe how people can find and join a server:

  • Friend Server: Friend Servers are invite-only spaces designed to discuss, connect, and share with your friends or smaller groups.
  • Community Server: Community Servers are invite-only spaces designed for people to share, connect, and learn from others all over the world who share common interests. Moderators in Community Servers have access to tools like Server Insights, Raid Protection, Rules and Onboarding.
  • Discoverable Server: Discoverable Servers are Community Servers that meet extra requirements for size, safety, and activity, and whose admins have chosen to list them in Server Discovery. Anyone can find and join them without an invite, through Server Discovery, discord.com/servers, and web search. They also have their own Server Web Page, so people can learn about them before joining.
Becoming a Community Server

Friend Servers who wish to have access to Community features may opt in to become a Community Server at any time in server settings.

Becoming a Community Server does not mean that anyone can find or join your server. Prospective members have to be sent an invite link. To support Community Server growth, invite links for Community Servers never expire.

Turning Off Community

Important: If your server is Discoverable, disabling Community also turns off Discoverability automatically.

  1. Open Server Settings.

  2. Under the Community category, select Overview.

  3. Select Disable Community at the bottom of the page.

Disable Community Option in Server Settings
Becoming a Discoverable Server

Community Servers that meet our eligibility criteria (including a 1,000+ member minimum, active engagement, safety checks, and two-factor authentication for moderators) can choose to become a Discoverable Server. Eligibility criteria may be updated over time, and servers are expected to continue meeting them to remain Discoverable.

Becoming a Discoverable Server means your server can be found and joined by people who haven’t received an invite, including people searching the web for what your community talks about.

Verified servers automatically qualify as Discoverable Servers. Learn more in Discord Verified Server Program FAQ.

Turning Off Discoverability

If you’d rather your server not be Discoverable, you can turn this off at any time.

  1. Open Server Settings.

  2. Select Access.

  3. Turn off Discoverable.

Turning off Discoverability reverts your server to a Community Server. This means:

  • Your server can no longer be found through Server Discovery or discord.com/servers.
  • Your server web pages are taken down. Search engines may take some time to remove it from their results.
  • Prospective members will need an invite link to join, same as any Community Server. You can turn Discoverability back on at any time, as long as your server still meets the eligibility criteria.

Note: If your server is removed from Discovery for a guideline violation, the server owner can request a review. Learn how in Discord Warning System.

Server Badges

Your server’s badge reflects its server type: Community or Discoverable. If your server also holds Partnered or Verified status, that badge takes priority and displays instead, with the tooltip noting the underlying server type as well.

Like Server Boosting, Partnered and Verified status add recognition and perks, but they don’t change your server type or who can find and join it. Learn more in Partnered vs. Verified Servers.

Each badge’s tooltip shows more detail, including whether anyone can join and Boost level.

Example of a Server Badge Tooltip

Servers that have Partnered and Verified status will receive the “Verified” badge, and the tooltip will denote both statuses.

Verified Badge Tooltip for a Verified and Partnered Server

For more information on our approach to safety across server types, please visit our Safety Center.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What’s the difference between a server type and a badge like Partnered or Verified?

A: Your server type (Friend, Community, or Discoverable) describes how people can find and join your server, depending on size, safety, and activity. Partnered and Verified are separate statuses Discord grants to select servers on top of their type, such as official game servers.

Q: How do I know if my server is Discoverable?

A: Open Server Settings, select Access, and find the Discoverable setting. If it’s turned on, your server is Discoverable. If you can’t find it or turn it on, your server isn’t Discoverable yet. Learn what’s needed in Enabling Server Discovery.

Q: Will my server become Discoverable automatically?

A: No. Community Servers that meet the eligibility criteria can choose to become Discoverable. Verified servers automatically qualify as Discoverable Servers.

Q: What happens with badges if you’re verified and partnered?

A: We’ll display your Verified badge, and the tooltip will indicate that the server is Verified & Partnered.

Collapse Syncing

Do you use multiple Discord clients and find yourself having to collapse and expand categories every time in each server you’re in? Well, with our new Collapse Syncing feature, that will be a thing of the past! Now when you collapse or expand a category within a server, this will be reflected across all Discord clients.

Note: This feature is only available on desktop at this time. Stay tuned for more details on syncing across mobile clients as well!

How Does It Work

The first client that connects to Discord will have all of the currently collapsed categories saved to the server. After you log into another client, those saved settings will be downloaded and used - syncing them and making sure you don’t have to redo the work again!

Need Further Help?

For more information regarding channels and categories, you can check out our Channel Categories support article.

If you have any further questions about Collapse Syncing, please reach out to support through dis.gd/contact. To receive help as quickly as possible, please make sure that you are using the email address that’s associated with your Discord account.

Discord Server Setup Guide

Setting up a Discord server is easy with this comprehensive guide. Whether you’re building a community for gaming, study groups, or other hobbies, we’ll walk you through the steps to create a server as well as share the different features and tools to manage it.

What this article covers:

  • What is a Discord Server?
  • Understanding Different Types of Servers
    • Friend Servers
    • Community Servers
    • Discoverable Servers
  • Getting Started with Discord Servers
  • Understanding Key Features of Discord Servers
  • Tools for Discord Server Owners and Moderators
  • Advanced Server Setup Features

What is a Discord Server?

A Discord server is a customizable digital space where communities can gather, communicate, and share content. Think of servers as virtual meeting places that bring people together around shared interests, hobbies, or relationships. Each server is organized with different channels dedicated to specific purposes, whether that’s text conversations, voice chats, or media sharing, making it easy to keep discussions organized and accessible.

Discord servers are free to create and can accommodate anywhere from a small group of friends to massive communities with thousands of members. They offer flexibility in organization, moderation tools, and customization options that make them suitable for virtually any type of group or community.

Understanding Different Types of Servers

Discord offers three main server types, each designed for different community needs and scales:

Friend Servers

Friend servers are private, invite-only spaces perfect for staying connected with your close friends or smaller groups. These servers provide an intimate environment where you can chat, share memories, coordinate activities, and maintain relationships with people you know personally. The smaller scale makes them ideal for casual conversations and personal connections.

Community Servers

Community servers are larger, invite-only spaces designed to bring together people from around the world who share common interests, hobbies, or goals. These servers focus on fostering learning, discussion, and connection within specific communities, whether that’s gaming, art, technology, or countless other topics.

Community servers come with enhanced moderation tools to help manage larger groups effectively, including:

  • Server Insights: Analytics to understand your community’s activity, growth patterns, and member engagement
  • Raid Protection: Advanced security features to protect against spam, bot attacks, and disruptive behavior
  • Rules and Onboarding: Structured systems to welcome new members, establish community guidelines, and create screening processes
  • Welcome Screen: Customizable introduction for new members
  • Server Discovery: A path to becoming a Discoverable server, which can be found and joined without an invite (eligibility requirements apply) These tools make Community servers well-suited for building thriving, organized communities that can scale while maintaining a positive environment for all members.
Discoverable Servers

Discoverable servers are Community servers that meet extra requirements for size, safety, and activity, and whose admins have chosen to list them in Server Discovery. Anyone can find and join them without an invite, through Server Discovery, discord.com/servers, and web search. They also have their own Server Web Page, so people can learn about them before joining.

Want to learn more?

For a deeper dive into server types and their specific features, check out our comprehensive Clarifying Server Types article, which covers additional details and best practices for choosing the right server type for your community.

Getting Started with Discord Servers

Creating your first Discord server is a simple process that takes just a few minutes. Here’s how to get started:

  1. On the Discord desktop app or browser client, locate the Add a Server icon [] on the left sidebar of the app.

  2. Select either Create My Own or choose a template.

  3. If creating your own server, choose between:

  • For a club or community
  • For me and my friends

  1. Name your server and add an optional server icon.

  2. When you’re all set, select Create.

Example of Creating a Discord Server on Desktop

Want to learn more?

You can learn more about creating servers or managing them in these detailed articles:

  • How do I create a server?
  • How do I delete a server?
  • Server Templates

Understanding Key Features of Discord Servers

Discord servers come with many powerful features available even without Server Boosting. Understanding these features will help you create a well-organized and engaging community space.

Server Channels

Channels are the foundation of server organization. You can create different types of channels to help organize conversations and activities:

  • Text Channels & Text Chat in Voice Channels: For text-based communication, file sharing, and ongoing discussions
  • Voice Channels: For voice and video communication, perfect for meetings, gaming, or casual hangouts
  • Forum Channels: Organized discussion spaces where you can create topic-specific posts without conversations overlapping (available only for Community servers) Advanced Channel Features

To make the most of your server channels, consider these additional features:

  • Channel Categories: Group similar channels together for better organization
  • Drag and drop reordering: Easily reorganize channels and categories
  • Channel-specific permissions: Control who can access specific channels
  • Role-exclusive channels: Create private channels for specific member groups
  • Threads: Keep conversations organized within channels
  • Polls: Create polls for community decisions and feedback
Server Invites

Once your server is set up, you’ll want to invite people to join. Discord provides several flexible ways to create and manage invites.

Info: You must be the server owner or have permissions to create and manage invites.

Here are the different types of invites you can create:

  • Instant Invites: One-click links that bring people directly to your server
  • Custom Invite Links: Personalized invite URLs that are easier to remember
  • Temporary Invites: Links that expire after a set time or number of uses
  • Permanent Invites: Links that never expire (use with caution) Want to learn more?

Learn more about managing invites:

  • Invites 101
  • How do I invite friends to my server?
  • Custom Invite Link
  • Pause Invites FAQ

Tools for Discord Server Owners and Moderators

Effective server management requires understanding Discord’s moderation tools and permission systems. These tools help you maintain a positive community environment while giving members appropriate levels of access and responsibility.

Essential moderation tools:

  • Discord Roles and Permissions: The cornerstone of Discord server moderation, allowing you to create different member tiers with specific permissions
  • Members Page: Get an overview of your server members, their roles, and activity
  • Verification Levels: Control who can send messages and participate in your server
  • How to Prune: Remove inactive members to keep your member list current

Advanced Server Setup Features

For servers that grow beyond basic friend groups, Discord offers advanced features that help manage larger communities effectively. Many of these features become available through server boosting or by meeting Community server requirements.

  • Server Boosting: Discord’s premium feature system that unlocks enhanced server capabilities.
  • Community Server Guidelines: For servers focused on building larger communities, enabling Community features provides additional moderation tools.
  • Server Member Application: Learn more about implementing applications to screen potential members before they join.
  • Discovery Guidelines: The requirements Discoverable servers are expected to meet.
  • Server Web Pages: A public page that helps prospective members learn about a Discoverable server before joining. For additional support, explore Discord’s Server Settings help center.

What are Forum Channels?

Forum Channels provide a space for organized discussions. With forums, you can discuss specific topics and not worry about talking over each other. Since discussions are contained in posts, it’s easier to jump in on an existing one (or start a new one) without worrying about your message getting buried!

How Do I Create a Forum Channel?

Note: In order to create and have forum channels on your server, you must enable Community on your server. You can learn how to enable Community in the Enabling Your Community Server Help Center article.

  1. In the channel list, hover over the channel category where you want your Forum Channel and then press the plus sign () to create a channel.

  2. Select Forum as the channel type, and enter a channel name.

  3. Then press Create Channel when you’re done!

Permissions

First up is channel permissions. These permissions determine which members have access to Forum channels.

Press Set recommended permissions. From here, you can limit access to the Forum Channel to specific roles. Or you can also enable @everyone to allow all users to gain access.

Tip: Allowing everyone to post in a forum channel helps increase overall engagement and usage of the channel!

Post Guidelines

Next, you can create guidelines for your Forum Channel.

Pressing Create post guidelines will take you to the Guidelines settings page. From here, you can change the channel name, add guidelines, and designate tags to help your members.

Tags

Tags can help label specific posts and can also be a requirement before a member of your server makes a post.

I Forgot to add Tags in my Post!

If you forgot to add tags to your post, you can add them by right-clicking on your post and navigating to Edit Tags. Here you can select all tags that are applicable.

Hide After Inactivity

Note: Unless a forum post is locked, the post can be reopened at any time. Even if it’s closed.

Once a post has been inactive for a certain period of time, it’ll automatically be moved to the Older Posts section. You can choose one of the following:

  • 1 hour
  • 24 hours
  • 3 days (this setting is selected by default)
  • 1 week Now you can make your first post in the forum channel!
Setting a Default Layout

You can choose between List View and Gallery View as the default layout for your forum channel. What you choose will be dependent on what your forum channel is all about.

List View

This option works better for text-based discussions and allows users to easily jump in.

Gallery View

This tends to work better for media-focused forum channels and allows members of your servers to see exactly what media is in the post.

How to Search for a Forum Post

Looking for a specific discussion in a forum channel? You can search for the post using the forum channel’s dedicated search bar!

  1. Go to your server’s channel list and find the forum channel with the post that you want to search for.

  2. In the search bar at the top of the page, input the key word or phase of the post title you’re looking for. The search bar will show results that match with your searched word.

Filtering Posts with Tags

In a forum channel’s posts, specific tags can be associated with certain posts to help organize your forum channel and the numerous different posts under one discussion topic.

You can filter posts in a forum channel by selecting tags. You can also tap on All and select tags through there. Forum channel posts can have numerous tags, so you can filter posts further by selecting multiple tags.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Who has access to Forum Channels right now?

A: Forum Channels are currently available to 100% of Community servers.

Q: When will Forum Channels be available for non-Community servers?

A: Forum Channels are currently only available to Community-enabled servers. If you’re ready to convert your server into a Community server, please check out this Help Center article for a detailed guide on how to make the switch.

Q: What’s the difference between Forums and Text channels?

A: While Text channels are great for in-the-moment discussions, Forum channels provide a place for more drawn-out discussion around specific topics. Discussions are tied to individual posts so they are more organized and easier for members of your community to get up to speed and join a conversation.

Q: What’s the difference between Forums and Threads?

A: The main difference is that Forums are a type of channel, while threads are a type of message. While they are similar in that they both create dedicated spaces for organized discussions, Forum Channels are more persistent, while threads are more temporary.

Q: What kind of tools are available to moderate Forum Channels?

A: To ensure moderation of forum channels is easy and manageable, we’ve implemented 3 types of moderation support:

  • AutoMod: Forum Channels are supported by AutoMod, our built-in moderation tool that helps detect and remove problematic content automatically.
  • Slow Mode: If the volume of posts and message activity is concerning, mods can place limits.
  • API: We’ve updated our API Documentation, so developers can integrate support for forums into their products. Q: Is there a way to close or lock a post in a forum channel?

A: If a conversation has reached its end or you need to close it for any reason, you can right click the post and click Close Post. This will cause the post to no longer appear in the new posts section of the list and also lock the post so that only moderators can re-open it.

Q: What’s the best way to test forums with my community?

A: While all communities are different, we recommend rolling out forums to your community gradually. This way, your community won’t experience big, jarring changes, and they’ll have time to get used to it. One example of a roll-out could look like this:

  • Create a private forum for you and your moderators to test and discuss plans
  • Identify existing text channels where forums might be a good fit and replace them
  • Create new forum channels with the proper guidelines and tags
  • Make an announcement to inform your community about the changes and encourage them to provide feedback
  • If your community’s feedback is largely positive, identify larger “core” text channels that could benefit from the organization forums bring Q: How many posts can be pinned to the top? How long do they stay pinned?

A: Forum channels currently only support having one pinned post. Pinned posts aren’t on a timer, so they will remain pinned until it’s unpinned or another post is pinned (replacing the original pinned post).

Q: How do you add or replace a thumbnail to a post?

A: If you forgot to add a thumbnail to your original post, you can do so by being the first to reply to your original post with a photo. When you do this, the option to add the media to the original post will appear. If you select Add to Post, it will append your media to the original post and act as the thumbnail.

Q: Can I ping people within a forum channel? Will they be notified when a new thread is created with a ping in it?

A: Yes, you can ping people in a forum channel. They’ll be able to continue receiving notifications if they’re following that specific forum post! That is not the case for the forum channel as a whole. They won’t be pinged for every new thread. Mentions in forum posts work in the same way as threads, which you can read more about in the Threads FAQ.

How do I create a server?

Whether this is the first or tenth server you’ve made, you’re in the right place for going over the server creation process! Before we begin, keep in mind that the Add a Server () icon can be hidden if you have a lot of servers. Simply scroll down the server list on the left side of the app to find where the Add a Server () icon is hiding.

After you select the Add a Server button, you will see a pop-up window that will give you the option of choosing a blank slate for your new server or a template. It also has a spot at the bottom of the pop-up if you have an invite code you’re trying to use. For this example, we’ll be creating a server using the Create My Own option.

Not sure how you want to customize your server? You can always download a Server Template! Check out this Help Center article for more information.

We try to make it easy for you by offering to guide you through a set up for a community or friends server, but you can always skip if you’re unsure - no need to commit now!

Next, you can enter in the server name, and change the server icon by locating it in your devices files. Everyone knows the name and icon are the most important details for a server!

The minimum size for icons is 128x128. If you’d like to select a specific area from a large image, crop it in multiples of 128 (128X2=256, 128X3=384, etc.).

Press “Create” and you’ve started a brand new server. Now, send your friends an invitation and start chatting!

Don’t feel pressured to perfect your server in the creation process - you can always update the name and icon of your server at a later time!

Want to upgrade your server and take it to the next level? Check out these support articles for more ways to customize your server:

  • Setting Up Permissions FAQ
  • Invites 101
  • Server Guide FAQ
  • How do I set up a Role-Exclusive channel?
  • Server Boosting FAQ

How do I hide muted channels?

As an extension of muting channels, you can make any server’s channel list a little more compact by hiding muted channels. There are a couple of ways to do this:

  1. Mute desired channels

You can mute the channels you want to hide, either by clicking the bell icon in the top-right corner:

… Or by opening up the server’s notification settings, accessed here:

  1. Click the ‘Hide Muted Channels’ option in the Server Settings Dropdown Menu

Once you click the Server Name (in the upper left corner), you’ll see the ‘Hide Muted Channels’ option in the Server Settings dropdown menu.

Clicking that option will hide any muted channels away, leaving just your desired channels:

Before:

After:

How do I set up a private server?

Want to prevent outsiders from being able to view all the channels on your server? If so, you’re in the right place as this article covers the steps for setting up a “private” server.

Setting up a “private” server will restrict access to your server and channels to only the members you specify.

We’ll walk you through the four steps below!

  • Disable all permissions for @everyone
  • Create a new role in the server
  • Enable permissions for the role
  • Assign the role to your server members

1. Disable all permission for @everyone

Firstly, you’ll want to disable all permissions for @everyone using these steps below:

  • Head into the Roles tab in your Server Settings menu
  • Select the default @everyone role and then scroll all the way to the bottom of the permissions page
  • Once you scroll all the way down, you’ll be able to click on the Clear Role Permissions button!
    • This Clear Role Permissions button will automatically disable all toggles for all permissions (which is exactly what we want)!
  • Last but not least, make sure to save your changes!
Note: The Discord mobile client does not have the Clear Role Permissions button so you would need to manually uncheck each of the permission boxes if you’re on mobile.

2. Create a new role in the server

Within this same Roles tab in the Server Settings, create a new role by clicking on the ‘+’ symbol.

Once clicked, you can then type your preferred role name in the box under Role Name and then select the color you’d like for the role to appear in the server!

3. Enable permissions for your new role

Enable permissions for your new role by selecting the role and then selecting the permission check boxes you want activated for the role - just make sure to scroll down the role permission list to review all permissions.

When you have finished enabling the right permission, make sure to save your changes!

  • In this example below, we’ve started by enabling View Channels and Manage Emojis and after scrolling down the permission list, you’ll see we’ve also enabled the Send Messages and Attach Files permissions to the new role.

4. Assign the new role to your server members

After saving the permission changes, you can assign your new role to all members who should have access by selecting the Members tab in your Server Settings menu.

Within the Members tab, you can directly add the role to the appropriate members by selecting the ‘+’ and then selecting the role name that appears.

And that’s it!

Now you have a “private” server. When you invite new members to the server, you will need to give them a role before they’re able to participate in the channels.

If you’re new to setting up permissions on a server, we would recommend reviewing our general overview of the permission system here.
- Some other suggested permission settings articles include creating a leaders channel and creating an announcements channel.
- Additionally, to see how the Discord permission hierarchy works click here.

In-Channel Conversation Summaries

What this article covers:

  • What are In-Channel Conversation Summaries?
  • Where to find In-Channel Conversation Summaries
    • Topic Subheader
    • Summaries List
    • How to Hide In-Channel Conversation Summaries
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are In-Channel Conversation Summaries?

Info: This feature is currently an experiment and limited to a few servers.

Have you ever stepped away from your phone and came back to dozens of missed messages? Overwhelmed at trying to catch up on what everyone is talking about? We know it can be hard to quickly identify topics and find your conversations without having to scroll your way through endless messages.

To fix all of that, Discord is excited to introduce In-Channel Conversation Summaries. This feature helps keep you in the know and lets you jump back into the action in seconds. In-Channel Conversation Summaries consolidates the messages you receive into easy-to-navigate topics. These topics let you quickly see what others are chatting about, catch-up, and engage more immediately in important conversations. You’ll also be able to see a conversation preview, the number of messages about a specific topic, and who is part of the discussion.

Being able to quickly jump back into a conversation is that much easier, no matter how much you’ve missed.

Where to find In-Channel Conversation Summaries

In-Channel Conversation Summaries are currently available in select servers as part of a text channel’s subheader. You can see the different topics being discussed in the In-Channel Conversation Summaries subheader or dive deeper by opening up the subheader to show summarized snippets.

Topic Subheader

In a text channel, you’ll see a subheader showing the currently viewed topic. Instead of having to read individual messages to figure out what’s going on, you can get a quick sense for what is being talked about. Small arrows help you go back and forth between previous topics.

Summaries List

To skim through a list of conversations, select the currently shown topic in the subheader. This opens a panel where you can see a list of conversations, their associated topic, a short snippet, and some of the participants involved. Selecting any of these conversations navigates you to the beginning of that discussion.

How to Hide the In-Channel Conversation Summaries UI

There are two ways to hide the In-Channel Conversation Summaries UI depending on your server role:

  1. Any member can show/hide the In-Channel Conversation Summaries UI in text channels with the In-Channel Conversation Summaries icon in the header.

  2. The owner of that server or administrators with the Manage Channel<></>permission can hide the In-Channel Conversation Summaries UI in any channel through the channel’s settings by selecting the cog wheel next to the channel [<>. Once there, toggle Enable Channel Summaries<></> to disable this setting. </>

Server owners and admins with Manage Channel permissions can also hide the UI for the whole server in Server Settings > Overview.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What spaces on Discord can use In-Channel Conversation Summaries?

A: In-Channel Conversation Summaries is currently available to a limited number of servers on Discord.

Q: How does In-Channel Conversation Summaries work?

A: This feature automatically summarizes the messages you receive in a server to display a list of conversations, their associated topic, a short snippet, and some of the participants involved. You won’t receive summaries for messages you don’t have access to (e.g., messages from a private channel you’re not a part of).

Q: What if I don’t want to receive summaries from In-Channel Conversation Summaries?

A: Users can always hide the In-Channel Conversation Summaries UI by following the steps listed above. In-Channel Conversation Summaries will be a core part of the server experience and how users on Discord stay engaged and up-to-date with their servers, similar to Highlight Notifications.

Intro to Webhooks

Discord’s built in Webhooks function as an easy way to get automated messages and data updates sent to a text channel in your server.

Think of them as one of those fancy pneumatic tube things you used to love sending money into at a bank and watch disappear, but instead of never seeing your money again, you’re actually sending messages into Discord from another platform.

By creating a webhook endpoint in your server, you’ll generate a Webhook URL that you can drop into a number of different other services to link the two.

While everyone absolutely loves pneumatic tubes (100% true), it’s important to note that webhooks require another website to use (though programming-inclined users can make their own tube schoomper themselves).

Some services and websites are built to easily incorporate webhooks and send messages outwards, but some aren’t. Here’s a little handy reference list:

Can use webhooks:

Can’t really use webhooks:

GitHub

Twitch / YouTube

CircleCI

Nelly The Hamster

DataDog

Facebook

Making a Webhook

With that in mind, if you want to update your Discord server with GitHub commits and pull requests or track analytics from DataDog or anything similar, here’s how!

  • Open your Server Settings and head into the Integrations tab:

  • Click the “Create Webhook” button to create a new webhook! You’ll have a few options here. You can:

  • Edit the avatar: By clicking the avatar next to the Name in the top left

  • Choose what channel the Webhook posts to: By selecting the desired text channel in the dropdown menu.

  • Name your Webhook: Good for distinguishing multiple webhooks for multiple different services. You now have your own handy URL / pneumatic tube schoomp-er that you can link to more websites to receive messages from.

Quick Example: GitHub Webhook Integration

Since webhooks can’t really function on their own and need to be linked to another website to function as intended, I figured it’d be best to include a sample integration for any of you GitHub enthusiasts and code-pushers.

You can use Discord’s webhooks to send any code merge or push updates in a repository of yours into a text channel in your server.

  1. Get the webhook URL for the server/channel you want to receive messages:

In my server, I’ve created a text channel labeled #general-chat and I want my repo updates to post messages here!

Therefore, I’ll grab the webhook URL for this channel by pressing the Copy Webhook URL button:

  1. Add the webhook URL into your GitHub repo settings

Choose the repository that you’d like to get updates from in your Discord server. Once you’ve selected the repo, go into the Settings > Webhooks menu

And then click the “Add webhook” button, and enter the Discord-generated URL in the “Payload URL” blank.

To make the webhook display messages properly, it’s really really really REALLY really important that you append ‘/github’ at the end of it. Yes, like five-reallys important.

In addition to the URL, you have some more GitHub-specific options to choose from. For content type, stick with application/json. Discord’s webhook format really likes JSON. In the next section, you can choose to customize what kind of events trigger webhook messages.

Click the last “Add webhook” button beneath the event notifications customization option, and you’re all set! Pushing any updates in the repo (including editing the readme file) will show up in your text channel:

And you’re all set! GitHub is just one example of an integration that can post messages via webhook. If you’ve got a knack for JSON application-building or HTTP POST requests and want to customize your own webhooks, you can dig up some more information in our developer docs.

Members List Recent Activity FAQ

To learn more about activity status, check out the Activity Status (Recent Activity) article.

What this article covers:

  • What is the Members List Recent Activity Feature?
  • How does the Feature Work?
    • Viewing Activity Cards
    • Engaging with Activity Cards
    • Types of Activity Content
    • Activity Privacy
  • Game Profile
  • Have Ideas or Feedback?

What is the Members List Recent Activity Feature?

This feature is currently in beta. It is limited to a small percentage of users within English-prominent regions and available only on the desktop app. The experiment may be modified or discontinued.

Want to easily catch up with your friends and create more shared experiences together?

With the Members List Recent Activity feature, you’ll be able to view the recent activities of your friends and recent contacts - including the video games they’re playing, the music they’re listening to, and much more!

How does the Feature Work?

Viewing Activity Cards

With the Members List Recent Activity feature, you’ll be able to view activity cards within Discord. Activity cards will show live and recent activities of those you’ve interacted with - within servers and your friends.

If an activity is currently taking place, it’ll show an incrementing timer for how much time has elapsed. Otherwise, it’ll show how long ago the activity took place.

You can collapse the view down to three activity cards and expand to see everything (up to 50 recent activities).

You can also choose to fully collapse activity cards or hide activity cards by selecting the cogwheel [] (within the activity card) and pressing the checkbox for the Hide Activity Cards option.

Engaging with Activity Cards

Want to ask a friend about that new game they’re playing? By selecting the activity cards, you can reply directly to the activity or even send them an emoji. In either case, this will send a direct message (DM) with a reference to the activity.

Types of Activity Content

Initially, the content shown within activity cards will reflect gaming activity, but over time, other types of activity will also be shown - including game achievements, Spotify, Crunchyroll, and more.

Activity Privacy

You can prevent your activity from appearing in this feature in three ways: (1) globally, (2) for a specific server, or (3) for a specific game.

Globally

If you want to control whether any detected game is shared, you can enable or disable your global settings in the Activity Privacy settings.

  1. Head over to your User Settings by selecting the cogwheel [] in the bottom left corner.

  2. Then under the Activity Settings section, select Activity Privacy.

  3. From here, you can use the toggle to enable or disable Share Activity with Others.

Note: Connected Accounts such as Xbox, PlayStation, Spotify, or Crunchyroll have their own settings for activity sharing. To disable sharing these activities, you can adjust the settings in Connections > toggle Display as your status.

Specific Server

If you only want to prevent your detected game activity from appearing in a specific server, you can adjust your server-specific Privacy Settings. Select the dropdown menu [] next to the server’s name, select Privacy Settings, and then toggle Activity Status.

Note: Anyone you’ve friended in this server can still see your activity.

Specific Games

Alternatively, if you just want to prevent a specific game from being shared, you can disable specific games through the Registered Games menu.

  1. Head over to your User Settings by selecting the cogwheel [] in the bottom left corner.

  2. Then under the Activity Settings section, select Registered Games.

  3. From here, you can select the icon for Toggle Detection to prevent a game from showing up in the activity cards going forward.

Game Profile

This feature does not display on the browser or mobile app and is only available on the desktop app (Windows, Mac, and Linux).

If someone is playing a game and a game profile exists for this game, you can tap on the game icon within the app and be provided with additional information. Here is how to access this.

  1. Tap on the profile of the user you want to view (this can be done through a server’s members list in a server, DM, group chat message, or your friend’s list) and tap on the icon of the game they’re playing.

  2. If the game has a game profile, the game icon will not only be clickable, but a page within the app will open to display information about the game.

  3. On a game profile, you can find any available information about the game (eg. genre, game summary, social links, Discord server, publisher, available platforms like device type, consoles, etc.)

It will also include screenshots and promotional art of the game, recommendations for similar games, and usernames of friends who have played the same game.

If a game does not have a game profile, it’s because not enough users have played the game to display any data.

New Member Messages

Anyways, if you’re the accommodating présentateur type, you can choose which text channel you’d like to display these welcome messages for newcomers. It’s a pretty simple process:

You can select which Text channel to be your welcome channel from the dropdown menu in the System Messages Channel section.

If you don’t feel like announcing a fanfare anytime a new friend comes around, just select the No System Messages option at the top!

Have you wanted to personalize your identity across different servers? Whether you’re roleplaying in a gaming server and want your profile to match your character’s aesthetic, or sharing your passion for coffee with themed avatars - our Nitro perk per-server profiles makes it possible!

What are per-server profiles?

Per-server profiles are a new customization feature for Nitro users! With per-server profiles, users can set a different server-specific avatar, banner, and about me section for each of the servers they’re in.

How to Customize Your Profile for Different Servers

NOTE: Even if you change your per-server profile, your user profile will be unaffected and remain as your primary avatar in servers where you don’t upload server avatars.

How can I change my Server Avatar?

Desktop/Browser: Right-Click on your Avatar

  1. In the browser or desktop app, you can right-click your avatar in a text channel. This will activate the drop-down menu.

  2. Select Edit Per-server Profile to navigate to the Per-server Profiles page.

  3. You can then press on your avatar or Change Avatar to upload the specific avatar you would like to use for that per-server profile.

Like profile avatars, PNG and JPG are the supported file types and Nitro users can upload a GIF for their server avatars.

Right-click your avatar and select Edit Per-server Profile to customize it for specific servers
  1. Once you have chosen your avatar, press Save Changes to confirm.
Save Changes Button

After uploading a server avatar, you can crop, center, and rotate PNG, JPG, and GIF files.

Edit your avatar: Crop, center, and rotate your profile picture
Desktop/Browser: Left-Click on your Avatar

  1. Alternatively, you can left-click your avatar in the server’s Member List, which is the sidebar located to the right, to open the mini profile pop-up. You can also open this when left-clicking on your avatar within a text channel, or in a voice channel.

  2. You’ll then see an Edit Profile option that you can press.

  3. Select Edit per-server profile to change your server avatar in the per-server profile page.

Left-click your avatar in the Member List and select Edit Per-server Profile
  1. When you’re all set, press Save Changes to confirm your avatar change.
Save Changes Button
Desktop/Browser: Resetting My Server Avatar to a Recent Avatar

Recent Avatars automatically saves your 6 most recent avatar uploads across all platforms. While avatars uploaded from mobile are stored in your history, you can only view and select from your Recent Avatars when using Discord on desktop or browser versions.

To return to a recent avatar, navigate to the Profiles page. You can do this using either of the methods described above.

If you’d like to use a different recent avatar instead, select Change Avatar and choose one from the Recent Avatars section.

After making your selection, press Apply and Save Changes to confirm.

Selecting a Recent Avatar
Mobile: Changing your Server Avatar

You can customize your server avatar on iOS or Android through two methods: User Profile and Per-server Profiles.

Through the User Profile:

  1. Navigate to the specific server and select your avatar from either a channel where you’ve posted messages or from the server’s Member List.

  2. Tap Edit Per-server Profile to access your Per-server Profiles settings.

  3. In the Per-server Profiles page, tap your current server avatar and select Upload Image to set a new avatar.

Per-server Profiles on Mobile
  1. After a new server avatar has been uploaded, tap Save in the top right corner to confirm the change.
Remember to tap Save on mobile devices to confirm your profile changes

Through Per-server Profiles:

  1. Tap on the server’s name and select Edit Per-server Profile to open your Per-server Profiles settings.

  2. Select your current server avatar and tap Upload Image to choose a new image.

Uploading an image in per-server profiles
  1. After making your changes, tap Save in the top-right corner to confirm.
Tap Save on mobile devices to confirm your profile changes

How do I change my profile theme?

Nitro members can customize each of their per-server profile themes! This will specifically change the colors of your mini profile card. You can choose a Primary color and an Accent color.

On Desktop/Browser

In your Profiles tab > Per-server Profiles page, under the Profile Theme, press the Primary color square to choose the main color of your mini profile card. Then, press the Accent color square to choose a secondary color.

Select Profile Theme Colors: Choose a primary and accent color on desktop
On Mobile

To access your Per-server Profile page on your mobile clients, swipe right while in the Discord app and tap on your avatar icon in the bottom right corner to open up your profile. Then, tap Edit Profile.

To customize your User Profile and per-server profiles, tap your avatar and Edit Profile

You can also tap on your avatar icon in a channel of your desired server and select Edit Per-server Profile in your mini profile card.

In the Profile page, make sure the profile option slider is towards the right for Per-server Profile and that server you intend to customize your per-server profile is chosen in the dropdown menu.

Per-server Profiles Tab on Mobile

Under the Profile Themes section, press the Primary color square to choose the main color of your mini profile card. Then, press the Accent color square to choose a secondary color.

Pick a Primary and Accent color under Profile Theme

Please note: if you have Sync profile themes enabled in your Accessibility settings page, which syncs your profile themes to your chosen Discord client theme, the background color of your profile card will reflect the color of your client theme (Light or Dark).

How do I change my profile banner?

Head over to your User Settings > Profiles > Per-server Profiles and press Change Banner to upload your server banner.

Changing your Profile Banner on Desktop

Nitro members can upload an image or animated GIF as their profile banner. Supported file types are PNG, JPG, and animated GIFs under 10MB. The recommended minimum size is 600x240.

How do I set up an “About Me” for my Per-Server Profile?

In the Per-server Profiles settings page, you can write a small blurb in the text box under About Me that’s specific to your per-server profile.

Your About Me for your per-server profile can have:

  • Up to 190 characters
  • Markdown text and links
  • Emojis
  • Unicode NOTE: Nitro and Nitro Classic members can use custom emojis in their About Me.
About Me section in Profiles

How do I add avatar decorations and profile effects to my per-server profile?

  1. In your Per-server Profiles settings, be sure to choose the server you would like to update within the Choose A Server selection box.
Choose Server dropdown in Per-server Profiles
  1. Once you have chosen the server, press Change Decoration or Change Effect to select the avatar decoration or profile effect you would like to set for the per-server profile.
Example of Adding an Avatar Decoration and a Profile Effect
  1. When you’re ready, be sure to confirm your changes by pressing Save Changes in the pop up box located at the bottom.

NOTE: Avatar decorations and profile effects can be found in the Shop. You must purchase a profile cosmetic before being able to add to your profile.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What happened to server nicknames?

A: Server nicknames still exist and are free to all Discord users! To change your server nickname, you can follow the same steps to change your server avatar, but instead input/change your server nickname in the in-app pop-up window.

Learn more about server nicknames in this article!

Q: Do I get custom server avatars with Nitro Classic?

A: Nitro Classic users can still set server nicknames; however only Nitro users will be able to set custom server avatars.

Learn more about Nitro and Nitro Classic in this article!

Q: What are the size limits and accepted file types for server avatars?

A: Accepted file types for server avatars are JPG, PNG, and GIF files. The maximum file size is 8 MB.

Q: Can I edit avatars after I upload them?

A: You can crop, center, and rotate files after uploading them.

Q: Is there a limit to the number of custom server avatars I can have?

A: No, but there is a limit to the number of servers you can join. Nitro users can join up to 200 servers.

Q: Can I have more than 1 avatar in a server?

A: At this time, you may only set 1 custom avatar per server.

Q: Can I reset all my server avatars at once?

A: Unfortunately, there is no bulk editing option at this time. You will need to manually reset your avatar in each server.

Q: Can I change my server-specific avatar decoration and profile effect on my mobile device?

A: At this time, you can only change server-specific avatar decoration and profile effects on the desktop/browser app.

Q: Will I get in trouble for using an inappropriate image as a server avatar?

A: As is true for all content that you use on Discord, you are responsible for ensuring that any content you use for server avatars complies with our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.

Q: Are server owners or admins able to change another server member’s avatar like how they can change nicknames?

A: No, server owners and/or admins do not have the ability to change a server member’s server avatar or reset it to their primary avatar.

If you notice someone using a server avatar that violates our Terms of Service or Community Guidelines, please use our report form to report the user to our Trust and Safety team.

Polls FAQ

What this article covers:

  • What is Polls?
  • How do I create a Poll?
    • Desktop
    • Mobile
  • How do I vote in a Poll?
    • Desktop
    • Mobile
  • How to manage Poll Permissions as a Server Owner/Administrator
    • Role Permission
    • Channel Permission
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What is Polls?

Polls is a feature on Discord with which you can create a poll to have your friends and community members vote on anything! You can add up to 10 answers for people to vote on in each poll. This can help decide the next game you’ll play together for game night, if pineapple belongs on pizza, and so much more!

How do I create a Poll?

A poll can have up to 10 answers listed.
Any text within a poll (including questions and answers), will apply filters set by AutoMod.
Desktop

  1. Tap on the plus sign [] located in the text field of the text channel, text chat of a voice channel, or group message that you want to share the poll in.

  2. Next, tap Poll to create a new poll.

  3. You can input the following information for your poll:

  • What the actual poll is about
  • All possible selectable answers users can vote on (you can also select an emoji or custom emoji to represent each one too)
  • How long the poll will available (1 hour, 4 hours, 8 hours, 24 hours, 3 days, or 1 week)
  • If those voting can select more than one answer
  1. Once everything has been filled out, you can tap Post to send your poll!
Mobile
For the best experience with Polls on mobile, please make sure you’re running Discord app version 221 or higher.

  1. Tap on the plus sign [] located in the text field of the text channel, text chat of a voice channel, or group message that you want to share the poll in.

  2. Next, tap Poll to create a poll.

  3. You can input the following information for your poll:

  • What the actual poll is about
  • All possible selectable answers users can vote on (you can also select an emoji or custom emoji to represent each one too)
  • How long the poll will be available (1 hour, 4 hours, 8 hours, 24 hours, 3 days, or 1 week)
  • If those voting can select more than one answer
  1. Once everything has been filled out, you can tap on Post to send your poll!

How do I vote in a Poll?

Want to change your selection on a poll? Tap on Remove Vote to remove your vote and then you can vote again.
Desktop

  1. Navigate to the poll you want to vote in and then tap on one answer or multiple answers to the poll. Once selected, you’ll see a check mark appear on the right hand side of the poll selection.

  2. Tap Vote to submit your answer.

  3. You know your vote has gone through once a check mark appears on the selection, and you’ll see the option to change your vote.

Mobile

  1. Navigate to the poll you want to vote on and tap on your vote.

  2. Next, tap on Vote to submit your answer.

  3. You’ll know your vote has gone through because you’ll see a check mark next to your vote.

How to manage Poll Permissions as a Server Owner/Administrator

Permissions for Polls can be managed from a server or channel level.

Role Permission

  1. Tap on your server’s name in the top left corner and then tap on Server Settings.

  2. Navigate to Roles and then select which role you’d like to change the permission for, or tap on Default Permissions to edit this role for everyone.

  3. Scroll down until you see Create Polls. A “check mark” means this feature is enabled and an “x” means it’s disabled.

  4. Lastly, save your changes to apply them.

Channel Permission

  1. Navigate to the channel you want to edit and tap on the cogwheel [].

  2. Then, tap on Permissions.

  3. Under this setting you can enable or disable Polls per role. To do so, tap on the role you want to edit.

  4. Now scroll down until you see Create Polls. A “check mark” means this feature is enabled and an “x” means it’s disabled.

  5. Lastly, save your changes to apply them.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Where can I start a poll?

A: A poll can take place in a text channel, direct message, group message, or announcement channel.

Q: How can I delete a poll?

A: The only way to delete a poll is to delete the entire message (by tapping on the “…” next to a message). Once the poll has been deleted, it can not be restored.

Q: Can I vote anonymously in a poll?

A: No, there is no option to vote anonymously at this time.

Q: How long can a poll be open for?

A: The poll creator chooses how long they want the poll to be open when creating the poll. The poll creator can choose to end the poll early at any time. Unless it ends early, a poll can be left open for up to 1 week.

Q: Can I use slash commands (for example: /poll) to create a poll?

A: No, it is not possible to create a poll using a slash command at this time.

Q: Can poll choices be modified at any time?

A: As long as the poll is still open, you can modify your poll choice.

Q: Can poll results be saved and/or deleted?

A: While polls behave like messages in terms of being deleted, there is no separate function to archive polls at this time. You can pin a poll to Pinned Messages.

Quick Switcher

Discord’s Quick Switch feature is an essential tool that helps you navigate Discord faster and more efficiently than ever before.

What this article covers:

  • What’s the Quick Switcher?
  • How do I use the Quick Switcher?

What’s the Quick Switcher?

The Quick Switcher is a powerful navigation tool in Discord that lets you instantly jump between different parts of the app. Think of it as a search bar that helps you quickly find and switch to any channel, direct message, or server without clicking through menus. It’s especially useful for power users who want to navigate Discord efficiently using their keyboard.

How do I use the Quick Switcher?

Navigate effortlessly between channels, DMs, and servers with Quick Switch. Simply press CTRL+K or ⌘+K to open the switcher and instantly jump to your desired destination.

Use these Quick Switch prefixes to find exactly what you need:

Prefix

Action

Find and switch between servers

@

Access direct messages with users

Navigate to text channels

!

Find and join voice channels

Using the @ Prefix in Quick Switcher

Need to return to the most recent channel? Just hit the RETURN or ENTER key to return to your previous channel.

Ready to become a Quick Switch expert? Give it a try!

Rules Screening FAQ

Joining a community server can be extremely overwhelming and confusing. It’s common to have to go through a series of convoluted steps that take you from channels to channels before you can participate in the server. It should not be this hard. Introducing Rules Screening!

In order to see this feature, you must enable Community for your Discord server.

What this article covers:

  • What is Rules Screening?
  • Admin Settings
    • How to Customize Rules Screening
  • Rules Screening for Joining Server Members
  • Frequently Asked Questions
What is Rules Screening?

Rules screening allows you to set up rules that new members must explicitly agree to before they can talk, react, or DM Other members.

Note: Manually verifying a member (Server Settings > Members) will bypass this requirement.
Admin Settings

If you are the owner of the server or a server admin, you can customize the rules and review applications within the server.

  1. To get started, head over to Server Settings by selecting the dropdown menu next to the server name.

  2. Then, head to the Safety Setup tab under the Moderation category in the left side bar.

  3. Once you arrive at the Safety Set Up page, you will be able to customize the Rules Screening, Verification Level, and Automod settings.

How to Customize Rules Screening

If you’d like to add Rules Screening to your server, navigate to the Safety Set Up tab within your Server Settings to get started.

  1. Once in the Safety Set Up page, select the Edit button within DM and Spam Protection.

  2. Within DM and Spam Protection, press Members must accept rules before they can talk or DM. This will open the Set up server rules menu.

  3. To set up the rules you would like to add for Rules Screening, press the Get Started button to open the Server Rules menu.

  4. Within Server Rules, you can select any example rules provided or you can create customized rules. If you’d like to add additional rules, select Add a Rule.

You can create a maximum of 16 server rules.
  1. Once the rules have been set, be sure to press Save and enable Members must accept rules before they can talk for Rules Screening.
- We know communities often need more sophisticated screening methods like custom response/manual application, oAuth, and Linked Roles.
- We are hard at work building these features so that we can release them to you soon as well! We sadly don’t have an exact ETA when these features will be released, but stay tuned for more details soon!
Rules Screening for Joining Server Members

If you are joining a server with Rules Screening enabled, you will see a bar at the bottom that asks you to complete a few more steps before you can talk.

Before you can participate in the server, you will need to read and agree to the Server Rules.

Once you agree to the rules, press submit and you will have access to the server!

Before proceeding further:
- If you have a bot role gate currently enabled, make sure you re-enable perms on @everyone when you enact Rules Screening to ensure it works properly.
