Another way to let us know if the media was incorrectly flagged is to right-click or long press the media and find the option to Mark as Not Sensitive. By selecting this, adults will see the media again with the ability to confirm “Mark as not sensitive.”

“Mark as not sensitive” flow, showing a blocked DM image with a Clyde message and a Mark as Not Sensitive option

Note: Once these filter preferences are changed to show or blur all historic and new media will follow your selected settings. If you change the setting to block, it will only impact image-based media detected by the filters going forward.

Future Updates

Discord plans to continue improving our Sensitive Media filters to better detect sensitive content and provide users with more control over their Discord experience. We are also exploring additional filter categories and detection methods to help create a more comfortable environment for all users.

Check our Safety News Hub for the latest information about updates to our safety features and content filters.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is the difference between “blur”, “block”, and “show” when it comes to sensitive media?

A: There are a few important differences between these options, namely:

  • Block: This option prevents potentially sensitive content from appearing in your Discord experience.
  • Blur: This option conceals content behind a cover that adult users and teen users in some countries can press to reveal when they choose to view it.
  • Show: This option displays potentially sensitive content. Q: Can teens turn off the filters completely?

A: No. Sensitive content is filtered by default. Images flagged by Discord’s content filters are blurred or blocked for teens depending on where they appear:

  • Direct messages from friends: blurred
  • Direct messages from strangers: blocked
  • Server channel messages: blurred These filters apply only to images. They do not scan text messages, voice, or calls. Viewing blurred content, or changing these settings to “Show,” requires confirming you’re an adult.

Q: What’s the difference between the Mature Sexual Media and Graphic Media filters?

A: The Mature Sexual Media filter detects content that may contain sexually explicit or suggestive material involving adults.

The Graphic Media filter detects content that may contain violent or potentially disturbing visual content.

Both filters work together to help reduce exposure to potentially distressing image-based media.

Q: How does Discord detect sensitive media?

A: When these filters are enabled, messages containing image-based media are processed by our automated systems to identify content that may fall under either filter category. While our technology continues to improve, no automated system is perfect, which is why we provide ways for users to report incorrect detections.

Q: Does Discord review all the content detected by the filters?

A: No. These filters have been developed to help improve the user experience on Discord by limiting exposure to image-based media that users may find sensitive or inappropriate.

Users can always report content detected by the filters to Discord for review if you believe the content violates Discord’s Community Guidelines.

Discord Student Hubs Guidelines

Discord Hubs for Students allow students to verify their Discord account with their official student email, and unlock access to an exclusive hub for students at their school. Within the hub, they can connect with other verified students, discover servers for study groups or classes, and share their own servers for fellow students to join.

Note to All Hub Members

Please be mindful that:

  • Hubs are not affiliated with or managed by a school or school staff.
  • Servers in a Hub are student-run but may include non-students.
Note to Server Owners and Moderators of Servers in a Hub

Server owners and moderators are responsible and accountable for their server’s affiliation in a Student Hub. We empower and equip our communities to have the tools to help them properly ensure that these spaces are not engaging in any violations and are kept safe and welcoming. Student Hubs have some different features and servers must follow additional requirements as described below.

Student Hub Guidelines
  1. Abide by the Community Guidelines and Terms of Service. This means that issues reported to your server should be addressed by your moderators and admins. Your moderator team should know when to escalate issues to Trust & Safety. Servers that violate Discord’s Community Guidelines and Terms of Service will be subject to further action from our Trust & Safety Team.
  • We want Discord to be a safe, positive, and inclusive experience. Our Trust & Safety team will investigate Student Hubs that are reported to us or that we proactively identify as likely in violation of our policies, and Trust & Safety team members may temporarily join a Student Hub to investigate potential violations.
  • We may remove an affiliated server or account from the Student Hub if the server or account recently violated our Community Guidelines and received an enforcement action.
  1. Foster a healthy and positive environment. People should feel welcome in your Student Hub and affiliated-server. Create environments where people want to spend time with each other, share interests, participate in community events, and build friendships. Examples include:
  • No content or behavior meant to single out, bully, or harass other students, faculty, or server members.
  • No discussions about controlled substances or drugs. This may get you reported to law enforcement.
  • No servers dedicated to using regulated goods, such as alcohol.
  • Do not cultivate general toxic behavior or other derogatory content.

  1. Ensure academic honesty. No content or behavior promoting, facilitating, or conducting academic dishonesty, including cheating and plagiarism. Study groups and class discussions are allowed and highly recommended!

  2. Do not host graphic or sexual content. Graphic violence and sexual content is not allowed in Student Hubs. Servers linked to Student Hubs should be appropriate for audiences of all ages 13+ and cannot include age-gated servers.

  3. Have a server name and description that accurately describes the server that is free of profanity. Help potential members understand why they want to join the server you listed in your Student Hub.

  4. Respect people’s intellectual property and other rights. Only incorporate content that you own or have a license to use. Do not invade anyone’s privacy, libel them, or otherwise violate their rights.

  5. Have a moderator team. Moderators can help ensure nothing rule-breaking is happening in your Student Hub-affiliated server and can find meaningful ways for your members to engage. Build a moderator team that members of your community can trust and turn to for help.

We may consider off-platform behavior when assessing an account or server for violation of the Student Hub guidelines.

Enforcement

If you or your affiliated-Server violate any of the above guidelines, we may take any of the following enforcement actions:

  • Temporarily banning your server from the Student Hub until abides by the above guidelines.

  • Removing your server from the Student Hub permanently.

  • Temporarily banning your account from the Student Hub.

  • Removing your account and school email from being able to participate in the Student Hub.

  • Temporarily banning your account from Discord. If your server or account is violating our Community Guidelines, you will receive additional enforcement actions, which include:

  • Removing violative content.

  • Warning an account/server.

  • Temporarily banning your account.

  • Permanently banning your account.

  • Temporarily banning a server.

  • Permanently banning your server.

Discord Warning System

The Discord Warning System informs users when they have broken our rules, what actions we have taken, and how it may impact their overall account standing. This system includes multiple touchpoints for users to have more transparency into Discord interventions in order to better understand what happens when our rules are broken and how to avoid receiving a warning or violation in the future.

This system is built to be fair and transparent to users. We want users to learn our rules and stay on the platform, whenever possible. We have designed the system to show users what they did wrong, provide more educational resources about our rules, and to place appropriate restrictions on accounts so that Discord users get a chance to make things right.

The system gives users room to learn from their mistakes and change their behavior. We believe that helping people learn how to follow Discord’s rules makes the platform safer.

However, because protecting our users is a top priority, when we become aware of a user engaging in repeated violations or particularly egregious harms, we will take swift action to permanently remove that user and the violating content.

What this article covers:

  • Violations
  • Account Standing
  • Suspensions (aka Bans)
  • Server Violations
  • Warnings
  • Requesting a Review
  • Frequently Asked Questions
Violations

Users who break the rules will receive a system direct message (DM) from Discord letting them know they received a violation. Users will receive a DM each time they break our rules.

Within the DM, users will see a card that summarizes the violation. Pressing on the card will reveal further details for the violation.

The card will go over the following with the user:

  • which specific policy they violated
  • it may include detail about which content broke our rules
  • it lists any actions that Discord has taken on the user
  • a link to a policy explanation for the relevant Discord Community Guidelines Our system determines a relevant and specific set of actions to take for a particular violation of our policies. When weighing what action to take, we consider the severity of the harm, the type of user content (i.e. text, image, behavior), and the user’s history of past violations.

For example, if a user posted an image that broke the rules, they may temporarily lose the ability to post images. If the violation was not particularly severe, they may lose these features for a few hours. If it was a repeated violation or higher severity violation, they may lose some features for a few days or up to one year. Similarly, violations related to specific Discord features, such as Quests may result in loss of eligibility for that feature or removal of rewards obtained through prohibited behavior.

For the most severe harms, users will be immediately subject to a permanent suspension and should look to their email inbox for more information from Discord.

Suspension Notification on Desktop (Left) and Mobile (Right)
Account Standing
Reviewing Account Standing in User Settings on Desktop

Users will be able to see their account’s standing with Discord by heading into your User Settings > My Account > Standing. For most users, they will see that they’re all good, and not much else.

Important: When users break our rules and receive a violation, they will be brought to the Account Standing section. in-app This section will show users a summary of their violations and how they have affected their standing. Repeated violations will add up to trigger increasingly strong penalties, up to permanent suspensions.

Users will be able to see where they stand based on their track record. Since we weigh each violation based on the severity of the harm, a user does not have a fixed number of chances before they receive a harsher penalty. Where they stand will depend on the severity of the violation.

Users will find themselves in one of the following standings:

  • All good: The user has no active violations and has access to all Discord features
  • Limited: The user has an active violation that temporarily limited access to some features. Further violations will result in more or longer limits.
  • Very Limited: The user has one or more active violations that temporarily limited access to more features for a longer period of time. Further violations may put the account at risk.
  • At Risk: The user has one or more active violations. Any further violations may result in a permanent suspension.
  • Permanent suspension: The user no longer has access to Discord due to severe or repeated violations. Your account standing reflects any active violations and their severity, which you can view in the Active Violations section under Account Standing.

It’s important to understand that violations and their associated restrictions are two separate things. A restriction (such as a temporary limit on messaging or posting) may lift before the violation itself fully expires. Until a violation expires, it will remain listed under Active Violations and may continue to affect your account standing, even if its associated restriction is no longer active.

Most violations expire after 90 days, at which point they move to the Expired Violations section and no longer impact your account standing. More severe violations may remain active longer — check the violation detail for its specific expiration date.

After violations expire, they can still be viewed in the Expired Violation section.

Suspensions (aka Bans)

When a user repeatedly breaks Discord’s rules or has a particularly serious violation, they will lose access to Discord. This suspension can be temporary (i.e. temp ban) or permanent (i.e. ban).

A suspended user will still be able to log-in to review their Account Standing, and see both their violations and the duration of their suspension. This view will be available for the duration of the suspension. Users will also be able to submit feedback and request a review of a violation if they believe we made a mistake. (See below for more information on submitting feedback).

Suspended Account in Account Standing Page
Server Violations

When a server is focused on or contains a lot of content that breaks Discord’s rules, the owner will receive a violation and the guild may be removed or restricted. Just like user violations, the server owner will receive a system DM that summarizes the violation and provides them with more detail.

Example of a Server Violation Notification

Our system determines relevant actions for server violations depending on the particular violation. The server may be removed or lose access to certain features. The owner may lose the ability to create more servers or be permanently suspended.

When a server is engaged in serious violations of Discord rules, the server’s members may also receive a violation that affects their account standing.

Only the server owner can request a review of server violations.

Warnings

Discord sends warnings to inform users about our rules. We issue these warnings if a user was in a server that violated our rules or if they interacted with rule-breaking content—even if they didn’t participate in the violation themselves. Learn more about Discord Official Messages here.

Warning Message Sent from Discord

Warnings will come via a system DM and will contain information about what happened and more information about our rules. Warnings do not impact account standing but are still important for users to understand our rules so they can correct future behavior. These warnings are similar to those that Discord has sent in the past.

Requesting a Review

Sometimes we get it wrong. Every violation notice includes a link to our webform, where users can provide feedback or ask that Discord review a violation and penalty applied to their account. While it may take time to respond to every request, we prioritize helping users that believe they have been permanently suspended in error.

Users can let us know if they feel Discord took an unwarranted action against their account.

The Warning System started rolling out on October 24th, 2023 in select regions. View our Safety News Hub for many more updates to our Warning System in the future.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Are suspensions temporary or permanent?

A: Temporary suspensions can last up to 1 year. A user’s account and username will be preserved for that time. They will regain access at the end of the suspension.

Permanent suspensions (formerly called “bans”) do not expire. The user will lose their account. They will have a grace period to appeal, after which their username will be made available again.

Q: Do any current or past violations I received before the launch of the Warning System count against my account standing?

A: No, only violations that have occurred after the launch of the Warning System will count against your account standing.

Q: Why did my account standing jump from “All Good” to a permanent suspension?

A: Each violation is weighed differently – depending on the severity of the incident. A high severity violation may cause the account standing to change more dramatically. The most severe violations lead straight to a permanent suspension (i.e. violations ofto a child safety policy).

Q: How many chances do I get? What are the penalties for one violation or five violations?

A: Discord’s violations are not strikes and there is no simple formula from number of violations to specific penalties. We weigh the severity and context of each violation and we look at a user’s history of past violations when calculating the user’s account standing.

Q: What to do if I want to report another Discord user’s actions?

A: See our article about how to report abuse to Discord.

Q: Can I appeal my account standing overall?

A: No, you cannot appeal your account standing overall. You should appeal specific violations that contribute to your account standing.

Q: What’s the difference between a violation and a warning?

A: Discord issues violations when we become aware of users who have broken our rules. Discord will take action on their account and their account standing will be impacted. The intervention depends on each unique violation. The account standing impact depends both on the unique violation and culmination of active violations.

Warnings may be issued when a user was in a server that broke our rules or engaged with content that broke our rules, but the user did not do anything themselves. Warnings do not affect account standing. They provide users with more information about the rules.

Q: Are you now scanning all my messages in servers, group chats and DMs?

A: Our Warning System doesn’t introduce any new scanning of content or messages. This feature is a new way for users to have more transparency into Discord content moderation decisions and the status of their account.

As described in our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, Discord does scan all spaces for high harm content like malware and child sexual abuse material, and we may scan for other policy violations in large communities. We do not scan all content in smaller spaces such as direct messages (DM), group chats, and small/non-community servers–for other violations of our Community Guidelines. For content in teen spaces, learn more about protective features like our safety alerts.

Filter Messages Using Regular Expressions (Regex)

AutoMod allows you to filter messages based on regular expression (regex) patterns in your Custom Keyword rules.

Regular expressions let you define patterns that you want AutoMod to detect in messages and respond to accordingly, and can be a more efficient and effective way to filter out unwanted messages in your community.

How it Works

A regex pattern is like a bunch of keywords all packed into one. By filtering based on patterns instead of individual keywords, you can save time and effort from having to think of 50 variations of “free Nitro” that you’d want to filter out and adding each of them to your rules - instead, you could write a singular regex pattern that’ll do the same job.

This also makes regex an effective way to prevent people who try to bypass your keyword filters by intentionally misspelling words or using word variants, or block messages containing non-words like phone numbers, addresses (email, IP, physical), and that weird-lookin’ zalgo text.

For Example: Trying to block or receive alerts whenever someone posts a message containing an email address in your server? You can’t enter every possible email address that exists into your keyword filters (and you really don’t want to), but you can use a regex pattern like the above to pattern-match the format of a typical email address. This lets AutoMod flag messages containing all kinds of email addresses!

As you begin, note the following:

  • Find regex filtering in Server Settings > AutoMod > any of your Custom Keyword Rules (must have “Manage Server” or “Administrator” permissions)
  • We use the Rust flavor of regex and recommend writing your regex in Rust syntax to minimize errors. To edit and test your regex syntax in Rust, we recommend using Rustexp.
  • Case-insensitive and unicode support flags are on by default for every regex pattern.
Be careful!

Regex filtering is advanced and not for the faint of heart. Improper regular expressions could prevent all users from being able to send messages that are acceptable in your community. We recommend only using this if you know what you’re doing.

Be sure to use an external tool like Rustexp to validate your Regex and make sure it works as expected.

FAQ

Q: What do I do if my regex syntax is invalid or doesn’t work?

A: Considerations to keep in mind to validate your regex:

  • Always test and validate your syntax before saving your changes. Valid syntax means your regex does not contain any syntax errors.

  • Ensure your syntax compiles below our limits - even if your regex has valid syntax, it might still not be accepted if it is too complex and exceeds some of our technical limits.

  • Regular expressions must not include backreferences since those are not supported. If you find your regex isn’t working, go through these steps:

  • Check that your syntax is valid. Because AutoMod uses the Rust-flavor of regex, we recommend testing your regular expressions in an engine that also uses Rust, such as Rustexp.

  • Make sure the word or type of message you’re targeting works as expected.

  • Paste your regex into AutoMod and confirm your syntax doesn’t contain errors. Save the rule to enable the regular expression.

  • It is recommended to send a few messages that you expect to be blocked, as well as a few messages that you expect to go through from a non-moderator account to ensure your regular expression is behaving as expected. Q: What are all the different types of regex errors and what do they mean OR and how do I fix them?

A: The different type of errors include:

  • Invalid syntax - Your regex contains a syntax error(s).
  • Compile size exceeded limit. The regular expression compiled above our size limit.
  • Too long. Regular expressions are limited to 10 expressions total with 75 characters each. Q: How can I enable or disable regular expression flags, such as case insensitivity?

A: Regular expressions can be used with flags to instruct the compiler how to evaluate the regular expression. The Rust regex crate supports the following flags:

  • u unicode
  • i case insensitive
  • s dot matches newline
  • m multiline Case-insensitive and unicode support flags are on by default for every regex pattern. However, you can overwrite these flags or enable other flags by prefixing your regular expression with a modifier. The syntax to enable a modifier is: (?a), and the syntax to disable a monitor is:(?-a), where a is the flag you wish to enable to disable.

Q: Do you have any examples of starter regular expressions?

A: Match all braille characters detailed in this link here!

  • [800-8FF]+ Match all Greek letters except beta:

  • [–β]+

Help! I’m old enough to use Discord in my country but I got locked out?

We require all users to meet the minimum age requirement for their region. If you meet that requirement and have been locked out of Discord, you can appeal your banned account by following the instructions below.

“Your account is suspended” screen, showing an Active Violations card for a minimum age requirements violation
How to Confirm Your Age Group to Unlock Your Account

  1. Log in to your locked Discord account.

  2. Locate your Active Violations and open the Minimum Age Requirements violation card.

“Minimum Age Requirements” Violation Card
  1. Press “Confirm you meet the minimum age requirement in your region” to start the appeal process.
Violation detail card open, with the “Confirm you meet the minimum age requirement in your region” button highlighted
  1. From here you’d choose a method to confirm your age group from the options and follow the detailed instructions here. What options are actually available to you depends on factors such as your region or device, so the options you see may not be the same for everyone.
“Confirm your age group” screen listing method options: Credit Card, Video Selfie, and ID Scan
  1. If we determine you do meet the minimum age requirement in your region (which is typically processed within seconds), you’ll see “You’re all set” at the top of your Active Violations screen, and you can now log back into your account as your access should be fully restored.

How to Access an Age-Restricted Server FAQ

Age-restricted servers are Discord communities marked as 18+ to ensure adult content is only accessible to users who meet age requirements. These servers can be designated by server owners or admins.

What this article covers:

  • Why Is A Server Labeled As Age-Restricted?
  • I Can’t View or Join Age-Restricted servers. What Should I Do? Want to learn more?

Check out our support article here to learn more about what age-restricted servers are and how to manage them.

Why Is A Server Labeled As Age-Restricted?

Our Community Guidelines explain that adult content posted to Discord must be shared in age-restricted spaces. For servers, this can be done in two ways:

  • Server owners or users with the “Manage Server” permission can self-designate entire servers as being 18+ by adding an age-restriction..
  • Discord can classify an entire servers as 18+ through the use of an age-restricted server designation. Servers must be classified as age-restricted if the community is organized around age-restricted themes or if the majority of the server’s content is focused on 18+ content.
I Can’t View or Join Age-Restricted servers. What Should I Do?

Only users in the adult age group can enter or join servers marked as age-restricted by their server owner. This applies to the server owners and moderators as well. If you are in the teen age group, you will not be able to join or view the content in age-restricted servers.

Example of an Age-Restricted Server Confirmation Window

You can check what age group you are in at User Settings > Account Status. If you are an adult and aren’t able to access age-restricted servers, you can confirm your age group by following the instructions here.

Note: Teen safety protections may vary slightly depending on where you live, as some regions have specific requirements under local regulation. For region-specific information, see our directory here.

Note: For adults, age-restricted servers can only be joined on desktop or Android devices.

Those with iOS devices are required to “opt-in on desktop” in order to view age-restricted servers from their iOS device.

How to opt in for iOS:

  1. Sign in to Discord on desktop and navigate to your User Settings by selecting the cogwheel icon [] in the bottom left corner of the app.
Cogwheel Icon: Access User Settings

  1. In User Settings, select Messaging Permissions.

  2. Enable Allow access to age-restricted content on iOS by pressing the toggle. This will let you view age-restricted servers you are already a member of from your iOS device.

Allowing Access to Age-restricted Servers on iOS Permission

Additionally, a subset of age-restricted servers that are specifically focused on explicit content will be blocked entirely on iOS.

  • iOS users aged 18+ will only be able to join and access servers dedicated to this content on the desktop and web versions of Discord. Note: Only age-restricted server owners and moderators will be allowed to view and manage this specific subset of age-restricted servers on iOS.

How to Protect Your Server from Raids 101

On Discord, a raid is when a large number of users or bots join a server at once for disruptive or malicious intents and purposes. Raiding is against our Terms of Service guidelines.

While there are different types of behavior and activities that raiders engage in, there are a number of steps you can take to prevent raids of all types before they occur, or minimize damage as they’re happening.

Raid prevention tips:
  1. Turn on AutoMod.

Go to Server Settings > AutoMod

AutoMod lets you detect and block undesirable messages before they’re ever posted. Prevent raids from happening by using AutoMod to proactively identify potential raiders via alerts and block their messages from being posted in your server.

Here’s how:

Create your own Custom Rules to detect raiders - Enter keywords or phrases you think raiders may post in your server - or what they may have posted in the past - in the event of a raid. Turn on the “Send alert” response to receive alerts that allow you to identify potential raiders, and the “Block message” response to have AutoMod prevent raiders’ messages from being posted in your server when containing any of your keywords.

Tip: You can set up AutoMod to work as an alert system for potential raiders without resorting to blocking people’s messages from the get-go by turning on “Send alert” and turning off “Block message” in your rules.

Customize your Block Mention Spam rule - Mention raids are when raiders join your server to annoy or expose your members to undesirable content by spamming mentions via @usernames or @roles. To minimize the likelihood of raiders pulling this off successfully, turn on AutoMod’s “Block Mention Spam” rule.

Set a mention limit you think works best for your server, and enable “Block message,” “Send alert”, and/or “Timeout member” responses. This way, members can’t post messages containing an excessive number of unique mentions.

  1. Disable @here and @everyone permissions.

Go to Server Settings > Roles > Select a non-Admin or non-Moderator role > Toggle off “Mention @everyone, @here, and All Roles.”

This prevents raiders from being able to spam mentions to your entire server and/or particular channels. We recommend only granting this permission to people with roles you trust (e.g. Administrators, Moderators).

  1. Set up Raid Protection alerts.

Go to Server Settings > Safety Setup > Raid Protection

Our Raid Protection system provides protection from join-raids by using machine learning to evaluate various signals that are likely indicative of an upcoming raid and taking automated actions to safeguard your server. Set up Raid Protection alerts to stay notified whenever a raid is detected.

When a raid has been detected, we’ll automatically take action against suspicious joiners by sending you an alert to a dedicated channel of your choice and require CAPTCHA for new joiners within the next hour to prevent raiders from joining your server. You can disable CAPTCHA at any time.

Left: Set up to receive alerts when a possible join-raid has been detected in your server.

Right: What an alert looks like in a text channel

We’re gradually rolling out Raid Protection alerts to community servers! At this time, availability may be limited.
  1. Set a Verification Level.

Go to Server Settings > Safety Setup > Verification Level

To prevent raids on your Discord server, you can set a Verification Level in the Server Settings. Verification Levels require users to verify their email address or phone number before sending messages, which can help prevent bots and spam accounts from joining your server. We recommend setting the Verification Level to “Low” for basic security on public servers.

  1. Set your Explicit Media Content Filter to Medium or High.

Go to Server Settings > Safety Setup > Explicit Media Content Filter

Raiders may often try to raid your server and post explicit content to shock, harass, or spur your members to leave. Enable this filter to automatically scan and block explicit media from being posted in your server. Community-enabled servers have the High Explicit Media Content filter on by default.

  1. Find and recruit moderators. It’s always useful to have a moderator you trust online to immediately prevent or de-escalate a raid should one occur. Our Identifying and Assigning Moderators article covers best practices you should know on finding and recruiting moderators.
Being raided? Here are ways to de-escalate the raid:
  1. Pause invitations to your server.

Go to Server Settings > Invites > Pause Invites

Prevent incoming raiders from joining your server through your invite links for as long as needed by pausing your invite links. Pausing invites to your server is a great means of crowd control if your server is being raided so you can tend to your server and de-escalate a raid without having to resort to drastic measures like deleting your invite links. You can unpause at any time.

  1. Enable Slowmode.

Right-click a channel or press the cog wheel next to the channel name > Edit Channel > Overview > Slowmode

If raiders have made their way in and are spamming large volumes of messages, turn on Slowmode to limit the number of messages they’re able to send in a channel based on a timed cooldown. This will help you reduce the chaos and make it easier for you to weed out bad actors.

  1. Adjust your AutoMod rules as needed.

Go to Server Settings > AutoMod

During a raid, it’s important to identify the raiders, prevent them from posting in your server, and remove them as soon as possible.

If your server is being raided, consider fine-tuning your AutoMod rules as such:

  • Add words or phrases you see raiders spamming to one of your Custom Rules, and turn on the “Block Message” response to prevent raiders’ messages from being posted.
  • Identify raiders and remove them by turning on “Send alerts” to receive alerts containing who-what-where information on raiders.
  • Enable the “Timeout member” response to temporarily disable a raider’s ability to send messages or join voice channels.
  • Depending on what raiders are doing, consider enabling the “Block Message,” “Send alerts” and “Timeout member” responses across all of your other AutoMod rules.
  • Adjust your “Block Mention Spam” filter - Set a lower, more restrictive mention limit if raiders are spamming mentions in your server. Note that your mention limit means that members can’t exceed that number of unique mentions per individual message.
  1. Increase your Verification to High or Highest.

Go to Server Settings > Safety Setup > Verification Level

To strengthen the security of your Discord server during a raid, you can increase the Verification Level in the Server Settings.

Higher Verification Levels require users to verify their email address, phone number, and/or have been a member of the server for a certain amount of time before they can interact in the server. This can give you time to focus on de-escalating the raid without worrying about incoming raiders. Once the raid has been stopped, you can return your Verification Level to its prior settings.

  1. Report the raid to Discord.

Click on your server name to open the server dropdown menu > Report Raid

Be our partner-in-crime (or against crime…?) in combating raids by reporting them directly to us from your server dropdown menu. If your Community is being raided, you can help us in our moderation efforts by reporting the situation as we’ll be regularly reviewing your raid reports to develop tooling designed to prevent future raids.

To use Report Raid, you must have “Ban Members” or “Kick Members” permissions. Only accessible on the Desktop client and in Community servers.

Safer Messaging on Discord

We know it’s important for users to understand what controls they have over their experience on Discord and how to be safer. Part of delivering a better, safer experience is making sure people don’t see content they don’t want to – whether that’s intrusive spam or unwanted explicit images. This article covers direct message filters, which can help reduce the amount of unwanted content you see on Discord and promote a safer environment for you.

What this article covers:

  • For Individuals
  • Sensitive Content Filters
  • DM Spam Filter
  • For Server Owners
For Individuals

You can control these settings by going into User Settings and selecting the Content & Social tab. You can learn more about sensitive content filters here.

Sensitive Content Filters

Discord works to detect if media posted on our platform may be sensitive. When these new filters are set to blur, they apply to all historic and new media. Navigate to User Settings > Content & Social to adjust your Sensitive content filter settings.

Sensitive Media settings in Content & Social
DM Spam Filter

Automatically send direct messages that may contain spam into a separate spam inbox by navigating to User Settings > Content & Social to find your Direct Message spam settings.

Direct Message spam settings in Content & Social

These filters are customizable and you can choose to turn them off. By default, these filters are set to Filter direct messages from non-friends. Choose Filter all direct messages if you want all direct messages that you receive to be filtered, or select Do not filter direct messages to turn these filters off.

For Server Owners

With the explicit image filter, you can automatically block messages in your server that may contain explicit images in channels that are not marked as Age-restricted.

You have the ability to manage this feature and determine whether it should apply to all members within the server or only to those who do not have assigned roles. Additionally, if this feature is not desired, it can be disabled entirely.

You can access this setting by navigating to Server Settings, and under Moderation, select Safety Setup, and then find the Explicit image filter section.

Explicit image filter settings in Server Settings

Age-restricted channels are exempt from the explicit image filter. Turning this filter on allows your server members to share content while reducing the risk of explicit images being posted in channels that are not age-restricted.

Stage Channel Guidelines

Stages are a new way to connect you and your community to the things that everyone is passionate about in a more personal way — whether it be a specific video game, an artist, a hobby, or topics like if Yoda really knew about Order 66 beforehand. We want to expand these opportunities to allow our communities to let new users find these spaces, which means we’re here to help provide some guidance into some of the best ways to use these spaces and what is not allowed.

Note to Server Owners and Moderators

Since Stages will be spaces that exist within your server, server owners and stage moderators are responsible and accountable for the Stages being held. We empower and equip our communities to have the tools to help them properly ensure that these spaces are not engaging in any violations and are kept safe and welcoming. Stages are extensions of your server and activity that happens within them will be representative of your server. You’ll have the ability to make your stage available only to members of your server or open to anyone on Discord. Public Stages have some different features and must follow additional requirements as described below.

Stage Guidelines:
  1. Abide by the Community Guidelines and Terms of Service. This means that issues reported to your server should be addressed by your moderators and admins. Your moderator team should know when to escalate issues to Trust & Safety. Servers that violate Discord’s Community Guidelines and Terms of Service will be subject to further action from our Trust & Safety Team.
  • We want Discord to be a safe, positive, and inclusive experience. Our Trust & Safety team will investigate Stages that are reported to us or that we proactively identify as likely in violation of our policies, and Trust & Safety team members may temporarily join a live Stage to investigate potential violations.

  1. Respect people’s intellectual property and other rights. Only incorporate content that you own or have a license to use. Do not invade anyone’s privacy, libel them, or otherwise violate their rights.

    • Discord does not currently provide a recording or transcript feature. If you choose to use third-party tools to record or transcribe your event, you must make sure that you are following relevant laws, including getting consent from speakers and audience members if needed.

  2. Foster a healthy and positive environment. People should feel welcome in your Stage. Create environments where people want to spend time with each other, share interests, participate in community events, and build friendships. Do not cultivate general toxic behavior, harassment of others, or other derogatory content.

  3. Have a moderator team. Moderators can help ensure nothing rule-breaking is happening during your Stage events and can find meaningful ways for your members to engage. Build a moderator team that members of your community can trust and turn to for help. Note: Moderators will help facilitate your conversations in your Stage and should help enforce your server-specific rules as well!

  4. Have a topic and description that accurately describes the Stage that is free of profanity. Help potential members understand why they want to join the Stage. The Stage title and description should accurately reflect the nature of the event, and not mislead users about who will be speaking or what will be discussed.

  5. Do not host explicit, graphic, or sexual content. Explicit and age-restricted content is not allowed in Stages. Stages should be appropriate for audiences of all ages 13+.

  6. Public Stages: Be mindful anyone can join your server while your public Stage is live. Though these Stages are extensions of your community, when you opt-in to make your Stage public, you are also temporarily making your server public while the event is live. This means that you should make sure that any and all sensitive channels are marked private and have the appropriate roles and permissions set up.

What are Age-Restricted Servers on Discord?

Discord’s age-restricted server designation helps ensure that communities centered around adult content remain accessible only to users aged 18+, as indicated in our Community Guidelines. Servers can either be self-designated as 18+ by their owners or classified as age-restricted by Discord when they focus primarily on mature themes or content.

What this article covers:

  • What is classified as an age-restricted server?
    • What does this mean for age-restricted server members?
    • What about age-restricted Channels?
  • How Do I Mark My Server as Age-Restricted?
    • On Desktop/Browser
    • On Mobile
  • Appealing an Age-restricted Server Designation
  • Updating User’s Age Information Want to learn more?

Check out our support article here to learn more about how to access age-restricted servers.

What is classified as an age-restricted server?

Servers must be classified as age-restricted if the community is organized around age-restricted themes or if the majority of the server’s content is focused on 18+ content.

Discord will mark servers meeting these criteria as age-restricted if they are not appropriately designated. We will notify server owners letting them know if their server has been impacted through a system message.

Note: Server owners or admins with the Manage Server permission who are 18+ can mark their server as age-restricted.

What does this mean for age-restricted server members?

Users between the ages of 13 and 17 will not be able to join or view the content in age-restricted servers.

Important: Users in regions with regional restrictions may have to complete age assurance in order to view or enter servers marked as age-restricted by their server owner. Please refer to the article below that corresponds to your region for further details.

  • United Kingdom
  • Australia
  • Brazil Users aged 18+ that are attempting to join or access new age-restricted servers on iOS will be required to opt-in to viewing age-restricted content on desktop before being allowed into these spaces.

Additionally, a subset of age-restricted servers that are specifically focused on explicit pornographic content will be blocked entirely on iOS. iOS users aged 18+ will only be able to join and access these dedicated pornography servers on the desktop and web versions of Discord.

Learn more about accessing age-restricted servers here.

What about age-restricted Channels?

All Discord server owners must still apply age-restricted gates to channels with mature content.

Having age-restricted channels in a server does not, however, automatically mean that an entire server should be designated age-restricted. An age-restricted designation is only necessary if the majority of the server’s content is focused on 18+ content.

Note: Users who have not confirmed their age need to complete age assurance in order to view or enter channels marked as age-restricted.

How Do I Mark My Server as Age-Restricted?

Note: Server owners or admins with the Manage Server permission who are 18+ can mark a server as age-restricted.

On Desktop/Browser

In your Server Settings > Access, you will find a setting called Age-Restricted Server that can be enabled. You can toggle this on or off at any time.

Age-Restricted Server Setting on Desktop
On Mobile

In Server Settings > Moderation, you will find the Age-Restricted Server setting that can be enabled. You can toggle this on or off at any time.

Age-Restricted Server Setting on Mobile
Appealing an Age-restricted Server Designation

Owners of communities designated age-restricted by Discord will have to submit an appeal if they wish to have the age-restricted server-level designation removed.

Server owners can write in to Trust & Safety’s support queue here:

  • Select NSFW Server Owner Appeals
  • Enter the required details of the server Server owners should provide their server’s ID as well as an explanation why their community should be considered safe-for-work (SFW). We cannot accept server-level appeals from anyone besides the server owner. Communities determined to be SFW will have the age-restricted designation removed — at which time users between the ages of 13 and 17 will be allowed to rejoin.
Updating User’s Age Information

Note for users in regions where age assurance is required: You will have to age assure into the adult age group in order to join age-restricted servers.

If you are over the age of 18 and have been locked out of an age-restricted channel, or are unable to use age-restricted commands in DMs, you can appeal by following the instructions in this Help Center article.

Why is Discord asking for my birthday?

You must be over a minimum age to use Discord or access certain features or content. The minimum age requirements are different in different countries: you must be at least 13 to use Discord, but in some countries you may need to be as old as 16. We require you to confirm their age group to satisfy that minimum age requirement for your region.

If you satisfy the minimum age requirement and are old enough to use Discord, we use your age group (adult or teen) to determine if you can access content and settings meant for adults.

For the full breakdown of what the teen experience is on Discord, see here.

If we learn you may not be old enough to use Discord, your account will be permanently suspended. If you are old enough to use Discord, you can find more about how to appeal and confirm your age group here.

10 Days of Discord: Limited-Time Winter Collection

Celebrate the season with our Shop exclusive winter collection! From December 1, 2025 (9AM PT) to December 11, 2025 (9AM PT), collect four festive decorations at discounted prices and unlock an exclusive gift!

What this article covers:

  • What is 10 Days of Discord?
  • How to Access 10 Days of Discord
  • How to Unlock the Exclusive Gift
    • Collecting Winter Shop Items
    • Claiming Your Exclusive Gift
  • Managing Your Winter Collection
    • Using Your Decorations
  • Frequently Asked Questions
What is 10 Days of Discord?

Note: This limited-time collection is currently available to purchase on the Discord desktop/browser. Items you purchase or claim will be visible and usable across all platforms.

10 Days of Discord is a special Shop event where you can collect winter-themed profile decorations at our lowest holiday prices. Here’s what makes it special:

  • Four collectible items available at discounted prices
  • One exclusive gift unlocked when you complete your collection
  • Available for 11 days only – December 1-11, 2025 Collect all of the winter-themed collectibles and you’ll earn an exclusive gift!
How to Access 10 Days of Discord

Note: This winter collection is currently only available to purchase on Discord desktop/browser (not mobile).

  1. Open the Discord desktop app.

  2. Navigate to the Shop. You can access the Shop in two ways:

    1. From Direct Messages List: Select the Discord app icon [] in the upper-left corner, then select the Shop tab.
    1. From User Settings: Select the cogwheel icon [] in the lower-left corner > select Edit Profiles > select the Shop banner or any Shop icon in your profile customization options
Shop tab under Direct Messages List
  1. In the Shop, you can search for the winter collection. The featured winter items should be displayed at the top of the main Shop page, including a locked item marked as “Exclusive Gift”.
10 Days of Discord in the Shop
How to Unlock the Exclusive Gift
Collecting the Winter Shop Items

  1. Browse the four available winter decorations in 10 Days of Discord. Each item features a festive winter theme and is available at a special discounted price.

  2. Purchase items individually. Select any winter decoration to view details and purchase. You can buy them in any order.

  3. Track your progress as you collect items. You’ll see your progress indicator update (0/4 → 1/4 → 2/4 → 3/4 → 4/4).

Progress for your Exclusive Gift
Claiming Your Exclusive Gift

Once you’ve purchased all four winter items:

  1. When you return to the Shop, you’ll see the locked item is now revealed.

  2. Claim your exclusive gift by selecting Claim Gift to add it to your collection at no additional cost.

Claim Gift button
  1. All five items will appear in your profile customization options in the Profile tab and can be used immediately.
Managing Your Winter Collection
Using Your Decorations

After purchasing or claiming items:

  1. Navigate to User Settings by selecting the cogwheel icon [].

  2. Select Edit Profiles and choose which profile customization you’d like to apply (e.g. Avatar Decorations, Profile Effects, or Nameplates).

Edit Profiles button
Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why can’t I see this collection to purchase on mobile?

A: The 10 Days of Discord is currently available on Discord through desktop/browser only. However, items you purchase or claim on desktop will be visible and usable across all platforms (mobile, desktop, and web) even after the campaign ends.

Q: How long is this collection available?

A: The winter collection runs from December 1-11, 2025. After December 11, 2025 (9AM PT), these items will no longer be available for purchase.

Q: Do I need to buy all items at once?

A: No! You can purchase the winter decorations at your own pace during the 10-day campaign window. Buy them individually whenever you’re ready, and your progress will be saved.

Note: You must purchase all four winter items by December 11, 2025 (9AM PT) to unlock the exclusive item.

Q: I purchased all four items but didn’t see the exclusive item. What should I do?

A: The exclusive gift must be claimed after your fourth purchase between December 1, 2025 - December 11, 2025 (9AM PT). If you did not claim the item during this timeframe, it will no longer be available. If you run into any issues claiming your exclusive item, please reach out to Discord Support.

Q: Can I refund an item after I’ve unlocked the exclusive gift?

A: All Shop purchases are final and cannot be refunded. Please review items carefully before completing your purchase. For more information, review our Refund Policy.

Q: What happens to my items after December 11, 2025?

A: Any items you’ve purchased or claimed will remain in yours to keep. You can continue using them across all platforms even after the campaign ends. Only the ability to purchase new items from this collection ends on December 11, 2025 (9:00AM PT).

Q: What happens if I don’t claim my gift after purchasing all 4 items?

A: Once the collection is completed by December 11, 2025 (9:00AM PT), you can no longer claim the exclusive gift if you did not claim it before this period.

Q: If someone buys an item for me as a gift, who gets credit toward claiming the exclusive item?

A: The person who receives the items will be the one who gets credit toward the exclusive gift. If someone purchases an item for you, it counts toward your progress, not theirs.

What are Discord Orbs?

By using Discord Orbs, you agree to the Discord Orbs Terms in our Paid Services Terms.

Discord Orbs are rewards you earn by completing Quests. Orbs can also be earned through select promotions on Discord. You can use them in the Orbs Shop to get Nitro credits, items from the main collections, and more. It’s an easy way to unlock Discord upgrades, no payment method required.

How do I earn Discord Orbs?

Note: Orbs can also be earned through select promotions on Discord, separate from Quests. Check individual promotion details for eligibility.

Desktop/Browser
  1. To start earning Orbs, accept a Quest that offers them as a reward. You can do this in several ways on the desktop app and browser client:
  • Through the Quest Bar
    • You will occasionally see the Quest bar pop up in the bottom-left of the app when you’re eligible for a Quest. Hover over it to learn more about the Quest details and get started.
Quest Bar in Discord Desktop App
  • Through Quest Home (Discover > Quests)
Navigating to Quest Home through Discover Tab
  1. Complete the Quest and claim your Orbs reward.
Example of Claiming Discord Orbs from a Quest
  1. You can check your Orbs balance in the top-right corner of Quest Home and Shop.
Orbs Balance
Mobile
  1. On mobile, accept a Quest that offers Orbs as a reward. You can find eligible Quests by tapping your avatar > Settings > Quests, or by tapping your avatar > Orbs Balance.
Navigating to Settings > Quest Home (Left) or Tap Orbs Balance in Your Profile (Right) to find Quests
  1. Complete the Quest and claim your Orbs reward.
Example of Claiming Discord Orbs from a Quest
Discord Orbs Multiplier for Nitro Members

For eligible Nitro subscribers, you can claim bonus Orbs through Quests! When you complete a Quest with Orb rewards as a Nitro subscriber, your Orb rewards have a 1.2x multiplier applied. The Orbs Multiplier perk is currently available for Quests starting May 8, 2026 that have Orbs as the reward.

Discord Orbs Multiplier detail in a Discord Quest with Orbs rewards

Eligibility Requirements:

  • This perk is available to Nitro subscribers, including those on trial or gifted Nitro subscriptions.
  • This perk is not available to Nitro subscribers through Nitro Credits or Nitro Basic. Note: Nitro subscribers now receive 250 Discord Orbs on a monthly basis just for maintaining their subscription. Learn more in our Monthly Orbs Drop for Nitro Members FAQ article.
Earning Orbs Through Orb Challenges

Important: Orb Challenges are currently an experiment on desktop and browser, and are not widely available at this time.

Orb Challenges give you another way to earn Orbs beyond completing Quests. Each Orb Challenge rewards you with Orbs for taking a specific action on Discord. New Orb Challenges may be added over time, and each one shows what you need to do to complete it.

You can view and track your Orb Challenges from three places on desktop or browser:

  • Quest Home
Orb Challenges in Quest Home
  • The Shop
Orb Challenges in the Shop
  • Your Profile: select your avatar, then hover over or select the Orbs menu item in the account pop-out
Orbs Menu Item in the Account Pop-out

Eligibility Requirements:

  • Each Orb Challenge shows what you need to do to complete it and how many Orbs you’ll earn.
  • Available Orb Challenges may vary between users and can change over time.
  • Some Orb Challenges are only available for a limited time, and some can only be completed once.
  • Purchases made with Orbs don’t count toward Orb Challenges that involve a purchase. Only purchases made with a payment method are eligible.
Spending Your Discord Orbs
Where can I spend Orbs?

Head to the Shop tab to begin spending your Discord Orbs!

Desktop/Browser

  1. Navigate to your Direct Messages list by selecting the Discord app icon in the upper-left corner.
Discord App Icon
  1. Then, press the Shop tab [] to the right of your server list to enter the Shop.
Shop Tab
  1. In the Shop, select the Orbs Shop tab at the top to view Orbs-exclusive items.
Orbs Shop Tab in the Shop

Mobile

  1. On mobile, tap your avatar to navigate to your Profile.

  2. Tap the Shop icon [] in the upper-right corner.

  3. In the Shop, tap the Shop Menu icon [] in the upper-right corner, then select Orbs Exclusives.

Navigate to the Shop to Find Orb Exclusive Items
What can I buy with Orbs?

Here’s what you can purchase with Orbs in the Shop:

  • Shop items from the Orbs Shop

  • Orbs-exclusives: Nitro credits, a profile badge, special Avatar Decoration, and special Profile Effect.

  • Orbs redeemable items: Select popular items redeemable with Orbs You cannot purchase these items with Orbs:

  • Gifts

  • Partner-branded Shop items

  • Recurring Nitro or Boosting subscriptions Nitro credits are considered an Orbs-exclusive item within the Orbs Shop. However, you can also earn them occasionally by completing specific Quests.

How to Spend Orbs

Desktop/Browser

  1. On desktop or browser, browse Orbs-redeemable items in the Orbs Shop tab of the Shop, or check the Shop All tab to see the full collection of items that can be claimed with Orbs.

Note: If you don’t see an Orbs price on an item, it means it’s not eligible to be claimed with Orbs.

  1. Each item will display whether you can claim with Orbs or spend money to make your purchase. Select an item to view both pricing options.

For eligible items, the Shop automatically displays the Orbs price if you have enough Orbs. If you don’t have enough Orbs for an item, the regular monetary price will be displayed instead.

  1. To make a purchase, select your desired item and press Claim in the Shop window.

Important: Discord Orb purchases are final and cannot be refunded.

Orbs Shop Items

Tip: To switch from Orbs to regular payment during purchase confirmation, exit and select the Buy button instead.

Buy Option in Shop Window

Mobile

  1. To browse Orb Exclusive items on mobile, tap the Shop Menu icon [] in the upper-right corner of the Shop page, then select Orbs Exclusives.

  2. To make a purchase using your Orbs, select the item, tap Redeem, then tap Redeem using Orbs to confirm.

Purchasing an Orbs Exclusive Shop Item on Mobile
Important Discord Orbs Information
  • Switch between earning and spending Orbs by selecting the buttons in the Shop banner (Orbs Shop tab, Quest Home, or through your Orbs balance).
  • Orbs can only be used within Discord–they cannot be converted to real money.
  • Earned Orbs do not expire once earned, and they remain in your account until you spend them.
  • Orbs are attached to your account and cannot be shared or transferred between users.
Frequently Asked Questions

This FAQ is divided into sections:

  • General Orbs Information
  • Earning and Obtaining Orbs
  • Spending Orbs
  • Sharing and Transferring Orbs
  • Support and Issues
General Orbs Information

Q: Will my Orbs expire?

A: Your Orbs stay in your account until you decide to spend them. However, as we continue monitoring how users earn and spend Orbs we might make future adjustments to keep the experience balanced for everyone. Additionally, keep in mind that if you lose access to your Discord account for any reason, including violating our Terms of Service or Community Guidelines, you may lose access to any Orbs associated with that account.

Q: What happens to my Orbs if my account is compromised or banned?

A: If you lose access to your Discord account for any reason, including violating our Terms of Service or Community Guidelines, you may lose access to any Orbs associated with that account. For cases involving compromised accounts or fraudulent purchases, please contact our support team for assistance.

Earning and Obtaining Orbs

Q: Can I buy or gift Orbs to someone?

A: No, you cannot gift or buy Orbs.

Q: Is there any other way to obtain Orbs? Can I only earn Orbs from Quests?

A: Orbs are primarily earned through Quests, with additional opportunities available through select promotional offers, subject to eligibility.

Q: What should I do if I see someone selling Orbs?

A: Please report any attempts to sell or trade Orbs, as this violates the Discord Orbs Terms and may result in account penalties.

Q: Why am I seeing more Orbs in my account than expected?

A: Some users who link their Discord and Riot Games (VALORANT or League of Legends) accounts or their Battle.net accounts may receive an Orbs reward. If you recently connected these accounts, that’s likely the reason for the change.

Q: What are Orb Challenges?

A: Orb Challenges are a way to earn Orbs for completing specific actions on Discord, separate from Quests. You can view and track your Orb Challenges from Quest Home, the Shop, or your profile on desktop or browser.

Spending Orbs

Q: I noticed I can’t buy a specific Shop item. Why not?

A: You can spend Orbs on most Shop items, including items in the Orbs Shop. Items redeemable with Orbs will display Orbs amount

Q: Can I refund something I claimed in the Shop with Orbs?

A: Any items you claim in the Shop with Orbs are not refundable.

Q: If I claim Nitro credits using Orbs, will it apply to my account right away?

A: It depends on if you have an active subscription. See our Help Center article for more information on how Nitro credits work.

Sharing and Transferring Orbs

Q: Can I share or trade my Orbs with friends?

A: No, Orbs are tied to your personal Discord account and cannot be transferred between users.

Q: Can I exchange my Orbs for real money or transfer them to other platforms?

A: No, you cannot convert Orbs to real money or transfer them to other platforms.

Q: What happens to my Orbs if I change accounts?

A: Orbs remain tied to the original account where they were earned. They cannot be transferred between accounts, even if both accounts belong to you.

Support and Issues

Q: I’m experiencing issues with Discord Orbs. What should I do?

A: Contact Discord Support directly for assistance with any Orbs-related concerns.

Emoji Confetti FAQ

Want to make a Discord message stand out? Emoji Confetti lets you add pizzazz to any message! Sharing your epic gaming moments or posting server announcements is going to be a lot more fun and memorable.

What this article covers:

  • What is Emoji Confetti?
  • Why and When should I use Emoji Confetti?
  • How do I apply Emoji Confetti to a message?
  • Frequently Asked Questions
What is Emoji Confetti?

Emoji Confetti is an experimental feature currently available to select desktop users.

Emoji Confetti adds eye-catching flair to your Discord messages. Pick an emoji and watch it burst as confetti on any message—yours or someone else’s—to make it stand out with personality and pizzazz.

Example of Emoji Confetti
Why and When should I use Emoji Confetti?

Emoji Confetti turns ordinary messages into extraordinary ones, going beyond standard emoji reactions to create more fun moments and interactions in your conversations.

Here are moments where adding Emoji Confetti to a message can be a game-changer:

  • Celebrations: If someone posted a message of a gaming milestone or accomplishing a personal goal, shower that message with emoji confetti!
  • Special Announcements: Make important messages stand out in busy conversations or dedicated announcement channels.
  • Spreading Joy & Appreciation: Add confetti to messages to brighten someone’s day or show your appreciation.
  • Just for Fun: Sometimes a conversation needs that extra touch of magic - no special occasion required!
How do I apply Emoji Confetti to a message?
  1. To apply Emoji Confetti to a message, select the Add Emoji Confetti icon [] when hovering over a posted message or in the lower-right corner of the text box while typing.
Add Emoji Confetti Icon While Hovering a Message or in Text Chat

NOTE: As part of this experiment, start your Emoji Confetti fun with 2 free Emoji Confetti!

  1. To add Emoji Confetti when typing a message, press the emoji icon [] in the Select an emoji to apply to your message banner located above the text box. Then, choose an emoji from the emoji picker.
Selecting the Emoji Icon in the Banner Above the Text Box

For a posted message, pick an emoji using the Pick Emoji box. Then, choose an emoji from the emoji picker.

Selecting the Pick Emoji Box to and Choosing an Emoji from the Picker
  1. Once you’ve sent your message or applied confetti to an existing message, you’re all set! Hover over the emoji on a message with Emoji Confetti applied to cause an explosion of confetti!
Hovering over Messages with Emoji Confetti

Ready for even more fun? Get a pack of 5 additional Emoji Confetti for $0.99. To purchase more, simply open the Emoji Confetti menu by selecting the Add Emoji Confetti icon [] and press Get 5 more for $0.99.

Get 5 more for $0.99 Button in Emoji Confetti Menu
Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What platforms is Emoji Confetti available on?

A: Currently, Emoji Confetti can only be applied to messages on desktop devices.

Q: Is there a way to disable the Emoji Confetti explosion?

A: The confetti explosion is an opt-in effect that you can choose to trigger. You can disable the Emoji Confetti effect and reduce motion across the app by going to your User Settings > Accessibility > toggle Enable Reduced Motion. You can learn more about reduced motion here.

Q: What’s your refund policy for Emoji Confetti?

A: Emoji Confetti is non-refundable—we cannot provide refunds after purchase or use.

Q: Can I see who applied Emoji Confetti to a message?

A: Yes—simply hover your cursor over the CONFETTI badge on a message to see who applied it.

Example of CONFETTI Badge

Q: Can everyone in the server see Emoji Confetti on a message?

A: Yes, everyone in the server can see Emoji Confetti on a message and trigger the effect. However, Emoji Confetti that you trigger will only appear for you.

Q: Can I remove or change Emoji Confetti after applying it?

A: No, once you’ve applied Emoji Confetti to a message, it cannot be removed or modified.

Q: What happens to Emoji Confetti after the experiment ends?

A: As an experimental feature, Emoji Confetti on messages and any remaining in your inventory may expire in the future.

Game Shops FAQ

Buy, gift, and wishlist in-game items for your favorite games directly on Discord. Browse items in the Discord Shop or in a game’s official server, gift items to friends in just a few steps, and add items to your Wishlist so friends know exactly what to get you. This article covers everything you need to know about how it all works.

What this article covers:

  • What Are Game Shops?
  • Where To Find In-Game Items On Discord
    • Through the Discord Shop
    • Through a Game’s Official Server
  • How to Purchase Items
  • Gifting Items

What Are Game Shops?

Game Shops let you browse, purchase, and gift in-game items directly on Discord. You can find in-game items through the Discord Shop or in a game’s official Discord server, and you can gift items to friends from places you’re already hanging out, like DMs and voice channels.

Games currently available on Discord:

  • Marvel Rivals: Marvel Rivals Shop
  • Rust: Rust Shop
  • Bloons TD 6: Ninja Kiwi Game Shop
Where To Find In-Game Items On Discord

Note: Game Shops are currently available on the Discord desktop app and browser. Mobile users may encounter Game Shop embeds or item listings that are available for purchase, but the full Game Shop experience is only available on desktop and browser. Platform support for item redemption varies by game, so check the FAQ section for your specific game below for details.

There are two ways to find in-game items on Discord:

Through the Discord Shop

  1. Navigate to the Discord Shop by selecting the Shop tab to the right of your server list.

  2. Select Game Shops at the top of the Shop.

  3. Browse available games and select a game to see its items.

Game Shops tab in the Discord Shop
Through a Game’s Official Server

  1. Visit the game’s official Discord server.

  2. Select the Game Shop tab towards the top of the server’s channel list.

  3. You can now browse all available items in the Game Shop.

Game Shop (Example: Marvel Rivals)
How To Purchase Items

Note: The items available in each Game Shop will refresh periodically, so check back to see what’s new.

  1. Find the item you’d like to purchase, either through the Discord Shop or in the game’s official server.

  2. Select the item and review details including the price and preview.

Item detail view in a Game Shop

  1. Select Buy Now and follow the prompts to complete your purchase.

  2. When you buy an item, it’s delivered straight to your in-game inventory. If you’ve already linked your game account to Discord, you’re all set. If not, you’ll see a prompt to link your account. Press the Link Account button.

Link Account button

Want to learn more?

For more information on linking your game account to Discord, check out this Help Center article.

  1. Follow the prompts to fully link your account. Once linked, your item will be delivered to your game account!
Launch game
Gifting Items

Want to surprise a friend with an in-game item? You can gift items directly from any Game Shop on Discord.

  1. Browse a Game Shop and select an item you’d like to gift.

  2. Select the Gift Item button.

  3. You can personalize your gift with a custom message.

  4. Once you’re ready, complete your purchase by following the prompts and send your gift.

Gifting a Marvel Rivals Shop item
  1. The recipient will receive the gift in their DMs. Before claiming the gift, they should make sure their game account is linked to their Discord account. After linking, they can claim their gift by selecting Open Gift.
Open Gift button
Other Ways To Gift

Gifting is woven throughout Discord, so you don’t always have to go to a Game Shop to give a friend something. Here are some other ways to gift in-game items:

  • From a friend’s Wishlist: Open the Wishlist tab on anyone’s Discord profile to see which Game Shop items they’ve been eyeing, and send them a gift right from there.
  • From DMs: Use the gift icon in a DM to send a friend an in-game item.
  • From a link in chat: If someone drops a link to an in-game item in chat, you can gift that item straight from the link.
  • From voice channels: While streaming a game that has a Game Shop in a voice channel, you can gift items to friends right from there.
Frequently Asked Questions

  • Purchases and Refunds
  • Pricing
