Purchases and Refunds

Q: Can I refund a Game Shop purchase?

A: Generally, purchases in Game Shops are non-refundable. However, if you’re unable to claim the in-game item on a supported platform, and you attempt to claim the item within the 14-day claim period, you can reach out to Discord support to request a refund: dis.gd.

Check the game-specific sections below for which platforms are supported.

Q: How do I see what items I’ve purchased?

A: You can see any purchases on your Billing tab in settings in the ‘Transaction History’ section.

Q: What happens if I receive a gift of an item I already own in the game?

A: If you attempt to claim a gifted item that you already own in-game, the gift sender will be refunded. Note that gift receivers must attempt to claim items within 14 days to ensure Discord can issue any eligible refunds.

Q: Why do I see “You already own this item or it’s not supported on your platform”?

A: This message appears when you already own the item, your linked game account is on an unsupported platform, or you own an item that’s included in a bundle you’re trying to purchase. If you already own the item, you’ll only be able to purchase it as a gift for someone else.

“You already own this item or it’s not supported on your platform” message

Q: Can I use a Discord gift card to purchase items in Game Shops?

A: Yes! You can use your Discord gift card balance to purchase items in Game Shops. Learn more about gift cards, or redeem a gift card here.

Pricing

Q: What currency do Game Shops support?

A: Prices in Game Shops may be shown in your local currency where available. Otherwise, prices are shown in U.S. dollars (USD).

Gifting

Q: Can I gift items to someone who doesn’t play the game?

A: Yes, you can send a gift to any Discord user. The recipient will need to link their game account to their Discord account to claim the gift. If they don’t have a game account yet, they can create one and link it to Discord.

Q: How do I know what my friends want?

A: You can check a friend’s Wishlist on their Discord profile. Open the Wishlist tab to see which items they’ve saved, and gift them something right from there. You can also add items to your own Wishlist so friends know what to get you. Learn more in our Wishlist FAQ.

Account Linking

Q: Can I purchase from a Game Shop without linking my account?

A: Yes, you can purchase from the shop without linking your account, but you will need to link your account to claim the item. You can find the account linking entrance in Settings > Billing > navigate to the item you purchased > Connect Account.

Rust Players: If you made a purchase and didn’t get your item after linking, please launch Rust and re-link your Discord account from inside the game. You can do this by selecting ‘Social’ in the bottom right, then ‘Find your Friends on Discord’.

General

Q: Which games have Game Shops on Discord?

A: Game Shops are currently available for Marvel Rivals, Rust, and Bloons TD 6.

Q: Are Game Shops available on mobile?

A: Game Shops are currently available on the Discord desktop app and browser.

Marvel Rivals Game Shop

Q: Which platforms can I redeem Marvel Rivals Shop items on?

A: Currently supported on PC desktop platforms (Steam, Epic, Loading Bay) and Xbox. If your connected account is on PlayStation and therefore unable to receive the item, we may offer a refund, provided that you or the gift recipient attempted to claim the item within 14 days of purchase.

Q: Where can I find the Marvel Rivals Shop on Discord?

A: You can select this link to go directly to the Marvel Rivals Shop on Discord.

Q: I bought an item, but I can’t find it in my game.

A: Purchases are delivered to the game account linked to your Discord account. Try these in order:

  • Fully restart the game. New items sometimes won’t appear until the game reloads your inventory.
  • Check you’re playing on the linked account. If you have more than one game account, the item went to whichever one is connected to Discord.
  • Disconnect and reconnect your accounts. In Marvel Rivals, go to Settings and fully disconnect your Discord connection, then reconnect either from Marvel Rivals Settings or from Discord. Still missing? Please visit our Help Center article on how to submit a support ticket so our Discord Support team can investigate further.
Rust Game Shop

From October 22 (11:00 AM PT) through November 5 (11:00 AM PT), eligible Nitro subscribers can claim the exclusive Zombie Wumpus Plush in-game item in the Rust Game Shop on Discord using Discord Orbs. Nitro monthly and Nitro yearly subscriptions are eligible. Nitro Basic, trial subscriptions, and other subscription types are not eligible for this offer. Claiming with Orbs applies to self-purchases only and cannot be used for gifted items purchased for other users. All users, including Nitro subscribers, can also purchase the Zombie Wumpus Plush at its regular price in the Rust Game Shop, during the offer period.

For more information about Discord Orbs, including how to use and redeem them, please see the Discord Orbs FAQ. For details around eligibility, terms and policy please see the Discord Nitro Offers & Promotions: Eligibility Guide

Note: Users who subscribe to Nitro on mobile are still eligible for this offer. However, they must sign in on the Discord desktop or web app to claim the Zombie Wumpus Plush item in the Rust Game Shop.

Q: I’m having trouble linking my Rust account to receive my item. What should I do?

A: If you made a purchase and didn’t receive your item after linking, please launch Rust and re-link your Discord account from inside the game.

  1. Launch Rust

  2. Select Social in the bottom-right corner

  3. Select “Find your friends on Discord” and follow the prompts

This is the recommended linking method for Rust at this time.

Q: Which platforms can I redeem Rust Shop items on?

A: Currently supported on PC via Steam.

Q: What happens if I receive a Rust item but don’t own the game?

A: The item will be added to your Steam inventory and will be waiting for you when you purchase Rust. Once you own the game on that Steam account, the item will be available to use. The same applies if you gift a Rust item to a friend who doesn’t own the game yet.

Q: Where can I find the Rust Shop on Discord?

A: You can select this link to go directly to the Rust Shop on Discord.

Ninja Kiwi (Bloons TD 6) Game Shop

Q: Which platforms can I redeem Bloons TD6 Shop items on?

A: Currently supported on PC (via Steam, Epic Games Store and Microsoft Store), and mobile (iOS, Android, Epic iOS, Epic Android and Amazon). Items are tied to your linked Bloons TD 6 account rather than a specific device, so once your account is linked, your item should be available on all supported platforms.

Q: I’m having trouble linking my Bloons TD 6 account to receive my item. What should I do?

A: If you made a purchase and didn’t receive your item, re-linking your Bloons TD 6 and Discord accounts usually fixes it. You’ll need a Ninja Kiwi account (used for Bloons TD 6) to do this, so make sure you’re signed in before you start.

Start the same way on any device:

  1. Open Bloons TD 6 and go to Settings > Account > Discord. (Or find Discord under Sign in providers).

  2. Select Link Accounts.

What happens next depends on your platform.

In-game linking (PC or Mac):

  1. The Discord account-linking authorization modal will open.

  2. Select Authorize to confirm. You’re now linked.

Web-based linking (PC, Mac, or mobile):

  1. You’ll be taken to a web page to sign in to your Ninja Kiwi account. Choose one:
  • Sign in with Steam
  • Log in with your email and password
  • Use a linking code Then, scroll down and select Authorize to confirm.

Note: Account linking isn’t supported through Epic Games Store or Microsoft Store. Link your account in-game or on the web, and your purchased items will automatically sync.

Your accounts are now linked, and your item should appear.

Q: What happens if I receive a Bloons TD6 item but don’t own the game?

A: You’ll be taken to the account-linking page first, since you’ll need to link a Bloons TD 6 account before you can claim the item. If you don’t already have the game, download Bloons TD 6, create an account, and link it to Discord. Once that’s done, your item is ready to use.

Gifting works the same way. If a friend claims a gifted item without a linked account, they’ll be prompted to link one on that same page before the item lands.

Q: How does this work on mobile?

A: The same way as on PC. If you don’t have a linked account, you’ll be redirected to the account-linking page to log into your Bloons TD6 account. It doesn’t matter which platform you link from. Once linked, your item should be available on all supported platforms.

Gifting follows the same flow. Claim the gift, link your account if needed, then the item is yours.

Q: I’ve linked my account, but I’m still having trouble accessing my item in Bloons TD 6. What should I do?

A: If you’re still having trouble accessing your item after linking, please visit our Help Center article on how to submit a support ticket so our Discord Support team can investigate further.

Q: Where can I find the Bloons TD 6 Shop on Discord?

A: You can select this link to go directly to the Bloons TD 6 Game Shop.

What are nameplates?

Nameplates are unique designs that let you customize how your display name appears on Discord. While Avatar Decorations and Profile Effects let you personalize your profile, Nameplates let you add more flair to your name so it stands out with style in your DMs, group chats, and servers.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can everyone see my Nameplate or just me?

A: Everyone can see your Nameplate.

Q: Do Nitro subscribers get discounts on Nameplates?

A: Yes, Nitro subscribers receive discounts on all items in the Shop, including Nameplates.

Q: Are Nameplates available to purchase and edit on mobile?

A: Currently, you can only purchase and edit Nameplates on desktop. However, Nameplates are visible on both desktop and mobile devices.

Q: Can I get a refund for my Nameplate purchase?

A: While Nameplates are generally non-refundable, as stated in our Refund Policy, if you purchased one during our experimental phase (before April 21, 2025), you can submit a refund request to Discord support here by May 5th, 2025. Otherwise, all Nameplate purchases are final and non-refundable.

Q: Can I refund Nitro after buying a Nameplate?

A: No, if you’ve purchased a Nameplate within 5 days of starting or renewing your Nitro subscription, you will not be eligible to refund your Nitro subscription.

Q: Can Nameplates be turned off? I don’t want to see them.

A: Nameplates cannot be disabled, but you can go to User Settings > Accessibility > Enable Reduced Motion to minimize Nameplate animations and effects.

Q: I purchased and applied a Nameplate to my profile - but I don’t see it enabled or active?

A: Currently, Nameplates show when you are active on Discord—so make sure you are not in invisible mode or offline.

Q: Is localized pricing available for nameplates?

A: Localized pricing is available for some nameplate purchases and gifts. You should see at checkout whether localized pricing is available. Otherwise, the purchase will default to USD ($). You can learn more about localized pricing here.

Where do Profile Frames appear?

Profile Frames as seen in pop-out profile cards.

Profile Frames are built to look great across different platforms and profile layouts, but you may notice that a Frame looks slightly different depending on where it’s being viewed. Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Are Profile Frames available to everyone?

If you’re not a Nitro subscriber, you can still see Frames on other users’ profiles.

Want early access? Subscribe to Nitro to shop Profile Frames now.

Q: When can I buy Profile Frames with Orbs?

A: Profile Frames are not currently eligible for Orbs purchases. Orbs purchasing will be rolling out over the next 2 months.

In the meantime, Profile Frames can be purchased with USD and other supported currencies through the Shop.

Q: Can everyone see my Profile Frame or just me?

A: Everyone can see your Profile Frame.

Q: Do Nitro subscribers get discounts on Profile Frames?

A: Yes, Nitro subscribers get discounts across the Discord Shop, including on Profile Frames. Your discount is applied automatically at checkout—no code needed.

Q: Are Profile Frames available to purchase and edit on mobile?

A: Yes, Profile Frames can be purchased and edited on the Discord mobile app.

Q: Can I get a refund for my Profile Frame purchase?

A: Profile Frames are non-refundable, as stated in our Refund Policy.

Q: Can I refund Nitro after buying a Profile Frame?

A: No, if you’ve purchased a Profile Frame within 5 days of starting or renewing your Nitro subscription, you will not be eligible to refund your Nitro subscription.

Q: How do Profile Frames interact with Profile Effects?

A: Profile Effects are another type of Discord profile decoration that can be purchased in the Shop. While the Profile Frames wrap around your Discord profile, Profile Effects render on the profile itself.

Q: I purchased and applied a Profile Frame to my profile but I don’t see it.

A: Make sure your Discord app is updated to the latest version. If you can’t see it, go to your User Settings > Edit Profile to confirm the Profile Frame is selected. And if you still don’t see it, restart your app.

Q: Is localized pricing available for profile frames?

A: Localized pricing is available for some profile frame purchases and gifts. You should see at checkout whether localized pricing is available. Otherwise, the purchase will default to USD ($). You can learn more about localized pricing here.

Refunds and Account-related

Q: What is your refund policy for Shop purchases?

Q: What happens to my purchased items if my account is deleted?

A: Your use of Discord is subject to our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines, and access to any items purchased on Discord may be lost in the case of temporary or permanent account suspension or self-requested deletion. Additionally, you are responsible for maintaining the security of your account.

Pricing and Discounts

Q: How do I get a discount on items in the Shop?

Q: Is localized pricing available for Shop purchases?

Bundles and Items

Q: I already have the avatar decoration which is part of a Shop Bundle. Why am I unable to purchase the Shop Bundle to obtain the profile effect?

A: Shop Bundles allow you to buy two items from the same collection at a discounted price. These bundles are available only if you haven’t purchased any of the items included. Q: What if my friend sends me a gift from the Shop, but I already have the item in my collection?

A: Don’t worry, your friend will not be able to send an item that has already been claimed and added to your collection.

However, if a gifted item has not been claimed and added to your collection, it is possible that you may receive the same gifted item again. If this is the case, you can choose to claim one of the gifts. Activity Sharing on Discord FAQ

What this article covers:

  • What is Activity Sharing on Discord?
  • How to View Activity
    • Within User Profiles

    • As a Status Message
  • How do I control who sees my activity?
    • Activity Sharing for the Teen Age Group

    • Recent Activity History
    • Who Can Join My Game
  • How Activity Sharing Works with Profile Privacy Setting
What is Activity Sharing on Discord?

When you engage in certain detectable activities (like playing a game or listening to music), Discord can display information about those activities. This includes when and how you engaged, as well as information about the activity. Some examples of the types of activity we show:

  1. Detectable games you’re playing on a computer

  2. Games you’re playing on Xbox or Playstation

  3. Spotify

  4. Crunchyroll

  5. 1st and 3rd party Activities on Discord

  6. And more!

Games and activities that support Rich Presence will show even more cool stuff about what’s happening in the activity.

And some activities from other services like Spotify or Crunchyroll require you to connect your account to Discord. You can learn more about these through our connections article here.

Note: Game activity notifications are currently an experiment on the desktop app. To turn off these notifications, go to User Settings > Notifications and adjust your Game Activity Notifications settings. To stop sharing your game activities entirely, update your Activity Privacy settings instead. Learn more details on managing your activity settings here.

Example of Game Activity Notification
How to View Activity

Activity can be seen in multiple places within the Discord app.

Within User Profiles

When viewing your User Profile, you will be able to see your Recent Activity history within the last 30 days.

Recent Activity History on User Profile
On Global Activity Cards

You can also view activity cards by checking a user’s profile on mobile or in the Friends List on desktop. These cards display the recent activity of friends and people you interact with in your servers.

Activity Card in Friends List on Desktop (Top) & Activity Card on User Profile on Mobile (Bottom)

Note: Activity Cards may also appear in the server’s Members List during the Recent Activity experiment. You can learn more about this experiment here.

As a Status Message

While in a server, the activity may appear as a status in the Members list depending on your settings.

Activity Status in Members List on Desktop
How do I control who sees my activity?
Activity Sharing for the Teen Age Group

As part of our additional teen safety protections, we have standard activity sharing settings for users in the teen age group. You can change this setting at any time, you don’t have to be in the adult age group.

Users in the teen age group: Start with their activity sharing set to Friends & Small Servers. This means their full profile details will only be visible to their friends and members of any small servers (< 200 members) they join, not members of all shared servers.

Users in the adult age group or users who are unconfirmed: Start with their activity sharing set to Friends & All Servers everywhere.

Note: Teen safety protections may vary slightly depending on where you live, as some regions have specific requirements under local regulation. For region-specific information, see our directory here.

Note: You’re always in control. You can update your Activity Sharing setting whenever you like in User Settings > Activity Privacy > Where I Share Activity. You don’t have to be an adult to make a change.

Global Settings

In your global settings, you can control whether any activity of any kind is shown to others, regardless of whether they’re friends or not.

  1. Select the cogwheel [] next to your Discord username to access your User Settings.

  2. Then, select Activity Sharing where you will find your Activity settings.

  3. Here you can determine your activity sharing settings.

First, decide whether you’d like to share your activity with others:

  • Share my activity - This toggle controls whether or not others on Discord can see your activity sharing.
  1. You can also determine your Default Sharing settings to control who can see your game and app activity when you join a new server:
  • Automatically share my activity with
    • Friends & All Servers: Your activity is shared with friends and members of any server you join.
    • Friends & Small Servers Only: Your activity is shared with friends and members of any servers you join with 200 or fewer members.
    • Friends Only: Your activity is shared with your friends only.
  • My Servers - Further customize your activity sharing by enabling or disabling your activity sharing on a per-server basis. If your activity sharing is enabled in a server, the toggle next to the server will be ON. If disabled, the server will be toggled OFF.
“Share my activity toggle” in What Activity I Share

In certain countries and situations, this setting might be disabled by default for you. You can always change your settings by following the instructions above.

Per-server Control

Note: Sharing your activity is automatically enabled for servers you join. However, you can adjust this default setting for servers with over 200 members in your Global Settings menu.

If you want to control which servers can see your recent activity, you can disable or enable settings per server.

  1. Navigate to the server where you would like to enable or disable the Activity Status settings.

  2. Right-click the server’s name or select the dropdown menu.

  3. Then, select Privacy Settings. This will give you the option to toggle the Activity Status setting.

Activity Status Toggle in Privacy Settings within a Server

Note:

  • Members of a disabled server will still be able to see your activity if they’re also friends with you or if they share another server with you where your activity is allowed.
  • Although the Activity Status may be turned off for a specific server, you’ll still see the status on your end unless you have it fully disabled. Important: For the experiment that displays Activity Cards in a server’s Members List, the server-specific privacy settings will not affect the experiment at this time. The activity shown in that experiment features are controlled by global, connection, and game-level controls within Discord.
Connections Settings

For any connected accounts that support sharing recent activity or rich presence, you’ll see a toggle to share your activity with others in the Connections menu located within your User Settings > Connected Apps.

Activity Sharing Toggle in Connected Apps

You can enable or disable each individual connection, but activity will only be shared as long as the global settings are also on.

Game Detection

You can enable or disable individual games from being displayed as activity in the Registered Games menu located within your User Settings > under Games & Apps. Activity will be shared as long as the global setting is also on.

Registered Games in Games & Apps Settings
Recent Activity History

While viewing your User Profile, you can also clear your Game History to clear it from your activity history.

  1. Select your User Profile in the lower-left corner of the app to view your User Status menu.

  2. Select your profile avatar to view your full profile.

User Profile Showing Activity
  1. While here, press Activity within the profile categories.
Activity Tab in Full Profile

  1. This will bring you to your activity history where you can select the ellipsis [] to the right of the activity and press Clear Game History.

  2. Within Clear Game History press the Clear button in the lower-right corner to remove the activity from your history.

Clear Game History Option in Activity Menu (Top) & Clear Game History Confirmation (Bottom)
Who Can Join My Games

If you are sharing your activity and playing a game that supports rich presence, friends and other server members who are in the same voice channel as you can join the same game you’re playing. You have two options that you can enable:

Game Join Settings
  • Allow friends to join my game: This allows for your Discord friends to join the game you’re playing, which is being shared as your activity.
  • Allow voice channel participants to join my game: This allows for other server members who are in the same voice channel as you to join the game you’re playing, which is being shared as your activity. However, this feature is only available in non-Community servers. You can read more about how Game Invites work on Discord at this article.
How Activity Sharing Works With Profile Privacy Setting

Profile Privacy setting and Activity Sharing are separate settings, but they work together to give you consistent control over your visibility on Discord.

When you change your Profile Privacy setting, you’ll be prompted to update your Activity Sharing setting to match and vice versa. For example, if you set your Profile Privacy to Friends Only, Discord will ask if you’d like to restrict your Activity Sharing to friends only as well. You can choose to update both settings at once, or decline and manage them independently.

Changing Online Status

Sometimes, that homework assignment needs your full attention, or maybe you’re just casually hanging out chatting it up with friends. Luckily Discord has 4 separate online statuses that let you pick and choose how you appear to others and keep your focus intact in other places if you need it.

Manual Override

To change your status, it’s as simple as left-clicking your user avatar that you’ll find in the lower-left corner of the client:

You’ll see the status-picker menu pop up. You’ve got four options:

Business as usual. You’ll appear online with a green circle beside your avatar.

Normally, you’ll automatically switch to idle if you’re AFK for a certain amount of time, but you can manually select it in the pop-up menu. Unlike the auto-idle status, manually setting idle will allow you to stay that way indefinitely.

Setting yourself to Do Not Disturb (DnD) will show your avatar with a red circle and automatically mute any and all desktop notifications you’d normally receive.

Setting yourself as Invisible will make you appear offline entirely, but you’ll still be able to access all of Discord as normal. This includes messaging your friends without appearing online.

You also have the ability to create a custom status to let you personalize this status a bit further! Check out this guide for all you need to know about custom statuses.

What is a Custom Status?

Do you ever wish you could tell your Discord friends you’re busy battling dragons or waiting for your sourdough to rise? Custom status is a feature that lets your creativity rise higher than perfectly proofed bread dough. Share your mood, activity, or a witty one-liner, making your presence as unique as your secret family recipe.

Ready to spice up your Discord profile? Grab your favorite emoji (🍞 anyone?) and let’s dive in!

Setting a Custom Status
Desktop/Browser

  1. On the desktop or browser app, press your profile icon in the lower-left corner of the app to view your profile menu.

  2. Select the Add Status bubble to create a custom status.

Tip: Press the emoji icon to set an emoji to your custom status. With Discord Nitro or Nitro Basic, you can use custom server emojis too!

You can also manage when your custom status clears and what status you would like to set by selecting an option from the Clear After pull-down menu and Status pull-down menu.

  1. When your custom status is all set, press Save in the lower-right corner of the Set a custom status menu.

Note: Custom statuses expire after one day by default, but you can configure them to last for shorter or longer periods.

Mobile

  1. On the mobile app, long-press your profile icon in the lower-right corner of the app to view your profile menu in Account. You can also tap your profile icon > Add Status.

  2. Select Set a custom status to create a custom status.

  3. In Edit Status, you can create a custom status and choose from the Status Duration menu to set when your status will automatically clear.

  4. Once your custom status is ready, tap Save in the upper-right corner to confirm.

  5. This will lead you back to Account where you can also manage your profile status by selecting from the Online Status menu.

Editing or Clearing a Custom Status
Desktop/Browser

  1. To edit or clear your custom status on desktop or browser, press on your profile icon in the lower-left corner of your app, and select your custom status.

  2. Follow these steps:

  • To clear your custom status, press the trash icon [] to remove it.
  • To edit your custom status, press the pencil icon [] to make changes. .
Left: Trash icon - Used to clear custom status
Right: Pencil icon - Used to edit custom status

Note: Custom statuses override other activity statuses in a server’s members list and friends list within direct messages (DMs) and group chats. However, activity statuses will still show when viewing a user’s full profile.

Mobile

  1. To edit or clear your custom status on mobile, long-press your profile icon in the lower-right corner of your app. You can also tap your profile icon > Edit Status to make edits.

  2. Follow these steps:

  • To clear your custom status, tap the x icon [] to the right of your custom status to remove it.
  • To edit your custom status, tap your current custom status to make changes.
Left: X icon - Clear custom status
Right: Current custom status - Edit custom status
Reacting and Replying to a Custom Status

Reacting and replying to custom statuses is currently an experimental feature available to a limited number of users.

Reacting on Desktop/Browser

  1. To react to a user’s custom status on desktop or browser, select their profile icon to view their profile.

  2. You’ll notice a Send Reaction icon [] above their custom status. Press this icon to choose and send a reaction.

  3. A Reaction sent bubble will confirm that your reaction has been delivered to the user. The reaction will also appear in a DM with the recipient.

Replying on Desktop/Browser

  1. To reply to a user’s custom status on desktop or browser, select their profile icon to view their profile.

  2. You’ll notice a Reply to Status icon [] above their custom status. Press this icon to send a reply.

  3. A Reply sent bubble will confirm that your reply has been delivered to the user. The reply will also appear in a DM with the recipient.

Reacting or Replying on Mobile

  1. To react to a user’s custom status on mobile, tap their profile icon to view their profile.

  2. Next, tap the custom status bubble. This will direct you to the Respond to Status page where you can:

  • Send a reaction by selecting an emoji
  • Reply with a message and tap the send icon []
  1. A Reaction sent or Reply sent bubble will confirm that your response has been delivered to the user.
Left: Reaction sent
Right: Reply sent

The reaction or reply will also appear in a DM with the recipient.

.

Left: Delivered reaction within DM
Right: Delivered reply within DM

Leaderboards allow users to share their stats for a game, activity or application, and compete against other members in a server.

Viewing the Leaderboard

Recently Played Games on Profiles

What this article covers:

  • What is Recently Played Games?
  • How to Manage your Recently Played Games Settings
  • Frequently Asked Questions
What is Recently Played Games?
This feature is currently an experiment and limited to a small percentage of users.

Recently Played Games will display a maximum of 3 tiles on a user’s profile showcasing the recent games that they played. The game, how long ago it was last played, and how much time has been spent playing the game will be displayed in these tiles.

How to Manage your Recently Played Games Settings

If a detectable game you recently played is not showing, here is how to enable it.

Option 1

  1. Tap on the cogwheel [] to enter your User Settings.

  2. Select Connections. If the game you are playing is a verified game, the game should be available for you to add as a connection.

Option 2

  1. Tap on the cogwheel [] to enter your User Settings.

  2. Then head to Registered Games.

  3. If you don’t see your game here, tap on Add it to add the game (make sure your game is open when trying to add it).

  4. If you want to prevent future sharing of a game, tap on the eye icon to disable detection.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How can I disable Recently Played Games from displaying on my profile?

A: Tap on the cogwheel [] to enter your User Settings, then head to Profiles. You should see the option to toggle this feature. A checkmark [] means it’s enabled and an [] means it’s disabled.

Q: How far back/how long can a game activity be displayed on my profile?

A: A game activity will be displayed on your profile for 1 month.

Q: Are Activities also captured in the recently played?

A: Activities will not be displayed.

Q: How many games can be displayed at a time?

A: Only 4 games can be displayed.

Q: Who can see Recent Games on my profile?

Recent Games will be visible to another user if you are friends, if you are suggested friends, if you’ve sent a friend request, or if you share at least one server where you have not disabled Activity Display.

Q: Will disabling Activity Display in a specific server prevent Recent Played Games from appearing on my profile?

Yes. However, if you enable it again at any point, your Recent Played Games (including anything that was played when it was turned off) will then be displayed in your profile.

What do those colored dots next to my avatar mean?

Discord has 5 status icons that are pretty simple representations of user status. They are as follows:

Green = Online

Yellow = Idle

Red = Do Not Disturb

Purple = Streaming

Gray = Invisible/Offline

Keep in mind that you only get put into idle status when you’ve been away from your device for a while- similar to being moved to an AFK (away from keyboard) voice channel. And while Offline doesn’t have a dot, you’ll see the user’s name and avatar grayed out pretty thoroughly.

  • What if I Can’t Access My Discord and Need to Cancel You can cancel your Nitro or Nitro Basic subscription at any time. Once canceled, your subscription will end at the end of your current billing period.

Note: Subscriptions need to be canceled on the same device type where the purchase was originally made.

For example:

If you purchased Nitro through the desktop or browser app, you must cancel it through the desktop app or browser.

If you purchased through a mobile device, you can only cancel through a mobile device. If you don’t have access to your device to cancel yourself, please check out this section.

How to Cancel Nitro Subscription on Desktop/Browser

  1. Tap on the cogwheel [] next to your Discord username to access your User Settings.

  2. Navigate to the Subscriptions tab.

  3. Tap on Cancel within the Nitro or Nitro Basic banner to start the process to cancel your subscription.

  4. Follow the prompts to cancel your subscription.

How to Cancel Nitro Subscription on Mobile

  1. Tap on your avatar in the bottom right.

  2. Tap on the cogwheel [] in the top right.

  3. Scroll down to Billing Settings and tap on Manage Nitro.

  4. Here, you can cancel your Nitro or Nitro Basic subscription. Follow the prompts on screen until the cancellation is confirmed.

Once the cancellation has been completed, your Manage Nitro settings will show the date on which your subscription will expire and you will lose your Nitro benefits.

Alternatively, you can also cancel your Discord subscriptions directly on your mobile device settings by following these instructions for Apple iOS subscriptions or Google Play subscriptions

How Do I Re-Subscribe After Canceling My Subscription?

Note: If you’re trying to re-subscribe on your mobile device, the steps might be a little different. Please head to the Manage Nitro tab under your User Settings in order to re-subscribe your subscription.

If you change your mind and no longer wish for your Nitro subscription to end at the end of your billing period, then you can always reactivate it. Just make sure you do so before the billing period ends, otherwise you’ll just have to purchase a new subscription. Here’s how to re-subscribe:

  1. Tap on cogwheel [] next to your Discord username to access your User Settings.

  2. Navigate to the Subscriptions tab.

  3. Tap on Re-Subscribe within the corresponding banner to uncancel your subscription.

You’ll be able to tell it was reactivated because you’ll see the banner no longer has Pending Cancellation displayed.

What if I Can’t Access my Discord and Need to Cancel?

Note: If your Discord purchase was through an Apple device, please reach out to Apple to cancel your subscription. The Discord Support team is not able to manage your iOS subscription.

If you’re unable to log into your Discord account for any reason and cancel your subscription (for desktop, browser, or even through an Android device), you can reach out to our Billing Support team with the email address tied to your Discord account and request it to be canceled through this support form: dis.gd.

If you want to submit a refund request instead, and your purchase is within our Refund Policy, please follow the steps outlined in our Refund Policy.

Discord Nitro gives you access to enhanced features and perks. If you’re looking to upgrade your current subscription, here’s how to do it.

Upgrading Your Nitro Subscription

You can upgrade your subscription in two ways—either change the product type or subscription length:

  • Current Nitro Basic or Nitro Classic subscriptions can be upgraded to Nitro
  • Monthly subscriptions (Nitro Basic or Nitro) can be upgraded to yearly plans Info: Nitro Classic subscribers can only upgrade to Nitro.

Important requirements for upgrading:

  • Your subscription must be active
  • You can upgrade from Nitro Basic to Nitro whenever you want
  • All upgrades take effect right away
  • Subscription upgrades during a billing period or payments under 50 cents may not qualify for proration. Instead, a new billing period will start with a discount for remaining time.
How to Upgrade Your Subscription
Desktop/Browser

  1. Open the Discord desktop app or browser and navigate to your User Settings by selecting the cogwheel icon [] in the bottom-left corner.

  2. Select the Subscriptions tab and press Switch Plans in the subscription banner.

  3. Follow the prompts to upgrade your subscription.

Upgrading Subscription on Desktop
Mobile

  1. In the Discord mobile app, tap your avatar in the bottom-right corner.

  2. Tap the cogwheel [] in the upper-right corner to navigate to Settings > Manage Nitro.

  3. Tap the cogwheel [] in the upper-right corner to view your Nitro plan.

Navigating to Your Nitro Plan on Mobile
  1. In the subscription banner, tap Switch plans and follow the prompts to upgrade your subscription.
Switch plans Button in Subscription Banner
What Happens When You Upgrade?

When you upgrade your subscription:

  • Your new benefits will be available immediately
  • You’ll be charged the price difference prorated for the remaining time on your current subscription
  • Your next billing date will remain the same
Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What happens to my unused time when I upgrade?

A: When you upgrade, the remaining time on your current subscription will be prorated and applied as credit toward your new subscription.

Q: Can I switch between different types of Nitro subscriptions?

A: Yes, you can upgrade from Nitro Basic or Nitro Classic to Nitro. However, you cannot downgrade subscriptions - you’ll need to wait until your current subscription ends to switch to a lower tier.

Please note that if you upgrade or cancel your Nitro Classic subscription, you will not be able to re-subscribe to Classic.

Q: Why do I need to use the same payment method for upgrades as my subscription?

A: For security and billing consistency, your payment method for upgrades must match the one used for your recurring subscription.

Q: How can I use a different payment method for my upgrade?

A: To use a different payment method:

  • First change your subscription’s payment method
  • Then proceed with the upgrade Please note: The payment method you choose for the upgrade will become your new default payment method for future subscription payments.

Q: Will upgrading change my billing date?

A: No, upgrading your subscription will not change your billing date. Your next payment will still occur on the same day.

Q: What happens if I upgrade from a monthly to yearly subscription?

A: When upgrading from monthly to yearly, you’ll be charged for the yearly plan minus the prorated credit from your remaining monthly subscription time.

Q: Will I lose my current benefits when upgrading?

A: No, you’ll keep all your current benefits plus gain additional features from the upgraded tier.

Q: Can I upgrade from a monthly to an annual plan?

A: Yes, you can change your billing cycle when upgrading. Nitro annual plans offer a better value for your Discord experience!

Q: What payment methods are accepted?

A: Discord accepts credit/debit cards, PayPal, and various regional payment methods based on your location. Learn more about acceptable payment methods here.

Info: Pricing varies by region. Please check the current rates in your location before upgrading. For details about localized pricing on Discord, press here.

Q: How do I cancel my Nitro subscription?

A: You can cancel your Nitro subscription at any time through User Settings > Subscriptions on the device you initially made your purchase. After cancellation, you’ll continue to have access to Nitro features until the end of your current billing period. Note that if you purchased through a third party (like the App Store or Google Play), you’ll need to cancel through that platform instead. For detailed instructions, see our guide on canceling Nitro subscriptions.

iOS Purchases on Discord FAQ

What this article covers:

  • iOS Purchases on Discord
  • Frequently Asked Questions
iOS Purchases on Discord

When making most purchases on Discord via iOS, there are a few important considerations to keep in mind.

Most Discord subscriptions bought through iOS (such as a Nitro, Nitro gifting, or Server Boost) or the Apple App Store are linked to your Apple ID. This is similar to how purchases work with the Google Play Store. Here’s what you need to know:

  • The Discord account used for the first-time purchase of a subscription will link to the Apple ID used for the purchase.

  • Future iOS subscriptions will automatically apply to that same Discord account.

  • You cannot purchase or manage multiple subscriptions for two different Discord accounts through iOS. If you want to purchase a Discord subscription on iOS for a different account than the one linked to your Apple account, there are a few options:

  • Try using a different device or Discord platform, such as the desktop app, to purchase the subscription on the secondary Discord account.

  • If you’re not using your original Discord account, you can cancel the subscription tied to it and delete the account. Once both steps are complete, you will be able to use your Apple ID on the new account. Please note: the account deletion process will take up to 15 days to complete. ’ Note: Discord is unable to assist with Apple subscription issues. Discord subscriptions purchased through the Apple App Store can only be managed in your Apple settings. Users can’t manage these subscriptions via desktop, browser, or Android.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I know if my subscription is managed through Apple?

A: To check if Apple manages your Discord subscription on your iOS device, follow the steps on Apple’s official website: support.apple.com.

To review your subscription on Discord, head into to your User Settings in the desktop/browser Discord app by selecting the cogwheel icon [] in the bottom-right corner of the app. Once there, navigate to Subscriptions where you will find you are able to review your subscription details.

Example of Apple managed subscription within Discord

Q: What should I do if my Discord purchase made via iOS is marked as Past Due?

A: If your Discord purchase made via iOS is marked as Past Due, try these steps:

  • Verify that the billing address for the charged card is up-to-date and matches your bank’s information.
  • Double-check that your card details are entered correctly.
  • Make sure the card hasn’t expired.
  • Ensure there are sufficient funds in the account or that you haven’t exceeded the credit limit.
  • Check if you’ve reached a pre-set spending limit on the card. If you’re still having trouble processing your subscription renewal after trying these steps, contact Apple’s Support team. Visit the Apple Support page and log in with the Apple ID you used for the purchase.

Q: I purchased a subscription (Nitro, Server Boosts, etc.) on my Apple device and would like a refund. What should I do?

A: We are unable to process refunds for Discord purchases through iOS, including Nitro, Nitro Classic, Nitro Basic, gift subscriptions, and premium apps. For further assistance, please contact Apple Support by visiting reportaproblem.apple.com and logging in with the Apple ID used to make your purchase(s). For more information about both refund policies, please see Discord’s refund policy, and Apple’s refund policy.

Q: I made a Server Subscription purchase via iOS and would like a refund. What should I do?

A: Discord’s support team can help refund a Server Subscription purchase if the request was made within 5 days from your initial purchase date. Additionally, Server Subscription refunds are a one-time only exception. To submit a refund request, head over to dis.gd/support to submit a ticket.

Q: My friend gave me a gift credit, but I have an active subscription managed through iOS. What should I do?

A: Please be aware that gift credits cannot be redeemed on mobile devices.

To use the gift credit, you will need to cancel your current subscription through your Apple device. Note that subscriptions do not end immediately; they will terminate at the end of the current billing period. Once your subscription has ended, you can redeem your gift credit by subscribing to a matching subscription using the web or desktop client.

Q: I purchased a Nitro subscription and it’s not appearing or working. What should I do?

A: If you purchased a subscription directly from the Apple App Store via your Apple device, the purchase should appear under the Discord account associated with your Apple ID. Check the User Settings > Billing tab within the Discord account you originally made purchases on.

Q: I purchased Nitro Basic and now I want to upgrade to Nitro or add additional Server Boosts to my Server Boost subscription purchased through the Apple App Store. How can I do this?

A: To upgrade your subscription from Nitro Basic to Nitro, you’ll need to manage it through your Apple device. Follow these steps:

  1. Open your Settings.

  2. Select Apple ID.

  3. Go to Subscriptions.

  4. Tap on the active subscription.

  5. Select “See all Plan Types” and select the subscription you wish to have.

If you encounter any issues with your subscription or the upgrade process, please contact Apple Support for further assistance.

Q: I’m trying to make a Discord purchase through my Apple device and it’s not working. What should I do?

A: If you’re experiencing issues while attempting to make a Discord purchase on your Apple device, we recommend trying to complete the purchase on the Desktop or Web client instead. If using a different device is not an option, the problem might be related to the Apple App Store. In this case, please contact Apple Support for further assistance.

Subscription Credit FAQ

Subscription Credit can only be used for desktop/browser subscriptions. They cannot be used on Google Play or iOS App Store subscriptions.

What this article covers:

  • What is Subscription Credit?
    • What are the limitations of Subscription Credit?
  • How do I activate my Subscription Credit?
    • What if I have an active Subscription?
  • What happens if I cancel my Subscription?
What is Subscription Credit?

Instead of gifted subscription time being automatically added onto your already existing subscription, gifted subscription time will become Subscription Credit!

When you activate your subscription credit, your subscription will renew at its usual renewal date, and subscription credit will be applied.

You will not be charged and you will receive an email confirming renewal at $0.

To view your Subscription Credit:

  1. Start by logging into your Discord account on the desktop or browser version of the app.

  2. Tap on the cog wheel icon next to your username to open up User Settings.

  3. Then tap on the Subscriptions tab in the left side bar.

What are the limitations of Subscription Credit?
Subscription credit can only be consumed and redeemed for matching Nitro subscriptions. Nitro for Nitro, Nitro Basic for Nitro Basic, and Nitro Classic for Nitro Classic.

If you have Nitro Basic Monthly subscription credits, you will deplete that subscription credit only while subscribed at the Nitro Basic Monthly subscription (not Nitro).

These same rules apply if you have Nitro subscription credits. In that instance, you can only deplete your subscription credit if you’re currently subscribed to Nitro (not Nitro Basic)!

How do I activate my Subscription Credit?

When your current Nitro subscription has expired or is removed, the subscription credit for the gift will apply when you activate that matching subscription on the desktop/browser Discord app.

For example, if you currently have Nitro Monthly Credit, you will need to activate a Nitro Monthly subscription to use this subscription credit!

To activate the matching subscription:

  1. Start by heading to the Subscription tab and pressing the Subscribe button for the matching subscription type for Nitro, Nitro Classic, or Nitro Basic.

  2. A new window will pop up where you will need to select the matching plan for the subscription.

  3. If your Discord account does not have your payment information, you’ll be asked to fill out your payment details. (Note: You will not be charged unless the subscription renews)

  4. Once you’ve finished submitting that information, you’ll then see a “Subscription Credit applied” message as you are reviewing the purchase details for activating the subscription.

  5. After you confirm your activation, your subscription credit will then be activated!

What if I already have an active Subscription?

If you already have an active Nitro/Nitro Classic/Nitro Basic subscription and you have a matching subscription credit, the Subscription Credit will be stored on your account to be automatically used when your subscription renews.

If you already have an active Server Boost subscription (which does not come from the boosts included with a Nitro subscription) and you sign up for a matching Nitro/Nitro Classic/Nitro Basic subscription, you won’t automatically activate the subscription credit, and will instead be charged a prorated amount for the remaining time of that month’s billing cycle. Your Subscription Credit, if it matches the subscription type, would be used the following month on the renewal date. This ensures you get the full benefit of the subscription credit!

What happens if I cancel my Subscription?

If you cancel your subscription and you don’t have any subscription credit, your subscription will end at the renewal date instead of billing you again.

But if your subscription is canceled and you do have subscription credit on your account, you will need to go through the process of making a purchase of that same Nitro plan as the subscription credit - but instead of being charged, Discord will utilize the subscription credit already associated with your account before charging your card for another months time.

If you have any further questions about Subscription Credits, please reach out to our support team through dis.gd/billing.
To receive help as quickly as possible, please make sure that you are using the email address that’s associated with your Discord account.

Why Does My Payment Show As A Pending Charge?

What this article covers:

  • What is a Pending Charge?
  • What if I See Multiple Pending Charges?
What is a Pending Charge?
Example of a Pending purchase in the Billing tab

If you see a pending charge on Discord, this indicates that the charge was unsuccessful because it requires further verification from your bank or card provider. You’ll need to reach out to your payment provider for steps on how to correct this pending charge.

If the pending charge isn’t resolved, it will automatically cancel within 3 days. The status of the charge will then change to Failed in your User Settings > Billing. If a pending charge still appears on your bank statement, it should be removed within 5-10 business days.

What if I see Multiple Pending Charges?

The only time you may see multiple pending charges are when your payments have not been successfully processed, or they’re in a Past Due state.

When renewing a subscription and your renewal payment does not successfully go through, we will attempt the purchase again to ensure that your subscription goes uninterrupted. Once a payment successfully goes through, our system will attempt to cancel all other pending payments.

Note: If you are still seeing the pending charge after 10 business days, you can reach out to the Billing Support team for them to review through here: dis.gd/billing

Why is My Payment Showing as Failed or Invalid?

What this article covers:

  • Why is My Payment Showing As Failed?
  • Why is My Payment showing as Invalid Payment?
  • Why is My Payment Method showing as Invalid?
Why is my Payment Showing As Failed?
Billing tab under User Settings on desktop/browser

There are several reasons that can cause a payment to fail. To figure out what’s going on, we recommend following the steps below:

  1. Ensure that the billing address associated with the card being charged is current and matches the information filed with your bank. You can learn how to manage your billing information here.

  2. Ensure your card details are entered correctly.

  3. Ensure the card hasn’t expired.

  4. Depending on the card, ensure there are sufficient funds in the account or that the credit limit hasn’t been exceeded.

  5. It’s possible a pre-set spending limit on the card was reached. Double-check if a spending limit has been set.

Note: If issues persist after following the steps above, Discord’s Support team cannot provide further assistance. We recommend contacting your bank or using another payment method.

Why is my Payment showing as Invalid Payment?

If you’re receiving an Invalid payment error message, it means there is an error with the payment method you are trying to use. Please review the information you provided and try again.

Example of an Invalid payment message when making a purchase
Why is My Payment Method showing as Invalid?

If you’re seeing the Invalid error for one of your listed payment methods, try to attempt your purchase again.

Example of an Invalid payment error under Payment Methods

Note: If you’re still getting an error message, please reach out to our Support team for further assistance through here: dis.gd/billing

Why is My Subscription Showing as Past Due?

What this article covers:

  • What Does it mean when my Subscription shows as Past Due?
    • What happens to my subscription when it’s Past Due?
  • Frequently Asked Questions
What Does It Mean When My Subscription Shows As Past Due?

When taking a look in your Subscriptions tab, you may notice that your Billing Information shows as past due.

Examples of a Past Due Subscription on desktop (left) and mobile (right)

When a subscription is past due, it means that your subscription renewal payment failed. This happens when a payment fails to process on the renewal date.

What Happens To My Subscription When It’s Past Due?

If your Nitro, Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or Server Boost subscription is past due, you will have 30 to 60 days to pay for your subscription depending on where you signed up:

  • Desktop: 30 days from the renewal date
  • Google Play Store: 30 days from the renewal date
  • iOS App Store: 60 days from the renewal date While your subscription is in the past due state, you will retain access to your perks for the duration of time listed above.

If a successful payment for the subscription is not made before the window ends, the subscription will automatically end and you’ll lose access to your subscription perks and related streaks.

After you successfully make the past due payment, keep in mind that your next renewal charge may occur soon after depending on your renewal date. You can find your renewal date under Payment information in the Subscriptions Tab.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: I just paid for my past due subscription? Why was I charged twice?

A: After you have paid for your past due subscription, your next subscription renewal may be charged immediately depending on the renewal date of your subscription. You can find the date your subscription renews under User Settings > Subscriptions > Payment.

Q: Can I cancel or change my subscription plan while it has a past due payment?

A: You can cancel your subscription while it’s in a past due state by visiting User Settings > Subscriptions > Cancel. However, you won’t be able to change the plan you’re on until you pay for the past due payment on your current plan. Learn more about managing your subscription here.

Q: Can I redeem my Nitro gift credits while my subscription is past due?

A: Yes, you can redeem Nitro gift credits even if your subscription is past due. If you have a Nitro gift credit before your payment fails, the credit will be applied immediately to your subscription’s upcoming billing cycle.

Also, if your account is already past due and you receive a gift credit, the credit will be applied during the next renewal attempt, and your subscription will become active again.

Note: Using a gift credit does not change the billing date for your subscription. If your account has been past due for some time (e.g., 10 days), part of the gift credit will be used to cover that period.

Q: If my payment is not made on time, what happens to my perks?

A: Depending on which platform you purchased the subscription, you’ll have access to your subscription perks for 30-60 days after your payment fails. If you do not make the payment before this window ends, your subscription will automatically end, and you will lose any perks associated with your subscription.

Q: Does my billing date change if I resolve my payment issues after my subscription is past due?

A: No. Making a payment on a subscription that’s past due does not change your renewal date.

Q: Why do I see multiple charges on my bank account?

A: The only time you should see multiple pending charges are when your payments have not been successfully processed. When renewing a subscription and your renewal payment does not successfully go through, we will attempt the purchase again to ensure that your subscription goes uninterrupted. Once a payment successfully goes through, all other pending payments are canceled.

Q: My subscription is managed by iOS or Android and my subscription went past due, what do I do?

A: The Google Play Store allows subscriptions to be past due for a total of 30 days, while Apple (iOS) has 60 days to be past due. You will need to complete your payment through where your subscription is managed.

Q: What happens to my streaks when my subscription is past due?

A: Your streak will not be affected, as long as you make a payment during the grace period. However, if the payment is not made within the grace period then the streak will reset and can not be restored.

Troubleshooting Help

“Email is Already Registered” Errors

There are some error messages that you might notice when trying to log in or register an account through an email address. Let’s go over those cases and what to do if you’re experiencing those specific errors!

What this article covers:

  • Email is Already Registered
  • Email Does Not Exist
Email is Already Registered

The system only allows for one email address to be tied to an account, this means you cannot have multiple Discord accounts that are associated with one email address.

If you try to register an email address with an account and you receive the error message, “Email is Already Registered”, this means there’s another Discord account with this email address already. In that case, please try logging into the account instead of trying to register a new one!

If you suspect you might have created an accidental account you can refer to this article for further steps on how to proceed.
Email Does Not Exist

If you are trying to log into an account using your email address and you’re receiving the error message “Email does not exist”, this means that the email address you are entering is not registered with a Discord account.

Please double-check the spelling and if it’s still not working, please try another email address to log in or your phone number if it was tied to your account.

If you’re still having trouble logging into your account, please reach out to our Support team for further assistance: dis.gd.

iOS What is happening with my game audio?

Discord utilizes iPhone’s built-in audio processing unit for echo cancellation and automatic gain control. As a result, you get higher quality voice with Discord on your device. Unfortunately, when you put Discord to the background to play a game, iOS reduces the audio output level of your game.

For the best experience, we recommend to use a headset. iOS still reduces your game audio output level, but you can hear both the game and your Discord buddies.

Occasionally, when joining a voice channel on Discord (your game is in the background), your game audio may get paused. If you restart the game, you should hear both Discord and the game.

Note: This is a feature that iOS has built into their system & unfortunately there are currently no settings within iOS to disable it.

Known Issues MacBook Audio Issue (7/1/2020)

Our team has received reports regarding output audio issues in voice calls on the Macbook Discord client. Specifically, audio coming from the left side of the Macbook is very faint.

We would like to clarify that this behavior is by design to reduce echos going into the mic. MacBooks have their microphone under the left speaker.

However, our browser client does not share this behavior. If you would like to switch to our browser client, you can log in here [http://discord.com/login].

macOS Install and Updating Errors

Hey, listen! If you’re having issues updating or installing Discord on your shiny Macintosh machine, we can help! Though not intentional, there are various issues that can cause the install or update process to fail. You’ll see this as an endless update, or an unexplained install error! In cases like these, completely reinstalling Discord will often improve our updater’s performance and clear out any issues. Follow these steps!

Note: Remember that Discord only supports MacOS 10.11 and up (El Capitan) or above! Also, if you’re running macOS on a machine that wasn’t produced by Apple (IE, a Hackintosh), you may run into unique issues!
Reinstalling Discord
  • Close Discord by using ⌘+Q or selecting the Quit option from the menubar, then make sure all Discord processes are terminated from within your Mac’s Activity Monitor. (You can quickly launch the Activity Monitor by using Spotlight or Siri on your Mac!)
  • Delete the 2 following folders:
    • ~/Library/Application Support/Discord
    • /Library/Application Support/Discord To find those folders, open Finder, press ⇧⌘+G (or Go > Go to Folder in the menubar), and enter:

~/Library/Application Support in the window and hit enter:

Then /Library/Application Support in the run window and hit enter:

In both of these cases, find the Discord folders in these files and drag them to your Trash. Note: There may not be a Discord folder in the second file (/Library/Application Support). If there isn’t, that’s okay!

Next, open your Applications folder. Find Discord and drag it to your Trash. Finally, empty your Trash!

If your OS tells you that the file cannot be deleted because it’s still in use. Open up the Activity Monitor and terminate all instances of Discord.

  • Restart your system.
  • Reinstall via discord.com
Note: Make sure that all instances of Discord are closed out before attempting these steps!
Diagnosing Network Issues

If reinstalling Discord doesn’t do the trick, it’s possible your network configuration is preventing our updater from doing its job! To clear up any networking issues, there’s some basic troubleshooting steps you should try!

First, try setting your DNS to Google Public DNS!

  • Open System Preferences from your Mac’s Apple menu, then select Network. From there, choose the network you’re currently using (for example, Wi-Fi)

  • Select Advanced…, select the DNS tab in the top bar, then use the Plus button under DNS Servers to add the following DNS server options!

    • 8.8.8.8
    • 8.8.4.4
    • 2001:4860:4860::8888
    • 2001:4860:4860::8844

  • Click OK, then close System Preferences and try relaunching Discord! If that doesn’t do the trick, try renewing your Mac’s IP address!

  • Open System Preferences from your Mac’s Apple menu, then select Network. From there, choose the network you’re currently using (for example, Wi-Fi)

  • Select Advanced…, then select the TCP/IP tab

  • Click Renew DHCP Lease

  • Select OK, close System Preferences, then try relaunching Discord once more!

Note: If none of these steps do the trick, reach out to our Support Team at dis.gd

[Windows 10] Allowing Access for Microphone & Camera

Before using your Microphone for Voice Calls, and your Camera for Video Calls, you may have to grant permission for apps to access your Microphone and Camera. This guide will show you how!

To get started, go into Windows Settings > Privacy > Microphone AND Camera.

You’ll see two toggles under the “Allow apps to access your camera/microphone,” turn both of these to “On” and voilà!

&

You’ve just enabled permission for apps to use both! Do a little happy dance, you’ve earned it!

Windows Capturing Application Window for Screen Share and Go Live

Discord uses multiple techniques to capture an application window for Go Live and Screen Share. We are thrilled to introduce a new capture method for Windows user: Windows Graphics Capture.

Windows Graphics Capture is available on Windows 10 and above and is the latest Windows API to capture an application window.

Discord uses multiple technologies to capture your screen. Our current default capture method uses similar technology to capture your screen that is used for overlay - “Use our advanced technology to capture your screen”. Our signed DLL is injected into the application to extract rendered frames as they are being sent to Windows for display.

On Windows 11 and higher, we will change the default capture method to Windows Graphics Capture. Unfortunately, it does not work for full screen exclusive (FSE) games.

We use SHQueryUserNotificationState to determine whether the game is running in full screen exclusive mode. However, this method may give false positive and we fall back to other capture methods.

How do I check which capture method is used?

If you enable Developer Mode under Advanced User Settings, you can open Debug panel by clicking Voice/Video Connected.

Under the Screen Share tab, Discord shows the number of frames captured for each screen share method.

How do I check whether the game is running in full screen exclusive mode?

Open Xbox Game Bar (Windows + G). If the game minimizes, it uses FSE. If Xbox Game Bar renders smoothly on top of your game, it uses borderless fullscreen.

Certain games offer to use the Full Screen or Borderless option. If the Full Screen option is selected, we may misclassify the game as using FSE and disable Windows Graphics Capture.

If you would like to get the best screen share performance, please select the Borderless option.

Windows Corrupt Installation

We’re constantly working on improving Discord’s infrastructure to make your chat & voice experience as seamless as possible, but sometimes we confuse this with that and as a result, your version of Discord might not be completely up to date. If you clicked the “Well, it looks like your Discord installation is corrupt.” banner, reinstall Discord using the following steps to get all caught up:

  • Close Discord in the system tray and make sure all Discord processes are terminated. (Sometimes stray processes can hide in your system tray or your task manager- double-check those!)
  • Delete the 2 following folders:
    • %AppData%/Discord
    • %LocalAppData%/Discord To find those folders, hit the Start button + R, and enter:

%appdata% in the run window and hit enter:

Then %localappdata% in the run window and hit enter:

Then find the “Discord” folder in both of those windows, and delete it.

If your OS tells you that the file cannot be deleted because it’s still in use, open up the Task Manager and terminate all instances of Discord there and in the startup tab.

  • Restart your system.
  • Reinstall via Windows Download In some cases, these extra steps may be necessary.

Set the Discord application (%LocalAppData%/Discord/most recent version) to run as Administrator and set Compatibility to Windows 7 or 8 (try both)

Make sure that all instances of Discord, including the browser version, are closed out before attempting the steps.

Windows DirectX Diagnostic
